## Chapter eleven on the strengths of any planet in any of its dignities.

**S**ince we previously spoke of the powers of each planet in any of the signs: it now seems appropriate to treat their strengths within them. **Alchabicius** <note>original: "Alchabicius"; referring to Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> said that every **House** <note>The primary sign a planet rules.</note> has five strengths; the lord of **Exaltation** has four strengths; the lord of **Triplicity** has three strengths; the lord of **Term** has two strengths; the lord of **Face** <note>Also known as a decan, a 10-degree subdivision of a sign.</note> has one strength. And according to this method, you can know the strengths of the planets in the signs; thus, whichever planet has more of these strengths in a particular sign is said to be stronger in that place, more powerful, and of greater authority. Regarding this, **Messahallah** <note>An influential 8th-century Jewish-Persian astrologer.</note> placed the lord of the Term above the lord of the Triplicity; however, **Al-Andarzaghar** <note>original: "alędegoq"; likely a corruption of Al-Andarzaghar, a Sassanid Persian astrologer.</note> placed the lord of the Triplicity above the lord of the Term. They appear to be in contradiction, but it is not so: for **Messahallah** was speaking with his intention focused on "direction" <note>A technique for predicting the timing of life events.</note>, while **Al-Andarzaghar** spoke with his intention focused on "nutrition" <note>Referring to the physical growth and vital essence of the person.</note>; thus both spoke well, and the statements of both are preserved. What direction is and what nutrition is, I believe has been made sufficiently clear to you above. And he gave this sort of analogy for this matter: because when a planet is in its own house, it is like a man who is in his own home. For everyone is stronger by right in their own house than in another's, and yet we see in fact that another may be stronger there than he who otherwise would be; hence the common proverb:
> Every cock stands before his own gate, as does every vassal. <note>original: "Ante suum gallus stat portam quisq; vasallus"</note>
And when it is in its **Exaltation**, it is like a man who is in his kingdom and in his glory: such as a kingship, a power, or a dukedom; and like other secular dignities which can fail him sooner than his own personal property. And when it is in its **Term**, it is like that man who is among his relatives, kinsmen, paternal relations, maternal relations, in-laws, and those belonging to him by parentage. And when it is in its **Triplicity**, it is like a man who is among his helpers, his people, his ministers, and his followers who obey him and follow him but are not related to him by birth. And when it is in its **Face**, it is like a man who is among people who are not well known to him, as sometimes happens to travelers and the like; but he lives among them by his skill, his mastery, his service, or by whatever other craft or secular art.

## Chapter twenty: which of the signs are called rational, and which have beautiful voices, and which are domestic, and which have other qualities, and which are quadrupeds.

**A**lchabicius said that four whole signs are called **rational**—namely **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**—and also the first half of **Sagittarius**, because their images are formed after the images of humans. And they are said to have **beautiful voices**; and they are said to flourish when they are in the East: since their power appears better and is more effective when they are in the Eastern quarter than in any of the other quarters. And three of them are said to have **wings**: namely **Gemini**, **Virgo**, and **Pisces**. And four whole signs are called **quadrupeds** <note>Four-footed animals.</note>: namely **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, and **Capricorn**, along with the last part of **Sagittarius**. And three of them are called **domestic** because they are formed after the images of domestic animals: namely **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Capricorn**. And those two—namely **Aries** and **Taurus**—are said to flourish in the South, because their power appears more suited and fitting in the Southern quarter than in any of the other quarters. And two of them are said to flourish in the North: namely **Virgo** and **Aquarius**. Some indeed have said that **Virgo** flourishes in the East and in the North. **Capricorn** flourishes in the South and in the North. **Aries** and **Taurus** flourish in the South, as **Alchabicius** said.

<column-break/>

**Virgo**, **Capricorn**, and **Aquarius** are said to flourish when they are in the North. And of the signs, some are called **vicious** and **twisted** <note>Signs that rise "crookedly" or are associated with physical deformities.</note>, such as **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Capricorn**. And some of them are said to have **many offspring**: namely **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. Therefore, if a question is asked about children, and the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart.</note> or the lord of the Ascendant or the House of Children <note>The 5th house of a zodiac chart.</note> or its lord, or the **Moon**, is in one of those signs, it is said to signify many children, unless something else prevents it, as will be said in the chapter on children. And these three are said to flourish in the West. And three of them are called **sterile**: namely **Gemini**, **Leo**, and **Virgo**. Therefore, if a question is asked about children and any of the aforementioned significators is found in one of those signs, it signifies sterility, unless something else helps, as will be said below in the chapter on children. And six of them are said to have **few children**: namely **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Libra**, **Sagittarius**, **Capricorn**, and **Aquarius**. Thus, if a question is asked about children and any of the aforementioned significators is found in one of those six signs, it signifies a scarcity of children. And four of them are called **very vicious**: namely **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, and **Capricorn**. And among the signs, some are said to have a **half-voice**, such as those formed in the images of animals that bleat, low, or roar, like **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, and **Capricorn**, and the last part of **Sagittarius**. Therefore, if the **Ascendant**, its lord, or the **Moon** in someone's birth chart is in one of those signs, the newborn will be of little speech, unless something else helps, as will be said in the treatise on births. And some of them are called **voiceless** <note>Also called "mute" signs.</note>: namely those formed in the images of animals without voices, such as **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. Therefore, if the **Ascendant**, its lord, or the **Moon** is in those signs, it signifies that the newborn will lack a voice, unless something else helps, as I shall tell you in the said treatise on births (if God wills). And two of them are called **dark** <note>original: "tenebrosa"</note>: namely **Libra** and **Capricorn**. Thus, if the **Ascendant**, its lord, or the **Moon** is in any of those signs in the birth chart of someone who is afflicted, it signifies that the newborn will be dull-witted and have a dark face. There is also a certain place in the signs called **combust**: namely the **Combust Way** <note>original: "via combusta"; a traditionally debilitated area of the zodiac.</note>, which is from the middle of **Libra** to the middle of **Scorpio**. But you might ask: what is the use of **Alchabicius** saying that signs flourish in the East, South, West, or North; and that some are called rational, some quadrupeds, some domestic, some having a beautiful voice, some a half-voice, and some lacking a voice? To this it must be answered that the philosopher's intention in this was that when someone is born and their significator or the **Moon** is in those signs, the nature and being of the newborn will be according to the being of the significator or the **Moon** in that sign. For example, if the significator, the **Moon**, and the **Ascendant** are in any of the signs formed after the images of humans, the newborn will be more **rational** and a better speaker than one born when the significators are in other signs. And if someone is born with the significator, the **Moon**, and the **Ascendant** in any of the signs formed in the image of animals that low, bleat, or roar, then the newborn will speak less and be less capable of organizing his words. And if someone is born with the **Moon**, the significator, and the **Ascendant** in signs that lack a voice, roar, lowing, or bleating, then the newborn will be a stutterer and speak very little. And if the significator of the birth or the **Moon** is afflicted (namely one of them), then the newborn will speak less according to the amount of the affliction. And if both are afflicted, the newborn will speak even less and worse, so that he can hardly utter a word...

Indeed, if the significator of the birth and the Moon are hindered in any of the signs lacking a voice, then the newborn will be mute and a companion [to the deaf] if that sign was ascending. And they say that the signs flourish in the fourth [quarter] just as it was said, because their power appears then more than when they are in those quarters; not that they have other significations in one quarter than in another. Rather, it is a description just like that of a certain tree which is the same in winter as it is in summer and spring; yet nevertheless, in the beginning of spring it begins to turn green when it expands both leaves and flowers; however, it remains the same tree that it was before. And Leo, which flourishes in all quarters, is likened to trees that flourish in all seasons of the year, such as the olive, the pine, the holm oak, the juniper, and so on.

### Chapter twenty-one: which part of the body each sign is said to rule, its significance for every limb, human character, and what it signifies concerning seeds, regions, and similar things.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a ram, representing the zodiac sign Aries.</image-desc>

The human body is divided into 12 parts according to the likeness of the 12 signs: and each sign is said to rule one of those parts.

### Concerning Aries.

Aries rules the head and the entire face of the human body; hence the saying: "And because spring's path is no greater at the vertex, therefore it deservedly possesses the head." <note>original: "Et qz ver nec vie este i vertice maior: inde nec merito possidet ille caput." This refers to Aries being the start of the astrological year at the spring equinox.</note> And of regions, it rules Babylonia, Babel, Persia, Azerbaijan <note>original: "adrabigen"</note>, and Palestine. And Aries is said to rule the head because the virtue or force of Aries flourishes more in the head than in any other part of itself. And Aries is said to rule the aforementioned regions because those things which are signified by Aries appear more in those regions than in others.

### Concerning Taurus.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a bull, representing the zodiac sign Taurus.</image-desc>

Taurus rules the neck of the human body down to the beginning of the shoulders; hence the saying: "Thence the Bull holds the neck for a similar reason, wherefore the second place is said to be." <note>original: "Inde colluz tenet Taurus simili rōne vñ secūdus est dicť eē locus." Taurus is the second sign of the zodiac.</note> And it has power over trees that are planted. And Taurus is said to rule the neck because its force flourishes more in the neck than in any other part of itself. And of regions, it rules Egypt <note>original: "alcemiet," likely referring to Al-Kimiya/Egypt.</note>, Elmechin, and Azerbaijan. And Taurus is said to rule those regions because its significations appear more in those regions than in others.

### Concerning Gemini.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of two nude figures (twins), representing the zodiac sign Gemini.</image-desc>

Gemini rules the shoulders of the human body from the beginning forward, as well as the arms and hands; hence the saying: "It leans from the shoulders, Gemini possesses both; since by the shoulders man is made double." <note>original: "Nititur ex humeris geminanos possidet ābos: inde q̄ per humeris ſit geminatus homo."</note> And it signifies the generosity and goodness of soul of the newborn if it was the ascendant of someone's birth. And of regions, it is said to rule Georgia <note>original: "iurgen"</note>, Greater Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Egypt. And it is said to rule the shoulders, arms, and hands because a person is "doubled" from the shoulders forward toward the hands. And it is said to rule those regions because its significations appear more in those regions than in others.

<column-break/>

### Concerning Cancer.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a crab, representing the zodiac sign Cancer.</image-desc>

Cancer rules the part of the human body from the chest down near the diaphragm, the adjacent parts in those areas, and the lungs. And **Alchabicius** <note>original: "Alcabicius"; a 10th-century Arab astrologer.</note> said that it likewise rules the spleen; hence the saying: "Cancer: and for that reason it is called a celestial sign. In the chest, because it holds the hollows of the great chest." <note>original: "Cancer: z idcirco signū celeste vocatur. Pectore quod magno pectoris antra tenet."</note> And of regions, it rules Lesser Armenia; and it rules the eastern part, Khorasan <note>original: "huracen"</note> and Asir <note>original: "acin"</note>; and it has a part in Bharat <note>original: "baurath"</note> and Azerbaijan. And it has power over tall trees that lose their leaves in autumn, such as poplars and the like. And it is said to rule those regions because its significations appear more in those regions than in others.

### Concerning Leo.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a lion, representing the zodiac sign Leo.</image-desc>

Leo rules the stomach and heart of the human body, the lower part of the chest where spiritedness flourishes, the diaphragm, and the side of the spine. It signifies a person who is clever, versatile, and who suffers much from anguish and sadness; and likewise the spine and the flanks. Hence the saying: "Thence the Lion likewise rules the lower part of the chest, within which the spirited part flourishes." <note>original: "Inde Leo pariter partē regiť inferiorē pectoris istra quā pars animosa viget."</note> And it has power over noble trees such as firs and pines and other trees that produce many leaves without fruit and keep them in winter. And of regions, it is said to rule Ethiopia <note>original: "achuthu"</note> up to the ends of the habitable parts; and it rules Mauritania and all its borders. And it is said to rule those regions because its significations appear more in those regions than in others.

### Concerning Virgo.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a young woman (the Virgin) holding a sheaf or stalk, representing the zodiac sign Virgo.</image-desc>

Virgo rules the belly and the navel of the human body, the parts adjacent to the navel, and the intestines. Hence the saying: "The boundary of the Virgin holds the navel: because that sign cherishes those [parts]." <note>original: "vmbilicū hēt p̄finia virginis tē: ppterea signū q̄̄ vīginti illa fouet."</note> And it signifies the generosity and good will of the person for whom it was the ascendant at the hour of birth. And it signifies all seeds that are sown. And of regions, it rules Algeria <note>original: "algerantca"</note>, Asten, the regions near the Euphrates, Great Spain <note>original: "hispaniā magnā"</note>, and Serica <note>original: "ſeriz"</note>. And it is said to rule those regions because its significations appear more in those regions than in others, except for the signification it has over seeds, which extends across the whole earth.

### Concerning Libra.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a pair of balance scales, representing the zodiac sign Libra.</image-desc>

Libra rules the loins and hips of the human body, the lower part of the belly down to the upper parts of the thighs; it rules the lower part of the flanks and also the buttocks. And it is said to rule the hips because a person begins to be "balanced" <term>librari</term> <note>From the Latin "libra," meaning scales or balance.</note> there, since the hips are made in a certain way like a pair of scales. Hence the saying: "Here the balanced man begins to be bifurcated. And the omen of the Scales takes its name from there." <note>original: "Huiſc librar⁹ hō sic icipit eē bifrucus. Librazq3 auſpiciū noiē inde trahit."</note> And Libra rules all the trees that Leo rules, and in addition those that grow quickly and fruit quickly, such as peaches, almonds, and the like. And it also signifies generosity and goodness of soul, just like Virgo. And...

And it rules over meat, crops, and the regions of Chebil, Cubrasten, Hauguerath, Bacharch, and Haugth. And it is said to rule those regions because its influences appear more clearly in those regions than in others.

### ¶ Concerning Scorpio.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a scorpion facing right.</image-desc>

Scorpio has significance in the human body over the private parts, the whole thigh, and the bladder. Hence it was said: "Scorpio, with its raised tail stinging itself, rules the individual members of the groin and of Venus." <note>original: "Scorpius a cauda semet stimulante leuata pectinis ꝛ veneris singula membra regit."</note> And it signifies generosity and goodness of mind, just like Virgo and Libra. And it signifies the same trees that Cancer signifies, namely poplars and those that are of great height which lose their leaves in autumn. And of regions, it holds Helohiget and the land of the Arabs and their borders as far as Argemon. And it has a share in Aceuith. And it is said to rule those regions because its influences appear more clearly in those regions than in others.

### ¶ Concerning Sagittarius.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Sagittarius, depicted as a centaur archer drawing a bow.</image-desc>

Sagittarius holds the hips of the human body. Hence it was said: "Venus and the arrow stretch together from the bow: the powerful horse provides for the flowing thighs." <note>original: "Tendit ex arcu pariter venus atqȝ sagitta: femozib’ que potēs fluxa ministrat equ’." This verse links the Archer's bow to the anatomical structure of the hips.</note> And it signifies an ingenious and clever person, one who knows how to do many things and bring the matters he undertakes to the end he desires; and one who knows how to seduce people and lead them to what he wants, whether he wishes to do good or evil. People trust him, yet he sometimes deceives them, though not always, under the appearance of doing well; and he is a seducer, though he is not believed to be one; rather, he is believed to be loyal, yet he is neither entirely faithful nor entirely unfaithful. And of regions, it holds Ethiopia, Mahazobean, and India. And it is said to rule those regions because its influences appear more clearly in those regions than in others.

### ¶ Concerning Capricorn.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Capricorn, depicted as a goat with a fish tail (sea-goat).</image-desc>

Capricorn holds the knees of the human body. Hence it was said: "The little goat grazing on the bank leans upon its knees." And it signifies a person who knows how to lead a good but hot-tempered life, and who will know how to provide well for his own business and even for others'; and he will know how to give good counsel to those seeking advice from him; and he is clever in a good or bad way if he wishes; and likewise a person who is greatly and easily saddened. And of regions and lands, it signifies the western part of Ethiopia as far as Rimmon, where two seas join, and as far as Jacinthus and Lower India. And it is said to rule those regions because its influences appear more clearly in those regions than in others.

### ¶ Concerning Aquarius.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Aquarius, a man seated and pouring water from two jugs.</image-desc>

Aquarius holds the shins of the human body, from the knees down to the ankles of the feet, so that it holds the whole 

<column-break/>

ankles. Hence it was said: "Legs that lead a long form of strength." <note>original: "Crura que valoꝝ longā oucētia formā."</note> Or because it signifies the coldness of the waters above. And of regions, it signifies Azenguch and part of the land of the Black Ceclere and Al-Kufa and its territories, and all of Efigem; and the western part of Egypt and the western part of Acuich. And it is said to rule those regions because its influences appear more clearly in those regions than in others.

### ¶ Concerning Pisces.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Pisces, depicted as two fish swimming in opposite directions linked by a cord.</image-desc>

"Joined together as if with thorny bones: fortune makes feet for the fish." <note>original: "Compactos simł quasi spinis ossibus ipsos: fortuna facit piscib’ esse pedes."</note> And it signifies a hot-tempered, mixed person who does not remain long in his purpose. And sometimes it signifies a very choleric <term>choleric</term><note>In medieval medicine, a choleric person was thought to be dominated by yellow bile, making them prone to anger and quick action.</note> person; and sometimes it signifies a person of mixed colors. And of regions, it holds Thabracen and the northern part of Jurgan. And it has significance over the land of the Romans and their borders. And over Italy it likewise has significance, and especially over Romagna and both Marches <note>Refers to the March of Ancona and the March of Treviso.</note> as far as Venice. ### ¶ Chapter twenty-two: which part of the body each planet signifies in each sign.

It was said above concerning the 12 signs and which part of the body each of them signifies; now, however, it must be said which part of the body each <term>planeta</term><note>In traditional astrology, the "planets" include the Sun and Moon as well as Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury.</note> signifies in each sign. And we must begin with Saturn, the first planet, and with Aries, the first sign. Therefore, if a question is put to you concerning some infirmity, or concerning some pain which someone suffers, look then in which sign the <term>significator</term><note>The specific planet that represents the person asking the question or the person who is ill.</note> of the seeker (that is, the sick person) is, and who that planet is. If it is Saturn and it is in Aries, it signifies the sickness or pain is in the chest; for when Saturn is in Aries, it signifies the chest of the human body; Jupiter signifies the belly; Mars the head; the Sun the thighs; Venus the feet; Mercury the shins; the Moon the knees. And understand this in the same way for all the signs.

In **Taurus**: Saturn signifies the belly; Jupiter the back; Mars the neck; the Sun the knees; Venus the head; Mercury the feet; the Moon the shins.

In **Gemini**: Saturn the belly; Jupiter the private parts and what follows them; Mars the chest; the Sun the shins and ankles; Venus the neck; Mercury the head; the Moon the thighs.

In **Cancer**: Saturn the genitals and their surroundings; Jupiter the thighs; Mars the chest; the Sun the feet; Venus the shoulders, arms, and hands; Mercury the eyes; the Moon the head.

In **Leo**: Saturn the private parts and their surroundings; Jupiter the thighs and knees; Mars the belly; the Sun the head; Venus the same; Mercury the shoulders and throat; the Moon the neck.

In **Virgo**: Saturn the feet; Jupiter the knees; Mars the belly; the Sun the neck; Venus the navel and adjacent parts; Mercury the same; the Moon the shoulders.

In **Libra**: Saturn the knees and their surroundings; Jupiter the eyes and their sockets; Mars the private parts and their surroundings; the Sun the shoulders; Venus the head; Mercury the private parts; the Moon the same.

In **Scorpio**: Saturn the ankles and their surroundings; Jupiter the feet; Mars the head, arms, and thighs; the Sun the heart; Venus the private parts and their surroundings; Mercury the back; the Moon the belly.

In **Sagittarius**: Saturn the feet; Jupiter the shins and head; Mars the feet and hands; the Sun the belly; Venus the thighs and arms; Mercury the private parts and their surroundings; the Moon the back.

### Chapter Twenty-Four concerning lucid, tenebrous, fumous, and vacant degrees.

The first three degrees of Taurus are tenebrous; 4 lucid; 4 vacant; 3 lucid; 5 vacant; 8 lucid; 3 tenebrous. ## Chapter 28 concerning degrees that are coordinate and consonant in power.

Al-Qabisi <note>original: "alkabicius"; a famous 10th-century Arab astrologer.</note> said that two degrees which are of equal distance from the "head" of the moveable signs <note>The "moveable" or cardinal signs are Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which mark the start of the seasons.</note> are **coordinate**, meaning they are of equal strength. They are said to be sharers and equally strong in virtue. For example, the 20th degree of Capricorn—counting so that the 20th degree is the limit—and the 10th degree of Sagittarius—counting so that the 10th is included—are coordinate. This is also true for the 20th degree of Cancer and the 10th degree of Gemini. For indeed, the 10th degree of Sagittarius is as far from the beginning of Capricorn as the 20th degree of Capricorn is [from its own beginning]. Likewise, the 20th degree of Cancer is as far from its beginning as the 10th degree of Cancer is from that same beginning. Between the included 10th degree of Sagittarius and its end are 20 degrees; and between the beginning of the same Capricorn and the included 20th degree are 20 degrees. Similarly, it is said that a degree of Gemini is as far from the beginning of Cancer (or from the end of the sign of Gemini itself, which touches the start of Cancer) as the 20th degree of the same Cancer is from the start of Cancer itself. And the 20th degree of Aries is as far from the beginning of Aries itself as the 10th degree of Pisces is from the end of Pisces itself, which touches the start of Aries. And the 20th degree of Libra is as far—

## Chapter twenty-six concerning the azemene degrees.

Ptolemy and Al-Qabisi and others said that there are certain degrees in certain signs which are called **azemene** <note>original: "azemena"; from Arabic *al-zamāna*, meaning "chronically ill" or "infirm."</note>, which here means "debilitated." The cause of the *azemena* is a certain sickness inseparable from the body, which very often happens in the mother's womb, so that as long as the person born shall live, they will always have it with them. # Here begins the third part of the second treatise: regarding the accidental existence of the circle.
## Chapter one: on the division of the circle by houses.

A division occurs in the circle of the signs <note>The Zodiac</note> whereby it is divided into four equal parts by two "great circles" that cross it. One of these is the **horizon**, or the circle of the hemisphere. The other is called the **meridian circle**, or the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medium celi"; the highest point the sun reaches in the sky during the day</note>. Each of these quarters is further divided into three equal parts: thus the entire circle is divided into 12 unequal parts. This occurs because of the "reflection of horizons" in different climates <note>A "climate" in medieval geography refers to a latitudinal zone; the size of the houses changes based on how far north or south the observer is</note> and because of the diversity of regions, as **Thabit** <note>Thabit ibn Qurra (826–901 AD), a foundational astronomer and mathematician</note> well demonstrates in his *Introduction to the Celestial Sphere* in the treatise on how the circles in the sphere are to be imagined; you will also find this in the book of the *Canon on the Equations of the Stars*.

This division always begins from the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>. Each of these divisions is called a **house**, a **cusp**, or a **tower**, and not simply a "sign." The first of these houses is that ascending sign, for example, the one in Aries. **Ptolemy** said that the 5 degrees that have passed a line dividing one house from another are counted as belonging to the house given to that line. For example, if the 5th degree of a sign is ascending, those five degrees that have already passed the line of the Ascendant are counted as part of the **first house**; the remaining 25 degrees are considered to be "under the line." Understand that this should be done for the other houses as well. Always, the five degrees that have passed the line of any house are counted in that house, while the 25 that have not yet reached it are not <note>This "5-degree rule" is still debated in modern astrology; it suggests a planet near the end of one house already influences the next</note>. Following this, there is the second house, then the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and finally the twelfth, which is the last of all the houses.

## Chapter two: on the division of the quarters of the circle.

**Al-Qabisi** <note>Alcabitius</note> and **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel</note> held that the quarter of the circle between the Ascendant and the Midheaven—which contains the twelfth, eleventh, and tenth houses—is called the **Oriental Quarter**. It is masculine,

<column-break/>

advancing, sanguine, vernal <note>associated with Spring</note>, and signifies **childhood**: specifically, it governs the life of the newborn from birth until the end of adolescence, which is from the day of birth until the 21st year is completed.

The quarter that is from the Midheaven to the western line—which contains the ninth, eighth, and seventh houses—is called the **Southern Quarter**. It is receding, aestival <note>associated with Summer</note>, choleric, and youthful. It represents the "perfection of youth." This quarter is to the other quarters as youth is to the other ages, lasting from the beginning of the 22nd year to the end of the 41st.

The third quarter—from the seventh house to the fourth, containing the seventh, sixth, and fourth <insert>houses</insert> which are below the earth—is called the **Western Quarter**. It is masculine, advancing, autumnal, melancholic, and elderly. This quarter is to the others as old age is to the other ages of the native, lasting from the 41st year until the 60th. Some have said this stage lasts from old age until the end of life, which does not seem appropriate to me; however, they considered that many men fail around the 60th year or only slightly exceed it.

The final quarter—from the fourth house to the Ascendant, containing the third, second, and first houses—is the **Northern Quarter**. It is feminine, receding, phlegmatic, hibernal <note>associated with Winter</note>, signifies decline, and is called **decrepitude**. It represents the end of life, from the end of old age (the 60th year) until the 90th. This covers the end of life, though some may live beyond 90—which happens to few, though some claim to be 100 or more when they are perhaps only 90 or a bit more. This is because the life of all men pertains to the **three kingdoms of Saturn**, which are 90 degrees <note>In traditional astrology, Saturn is the slowest visible planet and governs time and death; a quarter of the circle is 90 degrees</note>. Furthermore, this is the quarter that symbolizes what happens to a person **after their death**: what happens to their goods and inheritance, and what is said of them—whether they are praised or cursed, whether their corpse is buried or burned, whether they are buried honorably or shamefully, and whether their blood relatives and friends weep and grieve for them or laugh and rejoice at their death.

## Chapter three: which half is called 
## ascending or descending, and which part is called right or left.

Know that of the aforementioned quarters, the one from the Midheaven line to the Ascendant, and from there to the line of the fourth house, is called the **ascending half**. The remaining two quarters—from the line of the fourth house to the seventh, and from there back to the Midheaven—are called the **descending half**.

The part of the sky that is **above the earth** is called the **Right side of heaven**: it is the more noble and stronger part. The part **below the earth** is called the **Left side of heaven**, being weaker and less noble. This is because the circle of the horizon of any region divides the sky into two halves.

The part of the sky from the Ascendant to the seventh house <insert>above the earth</insert> is called the **quarter of the Ascendant**, while the part from the Ascendant to the seventh house above the earth is also called the **Left of the Ascendant**. The part from the Ascendant passing through the North to the seventh house—where the horizon divides the part of the sky above the earth from that below—is called the **Eastern Quarter**. The part from the Ascendant passing through the South to the seventh house is called the **Left of the East**. In this way, the "Right of Heaven," the "Right of the Ascendant," and the "Right of the East" all differ.

## Chapter four: on the angles, 
## cadent, and succedent houses.

From all the aforementioned halves and quarters, twelve houses are formed...

...out of which four are called **angles**: namely, the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth. These four houses are the strongest and most stable parts of the sky. They also differ in strength among themselves: for the **first** is the strongest <note>The Ascendant</note>, except in matters of dignity regarding worldly glory—such as kingdoms, duchies, powers, and the like—because in those matters, the **tenth** <note>The Midheaven</note> is preferred above all others. Furthermore, the tenth is stronger than the seventh, and the seventh is stronger than the fourth.

The **second**, **fifth**, **eighth**, and **eleventh** houses are called the **succedents** of the angles because they follow immediately after the angles. They are half as strong as the angles, except for the eleventh, which is very strong in matters regarding fortune and things for which one has hope; for it is the house of fortune, trust, and hope, as is said in the treatise on the houses.

The **third**, **sixth**, **ninth**, and **twelfth** houses are called **cadent** from the angles. These are very weak houses and do not promise good, nor stability, nor durability, nor the prolongation of any matter—except for the **ninth house**, which is preferred in matters of religion and is more suitable for them than all other houses, as well as for things regarding clerical dignities such as bishoprics, abbacies, priories, and the like.

Therefore, when a planet is the "significator" <note>The planet representing a specific person or topic</note> of any matter and is in an angle, it promises good and is said to "prosper." But if it is in a succedent house, it prospers less than in an angle. In a cadent house, a planet is said to "fail" and be weak and useless—except for what I told you regarding the ninth and eleventh houses. Each of the aforementioned houses has its own specific meaning in the affairs of human existence, as I am about to tell you in the following sections.

## Chapter five: regarding the meanings of the twelve houses.

<margin>
Regarding the meanings of the houses.
</margin>

### Regarding the first house.

<margin>
1st house.
</margin>

<margin>
Meaning: the life of the Querent <note>The person asking the question</note>.
</margin>

The first house, the beginning of which is in the East, is called the **Ascendant**. As **Adila**, **Zael**, **Alchabitius**, and all other wise men have said, this house signifies the life and the body of anyone born (the "native") or even the person asking a question (the "querent"). It signifies the beginning of any work and has meaning over every "election" <note>Choosing the best time to start an action</note> and every beginning. It signifies the start of life for any birth; for this reason, the first house is called the principle of all houses. 

There is a certain similarity between the first house and those being born or asking questions: for just as this house "ascends" from that part of the sky hidden from our sight below the horizon toward the upper part which we see above the earth—coming from the hidden into the light and from hidden places to manifest ones—so too does the one who is born emerge from the darkness and narrowness of the mother’s womb and arrive at the light of this world and the breadth of the air. Likewise, the one who asks a question reveals their intention and the secrets of their heart, and those things which were first hidden later shine and are made clear.

**Adila** and **Andarzaghar** <note>original: "alezdegoz"</note> said regarding births that the **first lord of the triplicity** <note>In astrology, each house is ruled by three planets known as 'lords of triplicity' who govern different periods of time</note> of the first house signifies the life and nature of the native or querent, their pleasures, what they delight in, what they love or hate, and what happens to them—whether good or evil—at the beginning of their life, namely in the first third part of it. The **second lord of the triplicity** signifies life, vigor, virtue, and strength, and what happens to them in the second third of their life's course. The **third lord of the triplicity** signifies what the first and second signify, but specifically the end of life and whatever happens in the final third of their life. 

Therefore, if a birth chart is shown to you, or a general question is made to you about someone's fortune or their state of being in general:

<margin>
The 1st Lord of the Triplicity signifies the life and nature of the native and what happens in the 1st 3rd part of life.
</margin>

<margin>
The 2nd Lord of the Triplicity signifies the life and vigor of those born and what happens in the 2nd 3rd of life's course.
</margin>

<margin>
The 3rd Lord of the Triplicity signifies the end of life after the final part of life.
</margin>

<column-break/>

look then at the lords of the triplicity of the first house: namely, the first, second, and third. See what the condition of each of them is, and judge according to what you see of their state. If the first lord signifies good, judge that good will happen to the native or querent in the first third of their life. If the second lord of the same triplicity signifies good, good will happen in the [middle] part of life. If the third lord signifies good, it will happen in the final third part of their life. Say the same regarding evil: whichever of the said significators signifies evil, it will happen in that third part of life which that lord signifies, as was said regarding the nurturing.

**Regarding other meanings of the first house:** The first house also signifies the substance or wealth of **hidden enemies**, because it is the second house from the twelfth <note>In "derived houses," the house immediately following any house represents its money or assets</note>. For hidden enemies are all those who pretend to be friends, who laugh and act joyful in front of men and say they love them and openly announce good things to them, yet they envy them, grieve at their prosperity, rejoice at their adversity, and strive to harm them secretly in every way they can. 

This house also signifies the **siblings of friends**, as it is the third from the eleventh; and the **parents of kings**, as it is the fourth from the tenth; and the **children of religious people**, as it is the fifth from the ninth; and the **infirmities of household companions**, public enemies, and wives who do not live with their husbands, as it is the sixth from the eighth; and **their wives**, as it is the seventh from the seventh; and the **death of servants**, as it is the eighth from the sixth; and the **religion of children** and their long journeys, as it is the ninth from the fifth; and the **magistracies or dignities of fathers**, as it is the tenth from the fourth; and the **friends of siblings**, as it is the eleventh from the third; and their fortune; and the **hidden enemies of household members** and their larger animals, as it is the twelfth from the second.

<margin>
The 1st House signifies the substance of enemies.
</margin>

### Regarding the second house.

<margin>
2nd house.
</margin>

The second house, as **Alchabitius** said, signifies substance, acquisition, and ministers; it also signifies the end of youth. **Adila** said that it signifies the gathering of substance, whether possessions, money, or gold coins <note>original: "biçantiorum" - bezants</note>, as well as takings and gift-givings. **Zael** said that the second house signifies substance, it does not "aspect" <note>An astrological term meaning the house cannot 'see' the Ascendant by a traditional geometric angle</note> the Ascendant, and it signifies helpers and letters.

**Andarzaghar** said regarding the lords of the triplicity of the second house—the first, second, and third—to see which of them is stronger in its state and position. You shall rightly make this one the "author" of substance and the significator of the acquisitions of the native or querent. If this lord is in the Midheaven <note>The 10th house</note>, the person will find wealth through a king. If it is in the house of one of the Luminaries <note>The Sun or Moon</note>, they will find it by reason of religion; understand the other houses in a similar way.

Likewise, the first lord of the triplicity of the second house gives substance at the beginning of life (the first third); the second gives it in the middle of life (the second third); the third gives it in the final third of the native's life. However, what **Andarzaghar** said regarding these significators should be understood as follows: in whatever age the significator shows wealth, if it is in the first house, the native will find wealth or money through their own body—namely, from the labor of their hands and their own industry and diligence. If it is in the second house, they will find it by means of their existing substance, such as from the fruits of their possessions and goods, or from trade and other mechanical or smithing arts which are practiced with capital—such as shoemaking, skinning, and the like—or by reason of any of those things signified by the second house. ### On the third house.

**Alchabitius** <note>original: Alkabiaeus, a famous 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> said: the third house signifies brothers and sisters, relatives, friendships, and the de-

<column-break/>

-votion of faith, religion, commands, messengers, changes, and minor journeys; and it signifies the state of life before death. <margin>Male and female relatives</margin> And **Adila** <note>Likely referring to a traditional astrological authority</note> said it signifies male and female relatives, their state, moving from house to house, patience, and the like. If someone is born and you want to know what fortune he will have from brothers or any of those mentioned above, see how the lord of the first house stands with the lord of the third, and how they aspect <note>Geometric relationship between planets</note> each other. If they look at each other with an aspect of love <note>Trine or sextile</note> and receive each other, there will be love and good between them; but if they look at each other with an aspect of enmity <note>Square or opposition</note>, he will not rejoice because of them or with them, nor will there be good for them from him. 

Furthermore, you must look at the lords of the triplicity of the third house. If the first of them looks at the lord of the Ascendant <note>the rising sign</note> with a good aspect (such as a trine or a "fertile" aspect) or receives him well, there will be good for him from those brothers signified by that planet; and understand the same for the other two. But with whichever of them the lord of the first looks at with an evil aspect, there will be evil from those brothers signified by that planet. And if the lord of the first does not aspect any of them, he will be with all brothers and they with him as if they were strangers. Understand the same thing about the Moon that I told you about the lord of the first. Also, whichever of those significators is in a better state, things will be better for those brothers signified by that planet, both in their fortune and other matters; and whichever is in a worse state, the condition of those brothers signified by it will be worse. <margin>It is the Ascendant for brothers, relatives, neighbors, etc.</margin>

Therefore, you should not judge by the lord of the Ascendant, but by the lord of the third; and according to what you see of the state of the lord of the third, so you shall judge the affairs of the questioner’s brother. It relies heavily on the authority of medieval and ancient astrologers like Al-Qabisi (Alchabitius) and Vettius Valens.</meta>

it will be well for the person born <note>Latin: "nato"</note> or the person asking the question <note>Latin: "querenti"; the querent in a horary chart</note> regarding brothers, neighbors, and younger relatives, and other things signified by the third house, during the first third of his life, and likewise for them regarding him. And if it is well with the second <term>lord of the triplicity<gloss>In medieval astrology, each zodiac sign belongs to an element (fire, earth, air, or water), and each element is governed by three specific planets called "lords of the triplicity" which represent different stages of life or aspects of a topic.</gloss></term>, it will be well for him through them, and for them through him, in the second third of his life. If it is well with the third lord, it will be well in the final third of his life. And conversely, if they are poorly positioned, there will be trouble between them.

This third house has other meanings as well, as it signifies the substance <note>wealth or material assets</note> of household members, because it is the second house from the second; and the fathers of secret enemies and their homes, etc., because it is the fourth from the twelfth; and it signifies the children of friends, because it is the fifth from the eleventh; and the illnesses of kings, because it is the sixth from the tenth; and the enemies of religious people and their associates and lovers, because it is the seventh from the ninth; and the death of those who are absent and the household members of their enemies and their helpers, because it is the eighth from the eighth; and the religion of wives, because it is the ninth from the seventh; and the professions <note>Latin: "magisteria"</note> of servants, because it is the tenth from the sixth; and the friends of children and their fortune, because it is the eleventh from the fifth; and the secret enemies of fathers and their larger animals, because it is the twelfth from the fourth house. <note>This technique of "turning the chart" allows an astrologer to find information about any person in the native's life by counting houses away from the house representing that person.</note>

<term>Alchabitius<gloss>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose "Introduction to the Art of Judgments of the Stars" was a standard textbook in Europe.</gloss></term> says the fourth house signifies fathers, homes, lands, grandfathers, and all ancestors in a direct line of ascent, specifically male elders and sisters, and all inheritances except those inherited from the dead (which are discussed in the eighth house). It also signifies all immovable goods that are in or upon the earth, such as buildings, towers, cities, castles, and the like. It signifies hidden treasures and whatever is buried or underground. <term>Adila<gloss>Likely a reference to a specific Arabic source or a corruption of a name like Al-Adil.</gloss></term> says it signifies secrets and hidden things, prisons and the imprisoned, things concealed or placed in the earth, and whatever happens to a dead man in his burial and after burial: whether he is buried or crushed, or if his corpse is left behind so that it is not cared for, as sometimes happens to those who are hanged, decapitated, or otherwise killed. <term>Mansor<gloss>Al-Mansur, often associated with a collection of astrological aphorisms.</gloss></term> says it signifies the "end of things." <term>Alezdegos<gloss>A corruption of the name Al-Andarzaghar, a famous Sassanid-era Persian astrologer.</gloss></term> says of the lords of the triplicity of the house of fathers: the first signifies fathers, the second signifies cities and lands, and the third signifies the end of things and prisons. 

Therefore, one must consider these things in the birth of anyone or in any question put to you regarding these matters, because you must look to the fourth house if you wish to know what will happen to the native or querent regarding those things signified by the fourth house or its triplicity lords; see which of them is in a better state, and judge the outcome based on it. For if the first lord of the triplicity of the fourth house is in a good state and aspects the lord of the Ascendant <note>the planet ruling the 1st house</note> with a good aspect—namely <term>trine<gloss>An aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, considered very harmonious.</gloss></term> or <term>sextile<gloss>An aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart, considered harmonious.</gloss></term>—it will be well for the native or the interrogator regarding his father, and for the father regarding him, as well as the grandfather, great-grandfather, and father-in-law, and all elder relatives, although the father-in-law is signified by the fourth house only indirectly. And if the second lord is in a good state, it will be well for him regarding houses, lands, and inheritances which he shall inherit from the aforementioned persons. And if the third lord is in a good state, it will be well for him regarding prisons and the imprisoned, as sometimes happens to the guards of captives and similar people; and regarding the end of things, as sometimes happens to someone settling a lawsuit or a war, or mediating a deal, as often happens with horse-sellers or other things where sales require a mediator. But if they are unfortunate or in a bad state,

the aforementioned significators will bring ill fortune from those same things. And consider in which part of life this happens to him: for the first lord of this triplicity signifies what happens to the native in the first third part of his life, the second lord in the second part, and the third in the third, as was said regarding the other houses. 

The fourth house also signifies the substance of brothers, because it is the second from the third; and the brothers of household members and helpers, because it is the third from the second; and the children of secret enemies, because it is the fifth from the twelfth; and the illnesses of friends and of the king's household, because it is the sixth from the eleventh; and the enemies of kings, because it is the seventh from the tenth; and the death of religious people, because it is the eighth from the ninth; and the religion of those who are absent, because it is the ninth from the eighth; and the professions of enemies and associates and their mothers, because it is the tenth from the seventh; and the friends of servants and their fortune, because it is the eleventh from the sixth; and it also signifies the secret enemies of children and their larger animals, because it is the twelfth from the fifth.

### Of the Fifth House.

<margin>
Of the
5th house
</margin>

Alchabitius says the fifth house signifies children, delights, legates <note>ambassadors or messengers</note>, gifts, and what is said of a man after his death. Adila says it signifies joy and clothing. <term>Vuellius<gloss>Vettius Valens, a 2nd-century Greek astrologer whose works were influential in the medieval period.</gloss></term> says it signifies documents, books, messengers, and news. <term>Alchaiat<gloss>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a student of the famous astrologer Mashallah; he wrote a well-known book on nativities.</gloss></term> says it signifies everything in which one has trust, honor, petitions, women, friendship, the state of citizens, and the fruits of inheritance. Alezdegos says of the lords of the triplicity of the fifth: the first signifies children and their life, the second signifies delights, and the third signifies legates. 

Therefore, one must look at the lord of the birth or the question and see how it relates to the first lord of the triplicity of the fifth house, which is called the house of children; for if it relates well to him, it will be well for him regarding children and for them regarding him in the first third of his life; if with the second lord, in the second part; if with the third, in the third. However, the life of the children is taken more from the first lord of that triplicity than from the second or third. 

Now look at how the lord of the fifth house relates to the lord of the first house: for if the lord of the fifth is joined to the lord of the first with a praiseworthy aspect—namely trine or sextile—or if the lord of the fifth is in the first house, or the lord of the first is in the fifth, he will have children. This is especially true if **Jupiter** <note>the "Great Benefic" planet associated with growth and children</note> is then in the fifth, or is joined to the lord of the fifth or the lord of the first with a good aspect, or is in the third, eighth, or eleventh house with the lord of the first or the lord of the fifth or with the Moon; then they shall live and it will be well for them. If, however, **Mars** <note>the "Lesser Malefic" planet associated with conflict and heat</note> is in the place of Jupiter, the native will have children, as we shall see in the chapter on children, but also their death, as will be said more extensively in the judgments on births. Likewise, one must look at all the lords of the triplicity of the house of children and see which of them best aspects the lord of the first, or the lord of the fifth, or the fifth house itself: for if the first lord aspects best, he will have children in the first third of his life; if the second, in the second part. And if any of them is the lord of the first or the lord of the fifth, as sometimes happens, it signifies children born in that lord's respective third of the native's life. This house also has other significations, as it signifies the goods of fathers and other elder relatives, because it is the second house from the fourth. Therefore, if its lord is joined to the lord of the first or the lord of the second and is received by either of them, the native or the querent will obtain their goods.

# Of the sixth house.

<margin>Of the 6th house</margin>
They have said that the sixth house is the house of illnesses, male servants, and maidservants. The whole of this house concerns infirmity because it lies outside the house of play and delight (the fifth) and moves toward the seventh, which is the house of public enemies. <term>Alchabicius<gloss>The Latin name for Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose "Introduction to the Art of Judgments of the Stars" was a standard university textbook in Europe.</gloss></term> said it signifies whatever shall happen before old age and signifies the end of life. <term>Adila<gloss>Possibly a reference to a specific medieval authority, though the name is less common than others in this text.</gloss></term> said it signifies attendants and beasts that are not ridden <note>Usually small livestock like sheep or goats, as opposed to horses which belong to the 12th house.</note>. The sixth house also signifies vassals, justice, and moving from place to place. <term>Zahel<gloss>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician whose works were foundational to Western horary astrology.</gloss></term> said the sixth house is "cadent" from the ascendant <note>A "cadent" house is one that does not "see" the first house, making it traditionally considered weak or unfortunate.</note> and does not look upon it, and is a malicious place. <term>Alezdegoz<gloss>The Latinized name for Al-Andarzaghar, a 7th-century Persian astrologer.</gloss></term> said the first <term>lord of the triplicity<gloss>Astrological signs are grouped into fours (elements). Each element is ruled by three planets called "lords," which are used to divide a person's life into three stages.</gloss></term> of the sixth house signifies illnesses and recovery from them or from evils. The second signifies home-born servants and slaves. The third signifies what may be gained from them, their utility and labor; it is also the significator of beasts, flocks, and all four-footed animals, their strength, their numbers, and whether they remain in one's hand or are lost, as well as imprisonment and restraint. 

Therefore, one must see how the lord of the nativity or the lord of the question stands with the lord of the sixth house: specifically, if they are joined by a "trine" or "sextile" aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note>, or by conjunction <note>Latin: "per corpus," meaning in the same physical degree.</note> with mutual reception. If this is the case, the native or querent will have good fortune in all things signified by that house. If they aspect each other in those ways but without "reception," he will not have great fortune from them, though he may have some. If they aspect each other by a "square" or "opposition" <note>Challenging angles of 90 and 180 degrees.</note> without reception, it will go poorly for him in all the aforementioned things. If it is with reception, it will be less bad. If the lord of the first house "receives" the lord of the sixth, but the lord of the sixth does not receive him, it will be better for the servants and slaves than for him, for they will be unfaithful and fraudulent toward him. If the lord of the sixth receives the lord of the first, but the lord of the first does not receive the lord of the sixth, it will be better for him than for them; he will not love them or do well by them, even if they do well by him, remain faithful, and manage his business well. And look to the lords of that triplicity: if the first is in a good state, these good things will happen in the first third of his life; if the second, in the middle; if the third, in the last third. The same applies to bad states. Servants differ in condition from "vernaculi" <note>Home-born slaves or household dependents.</note> because servants are subject to him by law of servitude, while the vernaculi are part of the family without that same bond. When Alezdegoz said this house signifies four-footed animals, his intention was only those that are not ridden, such as sheep, goats, pigs, dogs, and the like. This also includes chickens, geese, ducks, ostriches, bees, and similar creatures; he did not mean oxen or horses and 

<column-break/>

the like. ¶ Furthermore, this house has certain other meanings: it signifies the substance <note>The wealth or money</note> of children, because it is the second house from the fifth; the brothers of fathers, because it is the third from the fourth; the fathers of brothers from another father, because it is the fourth from the third; the children of household members, because it is the fifth from the second; the enemies of hidden enemies, because it is the seventh from the twelfth; the death of friends, because it is the eighth from the eleventh; the religion of mothers and the long journeys of kings, because it is the ninth from the tenth; and the masteries and secular dignities of religious people, because it is the tenth from the ninth. For it happens sometimes that bishops and other religious figures receive secular powers and similar dignities. It also signifies the friends of those absent, the household members of enemies and associates, because it is the eleventh from the eighth; and the hidden enemies of wives, associates, and enemies, because it is the twelfth from the seventh.

# Of the seventh house.

<margin>Of the 7th house</margin>
According to the *Giris argaphalon* <note>Likely a corrupted reference to a specific Arabic or Greek astrological source.</note>, the seventh house is the house of women and signifies marriages and contentions. <term>Albategni<gloss>Al-Battani, a famous 9th-century astronomer and astrologer whose work influenced Copernicus.</gloss></term> said it signifies partnership, opposition, and every opposing thing. Adila said it signifies wives, war, and enemy matters. Alchabicius said it signifies the middle of the end of life toward old age. <term>Venz<gloss>Likely Vettius Valens, a 2nd-century Greek astrologer.</gloss></term> said it signifies thieves, litigants, and partners; it is the house of buying and selling, and signifies marriages, the business of marriage, fugitives, thieves hiding by the roads, and lost things. Zahel said it signifies battles, because it is the "western angle" and the seventh house is directly opposite the ascendant. It signifies the contrarieties that arise between people, the querent and the thing sought. According to some, it signifies journeys of moderate length, just as the first house signifies very short journeys from one district to another in the same land, or from the city to the gardens or nearby enclosures. It also signifies the pure and simple worship of the deity, all houses of philosophers, the presence of things, the science of the stars, the diviner, letters, messengers, dreams, faith, divine wisdom, health, religion, rumors, and every past and preceding matter. It signifies a man deposed from his burden or work, the presence of future things, matters of the world to come, thieves and those like them, pilgrimages or wanderings, the loss of things, and the causes of those losses. This sign is the enemy of the ascendant. Alezdegoz said that the first lord of the triplicity of the seventh signifies women, the second signifies contentions, and the third signifies unions. It also has these other meanings: the substance of servants (the second from the sixth); the brothers of children from another father (the third from the fifth); the fathers of fathers while the fathers are living (the fourth from the fourth); the children of brothers (the fifth from the third); the illnesses of household members (the sixth from the second); and the death of hidden enemies (the eighth from the twelfth). It could also be said to signify the death of larger animals. It signifies the religion of friends and their long journeys (the ninth from the eleventh). It might also signify the masteries of kings, although this seems not entirely fitting, because it is the tenth from the tenth. It signifies the friends of religious people and their fortune (the eleventh from the ninth) and the hidden enemies of those absent, household members, and enemies (the twelfth from the eighth).

<margin>of the 8th House</margin>
### ¶ Of the eighth house.
Adila <note>Likely a reference to an early authority, possibly a corruption of a name like Al-Andarzaghar.</note> said the eighth house is the house of fear and is called the house of death. This is because it is the "helper" of public enemies <note>meaning it supports the 7th house of open enemies</note> and it follows the seventh, which is the opposition of the Ascendant <note>The Ascendant represents the life and body of the person; the opposite point represents their end.</note>. And Abu Ali <note>Abu Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century astrologer.</note> said that it signifies labor, sadness, wars, and those who are contemptuous, warlike, and the clients of adversaries. And Al-Qabisi said it signifies deposits, management, craftiness, and ingenuity. And Sahl said the eighth house follows the western angle <note>The 7th house is the western angle; the 8th is "succedent" to it.</note>; it signifies killing, lethal poisons, whatever is inherited from the dead, everything that perishes, labor, sadness, and the helpers of enemies or adversaries. And Al-Qabisi said it signifies *inheritance* <note>Original Latin: "almauerith," a transliteration of the Arabic word for inheritance.</note>, that is, everything inherited from the dead—meaning from both strangers and relatives—which heirs ought to possess after their death. It also signifies the end of the years of life after old age. And Al-Andarzaghar said that the first lord of the triplicity <note>A system where three planets "rule" a house based on its zodiac sign's element.</note> of the ninth house <note>The text likely means eighth here, or is referring to a specific derivative calculation.</note> signifies death; the second signifies ancient things; the third signifies inheritance and whatever its associates signify. And I agree with what the aforementioned wise men have said, and I say that the eighth house also signifies the dowries of women, or the wealth and property of enemies and associates. Someone said that it signifies usury. It also has other meanings: it signifies the brothers of servants, because it is the third house from the sixth; the illnesses of brothers, because it is the sixth from the third; and the enemies, wives, and associates of one's household, because it is the seventh from the second; and the religion and long journeys of hidden enemies, because it is the ninth from the twelfth. It also signifies the expertise and dignities of friends, as it is the tenth from the eleventh; the friends of kings, as it is the eleventh from the tenth; and the hidden enemies of religious people, as it is the twelfth from the ninth.

<margin>of the 9th house</margin>
### ¶ Of the ninth house.
And Tiberiades <note>Umar al-Tabari, an early Persian astrologer.</note> said the ninth house is the house of faith, religion, and long journeys. And Adila said it signifies vision, wisdom, the worship of the deity, and all houses of religion and the aforementioned things. And Al-Qabisi said it signifies wisdom, philosophy, writing, books, letters, messengers, the telling of the future, dreams, and it signifies the middle of life. And Sahl said the ninth house is "falling" <note>A "cadent" house, meaning it falls away from the strength of the main angles.</note> from the angle of the tenth house. And I say that it signifies a person's fame if its lord is well-disposed. For if the lord of the ninth house is in a good state and well-placed, and if the "fortunes" are in it—namely Jupiter or Venus—and they are free and not hindered, or if the Head of the Dragon <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered lucky.</note> is there, it signifies the fame of the native and his great honor. But if the "infortunes"—namely Saturn or Mars—or the Tail of the Dragon <note>The South Node of the Moon, considered unlucky.</note> are in it, it signifies his infamy; and the more that malefic planet is hindered, the more the native's infamy will be increased. Al-Andarzaghar said that the first lord of the triplicity of the ninth house signifies travel and what will happen to the native (or the person asking the question) on long journeys. The second signifies faith and religion, their health, and their manner. The third signifies wisdom, dreams, the science of the stars <note>astrology</note> and their truth, auguries, and practice in them. This 9th house also has these other meanings: namely, the substance of the households of enemies, associates, wives, and those who are absent and their helpers, because it is the second from the eighth; and the brothers of enemies, etc., because it is the third from the seventh; and the fathers of servants, because it is the fourth from the sixth; and the children of children, because it is the fifth from the fifth; and the illnesses of fathers, because it is the sixth from the fourth; and the wives, associates, and enemies of brothers, which is

<column-break/>

the seventh from the third; and the death of households, because it is the eighth from the second. It also signifies the dignities of hidden enemies, because it is the tenth from the twelfth; and the friends of friends, because it is the eleventh from the eleventh; and the hidden enemies of kings, because it is the twelfth from the tenth. And this is the reason why prelates and other religious figures are always secretly hostile to kings.

<margin>of the 10th House</margin>
### ¶ Of the tenth house.
Albumasar and other ancients have said the tenth house is the royal house and signifies empire, kingship, expertise, dignities, offices, and every art which someone practices, which is why they are called a "master." And a master whom God willed <note>Likely referring to a specific sage or a pious phrasing for an author.</note> said it signifies mothers, grandmothers, and all such elderly female ancestors and midwives. And Adila said it signifies divine things, honors, powers, and the household. And Al-Kindi said it signifies the king, glory, and the fame of praise. And Al-Battani said it signifies judges deciding a case and those who oversee works. And some of the ancients said it signifies the substance of stolen property. And Al-Qabisi said it signifies the half-point of the years of life. And Al-Andarzaghar said the first lord of the triplicity of the royal house signifies work, exaltation, the lifting up of one's seat, and the highest dwelling. The second signifies the voice of command and boldness in the same. The third signifies its stability and durability. Furthermore, this tenth house has these other meanings: it signifies the substance of religious people, because it is the second from the ninth; and the brothers of the households of enemies, because it is the third from the eighth; and the fathers of enemies, associates, and wives, because it is the fourth from the seventh; and the children of servants, because it is the fifth from the sixth; and the illness of children, because it is the sixth from the fifth; and the enemies, wives, and associates of paternal uncles, because it is the seventh from the fourth; and the death of brothers, because it is the eighth from the third. And the religion of households and those who are absent and their long journeys, because it is the ninth from the second; and the friends of hidden enemies, because it is the eleventh from the twelfth; and the hidden enemies of friends, because it is the twelfth from the eleventh.

<margin>of the 11th house</margin>
### ¶ Of the eleventh house.
The eleventh house is the house of fortune, trust, and hope. And Sahl said that it follows the angle of the Midheaven <note>The 10th house.</note>; it signifies the substance of the king and his revenues or taxes, his soldiers and infantry or helpers, and the man who succeeds the king (the first prince after him), and it signifies praises and children. And Al-Qabisi said it signifies ministers and signifies the end of the years of the middle of life, and from the middle onward. And Al-Andarzaghar said that the first lord of the triplicity of the house of trust signifies trust. The second signifies friends. The third signifies their utility or profit. ¶ And this eleventh house has these other meanings: it signifies the substance of the king, because it is the second from the tenth; and the brothers of religious people, because it is the third from the ninth; and the quarters of the households of enemies, because it is the fourth from the eighth. And the children of enemies and associates, because it is the fifth from the seventh; and the hindrances and illnesses of servants, because it is the sixth from the sixth. And the enemies and wives of children, because it is the seventh from the fifth; and the death of fathers, because it is the eighth from the fourth; and the religion of brothers and their long journeys, because it is the ninth from the third; and the expertise of households, because it is the tenth from the second; and the hidden enemies of hidden enemies, because it is the twelfth from the twelfth.

<meta>The previous page concluded the discussion of the eighth house, which governs death and inheritance. This page moves to the twelfth and final house of the zodiac, traditionally considered the "Evil Fortune" or the house of hidden trials. The text continues to synthesize the teachings of Sahl ibn Bishr (Zahel) and Al-Qabisi (Alchabicius), standard authorities in medieval European astrology.</meta>

<margin>Of the 12th house</margin>

### Of the twelfth house.

**I**t arises that the twelfth house signifies hidden enemies, deceivers, and the envious. It also signifies oxen, horses, donkeys, camels, and all animals that are ridden, and similar creatures. It signifies misery, sadness, mourning, weeping, lamentations, whisperings <note>likely referring to gossip or secret plots</note>, and the like; blasphemies, prisons, and ill-will. And Zahel <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer who wrote in Arabic</note> said that it signifies cunning and evil thoughts. And Alchabicius <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century authority</note> said it signifies labors and evil schemes; it signifies the end of life, and what happens to women regarding conception and childbirth, whether good or evil. And Alazdegos <note>Al-Andarzaghar, a Persian astrologer</note> said the first lord of the triplicity <note>a group of three signs of the same element</note> of the twelfth house signifies enemies; the second signifies labors; the third signifies beasts and cattle. Some others say that all the lords of the triplicity of the twelfth house and its own lord signify prisons and the imprisoned. Others said that the eighth house signifies the imprisoned. Still others said the fourth house signifies prisons. However, they do not contradict one another: for the fourth house signifies prisons because it signifies the capture and the actual act of catching. The eighth signifies prisons because it signifies the act of incarcerating. But the twelfth signifies prisons because it signifies the *place* of the prison, and the captive already imprisoned; in this they differ. Nevertheless, all the wise men agreed that the fourth house signifies prisons because it is the beginning of the prison and of incarceration; for if there were no capture or act of catching, there would be no incarceration nor act of incarcerating. And if there were no capture, no act of catching, no incarceration, and no act of incarcerating, there would be no place of imprisonment, nor a place where someone would stay imprisoned. And this is called the house of the act of incarceration for this reason: because it "falls" away from the eastern line <note>it is a "cadent" house, which was considered weak or unfortunate</note>, and because the <term>Joy of Saturn</term> <note>The planet Saturn is said to "rejoice" here because the house's themes of isolation and gloom match his nature.</note> is in it, for he rejoices in weeping, lamentation, and the like. <term>AND</term> this twelfth house has these other significations: it signifies the substance <note>wealth or property</note> of friends, because it is the second house from the eleventh; and the brothers of the king, because it is the third from the tenth; and the fathers of religious people, because it is the fourth from the ninth; and the children of the enemies of the family, etc., because it is the fifth from the eighth. And the illnesses of wives, etc., because it is the sixth from the seventh; and the wives and enemies of servants, because it is the seventh from the sixth; and the death of children, because it is the eighth from the fifth; and the religion and long journeys of fathers, because it is the ninth from the fourth; and the professions of brothers, because it is the tenth from the third; and the friends of the family, because it is the eleventh from the second; and the hidden enemies of the native <note>the person for whom the chart is cast</note> or the seeker, because it is the twelfth from the first. And I found a certain Florentine <note>Likely Guido Bonatti, a famous 13th-century Italian astrologer</note> who gave the twelfth house to the <term>pilgrim</term> <note>In astrology, "peregrine" refers to a planet with no essential dignity; here it may also refer to literal travelers.</note>. <term>ALL</term> these significations of any of the aforementioned houses must be considered and known, so that if a question is put to you about any of these things, or if the birth chart of someone is shown to you, or a general question, you can judge that question regarding all the accidents of the native or the seeker. Even though it is very difficult to find every person mentioned under one ascendant, it is easier for you to find whatever thing you ought to consider in your judgment: for if you have someone’s birth chart or a general question, you can judge what should happen to them regarding all the aforementioned significations, all the aforementioned persons, and what comes to all of them from that place and from him. For you can judge what should be of his own person, of his substance, and of those things

<column-break/>
