## Of the eleventh house and its lord.

<note>The eleventh house traditionally governs friends, hopes, and social gains.</note>

If the lord of the eleventh house is in the 12th house and the question is about profit, it signifies that he will indeed profit in his absence through his family or through those of equal standing. ¶ If it is in the first house and the question is about a short journey, it signifies that the journey will be useful and profitable. ¶ If however it is in the second house and the question is about hidden things, it signifies that they will come into the hands of the seeker <note>Latin: *querens*</note>. Say the same for immovable property. And if the question is about elder parents, it signifies their state according to the condition of that planet. ¶ If it is in the third house and the question is about children, it signifies their well-being; it also signifies joy and gladness from them, useful garments, and every good thing. And if it is in the fourth house and it is a birth <note>Latin: *nativitas*</note> or a universal question, it signifies that the person born or the seeker will be prone to anger, hardworking, and surrounded by infirmities. ¶ If it is another specific question, it signifies that the seeker will lose his smaller animals, servants, attendants, and household. ¶ If it is in the fifth house, it signifies that the person born will be litigious and that his lawsuits will turn out badly for him; a son will also come to the seeker. If however the planet is Venus, it signifies he will contract a marriage with a beautiful woman. If it is Jupiter, it signifies he will have good partners and fortune in trade. If it is any of the others, the predicted things will happen according to its disposition. For if it is well-disposed, it will signify good things. If poorly, it will portend evil and signify the deprivation of his goods or expulsion from them. If it is in the sixth house and it is any of the aforementioned "infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, it will signify the death of the seeker. And if it is in the birth of someone, it will signify that he will die a bad death. But if it is Jupiter, the Sun, or even Venus, it will signify profit by way of a dowry or perhaps the occupation of others' goods. If however it is Mercury or the Moon and the question is about a fearful matter, it signifies its emptying and annulment. ¶ If it is in the seventh house and it is a birth or a universal question about a journey, and it is one of the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it signifies profitable and lucrative journeys. If however it is one of the infortunes, you may judge the opposite. ¶ If it is in the eighth house, it signifies dominion and honor coming to him, or his attachment to masteries of the nature of that significator (as it pertains to it) or to some great man; or that his mother will love him above her other children. If it remains in the ninth, it signifies that the person born or the seeker will fulfill much of his desires and those things for which he has hope, as much by cause of friends as for other reasons. ¶ If it is in the tenth, it signifies sadness, alteration, tribulation, and prison, and also the taking away of large animals, both in births and in questions.

## Of the tenth house and its lord.

<note>The tenth house governs career, social standing, and kings.</note>

If indeed the lord of the tenth house is found in the eleventh in any question or birth, it signifies that the person born or seeker will enter into the household of a king or some magnate suited to a kingdom, or that he will have profit suited to himself. If indeed it is in the twelfth and the question is about a short journey, it signifies that it is not useful to him, especially if the journey is to prisoners

<column-break/>

and to kinsmen younger than himself; and it makes him doubtful unless it were for the sake of large animals <note>such as horses or oxen</note>. ¶ If however it is in the first house, it signifies the acquisition of houses and the other aforementioned things, and for the utility of both the seeker and the person born; and a good and long life is signified for him, and fortune from his elder kinsmen. ¶ But if it is in the second house, it signifies that the person born or the seeker will be fortunate in children and will rejoice in them, and in meals and garments, and in gaining substance—even more so if the "Part of Fortune" <note>an Arabic Part or calculated point in the chart</note> is there. ¶ If indeed it is in the third house, it signifies anger, labor, sadness, and infirmities; nor will he be fortunate in small animals or persons subject to him; nor will it turn out well for him there. ¶ But if it is in the fourth house and it is Venus or any of the changeable planets, and the question is about marriage, it signifies that it will be completed. And if it is Jupiter, it will signify that the person born or seeker will have good wives and good partners and fortune in trade. If indeed it is any of the infortunes, it will signify that he will have lawsuits and discords or separation in life from the place in which you find him or from his own goods—all the more so if it is from the lighter <note>faster-moving</note> planets, and again more so if the fourth house is a "mobile" <note>cardinal</note> sign. And if it is in the fifth house and is unfortunate, it signifies evil for the person born or seeker, receiving death and destruction. If however it is a fortune, it will signify that the person born or seeker will have fortune in the dowries of women and the occupation of other goods. And if the question is about profit, it will signify his fortune in foreign lands. ¶ If however it is in the sixth house, it signifies long journeys that are not good for the person born or seeker, being both laborious and unfortunate, unless it were a journey for domestic servants or other attendants or animals; nor is he fortunate in the clergy. ¶ But if it is in the seventh house, it signifies that the person born or seeker will acquire honor or arts and profit with women and because of women. ¶ If indeed it is in the eighth house, it signifies that he will fulfill many of his desires and those things which he hoped for, especially regarding the things of the dead; and mostly on the occasion of friends or some fortunate woman. If indeed it is in the ninth, it signifies anger and tribulation coming to the person born or seeker regarding things from which he desired to have good and utility, and in which he had trust.

## Of the ninth house and its lord.

<note>The ninth house governs long travel, religion, and philosophy.</note>

If however the lord of the ninth house is in the tenth in the birth of someone or in a question, it signifies that the person born or seeker will have a good, decent, and honorable familiarity with men, and especially with nobles and magnates and the domestics of magnates; and he will contract a stay or remain with them and have profit from them or from other magistrates. ¶ But if it is in the eleventh and the question is about a journey, it signifies that it will be fortunate and fruitful, and even more so if it is a journey to friends or with friends; it will also signify that the person born or seeker will bring many of his thoughts to his desired perfection, or that he will attach himself to some great family connection that is known to him. ¶ If indeed it is in the twelfth, it signifies that certain immovable and unfortunate things will come to the person born or seeker, as well as things harmful to you (though not lasting long), or that he will be hurt or damaged by large animals. ¶ If however it is in the first house and the interrogation was about children, it signifies the seeker...

If the lord is in the second house and the question concerns children or home-born servants <note>Latin: *vernaculis*</note>—as with smaller animals—it signifies gain, profit, and utility from them; you may judge the same for the one born.

In the case that it is in the third house and the question is about marriage, a partnership to be formed, or a business transaction, it signifies good fortune in all the aforementioned things. This is even more certain if that significator <note>The specific planet representing the matter</note> is well-placed. The subject or seeker will be fortunate regarding relatives, and especially in partnerships and social circles. He will be successful in legal disputes—though great lawsuits may occur—and fortunate in his associates and business deals. If the planet is Venus, it signifies he will be fortunate with women. If, however, it is one of the "unfortunates" <note>The "unfortunates" or malefics are typically Saturn or Mars, planets associated with challenge and hardship</note>, it will signify the opposite.

If it is in the fourth house and the question is about death, it signifies that death is coming; its nature will match the planet that is the significator of the matter. It also signifies that the subject or seeker will inherit the goods of the dead, especially immovable property <term>immovables: assets like land and buildings that cannot be moved</term>, and will acquire wealth through dowries or because of women. If he has not gained wealth from these causes, it suggests he is likely to find profit in a foreign land. However, if one of the "evils" is the significator of death—namely Saturn or Mars—it signifies an unpraiseworthy death, which will happen to him in some dwelling.

If it is in the fifth house, it signifies a successful journey for the sake of children, clothing, food, or because of messengers and news; he will be moderately fortunate in his travels.

If it is in the sixth house, it signifies the subject or seeker being placed over and outlasting lowly and lesser people, and that he will profit from small animals or through them.

If it is in the seventh house, it signifies his fortune in marriage, with women, in trade and partnerships, and also in lands that are not his own.

If it is in the eighth house, it signifies the subject or seeker falling into prison, or a heavy or mortal illness and tribulation. Indeed, if he involves himself with large animals, loss and harm will follow, and they will not help his profit; he should fear lest they hurt or offend him.

### Of the eighth house and its lord.
<note>The eighth house traditionally governs death, taxes, inheritance, and the resources of others.</note>

If the lord of the eighth house is in the ninth and the question is about someone who is absent, it signifies that the absent person is doing well, especially if his significator is a "fortune" <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>. For example, if it is Jupiter, it signifies he is spending time with judges or churchmen, or studying to acquire knowledge. If it is Venus, it signifies he is with women or with those who enjoy eating and drinking. If, however, it is the Moon or Mercury, it signifies he is with various and diverse people and that he does not stay stably or firmly in one place or land.

But if it is Mars, and he is well-placed and strong, it signifies he is practicing some art that involves iron, fire, and the shedding of blood; it appears that his association with the aforementioned people will be useful and fruitful for him.

If it is in the tenth house and the question is about a short journey—especially a journey to some great man or on the occasion of some magistracy or something that brings honor to the seeker—it will signify those coming events according to the seeker's intention.

If it is in the eleventh house, it signifies that his friends are striving to ensure he acquires

<column-break/>

some immovable thing that is useful and honorable for him, if the question was about this.

If, however, it is in the twelfth house and the question is about children, it signifies their bad parentage or that they will not live; and if they do live, he will not rejoice with them or because of them. It also signifies poison offered to the seeker or subject in food, and that he will not be fortunate in his clothing. Furthermore, messages and news that are displeasing to him will frequently be brought.

If it is in the first house, it signifies he will have moderate fortune in servants and home-born staff and in small animals; he will not be greatly burdened by heavy illnesses.

If it is in the second house, it signifies the subject or seeker will obtain a woman through whom gain and utility will follow, and that he will have fortune in the trade of movable goods. Nevertheless, if he enters into a partnership with anyone, it will not last long, and he will be quarrelsome with his own family.

If it is in the third house and the question is about a short journey, it signifies death on that journey. If the question is about a dowry, it signifies he will receive it, either from neighbors or in the region where the seeker lives; the same applies if the question is about an inheritance.

If it is in the fourth house and the question is about a long journey, it signifies that the journey will be bad, heavy, and hard; it also signifies the seeker will acquire a bad reputation during it. If the question is about some cleric <note>A member of the clergy</note>, it signifies he is bad, dishonest, and has little faith in divine matters. You may say the same about an absent person if the question concerns him.

If it is in the fifth house, it signifies the subject or seeker will have fortune in children, food, and clothing. If the question is about a wedding or a letter, it signifies good messengers and good things in the letter.

If it is in the sixth house and the question is about fortune, it signifies it is weak and not well-established; the subject or seeker will not be fortunate in friends, nor will they be truthful to him. However, he will be fortunate in servants, attendants, and small animals.

If it is in the seventh house and the question is about prison or an illness that is feared, it signifies the seeker will fall into the vice or the very thing he feared or doubted. This will happen to him because of a woman, a partner, or a merchant. He should also fear harm from thieves, exiles, or those who have been expelled, or through gambling or the betrayal of women.

### Of the seventh house and its lord.
<note>The seventh house governs marriage, known enemies, and legal partnerships.</note>

If the lord of the seventh house is in the eighth at the birth of someone or in a question, it signifies the subject or seeker will profit because of someone's death, or that he will inherit the goods of the dead. If the question is about the death of a business partner, a wife, or an enemy, it will signify that death. If the question is about an absent person, it signifies the person is delayed in that absence; it is possible he will be imprisoned because of a woman.

If it is in the ninth house and the question is about some journey, it signifies the journey is useless and not profitable, but rather harmful—and even more so if the ninth house belongs to an "unfortune" or if an "unfortune" is hindered within it. But if the question is whether a man should be joined with a certain woman, or about someone who desires to enter a church, it will signify that <note>i.e., it indicates the outcome of those specific desires</note>. If the question is whether one will encounter enemies on the road, or about a wife suspected of adultery <note>Latin: *mechari*</note> with a cleric, or that she intends to go to another land or place, or whether a cleric whom he mentions will be an enemy to the seeker, it will signify that.

### Of the sixth house and its lord.

If the lord of the sixth house is in the seventh: and the question is about an illness, it signifies it is caused by love, such as *hereos* <note>original: "hereos"; a medieval medical term for "lovesickness" or extreme erotic melancholy</note>. And if someone asks whether his lord <note>his master or superior</note> is falling ill, or being deposed from his honor, it appears one must fear lest it happen so. And if the question is about a mother or a teacher, lest they fall ill, it appears to signify that. ¶ If it is in the eleventh and the question is about animals, it signifies them to be useful. And if the question is whether a friend is falling ill, it will signify that: in other matters, the fortune of the seeker will not be well-disposed. ¶ If it is in the twelfth and the question is about the illness of servants, or imprisonment, or animals, it will signify that. ¶ If it is in the first: and the question is about servants, or about smaller animals, regarding what will become of them, it signifies they will not remain long in his hands: and if they do stay, they will fall ill; it will, however, be useful for the person of the seeker. ¶ And if it is in the second and the question is about entering into some church or about a long journey, it will signify that to be good, useful, and profitable. ¶ If it is in the third and the question is about dignity or an art with neighbors, or about a magistracy with relatives, it signifies the sought thing will fall to him, nor will it take much time for this. ¶ If it is in the fourth: and the question is about stable things or about future relatives older than himself, it signifies fortune in them. ¶ But if the question is about a city or a castle: it will signify illnesses coming into it, and the habitation of evil men in it, and of those studying and laboring to do evil. ¶ If it is in the fifth and the question is about things in which the seeker ought to rejoice or be glad: or about clothing: or about pregnancy, it will signify that. ¶ And if the question is about some illness, it will signify it to be from maleficence or sorcery <note>original: "maleficijs siue de facturio"; refers to physical harm caused by magic or hexes</note>.

### Of the fifth house and its lord.

If the lord of the fifth house is in the sixth and the question is whether a son is going to fall ill, it signifies that event: and if it is about the employment of servants or small animals, according to what the question was, it signifies it will be so. ¶ If the question is about eating or about clothing, it would signify something unfavorable therein.

### ¶ Concerning the Ease of Finding the Signification of Each House.

Lest I introduce everything to you regarding the significations of the twelve houses, so that it might be easy for you to find the meaning of each house; for there were once some—of whom I saw many—who believed that astrologers should work only through the first and the seventh houses. They gave the first house to the seeker and the seventh to the sought or the thing sought, which in my judgment was not appropriate. And I have done this for your lesser labor, since it was always difficult to search through all the houses to find the significator of any thing sought. And because I have not found any predecessor of ours who involved himself in this as I have, as far as I can remember—not that I believe they were ignorant of it, but because it wearied them to undergo such labor, and also they left it to the diligence of the wise. Wherefore, if a question is put to you about some matter, you will be able to know through which house you can find the significator of the thing sought. And I could tell you many other significations of the twelve houses, but I would lead you into such long-windedness and confusion that it would generate weariness for you; wherefore it seems to me that those things I have told you might suffice: for a man or a messenger will bring such questions or such births to you that you could well satisfy through the aforesaid things. For you will be able to predict for the newborn or the seeker what should happen to him from all the above-mentioned things for the whole time of his life, if you know the hour of his birth well and wish to correctly find all the above-mentioned things with discretion. And I will tell you in its proper place and time how any person ought to be considered, whether he asks for himself or for another, and who ought to ask for another and how. For he who asks for himself is viewed one way. Another way for one who asks for another. Another way if a citizen or inhabitant of some place asks. Another way if an expelled or banished or exiled or absent person asks. Another way if a clergyman <note>original: *clericus*</note> asks. Another way if a layman <note>original: *laicus*</note> asks. Another way if a clergyman asks about a layman and vice-versa. And another way if a king <note>original: *rer*, likely a typo for *rex*</note> asks about a subject and vice-versa. Another way if a king asks about the people. Another way if vice-versa. Another way if a Pope asks about a bishop. Another way if a bishop about a Pope. Another way if a bishop about his clergyman. Another way if a clergyman about his bishop. Another way if a master about a servant. Another way if vice-versa. And so understand regarding all the diversities of persons; these diversities and the houses which are given to them I will tell you after this in the business of judgments <note>astrological prognostications</note>: for thus any person will find the matter of the question and the judgment.

### ¶ Chapter Seven: Concerning the numbering of the houses and why they begin from the first and go toward the fourth, and from the fourth into the seventh, and from the seventh into the tenth, and from the tenth into the first.

To satisfy the question and the seeker regarding the numbering of the twelve houses. If anyone should wish to say that they are not to be numbered according to the right order: for we number them starting from the first going under the earth toward the fourth, and from the fourth toward the seventh, and from the seventh toward the tenth, and from the tenth toward the first; which numbering or computation of houses seems to be done from right to left. For it seems that we ought to number them from the first going toward the tenth, and from the tenth into the seventh, and from the seventh into the fourth, and from the fourth into the first. For then we would proceed according to the order in which we write, starting from the left going toward the right. The cause why this is so is this: since although the sky revolves from east to west by the first motion <note>The daily rotation of the celestial sphere</note>, nevertheless the planets, which have the power to imprint upon lower bodies, are moved from west to east by the second motion in the opposite direction...

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of planetary motion and the relative power of the twelve astrological houses. It transitions from the physical direction of the heavens to the qualitative strength of the houses, and then explains the "proper motion" of planets versus the general rotation of the stars.</meta>

...the part of the first motion <note>The "first motion" refers to the daily rotation of the entire sky from East to West, caused by the Earth's rotation.</note> which is from right to left: because it is against the succession of the signs. For the signs rise from beneath the earth (which is the "left" of the sky) toward that which is above the earth (which is its "right"). <term>But you might perhaps say that planets sometimes run in the direction of the first motion—namely, when they are retrograde.</term> To this it can be answered that the motion of retrogradation <note>The apparent backward movement of a planet in the sky.</note> is not natural, but rather accidental; nor is it entirely in sync with the first motion, but is always somewhat contrary to it—that is, resulting from the movement of the "carrying circles" <note>The epicycles and deferents used in medieval astronomy to explain planetary paths.</note> that move them toward the East, contrary to the direction of the first motion.

### Chapter Eight: Which houses are strong, which are stronger, which are weak, which are weaker, and which are average.

I have mentioned to you above the twelve houses, which are called "towers" or "cusps," and their significance from the first to the twelfth in forward order, and from the twelfth to the first in backward order. It now remains to be said which of them are strong, which are stronger, which are weak, which are weaker, and which are average. The **strong** houses are the four "angles": namely, the first house, which is the Eastern angle <note>The Ascendant</note>; the tenth, which is the Southern angle <note>The Midheaven</note>; the seventh, which is the Western angle <note>The Descendant</note>; and the fourth, which is the Northern angle <note>The Bottom of the Sky or Imum Coeli</note>. And of these four, two are stronger than the others: the first and the tenth. The **weak** houses are the four that "fall" away from the angles <note>Known as "cadent" houses</note>: namely, the third, which falls from the angle of the earth (the fourth house); the ninth, which falls from the Southern angle (the tenth house); the twelfth, which falls from the Eastern angle (the first house); and the sixth, which falls from the Western angle (the seventh house). And of these four, two are weaker than the others: the sixth and the twelfth. The remaining four—the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th—are **average** <note>Known as "succedent" houses</note>; however, they participate more in the strength of the "strong" houses than the "weak" ones because they move toward the strong houses. For although they are next to the weak houses as well as the strong, they move away from the weak and toward the strong. For the second house, which follows the first, moves toward it; the fifth, which follows the fourth, moves toward it; the eighth, which follows the seventh, moves toward it; and the eleventh, which follows the tenth, moves toward it. And Cahal <note>Likely a reference to a medieval astrological authority, possibly Zahel/Sahl ibn Bishr</note> said that the most worthy and strongest places of the circle are the angles; less worthy and less strong are the "following" houses; and weaker than all other places are the "falling" houses. He also said that the **angles** signify present matters (1, 10, 7, 4); the **following** houses signify what is to come and what follows the present (2, 5, 8, 11); and the **falling** houses signify what has already been, what has passed away, and what is no longer (3, 6, 9, 12). Among these, the Eastern angle (the Ascendant) is the strongest and most worthy, and a planet within it is stronger—especially if it has some dignity there, such as its own house, exaltation, term, triplicity, or face <note>These are technical terms for specific degrees of the zodiac where a planet exerts more influence.</note>—unless it is in certain excepted cases. Alternatively, if the Lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant, it is similarly strong. Next in strength follows the angle of the Midheaven (the 10th). Thus, a planet in the 10th house is said to be less strong than one in the Ascendant, except in matters of honors, magistracies, mastership, or other secular offices and things pertaining to laypeople, as has been said elsewhere. Again, a planet in the Western angle (the 7th) will be slightly less strong than one in the 10th. And even less strong will be one in the angle of the earth (the 4th) than one in the 7th. After the angles, the "following" houses are stronger, as I told you; but the eleventh house is stronger than the other following houses, and follows the fourth in strength; but

<column-break/>

even so, a planet in the 11th will be less strong than one in the 4th. The 5th follows the 11th in strength; thus, a planet in the 5th will be slightly less strong than one in the 11th, except for the specific meanings of each house, in which its own Lord is stronger than any other (the meanings being distinguished as they are). However, although the "following" houses are said to be stronger than the "falling" ones, the 9th house (which is a falling house) is stronger than the 2nd or 8th (which are following houses). And a planet in the 9th will be slightly less strong than one in the 5th, but stronger than one in the 2nd or 8th. The 3rd house follows the 9th in strength and precedes the 2nd and 8th in certain cases; thus, a planet in the 3rd will be less "weak" than one in the 2nd. Therefore, the aforementioned seven locations are better, stronger, and more praiseworthy than all others: the Ascendant (strongest), then the 10th, then the 7th, then the 4th, then the 11th, then the 5th, then the 9th, and finally the 3rd, which is stronger than the remaining houses. After those seven, the 3rd is stronger (or less weak) because it is the house in which the **Moon rejoices** <note>The concept of "Joy" refers to a house where a specific planet's nature is ideally expressed.</note>; for then the 3rd prevails over the 2nd and 8th in matters of journeys and similar things. Next is the 2nd, because it rejoices in the present first. The 8th house, however, is said to be a great misfortune, because it is the house of death and does not "behold" <note>An astrological aspect; houses that do not form a geometric angle with the Ascendant are considered "blind" or disconnected.</note> the Ascendant. The remaining two houses, namely the 6th and 12th, are evil, very weak, and unfortunate, and are called the worst of all houses. Any planet in these will be of no use, because the 6th does not behold the Ascendant and falls away from it; it is the house of infirmity and of all vices and diseases, both curable and incurable. It is the place of the <term>Joy of Mars</term>, who rejoices in burnings, the shedding of blood, and all evils committed with iron or fire. The 12th house similarly falls away from the Ascendant and does not behold it; it is the place of hidden enemies (those who do not oppose you publicly) and the place of anguish, sorrow, labor, sadness, weeping, and lamentation. It is the place of the <term>Joy of Saturn</term>, who rejoices in weeping, sadness, and lamentation.

### Chapter Nine: Why the planets move against the firmament, that is, against the first motion.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous Persian astrologer (787–886 AD).</note> and the philosophers agree on this: that all planets move by their own motion against the motion of the firmament, unless they happen to be retrograde. Retrogradation happens to the three superior planets—**Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars**—and the two inferior ones—**Venus and Mercury**. The "luminaries" <note>The Sun and Moon</note> do not undergo retrogradation, though they do experience speed and slowness in their course. However, the **Tail and Head of the Dragon** <note>The Lunar Nodes: the points where the Moon's path crosses the Sun's path, essential for predicting eclipses.</note> move in the opposite direction of the planets' motion—that is, against the succession of the signs. For the planets move from Aries into Taurus, from Taurus into Gemini, from Gemini into Cancer, from Cancer into Leo, from Leo into Virgo, from Virgo into Libra, from Libra into Scorpio, from Scorpio into Sagittarius, from Sagittarius into Capricorn, from Capricorn into Aquarius, from Aquarius into Pisces, and from Pisces back to Aries. But the Head and Tail move contrary to this: they move from Aries into Pisces, from Pisces into Aquarius, from Aquarius into Capricorn, and so on through the signs in reverse. And Cahal and Caucaph <note>Likely "Kokhab," the Hebrew word for star/planet, or a corruption of another authority's name</note> say again that the Head and Tail of the Dragon are nothing other than the intersection of the circles of the luminaries...

### ¶ Chapter ten: On the colors which the houses signify.

Since the aforementioned twelve houses have meanings as stated previously, someone might perhaps think they do not signify anything else. But it is not so; rather, they signify not only all the things mentioned before, but they also signify various colors. For the **first** and **seventh** houses signify whiteness; the **second** and **twelfth** signify greenness; the **third** and **eleventh** signify saffron-yellow; the **fourth** and **tenth** signify redness; the **fifth** and **ninth** signify a honey-colored hue; the **sixth** and **eighth** signify blackness. Therefore, if it is necessary for you to look for the color of any thing, look in which of the houses you find its "significator" <note>The planet or house representing the subject of the question</note> and judge the color of the thing you seek according to that house.

### ¶ Chapter eleven: In which houses the planets rejoice.

¶ Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> and Alchabitius <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> say that each of the seven planets has a certain "accidental power" in one of the above-mentioned twelve houses, which is called its **joy**. ¶ For **Mercury** rejoices in the first house because the first house signifies the body of the person born or the "querent" <note>the person asking the astrological question</note>. For this reason, Mercury rejoices in it, because he himself signifies thought and judgment, and this is the quality that is better suited to the person of the born or the querent than any other; for it alone can ennoble a human being, which no other accidental quality can do. ¶ The **Moon** rejoices in the third house because the third signifies short and hurried journeys, and things that are quickly changed or repeated. Therefore, because the Moon also signifies swift and hurried changes from one purpose to another and from one thing to another, she rejoices in it, for no other house signifies this. ¶ **Venus** rejoices in the fifth house because it is the house of joy, delight, and dancing; and she herself signifies this. Therefore, she rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this. ¶ **Mars** rejoices in the sixth house because it is the house of deception, illness, and servants; and he himself signifies servants, deceivers, liars, and the untruthful, and therefore he rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this. ¶ The **Sun** rejoices in the ninth house, which is the house of religion, because he naturally signifies religion; and therefore he rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this, although he also signifies other things. ¶ **Jupiter** rejoices in the eleventh house because he himself is "fortune" <note>the "Greater Benefic"</note> and signifies luck and profit; he is naturally the significator of money and gain, and the eleventh house signifies that. ¶ **Saturn** rejoices in the twelfth house because it is the house of misery, sadness, labor, lamentation, and weeping, and Saturn rejoices in these and similar things.

### ¶ Chapter twelve: On the significations of the houses or "succedent" angles, and the lords of the angles, succedents, and "cadents."

It was said in the signification of the twelve houses that the **angles** <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, and 10</note> signify strength, perfection, and a swift or more rapid action; the angles and their lords signify the greatness of honor, worth, and fortune. The **cadent** <note>Houses 3, 6, 9, and 12</note> houses from the angles signify weakness, loss, misfortune, and the hiding of things—except for the ninth and third, which signify "appearing" <note>becoming visible or manifest</note>. The sixth and twelfth signify concealment, hiding, the lowliness of things, disgrace, and a swift fall. The **succedent** <note>Houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which "succeed" or follow the angles</note> houses of the angles signify strength and

<column-break/>

average fortune. For the **eleventh**, which follows the tenth, is stronger and more worthy than the others and signifies average fortune through friends and through that which one has some confidence in, or from other causes among those signified by the eleventh house. The **fifth** house, which follows the fourth, signifies average fortune through gifts, the cause of children, cheerfulness, and joy, or from other causes among those signified by the fifth house. ¶ The **second**, which follows the first, signifies average fortune from the cause of substance <note>wealth/possessions</note>, assistants, and household members, or from any of those things signified by the second house. ¶ The **eighth**, which follows the seventh, signifies average fortune from substance inherited from the dead, which some call *almanerith* <note>original: "almanerith," a Latinized Arabic term for inheritance</note>. And Alchabitius said that it signifies fortune from hidden things, or at least from another cause among those signified by the eighth house.

### ¶ Chapter 13: On the signification of the lords of the angles and the angles, and first concerning the lord of the first in the first.

When the lords of the angles are in the angles, it signifies well. For when the **lord of the first** is in the **first**, it signifies the fortune of the person born and their acquisition by themselves, through their own industry, the labor of their body, through their family, through their study, through their diligence, and through those things signified by the first house. ¶ When, however, he is in the **tenth**, it signifies his fortune through his masters and offices or positions of power, through high and lofty masteries, and through the king and communication with kings or great men and the like, and through those things also signified by the tenth house. ¶ When, however, he is in the **seventh**, it signifies his fortune through agreements and contracts which he will make with men who will be useful to him, and also through wives and by cause of women and partners, and through those things signified by the seventh house. ¶ When, however, he is in the **fourth**, it signifies his fortune by cause of a father or grandfather or partner, or by cause of some inheritance which will come to him from which he will profit; and through the creation of rivers or other waters, the planting of trees, the building of houses, and by cause of ancient and foundational things; or through hidden treasure which he will find buried, and similar things, or through those things signified by the fourth house.

### ¶ Concerning the lord of the tenth in the tenth.

When the **lord of the tenth** is in the **tenth**, it signifies fortune through a great kingdom, through the king, through higher masteries, and through those things signified by the tenth house. ¶ And when the lord of the tenth is in the **seventh**, it signifies fortune through contentions involving kings or the kingdom, through victory in contentions, and through those whom he will have contending against him, and from the causes of women or through those things signified by the seventh house. ¶ When the lord of the tenth is in the **fourth**, it signifies fortune through the kingdom, through the collection of tributes and the causes or occasions of tributes, through the cultivation of lands, the building of cities, fortresses, and the like, through the leading and dividing of waters and rivers, through the guarding of cities and fortresses and the like, and through ancient things and outflows beneath the earth, or through any of the things signified by the fourth house. ¶ When, however, he is in the **first**, it signifies fortune through the kingdom, through a praiseworthy and famous matter, through the genius of his own person, through dwelling with kings and great men and being near them, and from the cause of the common people, or through those things signified by the first house.

### ¶ Concerning the lord of the seventh in the seventh.

When the Lord of the **seventh** house is located in the **seventh**, it signifies fortune through business dealings, legal questions, and exchanges. If the subject is a woman, it suggests gain through nursing and nourishing; for a man, it signifies gain through women, business partners, the act of sowing, or through daughters—or generally through those things signified by the seventh house. When the Lord of the seventh is in the **fourth**, it signifies fortune through the inquiries of women; women will earn on his behalf and for his benefit. It also signifies fortune through the business and causes of fathers and grandfathers, inheritance cases, the planting of trees and vines, the cultivation of the earth, and similar matters, or things signified by the fourth house. When the Lord of the seventh is in the **first**, it signifies fortune, gain, and business through medical matters, through **astronomy** <note>In this period, "astronomy" and "astrology" were often used interchangeably as the study of the stars' effects.</note>, and through works involving spiritual things and ingenuity, or things signified by the first house. However, when the Lord of the seventh is in the **tenth**, it signifies good fortune through the causes of the king or matters signified by the tenth house.

### On the Lord of the fourth in the fourth.

When the Lord of the **fourth** house is in the **fourth**, it signifies fortune by means of mastery and the smithing arts <note>mechanical or manual crafts</note>. If the person is from a family of farmers, it signifies fortune for them through the cultivation of the land, from its fruit or profit, through the affairs of fathers and family, and through ancient things, or those things signified by the fourth house. However, when the Lord of the fourth is in the **Ascendant** <note>the first house</note>, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of the land and its fruit through ingenuity and the "depth" <note>intellectual capacity or profound nature</note> of the son, and through things signified by the first house.

### On the Lord of the fourth in the tenth.

However, when the Lord of the **fourth** is in the **tenth**, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of lands and from fruit or profit through the affairs of kings, magnates, nobles, and the wealthy; also through the fruits of mastery, their causes, and daughters, or through things signified by the tenth house.

### On the Lord of the fourth in the seventh.

But when the Lord of the **fourth** is in the **seventh**, it signifies fortune, gain, profit, and success from the cultivation of the land and from fruit through the affairs of wives, partners, and enemies, as well as through contentions, business, and daughters, which are signified by the seventh house.

### On the significance of the Lords of the succeedent houses in succeedent houses.

Truly, whenever the Lords of the **succeedent houses** <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow the "angles" or corners of the chart</note> are in succeedent houses—any one of them in any succeedent house—they signify "middling" or average fortune through the things signified by that succeedent house, just as was said regarding the Lords of the angles in any angle according to their meanings.

### On the significance of the Lords of the cadent houses in cadent houses.

Furthermore, whenever the Lords of the **cadent houses** <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which "fall away" from the angles and are considered the weakest</note> are in cadent houses—any one of them in any cadent house—it signifies misfortune and impediment through the things signified by that cadent house, just as was said regarding the Lords of the angles in any angle according to their meanings. These are the things which the Lords of the aforementioned houses signify in the aforementioned houses, but the explanation was given using the Lords of the angles so that it might serve as an example for the Lords of the succeedent and cadent houses.

## Chapter 14: On finding the significator of the thing sought.

<margin>
Note the
method
of finding
the sought
significator
</margin>

In order that you do not fall into error or ambiguity regarding the meanings of things signified by any house, I will teach you to find the planet which is the **significator** <note>the specific planet that represents the topic of the question</note> of the thing you seek. For it is not always the Lord of the sign <note>the ruling planet of the zodiac sign on the house cusp</note> that is the significator of the thing signified by that house; rather, sometimes another planet is the Lord of the house, and another (who is not the Lord of the house) is stronger in that house. For that planet is called "stronger" which has more "dignities" or **fortitudes** <note>points of strength based on its position in the zodiac</note> there; and he who has the most fortitudes in the house of the matter, or who has the right to signify that matter which is being questioned, that planet is called the significator,

<column-break/>

whom Alchabitius <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> calls the **Almuten** <note>original: "almuten", a term meaning the "winner" or most powerful planet in a specific degree</note>, which is to say, the **Victor**. He is called the Victor because he exceeds the other planets in strength in the house being questioned. Here is an example: a certain question was asked regarding **substance** <note>original: "substantia", meaning wealth or possessions</note> where the Ascendant was the first degree of **Pisces**. **Aries** was the second house (specifically its sixth degree), which is the house of wealth. It might seem that **Mars**, who is the Lord of Aries, should be the significator of wealth, but it is not so. For Mars has only six fortitudes there—five from being the house ruler and one from the **face** <note>a 10-degree division of a sign</note>—and thus there are six fortitudes for Mars. But in that same sign is the **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note> of the **Sun**, who has seven fortitudes there: four from exaltation and three from **triplicity** <note>the element group (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) the sign belongs to</note>; and thus the Sun has the seven aforementioned fortitudes. Therefore, the Sun remains the significator of wealth, and not Mars, because of the greater number of fortitudes the Sun holds there. Nevertheless, although the Sun is the primary ruler over wealth in this question, Mars will be its "partner," though he can do less there than the Sun. And if the Sun were so "impeded" <note>afflicted or weakened by other factors</note> that he could not be the significator, then the significance would fall to Mars; and so on to **Jupiter** if Mars were too weak to be the significator. And the **Moon** will always be a partner. Furthermore, Jupiter has something to do there, having some level of partnership with them, for he has two fortitudes there because of the **term** <note>a specific division of a sign ruled by a planet</note> he holds there; he is also a partner for another reason, as he is the natural significator of wealth. In this same question, the 12th degree of **Taurus** was the third house; so if the question were about brothers or any of those things signified by the third house, you would then need to look for the planet that was stronger in it. Understand the same for the rest of the houses and their meanings. In a question of wealth, you should also look for the **Part of Substance**, which you can find in this way: see which of the planets is the significator of wealth; see in what degree of which sign it is; and subtract that from the degree of the house of wealth. What remains is the location of the Part of Substance, as you will find when the "Parts" are treated in their own section. However, I will give you an example here using the second house of this question (the house of wealth), which was at 6 degrees of Aries. Mars, the Lord of Aries, was found in the 8th degree of **Scorpio**. You must now subtract Scorpio from Aries, but you cannot do this because you cannot subtract 8 from 1. Add 12 signs <note>the full circle of the zodiac</note> and subtract the 8 degrees of Scorpio from the 12 signs and 6 degrees; there will remain 4 signs and 28 degrees. Starting your count from the 6th degree of Aries (the beginning of the house of wealth), the Part of Substance falls in **Leo**, in the 28th degree of that sign. You shall do the same for the **Part of Fortune** and the other Parts. But the Part of Fortune is calculated in another, easier way, as will be said in the treatise on the Parts. You shall do the same for the other houses: the third, fourth, fifth, etc. Thus you will always find the significator of the matter you seek by appointing the planet that holds the greatest strength in the house signifying the matter.

## Chapter fifteen: On accidental powers.

It is known that planets are in their "similitude" (while still observing the method described in the treatise on the Parts) which Alchabitius and other wise men call **Haym** <note>original: "haym", likely a corruption of the Arabic "Hayyiz", meaning sect or dignity by position</note>. This occurs when a **diurnal** <note>day-ruling</note> planet is above the earth by day and below the earth by night, and a **nocturnal** <note>night-ruling</note> planet is above the earth by night and below the earth by day. Also, when a masculine planet is in a masculine sign, and a feminine planet is in a feminine sign. When a planet is thus placed, it is in its similitude.

### Chapter Ten: Concerning the colors signified by the houses.

**S**ince the aforesaid twelve houses signify the things mentioned above, someone might perhaps think they do not signify anything else. But it is not so; indeed, they signify not only the things mentioned, but also various colors. For the **first** and **seventh** houses signify **whiteness**; the **second** and **twelfth** signify **greenness**; the **third** and **eleventh** signify **saffron-yellow**; the **fourth** and **tenth** signify **redness**; the **fifth** and **ninth** signify **honey-color**; the **sixth** and **eighth** signify **blackness**. Therefore, if it is necessary for you to look for the color of any thing, look in which house you find its significator <note>The "significator" is the planet or house representing the person or object being asked about.</note>, and according to that house, judge the color of the thing you seek.

### Chapter Eleven: In which houses the planets rejoice.

**A**bu Ma'shar <note>original: "Albumasar"; a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> and Al-Qabisi <note>original: "Alchabitius"; a 10th-century Arab astrologer.</note> say that each of the seven planets has a certain accidental power in one of the aforementioned twelve houses, which is called its **joy** <note>term: "joy" (Latin: *gaudium*); a specific house where a planet’s nature is most effectively expressed.</note>. For **Mercury** rejoices in the **first**, because the first house signifies the body of the person born or the seeker; and because of this, Mercury rejoices in it, for he signifies the intellect, and this is the thing that is most suited to the person of the born or the seeker more than any other thing. For it alone can ennoble a person in a way that no other accidental quality can. The **Moon** rejoices in the **third**, because the third house signifies short and frequent journeys that change and repeat quickly; since the Moon signifies these fast and frequent changes from one purpose to another and from one thing to another, she rejoices in it, because no other house signifies this. **Venus** rejoices in the **fifth**, because it is the house of joy, delight, and dance; she signifies this, and therefore rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this. **Mars** rejoices in the **sixth**, because it is the house of deception, infirmities, and servants; he signifies servants, deceivers, liars, and those who speak falsely, and therefore he rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this. The **Sun** rejoices in the **ninth**, which is the house of religion, because he naturally signifies religion; therefore he rejoices in it because the other houses do not signify this, even though he may signify other things as well. **Jupiter** rejoices in the **eleventh**, because he is the "Greater Fortune" and signifies fortune and profit; he is naturally the significator of money and gain, and the eleventh house signifies that. **Saturn** rejoices in the **twelfth**, because it is the house of misery, sadness, labor, lamentation, and weeping, and Saturn rejoices in these and similar things.

### Chapter Twelve: On the significations of the houses or angles, the succeedent houses, and the lords of the angular, succeedent, and cadent houses.

**I**t was said in the signification of the twelve houses that the **angles** <note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses; they are considered the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> signify strength, perfection, and the swift arrival of matters; the angles and their lords signify the greatness of honor, price, and fortune. The **cadent** houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses; usually considered weak or unlucky.</note> from the angles signify weakness, loss, misfortune, and the hiding of things—except for the ninth and third, which signify "appearance." The sixth and twelfth signify concealment, hiding, the [lack of] utility of things, disgrace, and a sudden fall. The **succeedent** houses <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses; they follow the angles and are considered of moderate strength.</note> of the angles signify strength and

<column-break/>

moderate fortune. For the **eleventh**, which follows the tenth, is stronger and more worthy than the others; it signifies moderate fortune from friends and from that which gives one confidence, or from other causes belonging to the eleventh house. The **fifth** house, which follows the fourth, signifies moderate fortune through gifts, children, cheerfulness, and joy, or other causes belonging to the fifth house. The **second**, which follows the first, signifies moderate fortune by reason of substance, ministers, and household members, or from things signified by the second house. The **eighth**, which follows the seventh, signifies moderate fortune from the substance inherited from the dead, which some call *almuerith* <note>original: "almuerith"; from the Arabic *al-mīrāth*, meaning inheritance.</note>. And Al-Qabisi said that it signifies this from hidden things, or at least from other causes among those signified by the eighth house.

### Chapter 13: On the significance of the lords of the angles and the angles; and first, on the lord of the first in the first.

**W**hen the lords of the angles are in the angles, it signifies the following: for when the **Lord of the First** is in the **first**, it signifies the fortune of the person born and their acquisitions through themselves, by their own industry and the labor of their body, and through their family, their study, their anxieties, and those things signified by the first house. When he is in the **tenth**, it signifies fortune through their masters, offices or powers, and through high and lofty positions; and also through the king and communication with kings or nobles and the like, and through things signified by the tenth house. When he is in the **seventh**, it signifies fortune through agreements and contracts they will make with men who will be useful to them, and also through wives and by cause of women and partners, and through things signified by the seventh house. When he is in the **fourth**, it signifies fortune by cause of the father, grandfather, or father-in-law, or by cause of some inheritance that will come to them from which they will profit; and through the creation of rivers or other waters, the planting of trees, the building of houses, and by cause of ancient and foundational things; or through hidden treasure which they will find under the earth and similar things, or through things signified by the fourth house.

When the Lord of the Tenth is in the **seventh**, it signifies fortune through the king or kingdom, and through victory in disputes, and through those who contend against them, and from the causes of women, or through things signified by the seventh house. When the lord of the seventh is in the seventh, it signifies fortune through trade and profits from loans. And if the client is a woman, it signifies fortune through nursing and breastfeeding <note>original: "lactationes & nutricatiões"; common occupations for women in the medieval period</note>; and if a man, through women and partners, and through the practices of sowing and tools <note>original: "stilia"; likely referring to pens or engraving tools</note>, or through those things signified by the seventh house. ### Concerning the lord of the fourth in the fourth.
When the lord of the fourth is in the fourth, it signifies fortune through the work of masters and the smithing arts. And if he be of the class of farmers, it signifies his fortune through the cultivation of the earth and fruit or profit through the affairs of fathers and similar things and ancient matters, or through those things signified by the fourth house. When, however, the lord of the fourth is in the ascendant <note>The "ascendant" is the first house.</note>, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of the earth and fruit through ingenuity and the depth of the son <note>original: "filij profunditatem"; this may be a scribal error or a specific technical term for deep-seated family matters</note>, and through those things signified by the first house.

### Concerning the lord of the fourth in the tenth.
When, however, the lord of the fourth is in the tenth, it signifies fortune from the cultivation of lands and fruit or profit through the affairs of kings and magnates or nobles and the wealthy, and through the fruits of masterships and from their affairs and daughters, or through those things signified by the tenth house.

### Concerning the lord of the fourth in the seventh.
When, truly, the lord of the fourth is in the seventh, it signifies fortune and gain or profit and benefit from the cultivation of the earth and from fruit through the affairs of wives, partners, and enemies, and through contentions and through business and daughters <note>original: "filia"</note> which are signified by the seventh house.

### Concerning the significance of the lords of the succedent houses in succedent houses.
The lords of the succedent <note>term: "succedent"; the houses (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th) that "follow" the four main angles of the chart.</note> houses when placed in succedent houses signify middling fortune; each of them in any succedent house signifies through those things signified by that succedent house, just as was said regarding the lords of the angles in any angle according to their significations.

### Concerning the significance of the lords of the cadent houses in cadent houses.
The lords of the cadent <note>term: "cadent"; the houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) that "fall away" from the angles, usually considered the weakest or most unfortunate positions.</note> houses signify misfortune and hindrance; each of them in any cadent house signifies through those things signified by that cadent house, just as was said regarding the lords of the angles in any angle according to their significations. These are the things which the lords of the aforesaid houses signify in the aforesaid houses, as has been explained concerning the lords of the angles, so that it may serve as an example for the lords of the succedent and cadent houses.

### Chapter 14: On finding the significator of the thing sought.
And so that you do not fall into error or ambiguity regarding the significations of things which are signified by any house, I will teach you to find the planet which is the significator of the thing you seek. For the lord of the sign is not always the significator of the thing which is signified by that house about which you inquire; rather, sometimes one planet is the lord of the house and another, who is not the lord of the house, is stronger in that house. For that one is said to be "stronger" who has more dignities <note>term: "dignities"; the various ways a planet gains strength in a specific location, such as being in its own sign or its exaltation.</note> or strengths there; and he who possesses the most strengths in the house of the matter, or who is meant to signify that thing which is the subject of the inquiry, that planet is called the significator,

<column-break/>

whom Al-Qabisi <note>original: "alchabidus"</note> calls the *Almuten* <note>original: "almutez"; from the Arabic *al-mubtazz*, meaning the "winner" or "victor" of a house.</note>, that is, the victor. And he is called the victor because he exceeds the other planets in strength in the house being questioned. Here is an example: a certain question was asked concerning "substance" <note>In astrology, "substance" refers to personal wealth and moveable property.</note> where the ascendant was the first degree of Pisces. Aries was the second house—namely its sixth degree—which is the house of substance. It might seem that Mars, who is the lord of Aries, should be the significator of substance, but it is not so. For Mars has only six strengths there, since he has five from being in his own house and one from being in his face <note>term: "face"; the smallest of the essential dignities, also called a "decan."</note>, and thus there are six strengths for Mars. And that same sign is the exaltation of the Sun, who has seven strengths there: four from exaltation and three from triplicity <note>term: "triplicity"; a dignity based on the element of the sign (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note>, and thus the Sun has the seven aforementioned strengths. Therefore, the Sun himself remains the significator of substance and not Mars, because of the greater number of strengths which the Sun has there. Nevertheless, although the Sun in this question is the ruler over the substance, Mars will be a participant in it, but he can do less there than the Sun. And if the Sun should be hindered in such a way that he cannot be the significator, the significance then falls to Mars; and thus to Jupiter if Mars were so weak that he could not be the significator. And the Moon will always be a participant.

Furthermore, Jupiter has something to do there, whence he has some degree of participation with them; for he has two strengths there because of the term <note>term: "term"; a dignity based on specific degrees of a sign assigned to the five non-luminary planets.</note> which he has there; and he is also a participant for another reason, because he is naturally a significator of substance. And in this question, the 12th degree of Taurus was the third house; whence if there were a question about brothers or about any of those things signified by the third house, it would behoove you then to look for the planet which was stronger in it. And understand the same for the other houses and their other significations. And you ought also to look in a question of substance for the "Part of Substance" <note>term: "Part of Substance"; one of the "Arabic Parts" or "Lots," calculated by adding and subtracting specific degrees in a chart.</note> which you can find thus: See which of the planets is the significator of substance, and see in what degree of whatever sign he may be; and subtract that from the degree of the house of substance, and that which remains is the location of the Part of Substance, just as you will find when it is treated in its own place concerning the Parts. However, I will give you here an example of the second house of this question, which is the house of substance, which was the 6th degree of Aries. And Mars, who is the lord of Aries, was found in the 8th degree of Scorpio. You must now subtract Scorpio from Aries, but you cannot do this because you cannot subtract 8 from 1. Add 12 signs to the 1, and subtract the 8 degrees of Scorpio from the 12 signs and 6 degrees, and there will remain for you 4 signs and 28 degrees; beginning to project this from the 6th degree of Aries, which is the beginning of the house of substance, the Part of Substance will fall in Leo, in the 28th degree of that same Leo. And so you shall do for the Part of Fortune and the other Parts. But the Part of Fortune is taken in another and easier way, as will be said in the treatise on the Parts. And you shall do the same for the other houses, namely the third, fourth, fifth, etc. And thus you will always find the significator of the thing you seek by appointing that significator who has the greater strength in the house signifying the thing sought.

### Chapter Fifteen: On accidental powers.
There arises from the planets a state where they are in their "similitude" <note>term: "similitude"; a condition where a planet's gender and sect match its environment.</note>, keeping however to the manner described in the treatise on the Parts, which Al-Qabisi and other wise men call *aym* <note>original: "aym"; likely a transliteration of an Arabic term for this condition, often called *hayyiz*.</note>: namely when a diurnal planet is above the earth by day and below the earth by night; and a nocturnal planet is above the earth by night and below the earth by day. And a masculine planet when it is in a masculine sign, and a feminine one in a feminine sign. When a planet is thus, it is in its similitude.

Since day-bound things rejoice in the day, night-bound things in the night, masculine things in masculinity, and feminine things in femininity: therefore, when a planet is the **significator** <note>The planet that "points to" or represents a specific person or question in a chart.</note> of any matter and is in its own likeness, it will complete the matter better and more perfectly than when it is not. There is also a certain strength called **haym** <note>original: "aym"; from the Arabic 'hayyiz', a dignity where a planet is in a sign and hemisphere matching its own gender and diurnal/nocturnal nature</note>, and then the planet is somewhat stronger than when it is not in its haym; just as a person who is in a state where they may profit, satisfies their intention in some way, succeeds, and fortune seems to favor them.

# Here begins the third treatise on the natures of the seven planets: and what is proper to them, and what they signify concerning the being of any thing according to their state and natures, and what they imprint upon the lower world according to the variety of the qualities of their motions.

## The first chapter concerning what Saturn signifies.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration representing the planet Saturn. Saturn is personified as an old man with a long beard, wearing a crown and robes. He sits on a high-backed throne mounted on a chariot with two large wheels. He holds a scepter in his right hand and a scythe in his left. Above his head to the left is a star or sun. To his right is the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄). Below the chariot, two smaller figures are visible, including one kneeling or working on the ground.</image-desc>

**P**ost-reaching the completion of what was intended regarding the circle of signs, its divisions, and its accidents, we must now provide a memorial of the seven planets and recount their natures, their significations, and the impressions they leave upon the lower world: and first concerning **Saturn**. **Alchabicius** <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> said: Saturn is a masculine, diurnal planet, and he works with imbalanced coldness and dryness. He is also the significator of fathers and grandfathers and all ancestors who are signified by the fourth house, but this is more by accident than by nature. For naturally, he signifies the person or the body of the **native** <note>The person born at the time the chart is cast.</note>; because the first thing that happens to a human is the physical person through which existence is given. Saturn is in the first circle of the planets and is the first planet in their order, for all others follow him. He is also the first to exercise his operation upon the conceptus after the falling of the seed into the womb, by binding and gathering together that matter from which the conceptus is formed. For the operations of the **fixed stars**—which are the primary agents—are not clearly felt in these matters, but only those of the planets, which are the secondary agents. Alchabicius and others who said Saturn signifies fathers and ancient or heavy things did so in respect to his slow and heavy motion and his weightiness; for this reason, they placed him as the significator of ancient parents and old, heavy things, and not without fitting cause. If he is the significator of any birth and is **oriental** <note>Rising before the sun.</note> and the birth is by day, the native will not easily reach the full span of a natural life, though they might reach the beginning of old age (which is from the 60th year onwards) unless something else hinders it against nature—just as we see the greatest part of men die before their due time by the sword, fire, accident, fall, ruin, drowning, and many other causes which are not

<column-break/>

part of nature's consideration nor its intention, as was said above. But if he is oriental and the birth is by night, it signifies the native’s life will last until the end of old age, unless the aforementioned things hinder it; of which we shall speak below in the treatise on births. He said that Saturn signifies everything involving the weight of cold and imbalanced dryness. Among the **humors** <note>The four bodily fluids thought to govern health and temperament.</note>, he signifies **melancholy**. Among the complexions of bodies, he signifies the melancholic; and perhaps that melancholy will be mixed with phlegm. Because of the weight and heaviness of the native's body, his walk will not be light, nor will he jump easily, nor will he learn behaviors or similar things that show physical agility. He will be fetid and bad-smelling, as if with the **stench of a bear** <note>original: "fetore vrcino"</note>, and he makes men of much eating. If Saturn should begin to love someone (which rarely happens), he loves them with a true love. If he begins to hate someone (which happens more often), he will hate them with an ultimate hatred and will hardly or never cease from that hate. **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, another influential 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said that if he is in a good state, he signifies depth of knowledge and good, deep counsel, such that a man will hardly ever know anything better. Among the **masteries** <note>Occupations or crafts.</note>, he signifies ancient, laborious, heavy, and precious things: and waterworks or those things made near water, such as mills, bridges, ships, and the like; the production of water; and the cultivation of the earth—namely the planting of fields, the planting of trees, the building of houses, and especially the houses of religious orders who wear black robes, if he is fortunate and in a good state. But if he is unfortunate and in a bad state, he signifies ancient and vile things: such as wood-cutting, the digging of lowly pits in stinking places, and the carrying of stones and cement on the neck to walls (especially underground walls or city walls made next to ditches) and the making of many things from which bricks and similar items are formed. For the most part, such people live in labor, anguish, and poverty, and eat bad and stinking food. Alchabicius said he signifies sailors—specifically lowly ones—when he is in a bad state. If he is in a good state, he signifies great and wealthy sailors, those who grow rich from navigation; and he will be of true love, expansive, and patient. If Saturn is in a bad state, the native will be indiscreet, sad, grieving, and of bad suspicion, dwelling in suspicion of every evil, and stirring up men with whisperings and evil instigations. If he is in a good state, he signifies ancient and durable things like inheritances that come from elsewhere—especially from the dead—and estates which they acquire through right rather than wrong. But if he is in a bad state, he signifies that the native will use putrid, filthy, marshy, stinking, and old waters that have stood a long time in one place, such as in pools and the like; and waters of bad taste, and he will not shrink from drinking them. He will willingly dwell in marshes or near them and eat rotten fish and rotten meat, nor does he seem to feel any harm from it. Regarding illnesses, he signifies **epilepsy** <note>original: "morbum caducum", the falling sickness.</note>; he signifies phlegmatic and melancholic diseases, and those that are frozen, hard, earthy, and compact. For the most part, he signifies diseases that are not cured, such as **leprosy**, **vitiligo** <note>original: "albaras"</note>, **morphew** <note>A skin disease causing scurfy spots.</note>, deep **fistulas**, and cavities. He signifies that these diseases will happen to the native when Saturn is the significator and is in such a state. In questions of illness, he will mostly signify such ailments. He also signifies long pilgrimages...
