...distant and laborious; and a man will become such when Saturn is the **significator** <note>The planet that represents a person or subject in an astrological chart.</note> of a journey, for the journey will be laborious, harsh, and almost intolerable. It signifies harsh and bitter prisons. It also signifies the taking of pledges from those who provide security to one another in custody, but he will not care much to reconcile them. It signifies heaviness of the body, slowness, labor, affliction of the mind, and evil thoughts. It represents the property of the dead that remains after them; fathers, grandfathers, and brothers older than the person born; and servants, eunuchs, and low-born persons. And if Saturn is the sole significator of a person's birth—meaning no other planet is combined with him—the person's occupation will be working with leather and making things from it.

### On the combination of Saturn with Jupiter and other planets.

If Jupiter is joined with him, it signifies the work of papers on which the books of the churches are written, divine words, and treatises on divinity, as well as those in which words are written concerning superior and heavenly things—such as the judgments of the stars, both theoretical and practical—and all subtle arts, the judgment of laws, and similar things. If Mars is joined with him, it signifies the working of leather from which soles <note>original: "solea"; the bottom parts of shoes or sandals</note> are made. If the Sun is joined with him, it signifies the working of those things which are gathered together from future materials, such as hides, inner-soles, and the like. If Venus is joined with him, it signifies the working of leather from which drums, cymbals, and all instruments are made for the sound of delight, play, and pipes. If Mercury is joined with him, it signifies the working of leather—namely, parchment—on which writings are made for perpetual memory, such as wills, instruments of buying and selling, and the like; and parchment on which are written the accounts of expenses made in the courts of nobles and the wealthy, and others who wish to keep a record of their expenses; and those in which the accounts of merchants and money-changers are written. And if the Moon is joined with him, it signifies the working or preparation of the leather of wild animals and also domestic ones that have died of natural causes, and things similar to these. Therefore, if a person born under these signs wishes to work in leather, judge for him according to what you see of the combination of Saturn with any of the planets, and let him involve himself in leatherworking in that manner.

Regarding religious sects, he signifies the Jewish faith—namely, the Old Testament—and every sect that confesses unity <note>Monotheism</note>. If he is in a bad state, he signifies a belief in unity accompanied by much hesitation or doubt. **Messahala** <note>Mashallah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a prominent Persian-Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note>, who was one of the most skilled astrologers and very distinguished in this science, says that he signifies the Jewish faith because it is among the oldest, and no positive law is found to be older than it. All other laws and sects acknowledge it, but it acknowledges no other law; nor does it acknowledge any other sect, just as all other planets join with Saturn, but he joins with no other of the planets. He also signifies black garments and those who wear black clothes, whether they are religious and cloistered people or others. Regarding metals, he signifies iron and lead. **Albubetri** <note>Abu Bakr al-Hasan ibn al-Khasib, a 9th-century Persian astrologer known in the West as Albubather.</note> said that he signifies the inner parts of the ear, the spleen, and the stomach. Of colors, he has black. Of tastes, the styptic <note>Astringent or mouth-puckering.</note> and the sour. Of days, Saturday; and of nights, that which precedes the day of Mercury <note>Tuesday night.</note>. The size of his orb is nine degrees. His **firdaria** <note>A system of planetary periods or "ages" used to predict stages of life.</note> years are 12. His maximum years are 464; his greater years are 57; his middle years are 43 and a half; and his minor years are 30. His greater years are said to be 57 because they are calculated according to the number of degrees of the **terms** <note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs that belong to specific planets.</note> that fall to him from the degrees of the 12 signs. His middle years are said to be 43 and a half because they are calculated from his greater and minor years

<column-break/>

added together, which make 87, the half of which is 43 and a half. His minor years are calculated from his slow course, since he completes it in 30 years; and from this, his minor years take their number, namely 30. His strength in the quarters of the circle is in the northern parts.

**Messahala** said that regarding the appearance of men, Saturn signifies a man between black and sallow who, when he walks, casts his eyes heavily toward the ground; when he walks, he keeps his feet together and has them curved; having small eyes, dry skin, and being sinewy; having a thin beard on his jaws; thick lips; being cunning, ingenious, a deceiver, and a killer—especially in secret. **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet.</note> said that he signifies a very hairy man with joined eyebrows. Of abstract parts, he possesses the part of strength and stability. He signifies matters of lands and inheritances, and those who oversee works, as well as boldness, labor, ingenuity, and the causes of death. **Adila** <note>Likely a reference to a specific astrological authority or a corrupted name of a source like Al-Kindi or similar.</note> said Saturn makes a man dusky, with thin hair in his beard, ugly, frequently working in water, heavy, lazy, and a man who never laughs. Those whom Saturn holds subject—that is, those for whom he is the significator—often suffer from fissures in the heels which the common people call **radias** <note>Cracks or "rays" in the skin of the heels.</note>. He makes a man of a grayish-blue color, sometimes with a thin chest, and with hair that is rough and unkempt. He commands them to wear foul garments, preferably black, and to do this until the end; because Saturnines always seem to be sad and to have ill will. Therefore, when you wish to judge anything about any Saturnine person, either in their birth chart or in a question, consider the things mentioned above, and you shall judge according to them.

If someone should ask why Saturn has these significations and exerts these impressions (though this may seem to belong to natural philosophy rather than astrology), the cause can be assigned as follows: the motion of the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars.</note> is found to move from East to West—not as it must be, but as it is naturally suited to be moved. It is said to have an external mover, and as it seemed to some, it is moved by the First Cause. The planets, however, must move from West to East, in the opposite direction to the first motion or the motion of the eighth sphere. They are said to have an internal mover—namely, an Intelligence—as it has appeared to some. From this, discord, contrariety, rebellion, and enmity must arise, from which hatred and malice are accustomed to spring up and rise. Saturn is closer to that contrariety <note>Being the outermost planet, Saturn is closest to the sphere of the fixed stars moving in the opposite direction.</note>; and therefore, more than the others who are remote from that contrariety, he signifies these things.

## Chapter Two concerning what Jupiter signifies.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personified planet Jupiter. Jupiter is depicted as a bearded, crowned king sitting in a chariot pulled by two eagles. **Alchabicius** <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose "Introduction to the Art of Judgments of the Stars" was a standard textbook.</note> said: Jupiter is a masculine, diurnal fortune. He is the significator of substance <note>Wealth or physical property.</note> by nature. This is because substance is an "accident" that happens to the person born after their birth; and because it is the first necessity that occurs to them, so Jupiter is the second planet, being the first in the order of planets after Saturn. Likewise, Jupiter is...

...he [God or Nature] made two planets that exercise their influence during conception, attributing to the child spirit and life. And he <note>Jupiter</note> works through his nature of heat and moisture, which is a tempered, airy, and sanguine <note>associated with the "blood" humor, signifying a cheerful and active temperament</note> mixture. Regarding age, he signifies youth up until the perfection of age which is called full maturity: and this is from the 14th year, or from the 21st until the 40th or 45th year. Regarding professions, he governs those pertaining to the law and judging justly and honestly. He also has the inclination, when he sees people quarreling or litigating among themselves, to bring peace between them, to cast out discord from them, and to always strive for good things. He also signifies an abundance of substance <note>wealth or material goods</note>. And he governs those businesses which are conducted without deception. He signifies the soul, the clerical life, religion, truth, patience, and every good, beautiful, and precious precept, and whatever pertains to honesty. He also signifies an abundance of Venus <note>here meaning physical pleasure or fertility</note>. Regarding illnesses, he signifies whatever comes from an increase of blood, provided the increase is not so excessive that it destroys one's nature, nor from burnt or corrupt blood. He is the planet of wisdom, intellect, and good conduct. If Jupiter is well-disposed and positioned in the East and in an "angle" <note>a powerful position in an astrological chart</note>, the person born will be of good quality, benign, and just; he will honor his elders, and be healthy and righteous, a helper of the needy, of good reputation, a lover of friends, and of good intellect. But if Jupiter should be unfortunate <note>ill-placed</note>, according to Ptolemy, the person born will be ignorant of how to do good: accustomed to diabolical works, he will study under the guise of hypocrisy; he will linger in places of prayer but prefer to live as a solitary in crypts, caves, and dark places; and on such occasions he might predict the future. He will love no one, and although he may have friends, he will have none in truth; he will loathe his children, flee from the company of men, and desire no honor from anyone. He will be unfaithful, no one will be able to trust him, and he will also be evil, weak, foolish, hardworking, and of wicked choices.

### On his combination with Saturn and other planets.

If he is joined with Saturn, it signifies the knowledge of necromancy, the magic arts, incantations, exorcisms, and the like. When Mars is joined with him, it signifies the science of medicine and especially surgery. When the Sun is joined with him, it signifies the knowledge of religious sects, and prudence in arguments and disputations; he will know how to defend the right faith and attack heretics of faith and the arts; he will not allow a false conclusion to be forced upon him, and in all things he will be a good and orderly debater, not a talkative one. And if Venus is joined with him, it signifies the composition of sounds and other delightful sciences. For the person born will be a lute player, a singer of joys, and wise in musical instruments. When Mercury is joined with him, it signifies the science of arithmetic and all things pertaining to numbers, and the science of writing beyond other scribes if he wishes to study it, and philosophy—namely astronomy—and all the other sciences of the *quadrivium* <note>The four mathematical arts: arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy</note>. When the Moon is joined with him, it signifies the science of the management of waters and their measurement, and of lands, and swimming, and the channeling of rivers and similar things. Regarding the quality of the mind, he signifies generosity, modesty, and justice. Regarding sects, he signifies plurality and simulation: for the person of whom Jupiter is the **significator** <note>The planet representing the person in a chart</note> will, when the Moon is joined to him, pretend to want to hold this sect and that one, and will keep neither well; yet his intention will not be evil. And the authorities Japhar and Guellius <note>likely referring to Abu Ma'shar and another Arabic source</note> said that he signifies the liver, the stomach, the left ear, the arms, and the belly—specifically from the navel downward and the lower parts of the pubic region—and he signifies the intestines. Among colors, he governs green and those similar to it. And among flavors

<column-break/>

he signifies sweet flavors. The quantity of his **orb** <note>The area of influence surrounding a planet's position</note> is nine degrees. Among days, he has Thursday, and among nights, he has the one that precedes Monday <note>Sunday night</note>. His **firdaria** years <note>A system of planetary periods governing different stages of life</note> are 12. His maximum years are 428; his Greater years are 79; his Mean years are 45 and a half; his Minor years are 12. The strength of his circle is in the West. They say his Greater years are 79 because they consider them according to the quantity of the degrees of the **terms** <note>specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> which belong to him in his own terms out of the degrees of the 12 signs. His Mean years are said to be 45 and a half because they consider the number that comes from the sum of his Greater and Minor years, which is 91, which when halved results in 45 and a half. His Minor years are considered according to his course in the **eccentric** <note>an off-center circular path in ancient astronomy</note> which he completes in 12 years; and from this his Minor years draw their number, namely 12. And Messahala <note>an influential 8th-century Jewish-Arab astrologer</note> said that regarding the appearance of men, he signifies a white-skinned man having eyes that are not entirely black, an uneven and short nose, bald, having some blackness in his teeth, of beautiful stature, of good mind, good morals, and a beautiful body. And Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> said he has large eyes with a wide pupil and a curly beard. Among "parts," he has the Part of Happiness and Profit. He signifies faith and an appetite for good things. Among works, he signifies health, security, and participation. Among regions, he governs Cairo, Babylon, and... <margin>Spain</margin>. And the Priest said that Jupiter makes a man good and honest, giving him a round beard, beautiful eyes, and two front teeth larger than the others and sometimes a little separated; in the face of this man, the color is golden mixed with white; he likes to wear beautiful clothing, has somewhat long and beautiful hair, has the appearance of a religious person, and looks at the ground while walking.

## Chapter three: on what Mars signifies.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting the god Mars. He is shown as a bearded warrior in armor, sitting in a chariot drawn by two horses. He holds a sword aloft in his right hand and a round shield in his left. Above the chariot is the astrological symbol for Mars (♂). To the left of the symbol is a star, and below the symbol are small representations of the zodiac signs Aries (♈) and Scorpio (♏).</image-desc>

Alchabitius <note>The 10th-century author of this treatise</note> says Mars is a masculine, nocturnal, and malefic planet; he works through his nature of heat and immoderate dryness, which is fiery, choleric, and of a bitter flavor. He is the natural significator of brothers and of journeys. Because of this, Mars is naturally the significator of brothers because brothers are the third "accident" that happens to the born person after conception—that is, after birth—and whom the born person loves most among those they first encounter; likewise, Mars is the third planet in the order of the planets, following Saturn as the third in their order. And the son <note>referring to Mars's place in the sequence</note> Mars is the third planet who exercises his operation in conception, namely by working in it through the blood and making it red. He is the significator of journeys because in journeys many inconveniences, many anxieties, robberies, and impious labors happen to travelers, and similar things which are likened to... <note>referring to the age range</note> from the 22nd year until the 45th, so that both are included. Among professions, he signifies every craft that is performed with iron, and he signifies striking iron with a hammer...

...[hammers] upon the anvil or in another way, and to practice brass works: and to practice the work of smiths, furnace-tenders, butchers, barbers, and the like.

### On his combination with Saturn and other planets.

If he <note>Mars</note> is joined with Saturn, he signifies the work of smiths that is done from iron only: and especially the iron tools with which the work of the fields is performed, such as hoes, <term>motoria</term> <note>likely heavy moving tools or levers</note>, plowshares, and similar things.

If however he is joined with Jupiter, he signifies the works of smiths which are made of brass and lead, such as works of pewter and the like.

But if the Sun is joined to him, he signifies the works of craftsmen which are made from gold not previously worked, such as <term>besants</term> <note>original: "bizantij"; gold coins from the Byzantine Empire</note>, Augustan limits, golden florins, medals of Massannicine <note>likely referring to a specific mint or region</note>, and every other work from raw gold.

And if Venus is joined to him, he signifies the works of craftsmen which are made for the ornaments of women, such as rings, necklaces, and the like.

And if Mercury is joined to him, he signifies the works of craftsmen which are made for sewing things together and for joining them together, such as awls, needles, and the like.

If indeed the Moon is joined to him, he signifies the crafting works through which scales, lances, balances, mixing bowls, silver cups, and vessels are made with which drink is measured in taverns: and with which people drink in the courts of the wealthy, and the like.

### On his significance when he is the sole significator.

And when he is the sole significator, he signifies the work of medicine, both surgery and the other parts of medicine. Indeed, if no other planet combines with him, he signifies the work of medicine that is performed by the opening of veins, such as <term>phlebotomy</term> <note>bloodletting</note>, the opening of abscesses, the drying of wounds, and similar things.

And Alchabitius <note>a 10th-century Arab astrologer and mathematician</note> said that when Saturn is combined with him, he signifies the medical work of wounds and the like.

And when Jupiter is combined with him, he signifies the work of natural things and the care of the eyes.

And if Venus is combined with him, he signifies the work of ornament which belongs to barbers, such as the cutting of hair and beards and the trimming of nails.

And if Mercury is combined with him, he signifies the cutting of veins.

And when the Moon is combined with him, he signifies the pulling of teeth, the cleaning of ears, and the like.

And when he is the significator by himself, he signifies the injuries of the wretched and that he will willingly harm those of lower status, as well as the shedding of blood, wounds, killings, burnings, decapitations, insults, thieves, tavern-keepers, daylight robbers, the proud, liars, mockers of the pious, and forgers of both money and documents. He signifies oppressions through force by harming whomever he can, as well as wrath, the blocking of roads, haste, the leadership of armies, shamelessness, and <unclear>lenitate</unclear> <note>possibly leniency or a typo for levity/frivolity</note>. Nor will he be ashamed of any evil he has done. He also signifies pilgrimages outside his land and outside his own country, and an abundance of sexual intercourse.

And if he is in a state of "ill-being" <note>poorly positioned in the sky</note> and is the significator of a woman, she will miscarry: and sometimes she herself will be to blame for that miscarriage.

He also signifies middle brothers and the knowledge and discernment of the care of beasts; for he will be an <term>archimandrica</term> <note>literally a leader of a fold; here meaning a master of livestock or a veterinarian</note>.

And among illnesses, he signifies hot fevers—specifically those which arise from <term>choler</term> <note>yellow bile, the humor associated with fire and aggression</note> that is not burnt and occurs without cause—as well as true frenzy <note>inflammation of the brain</note> and false frenzy. He also signifies bloody pustules, <term>impetigo</term> <note>a skin infection</note>, <term>albaras</term> <note>a skin condition, possibly leprosy or vitiligo</note>, and accidental rednesses which occur in the body unnaturally with roughness and foulness. He governs itching, freckles, and sicknesses that eat the flesh of the body such as the "royal disease" <note>jaundice or scrofula</note>, cancer, and the like. He also signifies migraines, "sacred fire" <note>St. Anthony's Fire or erysipelas</note>, and similar things.

And he also signifies that the person born will eat rotten and poorly cooked meats.

And he signifies fears and horrible thoughts disturbing men, which move and hinder them and

<column-break/>

render them empty. And he signifies whatever is accompanied by the inflammation of heat. Among the qualities of the soul, he signifies commotion and its disturbance.

### On his combination with Saturn.

If he is joined with Saturn, he signifies hatred and the greatest envy, and the person born will be very envious. He will rejoice and be glad when he sees evil, some tribulation, or some loss happen to someone. Among religious sects, he will love that in which there is discord and war, and he will willingly cling to it. He will quickly change from sect to sect and from one faith to another; nor will he persevere well in any of them unless perhaps by chance by constraining his own will. He will be consumed by hesitation and by changing with speed from one obligation to another, just as some people do who always hold onto debts and remain entangled in them, not knowing how to free themselves; rather, when they avoid one and are freed from it, they fall into another. When they want to satisfy one of their creditors, they borrow from another and always remain wrapped up in them and in distress for that reason. Now they do this, now they destroy that same thing; they change their wills and make others, and never stay long nor persevere in the same purpose. Yet all these things will be under a single nature.

And Alchafat and Albubeter <note>Abu Bakr al-Hasan, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that from the members of the body he governs the gallbladder, the kidneys, the veins, the flow of sperm, and the back. From colors he has redness, and from flavors, bitterness. The size of his "orb" <note>the range of his influence</note> is 8 degrees. Of the days he has Tuesday, and of the nights he has that which precedes Saturday <note>Friday night</note>.

His <term>firdaria</term> <note>a system of planetary periods governing stages of life</note> years will be seven. His Martian years are 284, and his greater years are 66. His middle years are 40 and a half, and his lesser years are 15.

His greater years are called 66 because they are calculated according to the number of degrees that fall to him from the 12 signs for his "terms" <note>subdivisions of the zodiac signs</note>. The middle years are called 40 and a half because they are calculated as half the sum of the greater and lesser years (which is 81). The lesser years are calculated differently, because he circles his <term>epicycle</term> 8 times in 15 years, and from this they took their name—namely 15—because he does this in no other number of years. His strength is in the southern regions.

And Messahala <note>an 8th-century Jewish-Arab astrologer</note> said that regarding the appearances of men, he signifies a man with a red face and red hair: a round face: easily shamed: having saffron-yellow eyes: horrible in appearance: bold: and having a mark or spot on his foot.

And Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, 1st-century astrologer</note> said that he signifies a man sharp in appearance. Among regions he governs Jerusalem and the land of the Romans as far as the west. Among "parts" <note>astrological points</note> he has the Part of Boldness. And he said that he signifies perseverance, the agreement of the mind, love, heat, pride, boldness, denial, and sharpness and haste in all things.

Adila <note>possibly a corruption of an Arabic source name</note> said: Mars gives a man a curved and thick body, and he will make a man <term>phasmatic</term> <note>likely meaning a spreader of illusions or a visionary</note>, that is, one who sows discord and strife among men. The color on his face is red mixed with black—that is, "Martian"—so that it might be called a twofold color, like those who go out into the sun and heat so that it is neither truly black nor truly red, but a horrible color. Sometimes he has red spots on his face and sparse hair in his beard, almost like eunuchs.

# Chapter four on what the Sun signifies.

<image-desc>A square woodcut illustration of the Sun featuring a human face. The Sun has sixteen rays, alternating between straight and wavy. It is set against a background of stars and small clouds, and the entire image is enclosed in a thin double-line border.</image-desc>

**A**lchabicius <note>original: "alchabicius"; the 10th-century Arab astrologer Al-Qabisi, whose work was a standard textbook in medieval Europe</note> said the Sun is a masculine, daytime planet, and a <term>fortune</term> <note>a "fortune" or "benefic" is a planet believed to have a positive or lucky influence</note> when viewed by aspect; however, through a physical conjunction <note>when another planet is positioned very close to the Sun, known as being "combust"</note> he works evil, causing heat and dryness by his nature. He is the natural significator of fathers if the birth occurs during the day. For this reason, the Sun is the natural significator of fathers because the fourth house of the zodiac signifies fathers, and the Sun is the fourth planet from Saturn, following him in the order of the spheres—being the third after him—and also because he is the fourth planet to exert his influence upon a conceptus <note>a developing embryo</note>. That is, he works upon it through natural heat or something similar, giving spirit and the functional limbs to the conceptus, providing the soul and the act of bringing it to life. And he represents those things which a person values above others (aside from brothers), regarding things that might happen to him before having children, with the aforementioned exceptions, and after birth. He is known to signify light, splendor, beauty, as well as intellect and faith. He also signifies a great kingdom and all high secular dignities, both of great nobles and others. This is because he is placed in the middle of the other planets like a king, and the others stand next to him: some on one side and some on the other. The "superior" planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note> are on his right, and the "inferior" planets <note>Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</note> are on his left. He has power over all planets because he "burns" them all <note>the astrological concept of combustion, where a planet's power is overwhelmed by the Sun's proximity</note>. Furthermore, his motion is essentially uniform; he does not vary or change but always keeps the same pace year after year. His motion is the most noble compared to the motions of other planets, nor does he ever move backward <note>retrograde</note> as the others do. ¶ But you might say that the Moon does not move backward either, which is true; however, although she does not move backward, she does experience such slowness that it can almost be equated to backward motion. You might also say that the Moon sometimes eclipses the Sun. To this, it must be said that the Moon also sometimes signifies kingdoms and magistracies, and she does so naturally. Yet the Sun holds a certain prerogative over the Moon: namely, because the Moon is not a shining or luminous body herself, but rather receives whatever light or splendor she has from the Sun. For this reason, she gives back less and hinders less. Why this is so, some—or rather many—clothed in fine robes <note>original: "tunicati"; likely referring to the pretentiously learned or those in religious habits who lacked true scientific understanding</note> do not dare to say; they rise up against those wishing to use true reason and causes consistent with truth, which they themselves are ignorant of. The wise among them, however, are not ignorant of it, nor do they reproach astrologers; rather, they commend and love them. But the foolish among them would say it is heresy, not even knowing what heresy is. Regarding the ages of man, the Sun signifies the end of youth, which is from the 45th year until the 60th. He participates with all the planets in the arrangement of the years. He rules over mastery, kingdoms, governments, and princedoms. He also signifies those who know well how to throw spears and hurl javelins, and hunting—specifically the kind of hunting done by means of poisoning, as 

<column-break/>

some do who poison the arrows with which they kill wild beasts. He also signifies the purging of the body with every kind of medicine that cleanses the bodies of men internally and externally. Among illnesses, he signifies hot and dry diseases appearing in the bodies of men. Regarding substances, he signifies a great deal of gold, especially in its raw state. Alchabicius said that he signifies all types of substance. Regarding the qualities of the mind, he signifies loftiness and subtlety, as well as those things that follow: honesty, generosity, glory, and a broadness of mind. Among religious sects, he signifies good worship and similar things. Alchabicius also said he signifies the command of the voice and the strength of speed.

### On his significance with Saturn and other planets.

**W**hen he is joined with Saturn, he signifies stewardship <note>the management of an estate</note> and similar types of leadership. If he is joined with Jupiter, he signifies leadership in faith and religion, and also signifies every judgment among men, judging the works of the lowly or those oppressed by the powerful. When he is joined with Mars, he signifies the leadership of armies and the investigation of wars, for the person born under this will excel in these things. When Venus is joined to him, it signifies a kingdom obtained through service to the powerful and through women. If, however, Mercury is joined to him, he signifies counselors to kings and those who labor over great books, works, and inheritances. And if the Moon is joined to him, he signifies the work of envoys, the discoveries of philosophers, and things similar to these. Guelius and Atabari said that the Sun signifies the image of a man's face: specifically the right eye for men and the left eye for women. Ben and Alboali <note>Abū 'Alī al-Khayyāt, a famous student of Mash'allah</note> said that among the body parts he signifies the marrow and the lungs <note>original: "fimoꝝ"; likely a transcription error for "pulmonum"</note>. Among illnesses, he signifies those that occur in the mouth, such as cancers and others that eat away the flesh of the mouth, and every defect of the mouth, as well as the "falling of water into the eye" <note>likely cataracts</note>. His power and strength are centered in the head. The Indians said that when he is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, he will be burning, and the person for whom he is the significator will have a mark on their face. Among colors, he has a changing color that seems to share in every color, though according to some, he signifies the color white. Among tastes, he is sharp or pungent. Among days, he has Sunday, and among nights, the one that precedes Thursday <note>Wednesday night</note>. The size of his <term>orb</term> <note>the range of degrees within which a planet's influence is felt</note> is 15 degrees, both in front and behind. Understand this regarding the orbs of all planets. His <term>firdaria</term> <note>a system of planetary periods governing blocks of time in a person's life</note> years are ten. His greatest years are 461, though according to some, if he exceeds those, it is a thousand. His "greater" years are 120, because they are calculated according to the number of degrees in the 12 signs. Although the Sun does not have "terms" <note>specific segments of signs assigned to planets</note> assigned through the signs as the five wandering planets do, he still has power in the aforementioned half of the circle of signs (from the beginning of Leo to the end of Capricorn) which the planets have in their own terms, which would be 180 years. But because in that half there are the two houses of the two "infortunes" <note>the "malefic" planets Mars and Saturn</note>, which are Scorpio and Capricorn, 60 years are subtracted—30 for each of those houses—leaving only 120, from which the <term>trine aspect</term> results. His "middle" years are extracted differently than others: his greater years are halved, his lesser years are added to one half, totaling 79; when this is halved, one part makes 39 and a half, and those are the Sun's middle years. His "lesser" years are considered from the number of the degree of his <term>exaltation</term> <note>the sign and degree where a planet is most powerful</note>, as was said above, in the 19th degree of Aries; that is the number of the Sun's lesser years. And his strength is in the parts...

And Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrological poet</note> said the figure of the Sun and Moon is like the figure of the planets that are with them, whichever is more dignified in their location. ¶ If, therefore, you wish to know the figure of the Sun, know that it is saffron-colored, having a portion of redness in the hair, and his eyes are somewhat saffron-colored. And from the regions, he governs Khurasan <note>original: "canacant," likely a corruption of a regional name</note> and Ozacen <note>possibly referring to Uzès or a corruption of an Eastern province</note> and Persia and the land of the Romans. ### ¶ Chapter five on what Venus signifies.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicts the astrological personification of Venus in a chariot. She is seated within a boat-like vessel pulled to the left by two birds, possibly swans or doves. Venus holds an object in her hand, perhaps a mirror. Above the chariot in the corners are celestial bodies: a radiant sun or star on the left and a smaller circular figure on the right. Below the chariot wheels are the astrological symbols for the zodiac signs of Taurus (left) and Libra (right).</image-desc>

Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "Albumasar"; a leading Persian astrologer of the Abbasid court</note> and Al-Qabisi <note>original: "alchabidus"</note> said Venus is a <term>fortune</term> <note>a "benefic" planet that brings good luck</note>: and she is a feminine, nocturnal planet, and she signifies women and wives. And if the birth occurs during the day, as Al-Qabisi says, she signifies mothers. and as the priest says, she signifies younger sisters. And she is the natural significator of children: since children are signified by the fifth house, and Venus is the fifth planet from Saturn, namely the fourth after him, following him in their order. And also because she is the fifth planet who exerts her influence in completing the conceptus <note>the developing embryo</note>, specifically the sex of the male and female, of whichever sex the conceptus may be, and in perfecting that birth, as well as the eyebrows and the entire arrangement of the face. And because Venus is the planet of delight and joy: and the fifth house is similarly attributed to children and signifies them, because children are an event in which the person born rejoices more, and nature delights in them more than in others. ¶ In the treatise on nativities <note>a "nativity" is a birth chart</note>, more will be said at length about what should be said here: however, I will tell you something of them now, since when you wish to know the state of the person born and wish to know what happens to him regarding women—namely the mother, or wives, or younger sisters and the like. Look in the state of the nativity if Venus is the <term>almuten</term> <note>the planet with the most combined astrological strength and dignity at a specific point</note> in the birth; then you should know that things will generally go well for him regarding women. And if she herself is not the significator of the birth because she is not the almuten over it, look how and from where she <term>aspects</term> <note>the geometric angle between planets</note> the Lord of the first house. For if she aspects him from the seventh house by a <term>trine</term> aspect <note>a harmonious 120-degree angle</note>, the person born will be loved by his wives with a perfect love. And if she aspects him from there by a <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>a helpful 60-degree angle</note>, he will be loved by his wives, but not with a perfect love: rather, there will sometimes be altercations and quarrels between them, and sometimes they will love each other: sometimes not; now this way, now that. And if she aspects him from the seventh house by a <term>square</term> aspect <note>a tense 90-degree angle</note>, then the person born will rarely rejoice with his wife; instead, there will often be some quarrels between them, and they will not live well together.

<column-break/>

¶ If, however, she aspects him from an <term>opposition</term> <note>a 180-degree angle, often indicating conflict</note>, the person born will never rejoice with his wife, and they fear this most with the first one, nor will it be well for him because of her: and there will always be brawls and discords between them. ¶ And if Venus aspects the significator of the birth from the tenth house by any of the aforementioned aspects: say that it will be for the person born from his mother just as you said it would be for him from his wife. Since if Venus aspects the significator from the seventh house with a good aspect, say that it will be good for the person born from his mother. If with a bad one, say that it will be bad for him from his mother. ¶ And if Venus aspects the significator of the person born from the fourth house by any of these aspects, say that it will happen to him from his younger sisters according to the aspect by which she viewed him, just as you said concerning the mother. And Venus, by her nature, has the power to produce coldness and moisture with temperance. And she signifies similarly, from the age of man, adolescence and especially in pure youth, which is from the 14th year until the 22nd. And she has the power over the crafts of knowing how to make instruments for games, and toys, and playing at pebbles <note>likely a game similar to marbles or backgammon</note> and playing at dice. ¶ These will be the duties of the one for whom Venus is the significator: and those things which will most closely approach him: and which he himself will know better how to do if he wishes to involve himself in them: and if he involves himself in others, he will neither learn nor know them as well as these. ¶ And he for whom Venus is the significator will be one who spends his time in leisure, and will better know how to lead his life and live more delicately and more courteously than another who might be much worse off than him. And he will be a fornicator and entirely a "son of fornication": and he will willingly practice every Venusian worship <note>referring here to sexual activity or rituals of love</note> and will abound in sexual intercourse, so much so that his nature will be exhausted by others for that reason: and he will know how to compose crowns and garlands and all ornaments: and especially those for women: and he will willingly use ornaments for his own body: and he will go about covered in beautiful and clean garments: and he will know how to work gold and silver and make necklaces: and all such things which pertain to the ornament of the body, and especially those which pertain to the ornaments of women, if he applies himself to those crafts. And this is why some are not permitted to reach the perfection of their crafts or duties, because they use arts and duties that are not theirs naturally: and they never perfectly learn them: and with labor they learn whatever they grasp from them: but those things which pertain to them naturally, they learn easily and well. ¶ And Venusian men are people of games and laughter and dancing, as well as of cheerfulness and joy, and they willingly partake in eating and drinking in moderation, yet the Venusian becomes intoxicated faster than others, and they trust others and are often deceived by them. And Venus signifies delight, generosity, love, and justice and the like. And Venusian people frequent houses of prayer <note>churches or temples</note> so that they may appear to be what they are not, yet they retain faith and desire to hear the sounds of musical instruments and excel in them more than other men.

### ¶ On the combination of Venus with Saturn and other planets.

If she is joined with Saturn, she signifies the sound of songs, of lamentations, and those by which the dead are mourned, as well as those which men use when they are building and such. ¶ If, however, she is joined with Jupiter, it signifies that the person born will be learned in the sounds of readings and ecclesiastical chants, and in every song pertaining to clerics and religious people, and those who use them in houses of prayer and at altars and for the praise of the Lord Jesus Christ.

### Chapter six on what Mercury signifies.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the planet Mercury. A male figure with a winged petasos (hat) and winged sandals sits in a two-wheeled chariot, holding a caduceus. The chariot is pulled to the right by two roosters. The wheels of the chariot contain the astrological symbols for Gemini (left) and Virgo (right). **Alchabicius says** Mercury is a mixed planet, masculine, and diurnal; it is inclined by its nature to those of the planets and signs it is joined with, such that if it joins a good planet, it becomes good; and if it joins a bad one, it becomes bad. If it joins a masculine planet, it is masculine; if a nocturnal one, nocturnal; if a diurnal one, diurnal. And it signifies younger brothers: therefore look into the birth of any native and see how Mercury relates to the lord of the first [house] or the significator of birth: for if Mercury looks upon him from a trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees</note>, it will be well for the native regarding his younger brothers, especially with <term>reception</term> <note>a condition where planets occupy each other's dignities</note>. And if it looks upon him from a square aspect or opposition, it will be bad for them, especially if reception intervenes: as is said of bodily conjunction; you should understand the same regarding its aspects with the Moon. ⸿ And a Mercurial person loves mistresses more than wives and will more willingly cling to them. ⸿ And Mercury signifies judgment and thoughts of love as far as it is from his knowledge, although otherwise he may be lustful in unlawful ways; and he will have good belief and live devotedly in temples and other oratories of churches: and will be of good faith and Catholic opinion. ⸿ And if Mercury alone is the significator of birth and is in its own nature so that no other planet is joined with it or participates with it, the native will be guided by his own sense in the beginning of his youth, and his will and his own pursuits will grow; and this will happen to him in the first ten years of his youth, namely, adolescence. ⸿ And <term>Alchabicius</term> said it signifies earthly things and the increase of things through growth. From age, it has full youth. Among occupations, it signifies those that indicate knowledge of truth and rhetoric: for he will be orderly in his speech. Mercury signifies geometry and the science of trade and the ability to manage many affairs and to involve oneself in many things, bringing them to effect. And he will have knowledge in many matters and will know about things for sale and others where there is profit. ⸿ And if he becomes a cleric, he will be a good and pleasing preacher. ⸿ And <term>Asla</term> said it signifies philosophy, augury, writing, and proverbs: he will be a good moralist; and they say he knows the science of arithmetic. For a Mercurial person will be a good verifier and will work mostly in this.

### Regarding its combination with Saturn and other planets.

**If it is joined with Saturn**, it signifies the work of practicing and measuring lands, and dividing possessions and inheritances among the offspring and heirs of the dead. And the science of counting and estimating what someone needs to build something like a tower and house or something similar. And the science of arranging fabrics like those who weave woolen or linen cloths or <term>pignolata</term> <note>original: "pignolatā"; a type of coarse linen or buckram used in the Middle Ages</note> and similar things. ⸿ When joined with Jupiter, it signifies the work of counting and making melodies for church books and other songs, and he will know without distinction the steps of dances and similar things. ⸿ When joined with Mars, it signifies that the native for whom it is the significator will know how to lead an army and know how to organize them well and pay them their wages and the war and revenues which they ought to receive: and

### Concerning Mercury when he is fortunate.

When Mercury is fortunate, his goodness and fortune will be according to the goodness and fortune of the planet that fortifies him, and according to the place in which he himself is well-disposed. And when he is bad and unfortunate, his malice and misfortune will be according to the nature, being, and misfortune of the planet that makes him unfortunate, and according to the place where he is bad or where he is made unfortunate. ⸿ And Al-Qabisi <note>original: "Alchabicius"; a 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> said that regarding religious sects, he signifies the cultivation of true unity and the law of rational people and those similar; yet he signifies this with hypocrisy and simulation, pretending to be as sweet as honey while not actually being so, though without heresy. ⸿ And Albus and Ebrianus <note>medieval astrological authorities</note> said that regarding the human body, he signifies the navel, thighs, legs, nerves, veins, and arteries. And of colors, he signifies every mixed and varied color. ⸿ And Guelius said that he signifies *aleçeminiũ* <note>original: "aleçeminiũ"; a medieval term for a specific pigment</note>, which is a certain color similar to the color of the wild lily. And of flavors, he signifies the acidic or sour. And the size of his orb is seven degrees. And of the days, he has the day of Mercury <note>Wednesday</note>, and of the nights, the one that precedes the Lord's Day <note>Saturday night/Sunday morning</note>. ⸿ And his firdaria years <note>a system of planetary periods governing life stages</note> are 13. And his major years are 76, his middle years 48, his minor years 20, and his maximum years 460. And they say his major years are 76 because 76 degrees of the 12 signs fall to him as his "terms" <note>specific subdivisions of the zodiac signs</note> according to the number by which they are considered. ⸿ Others are called 48 because they are considered according to the midpoint of the number of his major and minor years added together and divided by two—which is 96, the half of which is 48. ⸿ The minor years are 20 because Mercury is found to make 63 revolutions in his epicycle <note>a small circle moving along the circumference of a larger one in Ptolemaic astronomy</note> in 20 years, which he does not do in any other number of years, and from this they derived that number; he circuits the eccentric circle in almost ten months. ⸿ And Ja'far <note>likely Abu Ma'shar, often called "Iaphar" in Latin</note> said that Mercury, from the middle of his retrogradation <note>when a planet appears to move backward in the sky</note> until his second station, signifies childhood. And from his second station until his physical conjunction with the Sun, he signifies youth, delight, friendship, concord, its establishment, and the imitation of love. And from the conjunction with the Sun until his first station, he signifies old age. And from his first station until the middle of his retrogradation, he signifies decrepitude, contrariety, dissimulation, slowness, and shame ex-

### Chapter seven concerning the Moon and what it signifies.

Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "Albumasar"</note> and Al-Qabisi said the Moon is a feminine, nocturnal fortune; she works through her nature of coldness and moisture and is the significatrix of mothers. Hence, if the birth is at night, she signifies what will happen to the native regarding the mother. Therefore, you must consider how the Moon stands with the significator of the birth: for if she regards him with a good aspect—namely a trine or sextile—or if she receives him with perfect reception <note>an astrological relationship where planets "host" each other in their signs</note>, it will be well for the native through the mother. If, however, she regards him with a bad aspect, it will be ill for him through the mother. And understand the same regarding the mother through the son: because if the significator of the birth receives the Moon well, it will be well for the mother through the native. If, however, he regards her badly without reception, it will be ill for the mother through the native. ⸿ And Al-Qabisi said that there is tempered phlegm <note>one of the four bodily humors</note> in her. ⸿ And she signifies the age of childhood and the beginning of growth...

...scend. <note>original: "scendi", continuing the previous page's discussion of Mercury's influence on those who "descend" into service.</note> For [the Moon governs] the first four years from birth because of its frequent and rapid changes, much like the changing nature of children. And the same philosopher said that from its works it holds embassies, mandates, and the works of waters and lands, as well as the cultivation of the earth, according to the extent of its goodness or its malice. And it signifies sovereignty: namely, the management of the affairs of kings, princes, and magnates if it presides over them and is familiar; in such a case, it is fortunate and in a good aspect with the Sun or the lord of the tenth house <note>the "tenth house" in astrology typically governs career and public standing</note>, namely in a trine or sextile <note>original: "fertili"; a favorable astrological angle of 60 degrees</note> aspect. And regarding substance, it signifies silver. It also signifies fortune in the cultivation of the land if it holds dignity at the hour of birth in the fourth house. Regarding faith, it signifies religion, for lunar people often become religious, especially in their youth; yet sometimes they do not keep their promises to God well, and they rarely persevere in religious orders, often becoming the subjects of common gossip. Regarding infirmities, it signifies epilepsy and twisting of the belly, as well as those pertaining to paralysis, especially partial paralysis, and particularly those afflictions occurring in the tongue, lips, and eyes. It also signifies the commotion of the limbs that arises from certain illnesses, which often happens from cold and moist or phlegmatic diseases. It signifies the quality of the mind according to its mixture with the other planets; for if it is joined with a good planet, the quality of the native's <note>the "native" is the person whose birth chart is being read</note> mind will be good, but if joined with an evil one, it will be bad.

### Concerning the conjunction of the Moon with Saturn and other planets.

When it is joined with Saturn in the birth of any male or female, it signifies that the native will hold people in hatred while pretending to love them, and will be envious; he will rejoice in the losses of others and grieve at their successes, and it will seem to him that every good thing belonging to another is a harm to himself. And if it is joined with Jupiter, it signifies that the native will be cautious, honest, and kind in all things; he will lead a good, beautiful, honorable, and peaceful life, praiseworthy in every way. And if it is joined with Mars, it signifies that the native will be a whisperer <note>a gossip or slanderer</note> and envious; he will study malice and whispering, sowing discord among men in all things that might bring harm to others; nor will he care if he himself has vices, provided he believes them harmful to others—though it is foreseen that "reception" <note>a technical term where planets "host" each other in their respective zodiac signs</note> breaks the aforementioned malice. And if it is joined with the Sun in a trine or sextile aspect without reception, these significations are more perfectly fulfilled; it signifies that the native (or the person asking the question) will involve himself in disposing the royal affairs of magnates, nobles, and the wealthy who are fit for a kingdom. If, however, it is joined with Venus, it signifies that the native will be courtly, kind, sweet, of good spirit, and honest in character; he will be swift, light, and of fast movement; he will be devoted to divine service and will speak no evil of anyone, nor speak with any rudeness through his own fault. If it is joined with Mercury with reception, it signifies that the native will be an eloquent orator who adheres to scripture and rhetoric; he will be orderly in all his speech and in all his writing, whether in meter or prose. If it is joined without reception in a trine or sextile aspect, he will be somewhat below this. If, however, it is in a square aspect <note>an angle of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note> or opposition, he will be talkative and pour out many vain and useless words; he will not wish to give others a turn to speak and will interrupt their words, yet will not want his own to be interrupted. And Velicus and Albuam <note>likely referring to the Arabic astrologer Albumasar</note> said that it signifies thought, a novelty of spirit, a weakness of wit and sense, a heaviness of the tongue, and honest women. Therefore, you must consider in the nativities of

<column-break/>

women whether the Moon is joined to Mercury as has been said, for it then signifies that the woman will be honest, good, and of a good spirit; she will gladly nurse children and will be fortunate in this, acting as an assistant to those in labor <note>a midwife</note>; it also signifies mothers, aunts, and those who provide food, for she will know how to provide food for the native and others. And Thoz the Greek <note>likely Hermes or Thabit ibn Qurra</note> and Albuaz said that it then specifically signifies the lungs and the brain. Regarding colors, it signifies yellow. Regarding tastes, it signifies saltiness <note>original: "falsum", likely a scribal error for "salsum"</note>. Among women, it signifies the right eye, and among men, the left. Thus you must consider in nativities if the Moon is impeded <note>afflicted by a "bad" planet</note>; for it signifies an impediment of the eye, which happens most when it is impeded in Aries: in men it hinders the left, and in women the right. Either the person will be born with a hindered eye, or the eye will be hindered before their natural death by an inseparable impediment; sometimes the native will lose the eye entirely. Among the days, it holds Monday; and among the nights, that which precedes Friday. The size of its orb is 12 degrees. Its *firdaria* <note>planetary periods used to predict life stages</note> years are nine. Its lesser years are 25; its middle years are 39 and a half. Some have wished to say it is 66, but I see no reason to agree with their opposition. Its greater years are 108, and its greatest are 420. Its greater years are said to be 108 because it holds those virtues in that half of the circle of signs from the beginning of Aquarius to the end of Cancer which other planets have in their terms, which would be 180; but 60 are subtracted because of the two houses of the two misfortunes <note>Saturn and Mars</note> which are Aquarius and Aries; and another 12 years are subtracted because that half-circle diminishes in its elevations from the beginning of the first climate to the end of the seventh climate, which is attributed to the Moon—12 degrees, whereby only 108 remain. The middle years are said to be 39 and a half for the same reason the middle years of the Sun are calculated, and the aforementioned 12 degrees are not subtracted then. The lesser years are 25 for this reason: when the Moon is at the end of the 25th degree of Aries, which belongs to both luminaries <note>Sun and Moon</note>, it touches the 19th degree of Aries, which is the exaltation of the Sun, and it touches the third degree of Taurus, which is its own exaltation; because of the subtraction of the aforementioned 12 years from its greater years, it adds half of those years to the lesser years of the Sun, and thus they become 25 years. Its strength in the parts of the world is in the right side of the West.

### Concerning the forms which the Moon signifies.

<margin>Forms <image-desc>crescent moon symbol</image-desc></margin>
Messahala <note>an influential 8th-century Jewish-Arab astrologer</note> said that regarding the figures of men, it signifies a white man mixed with redness, with snowy eyebrows, being benevolent, having eyes that are not entirely large, a round face, and a handsome stature. Regarding lands, it signifies Artore, Exthoma, and Adila <note>place names from medieval geography/astrology</note>. The Priest said the Moon makes a man to be of no service, because he desires to go hither and thither day and night, wandering about; nor does he remain stable anywhere with ease; this is true if the Moon itself is slow in its course at birth without perfect reception and is joined to a planet of swift course, especially one of the lower planets. And it is said a lunar man has a round face and medium height. There is, however, a greater alteration in the eyes, or he is struck in the eye. And it is said he is a cross-eyed man or one with altogether higher eye sockets. To tell you the truth briefly, one of the eyes will in no way be without a defect. And Sardinator said in a certain treatise of his: the Moon signifies from the beginning of its new moon until seven days its years of childhood, and from the 7th day until the 14th it signifies the years of youth...

...age 14 up to 21 signifies the years of youth; and from 21 until the end of the month <note>original: "mensis", referring here to the lunar cycle</note> it signifies the years of elderly age. And when the Moon is "under the rays of the Sun" <note>an astrological term meaning the planet is too close to the Sun to be seen, usually within 15 degrees</note>, it signifies secrets and hidden things; it also signifies things that ought to remain concealed. Therefore, this is a good time to handle and perform those things that are meant to be hidden: namely, those things we wish to keep from the public before the Moon separates from the Sun. When there are 15 degrees between the body of the Moon and the opposition of the Sun, it signifies the beginning of opposition and its cause. ### On the significance of the Moon in the fourth aspect of the Sun.

<margin>Alchabitius</margin> **Alchabitius** said that if the Moon is in the "fourth aspect" <note>the square aspect, or 90 degrees</note> of the Sun, it signifies a descent from a high position to a low one, as often happens to those who hold great dignities and high magistracies and are deposed from them unwillingly and with reproach. The same happens in the second fourth aspect <note>the waning square</note>; indeed, the second fourth aspect is worse than the first. For although the first signifies a lessening of status, it still signifies the appearance of things and profit and an increase in restraint; but in the second fourth aspect, it signifies <unclear>ruin</unclear>.

### On the significance of the Moon from conjunction until the middle of its light.

<margin>Ptol. Arthe. Zar.</margin> **Ptolemy**, **Arthephius**, and **Zarchaphalan** <note>Reference to the famous astronomer Al-Zarqali</note>—who have been found to be most capable in this science—have said that from the Moon's conjunction with the Sun <note>the New Moon</note> until the middle of its light <note>First Quarter</note>, its nature will be humidity, for then it signifies moisture. From the middle of its light until its fullness <note>Full Moon</note>, its nature will be heat, for then it signifies warmth. From its fullness until the second middle of its light <note>Last Quarter</note>, its nature is dryness. And from the second middle of its light, its nature will be coldness. They also said that the remaining planets—namely **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**—from their rising until their first station <note>when a planet appears to stop before turning retrograde</note> will be of a humid nature and signify youth: namely, that which is from age 14 to 41. And from

<column-break/>

their first station until their opposition to the Sun, when they are in the middle of their retrogradation, they are of a hot nature, for then they signify heat; and they signify that "perfect age": namely, from age 41 to 62. From their opposition to the Sun—that is, when they are in the middle of their retrogradation—until their second station, they are of a dry nature, for then they signify dryness (though not a "true" dryness); and they signify that old age: namely, from age 62 to 90. From their second station until their concealment under the rays of the Sun, they will be of a cold nature, for then they signify coldness; and they signify that "seniority" or decrepitude: namely, from age 90 until the end of a man's life, which can sometimes be up to 120 years; few are found who transcend this, though some may claim otherwise. Furthermore, the "inferior" planets—namely **Venus** and **Mercury**—from the middle of their furthest distance until their first station signify what the Moon signifies in the first half of its light. From their first station until the middle of their closest distance, they signify what the Moon signifies from the middle of its light until its fullness. From the middle of their closest distance until their second station, they signify what the Moon signifies from its fullness until the second middle of its light. And from their second station until the middle of their furthest distance, they signify what the Moon signifies from the second middle of its light until its conjunction with the Sun. **The Sun**, however, signifies childhood from the beginning of **Aries** to the end of **Gemini**. From the beginning of **Cancer** to the end of **Virgo**, it signifies youth. From the beginning of **Libra** to the end of **Sagittarius**, it signifies mature age. From the beginning of **Capricorn** to the end of **Pisces**, it signifies old age. **Arthephius** and **Argafala** said that the Sun signifies the *soul* and the Moon signifies *thought*. Therefore, you must consider in a person's birth if the Sun is well-disposed and in a good place relative to the ascendant: for this signifies that their soul will be naturally benevolent. If it is ill-disposed and in a malignant place, it signifies that their soul will be naturally malevolent; however, by chance, they may be able to constrain and correct that evil will through their own free choice, as happens sometimes and often in these religious orders and among religious people, and also among other discreet persons who recognize their own malevolence. If the Moon is well-disposed (as was said of the Sun), the thoughts of the person born will be on good things and directed toward the good. If it is ill-disposed, their thoughts will be evil, dwelling on and directed toward evil. They also said that **Saturn** signifies sorrow, sadness, weeping, lamentation, labor, and evil. **Jupiter** signifies wisdom, reason, honesty, and good. **Mars** signifies anger, fury, conflict, and change for the worse rather than the better. **Venus** signifies delight, play, joy, and cheerfulness. **Mercury** signifies rationality, discretion, logic, and discipline. And the **Moon** is called the "pedagogue" <note>teacher or guide</note> and is said to have significance over every thing, participating with every planet in births, questions, journeys, and the beginnings, middles, and ends of all things; for she is the mediatrix <note>middle-man or intermediary</note> between the heavens, the other planets, and the elements. And although the heavens or celestial bodies act upon the elements, this always happens by means of the Moon; because she is located between the other planets and the elements, the elements cannot be corrupted or changed by them or any one of them unless that changing or altering power passes through her rays or through her power.

# Chapter eight: On the Head and Tail of the Dragon and what they signify.

<image-desc>A circular woodcut illustration featuring a winged, two-legged dragon-like creature curled into a circle, biting its own tail (Ouroboros). In the center of the circle are two smaller circles, possibly representing astronomical nodes.</image-desc>

The Head of the Dragon <note>original: "Caput draconis", also known as the North Node, the point where the Moon's orbit crosses the Sun's path moving northward</note> is naturally a benefic <note>a "fortune" or positive influence</note> and of a masculine nature; but by accident it sometimes becomes a malefic <note>an "infortune" or negative influence</note>. For its nature is composed of the nature of Jupiter and the nature of Venus. It possesses the power of increase and signifies things that undergo growth, such as kingship, dignities, substance, high status, and good fortune. And the authorities Adila and Argafalan <note>likely references to Arabic astrological authorities such as Al-Andarzaghar or similar figures</note> said that the specific property of the Head is to increase, except in the granting of years; for it diminishes a twelfth part of them when it is joined with a significator. Therefore, when it is with the benefics, it increases their good fortune; and when it is with the malefics, it increases their malice—and then it becomes a malefic by accident. Its years of the *firdaria* <term>firdaria: a system of planetary periods where each planet governs a specific number of years in a person's life</term> are 3.

Its Tail <note>original: "Cauda draconis", the South Node</note> is naturally evil and of a feminine nature; but by accident it sometimes becomes a benefic. Its nature is composed of the nature of Saturn and Mars. It signifies diminution, namely dejection, downfall, poverty, and the lessening of every good thing and every fortune. And the same philosophers said that the property of the Tail is to diminish: when it is with benefics, it lessens their fortune; and when it is with malefics, it lessens their malice—and then its "fortune" occurs by accident. Thus it is said that the Head is a benefic with the good and evil with the bad; the Tail, however, is evil with the good and good with the bad. Its years of the *firdaria* are 2.

# Chapter nine: What each of the planets performs in the conception of children.

I will set down here some things regarding what the planets perform in the conception of children. For in the first month, the authority said that Saturn coagulates the matter and constricts and dries it, yet without parching it. Therefore, if Saturn is well-disposed <note>astrologically well-placed in a favorable sign or house</note>, then the composition of that conceived child will be well-ordered and well-disposed, so that any of the other planets can well perform what belongs to them in the conception according to their own being and disposition. If, however, Saturn is then poorly disposed, the compaction or gathering of the matter of the conceived child will be poorly disposed, and the form or arrangement of that conception can never be well-ordered, even if the other planets are well-disposed.

In the second month, Jupiter bestows the spirit and the limbs; therefore, if Jupiter is then well-disposed and of good essence, the limbs of the conceived child will be well-arranged and well-ordered, formed everywhere in a natural way, and its spirit and its breath will be good; it will breathe in and out sweetly and well without labor or impediment to respiration. If, however, Jupiter is of an evil essence and poorly disposed, it will be the opposite.

In the third month, Mars works upon it through the blood, making it red and bringing it into the form of blood. Therefore, if Mars is then well-disposed and of good essence, the blood of the conceived child will be good and pure, well-nourishing the body of the conceived child; and only rarely

<column-break/>

will it be overabundant so as to cause injury, except perhaps on account of an irregular life which might affect the force of nature. If, however, Mars is then poorly disposed, it will be the opposite.

In the fourth month, the Sun gives or perfects the more principal members <note>the vital organs</note> and gives heat to the limbs and strengthens the natural heat, increasing it and rectifying it for the carrying out of all its operations. Therefore, if the Sun is then well-disposed, the natural heat of the conceived child will be good and useful, well-preserving its nature and completing all its operations well, and very rarely allowing itself to be overcome by unnatural heat; it will be long-lasting in the body of the person born. If indeed the Sun is then poorly disposed, it will be the opposite.

In the fifth month, Venus perfects by command the ears, nose, eyebrows, and the entire arrangement of the face, as well as the testicles, and she aids the operations of the other planets. Therefore, if Venus is then well-disposed, the child after its birth will be charming, having beautiful eyes, beautiful eyebrows, a beautiful nose, beautiful ears, and a whole facial arrangement blessed with cheerfulness. If, however, Venus is then poorly disposed, it will be the opposite.

In the sixth month, Mercury composes the kidneys, the tongue, and the lungs, and perfects all the openings and all the hollows of the body not yet completed; and all these are completed according to the disposition of Mercury.

In the seventh month, the Moon opens all the passages of the lungs and perfects them if anything was lacking; she also perfects the windpipe, the arteries, and the uvula; she then divides by her own limits all the members of the body not yet divided. Therefore, if she is then well-disposed, all these will be fit, each of them for the office assigned to it. If, however, she is poorly disposed, it will be the opposite. And this is the cause—that is, the impediment of the Moon—why certain children are born hindered <note>physically disabled or impaired</note> in some part of their body. For this happens because of the affliction of the Moon; and those hindrances occur in that member which is assigned to the zodiac sign in which the Moon was then afflicted. And if it was in the first half of the sign, it signifies that the hindrance will occur on the right side of the child. If, however, it was in the last half, it will happen on the left side of the child. 

And because in seven months every planet has worked its virtue into the conception, if a child is born then, it can by right be viable <note>original: "vitalis", able to survive</note>. And I have seen many who were born at the end of seven months after conception and lived for a long time; indeed, my father was one of those, as his mother asserted that he lived to 107 <unclear>years</unclear>. 

After this, the governance returns to Saturn, who in the eighth month solidifies the infant's limbs with his coldness and constricts and thickens them. Thus it happens that if a child is born then, it does not live; and this occurs because of the imbalance of Saturn's coldness acting upon the child's disposition.

In the ninth month, however, Jupiter reigns, who then, by separating the infant's limbs with his temperate nature, leads it out safely from the womb after the placenta <note>original: "cotilidone"</note> is broken; and thus children who are born then are believed to be viable.

It could then be said that Hermes (to whom Ptolemy agreed) noted that the stays of the conceived in the womb are three: namely, the greater, which consists of 288 days; the middle, which consists of 273 days; and the lesser, which consists of 258 days; yet none of these is divided by any number of the months mentioned above. To which you might respond that Ptolemy and Hermes considered those spans that commonly occur, not considering which children ought to be viable or not, but only the common movements of infants in the womb. They likewise spoke of those who pass the seventh month in movement; nor was their rule so general that it could not be set aside by a specific one. For they could not "cross that path with a dry foot" <note>a metaphor for dealing with a difficult or "sticky" intellectual problem</note>, nor is it the purpose of my interpretation to dispute these things, as it seems they can be reconciled and clarified. But at this point, we must return to the purpose of this work's intention.
