**T**hese are the resolutions of facts concerning the elements and the **material things composed of elements**, which occur because of their extreme proximity to the Earth. For the Moon herself has a smaller circle than any of the other planets. Beneath her circle, no other circle is contained, but only the elements and all other corruptible things. <note>The "corruptible things" refers to the sublunary world where things are born and die, unlike the "eternal" heavens.</note> ¶ If the Moon were indeed the mediator between the stars and the lower things, her circle is contained by the circle of Mercury. ¶ Mercury's circle is contained by the circle of Venus. ¶ Venus's circle is contained by the circle of the Sun. ¶ The Sun's circle is contained by the circle of Mars. ¶ Mars's circle is contained by the circle of Jupiter. ¶ Jupiter's circle is contained by the circle of Saturn. ¶ Saturn's circle is contained by the circle of the fixed stars, beyond which it does not concern the astrologer to involve himself, although it has seemed otherwise to some, a cause which I do not intend to dispute here. For you see that at the **new moon**, the Moon appears small, thin, and meager; then she increases her light and grows little by little until her whole body is illuminated on the side we see, and she reaches the fulfillment of her light. Then her light is diminished little by little and step by step until it comes to nothing. She does the same to the bodies of both rational and irrational beings, and to all plants. For see how men are born: they augment and grow until they are perfected in their determined size; then they diminish and begin to decline, and they continue to decline until their life is ended—and so do all other things. Therefore, the Moon must always be placed as the **significator** <note>In astrology, a "significator" is the planet that represents the person or subject being asked about.</note> of every matter and every beginning, and of every birth. Her "being well" is the "being well" of every matter, and her "being ill" is the "being ill" of every matter. Her virtue and power are so great that if the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> or any other significator of a matter is so hindered that it cannot do or complete what it ought, and she is found to be strong, she will nevertheless complete the matter. For she is the **governess** <note>original: "pedagoga"</note> of all things and is the **carrier** of the virtues of all the planets from one planet to another—that is, from one to another—so that she receives the disposition of one planet and carries it to another. Some have thought she always does this. In this opinion was that **tyrant Ezzelino da Romano** <note>original: "Cillinus de Romano." Ezzelino III da Romano (1194–1259) was a powerful Ghibelline leader and patron of Bonatti.</note>, namely, that when she separates from one planet, she receives its virtue and carries it to another, committing it to the one she finds first. It seems to some that **Haly** <note>original: "Cael," likely referring to the Arabic astrologer Haly Abenragel or Ali ibn Ridwan.</note> said the same thing, but Haly’s intention was not absolute. For he believed that the Moon would carry that which was committed to her, and if it were not committed to her, she would not carry anything to anyone, an opinion with which I agree. ¶ For when the Moon joins a planet that "receives" her, then that planet commits its disposition to her, and she carries it with her and commits it to the one she first finds in another of her strengths, and to no other. According to this: **a planet gives nothing in a place where it promises nothing.**

**C**onsideration 10 is to look for the **fixed stars** that help or harm, about which it is spoken in the treatise on revolutions in its proper place and time; they have much work to do regarding judgments and often lead an astrologer into error.

**C**onsideration 11 is to look at and consider the **malefic planets** and see what they signify. For **Saturn** and **Mars**, as I told you above, are naturally "bad" or "evil." Saturn is so because of his excess of cold, while Mars is so because of the excess of heat winning or dominating in them—not because either of them is truly hot or cold in their essence, but they have this in their power, and that is their effect. Because of this, they signify evil, detriment, and hindrance in matters, unless they receive the "malice" of the significator or the Moon from their house, or from their exaltation, or from two of their minor dignities, or if they themselves are the significators of the evil; for then they restrain all their

<column-break/>

malice from the one whom they receive, nor do they hinder him by whatever **aspect** <note>The geometric angle between two planets.</note> they look upon him, though it is better if by a **trine** or **sextile** <note>original: "fertili." Friendly geometric angles of 120 and 60 degrees.</note>. If, however, they do not receive him, their malice is magnified, and all the more strongly if they look upon him by **opposition** or a **square** aspect. If the aspect is trine or sextile, even without reception, they will hinder less. **Haly**, however, seems to want to say that the malefics restrain their malice if they look by a trine or sextile aspect, but his intention was that they hinder *less*, yet he did not say their malice was entirely restrained.

**C**onsideration 12 is to look at the **benefics** and see what they signify. For **Jupiter** and **Venus** are naturally "fortunate" and are temperate; for this reason, they are said to be without any malice, for they harm no one unless perhaps by accident, which does not happen by their intention and occurs rarely. For they are inclined to impress with temperance and perfection, and they always strive to help their own and those who are not their own, whether they receive them or not. However, it is better if they do receive them; and a trine or sextile aspect is better than a square, and a square is better than an opposition.

**C**onsideration 13 is to see the **Sun** and its signification, for he is the source of all fortune by aspect, whatever that aspect may be, unless it is by opposition. However, by a **physical conjunction** <note>When the planet and the sun occupy the same degree.</note> he will be made evil, for then he is said to **combust** <note>term: "combure" (combustion). When a planet is too close to the sun, its power is "burned up" and weakened.</note> and bring misfortune to every star, unless that star is in the **sun's lap** <note>original: "canū solis," likely "camino" or "canum," but contextually "cazimi."</note> as was said above, for then it is in the **heart of the sun**, and every star in the heart of the sun is made strong.

**C**onsideration 14 is to look at **Mercury** and the **Moon** and see which planet they are joined to, because they signify that which the planet they are joined to signifies, for they are of a **changeable nature**.

**C**onsideration 15 is to consider the ways in which the **planets** impress themselves upon the lower things. There are two: one good and the other evil. For the benefics impress good naturally, and the malefics impress or bring evil naturally. Therefore, you must always hope for good when you see the benefics, and fear evil when you see the malefics, unless the aforementioned things diminish it.

**C**onsideration 16 is to see whether the planet that is the **significator** of any matter is hindered by any malefic. For a planet is not hindered by a malefic unless the malefic casts its rays upon the rays of the other according to the size of the circles of their lights. As long as it casts its light or rays upon the light or rays of the planet, the planet is called "hindered" until the malefic passes it. **Haly** said that once the malefic planet has passed the planet it was hindering by one full degree, the planet is said to be liberated from the evil. To me, however, it seems that once the malefic has passed it by **one minute**, the planet should be called liberated and escaped, because the malefic can then send nothing but **fear**. Furthermore, it sends greater fear when it has passed it by only one minute than when it has passed it by one degree; but such is the fear which the malefic sends when it has passed the planet by only one minute that it does not seem to the one whose matter it is that he could escape, though not without some small branch of hope.

Under such an example, a certain man intending to go to **battle** asked a question whether he would return healthy from the battle or not. The **Ascendant** was 13 degrees of **Gemini**, and **Mercury** was at 7 degrees and 54 minutes of **Aquarius** in the **9th house**, joined to **Saturn** who was likewise in Aquarius at 7 degrees and 53 minutes. Mercury was already separating from Saturn (who was the **Lord of the House of Death**) by 1 minute. It seemed, therefore, that he ought to die in that battle because of the conjunction he made with Saturn in...

...at the 8th degree of Aquarius: hence he was in danger of death and feared with a final fear, believing he would be killed by his enemies and was so persecuted by them that it did not seem possible he could escape. Many times they laid hands upon him; yet at last he escaped from them, as if after a state of despair, because he did not believe he could get away. And this happened to him because of Mercury <note>original: "Mercurium"</note>, who was already separated from Saturn. And Zael <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and primary source for Bonatti.</note> said that if a malefic planet <note>A "malefic" is a planet traditionally associated with hardship, specifically Saturn or Mars.</note> which was hindering any business should be falling from the Ascendant <note>Meaning the planet is in a "cadent" house where its power to act is weakened.</note> so that it does not cast an aspect, it does not fully block the matter, but it does instill great fear.

**Consideration 17.** is to look whether the signifying planet <term>Significator: the planet that represents the person asking the question or the matter at hand.</term> is safe, so that it is not hindered by any of the malefics, and that some of the fortunes <note>The "fortunes" or "benefics" are Jupiter and Venus, considered lucky planets.</note> cast their rays or their light upon its own rays or light. For then the planet is said to be "safe" until that fortune passes it by a single minute; this signifies the perfection of the matter. However, after it has passed by one minute, the matter is not perfected, nor does it offer anything but hope—just as a malefic planet offers nothing but fear, as I said. And the hope given by a fortune is such that the seeker believes the matter will be completed, and it seems to them that they are certain of its success; yet it does not happen without some trace of doubt. For example: a certain question was asked about a difficult business matter, whether it would be completed or not. The Ascendant was 17 degrees of Scorpio, Mars was at 12 degrees and 13 minutes of Taurus, and Venus was at 12 degrees and 14 minutes of Capricorn. Venus was joined to Mars by a trine aspect <note>A trine is a favorable 120-degree angle.</note> and received him into her house, and Mars received her in his exaltation. <note>Reception occurs when two planets are in signs where the other has essential dignity; it suggests mutual agreement or cooperation.</note> It seemed to the seeker and all those handling the business that it ought to be completed because of that aspect of perfect friendship. They remained in that hope until Venus passed the aspect of Mars by one full degree; yet in the end, the matter was destroyed because Venus had already passed Mars by one minute at the time the question was asked. Perhaps sometimes a matter might be completed in such a case, but not without great persistence, great labor, great entanglement, and much study and importunity. And Zael said that if a fortune is falling from the Ascendant so that it does not cast an aspect, it gives hope only and does not complete the business.

**Consideration 18.** is that you consider when a planet is in the "straits of the malefics." For unless a malefic receives it, the planet is said to be in trouble, distress, and tribulation—just like a man who has been attacked and insulted, with no one to help him as he fights and defends himself against many; or like one who strives and labors against fortune and everything turns out adversely; or like one who has fallen into a whirlpool and does not know how to swim, yet moves his hands and feet so that he sometimes reaches the bank and escapes, though this does not always happen. A planet is said to be in the straits of a malefic when the malefic is in one sign and the planet is in the 4th, 7th, or 10th sign from it <note>These positions create the "square" and "opposition" aspects, which were considered stressful or hostile.</note>. For instance, if a malefic is in Aries and another planet is in Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, it is said to be in its straits. Understand the same regarding a physical conjunction. But if the malefic receives the planet, it does not hinder it, because reception breaks all malice, as is said elsewhere. Once the planet has passed the malefic by one full minute, it is said to have escaped the danger of that evil and its hindrance. And after it has passed it by one degree, it is said to be secure, because the malefic can then do little against it, though it may still instill some fear. Do not forget these things I tell you, because they will be useful to you in nativities <note>Birth charts.</note>, in

<column-break/>

questions, and in the beginnings of all things.

**Consideration 19.** is to look at the Moon when she is "void of course" <note>This occurs when the Moon makes no further aspects to other planets before leaving her current zodiac sign.</note>, for then it signifies an impediment; the matter of the question, or that which is being started or discussed, will not come to a good end. The matter will be brought to nothing and will not be done or completed for the one wishing to do it; the seeker will return from the matter empty-handed, soiled, and hindered.

**Consideration 20.** is to look whether the Moon or the significator is joined to any of the planets, for then it signifies what is to come. Hence you must consider whether the one to whom the Moon or the significator of the matter or question is joined "receives" them; for then it signifies fulfillment and the perfection of the matter, and its good and praiseworthy end—I say this if the receiving planet is a fortune. If, however, it does not receive, and the Moon or the lord or significator of the matter commits its disposition to it, the matter may still be completed. But if it is a malefic, even if the Moon or significator commits its disposition to it and no reception occurs, it will not be completed, and evil and detriment will intervene. But if it does receive, and is not otherwise hindered, it signifies the perfection of the matter, though with labor, persistence, and fatigue.

**Consideration 21.** is to see from which of the planets the Moon is separating; for that signifies what has already been and what is past. For if she separates from a fortune, it signifies good that has already been; if she separates from a malefic, it signifies evil that has already been. Hence, if you wish to judge concerning that which has already happened and is past, you can speak of it according to what you see of the Moon’s separation from any of the planets.

**Consideration 22.** is to consider to which of the planets the Moon is joined, for that signifies what is present. Hence, if you wish to judge anything about a present matter, it is necessary for you to consider to what the Moon is then joined, degree by degree, or by less than one degree; and you ought to judge good or evil according to the nature of the planet she is joined to.

**Twenty-third consideration** is to look at what the Moon is joining, provided that her conjunction is not yet complete; for that signifies what is to come in the future. Hence, if it is necessary for you to judge a matter which is not yet and is hoped to come into action, you must look at what the Moon then wishes to join; and you should judge good or evil according to the significations of the one you see she wishes to join.

**Twenty-fourth consideration** is to look whether the signifying planet is in its "descent" <note>Also called "Fall" or "Depression," a sign where a planet loses its power and dignity.</note>; for then it signifies an impediment to any matter of which it is the significator, and distress and sorrow because of it. If it is a question about a prison that someone fears, it signifies his falling into it, and shame as well as loss. And if it is about one already imprisoned, it signifies a long stay in prison and remaining in it longer than the prisoner believes.

**Twenty-fifth consideration** is to consider whether the planet that is the significator of any matter is retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky.</note> or stationary in its first station; for then it signifies evil, impediment, discord, diversity, contradiction, a repeating of evil, disobedience, and a bad return from whatever the return may be, and in a bad direction. But in a "station" <note>When a planet appears to stand still before changing direction.</note> it does not signify as much evil as in retrogradation; for retrogradation signifies present and past evil that is still as if present, and future evil that is already as if in the making.

...the first <note>The "first station" occurs when a planet appears to stop moving forward and begins its retrograde or backward motion.</note> truly signifies an evil that is already completed according to a past-incomplete time.

**Consideration 26.** is that you should see whether the signifying planet <term>Significator: the planet that represents the person asking the question or the specific subject of the inquiry.</term> is in its second station <note>The "second station" occurs when a retrograde planet stops and is about to move forward (direct) again.</note>, because then it signifies a hindrance and an evil that has already been and is in the past. Some, however, have said that the second station signifies the same as direct motion, but that is to be understood according to a certain way of speaking—just as it is said of someone who has been sick and is now recovering that he is "freed and healthy," but it is not simply true, though it is close to the truth. For just as the first station does not signify as much evil as retrograde motion does, so the second station does not signify as much good as direct motion does.

**Consideration 27.** is that you should perceive whether malefic planets <note>The "malefics" are Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with difficulty or misfortune.</note> are the significators of any thing, or any work, or any beginning, or any birth, or any of the things that happen daily or pass through the hands of men. For if they signify evil, they will signify it as even greater; and if they signify good, they will signify it as diminished and imperfect, and accompanied by sadness, anguish, difficulty, and pressure—so much so that the one whose business it is will hardly believe it will be completed for him, unless perhaps those malefics are in a very good state and well-disposed.

**Consideration 28.** is to see if the planet signifying a thing is slow in its course. For it then prolongs the effect of the matter sought. If it is the beginning of a building, its completion will be prolonged and delayed so that it is hardly ever finished. If a promise was made to someone, that promise will be delayed and will be completed for the recipient only with great difficulty or very slowly. And if threats were made to someone, their effect will not be hastened—nor will bad promises. Matters are also delayed if the significators are in Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces, whether their lords (namely Jupiter and Saturn) are slow or not; but if they are slow, they postpone the matter even more. If they are in Aries or Scorpio, they postpone less than in the aforementioned signs. If they are in Leo, they hasten. If in Taurus or Libra, they hasten more. If in Gemini or Virgo, they hasten even more than in the other signs.

**Consideration 29.** is that you should look whether the Moon is joined to any of the planets bodily or by aspect, and whether its conjunction was completed minute by minute. For then it signifies that the matter is "present." And when it has passed that minute, you must see which of the planets it is first joined to; for that planet will signify what ought to happen regarding that matter. You shall also look at the planet from which the Moon was then separated before it was joined to the one mentioned minute by minute; for that planet has the task of signifying what has already happened regarding that matter.

**The thirtieth consideration** is to look when the signifying planet or the Moon has already passed the 29th degree of the sign in which it was and has touched its 30th degree—and especially if it has passed one minute of that degree. For then it will have no strength in 그 sign, but will be in the following one. Hence, if it had first signified some evil, it would not hurt the one whom it seemed it ought to hurt—just as if some house that threatened to fall did not harm the one who was leaving it, who already had one foot on the threshold of the door <note>original: "limine hostij"</note> and the other in the act of throwing himself beyond the threshold, retreating quickly, and then the house fell.

<column-break/>

So too if it had signified some good to someone, it would not benefit him—except as one who had reached out a net toward a bird and touched the feathers of its tail but did not catch it.
¶ Regarding this, Zael <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century astrologer.</note> said: if a planet or the Moon is in the 29th degree of any sign, its strength is still in that sign where it is, because it has not yet passed the 29th degree entirely, both in the degree that is before it and that which is after it.

**The thirty-first consideration** is to perceive when one planet seeks a conjunction with another, if it is so near the end of the sign in which it is (or the one whose conjunction it seeks) that it departs from that sign before the conjunction is perfected. You must see if it joins it in the following sign to which it changes, for then the cause is perfected—provided that planet gives it something in the sign in which it joins it (that is, if reception <note>A technical state where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is connecting with.</note> intervenes). This is unless it, or the one it wishes to join, is first joined to another; for then the cause is annulled and will not be perfected, even if it is later joined to the one it originally wanted to join after it has been separated from the one it was joined to when it changed from the said sign—because the other planet interposed itself before that first conjunction was perfected.
¶ And do not forget that a bodily conjunction prohibits an aspect and cuts it off; but an aspect does not prohibit nor cut off a bodily conjunction.

**The thirty-second consideration** is that you look if a malefic planet is the significator of any matter, what its state might be. For if its state is good, it will be well with that matter. If it is bad, it will be bad with that matter, according to what the author <note>original: "farcinator," likely a reference to the author of the *Centiloquium*.</note> said in the fifteen: A malefic planet, when it is oriental <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> in its own house or exaltation and is not joined to a malefic who hinders it, is better and worthier than a fortune <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> that is retrograde and hindered.

**The thirty-third consideration** is to see whether any malefic is the significator of a matter and is joined to another malefic who hinders it, or if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to it by a bad aspect (namely, by a square or an opposition). For that malefic perfects the cause, but it does not make it reach a good end; rather, it will be destroyed after it appeared to be going straight and was believed to be perfected. But if that malefic which hinders is lighter <note>Moving faster in the zodiac.</note>, so that it seeks a conjunction with the significator, it hinders less than if the significator seeks a conjunction with the malefic who hinders; it is worse if the significator "knocks" than if it is "knocked upon."

**The thirty-fourth consideration** is that you look in questions, or in nativities <note>Birth charts.</note>, or any other matters upon which you must judge, whether the significator of the business at hand is a malefic and is the Lord of the Ascendant, and is himself direct in the Ascendant and in a good state. For if it is so, he perfects the thing and makes it reach a good end. And even if he is not the significator nor the Lord of the Ascendant, but is in the Ascendant, and the Ascendant is his exaltation, he puts away all his malice and is restrained from evil hindrance. If hindered, he increases his malice, and his harm and opposition are multiplied, and he will strive in every way to destroy the business.

**The thirty-fifth consideration** is that you look whether a malefic planet is in a sign similar to itself, for then it diminishes its malice; and he who has what he wants is secure, because then he is found to be of good will, more pious, more merciful, and less malicious. ...[whether Saturn] be in Capricorn, or Aquarius, or Libra, or in a cold sign: and especially if he has some dignity <term>Dignity: a sign where a planet has natural strength, like its own "home" or "kingdom."</term> there; and likewise when Mars is in Aries, or Scorpio, or in Capricorn, or in a warm sign: and especially if he has some dignity there, because then the matter is perfected. But if Saturn is in a warm sign outside of his dignities, or Mars is in a cold sign outside of his dignities, it will be bad, and the cause is not perfected—just as a mixture of water with oil does not easily blend, nor do they embrace each other. If, however, they are good and well-disposed as I have described, then they will be capable of combining for good and they perfect the cause, just as a mixture of water with wine, or with honey, or with milk is perfected.

**The thirty-sixth consideration** is that you should consider when the malefic planets <note>Saturn and Mars.</note> signify a true hindrance to fortune, whether the benefic planets <note>Jupiter and Venus.</note> behold them by a trine or sextile aspect <term>Trine/Sextile: favorable angles of 120 or 60 degrees between planets.</term>; for then their hindrance is diminished, and much more strongly so if they "receive" them <note>Reception occurs when one planet is in a sign where the other has dignity.</note>.

**The thirty-seventh consideration** is to see, if the benefics are the significators, whether the malefics behold them by an opposition or a square aspect <term>Square: a challenging 90-degree angle.</term>; for then they diminish their good fortune and their goodness.

**The thirty-eighth consideration** is that you should consider, if the benefics are the significators, whether they are "falling" from the angles <term>Cadent: planets in houses that do not support action (the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th).</term> or from the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon, representing the start of the matter.</term> so that they do not behold it, and are retrograde; for then they will be hindered and will be almost like the malefics, unless they are "received."

**The thirty-ninth consideration** is that you look to see if the planet which is the significator is received; for if it is a benefic, its significance will be better than otherwise. If, however, it is a malefic, its hindrance will be less; it will also be hindered if it was meant to hinder someone else after it has been received.

**The fortieth consideration** is that you look to see if a malefic planet is "peregrine" <term>Peregrine: a planet wandering in a sign where it has no essential dignity or strength.</term>, whether it is the significator itself or not; this means it is not in any of its dignities. For then its malice is magnified, as is the evil it signifies and its hindrance. And when it is in its own dignities, its hindrance is diminished and its malice is restrained—whether in its house, its exaltation, or its term <term>Term: a specific segment of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet.</term>. In its triplicity <term>Triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</term> and in its face <term>Face: a ten-degree subdivision of a sign; the weakest of the dignities.</term>, the malice is restrained less. In its "hayz" <term>Hayz: a condition of strength where a planet is in a sign and hemisphere matching its gender and sect (day or night).</term>, it is likewise restrained less.

**Consideration 41.** is that you look to see if a malefic planet is the significator of any matter or any beginning, and it is in its own house, or exaltation, or in its term or triplicity, and in the angles or the houses following the angles; for then it is said to be as strong as a benefic.

**Consideration 42.** is that you observe if a benefic is the significator or has lent its help to any of the planets, and it is in a house in which it has none of the aforementioned dignities; for then its good and its fortune are diminished. And if it is in any of its said dignities, it perfects the matter and increases its strength and goodness, and its good fortune is magnified.

**The forty-third consideration** is to see if the benefics and malefics are together in "malignant places"—that is, in any of the hindrances I have already mentioned to you above many times—which is to say, in houses in which they have no testimony and are "combust" <term>Combust: scorched by being too close to the Sun, which renders a planet nearly powerless.</term>. For then they signify weakly whatever they signify; they signify weak and despicable things. The good planets cannot signify good, nor the malefics signify evil, because of their excessive weakness. Regarding this, the

<column-break/>

philosopher says that for a planet that is retrograde and combust, there is no strength in its significance. Wherefore Cael <note>original: "Cael," likely referring to the 9th-century astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr.</note> said that when a planet is under the rays of the sun, combust, or in opposition to it, it will be weak; for in this place there is no utility. There is nothing good in the good planets, nor is there anything evil in the malefic planets; for the benefics signify no good or very little when they are combust. Malefics likewise, when they are combust, have little or no power of signifying evil, and they can then inflict less hindrance.

**The forty-fourth consideration** is that you look forward to see if the signifying planet, whether good or bad, is in its house, its exaltation, its triplicity, its term, or its face—but the face is not of as much power as the other aforementioned dignities. Thus, it is necessary that it be supported by another dignity, namely "light" or "hayz"; for then a malefic is restrained from its malice, just as a vicious horse is restrained from its vice by a strong bridle, and whatever malice is in it is turned into good; and a benefic strengthens and increases the good. And although this might seem like something of a marvel, nevertheless the greatest part of the philosophers testify to this, and I have seen it happen thus in my own times. Therefore, you ought to weigh all these things I have told you in this chapter, and you will thus be able to judge truly upon it; for I have not found them to fail.

**The forty-fifth consideration** is that you look to see if the malefics are in the angles of the Ascendant and hinder any of the planets by a square aspect or by opposition; for then they hinder and afflict more, and their harm will be greater—especially if the malefics are in a stronger place than the planet they have hindered. If, however, they behold it from a trine or sextile aspect, they are restrained from evil, and their malice and hindrance are diminished.

**The forty-sixth consideration** is to see whether the planet that is the significator is a benefic or a malefic; for a benefic naturally always signifies fortune, but a malefic naturally always signifies evil, which happens to it because of the excess of the malignancy of its nature. Thus, you must look at the locations of the planets from the Ascendant in which they are placed; for if a planet is in its "light" or in its "hayz," or in any of its dignities, or in a good place relative to the Ascendant, it signifies good. If it is already a benefic, it signifies even greater good.

**The forty-seventh consideration** is that you consider whether the significator is in its own "light"—that is, a diurnal planet above the earth by day and below the earth at night, or a nocturnal planet above the earth at night and below the earth by day. Or if a nocturnal planet is the significator of a matter during the day above the earth, or a diurnal planet during the night; or if that significator is peregrine, meaning it has no dignity in the place where it is; or if it is "falling" from the Ascendant so that it does not behold it, or falling from the angles; for then it is hindered and it hinders that which it is meant to signify, nor can it perfect it.

**The forty-eighth consideration** is that you see if a malefic planet is the significator and threatens evil, whether Jupiter beholds it or is joined to it by its body <note>Conjunction.</note>; for he himself will break its malice and turn its nature into good, whichever malefic it may be; for so great is his goodness...

<summary>This page details Considerations 36 through 48 of Bonatti's astrological system, explaining how the natural "malice" of planets like Saturn and Mars can be restrained by their placement in strong signs (dignities) or by favorable aspects from Jupiter. It also discusses the weakening effect of being "combust" (too close to the Sun) and the importance of planetary sect (day vs. night).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical breakdown of the "Considerations" of Guido Bonatti, a 13th-century astrologer. The text focuses on how different planets interact—specifically how "benefic" planets like Jupiter can soften the "malice" of "malefic" planets like Saturn and Mars, and how a planet's proximity to the Sun affects its power.</meta>

...strength and fortitude in the good: because he <note>Jupiter</note> breaks all the malice of Saturn and turns it into good. Wherefore, if Saturn does not give good in that place, nor grants the thing which he promised, Jupiter makes him give and complete the matter even if Saturn is unwilling; unless Jupiter himself is hindered by "fall" <term>Fall: A specific sign where a planet’s influence is at its weakest.</term>, or combustion <term>Combustion: When a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up" and hidden.</term>, or retrogradation: for he helps then, but does not complete the matter entirely. When he <note>Jupiter</note> breaks the malice of Mars, it is because of the great friendship found between them, unless the matter is very difficult, such as the noise of arms, wars, and the shedding of blood. However, the malice of Saturn cannot be broken without the assistance of Jupiter: for then he breaks the malice of Saturn just as at other times he breaks the malice of Mars. Saturn does not "applaud" Venus in any way, because Saturn is slow and Venus is swift; he is heavy, and she is light; he rejoices in lamentation, while she rejoices in delight.

**The forty-ninth consideration** is that you consider whether any of the malefics <note>Saturn or Mars.</note> is the significator <term>Significator: The planet that represents the person or the subject of the question in an astrological chart.</term> of anything, and if it joins with another of the misfortunes; for if it signified any good, it destroys that good. But if it signified any evil, it will increase it and it will become worse, or it will change into some greater evil—just as a pain around the navel might change into dry dropsy <note>An old medical term for swelling or edema.</note>. If, however, it is joined to a "fortune" <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> that "receives" it <term>Reception: A cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other.</term>, or if the fortune is received by it, then that evil is led toward the good. And if no reception intervenes, the evil is not entirely removed but is mitigated, so that the evil is lessened as much as that fortune was disposed to allow, so that it will seem to do only a little harm.

**The fiftieth consideration** is that you look at the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</term> of any matter, as well as the Moon: see if they are hindered—or if one of them is hindered—by any of the misfortunes, such as by conjunction, by opposition, or by a "quartile" <note>A square aspect (90 degrees).</note> aspect, for that hinders the matter if there is no aspect from a "fortune." But if a "fortune" should look upon it—namely Jupiter, Venus, the Sun, or the Moon—they dissolve the malice of that hindering misfortune. He whose significator was the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is then liberated, even if some danger threatened him from the fear of that misfortune’s influence. This is true even if the aspect was a "tetragon" <note>A square aspect.</note>, provided it is with reception. But if a fortune looks upon it without reception from a square or opposition, or if a malefic looks from a trine or sextile without reception, or from a square or opposition even with reception: then it will be possible for the person represented to be liberated from the hindrance that seemed to threaten him, but it turns into another evil equal to the first, or a little less, so that the liberation will not seem to have profited him.

**The fifty-first consideration** is that you look to see whether the planet that is the significator of a matter is "falling" from an angle <term>Cadent: A planet in a weak position in the chart, "falling away" from the important corners or angles.</term> and from the Ascendant, and is not in any of its "dignities," nor in any of its "joys" <term>Joy: A specific house where a planet is said to be particularly happy or effective.</term>; for then it signifies every evil and every doubt. No utility, no good, and no hope will be in that matter, and such a planet, so disposed, can signify nothing praiseworthy.

**The fifty-second consideration** is that when the three "inferior" planets—namely Venus, Mercury, and the Moon—come out from under the Sun's rays and come to their "evening rising" (that is, they appear in the evening after the setting of the Sun): before they come out from under the Sun's rays and are distant from him by 12 degrees, the strength of each of them (and of the others as well) will be weak, so that a "fortune" can do little good, and a "malefic" can do little harm. Wherefore, if a fortune does profit someone, it will be done with difficulty and slowly, with great labor, great insistence, and much entanglement. And if it be a malefic, that which is signified will appear slowly. In the case of the "superior" planets, who are

<column-break/>

Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, these things happen when they come out from under the Sun's rays so that they rise in the morning before the Sun and appear before his rising.

**The fifty-third consideration** is that you look to see whether the planet significator is "under the rays" of the Sun; for then it will be weak and of no strength in any matter. Nevertheless, the malefics will be somewhat more powerful in evil than the fortunes are in good, though not by much. A planet is said to be under the rays of the Sun when there are 12 degrees or less between it and the Sun, but more than 16 minutes. For when there are only 16 minutes or less between the planet and the Sun, it is said to be in the "fountain" or in the "heart of the Sun" <term>Cazimi: An Arabic term for being in the "heart" of the Sun, considered a position of great accidental strength.</term>, as I told you above. But when there are more than 12 degrees and less than 15 between the planet and the Sun, they are said to be "extending" out from under his rays.

**The fifty-fourth consideration** is that you look whether a superior planet is 12 degrees distant from the Sun, moving toward its "morning rising," or whether an inferior planet is 12 degrees distant and moving direct toward its "evening rising"; for then it is in a state of strength. After it has moved 15 degrees away, so that it appears from under the Sun's rays, it is said to be "stronger" than it can be in any other state—just like a man who has come out of battle having conquered all his enemies, and he rests and rejoices in his victory, nor does he fear any other who might rise against him or resist him in anything. He is then cheerful, of good mind, good disposition, and blessed in all ways. However, when the Sun follows the three superiors and there are fewer than 15 degrees between them and him, their weakness is said to increase until there are only seven degrees between them. After there are fewer than seven degrees between them and the Sun—until they are in the heart of the Sun—they are said to be in "ultimate weakness." The weakness of the three inferiors is the opposite of this. For they are said to increase in weakness when they follow the Sun and are between 15 and 7 degrees from him; and from 7 degrees until they are in the heart of the Sun, they are said to be in ultimate weakness.

**The fifty-fifth consideration** is that you look to see whether the planet significator is "peregrine" <term>Peregrine: A planet "wandering" in a sign where it has no essential dignity or strength; like a stranger in a foreign land.</term>. In that case, it signifies that the person represented—whether in a birth chart, a question, or at the beginning of any matter—will be crafty, shrewd, and malicious. He will know how to do both good and evil and proceed ingeniously in all acts he wishes to perform; however, his intention will be more prone to evil than to good. But if the planet is in any of its major dignities—namely in its "house" or "exaltation"—and is direct, and is in a good place relative to the Ascendant (in the tenth or eleventh house, or in some aspect of friendship to the Ascendant), then it will signify a good effect for the things sought or begun, and a good mind and good will for the person born or the one asking the question. If, however, it is only in one of its "minor dignities," its significance will be less than this.

**The fifty-sixth consideration** is that you look to see, if the planet significator of a matter has committed its "disposition" to another planet, whether that receiver is "oriental" or "occidental." For if it is oriental <term>Oriental: Rising before the Sun; associated with external, active energy.</term> and is one of the inferiors and is direct; or if it is occidental <term>Occidental: Setting after the Sun; associated with internal or passive energy.</term> and is one of the superiors and there are fewer than 20 degrees between it and the Sun, it will be weak—as the "Sarcinator" <note>original: "sarcinator" — Likely a reference to the astrologer Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, known as "The Tailor."</note> says—and that which it indicated or showed will not be perfected. For it then hinders many things with such a hindrance as that which affects a man who is beginning to fall ill; the sickness has already grown so strong that the sick man is forced to lie down, nor can he help himself without the assistance of another. It is like a building that has already begun to collapse: someone is needed to shore it up so that it does not fall.

It explains how a planet's distance from the Sun determines its ability to effect change, comparing a strong planet to a victorious soldier and a weak one to a collapsing building.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical breakdown of the "Considerations" of Guido Bonatti. Having previously discussed how planets like Jupiter can mitigate the malice of Saturn and Mars, the text now moves into specific rules regarding house placement, the strength of planets in "angles," and the nature of different zodiac signs.</meta>

And the further a planet is from the sun, the less it is hindered <note>A reference to "combustion," where a planet's power is weakened by being too close to the Sun's light.</note>. If it is "oriental" <term>Oriental: Rising before the Sun in the morning.</term> and is one of the "superior" planets <term>Superior Planets: Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, which are further from the Sun than Earth is.</term>, or if it is "occidental" <term>Occidental: Setting after the Sun in the evening.</term> and is one of the "inferior" planets <term>Inferior Planets: Venus and Mercury, which are closer to the Sun than Earth is.</term>, and is not retrograde, it will be strong and well-suited to accomplish what it indicates. It is like a man who was sick and is now entirely free of illness and has regained all his powers, or like a building that had fallen and is now repaired and newly raised up and improved in all its parts. Such is the case for all the aforementioned planets so disposed.

**The fifty-seventh consideration** is that you look at the planet representing the significator <term>Significator: The planet that represents the person or the subject of the question in an astrological chart.</term> to see whether it is in the eighth house from the ascendant. For if it is found there, even if it is a "fortune" <term>Fortune: A benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus, that usually brings positive outcomes.</term>, it will not perform good. If it is a "malific" <term>Malefic: A planet like Saturn or Mars that traditionally signifies difficulty.</term>, it will work great evil, more than in any other place of the whole figure, and its malice will be magnified. If the question is about going to war, do not persuade the person to go then, even if the planet is a fortune, because evil is always to be suspected—namely death or at least capture. For the eighth house is the place of darkness and death. If the planet is a malific, you could judge death for him unless it is then separating from the Lord of the Eighth House; for then it could signify wounds, blows, or a fall that makes it look like he might die, though perhaps he might escape. If it were a journey, especially a long one, you could also judge capture or at least great fear on the road. This is always understood if it separates from the Lord of the Eighth, and it is understood that a malific disposed as I have said always works more evil than a fortune.

**The fifty-eighth consideration** is to look at whether the significator planet is "fixed" in the sign in which it was found. It is said that a planet is not fixed in a sign until it has traveled five degrees into it. However, it seems that once a planet has traveled one full degree of a sign, it is firm in it. He <note>Likely referring to Ptolemy.</note> said this for greater evidence; he said a planet is not said to "fall" from the ascendant unless it is distant from it by five degrees. For example: the ascendant was at 9 degrees of Aries and the planet was in the 5th degree of that same Aries. Ptolemy and many other wise men say that such a planet is in the "angle" <term>Angle: One of the four most powerful points in an astrological chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</term>, with all of whom I agree. Some others, however, wanted a planet to be called "in the angle" only when it was in the exact degree of the ascendant, or one degree before or two after; but their intention was for the "revolutions of the years" <term>Revolutions of the years: A solar return chart used to predict a person's upcoming year.</term>, and they wanted to be so certain that they could not be deceived in anything. I, however, have proved that a planet is in the angle up to near the completion of five degrees beyond the "cusp" <term>Cusp: The line that marks the beginning of an astrological house.</term> of any angle. For in a certain year, when I was investigating the revolution of that year, I found Mars in the 5th degree beyond the cusp of the "angle of the earth" <term>Angle of the Earth: The 4th house or "Imum Coeli," the lowest point of the chart.</term> and it was in Capricorn and had southern latitude. That signified the killing of the Emperor of the Romans <note>Original: "impatoris romanorum." This refers to the Holy Roman Emperor, Frederick II.</note>. I signaled that to him then; for he was then in Grosseto and I was in Forlì. Pandulfus de Fasanella and Thebaldus Franciscus and many others of his secretaries were found to have made a conspiracy to kill him. None of his other astrologers found this because they did not believe Mars was in the angle; for it had passed the cusp of the angle by 4 degrees and 58 minutes according to their opinion. After a planet is distant from the cusp or from the line of any angle by five degrees, it is called "falling from the angle" <term>Cadent: From the Latin 'cadere' (to fall); planets in these positions are considered weaker.</term>.

**The fifty-ninth consideration** is to look at whether the significator planet is within 15 degrees after the line of the angle and no further; for it is said to be "in the angle" just as well as one that is right on the angle according to the view of the heavens. From then on, he said it was not in the angle, and said it had no strength in the angle beyond the 15th degree

<column-break/>

after the angle. For example: if the ascendant was the 4th degree of Taurus, everything up to the end of Taurus was "after the angle." But whichever planet was from that 4th degree of Taurus up to the 19th degree of the same was in the angle; whichever was beyond the 19th degree was not in the angle. Ptolemy, however, seems to want to suggest, though he does not say it expressly, that every planet that is five degrees before the angle and up to 25 degrees after it is in the angle. Zael <note>original: "Czael." This is Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer.</note> wanted to remove the doubt lest that great distance of the planet from the angle should hinder the matter. Ptolemy seems to want (and I do not disagree with him) that no part of any "house" <term>House: One of the twelve divisions of the sky, each representing a different area of life like wealth, health, or death.</term> should remain void of power. It seems to me—and I do not believe it in vain—that every planet that is in any house is said to be and is in that house in which it was found, from the beginning of that house until its end. And for this reason I say "in the house" and not "in the sign," because one house sometimes comprises more than one zodiac sign, and sometimes less than one sign. For it seems ridiculous that any part of any house should remain hateful or void of power.

**The sixtieth consideration** is to look at whether the significator planet is in a "fixed," "common," or "movable" sign. In a fixed sign <term>Fixed Signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius.</term>, it signifies firmness and stability and the durability of the thing begun or to be begun, or that which the question was about. When it is in a common sign <term>Common Sign: Also known as mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which represent change and transition.</term>, it signifies the change and repetition of the thing already begun or to be begun, or about which the question is made; and that the matter will be dissolved and begun again, or that another matter will be mixed with it, or something similar to an alteration or repetition will happen. Therefore, in matters where we desire change, such as buying, selling, and the like, we ought to place the significator planet and the Moon (or at least one of them) in a common sign. And when it is in a movable sign <term>Movable Sign: Also known as cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which represent action and initiation.</term>, it signifies a quick change or alteration of the matter, and its quick completion and a fast end, whether it signifies good or evil. Therefore, in things where we desire a quick end, we should place the significators in movable signs. But in things where we desire durability and long-lasting firmness, we should place the significators in fixed signs. In those where we desire a middle ground, we should place the significators in common signs. Understand the same concerning the nature of the Moon. And again, I recap for you: fixed signs signify firmness, durability, and unity; common signs signify plurality; and movable signs signify the speed of change.

**The sixty-first consideration** is to look at whether the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is with the Head or Tail of the Dragon <term>Head and Tail of the Dragon: The North and South Nodes of the Moon, traditionally viewed as points of great fortune or great misfortune.</term>. For then it signifies an impediment in everything; and the impediment will come from a cause signified by that house in which the conjunction occurs. And no other conjunction of the Head or Tail hurts except a "corporal" one <note>Meaning the planet must be at the exact same degree, as the Nodes do not have "aspects" or rays.</note>, because they have no aspect nor opposition. And it is worse when the significator or the Moon move toward them than when they recede from them. For when they move toward them, they signify the ultimate evil, like what happens to one who is in a ship when it is in danger and breaks apart in the open sea, for then there is no hope for him. But when they recede from them, it is like when the ship has already been endangered; because a sailor can cling to some piece of wood—namely a spar or a rope and similar things—which gives him hope of escaping, and sometimes he does escape. And it must be known that when the significator or the Moon moves toward the Head, the malice is increased; and it is worse when it recedes...

Within one degree, and from one degree forward, its malice is not as great as it is within that first degree, though it remains significant. **The sixty-second consideration** is that you observe whether the Moon is "void of course." <term>Void of Course: A state where the Moon makes no further major aspects to other planets before leaving its current zodiac sign.</term> Indeed, a void of course signifies that the matter about which a man inquires will either never be able to be completed or will not reach a good end. And if it is completed, it will be done with labor, as well as with distress and sorrow, unless the lord of the ascendant <term>Lord of the Ascendant: The planet ruling the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question.</term> or the significators of the matter are in an exceptionally good state. For if they are, although it may be hindered, the matter is not entirely taken away. However, it is a good time for someone to use quiet pursuits—namely, drinking, bathing, eating, and similar things—when the Moon is so hindered. It is similarly good to use a depilatory, especially when the Moon is in Scorpio, which is a kind of ointment for removing hair that is called *psilotrum* in Latin <note>original: "psilotrum"</note>, but is commonly called *sconapotum* <note>original: "sconapotum"</note>.

**The sixty-third consideration** is that you observe whether the Moon is far from conjunction with the "malifics" <term>Malefics: Traditionally Saturn and Mars, planets associated with difficulty or misfortune.</term>, provided she does not cast her rays upon the rays of the malefics. If this is the case, it signifies a good outcome for the matter being asked about or performed; it is even better if she casts her rays upon the rays of some "fortune" <term>Fortunes: Benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus.</term>, and much stronger still if the lord of the ascendant or the significators of the matter are in a good state. If, however, they are not well-disposed, that good significance will be diminished; yet it will not be entirely taken away, so that some good part of it remains.

**The sixty-fourth consideration** is to observe whether the Moon is in Cancer, Taurus, Sagittarius, or Pisces. If she is, it signifies good in the matter being dealt with, even if she is joined to malefics or not joined to fortunes. Nor does being void of course harm her as much in these places as it does in others, provided she is not "combust" <term>Combust: Being so close to the Sun (within 8.5 degrees) that the planet's power is symbolically "burned up."</term>; for these places do not benefit her then.

**The sixty-fifth consideration** is that you observe whether the lord of the seventh house is hindered or not. When it is hindered, it signifies a hindrance to the matter sought. Therefore, you must then delay judgment if you can, and consider and search by all possible means to see where that hindrance might come from: whether from the conjunction of the lord of the seventh with planets, or from its separation from them. Likewise, check the Moon, because the cause of the hindrance can then be found. Once you find where it comes from, you will be able to judge more safely.

**The sixty-sixth consideration** is that you observe in questions and in all things you intend to do, when the malefic planets threaten some evil: if that place where those threats fall is the "dignity" <term>Dignity: A place in the zodiac where a specific planet has natural strength or "citizenship."</term> of some fortune, look to see if that fortune then aspects that place by a trine or sextile aspect <term>Trine/Sextile: Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</term>. If so, it will take away all that evil and annihilate it entirely. If it aspects from a "square" aspect <term>Square: A challenging angle of 90 degrees.</term>, it will take away some of that evil and diminish it, though not entirely; it might diminish perhaps half or a little less. If it aspects from an "opposition," it will take away even less, perhaps a fourth, fifth, or sixth part, or at least an eighth. But if it does not aspect, the evil will happen according to what the hindering malefic threatened. And it will happen through good and just men who do not practice malice; this happens perhaps because those just men testify against the one who seeks the truth by speaking the truth against him, for which reason he suffers loss or

<column-break/>

detriment, perhaps from a judge or presiding official who will judge against him for the sake of justice. If, however, that place is the dignity of some "infortune" <term>Infortune: Another term for a malefic planet.</term>, that evil will happen through unjust men, who use neither justice nor truth but are wicked men who will perhaps bear witness against the truth—whether that testimony is true or false, it will be as I have said. Or it will happen to him through an evil ruler or judge who is wicked; even if he judges justly in that matter, he will still be such a man in himself: neither a lover, nor a fearer, nor a worshipper of God.

**The sixty-seventh consideration** is that you observe in questions or in any "beginnings" <note>This refers to "elections," the practice of choosing an auspicious start time for an endeavor.</note> whether there is any future eclipse near that question or that beginning, specifically one that is distant from the significator of that matter or from the Moon by less than 12 degrees. For that eclipse will bring damage and evil to the querent and to the matter that was to be started, unless there is a fortune there that has dignity in that place, because then that malice will be diminished. Nevertheless, you must observe, if no fortune is there, who and how a planet aspects the place of the eclipse. For if fortunes aspect it, they will increase that evil; but if malefics aspect it, they will diminish it—which seems like a kind of marvel.

**The sixty-eighth consideration** is that you observe in questions of the sick or in the onset of illnesses: whether the lord of the seventh house and the seventh house itself are free from hindrances or not. For if they are free from the malefics so that they are not hindered by any of them, then the sick person can safely commit themselves to the care of physicians; for then medicines will benefit them. If the seventh house and its lord are hindered, Ptolemy said that the physician should be removed from the sick person, because neither medicine nor the care of physicians will benefit them. For the seventh house signifies medicine, as it was hidden <note>Perhaps meaning "as it is traditionally ascribed."</note>, or perhaps the illness will become chronic. You can say the same if the aforementioned hindrance exists at the hour of beginning the treatment of any illness.

**The sixty-ninth [consideration]** is that you observe in questions of journeys or in their beginnings, or even in other matters: whether the significators of the ascendant and the house signifying the matter sought—whether already started or to be started—are equal in strength or weakness. For you will not be able to judge safely then. You must then look at the "Lord of the Conjunction or Prevention" <term>Conjunction or Prevention: The New Moon (Conjunction) or Full Moon (Prevention) that occurred immediately prior to the question.</term>, whichever occurred before the matter you intend to deal with, and you shall judge according to that. But if the lord of the conjunction or prevention and the lord of the matter sought are again equal, you cannot judge safely. You should then return to the Moon and see to what she is first joined, and you can judge according to that. If she is not joined to anything in the sign or from the sign in which she is, change her to the sign she is in and see what she is first joined to in the sign—or from the sign—into which she enters after her departure from the one she was in at the time of the question or the named beginning; and judge according to that. And this is such a chapter that you must consider it well.

**The seventieth consideration** is that you observe a certain other hidden thing, which is not well observed by astrologers and which sometimes harms them greatly. This is that you see in questions or the beginnings of matters whether the lord of the conjunction or prevention that was before that question or before that beginning is in any "angle" <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful areas of an astrological chart.</term> of that matter sought or started. For it will then signify that the matter will be completed and done, unless it is blocked by the querent or the one beginning—that is, if they resist it—even if it does not appear through other significators that it ought to be done.

**The Seventy-First Consideration** is that you look into the question which has been put to you concerning any matter, or if you wish to start something such as a journey or anything else, whether the <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing the person or the goal</note> falls between the Ascendant and the twelfth house; for then it shall signify the duration of time in which the matter ought to be done. If it has already been done, it signifies how long it should last, whether in days or hours. If, however, it is between the twelfth and the tenth houses, it shall signify half-weeks. If it is between the tenth and the seventh, it shall signify months or weeks. If it is between the seventh and the fourth, it shall signify years. And if it is between the fourth and the Ascendant, it shall signify half-years.

**The Seventy-Second Consideration** is that you look to see whether the question is about a journey or is the beginning of some journey; if the Moon is then <term>impedited</term> <note>hindered or afflicted by a "bad" planet</note>, say that no journey should be made at that time. If the journey cannot be avoided, put the planet that hinders the Moon as the Lord of the Ascendant.

**The Seventy-Third Consideration** is that you look in questions whether the question signifies good or evil. See if it signifies good and the <term>fortunes</term> <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> aspect the significator of the question or the Moon; for then that good will be increased. If, however, the <term>malifics</term> <note>unfavorable planets like Saturn or Mars</note> aspect them, the good will be diminished. If, however, it signifies evil and the fortunes aspect it, that evil will be diminished. But if the malifics aspect the significator or the Moon, the evil will be increased and become worse.

**Consideration 74** is that you look whether the planet that is the significator is in its **first station** <note>the point where a planet appears to stop before moving backward, or "retrograde"</note> wanting to become retrograde; for then it signifies "disobedience" and that the matter concerning the interrogation will not be done nor completed, even if it seems it should be. And if any work or building is begun then, it will not be finished. And as long as such a significator is so disposed "under the earth" <note>below the horizon</note>, it will not raise that building; it is said it may take up to 30 years to rise, and even then it will not be finished. If it is raised a little then, it will take another 30 years. If it is not completed then, it will not be completed until 90 years from the day of its first beginning. And if it is not completed then, it will never be completed, unless perhaps the lordship is transferred to strangers and not the original owners. But when it is in its **second station** wanting to go "direct" <note>moving forward again</note>, it signifies that the matter will be completed, though with slowness, entanglement, difficulty, heaviness, and great effort and anxiety. And if any building is begun then, it will be completed, though not as quickly as was believed at the start, provided the significator is not under the earth; for then the person who begins the building will not finish it, nor will he raise it much above the ground. Understand this: because a planet in its second station, when it wishes to move direct, signifies the adaptation, renewal, direction, and strength of any matter. But in its first station, when it wishes to move retrograde, it signifies the dissolution, heaviness, and destruction of any matter. Understand all these things well, for they will very often come into your hands.

**The Seventy-Fifth Consideration** is that you look whether the Moon is hindered by any of the planets in whatever matter one intends to do, regardless of what the question or the beginning is; for whatever is then done or begun will be hindered. However, if the Moon is in a good place from the Ascendant so that it looks upon it with a "praiseworthy aspect," namely a <term>trine</term> <note>120 degrees apart</note> or <term>sextile</term> <note>60 degrees apart</note>, and that planet which

<column-break/>

hindered the Moon aspects the Ascendant with any of the aforementioned aspects, it will lessen the hindrance and will not cause as much harm; and perhaps it will take it away entirely, provided that the hindering planet is well-disposed so that it is not "falling from the angles" <note>in a weak house</note> nor from the Ascendant as I have said, nor is it in its "fall"—that is, in the seventh sign from its own house <note>original: "in septimo a domo sua" - this actually refers to the sign of its "detriment"</note>. For then it will cause more fear than actual harm. <term>Zahel</term> <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century astrologer</note>, however, seems to want to say that if the "evil hinderer" is falling from the Ascendant or is retrograde, then it causes fear on the part of the seeker or the one beginning the work. I, however, have always remembered and feared the hindrance of the Moon above all other hindrances, nor do I remember seeing a good end to any matter in which the Moon was hindered. For in journeys, if the journey was for war, I feared for the person of the traveler. If it was for business or something else, I feared distress, loss, and sadness on the journey along with the loss of property.

**The Seventy-Sixth Consideration** is that you look from which planet the Moon most recently separated and to which she is being joined; for that from which she separates signifies that which has already happened. That to which she is joined signifies that which is to come, as is said elsewhere. If she separates from an evil planet and is joined to a good one, it signifies that what has already passed was not good—rather, it was a bad thing hindering the questioner—but that which is to come will be good, a thing in which the questioner will rejoice and which will be useful to him. But if she separates from a good planet and is joined to an evil one, the matter was good at the beginning, but the end will be bad. If she separates from a good planet and joins a good one, the matter was good, is good, and its end will be praiseworthy. If, however, she separates from an evil planet and joins another evil one, the matter was bad, is bad, and its end will be bad.

**The Seventy-Seventh Consideration** is that you look whether the Lord of the Ascendant of any question (or any other matter) or the Moon is in the **opposition of its own house** <note>the sign opposite the one it rules, known as "detriment"</note>. This is: the Moon in Capricorn; Mercury in Sagittarius or Pisces; Venus in Scorpio or Aries; the Sun in Aquarius; Mars in Taurus or Libra; Jupiter in Gemini or Virgo; Saturn in Cancer or Leo. For then the Lord of the question or of any other matter will be "abhorring" the cause about which he asks or which is being dealt with. Nor will it be a matter in which he takes delight or which he desires to be completed; it will seem rather that he does not want it finished than that he wants it finished or done.

**The Seventy-Eighth Consideration** is that you look at the sign which signifies the matter about which the question was asked. For the first house signifies the person; the second signifies substance <note>money/possessions</note>; the third signifies brothers; the fourth signifies fathers, and so on, as was said above in the treatise on the 12 houses. Look at the Lord of that house, and according to what it shows you concerning the thing it signifies, you will be able to judge, having carefully inspected all the other things I have told you.

**The Seventy-Ninth Consideration** is that you look whether the planet that is the significator or the Moon joins with good or evil planets, whether by conjunction or by aspect. And you must look into this carefully, for the bodily conjunction of the Sun <note>original: "iunctio solis corporalis" - known as "combustion"</note> is the worst misfortune that can happen to a planet.

**The Eightieth Consideration** is that you look in which sign the significator of the matter is located relative to its own house: whether in the same, or in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th. You shall judge based on the meaning of that sign in which it sits relative to its own house, just as you would judge a planet being in any of the houses relative to the Ascendant.
