<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for an astrologer from Guido Bonatti's "Book of Astronomy." It lists specific rules (Considerations) for interpreting a horoscope, focusing on the strength of planets, the role of the "Part of Fortune," and the influence of the Moon's subdivisions.</meta>

**The Eighty-First Consideration** is that you look to see whether the planet which is the <term>significator</term> <note>The planet that represents the person asking the question or the subject matter.</note> is in an <term>angle</term>, in a <term>succedent house</term>, or in a <term>cadent house</term>. For the closer a significator is to the line of the angle <note>The cusp or starting point of the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note>, the stronger it will be. The further it is removed from it, the less strong it will be; and the same applies to a succedent house. Furthermore, the closer it is to the line of a cadent house <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, which are considered weak or "falling away."</note> from an angle, the more weak it will be, and the further it is from that line, the less weak it will be.

**The Eighty-Second Consideration** is that you look to see whether the planet that is the significator of any matter receives its "disposition" <note>The influence or management of its affairs.</note> from any planet that is a <term>Fortune</term> <note>A benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus, which brings good results.</note> or a <term>Misfortune</term> <note>A malefic planet, like Saturn or Mars, which brings difficulty.</note>. If it receives its disposition from a Fortune, it signifies good; and it is even better if that Fortune is in a good state and well-disposed. If, however, it is not well-disposed, the result will be below this. If it is <term>impeded</term> <note>Weakened by bad aspects or being in a sign where it cannot function well.</note>, it will be even more below this. If it receives its disposition from a Misfortune, it signifies the opposite; and more strongly so if that Misfortune is impeded. If it is not impeded, it will be somewhat less severe. If it is well-disposed, it will further decrease the level of that malice.

**The Eighty-Third Consideration** is that you look to see whether the Fortunes and Misfortunes are equal in the question or whatever else is being judged. In that case, they will not signify any prolonged good judgment (that is, or evil), nor will the matter being dealt with bring profit or loss.

**The Eighty-Fourth Consideration** is that you look to see if the Fortunes are stronger in the questions than the Misfortunes. If both are strong and the Fortunes prevail in strength, they will signify a certain moderate good. If, however, the Misfortunes prevail, they will signify a certain moderate evil.

**The Eighty-Fifth Consideration** is that you look to see whether the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: "pars fortune"; a specific mathematical point in the chart calculated from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant, representing prosperity and success.</note> falls in a good place in the figure <note>the chart</note> or in a bad angle—that is, whether in a succedent or a cadent house. See how it is aspected and by whom: whether by a Fortune or a Misfortune, and whether it "receives" <note>An astrological relationship where one planet hosts another in its own sign.</note> the one that aspects it or not. For questions sometimes seem good, but the Part of Fortune falls in a bad place, which greatly weakens the question and makes it less useful than expected. For the asker will hope for good, but it will not come to him as the question seems to show. If the good that the question seemed to signify is found, it will be less than expected because the Part of Fortune is in a bad place in the figure or joined to an evil planet. And sometimes a question will seem to threaten evil and pronounce it; yet if the Part of Fortune is in a good place in the chart and is joined to a good planet, either by body <note>conjunction</note> or by an aspect that receives it, it will diminish that evil, and not as much harm will happen to the seeker as the question seemed to threaten.

**The Eighty-Sixth Consideration** is that you look in every question, or journey, or birth, or any other beginning, whether any of the evil planets aspects the significator. See if both are <term>retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward</note>, cadent, and <term>peregrine</term> <note>having no dignity or "home" in their current zodiac sign</note>, and in signs entirely contrary to their nature. Then they bring such loss and such harm that it can never be avoided, nor can anyone turn it away unless God alone does so; and it would be like a great miracle if the person facing the danger escaped. And if someone is born while things are in such a state, he will perpetually be a <note>The text says "medicus" (doctor), but in context of "pauper et indigens" (poor and needy), it is likely a scribal error for "mendicus" (beggar).</note> beggar, poor, and lacking food for his belly, and he will never be able to work hard enough to avoid beggary. And if a house is built then, no one will ever enjoy it, nor will they gather money in it that would benefit them; and often setbacks will come to them by which their goods will be destroyed, vanish, and come to nothing. And whenever he believes any of his business is being better directed and will reach a good and desired end, then it will rather be destroyed and broken apart, unless divine goodness interposes itself.

<column-break/>

**The Eighty-Seventh Consideration** is that you look at the <term>Novenary of the Moon</term> <note>A subdivision of a zodiac sign into nine parts, similar to the Vedic Navamsha. It was used to find hidden strengths or weaknesses.</note>, which is a thing to be greatly observed. For it many times hinders the astrologer so that he cannot clearly see the truth, and he is sometimes deceived in his judgment, not knowing the cause that makes him fail.

**The Eighty-Eighth Consideration** is that you consider the planet from which the Moon is separating, and how it is disposed; for that planet signifies what has already happened, as was said above. And see to which planet she is joined, so that there is no distance between them of more than 5 minutes; for that planet signifies what is currently happening according to how it is disposed. See also whose conjunction she seeks, or to whom she will first be joined after separating from the one she is currently joined to; for that planet will signify, according to its disposition, that which is in the future.

**The Eighty-Ninth Consideration** is that you look at the <term>Duodenaries of the Moon</term> <note>A subdivision of each zodiac sign into twelve parts of 2.5 degrees each.</note>, which is also a thing to be strongly observed in many judgments—even more than the aforementioned—for greater dangers can arise from it. It is among the most subtle considerations of astrologers and of births, which is poorly observed by many because of laziness rather than ignorance. Thus they sometimes fall into the disgrace of the common people <note>original: "laicorum"; literally "laypeople," referring to those not trained in the art.</note> because of their fear of the labor they do not wish to endure.

**The Ninetieth Consideration** is that you look in questions, or births, journeys, or any other things or beginnings, whether the Lord of the house in which the Sun is, the Lord of the house in which the Moon is, and the Lord of the Ascendant are <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the Sun or positioned in the eastern part of the chart</note> and in an angle—though this rarely happens—and whether they aspect each other from good places and with good and laudable aspects, namely <term>trines</term> or <term>sextiles</term>. For then they signify the greatest fortune, the greatest good, and the ultimate profit in every matter of whatever kind. If, however, they are not all so disposed, but only some of them, it will signify good according to that part for which they were so disposed.

**The Ninety-First Consideration** is that you look in questions, or births, or in other chosen matters, whether Mars is in any angle. This is especially significant if the angles are in <term>fixed signs</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, and particularly if Scorpio is his own house; for then he destroys much of the good which is signified by that question or by those figures. And if he does not entirely destroy it, he greatly hinders and diminishes it, unless by chance Jupiter aspects Mars from a trine or sextile aspect; for then the malice of Mars is diminished and mitigated because of the aspect of Jupiter, provided always that Jupiter is well-disposed in his own strength or weakness.

**The Ninety-Second Consideration** is that you look in births or in questions about wills or in questions about death. See if the Lord of the house of death <note>the 8th house</note>, or the significator of death, or the Lord of the house in which the Lord of the house of death is located, goes to the significator of the native or the querent, or if the significator goes to him. For the planet so disposed becomes the <term>interfector</term> <note>The "killer" or the planet that brings about the end of the matter or life.</note> and kills, whether it is a Fortune or a Misfortune, and whether <term>reception</term> occurs between them or not.

**The Ninety-Third Consideration** is that you look if there is a question about a thing which someone wishes to ask from another, or if it is a thing which he wants to dig up or extract from a hidden or secret place. See whether the significator of the seeker or the thing sought aspects Saturn, or joins him by body, or if Saturn is in the house of the thing sought. For then the thing which the asker seeks will be done with difficulty, and the hidden thing will be extracted from its place with great labor, entanglement, and slowness. This is true even if it seems the matter should be done quickly and with ease; for much after the asker thinks the matter is settled, it will be hindered and delayed more than he himself believes.

<meta>This page continues Guido Bonatti's 146 "Considerations," which serve as a comprehensive checklist for an astrologer before providing a judgment. The previous page discussed the strength of planets based on their house placement (angles, succedent, or cadent houses) and how they receive "disposition" from other planets.</meta>

**The Ninety-Fourth** consideration is that you should observe in questions or other beginnings whether the <term>significator</term> <note>The planet that represents the subject of the inquiry.</note> of the thing sought is "falling" <note>In a <term>cadent house</term> (the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th), which are considered weak positions.</note> from the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> or from other angles, or from the house of the thing sought; or if the planet is falling, <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, often symbolizing delays or reversals.</note>, or in a "bad state" with the Sun <note>original: *in malo esse cum sole*; likely referring to being <term>combust</term>, or scorched by the Sun's proximity.</note>, or in a bad place or bad disposition relative to it. For these things signify an impediment to the matter, even if the question otherwise appears to be good.

**The Ninety-Fifth** consideration is that you should consider whether the planets signifying the thing sought are joining one another; for that signifies the perfection of the matter itself. However, do not judge the matter to be completed until you see and well consider the nature of the sign in which they join, and whether that sign is of their own nature. For if it is of their nature, the matter will be perfected with ease and to the joy of the <term>querent</term> <note>The person asking the question.</note>. But if the planets do not agree in nature with the sign, the matter will not be perfected easily; indeed, only with difficulty or never. And if it is perfected, it will be with great labor and the highest anxiety for the querent, even if it otherwise seems that it ought to be perfected easily. If they agree somewhat, the matter will be done with less labor, yet not very easily.

**The Ninety-Sixth** consideration is to look at questions that seem to show that the matters about which the questions are made ought to be perfected: see whether the significator of the thing and the Moon are in <term>angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses—the "power centers" of a chart.</note> and are both remote from the <term>cusps</term> <note>The starting point or "border" of a house.</note> of those angles by more than 25 degrees. For this signifies that the matter will not be perfected, even if it seems straightforward. If, however, only one of them is remote from an angle in this way—namely the planet signifying the thing sought or the Moon—and the other is not remote, the matter will be perfected, though with difficulty; unless perhaps it is a journey, for that would nonetheless be completed even if the significators were remote from the angles.

**The Ninety-Seventh** consideration is that you consider in which <term>climate</term> <note>In medieval geography, a "climate" refers to a specific zone of latitude.</note> you receive the question, since judgments differ according to how the <term>ascensions</term> <note>The way signs of the zodiac rise over the horizon, which changes based on how far north or south you are.</note> of the climates and regions differ. For the order of the ascensions or elevations of the signs in one climate is not the same as in another, nor is the degree rising in one region the same as in another. Therefore, unless you are very careful in this, you could err in your judgment, which would be bad and highly disprovable or blameworthy. For the signs rise differently in the first climate than in the second, and differently in the third, and differently in the fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh. Because of this, it is necessary that you guard yourself well against these differences lest you fall into error in your judgments. For toward whichever part you go from one region to another—whether from east to west or west to east, or from south to north or north to south—for every 53 miles (and a small, barely perceptible amount more), the ascendant will vary from another by one degree. But perhaps some "fools in tunics" <note>original: *fatui tunicati*; likely a disparaging reference to uneducated people or perhaps certain religious orders Bonatti disliked.</note> might rise up and say that if judgments differ according to the locations of regions, then they are false—not knowing what lies hidden beneath. One should not answer them or argue with them, for they have no discretion, nor do they understand or believe, and to such people nothing can be proven. Yet there are some among them who are discreet and well-understand intelligible things, and with those you can certainly confer, though they are few. One of these was the venerable brother **Everard of Brussels** <note>original: *Eneruandus Bussiensis*.</note>,

<column-break/>

of the **Order of Preachers** <note>The Dominicans.</note>, whom I found to be very discreet and well-understanding of every truth and its use, and who, because of the depth of his knowledge, was made the **Bishop of Cesena**. Behold, the things I have told you could make an astrologer err, and I fear they have made some err at times; for a judgment cannot be given except according to the ascendant and the other houses. Thus, if the ascendants differ, the judgments must necessarily differ. And so you must not fear labor, nor let laziness overcome your diligence, but see to it that you have tables of the elevations of the signs for every climate in which you find yourself and for every region—whether made by you or another—by calculation or by such a comparison from one region to another that does not deceive you. However, it is harder to find the difference from climate to climate than from region to region along the same longitude. For if you have tables of the elevations of signs in some region from east to west, you can estimate and obtain the elevations of the signs from that region to another in whichever direction you wish, by taking the difference as I told you; but across different climates, you cannot estimate so easily.

**The Ninety-Eighth** consideration is that you look in questions to see if the thing signified through a question is shown by the planets through a physical conjunction, or by an <term>aspect</term> <note>A specific geometric angle between planets, like a square or a trine.</note>, or by a **translation of light**. For if the significators are joined by body or aspect, the matter will be done and perfected by the querent and the <term>quesited</term> <note>The person or thing being asked about.</note> without the intervention of another. If, however, they are not joined by body or aspect, but some planet "translates light" <note>A <term>translation of light</term> occurs when a fast-moving planet separates from an aspect with one significator and immediately applies to an aspect with the other, "carrying" the influence between them.</note> between them, the matter will be done by the hands of messengers or someone who intervenes and brings the matter to effect through some person or thing signified by the house of which that intervener is the lord. For if it is the lord of the **second house** who translates the light, the matter will be done with expenses or by some other way of using the querent's money. If it is the lord of the **third**, it will be through the querent's brothers (if he has brothers) or through something signified by the third house. If it is the lord of the **fourth**, it will be through the father; if the **fifth**, through a son; if the **sixth**, through servants; if the **seventh**, through a wife; if the **eighth**, through death or the wife’s money; if the **ninth**, through some bishop or religious person; if the **tenth**, through kings or a ruler; if the **eleventh**, through some friend; and if it is the lord of the **twelfth**, it will be through some hidden enemy or through something signified by the twelfth house.

**The Ninety-Ninth** consideration is that you observe in questions, <term>nativities</term> <note>Birth charts.</note>, or other beginnings what the future outcome will be. For you will sometimes see through a question that a matter ought to be done and fully perfected, yet it is not perfected in its entirety, but only in part; and sometimes it is perfected in its entirety; and sometimes neither in whole nor in part. And you should see why this happens. For astrologers are blamed and cursed for this, and they do not know how to excuse themselves well because they are ignorant...

The reason why this happens is an arduous and difficult matter, requiring the most subtle inquiry. This is why our ancestors did not involve themselves deeply in it, for the labor involved is very great. However, that most honorable predecessor, **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a preeminent Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to European medieval astrology.</note>, who is to be imitated in all things, said more about this than other astrologers. I have found his judgments, both for specific questions and for the <term>revolutions</term> <note>A "revolution" refers to the annual return of a planet (usually the Sun) to its original position, used to predict the year's events.</note> of years, to be more effective and careful than those of others. Even **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the Roman-Egyptian author of the *Tetrabiblos*.</note>, who was the great clarifier of this science in universal judgments, was found to be more authoritative by other astrologers.

This matter concerns the consideration of the <term>fixed stars</term> <note>Stars that appear not to move relative to each other, unlike "wandering" planets.</note>, which are significant. I will mention these to you in my treatise on revolutions and also touch upon them in the treatise on <term>nativities</term> <note>Birth charts.</note>. Nevertheless, I will name them here so that they are more readily at your fingertips, lest you delay too long in learning of them. 

Some stars are of the nature of the <term>fortunes</term> <note>The "benefic" planets: Jupiter and Venus.</note> or of the nature of good planets. Those of the nature of the fortunes bring things to completion that otherwise do not seem likely to succeed based on the planets' own <term>significators</term> <note>The specific planet acting as the representative for the person or thing being asked about.</note>. Others are of the nature of the <term>infortunes</term> <note>The "malefic" planets: Saturn and Mars.</note>, and these are the ones that do not permit matters to be completed. 

Of those which are of a harmful nature, some are found in every sign:

In **Aries**, there are two. One is at 13 degrees and 45 minutes; the other is at 14 degrees and 45 minutes. They are in the north and are of the nature of Saturn and Mars.

⸿ In **Taurus**, there are six stars at 9 degrees and 55 minutes which are called the **Pleiades** <note>A prominent star cluster in Taurus; historically associated with blindness or weeping.</note>, though they are all spoken of as one. They are all of the nature of Mars and the Moon. There is another at 13 degrees; another at 13 degrees and 2 minutes; another at 14 degrees and 45 minutes, and that one is called the **Devil**. Another at 15 degrees is called the **Head of the Devil** <note>original: *caput diaboli*; likely referring to the star Algol.</note>. Another is in the "belly of the bull" at 19 degrees and 15 minutes, called **Aldebaran**; all of these are of the nature of Mars and Mercury.

⸿ In **Gemini**, there is one at 8 degrees called the **Number of the Dog**, which is of the nature of Mars and Saturn. Another is at 10 degrees and 15 minutes, which is of the nature of Mars and is called **Bellatrix**. Another is at 17 degrees and 55 minutes. Another is at 18 degrees and 52 minutes, which is called **the Malefic** and is of the nature of the Sun and Mars.

⸿ In **Cancer**, there is one at 2 degrees and 3 minutes called **the Camel**, of the nature of Saturn and the Moon. Another is at 7 degrees and 55 minutes. Another is at 13 degrees, of the nature of the Sun and the Moon, called **the West of the Camel**. Another in the same degree is of the nature of Saturn and is called **the Dog's Foot**. Another is at 15 degrees and 55 minutes; both are of the nature of Saturn.

⸿ In **Leo**, there is one at 15 degrees and 55 minutes, of the nature of Saturn.

⸿ In **Virgo**, there are two stars: one at 7 degrees and 11 minutes (nature of Mars), and the other at 15 degrees (nature of Saturn).

⸿ In **Libra**, there is one star at 26 degrees, of the nature of Saturn.

⸿ In **Scorpio**, there are three stars: one at 1 degree and 3 minutes, another at 8 degrees and 7 minutes, and another at 9 degrees; all are of the nature of Mars.

⸿ In **Sagittarius**, there are two small stars: one at 19 degrees and 2 minutes, the other at 21 degrees and 1 minute; they are of the nature of Saturn.

⸿ In **Capricorn**, there are two stars: one at 27 degrees and 2 minutes, which is named **the Bad One**, and another at 27 degrees and 5 minutes; both are of the nature of Saturn.

⸿ In **Aquarius**, one star is at 9 degrees and 4 minutes, of the nature of Mars and Saturn.

⸿ In **Pisces**, there is one star at 4 degrees and 7 minutes, of the nature of Mars and Mercury.

All the aforementioned stars are harmful, malevolent, hindering, and destructive to things that seem destined to succeed, and they prevent completion. Therefore, you must always avoid them in all your actions as much as you are able—which is very difficult. Although I have mentioned them here, you will find this discussed more extensively and

<column-break/>

better said in the treatise on the revolutions of the years, God favoring my health and life.

**The One Hundredth** consideration is that you should look in your actions for the fixed stars that help matters to be realized and perfected. Their locations are as follows:

⸿ In **Aries**, there are two stars. One is at 15 degrees and 6 minutes, of the nature of Jupiter and Venus, whose nature is to help and be beneficial. The other is at 26 degrees and 1 minute, of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Taurus**, there are three stars. One is at 1 degree and 3 minutes; another is at 8 degrees and 7 minutes; another is at 9 degrees and 1 minute. All are of the nature of Venus.

⸿ In **Gemini**, there are two stars: one at 19 degrees and 2 minutes, and the other at 21 degrees and 3 minutes; they are of the nature of Jupiter and are of the second magnitude <note>Magnitude refers to the brightness of a star; second magnitude stars are bright, but less so than the first magnitude.</note>.

⸿ In **Cancer**, there are two stars: one at 27 degrees and 2 minutes, which is called **the Good One**, and another at 29 degrees and 5 minutes; both are of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Leo**, there is one star at 9 degrees and 4 minutes, of the nature of Jupiter and Venus.

⸿ In **Virgo**, there is one star at 4 degrees and 7 minutes, of the nature of Venus and the Moon.

⸿ In **Libra**, there are two stars of the nature of Jupiter and Venus: one at 13 degrees and 45 minutes, and the other at 14 degrees and 45 minutes.

⸿ In **Scorpio**, there are four stars: one at 9 degrees and 55 minutes, another at 13 degrees and 1 minute, another at 14 degrees and 45 minutes, and the fourth is at 19 degrees and 15 minutes. All are of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Sagittarius**, there are two stars: one at 10 degrees and 15 minutes, and the other at 7 degrees and 55 minutes. Both are of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Capricorn**, there are three stars: one at 2 degrees and 3 minutes, another at 7 degrees and 55 minutes, and another at 17 degrees and 55 minutes. All are of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Aquarius**, there is one star at 15 degrees and 55 minutes, of the nature of Jupiter.

⸿ In **Pisces**, there are two stars: one at 7 degrees and 11 minutes (nature of Venus), and the other at 14 degrees and 59 minutes (nature of Jupiter).

Whenever you see the <term>significator</term> of any matter bodily joined with any of these aforementioned helpful fixed stars, you shall predict good, an increase in the matter, and a good end.

**Consideration 101** is that you should look in nativities or <term>interrogations</term> <note>A horary chart, cast to answer a specific question.</note> for which planet is the **slayer** or **cutter of life** <note>original: *interfector vel abscisor vite*; the planet responsible for determining the end of life.</note>, or the cutter of years, or the prohibitor of a thing so that it is not done or perfected. For that planet is the one that destroys the life of the newborn, slays them, and prevents matters from being completed. This planet is the one that is stronger by its many dignities or powers in the birth, the question, or the beginning of a matter. 

However, **Messahala** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a prominent Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note> concealed this. It seems he did so with good reason, for he only revealed it to one of his disciples, along with another very useful secret; but that disciple, led by arrogance, claimed it for himself. 

Once you have identified the prohibitor, destroyer, or slayer, see to what the Lord of the <term>Ascendant</term> or the Moon is joined (for the Moon is a participant in all things, as has been said to you elsewhere). Also look at the Lord of the matter sought or begun, and the Lord of the house where the Moon is. If they are joined to a <term>retrograde</term> planet, a <term>combust</term> <note>Burned up by being too close to the Sun.</note> planet, or one falling from the Ascendant or an angle, or to one of the "evils" that does not "receive" <note>Reception is a technical term for a planet being in a sign where another planet has dignity, facilitating cooperation between them.</note> it, or to another unfortunate star that is afflicted by the "evils" <note>Mars or Saturn.</note>—which cuts off the light of the significator—it destroys the matter and it is not perfected. In this way, the years of the newborn are cut off and diminished, and they do not live long. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon or the Lord of the matter is joined to some planet...

...planet which is free from the conjunction of the **malefics** <note>In astrology, "malefics" (bad-doers) usually refer to Saturn and Mars, planets associated with challenge or hardship.</note> and is safe as far as it is in itself, but joins with another planet that is impeded by any of the aforementioned impediments, the matter will be destroyed even after it is seen and believed to be direct and destined to be perfected; and the life of the **native** <note>The "native" is the person for whom the astrological chart is cast.</note> will be cut off when it is seen and believed that they ought to live well. **Consideration 102** is that you should look at and consider in the things that are signified how the thing that is signified ought to be found, and from which significators it should be extracted. For it is extracted from the significator of the **querent** <note>The person asking the astrological question.</note> and from the significator of the thing being asked about. Whence if the significator of the querent and the significator of the thing sought are joined, and likewise the Moon, it signifies the total effect of the matter; but if they are not joined, it signifies the contrary. And from the conjunction of the significators, it should be known why the question is asked; and by the Lord of the house in which the conjunction occurs, it should be known what the question will be about. For if it is a **fortune** <note>A "fortune" or benefic planet, typically Jupiter or Venus, associated with positive outcomes.</note>, it will be about something good, according to the nature of that fortune and the house in which it is, and the nature of the Lord of that house and the place in which the Lord of the house of that conjunction is. But if it is an **infortune** <note>A "malefic" planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note>, it signifies the querent asks about something bad, according to the nature of that infortune and the house in which it is, and the nature of the Lord of that house. If the Lord of the house, or the Lord of the exaltation, or the Lord of the other two minor dignities <note>In medieval astrology, planets gain "dignity" or strength by being in specific parts of the zodiac.</note> should aspect it, or if there is a **translation of light** <note>A "translation of light" occurs when a fast planet (like the Moon) moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, connecting their influences.</note>, the cause of the question will be known. If none of these occur, the cause will not be determined; it will be from a cause not yet known, and the outcome will be known by the aspect of the fortunes or the malefics.

**Consideration 103** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions at which house the **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being.</note> is found; for from the meaning of that house will come the fortune or gain of the native or querent, if it is well-disposed. But if it is poorly disposed, it signifies misfortune and loss for that same cause.

**Consideration 104** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions (or any other matter) whether the significator of the native or querent is found in the seventh house from its own house, or in opposition to the Lord of the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart.</note>; for this will signify not gain from that house's topics, but rather loss and expense.

**Consideration 105** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions whether a malefic planet is found in the seventh house; for it signifies that the native or querent will not enjoy wives, lovers, or partners, but will always have quarrels and ill-will with them; it will rarely happen otherwise for him.

**Consideration 106** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions whether a well-disposed fortune, not impeded, is in the seventh house; for it signifies that the native or querent will be fortunate in having good wives and good partners. Nevertheless, he will have many rivals and many who hate him, both with and without cause; this is more from envy than his own fault, so that the man may achieve what he wishes, but he will complete those things with labor and persistence.

**Consideration 107** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions whether **Mars** <note>original: "mars"</note> is in the second house from the Ascendant or in the tenth, and is well-disposed; for it signifies that the native or querent will have 

<column-break/>

fortune in those things that are operated by iron or fire or "consumption," such as the work of smiths, bakers, and similar things; or in taverns, hospitality, and the household. But if he is an infortune and poorly disposed, you may judge the opposite.

**Consideration 108** is that you should look if any planet aspects two houses; for its strength will be in that house in which it has greater dignity and more strengths, and it will more greatly aid that house and its significance.

**Consideration 109** is that you should look in nativities or universal questions if the Lord of the fifth house is impeded in the seventh; for it signifies that the native will not be fortunate in banquets, and many inconveniences will happen to him in them. The worst dishes will be placed before him, more detestable than those given to other guests, and uglier plates and uglier cups; and perhaps they will not give him a cup unless he asks for it first—and the same for all others. If anything is taken from the table, it will be taken from him before anyone else; the same will happen to him regarding clothing and other ornaments of the body.

**Consideration 110** is that you should look in nativities and universal questions whether **Scorpio** <note>original: "scorpio"</note> is the Ascendant; for the person whose Ascendant it is will not have fortune in the **Roman Church** <note>original: "ecclesia romana"</note>. This is because of **Cancer** <note>original: "cancrū"</note>, the exaltation of **Jupiter** <note>original: "iouis"</note>, who naturally signifies clerics; Cancer would then be the ninth house, which signifies the Church, and Jupiter is the enemy of Mars, who is the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Scorpio is traditionally ruled by Mars. Because Mars and Jupiter are seen as contrary in nature here, the author suggests a natural friction between the person and the church hierarchy.</note>.

**Consideration 111** is that you should look in nativities and universal questions, and especially in lawsuits or controversies, whether the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>original: "cauda dracōis"; the South Node of the Moon, associated with decrease or loss.</note> is in the seventh house; for it signifies the detriment and "emptying out" of enemies, and the increase of the native or querent, because the **Head** <note>The North Node of the Moon, associated with increase.</note> will then be in the first house. If it is in the eighth, it signifies the emptying and diminution of substance and wealth. If in the seventh, it also signifies the increase of the wealth of the native, since the Head will be in the second. When it is in the third, it signifies the "emptying" of brothers; in the fourth, the emptying of fathers; in the fifth, the emptying of children; in the sixth, the emptying of servants; in the seventh and eighth, as I told you; in the ninth, the emptying of journeys; in the tenth, the emptying of honors; in the eleventh, the emptying of friends; in the twelfth, the emptying of harmful animals. And it also signifies in every house the emptying of other things signified by that house. **Saturn** and **Mars** do the same, but somewhat less than what the Tail does. Other malefics also empty the aforesaid significations, but less so than Saturn and Mars, unless they themselves were bad significators; for then much of their malice is diminished.

**Consideration 112** is that you should look in nativities or questions at the Ascendant; for if the Ascendant is **Virgo** <note>original: "virgo"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "mercurius"</note> is in a good state or at least not impeded, it signifies that if the native or querent applies himself to medicine, he will be fortunate in healing and it will go well for him in his medicines or cures. But he will be unfortunate in salaries and in profit for the sake of medicine, because those to whom he provides service will satisfy him poorly and unwillingly; a man will hardly be able to get from them what he is owed, except from a very few. He will also be unfortunate in his lawsuits. And if he applies himself to the law, he will be unfortunate in his advocacy and will be disdained even by the common people, let alone others; his words will not be heard and will be considered as nothing, even if he speaks words useful to those who hear them. And the words of the wise... <note>original: "vba sapi." (verba sapientis). This is a catchword intended to lead into the next page.</note>

**Consideration 114.** is that you should look in nativities or questions to see whether the Lord of the eighth house is a fortune and is in the second house; for it signifies that the native or querent will acquire and profit from the goods of the dead, from enemies, and from wives, and especially so if it is not hindered or has dignity there. **Consideration 115.** is that you should look in nativities or questions to see if the eighth house or its Lord is hindered; for it signifies that the native or querent will suffer loss because of the death of some woman whose dowry he will be obliged to restore at his own loss.

**Consideration 116.** is that you should look in nativities or questions to see which house is hindered or unfortunate, or if its Lord is hindered or unfortunate; for it signifies that through those things signified by that house, harm will come to the native or querent. But whichever house is fortunate, or its Lord is, good and utility will come to him through the things signified by that house.

**Consideration 117.** is that you should look in nativities or questions for the house in which the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>original: *cauda draconis*; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with loss or decrease.</note> is located in the fourth house; for it signifies that whatever the native or querent acquires or gains will be destroyed and come to nothing. And in whatever other house it is found, it signifies that loss and detriment will come to the native or querent in those matters signified by that house.

**Consideration 118.** is that you should look in nativities or questions to see in which house a fortune is located, being fortunate, strong, well-disposed, and not hindered; for it signifies that from those things and people signified by that house, the native or querent will profit and have good luck in them. And in whichever house a malefic is found, he will lose, and his misfortune will then come from the things signified by it.

**Consideration 119.** is that you should look in nativities or questions to see if the Lord of the second house is in the seventh, and the seventh house is Aries, Scorpio,

**Consideration 120.** is that you should look in nativities or questions whether any of the Lords of these eight houses—namely the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth—is in the seventh house. Whichever of them is there will act as an enemy to the native or querent, unless a perfect reception occurs via a good aspect, namely a **trine** <note>A 120-degree angle, very favorable.</note> or sextile. If it is a square <note>A 90-degree angle, indicating tension.</note> or opposition with reception, it lessens the malice but does not take it away entirely. For example: if it is the Lord of the third, his brothers will be hostile to him. If the Lord of the fourth, his father will be hostile. If the Lord of the fifth, his children will be hostile. If the Lord of the sixth, his servants will be hostile. If the Lord of the ninth, religious men will be hostile and oppose him and speak evil of him, nor will he deal perfectly with them. If the Lord of the tenth, kings, nobles, the rich, and the powerful will be hostile to him, nor will he profit with them or by their occasion without losing as much or more elsewhere; indeed, it will be worse for him with the powerful. And although sometimes one or more may seem favorable to him, he will be shown to be wished ill by others or perhaps by many; so that if some leave anything in the "syllables," others will recover it in the "tribute" <note>An idiomatic way of saying that what one powerful person spares, another will take through taxes or fines.</note>. And perhaps they will sometimes expel him from the city—some of the powerful ones—because of the misdeeds he commits, trusting in the intimacy he seems to have with the powerful or those he lives with; and the services he does for the powerful, or for the communities of cities, or for great men, will be lost and for the most part regarded as nothing. If it is the Lord of the eleventh, he will have no friends who love him except for their own benefit, even if they pretend to be friends; for they will promise him many things and keep few or none. But if it is the Lord of the twelfth, he will almost be unable to trust anyone; and if he gives anything to them for safekeeping, they will deny it and take it for themselves and not restore it, even if they are religious men, unless perhaps they are forced.

**Consideration 121.** is that you should look at the nativity and the Lord of the Ascendant being in the Ascendant, the second, or the twelfth house while **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, signifying weakness or internal focus.</note>; for this signifies that the native or querent will have no luck in games of dice, nor will the dice speak well to him.

**Consideration 122.** is that you should look in nativities or questions whether the **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity.</note> is in the first ten degrees of the fourth house with the **Head of the Dragon** <note>original: *capite draconis*; the North Node of the Moon, associated with increase or gain.</note>, the Moon, Venus, and Jupiter, and they are **direct** <note>Moving forward normally.</note>; for it signifies that the native or interrogator will acquire immense buried treasure. If it is in the second ten degrees with two of those, he will acquire it, but not in such a great quantity; he will perhaps acquire half of it or about half. If indeed none of these are present, he will not acquire it nor anything from it. ### Consideration 123.
is that you should look in **nativities** <note>Birth charts.</note> or **questions** <note>Horary astrology, where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked.</note> to see whether the **Sun** and **Moon** are joined in the same minute according to both longitude and latitude, and if any of the **fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, Jupiter or Venus.</note> is in the **Ascendant**—specifically within 15 minutes or less above the line of the **cusp** <note>The boundary line of an astrological house.</note>, or 44 minutes or less below the line of the cusp. This signifies that the **native** <note>The person for whom the birth chart is cast.</note> or the **querent** <note>The person asking the question.</note> will be fortunate in acquiring much **substance** <note>Wealth and material property.</note> and in accumulating it, because the fortune will then be in the Ascendant. If, however, they are joined at the same minute in longitude but not in latitude, and the distance of one from the other is 15 minutes or less, his fortune in acquiring substance will exist, but it will be less than this in proportion to how much the distance between them exceeds one, two, or fifteen minutes. But if the fortune in the Ascendant is more than 15 minutes below the cusp line, up to 45 minutes, the fortune of the native or querent will be less than what was said, proportioning the 15 to 45 minutes just as one would proportion 1 to 15. You may say the same if the Moon is in the minute of **opposition** to the Sun and a fortune is in the **seventh house** just as was said of the Ascendant; for the fortune will then be in the seventh, namely on the line of the cusp of the seventh house, which signifies the fortune of the native or querent by reason of wives or other women, and by reason of partners and enemies. But if at the hour of birth the Moon is in **Taurus** at the minute of the Ascendant (meaning Taurus is rising), or if **Leo** is the Ascendant and the Sun is at the minute of the Ascendant, and no malefic hinders him or her, it signifies that the native will acquire much money and arrive at great dignity and great exaltation. But if any of the **infortunes** <note>Malefic planets.</note> is in the place of the fortune—namely in the Ascendant or the seventh—it signifies the loss and destruction of the substance of the native or querent through the occasions mentioned above.

### Consideration 124.
is that you should look in nativities or questions at the **significator** <note>The planet representing a specific person or topic.</note> of the substance of the native or querent and the significator of his dignity or **mastery** <note>original: *magisterium*; refers to one's career, authority, or specialized craft.</note>, which you can perceive from the **Lord of the Tenth House** of the figure of the nativity or question, or even from the Lord of the Ascendant if the Lord of the Tenth is not fit to signify the dignity or mastery of the native or querent, according to whether the quality of his being and his lineage is fit to receive such dignity or mastery. If the Lord of the Tenth House or its **Almuten** <note>The planet with the most essential dignity or power at a specific point in the zodiac.</note> is **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> from the **luminary** <note>The Sun or Moon.</note> that holds authority, and is far from it by 60 degrees or more up to 90 (if it is one of the **superior planets** <note>Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn.</note>), or is far from it by 30 degrees (if it is one of the **inferior planets** <note>Venus or Mercury.</note>), and is in the **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful.</note> of the tenth house or the Ascendant—so that it is not further than 30 minutes beyond the line of the angle, or more than one and a half degrees below it—or if it is with the luminary that holds authority (the Moon as with others, or in the **heart of the Sun** <note>original: *in corde ipsius*; the "Cazimi" position, within 17 minutes of the Sun, considered a position of great strength.</note>) along with the **Part of Fortune** and not hindered, it will signify that the native will attain the dignity or mastery of his predecessors and will not exceed it; however, he will be greater, more excellent, and more perfect in that dignity or mastery than any of his ancestors were. If, however, there is any of the helpful and fortunate **fixed stars** in any of the aforesaid angles with the Part of Fortune or any of the planets, he will attain a much greater dignity than anyone in his family ever reached. If it is one of those stars of the **first magnitude** and they are the only significators, the native or querent will attain immense dignity and immense honor, and riches that are almost inestimable. If the Lord of the Ascendant aspects this, his fame and honor will exist in his own person. If the **Lord of the Second House** aspects it, it will exist in riches; if the Lord of the Tenth, it will exist in such highness and kingship as befits great kings; and even if he is of low persons and the lowest nation, and no matter how much lower his lineage, he will attain all the more to greater sublimity. Nevertheless, these things will not last long, nor will they easily transcend a span of twenty-seven years, and few reach that or more than thirty years. And the higher his rank is, the heavier his fall will be, and his dignity or highness will end in evil; for he will come to ultimate misery, and will die a blameworthy or most foul death. If this does not happen to him, it will happen to his nearest successor in that dignity.

### Consideration 125.

### Consideration 126
This is to look in nativities <note>Birth charts.</note> or questions whether **Mercury** is the significator of the birth or its lord, and if he is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, and located in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius**. This signifies that the native will be of deep and subtle wit, high intellect, and great understanding. He will understand fundamental matters, whatever they may be, to the very marrow; he will see from the very beginning to what end they might come. This is even stronger if Saturn then aspects Mercury according to the quality of the aspect and is not impeded; even more so if Mercury is in Aquarius,

in which is the "Joy" of Saturn <note>A specific zodiacal placement where a planet is thought to be particularly effective.</note>. Furthermore, it is stronger if a **Fortune** <note>A beneficial planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> is then joined with Mercury, or if he is with any of the fortunate fixed stars. But if he is in **Aries** or **Scorpio**, it signifies he will be strong through foolishness and perfidy, and through the agility and magnanimity of his own movement. He will be arrogant regarding his deeds of arms; he will be prudent and quick to understand things said to him or things he finds written, rather than at thinking things out for himself or by himself.

### Consideration 127
This is to look in nativities to see if the **Lord of the Ascendant** is naturally "evil" <note>A "malefic" planet.</note>, such as **Saturn** or **Mars**, and if he presides alone over the birth without the participation of any Fortune. This signifies that the native’s sense of taste or smell, or his physical temperament, will not be like the taste, smell, or temperament of other men. 

For if it is **Saturn** alone, it signifies his taste will delight in things that are insipid, harsh, and sour, as **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer.</note> testifies in his commentary on the 40th aphorism of **Ptolemy’s** *Centiloquium* <note>A famous collection of 100 astrological aphorisms.</note>. 

If, however, **Mars** alone is the significator, he will delight in sharp and bitter things. He will not shrink from turbid wine, nor dreggy wine, nor hanging wine <note>Possibly refers to wine that is spoiled or "on the vine" too long.</note>. He will not delight in sweet, subtle, or clear things. He will not shrink from vile meats, nor even semi-rotten ones, nor even rotten or stinking fish. He will affect horrible odors rather than sweet ones, such as **aloe**, **galbanum**, **serapinum**, **opopanax** <note>Resins used in medicine and incense, often with pungent or medicinal smells.</note>, extinguished candles, and burnt horns. Similarly, he may enjoy the smell of stables and other such places. His nature will also delight in ugly and deformed women more than in beautiful ones, and he will be more comforted by them than by others. The same may be said of women, who will delight more in deformed men than in beautiful ones.

### Consideration 128
Look in nativities whether the sign of the Ascendant is formed in the image of a human sign <note>Signs like Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>, or if its Lord is in a human sign. If it is so, it signifies the native will be civilized toward men and will gladly associate with them. If the Ascendant is a human sign and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a human sign, he will be even more civilized and sociable, conversing with them most gladly. 

But if the Ascendant is a sign formed in the likeness of some animal that men use in their work or actions—such as **Aries**, **Taurus**, the last part of **Sagittarius**, or **Capricorn**—it signifies the native will be humble toward men, but will not be very sociable with them. 

If it is in "semi-wild" signs, such as **Cancer** and **Pisces**, he will be even less sociable with them. 

If indeed it is in feral <note>Wild or predatory.</note>, furious, and woodland signs—such as **Leo** and **Scorpio**—he himself will be furious, feral, and wild toward men, nor will he wish to associate with them in anything. He will love to dwell in solitude rather than in company, for he will not wish to be with his parents or other blood relatives.

## Consideration 130: To observe in nativities

Whether the Moon is joined with **Mercury** by conjunction or by aspect, or if another planet transfers light between them. If this is not the case, and if the Ascendant is not a sign of the nature of Mercury or the Moon, and if **Saturn** is in a day-birth or **Mars** in a night-birth in an angle, the native will be insane, or furious, or **epileptic**, or demented, or a fool, or at the very least extremely forgetful—unless a **Fortune** <note>A "Fortune" refers to the beneficial planets, Jupiter or Venus.</note> in a strong position aspects the Ascendant, or Mercury, or the Moon. This is even more certain if the angle in which any of the aforementioned **Malefics** <note>The "Malefics" are the challenging planets, Saturn or Mars.</note> are found is **Cancer** (which is the exaltation of Jupiter), or **Virgo** (the exaltation of Mercury), or **Pisces** (the exaltation of Venus). This is because in nativities, the Moon signifies the body of the native, and the planet to which she is joined signifies the virtues or qualities appearing in him according to its own power. If she is joined to Mercury, or if she aspects him, he will be wise and preserve his senses and not lose them. But if Mercury is in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius** and not impeded, and he is of good condition, the native will be of great intellect, deep thought, wise, and a philosopher. If **Jupiter** and **Venus** are in the **beams of the Sun** <term>beams of the Sun: also called "under the sunbeams," referring to a planet being so close to the Sun that its influence is hidden or altered</term>, he will be a hermit and like a man who is a prophet; his words will be heard and received above the words of other men.

## Consideration 131: To observe in nativities

Whether it is the birth of a man, and whether the Sun and Moon are both in **masculine signs**, or both in a masculine quarter, or in one masculine sign; for if it is so, it signifies that the acts of the native and his operations will naturally be those pertaining to men, and he will naturally exert himself in them. But if it is the birth of a woman and the luminaries are disposed as stated, she will be a **virago** <note>original: "virago"; in this medieval context, a woman who displays traditionally masculine traits or takes on male roles.</note> and will naturally exert herself in those things pertaining to men and will scorn men. And if she marries, she will not wish to revere her husband nor be subject to him. 

If Venus and Mars are in masculine signs in the nativity of a man, his sexual conduct will be orderly according to nature and according to the law. If they are **oriental**, he will abound in sexual desire and exceed moderation in it; he will not be content with natural sex, but will instead affect **incest** <note>In medieval astrology, "incestum" often referred more broadly to any socially or religiously forbidden sexual act.</note> so that he scorns women and **abuses men** <note>original: "abutetur viris"; a reference to male-male sexual acts.</note>. But if they are **occidental** <note>Setting after the Sun.</note> and in feminine signs, his sexual conduct will be unnatural and unclean; and even more so if Saturn aspects them, as he signifies the uncleanness of sex. 

If indeed it is a woman, and Mars and Venus are in masculine signs and are oriental, she will abhor sex with men and take no delight in it; she will instead delight in the **rubbing of women** <note>original: "fricatione mulierum"; a medieval description of lesbianism.</note> and especially of girls. But if Mars and Venus are in feminine signs and are occidental, she will love sex with men and delight in it and use it according to nature. And if Jupiter is in a feminine sign and is occidental in the birth of both a man or a woman, and the aforementioned condition regarding Mars is not present, the native's sex will be natural and according to the law. If indeed Mars is the sole significator and Jupiter does not aspect him, their

sex will be largely against both natural and **apostolic laws**. ## Consideration 132: To observe in nativities

Whether Mars is bodily present in a nativity with a certain red star of his own nature which is in **Taurus**, called **Algol** <note>original: "algol"; known as the "Demon Star," historically associated with misfortune and violence.</note>, such that there is a distance of 16 minutes or less between them, with Mars moving toward it; and if the lord of the house in which the luminary holds authority—which is called the **Lord Anuba** <term>Lord Anuba: likely a Latinization of an Arabic term (Al-Anubah) referring to the planetary dispositor or governor of a luminary</term>—or the lord of its exaltation, or of two other dignities, is in opposition to Mars or in a square aspect to him, and none of the Fortunes aspect the degree of the Ascendant, nor are in the **eighth house** <note>The house of death.</note>: without a doubt, it signifies that the native will be **beheaded**. 

If Mars is not distant from that star by more than 16 minutes, this will happen infallibly and cannot be avoided unless God turns it away. But if a **retrograde** or **combust** <term>combust: a planet weakened by being too close to the Sun's heat</term> Fortune aspects the degree of the Ascendant, the man may be able to prevent the native from being beheaded, or he will not be beheaded through his own fault. If the Fortune is not impeded, it will relieve the native from a bad death; he will pass away in his chosen state, but will die of a "head illness" <note>decapitali egritudine</note> arising from a hot cause, and this within his 50th year. 

If the conditions regarding Mars are not as stated, but a Malefic is in the 8th house, the native will die a bad death. But if a Fortune is there and not impeded, he will die in his own dwelling a common death. If that Fortune is impeded, he will die from some inconvenience coming upon him. And **Ptolemy** said in the *Centiloquium* that if the luminary that holds authority is in the **Midheaven** <note>The 10th house, representing public life and honors.</note>—I mean with the conditions aforesaid—the native will be **hanged**. 

If one of the Malefics is then in **Gemini** and the other in **Pisces**, they will cut off his hands or feet, according to the significance of the sign in which you find the more malicious planet. If Mars is bodily joined with the **Lord of the Ascendant** in **Leo**, and Mars has no dignity in the Ascendant, and none of the Fortunes are in the 8th house, it signifies the native will be **burned**. If Mars is then retrograde, combust, or falling, this will happen through his own fault. If he is not impeded, it will happen from a cause he did not deserve. 

And **Ptolemy** said that if Saturn is in a nativity—I mean in the Midheaven—and the one who is the **Anuba** is opposite him, and the fourth sign is "dry," the native will die from a **fall**. If it is "wet," he will **drown**. If it is in a "human form" sign, he will be **strangled**. Furthermore, if either of the Malefics (Mars or Saturn) is in the Ascendant at the hour of birth and is **peregrine** <term>peregrine: a planet with no essential dignity, like a wanderer with no home or status</term>, the native will have a mark or sign on his face or head. If the planet is impeded, retrograde, or combust, that mark or sign will be ugly. If it is free, it will not be ugly.

The text continues detailing how specific planetary configurations at birth (nativities) influence a person's character, professional success, and physical destiny. It specifically follows a discussion on the financial habits dictated by the Ascendant.</meta>

...not <note>original: "ni"</note>, or if Sagittarius [is the Ascendant], he will not be a good spender but rather stingy. Furthermore, he whose **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is Gemini or Virgo may lose his wealth <note>original: "substantiam"</note> and be impoverished by it. But he whose Ascendant is Sagittarius or Pisces will never lose it, nor will he be impoverished. Likewise, observe if the Ascendant is Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius, for the **native** <term>native: the person born under this specific astrological chart</term> will be greedy, most wretched, and loathsome. But if **Jupiter** <note>Jupiter is considered the "Great Benefic," a planet of luck and expansion.</note> aspects the Ascendant then, it diminishes that misery, yet does not take it away.

### Consideration 134.
Consideration 134 is to observe in nativities whether **Mars** and **Venus** are in the 6th house and are otherwise well-disposed; for this signifies that the native is destined to be a naturally perfect physician in every branch of medicine. And if **Mercury** is joined bodily with Venus and she is **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky; usually considered a weakening or complicating factor.</note>, it signifies that the native will be a naturally perfect singer. But if Mercury is in the 12th house and is not otherwise hindered, it signifies that he will be naturally wise in all sciences and philosophies.

### Consideration 135.
Consideration 135 is to observe in nativities whether the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet that rules the sign of the Ascendant.</note>, the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are all in the Ascendant, or if Jupiter and Venus aspect the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon in the Ascendant from a **trine or sextile aspect** <note>Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees.</note> and are not themselves hindered: for if it is so, it signifies that the native will be very strong in body, and that no one will dare to ignore his commands.

### Consideration 136.
Consideration 136 is to observe in the nativities of kings, the wealthy, and the great—those, that is, who are fit for rule—if both **Luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> are in the degrees of their **exaltations** <note>Specific signs where a planet's power is most highly "exalted" or amplified.</note> or in their own houses, in such a degree that one is in the same degree as the other, and they are free from all impediments: for this signifies that the native will attain to great and sublime dignities. He shall become the **King of the Romans** <note>A title often used for the Holy Roman Emperor-elect.</note> or the one closest in royal dignity after the King of the Romans, so that it may be said of him that he is like a universal king in the world; and this shall extend to the fourth generation of his descendants. But if all the planets that are under Jupiter commit their disposition to him, and he receives it from each one—notwithstanding the conditions mentioned before—and afterward he commits their disposition and his own to **Saturn**, and Saturn receives them, and both are **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> from the Sun and in **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the "power corners" of a chart.</note>, it signifies that the native is destined to be a man of great name and great power, though not royal. He will establish his name on the earth, and his fame will last for a long time during his whole life; and after his death, it will endure through three "kingdoms of Saturn" <note>Saturn's cycles, each lasting roughly 30 years; thus, about 90 years.</note> or perhaps more.

### Consideration 137.
Consideration 137 is to observe whether Mercury is joined with Saturn in the Ascendant, for it signifies that the native will be fully talkative and will wish to be thought wise; he will speak ill of everyone, both men and women. Whatever wisdom is found in him will be used to invent many lies and use them to his advantage; he will hardly ever be able to speak without mixing some falsehood into his words, so natural will it be for him to lie. He will be very foul-mouthed; he will have malice of the tongue from Saturn, and the sharpness of that malice from Mercury.

### Consideration 138.
Consideration 138 is to observe in nativities whether both **Malefics** <note>The "bad-luck" planets, Saturn and Mars.</note> are in the boundary of the fourth house of the nativity, or if the angles are in **moveable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs that initiate change.</note> and Mars and Saturn are in them: for it signifies that the native will be poor, wretched, and more unfortunate than all other unfortunate people for the whole

<column-break/>

duration of his life, unless Jupiter or the Lord of the **Triplicity** <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> of the Ascendant acts to the contrary.

### Consideration 139.
Consideration 139 is to observe in nativities, and similarly in **questions** <term>questions: "horary astrology," where a chart is cast for the moment a specific question is asked</term>, in which house the **Dragon’s Tail** <note>original: "cauda draconis." Also known as the South Node; it generally signifies points of loss, emptying, or past karma.</note> is found: for this signifies the emptying and destruction of the things signified by that house, and especially of profit. For if it is in the first house, it signifies the emptying of profit which the native makes through his own person. If it is in the second, the emptying of profit made with money or his substance. If it is in the third, the emptying of profit made with brothers, or because of brothers, or with neighbors or minor relatives. If it is in the fourth, the emptying of profit made with the father, or grandfather, or father-in-law, or inheritance; and it also signifies that the native or the **querent** <note>The person asking the question in a horary chart.</note> will change many houses for the sake of improvement, yet he will not remain settled in them, nor will that change turn out well for him. If it is in the fifth, the emptying of profit made with children or because of children. If it is in the sixth, the emptying of profit made with servants or small animals. If it is in the seventh, the emptying of profit made with women, partners, or enemies. If it is in the ninth, the emptying of profit made with religious people or because of religious matters. If it is in the tenth, the emptying of profit made because of dignity or offices. If it is in the eleventh, the emptying of profit made with friends or because of friends. But if it is in the twelfth, the emptying of profit made with large animals or because of hidden enemies.

### Consideration 140.
Consideration 140 is to observe whether the **significator** <note>The planet representing a specific person or topic in a chart.</note> of the end of a matter or its completion is so weak that it cannot finish the matter, nor the Moon likewise. Take then the significator of the querent and the significator of the thing sought, and subtract the smaller from the larger; add the remainder to the degree of the Ascendant, and whatever [sign] results, count that from the Ascendant. Where it falls, the Lord of that sign will be the significator of what you seek, according to the substance of the matter being considered; and you shall judge according to its state, whether it is assisted, very fortunate, or unfortunate and weak. For if the matter concerns substance and that planet is in the second house, the substance of the querent will be disposed according to its state. If it is in the third, it will dispose of brothers. If in the fourth, major relatives. If in the fifth, children. If in the sixth, domestic servants. If in the seventh, wives. If in the eighth, dowries. If in the ninth, long journeys. If in the tenth, his offices. If in the eleventh, friends. If in the twelfth, enemies.

### Consideration 141.
Consideration 141 is to observe in nativities and consider the gifts or fortunes given to men by the **fixed stars** <note>Stars that do not move like planets; they were thought to give sudden, intense, but sometimes unstable power.</note> and the manner of their durability in their subjects; and why they do not last as long in them as those given by the planets, even though they seem like they should last longer. I do not remember finding anything else said of this except what **Ptolemy** said in the *Centiloquium*: "Fixed stars give an exceeding manner [of fortune], but many times they end in evil." And **Almansor** <note>A reference to an Arabic astrological authority, likely Al-Mansur.</note> said in the chapters offered to the Great King of the Saracens: "Fixed stars give great gifts and elevate from poverty to sublimity, which the seven planets do not do." The gifts that fixed stars give to men do not last in them as long as those given by planets. This happens because the fixed stars are acting...
