<meta>This page continues Guido Bonatti's discussion on the length of human life and the specific influences of celestial bodies. It shifts from the general planetary influences to the profound but rare impact of the "fixed stars," explaining why their effects are seldom seen in individual human lives compared to long-lasting entities like cities.</meta>

...[beings] and men are the subjects. Thus, the subjects upon which the stars act are not always suited to them, nor are they naturally fit to receive their impression. For it is necessary that between the agent and the patient there be a proportion or some shared nature. The **fixed stars** <term>Fixed stars: stars that appear to stay in the same position relative to each other, as opposed to "wandering stars" or planets.</term>, indeed, move and change most slowly; and therefore their impressions require subjects or "patients" that correspond to them—those of the longest durability which have a proportionality with the stars, so that their effects can be perfected or completed in them. For the circular motion of the fixed stars is not completed in less than 36,000 years <note>The author is referring to the "precession of the equinoxes," which medieval astronomers calculated as taking 36,000 years to complete a full circle.</note>. 

But the circular motion of men lasts through three realms of **Saturn** (who is the slowest of the planets), which is a space of 90 years; few transcend that, which might happen to some through the addition of years of some planet to the years of the **Alcocoden** <term>Alcocoden: In traditional astrology, the planet that determines the length of a person's life based on the birth chart.</term> in the root of the nativity. Hence, for the most part, a long human life is 90 years, although some eighty-year-olds or perhaps ninety-year-olds measure themselves to be centenarians when in truth they are not; this has no true proportionality nor any similarity with 36,000 years for perfecting the effect of those [stellar] impressions. 

For just as an eagle cannot extend nor exercise the full measure of its flight or its power upon a fly, nor can a stone hurled from a **trebuchet** <note>original: "funda trabuchi"; a medieval siege engine used for throwing heavy stones.</note> exercise its force upon a gnat; so the fixed stars cannot exercise the completion or effect of their impressions upon men. And therefore their gifts or fortune do not last in men for long, because men are of most rapid change and small durability in respect to the circularity of the fixed stars.

And for this reason, it is said that the fixed stars exercise [their power] in the building of cities, but the planets in the building of houses; because cities are things of the longest durability among corruptible things compared to houses. Houses, indeed, are of long durability compared to men; yet houses do not last forever in their individual states. Cities, however, last through the successive building and rebuilding of houses. Fortresses, although they are of long durability, are not as great as cities. Hence we can use the superior planets in the building of fortresses; yet it is safer to use the fixed stars in their construction, because fortresses are of greater durability than houses, even though sometimes certain fortresses are destroyed. 

And because cities are of greater durability than fortresses, they are closer to the fixed stars of which they are the subjects; for a solid thing produces a greater effect in a more solid thing than in a less solid thing. Again, it lasts much less in a non-solid thing than in a somewhat solid thing; and again, much less in a slippery thing than in a non-solid or less slippery thing. Hence those impressions which the fixed stars make upon cities are of greater durability than those they make upon fortresses, because cities are more correlative to them in terms of length of time. And those they make upon fortresses are of greater durability than those they make upon houses, because fortresses are closer to their correlation than houses. The bodies of men, however, are more remote from those [celestial] bodies than houses are, and therefore more corruptible; for this reason, their significations apply to them less; and if they do apply, they last less. For the significations of the fixed stars are so great, so noble, so high, and so remote from corruption and mutability that they cannot quickly sustain a mutable mixture with things that corrupt quickly or change rapidly, except as oil with water; for although it may leave an impression on it, that impression does not last long.

<column-break/>

For the fixed stars are endowed with such nobility that, because of their most remote distance from these corruptible, vile, and rapidly changing things, and their proximity to the supreme splendor, their significations cannot remain in them or with them for long. This is especially true in men, since they change and perish easily and quickly—indeed, most rapidly—and especially in those of vile birth and weakness or smallness of heart. For they [the stars] do not transcend the persons of those they touch while they are living, and very rarely does it happen otherwise; and for the most part, it results in their downfall, and in such a way that only God, and no other, can turn it away—I say "for the most part" because sometimes they could end in good, although this happens very rarely. 

Just as it sometimes happens that some have lived through the maximum years of the *Alcocoden*, of whom in my time I have seen only one, who was called Richard, who said he had been in the court of **Charlemagne** <note>King of the Franks and Emperor of the Romans (r. 768–814).</note>, King of France, and had lived 400 years. And he said then that there was a certain other person who had been in the time of **Jesus Christ** and was called **John Buttadeus** <note>original: "Joannes buttadeus"; a legendary figure also known as the "Wandering Jew," said to have been cursed to walk the earth until the Second Coming for taunting Jesus.</note> because he had pushed the Lord when He was being led to the gallows; and He said to him, "You shall wait for me until I come." And I saw Richard at Ravenna in the year of Christ 1233; and that John passed through Forlì going to Saint James [Compostela] in the year of Christ 1267.

Nor would the significations of the fixed stars apply to men, nor could they adhere to them, nor would they last in them perceptibly, were it not for a medium through which they act upon them: the planets, which are the secondary agents, while the fixed stars are the principal agents. For wherever there are multiple ordered actions attributed to different agents, it is necessary that the principal action be attributed to the principal agent; for they stand in relation to the effects of corruptible things as the First Cause, while the planets are like the Second Cause. For the corruption which these lower things suffer is because of their excessive removal or distance from the incorruptible superior things, which are not said to have motion since they do not appear to move perceptibly.

However, they [the effects of fixed stars] sometimes endure in great men and the wealthy who are fit for kingdoms and are high-minded and strong of heart. One of these in my time was **Frederick II** <note>Frederick II (1194–1250), Holy Roman Emperor, a central figure in medieval politics and science whom Bonatti personally knew.</note>, Emperor of the Romans, who, although he was impoverished and placed in great necessity, became Emperor with no one able to resist him. He acquired for himself Apulia, the Kingdom of Sicily, and Jerusalem, Cracow, Italy, and Romania—the whole Empire except for part of Lombardy. He also subjugated all his enemies, traitors, and rebels, and remained in such a state for nearly thirty years. At last, however, he died miserably; he was poisoned by his own people, and his entire lineage was extirpated so that almost none of them remained at all.

There was also another, **Ezzelino da Romano** <note>A notoriously cruel Ghibelline leader and ally of Frederick II; he is often used as an example of a "tyrant" in medieval literature.</note>, who, although he was not of very high birth, was exalted greatly above all Italians, so that his fame crossed the sea and sounded through many regions. For he ruled nearly the entire March of Treviso even unto Germany and unto Trento and unto near Venice by four or five miles; and he stood as a tyrant in those parts, and his tyranny lasted for 26 years. At last, however, all these things ended in his ruin. For when it seemed impossible that he could be cast down, he fell into the hands of his greatest enemies in a certain battle he fought in the county of Milan at Cassano, and he died miserably, and his whole progeny was destroyed with no one remaining.

There was similarly a certain man from the kingdom of Apulia of vile birth named **Peter de Vinea** <note>original: "petrus de vinea"; Pier delle Vigne (c. 1190–1249), a diplomat and poet who became a powerful advisor to Frederick II before falling from grace.</note>, who, when he was a student at Bologna, used to beg and had nothing to eat; and afterward, he was made a notary, then the Prothonotary of the court of Emperor Frederick II...

<summary>This page explores why the massive, slow cycles of the fixed stars rarely influence individual humans, who are too short-lived and "corruptible," but instead govern the fates of cities and empires. It cites the dramatic lives and falls of contemporary figures like Frederick II and Ezzelino da Romano as rare examples of this celestial power in action.</summary>

He reached such sublimity that he claimed to have raised eighteen people from the dead—though this could not be seen by anyone—and he claimed to cure every infirmity and drive away demons. I, however, was never able to see anyone delivered, though I studied much to see it; nor could I find anyone who would say firmly that they had seen any of his miracles. Yet it seemed as if the whole world was rushing after him. A person was considered blessed if they could have even a small thread from his hood, and it was kept as a holy relic. The Bolognese went about armed with him and around him for the common good, surrounding him with wooden barriers wherever he went so that no one could approach him. If any did approach him, they were treated badly: for some they slaughtered, others they wounded, and others they beat severely with clubs. He himself rejoiced and was glad at the slaughter, beatings, and woundings, and he healed no one.

**Consideration 142.** is that you should look in nativities <term>Nativity: an astrological birth chart</term> or in universal questions at the gifts or fortune given to men by the planets. These are attached to them and last with them longer, and extend to their successors if they were so disposed in the roots of their nativities; but they do not exceed moderation unless perhaps they are attached to fortunate **fixed stars**. This is because planets are of rapid mutability; hence they have a greater affinity with things of shorter duration than those gifts given by the fixed stars. This is especially true of the fortune given by the **inferior planets** <term>Inferior planets: In medieval astronomy, those closer to Earth than the Sun (Moon, Mercury, Venus)</term> because of their greater speed and their conformity with the subjects related to them. The fortune given by the **superior planets** <term>Superior planets: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</term> does not last as long in men as the aforementioned, yet they are worth more than others in the building of houses.

### ¶ Concerning the fortunes given by Saturn and the other planets.

For **Saturn**, when he is oriental, well-disposed, and fortunate (that is, strong and received in the place where he is), gives great fortune in buildings, the planting of trees, long durability in ruling over the cultivation of lands, in the production of waters, and similar things.

¶ **Jupiter**, indeed, gives great fortune in the sciences, such as laws, decrees, and decretals, and in dignities such as judgeships, bishoprics, and the like.

<margin>Mars</margin>
¶ **Mars**, however, gives great fortune in the raising of armies and their leadership, and similar things.

¶ The **Sun** gives great fortune in secular dignities, such as kingdoms, the government of cities, the office of podestà <note>The high-ranking magistrate or governor of a medieval Italian city</note>, and the like.

¶ The **Inferior Planets** give their great fortune in things attached to men and more durable in these corruptible things which are within cities and castles than the superior planets do, because of their proximity to them and their quick and rapid change and correlation with them.

¶ **Venus**, who is a planet above the lower ones, gives her fortune in those things which pertain to the affairs of women, such as ornaments and the seduction of them so they do not guard themselves, and profit because of them, and similar things.

¶ **Mercury**, however, gives his fortune from merchandise, writings, paintings, and things to come, and the like.

¶ The **Moon**, indeed, gives her fortune from navigation and merchandise (which are often mentioned in writings and paintings), the planting of vineyards, the sale of wine or the drinking of it, and also trade and similar things.

All these things provide excellence if they attach to those to whom they were naturally given by the planets, as I have said. And although the significations of the celestial bodies attach to men, they do not always last in them; yet the significations of the inferior planets last longer than the significations of the superior ones, and the significations of the superior ones last longer than those of the fixed stars. The significations or fortunes or riches given through the Moon can last up to the seventh age or generation, because she is the seventh planet after Saturn, counting from the superior ones. If they transcend the seventh, they cannot transcend the eighth, setting an "age" or "generation" at between 42 and 45 years, so that both are included. Those given through Mercury can last until the sixth age, because he is the sixth planet after Saturn; they certainly cannot transcend the seventh...

However, those things given through **Venus** can last until the fifth age <note>The author uses "age" to mean a generation or a specific epoch of time.</note> because she is the fifth planet from Saturn. They cannot, however, transcend the sixth, and can scarcely reach it. Those things given through the **Sun** can last until the fourth age because he is the fourth planet after Saturn; they cannot transcend the fifth and can scarcely reach it. Those things given through **Mars** can last until the third age because he is the third planet after Saturn; they cannot transcend the fourth and can scarcely reach it. Those things given through **Jupiter** can last until the second age because he is the second planet after Saturn; they cannot transcend the third and can scarcely reach it. Those things, indeed, given through **Saturn** can last for one age; they cannot transcend the second and can scarcely, if ever, reach it. 

And although they can last longer, I do not say that they do not end sooner; for authority has said that there are fixed limits <note>original: "termini"</note> which cannot be passed, but it did not say that they cannot be reached earlier; so it is in these matters. I say, in fact, that they cannot transcend those limits mentioned above without either being utterly destroyed or so depressed that they remain in such a state that they will not resemble the former state, except as green or blackish compares to the purest white—unless perhaps something new happens from elsewhere, which happens rarely; nor can it truly be said that it is the same thing, but rather it will be something different from the first. 

And from the aforementioned, there were some who wished to say that such riches or similar things could be called "ill-gotten" <note>original: "male queste"</note>; and from this comes the discussion of what laypeople say about ill-gotten gains: "their destruction is near." For they say that ill-gotten gains do not transcend the fifth age, and some say they do not transcend the third, being ignorant of where they get this idea, unless they have heard it from others long ago and because they have seen it often happen so. Yet this does not lack some degree of reason under the conditions mentioned—namely, that ill-gotten gains do not transcend the third or fifth age. I understand "ill-gotten gains" to be wealth that came to someone by way of <term>usury</term> <note>original: "fenerationis," the practice of lending money at interest, often condemned in this period.</note> and through matters in which many lies, many deceptions, robberies, thefts, and the like are committed.

### Consideration 143.
Is that you should consider the manner of judging: and by which paths it is necessary for you to arrive at a judgment so that you can examine it and discuss it rightly, and according to what the stars show you, to reveal the truth of it. The method of this consideration is this: you shall look at this in 14 ways.

¶ **The first way** is whether the <term>querent</term> <note>The person asking the question of the astrologer.</note> asks with true intention or not. For if the Lord of the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> and the Lord of the Hour are the same, or if the signs in which the aforementioned significators are found are of the same triplicity or the same complexion, the question is made with true intent. If it is not so, or if the Ascendant is at the very end of a sign, the question is not from true intent nor is it "radical" <note>An "unradical" chart was considered invalid or premature for judgment by medieval astrologers.</note>.

¶ **Second**, you shall look at the Ascendant and its Lord, and the **Moon**, and the planet from which she separates, and you shall give these to the querent. The **seventh house**, however, and the planet to which the Moon is joined, you shall give to the "quesited" <note>The person or thing being asked about.</note> as is said elsewhere; and if necessary, descend to persons according to how things are signified through the houses from the first to the twelfth.

¶ **Third**, you shall consider the house or sign signifying the matter questioned.

¶ **Fourth**, the aspect of good or bad planets to the significators of the matters questioned.

¶ **Fifth**, in what place from its own house each significator is found: whether in itself, or in the second, or in the third, or in the fourth, and so on up to the twelfth; or if it is found in the <term>Combust Way</term> <note>original: "via combusta," a specific section of the zodiac (late Libra/early Scorpio) considered unlucky or turbulent.</note> or in similar places.

¶ **Sixth**, whether it is found in the angles, succedents,

<column-break/>

or cadent houses <note>The "angles" (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses) were the strongest positions in a chart; "cadent" houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) were the weakest.</note>.

¶ **Seventh**, attend diligently to where help for the querents may come from—namely, whether from a father, or son, or king, or kinsmen, or friends, etc.; for good significators will judge good, but evil ones the contrary.

¶ **Eighth**, by the joy of the querent: as if the Lord of the first is found in the fifth or elsewhere joined with its Lord without the impediment of malefic planets; or by his sorrow: as if he is found in the sixth, or seventh, or eighth, or twelfth, unless the question is about matters signified by those houses; for according to what you find there, so shall you judge.

¶ **Ninth**, by the <term>fortunes</term> or <term>infortunes</term> <note>Benefic planets (Jupiter, Venus) or Malefic planets (Saturn, Mars).</note> according to how you find them in the places signifying the matters of the questions. For instance, if there are more fortunes, it is good; but if there are more evils, it is bad; if they are equal, you shall judge it as mediocre.

¶ **Tenth**, as if the Lord of the first were in the house of the matter questioned or joined anywhere with its Lord.

¶ **Eleventh**, that you consider in which house the Lord of the first was joined with the significator of the matter questioned; for by the significator of that house or the occasion of it, you will be able to judge the things to come.

¶ **Twelfth**, that if the significators are not joined, but some planet <term>translates light</term> <note>An astrological term for when a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "carrying" the influence between them.</note> between them or receives their disposition, you shall judge the same.

¶ **Thirteenth**, through the nature of the significators themselves, according to whether they agree with each other in their natures and significations.

¶ **Fourteenth**, according to whether the receiver of the disposition is a fortune or infortune, strong or weak, and whether it regards the significators or the Moon or any of them from friendship or enmity, you shall pronounce judgment.

### Consideration 144.
Is that you consider in questions or in **birth charts** <note>original: "natiuitatib," literally "nativities."</note> or other beginnings, when the significators do not show you clearly what you intend to know and their meaning is ambiguous such that you cannot weigh it well: take the place of the Lord of the Ascendant and the place of the Lord of the Moon’s house; and see the distance in degrees between them, starting from Aries, from which you shall make signs, and add the degrees of the ascending sign above it and cast it from the Ascendant, both by day and by night. And where the number ends, the Lord of that house will be the significator, and from him you shall take the meaning of the matter questioned; for according to his condition, you will be able to judge.

### Consideration 145.
Is that you look in daytime births if the **Heart of the Lion** <note>The star Regulus, the most important "royal" fixed star.</note> is in the Ascendant—that is, on the eastern line, or one degree above it, or three degrees below it—or if it is in the tenth house in similar degrees without the conjunction or aspect of any benefic planet. For this will signify that the native <note>The person born at that time.</note> will be of great name and great power, exceedingly exalted, and will arrive at sublime dignities, even if he is found to be born of the most base parents. And if any of the fortunes <note>Benefic planets.</note> regard the place, his sublimity will be increased even more. If, however, the birth is at night, it will be something less than this, but not by much. But if the malefics regard it, it will be much less. If the fortunes regard it, they will increase the goodness by a fourth part and diminish the malice by a fourth part. Take note: whatever of the aforementioned happens, it signifies that the native will die an evil death, or at least all his sublimity and all his greatness and power will end in evil.

Where the number ends, the Lord of that sign will be a partner to the Lord of the question and will be called the "first partner." Again, look...

If the question appears to be good, but those participants are poorly disposed, they will diminish the good that is signified by the question. But if they are well-disposed, they will increase the good. If, however, the question is found to be bad, and those participants are found to be well-disposed, they will diminish the evil signified by the question. If they are poorly disposed, they will increase it. ### Sixth Treatise on the parts of judgments, or introductions, given as a brief summary for the judgments of the stars.

### Chapter One.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'C' featuring a floral arrangement in a vase within a square frame.</image-desc>

**W**hen you intend to arrive at astronomical judgments, let it be your concern first to consider whether he who comes to you to move a question does so with sincere intent <note>original: "ex intentione"</note> or not, as is said elsewhere. It is similarly discussed there how you might know whether he asks out of intent or not; however, I will touch upon certain things here that are not touched upon there. For if the **Lord of the Ascendant** and the **Lord of the Hour** <note>The planet ruling the specific hour of the day when the question is asked.</note> are of the same **triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> or the same complexion, or if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Hour are the same, the question will be from sincere intent and "radical" <note>A "radical" question is one where the chart is considered fit for judgment because the alignment of the heavens matches the reality of the seeker's situation.</note>. If it is otherwise, it does not seem to be from intent or radical, unless perhaps in a sudden case. 

You shall attribute the Ascendant to the searcher; and if it is necessary for you to descend to the person, you will perceive the sign that signifies the thing sought and the planet ruling that sign. Carefully observe the aspect of the significators, and also the conjunction of the fortunes <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus.</note> and the malefics <note>Malefic planets like Saturn and Mars.</note> to the significators by body or by aspect. And know that the bodily conjunction of the **Sun** is more harmful than other impediments; this is called **combustion** <note>original: "combustio"; when a planet is so close to the Sun (usually within 8.5 degrees) that its power is said to be "burned up" or hidden.</note>. Likewise, you shall consider whether the significator of the searcher or of the thing sought is in its own house, or in any house from it, and whether it is free from impediments or not, and that it is not in the **combusted way** <note>original: "via combusta"; a specific section of the zodiac (traditionally late Libra to early Scorpio) considered unlucky or turbulent.</note>.

<column-break/>

Similarly, consider whether the significators—among which the **Moon** is always to be counted—are in strong places, weak places, or middling ones; and whether they are at the beginning of the houses, in the middle, or at their ends. You will see the faithful helpers of the significators and their rebels, each according to its being. When all these things have been diligently considered, you will be able to weigh the judgment of the question proposed to you: for the fortunes signify good, while the malefics will announce the opposite evil. If, however, you find equal fortunes and malefics, they will portend a middling judgment. But if the fortunes prevail, it is a good fortune; if the malefics, the opposite is to be judged. 

You shall also consider the person of the searcher: how and by what manner it concerns each of the questioners to ask; whether the questioner asks by himself and for himself, or through another and for another; and through which houses the searchers and the sought persons are signified; and similarly what is signified by each house, the meanings of which you have above in the chapter on the significations of the twelve houses.

### Chapter Two: How one should arrive at judgments.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'Q' containing foliate scrollwork within a square frame.</image-desc>

**S**ince judging the future is most difficult—and that this is true is clear from the considerations assigned to you above—**Hippocrates** <note>original: "ypocras"</note> did not wish to call judgment difficult in vain, because nothing in the world is more difficult than to predict the truth about future things. Before you arrive at judgments, it is necessary that I tell you certain things regarding the business of judgments, without which I believe it would be impossible for you to know how to judge according to the truth of the process, although I made some mention of it to you above. 

For it is first necessary to know which are the causes that perfect matters, and which of them show the truth; and which are those that prohibit them from being perfected; and from which causes the effects of things happen; and from which their detriment happens; and the signification of each thing that perfects, and also the destruction or prohibition of each cause. You must also know which signify the time when they ought to be perfected, or when they ought to be destroyed or prohibited, before you presume to judge. And this is the office which the Most High Creator gave to all the planets and signs and also the fixed stars. 

And **Messahala** <note>An 8th-century Jewish-Persian astrologer and astronomer who was a primary source for medieval European astrology.</note> and several others said that the effect and detriment of things in this world primarily happen in three ways. First, namely, that the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the thing sought and the Moon be joined together. Second, if the aforesaid significators are not joined together, that there be some planet that **transfers light** <note>original: "transferat lumen"; a condition where a fast planet moves from a conjunction with one significator to a conjunction with another, "carrying" the influence between them.</note> between them—namely, that it separates from one and joins to the other. Third, that there be a **collection of light** <note>original: "collectio luminis"; when two significators are not in aspect with each other, but both are moving toward an aspect with a third, heavier planet.</note> by some high planet that is heavier than them, and they both join to it, and each of them commits its disposition to it, for it is that planet which perfects the matter. And it happens sometimes that a matter is perfected according to the whole will of the questioner; sometimes it is perfected in part; sometimes neither in whole nor in part. I will explain all these things to you so that you may better understand and know how you can judge the matters occurring to you.

### On the explanation of the first mode.

<image-desc>Small decorative woodcut initial 'E' with foliage within a square frame.</image-desc>

**T**he explanation of the first mode, when a matter is perfected, is when the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon join with the Lord of the thing sought; for then the matter is perfected.

The matter would be more effectively completed if the <term>querent</term><note>The person asking the astrological question.</note> sought the thing for another rather than for himself. This is because although he joined himself by a <term>trine aspect</term><note>An auspicious 120-degree angle between planets, considered very harmonious.</note>, Saturn did not receive him with perfect <term>reception</term><note>A state where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting cooperation or "hospitality" between them.</note>. This mode of completing a matter is lasting.

### Concerning another mode of completing matters.

There is also another mode of completing matters which can be called "subordinate" to the preceding one; it is neither lasting nor perfect. This occurs, for instance, if two planets are joined to another planet heavier than themselves and commit the disposition and power to it—just as was said of Jupiter and the Sun, how they committed their power to Saturn—and that heavier planet which received the disposition is "impeded." This means it is <term>falling</term><note>Located in a weak "house" of the chart.</note>, <term>retrograde</term><note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, often signifying delays or reversals.</note>, <term>combust</term><note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns" up the planet's power.</note>, or joined to a "malefic" <note>Usually Mars or Saturn, planets associated with challenge or hardship.</note> who hinders it, or if it is besieged by malefics. I say that in such a case, it cannot complete the matter; or if it does sometimes complete it, the matter will be destroyed after it has been finished and will not remain in its perfection. Thus, you may judge for the person who asks you: it seems that this matter may be completed, but it will be destroyed after it is finished.

### Concerning certain other accidents of matters that are completed.

Something else occasionally happens in matters that are completed: namely, that some are achieved with heaviness, hardship, labor, and great effort; some are achieved with ease; some with constant petitioning and persistence; some with petitioning but without great persistence; and some are achieved without any petitioning or hardship—indeed, they come unexpectedly.

### Concerning those things that come easily.

Those things that come easily, without petitioning or any hardship—as if unlooked for—are when the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>The planet ruling the person asking the question.</note> (or the significator of the querent) and the significator of the thing sought are joined by a trine or sextile aspect with reception.

### Concerning those things that happen quickly.

Those things that happen quickly and without petitioning—even if there is no prior hope for them—occur when the Lord of the Ascendant joins with the Lord of the thing sought by a trine aspect without reception, or by a <term>sextile</term><note>A 60-degree angle, considered helpful and pleasant.</note> with reception.

### Concerning those things that happen with petitioning.

Those things that happen with petitioning and the effort of the querent are when the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with the significator of the thing sought by a <term>fourth aspect</term><note>A "Square" (90-degree angle), which indicates friction or the need for action.</note> with reception, or by a sextile without reception.

### Concerning those things that happen with petitioning, effort, and labor.

Furthermore, those things that happen with petitioning, effort, persistence, great labor, and urgency are when the significator of the querent is joined with the significator of the thing sought by an <term>opposition</term><note>A 180-degree angle, representing conflict or difficult confrontation.</note> or by a square aspect without reception.

### Concerning those things that happen with labor yet are scarcely completed.

<column-break/>

Those things that happen with the greatest labor, persistence, petitioning, effort, anguish, and anxiety—likewise with sadness and as if after the despair of friends and relatives—and yet are scarcely or never completed (and if they are completed, their effect will be delayed a long time and come with great expense) are those in which the Lord of the Ascendant (or the Moon) and the Lord of the thing sought are joined by an opposition without reception.

### When a matter which someone wants happens without his reception.

There is also another mode by which a matter someone intends to have may be completed; it is easier than all the other modes mentioned. That is, if the significator of that matter is joined to the significator of the one desiring it by a sextile aspect with reception, or by a trine without reception, or if the significator of the matter is in the Ascendant or in the "House" signifying the person for whom the matter is desired. Understand the same regarding a physical conjunction as you do for aspects: in that case, the matter happens most joyfully.

### When the thing sought is a magistracy or dignity.

If the thing being sought is a <term>magistracy</term><note>A public office or position of authority.</note> or a secular dignity which one hopes for from someone—and the questioner has hoped for this from a King or from some other lord of his—and the significator of the aforementioned thing is in the Ascendant, or joined to the Lord of the Ascendant or to the Moon by a trine or sextile aspect (or bodily conjunction) and with reception: it signifies that he will complete the matter without his own petition or that of another on his behalf.

### When something is hoped for from some nobleman, how the matter will happen.

And if someone hopes for something from someone who is below the rank of a King—or from some friend of his, or from the community of some land, or similar—that matter will happen and will come about by a fortunate chance.

### When neither conjunction nor aspect intervenes.

If, however, there is no aspect of conjunction between them, but there is a <term>translation of light</term><note>When a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "carrying" the influence between two planets that don't see each other.</note>, the matter will happen through the hands of messengers (legates) who involve themselves in it so that it may be completed. To know who those messengers are, look to the House whose Lord is the significator of either planet, or from the Houses in which you find them, just as has been sufficiently told to you. It would be tedious to describe that everywhere. Look then similarly to the Moon: if she was then separated from the significator of the one desiring the thing (or even from the querent), and was joined to the significator of the thing, it signifies that those who run between them will come from the side of the one desiring the thing, and by his knowledge and will. If, however, she was separated from the planet signifying the thing and was joined to the significator of the one desiring it, it signifies that the completion comes from the side of the matter itself, or from those who are able to complete it. And if the matter is completed through messengers, those messengers will be the kinds of persons signified by the Houses of which they are Lords. Look then at which persons are signified by those Houses, and judge according to them—whether it be a member of the household, a brother, a neighbor, a father, a son, a servant, a partner, an associate, a religious person, a King or ruler, a friend, or a hidden enemy. You should know that although I said matters are completed by trine or sextile aspects, this must be understood reasonably: for if the place from which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon "aspects" the Lord of the thing sought (through which it is signified), or the place from which the Lord or significator of the thing aspects the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is the <term>detriment</term><note>A sign where a planet is traditionally weak or ill-at-ease, usually the sign opposite the one it rules.</note> of the planet looking at it, the matter is not completed. This is true even if the aspect is a sextile or trine. For example: let the Ascendant be Leo, and the question be about whether a marriage would be completed or not. If the Sun is joined to Saturn, or the Moon (which has to signify the woman) is in Aries—which is the detriment <note>original: "detrimentum Saturni"; technically Saturn is in its "Fall" in Aries, but the author uses the term broadly for planetary weakness.</note> of Saturn—although the aspect itself is with reception, Saturn nevertheless does not complete the matter; rather, he hinders it so that it is not completed...

...not only hinders it, but rather strives to destroy it if it can. If it were joined to him in Cancer or Leo, it would do the same, as both of those are its **fall**<note>original: "casus"; a position of planetary weakness where a planet loses its influence.</note>. Similarly, if the **significator**<note>The planet representing either the person asking or the thing being asked about.</note> of any matter, or the Moon, should join the Sun in Libra (which is its **descension**) or in Aquarius (which is its **fall**), then the Sun would not receive either of them; thus it would destroy the matter and not permit it to be completed. The same applies if it joins Venus in Scorpio, Aries, or Virgo; or Jupiter in Capricorn, Gemini, or Virgo. You should understand the **detriment**<note>original: "detrimentum"; a sign opposite the one a planet naturally rules, causing it to be "out of its element."</note> of any planet in this way: no **aspect**<note>The angular relationship between planets.</note> is of value then unless **reception**<note>original: "receptio"; a cooperative state where one planet is "hosted" by another.</note> intervenes, which breaks that malice.

Understand this same principle if the significator or the Moon joins a planet that is in the detriment of that significator or the Moon: for example, if Mercury is the significator and joins a planet in Sagittarius or Pisces; or if the Moon joins a planet in Scorpio or Capricorn. Whether a planet joins another planet in its own descension, or one in its descension joins the one whose descension it is, it always strives to destroy the matter and annul it.

¶ There is also another thing that causes fear in these matters: if the planet that is the significator of the matter is an **unfortunate**<note>original: "infortuna"; a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> and shows that the matter ought to be completed through a square aspect or an opposition, the **querent**<note>The person asking the question.</note> fears that some injury may happen to them because of it. Thus, they would rather the matter not be completed at all than have it completed this way.

¶ But if there is a **trine** or **sextile** aspect with reception, it will be safe; without reception, however, it will not be safe, but rather as bad as the person feared—though perhaps not as safe as the querent would wish.

¶ Furthermore, if the significator of the querent and the significator of the matter are the same planet (as happens frequently) and it is not **received** in the place where it is, it signifies that the matter should not be completed. But if it is received, it signifies that the matter should be completed with a good perfection—unless the one that received it is hindered by **fall**, **combustion**, or **retrogradation**. In such cases, although it happens, it is not completed with as good a perfection as when it is not hindered.

¶ There is another way significator planets are helped to complete a matter: namely, that the signs agree in nature with the planets so that they assist them and some planets offer their "testimony" to them.

¶ And **Zael**<note>original: "Zael"; referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician.</note> said that it is necessary for the **ascendant**<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> to be a fixed or common sign. Understand that the ascendant must be differentiated according to the variety of persons, beginning from the first house through to the twelfth. The **angles**<note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> should not be remote but firm; that is, the 10th house should be the tenth sign from the ascendant, and the angle of the earth (the 4th house) should be the fourth sign from the ascendant, so that the 8th house is not the ninth sign from the ascendant, nor the 4th house the third sign from the ascendant.

### ¶ Chapter 3. By which significations it is known whether things ought to be completed.

You must also know the significations by which it is similarly known whether a matter should be completed or not. The first of these is the **Lord of the Ascendant**<note>The planet that rules the sign on the eastern horizon.</note>. The second is the Moon, since at other times she is the participant in every matter. The third is the planet signifying the matter sought. When all these are joined together, they signify the effect of the matter entirely in the houses signifying the matter. Always remember to differentiate the ascendants as I told you. If two of them—namely the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter, or the Moon and the Lord of the matter sought—are joined together, it signifies the matter will be two-thirds finished. If only one of them has "testimony," it signifies the matter will be completed for the querent by one third. Understand this in matters that allow for division; for in those matters that cannot be divided, it will either happen entirely or not at all. If, however, in matters that cannot be divided, you have two of the aforementioned testimonies, announce the total effect of the matter sought. If you have only one of them, it can rarely or never be completed; and if it were completed, it would happen

<column-break/>

with heaviness, slowness, great labor, and entanglement—like a marriage, which either happens entirely or does not happen at all, and similar things (if I say the marriage were a single one). For if there were many marriages at once, as sometimes happens when someone asks about several women and several men—such as when someone asks for themselves and for a partner, a brother, a son, or someone else—then some of them can be completed and some not, according to the significations and testimonies you see occurring in the question. These three testimonies or significations must be considered in every matter; if all are "safe," the matter will undoubtedly be completed for the querent entirely.

They will be "safe" when the significators are free from **combustion**<note>original: "combustione"; being too close to the Sun, which "burns up" a planet's power.</note>, **fall**, **retrogradation**, and from the square aspect or opposition of **malefics**<note>original: "malorum"; typically Saturn or Mars.</note> and their "obsession," as well as from a bodily conjunction with their lords—namely the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the matter sought—which happens rarely. And if, in addition to being safe, they are received by **fortunes**<note>original: "fortunis"; beneficial planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note> from any aspect, the matter will be completed and for the good.

¶ If they are received by a **fortune**, the good will be further increased, so much so that the querent will not know how to ask for anything better, nor would they believe that the matter they sought could be completed so perfectly. Do not object to these words, as they apply to everyone and serve every question and every matter which someone intends to do. Consideration of the fixed stars, whether helpful or harmful, is found only in the chapter speaking of them.

## Here begins the treatise on the principal judgments of astronomy.
### ¶ First chapter, which signifies the person of the querent and what may happen to them regarding any question and any matter they intend to do or begin, according to what pertains to them to ask or begin, and similarly concerning those things which naturally seem to look toward this.

-> <image-desc>An ornamental woodcut initial letter 'I' containing two human figures amidst floral and leaf patterns.</image-desc> <-

In this first chapter, we must deal with those things that pertain to the **first house** or seem to look toward it, which is the **ascending sign**. It signifies the querent, insofar as the question pertains to them, and I will tell you certain things you need to know about this. Questions can be diverse and made in diverse ways, according to how their qualities have diversified them. For questions can be diversified according to their essence: as if one was about one thing and another was different from it.

¶ They can also be diverse according to other different significations: for someone asks one way when they ask for themselves, and another way when they ask for another. And I will tell you how you ought to look at each one similarly, and which house to look at when someone asks. For it is not necessary that you always look at the first house as the ascendant significator of every question.

¶ But perhaps you might say: why did the ancient wise men not set down what you are saying? The cause of this was that they left it to the industry of the wise. They were not speaking then to those who needed introduction, but to those already introduced and advanced, to the wise and the instructed. For if someone asks about themselves, you should look at the first house.

¶ But if they ask about their own **substance**<note>original: "substantia"; wealth, money, or possessions.</note> or about other significations of the **second house**, you should look at the second.

¶ If they ask about brothers or other significations of the **third house**, you should look at the third.

¶ If they ask about the father or other significations of the **fourth house**, you should look at the fourth.

¶ If it is about children or other significations of the **fifth house**, you should look at the fifth.

¶ If they ask about servants or other significations of the **sixth house**, you should look at the sixth.

## Chapter 2: How you should examine the "shadows" when questions are put to you.

When you are asked about any matter regarding which the questioner wishes to pose a query: take the altitude of the sun if the question is asked during the day. If, however, it is at night, observe the altitude of some fixed star placed upon the **astrolabe**<note>A sophisticated hand-held instrument used by astronomers and astrologers to calculate the positions of celestial bodies and tell time.</note> or with another instrument suited for this, as accurately as you possibly can, immediately and without any delay or any intermediate action, at the very moment the words leave the mouth of the one asking the question. And take care that you do not deviate in any way, lest an error fall into the matter about which the question was moved to you. And observe the method I told you regarding the examination of that house which signifies the thing sought. 

Similarly, take care not to mix different matters asked at different times together. For if a question is put to you—let us say, about marriage—and when you have grasped it, and later that same person or perhaps another moves another question to you, whatever it may be, do not mix it with the other already received; for the **ascendant**<term>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the precise moment of the query</term> has already changed, and thus it is necessary that the judgment change. In this way, you could be blamefully deceived in your judgment. Alternatively, you can take up the new question with its own proper altitude, and it will be a different judgment from the first. 

Nevertheless, you can accept several questions from several different chapters under a single ascendant if the questioner has meditated upon them and held them in his mind for one day, or for a day and a night—provided the whole heaven revolves at least once—so long as the questions are diverse, such that one is not about the same material as another. And take care similarly lest he who asks comes to you for the sake of testing or deceiving you, as some are sometimes accustomed to do, or if he has held the question in his heart for a day and a night, as has been mentioned elsewhere if you remember well. For matters turn out according to the amount of concern, hope, and trust of the questioner. For when someone asks about a matter, the houses and the locations of the planets and their arrangement signify what will happen regarding the thing he seeks for the entire duration of his life. 

It is similar in **nativities**<note>Birth charts; the study of a person's life based on their moment of birth.</note>, although nativities are sometimes altered by the revolution of the years, sometimes by increase and sometimes by decrease. This is also true in universal questions about the fortune of someone, whether the question is for a lifetime or determined for a year, a month, or several weeks or days, and such things; since every agent intends some end for its acts and acts according to the requirement of the intended ends and according to the end which it foresaw. And let it be known to you: that everyone who asks only asks about that which the planets, signs, and their arrangement—whether for good or evil—overcome in the "root" of that person's birth.

## Chapter 3: What is the trunk and what are the branches of this tree.

For the questions are the trunks of this tree, and the considerations which you must have regarding 

<column-break/>

the questions are its branches. Thus, by observing, you will see how the **lord of the ascendant**<note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note> of any question, nativity, or beginning of any matter is favored; and how the Moon is favored; and how the lord of the house signifying the matter sought is favored. For no one asks about a thing unless it is arising for you now, unless perhaps they ask knowingly to test you. No one should look, as was said elsewhere: for no one is born or asks in a good hour and under a good and fortunate ascendant except a fortunate person whom good things and fortune ought to surround. And no one is born or asks under an evil and unfortunate ascendant except an unfortunate man whom evils and misfortunes ought to surround. It is from this that we see some people are fortunate and some are unfortunate.

## Chapter 4: That an astrologer should not examine questions for himself.

It seemed wise to the ancient sages, and especially to **Masha'allah**<note>original: "mesahale"; an influential 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer whose works were central to medieval European astrology.</note>, that an astrologer should not examine questions for himself, lest he be deceived in his own affairs. For a man can hardly be without some personal bias regarding his own ascendant. Therefore, he ought to ask another person according to the method predicted. After another has received his question, the astrologer may then look at the chart for himself to judge it; or he may give his question to another, either in writing or without writing, provided that the other person is concerned about his matter and brings it back to him later of his own accord. Or he may set it in his mind, saying: "When such a sign occurs to me, let it be the ascendant for the question I intend to make for myself," and it will be just as valid. 

Therefore, if it is a true question that ought to endure or be stable, or which ought to improve or worsen, or be quickly finished or altered, one must then look at the lord of the ascendant. See whether he is joined to the lord of the matter sought, or the lord of the matter sought is joined to him, and by what **aspect**<note>The angular relationship between two planets.</note>. For if they are joined by a **trine or sextile**<note>original: "trino vel sextili"; aspects of 120 and 60 degrees, considered harmonious and helpful.</note> and in an **angle**<note>A powerful position in the chart (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses).</note>, or coming from an angle or from succeeding houses, it signifies the success of the matter sought. It also signifies its durability, stability, and improvement. This is even better if the aspect occurs with **reception**<note>original: "receptione"; a condition where a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting, implying mutual support.</note>, for then it signifies the full goodness of the matter without any decrease. 

If, however, the aspect is a **square**<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually indicating tension or obstacles.</note>, it will greatly diminish the intention of the seeker and the goodness and durability of the matter itself, even if it occurs with reception. It will also diminish if it is a trine or sextile without reception, though more mildly. If it is a square or **opposition**<note>An aspect of 180 degrees, often signifying conflict or total failure.</note> without reception, it signifies the destruction of the matter and that no good or durability will be in it. 

And if the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the matter sought are joined to some planet that is heavier (slower) than them, and that planet receives their arrangement and aspects the ascendant, or aspects some planet that aspects the ascendant and has some dignity in it and is not itself hindered, it signifies goodness and the success of the matter, along with durability and stability. But if the receiver of the arrangement does not aspect the ascendant, nor is joined to a planet that aspects the ascendant from its place, it will be evil; for it signifies annulment, malice, and the destruction of the matter. If, however, the lord of the ascendant is heavier than the lord of the matter sought, and the lord of the matter is joined to him with a good aspect—or any aspect except opposition—with perfect reception, it signifies the goodness and durability of the matter. Similarly, if the lord of the matter sought is heavier than the lord of the ascendant, and the lord of the ascendant is joined to him with reception...

Then I began to work through the moon, which was in opposition to Jupiter, the significator of the thing sought. ...its perfections: and if it were destroyed in a bad way and not quietly, it will endure: since their aspect is from an opposition: and each significator is impeded.

## Chapter 5: How one must inspect the planets that impede matters from being completed.

<margin>
One must inspect the
impeding planet,
lest it [the matter] happen.
</margin>

Although perhaps it might seem more convenient to place this chapter elsewhere, it nevertheless seems to me that it should be placed here; for if it were delayed until the treatise on **nativities**<note>Birth charts.</note>, you might need it in many places. For it does not have a place only in nativities, but indeed in all **interrogations**<note>Questions asked of an astrologer; "horary" astrology.</note>, in all journeys, and in all beginnings of whatever things we sometimes wish to do. And it is so that you may look at the planet that impedes things so they do not happen or are not completed. That planet can be called "strongly harmful," or "prohibiting," or "destroying," or "**the hider**"<note>original: "abscondis" or "abscondentem" — a planet that conceals or brings a matter to an end prematurely.</note>; for it is he who hides the life of the newborn and destroys it, nor permits the newborn to arrive at a long life (that is, to old age), and who corrupts a matter and destroys it after it is thought to be perfected, and when it is seen that it ought to be completed. He is the one whom our ancestors called the "Hidden One" or the "Hider," and whom you must look at in nativities and in questions, so that you may know whether matters ought to be completed or not, and reach their due effect. And we take this from the planet with which the lord of the ascendant or the significator of the matter is joined,

<column-break/>

or the Moon, or if the Moon itself is the partner of the lord of the ascendant or is the significator of the sought-after thing. For you must consider the planet to which the significator of the seeker or the significator of the thing sought or the Moon is joined, and see how that planet is disposed, and also the one to whom that planet is ultimately joined. 

For if he is joined to the lord of the ascendant, or the Moon, or the significator of the thing sought by a bad planet that is poorly disposed without **reception**<note>An astrological relationship where a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is contacting, implying a "welcome" or mutual support.</note>; or if he himself is not poorly disposed but joins some bad and poorly disposed planet who does not receive him, it signifies the destruction of the thing sought. Now, by a "poorly disposed planet," I mean one that is **peregrine**<note>A planet in a sign where it has no special status or "dignity," like a stranger in a foreign land.</note>, and **retrograde**<note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually a sign of weakness or reversal.</note>, and **combust**<note>Being so close to the Sun that its power is "burnt up" or hidden.</note>, or **cadent**<note>Falling away from the powerful angles of the chart, thus weakened.</note> from the ascendant or from the house of the thing sought, so that it does not aspect it, or at least its lord (though the aspect of the house is stronger than the aspect of its lord in this). Or if he should be in his **fall**<note>A sign where the planet's influence is at its weakest or most debased.</note> or his **detriment**<note>The sign opposite to the one the planet rules, where it feels uncomfortable.</note>, he is indeed the one who is called the Hider or the Destroyer. 

Furthermore, if the significator of the seeker or of the thing sought, or the Moon, or the planet to which the Moon is joined (whether she is the significator herself or the partner of the lord of the ascendant) joins some **unfortunate** planet—that is, one that is retrograde or combust or cadent—you will see then if reception intervenes. If it does, although with heaviness and fatigue, it signifies the perfection of the thing sought. If, however, reception does not intervene, it signifies the corruption of the matter and its destruction, and that the matter will not be completed after it is thought to be set right. 

But if the one who receives the lord of the ascendant, or the Moon, or the lord of the thing sought, or the planet to which any of them is joined, should be free, not unfortunate, nor a receptor, nor receiving, it signifies the perfection of the matter with ease. And if the planet to which the lord of the ascendant or the Moon or the lord of the thing sought is joined should be free from evils, but joined to some good planet which is joined to some bad one who is impeded and does not receive him—and you should understand this from planet to planet through the seven planets—the matter will not be completed, nor will it come to a good end. 

Always understand this: if those conjunctions occur without reception, whereas with reception, it is completed, though with fatigue. This is provided that you consider and foresee that if any planet cuts off the light of any of the aforementioned when it wants to be joined to a bad one, it takes away the harm and is not prohibited from the matter being completed. But if the cutting off of light does not intervene, the matter is prohibited and not completed; and if it were completed, it will be destroyed. 

You will consider this if reception intervenes, lest it be from an **opposition** or a **square aspect**<note>Tense angles (180 or 90 degrees) that usually signify conflict or difficulty.</note>; for if the planet is then poorly disposed, that reception which happens from a square or opposition does not help, and especially if the receptor was impeded. But if the reception was from a **trine** or **sextile**<note>Harmonious angles (120 or 60 degrees) signifying ease and flow.</note>, it is valid, and it is believed that the matter then ought to be completed. If, however, the planet who receives was then well-disposed, from whatever aspect that reception might be, it completes the matter, and the square or opposition does not stand in the way. 

If it was from a trine or sextile, it completes the matter as soon as he to whom the significator is joined is well-disposed, whether it be with reception or without reception; provided, however, that the aspect or conjunction is not already completed, such that it begins in some way to separate. And if the significator is joined with a **fortune**<note>A beneficial planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note> that is not impeded, the matter is also completed. And if any of the planets should **transfer the light**<note>When a fast planet moves from a conjunction with one planet to another, "carrying" the influence between them.</note> or virtue between the significator and another, and the one to whom it transferred should be an **infortune**<note>A harmful planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note>, and should be impeded as was said, the matter is consumed, unless the bad impeding or receiving planet should be received in turn. Indeed, if the significator of the seeker or the Moon and the significator of the sought-after thing are joined to any planet that **collects the light**<note>When two planets both move toward a third, slower planet, which "collects" their influence.</note> of both, and that planet is an infortune or is unfortunate, it destroys the matter and does not permit it to be completed.

## On the Second House. Chapter one regarding the substance <note>In this context, 'substance' (Latin: substantia) refers to wealth, money, or material assets.</note> which the seeker hopes to have.

If anyone should ask you whether they will have the substance they hope for or not, you should know from them what kind of substance it is that they intend to have or acquire. Then, look at the ascendant, its lord, and the Moon, who are the universal significators of the seeker. Do not let this deceive you: whatever person it is who asks you about the substance they hope to acquire, the **first house** is assigned to them—whether they are a king, a cleric, a layman, a pope, or any prelate, noble, or any other person. For no one has a special privilege in this case; neither social condition, nor rank, nor sex takes precedence. All are equal in this, provided each asks for themselves. And look at the second house and its lord; nothing else specifically determines the seeker's substance. 

If the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is joined to the lord of the house of substance; or the lord of the house of substance to the lord of the ascendant; or if the lord of the house of substance is in the ascendant; or if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in the house of substance; or if the Moon or any of the other planets is **transferring light**<note>A technique where a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, essentially connecting their energies.</note> between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the house of substance—specifically from one of them to the other—it signifies that the seeker will obtain the substance they are asking about. And if this is not the case for the lord of the ascendant or the Moon or the lord of the house of substance, see then if **Jupiter** (who is the natural significator of substance), or **Venus** (who is naturally a **fortune**<note>A 'fortune' or benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus, is one that traditionally brings positive results.</note>), or the **Head of the Dragon**<note>Also known as the North Node of the Moon, traditionally viewed as an increasing and beneficial point.</note> is in the house of substance without being looked upon by any **misfortune**<note>A 'misfortune' or malefic planet, such as Mars or Saturn, which traditionally brings difficulty or loss.</note>; then the seeker will acquire the substance and obtain it. 

When this is said, understand it if the question about substance is "absolute"—meaning the seeker does not specify anything else in their inquiry except to say: "Will I acquire substance or not?" You ought to look at it as I have touched upon above. If you find no such signs of substance, tell him that he will not find the substance but will remain as he is; unless there are "evils" in the house of substance, which are **Mars**, **Saturn**, and the **Tail of the Dragon**<note>Also known as the South Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with decrease or loss.</note> alone without the aspect of any fortune, which have the power to destroy the substance—unless by chance they were **received** by the lord of the house of substance, or they were themselves the lords of said house and otherwise in good condition, not **retrograde**, not **combust**<note>A planet is 'combust' when it is so close to the Sun that its power is said to be scorched or hidden.</note>, nor hindered in any other way, for then their malice is diminished. And if the Tail is also with them in the house of substance, their malice will be increased and they will become worse. But if the Tail is in the house of substance with "fortunes," it diminishes much of their goodness and also takes away from the substance after it has been acquired—a fourth part and sometimes more. And if you find any of the "evils" in the house of substance to be in a bad state, and you find the Moon **void of course**<note>The Moon is 'void of course' when it makes no more major aspects to other planets before leaving its current sign; this usually suggests that 'nothing will come of the matter'.</note> or joining itself to the "evils" hindering her, this will signify that he will not acquire substance in his whole lifetime; indeed, he will see that what he has is diminished and that he will always be needy and a beggar.

## Chapter Two: From where he will acquire substance, from where he will lose it, and for what reason.

If, however, you see that the seeker is to obtain the substance and you wish to know from where he will acquire it and for what reason—or if he is to lose it, on what occasion he will lose it—look then at the planets I mentioned to you which have a share in the matter of substance. You will consider the one to which the other is joined; for the planet that is **heavier**<note>Slower-moving planets like Saturn or Jupiter are called 'heavy' because they receive the 'disposition' or influence of faster, 'lighter' planets like the Moon.</note> to which the other joins will signify by what mode and from where he will acquire the substance.

Look similarly at which house is ruled by that "heavy" planet which receives the influence: 
*   If it is in the **ascendant** or is the lord of the ascendant, the seeker will acquire substance through the labor of his own hands and his own person. 
*   If it is in the **second** or is the lord of the second, he will acquire it through his own existing wealth, such as from trade and similar things where people use their belongings to acquire what they do not yet have. 
*   If it is in the **third** or is the lord of the third, he will acquire it from brothers; if he has no brothers, he will acquire it from neighbors, fellow citizens, or certain acquaintances who feign being friends when they are not true friends, or by some occasion related to them. 
*   If it is in the **fourth** or is the lord of the fourth, he will acquire it from a father, grandfather, father-in-law, or another of his elder ancestors; if he has no such relatives, he will acquire it from lands, estates, or immovable goods. 
*   If it is in the **fifth** or is the lord of the fifth, he will acquire it from children; if he has no children, he will acquire it from certain people in whom he has trust that they may cause him to profit, though they are not true friends. 
*   If it is in the **sixth** or is the lord of the sixth, and the sixth sign is "human," he will acquire it from servants and attendants; if he has no servants, he will acquire it from smaller domestic animals like sheep, goats, and pigs, provided it is a "quadruped" sign; and if he has no animals, he will acquire it from illnesses or at least from lowly persons. 
*   If it is in the **seventh** or is the lord of the seventh, he will acquire it from a woman if the seventh is a feminine sign; or he will acquire it from enemies or perhaps in battles; or he will acquire it from business partners or from a dispute he will have with others. 
*   If it is in the **eighth** or is the lord of the eighth, he will acquire it from the goods of wives and from the inheritances of the dead; or he will acquire it in foreign lands to which he goes willingly. 
*   If it is in the **ninth** or is the lord of the ninth, he will acquire it from religious people; and if not from them, then from all consecrated clerics; or he will acquire it by occasion of long journeys to distant lands, as do the **Venetians, Pisans, Genoese, and Florentines**<note>The text highlights the famous merchant-republics of medieval Italy as the archetype of long-distance traders.</note> and all those who undertake long journeys. 
*   If it is in the **tenth** or is the lord of the tenth, he will acquire it from kings; or from other magnates; or from offices or positions of authority <note>Original: *potestarias*, referring to the office of a Podestà, a powerful local magistrate.</note> if he is the type of person suited for such power. If he is not suited for this, he will acquire it from his skills and expertise with honor. 
*   If it is in the **eleventh** or is the lord of the eleventh, he will acquire it from friends or certain persons in whom he has great hope; or from merchants with whom he deals in his own land or abroad—though more likely in his own—and from things that come to him unexpectedly through his good fortune. 
*   If it is in the **twelfth** or is the lord of the twelfth, he will acquire it from secret enemies or from those held in prison, if the twelfth sign is human—

### Chapter three on the cause of why one does not acquire substance.

**I**f indeed you see that the seeker ought not to acquire the **substance**<note>original: "substantia"; wealth, money, or material property.</note> and you wish to know the reason why they will not obtain it, or what cause prevents them from obtaining it, look at the receiver of the **disposition**<note>The planet that 'manages' the power of another because it rules the sign the other planet is currently in.</note> just as I told you above in this same chapter. And if the one who prohibits the acquisition of wealth is the **Lord of the Ascendant**<note>The planet ruling the rising sign, representing the seeker themselves.</note>, then the seeker themselves will be the reason why they do not obtain the wealth. If it is the Lord of the Second House, the wealth itself will be the cause. If it is the Lord of the Third, brothers will be the cause. And understand the same for the significators of all the houses in their proper place and time; that house will be the cause that the substance is not obtained by the seeker, following the same logic used for the causes of success through all twelve houses. Such are the meanings of the twelve houses: wherever you find the significator of wealth, you must judge the acquisition of wealth through that house; and wherever you find the **prohibitor** of wealth, you must judge the prevention of wealth through that house, so that it is not acquired by the seeker. Thus, look through all the houses for the significations of all things that pertain to you. 

**Zahel**<note>The text says "Cite," likely a corruption of "Zael" or Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century astrologer.</note> the master, whom God willed, says that if the question is whether substance should be had, we must establish the Ascendant and the House of Substance (which is the second from the Ascendant), as has been said elsewhere. We must look at the Lord of the House of Life (which is the Lord of the Ascendant); if we find it aspecting the Ascendant, or if it joins a planet that "returns light" to the Ascendant, we must work through that planet. If it does not aspect the Ascendant, nor any planet that aspects and returns its light to the Ascendant, then we must look at the Moon. If the Moon aspects the Ascendant, or aspects another planet that aspects the Ascendant and returns light to it, work through her. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon do not aspect the Ascendant, nor are they joined to a planet that aspects the Ascendant, we must then see which of them—the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon—has more degrees in the sign it occupies and will most quickly exit its sign and enter another; we must work through that one. And if, after it has exited its sign, it is joined to the Lord of the House of Substance immediately before it joins any other, the philosopher says the seeker will obtain the wealth, whether the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is "received" by the Lord of the House of Substance after the sign change or not. One should consider whether the Lord of the House of Substance is a **benefic**<note>original: "fortuna"; a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> or a **malefic**<note>original: "infortuna"; a challenging planet like Saturn or Mars.</note>, since the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon with the Lord of the House of Substance brings about the obtaining of the thing—namely, the matter of the question. But you must watch that the Lord of the House of the thing does not join another planet, or that another planet does not join it, before the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins it, to which the Lord of the House of the thing might commit its disposition. For this reason, I said "immediately," so that nothing interrupts the light or prohibits the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon with the Lord of the House of the thing. If the question is about a specific property, see which house signifies that

If, however, there is no conjunction, then look at all the factors as I told you: the Lord of the house of the thing changing signs, and the conjunction with the Lord of the specific thing being asked about. If the Lord of the house of the thing or the property sought commits its disposition to another planet before it joins the Lord of the Ascendant, or before the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins it: see who that planet is; for that planet is the significator of the impediment preventing the matter from being completed. See which house that planet rules, for the person signified by that house strives to ensure the matter does not succeed—especially if the planet to whom the disposition was committed is "impeded."
