If it is a **malefic** but not impeded by the aforementioned obstacles, and it receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, the matter will similarly be completed according to the aspect by which it was received. If the malefic does not receive the Lord of the Ascendant, and the conjunction is by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect<note>Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees.</note>, the matter will be completed, though with labor and delay. If the conjunction is by a **square** aspect or **opposition**<note>Challenging angles of 90 or 180 degrees.</note>, the matter will hardly ever be completed; and if it is completed, it will be with such distress and labor that the seeker will often say, "I wish I had never involved myself in this." But if **reception**<note>A mutual relationship where one planet is in a sign the other rules.</note> occurs, the matter will be completed. If the one who receives is a benefic, the matter is settled easily and quickly; if a malefic, with heaviness and delay. If reception occurs, there is no way the matter can fail; nothing can prohibit it unless the seeker themselves chooses to abandon the purpose. If the receiver of the disposition is in an **angle**<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, representing strength and speed.</note>, the effect will be swift; in **succedent** houses, it will be slower; in **cadent** houses, it will be prolonged even further, even if there is reception. Nevertheless, reception is of such great strength that it does not allow the matter to be nullified; though it be delayed, it eventually reaches the desired effect, whether concerning wealth or any other matter. Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are joined to the Lord of the House of Wealth or the sought thing, or joined to any benefic in that house, the seeker will obtain that wealth. And even if they are joined to a malefic in that house, if that malefic receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, the matter will be done. Even without reception, if the malefic has **dignity**<note>A position of traditional power, like ruling the sign.</note> in that house, the seeker will still acquire the thing, though it be delayed by the passage of time. ## Chapter four: whether one will acquire the substance which they seek, or have lent, or deposited.

If the question is from someone asking whether the person from whom they seek substance will give it to them: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, who are the **significators**<note>The specific planets representing the people involved in the question.</note> of the inquirer; the second house will be the house of their own substance. The seventh house and its Lord will be the significators of the person from whom they are asking; the eighth house and its Lord will be the significators of the substance of that person. See then if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the eighth house (which signifies the substance of the person being asked), or if one of them is joined to a planet present in the eighth house. If that planet is a Fortune, they will acquire the substance they are asking about; if they seek another’s property—namely, from the one they are asking—that person will give it to them. If they seek that which they lent or deposited, they will similarly acquire it, whether that Fortune receives them or not.

If, however, it is a Malefic and it receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, they will likewise acquire the substance about which they inquire. But if it does not receive them, they will hardly or never recover it; and if they do have it, they will hardly or never have it in its entirety, and they will obtain what they get only with heaviness, hardship, and insistence. Similarly, if the Lord of the eighth house is in the first or second house and the Lord of the second house receives it, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought. 

But if the Lord of the seventh or the Lord of the eighth is in the first or second house and the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, or the Lord of the second house does not receive it, it signifies that the inquirer will yet lose more of their own substance and increase their initial loss. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to a Fortune that has **dignity**<note>An astrological term meaning the planet has "rights" or power in a specific sign (e.g., by being its ruler).</note> in the 

<column-break/>

Ascendant, that matter will be achieved. Or if one of them is joined to a Malefic that has dignity in the Ascendant and receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, the thing the seeker asks about will be achieved. And if a Fortune is in a strong position and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins it, the matter will be achieved even without reception. 

Understand all these things mentioned above as applying to matters involving lower or common persons, such as inhabitants of cities, castles, villages, and the like, where one person does not greatly exceed another. By "exceeding persons," understand kings and magnates who are fit to be kings, such as the greatest dukes and the greatest marquises to whom kingdoms fall; or unless the matter is between religious persons, or between layfolk and religious persons, concerning things that are not strictly their own. I shall mention these matters in their proper place and time, if it pleases our Lord Jesus Christ, the true man.

## Chapter five: whether one will obtain substance from a king.

Other questions also occasionally come before astrologers regarding substance: such as if someone asks whether they will obtain substance from some king. For instance, sometimes **mercenaries**<note>original: "soldatarij"; soldiers or officials receiving "sold" (pay/salary).</note> of kings and other magnates ask whether they are to have their pay from the king; and the same applies if one asks about the king’s vicar, or any person asking about substance they believe they should have. Look then at the Ascendant and its Lord and the Moon, who are the significators of the seeker, and the second house from the Ascendant (which is the house of the seeker's substance) and its Lord. 

Then look at the tenth house and its Lord, who are the significators of the king, his vicar, or the magnate who receives the service. Look also at the eleventh house and its Lord, who are the significators of the substance of the king or magnate. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the eleventh, or if one of them is joined to a planet present in the eleventh house that is a Fortune—provided it is not hindered or poorly disposed—that inquirer will acquire what they seek of the kingly or magnate’s substance, whether they be a mercenary or anyone else, and whether that Fortune receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon or not. 

If, however, it is a Malefic and it receives them, they will likewise obtain what is sought. But if that Malefic does not receive the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, they will hardly or never obtain the thing sought.

## Chapter six: concerning the timing of the aforementioned things.

Furthermore, if the person who inquires of you wishes to know *when* that which they seek will happen: look then to the planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined and which signifies the effect of the matter. If it looks upon the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon from a trine or sextile aspect—whether that which received them is a Fortune or not—consider whether it casts its light or its rays upon the rays of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon. Count how many degrees are between them, namely from the degree in which one casts its rays to the other until the perfection of the aspect, degree by degree. 

Say then that there will be that many **days** until the time of the matter's effect if both are in **cadent** houses<note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered the weakest and fastest for timing.</note>. If they are in **succedent** houses<note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, indicating a moderate timeframe.</note>, they will be **weeks**<note>original: "ebdomade".</note>. If they are in **angular** houses, they will be **months**. 

And if it is a matter that seems able to be greatly delayed, you might say they would be **years**, especially if both significators—namely the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon and the planet it joins—are in angular houses. ### Of the third house.

### Chapter one concerning brothers and their state.

**I**f anyone asks about a brother, see by what manner he asks—that is, whether he asks about a brother who is present or absent, healthy or sick, or whatever the status of the seeker's brother may be. Give the **Ascendant** to the seeker, since it signifies him, and then give the **third house** to the brother.

If he asks about an absent brother, look then to the **Lord of the third house**, which must signify the brother, and see where the Lord of the brother's house is found. For his state and condition must be according to what is signified by the Lord of that house in which he is found. Look at how the planets **aspect**<note>An "aspect" is a specific geometric angle between planets that determines how they interact.</note> him: whether he is in the aspect of **Fortunes**<term>Fortunes: The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus, which indicate luck and positive outcomes.</term> or **Malefics**<term>Malefics: The "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars, associated with hardship or obstacles.</term>, and by what aspect they see him and he sees them, or if they are physically joined together. For if the significator of brothers is in his own house (the third), and the Malefics do not aspect him by **opposition** or a **fourth aspect**<note>original: "quarto aspectu"; a square aspect (90 degrees), considered a source of tension.</note>, you can then say that his brother is healthy.

But if the Malefics aspect him by opposition or square without **reception**<note>Reception occurs when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting, implying a "welcome" or cooperation.</note>, you can say that his brother is alive and healthy but is in great distress, anxiety, and worry. If, however, they aspect him from said aspects with reception, you can say that his brother is in the aforementioned worries but will be well-delivered and escape from them.

If, however, a Fortune aspects him from a **trine** or **sextile**<note>Harmonious aspects of 120 and 60 degrees, respectively.</note> aspect without reception, or from a square or opposition with reception, you can say that his brother is doing well and is staying comfortably in the land where he is. But if the Fortunes aspect him from a trine or sextile aspect with reception, say that his brother is healthy and well-settled, and all things are proceeding prosperously so that nothing he desires is lacking.

If, however, he is in the fourth house without the aspect of Malefics, he is striving to acquire money in the land where he is.

If he is in the fifth house and is joined with the Lord of the fifth with reception—whether it be a Fortune or not, provided that Lord of the fifth is not hindered in a bad way—

<column-break/>

it signifies that his brother is doing well, rejoicing and being glad with the people of that land where he is. If it is a Fortune with whom the significator of the brother joins, and the conjunction is physical or by trine or sextile aspect with reception, say that his brother is healthy, cheerful, and rejoicing with the men and women of that place. He enjoys food, drink, and fine clothing, and he devotes himself to the "cult of Venus"<note>original: "cultu venereo"; a euphemism for romantic or sexual pursuits.</note> and all things in which men delight, provided he is a man suited for this or one who delights in such things, as young men and those like them do.

If, however, he is in the fifth house **void of course**<note>A planet is "void of course" when it makes no further aspects to other planets before leaving its current zodiac sign, often indicating a lack of progress.</note>, or in physical conjunction with Malefics, or in their square or opposite aspect without reception, and those Malefics who hinder him are "sons" and are themselves hindered, it signifies his bad condition, his ill-being, and a "dyscrasia"<note>original: "discrasiam"; an imbalance of the bodily humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) believed to cause illness.</note> of the body, because the fifth is the third house from the house of brothers<note>Using "derivative houses": counting three houses starting from the 3rd house (the brother's 1st) leads to the 5th house, making it the brother's 3rd house (his own siblings/environment).</note>.

If you find him in other houses that are not excluded, such as the sixth, eighth, or twelfth, with the aforementioned significators, say the same thing, but it will be less intense. If, however, you find him in the eighth house joined to a Fortune by a trine or sextile aspect, say that his brother is not perfectly healthy, yet not so sick that he should be feared for; he is, however, out of balance.

But if he is joined to Malefics and is in the sixth house, or is joined to the Lord of the sixth, you can say that his brother is falling ill. And you can say the same if the Lord of the sixth is in the third, unless the Lord of the third is well-disposed as was said above. Then look to see if you find the seeker's brother is sick: if the Lord of the third joins the Lord of the eighth house or enters into combustion, it signifies that he will die from that illness.

If you find him in the seventh house, say that he is in the land to which he traveled, not yet departed from it, and stays there as a stranger; he is neither well-disposed nor very ill, but stands between the two.

If he is in the eighth, there is doubt about him, especially if he is combust or joined to the Lord of the eighth in the eighth house, or joined to Malefics hindering him in the eighth, because then it signifies his death.

If he is in the ninth, it signifies that he has traveled from the land where he first was to another more distant land; or perhaps he has given himself to a religious order, or otherwise leads a clerical or religious life.

If he is in the tenth and is joined to Fortunes by a trine or sextile aspect—and especially with reception—it signifies that he has acquired an office, some honor, or a dignity in the land where he is. But if he is joined to Malefics by a square aspect or by opposition, or in another way that hinders him, or if he is combust in the tenth, there will be doubt regarding his death.

If he is in the eleventh joined to Fortunes by a good aspect, or is joined with the Lord of the eleventh, it signifies that he is with some friend of his with whom he stays well, rejoicing and delighting with him. But if there are Malefics aspecting him, it signifies that he does not rejoice in these things, nor does it seem to him that he is in a good state.

If he is in the twelfth and is joined to Fortunes receiving him, and that Fortune which receives him is not hindered, it signifies that he has some mastership or carries on a trade in horses and oxen, from which he profits and leads a laudable life. But if that Fortune is hindered, or joined to Malefics hindering her, it signifies his bad condition: that he is sick or ill-disposed, so that if he joins with the Lord of the eighth, or is combust, or enters combustion, it is feared he may die from it.

If he is in the first, he rejoices and will be glad with those who love him, and he is well-disposed.

If he is in the second, he does not rejoice in any status he may have...

### On the Fourth House.

## Chapter 1: Concerning a house or inheritance which someone intends to buy or obtain in another way, and whether the inquirer shall have it.

If someone is anxious about some house, or a piece of land, a vineyard, a meadow, an olive grove, a forest, or some inheritance that he wishes to buy or otherwise hopes to have—and if his question was absolute, meaning he does not specify the land or house of a particular person—look at the **Ascendant**, its **Lord**, and the **Moon**, who signify the one asking the question. Look at the **Fourth Sign** and its **Lord**, which are the significations of the thing sought. 

If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Fourth, or if the Lord of the Fourth is in the First, or if one of them is joined to the other bodily or by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect with **reception**<term>Reception: A condition where one planet is in a sign or "house" ruled by another planet, suggesting cooperation or a favorable welcome.</term>, he will obtain the thing sought easily and without complication or hindrance. 

If indeed it is without reception, or they are joined together by a **quartile aspect**<note>Quartile aspect: A square (90-degree) angle, usually considered a sign of tension or difficulty.</note> or by opposition with perfect reception, the inquirer shall still obtain the thing sought. If, however, they are not joined together by aspect nor by body, but the Moon or another planet **transfers light** between them<term>Transfer of Light: When a fast-moving planet moves from a conjunction or aspect with one significator to another, "carrying" the influence between them like a messenger.</term>, the inquirer will obtain the thing sought through someone 

<column-break/>

who interposes himself and brings the matter to effect by his own wisdom and industry. If, however, that planet which is lighter and which joins the other is **retrograde** before it completes their conjunction degree by degree, it will destroy the matter after the inquirer thought it was finished, and it will be brought to nothing. 

When the matter is completed by the one who intervened to finish it, if it was the Moon that transferred the light, look at which house she is in; for the matter will be completed by the person signified by that house. If it was another planet that transferred the light between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the thing sought, look at which house that planet rules, for through that person the matter will be finished. For example, if it was the Lord of the **Third House**, the matter will be completed by a brother of the inquirer. If he has no brother, it will be finished by one of his younger relatives. If this is not the case, it will be finished by one of his neighbors. 

When it is the Lord of the **Fifth**, it will be finished by a son or by one of the persons signified by the Fifth House. When it is the Lord of the **Sixth**, it will be finished by a servant or a humble dependent, or by someone signified by the Sixth House. And if it is the Lord of the **Seventh**, it will be finished by a wife, a mistress, or a partner; if he has no wife, let it be finished by one of those signified by the Seventh House. When it is the Lord of the **Ninth**, it will be finished by a religious person. When it is the Lord of the **Tenth**, it will be finished by a nobleman or a ruler. When it is the Lord of the **Eleventh**, it will be finished by a friend of the inquirer. When it is the Lord of the **Twelfth**, it will be finished by someone who pretends to be a friend of the inquirer but is not. When it is the Lord of the **Second** or the **Eighth**, it will be finished by someone from whom he does not hope for help and of whom no mention will have been made in that matter. 

When, however, the Lord of the Fourth is not joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, nor the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the Fourth, nor the Moon; and there is no planet to transfer light between them; or if there is a planet that **prohibits** their conjunction, the matter will not be completed. When you wish to know who it is that will not permit the matter to be finished, look at that planet which prohibits the conjunction between the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon; see which house it rules, for the annulment of the matter will be caused by the person signified by that house.

## Chapter 2: On the nature and quality of the thing to be bought.

If the inquirer asks—as often happens—"What kind of thing is this that I intend to buy or obtain? Is it fruitful or sterile land? Is the structure of that house solid, or shaky, or otherwise flawed? Are its laborers good and faithful or not?" 

Look at this similarly from the **Ascendant** and its Lord; for then the Ascendant and its Lord signify the laborers of the land or vineyard, the foresters, and the inhabitants of the house. The sign of the **Fourth** signifies the land, house, or inheritance, and what kind it is and what is within it. The **Seventh** signifies that which is produced upon that land: namely wheat, barley, other common grains, and domestic herbs grown in gardens, such as cabbages, fennel, parsley, borage, beets, and the like, if it is the season when grains and garden herbs are in the fields or gardens; it could also signify vines, such as vineyards and the like. 

If **Jupiter** is in the Seventh, well-disposed and in good "essence"<note>Essence: The strength of a planet based on its position in the zodiac.</note>, it signifies that on that land there is wheat and herbs from which the most useful seeds are born and which are most edible for the benefit of men. If **Venus**, **Mercury**, the **Moon**, or the **Sun** are there, well-disposed and in good essence, it signifies that on that land are herbs in which men delight, such as rose gardens and others producing fragrant fruits and flowers from which wreaths and similar things are made. If, however, Jupiter, Venus, or the others there are impeded, there will be some of these things I have mentioned, but not many.

### Chapter 3: Concerning the quality of the laborers.

If you wish to know about the laborers of the land or vineyard, or about the guardians of the meadow or forest, or about the inhabitants and what sort they are: look at the **Ascendant** and see if **Jupiter** is **direct** <note>direct: Moving forward in its usual path, suggesting straightforward and honest behavior.</note> and in a good state. If so, the laborers will be good and faithful, and they will be men of middle age. If he is **oriental** <note>oriental: Rising before the sun, associated with youth and new beginnings.</note>, they will be youths of good spirit. If he is **occidental** <note>occidental: Setting after the sun, associated with maturity and endings.</note>, they will be those beginning to grow old, or perhaps elderly; in that case, all will be of good spirit. If Jupiter is direct, the laborers will remain in that work, and it will be useful to the seeker. If he is retrograde, they will leave the work, and the inquirer will hire other labo-

<column-break/>

-rers worse than those. 

If **Venus** is in the place of Jupiter, the laborers will be good and faithful, and in almost all things they will be like those signified by Jupiter, except that Venus signifies younger and more pleasant people within the quality mentioned above. If **Saturn** is in the place of Jupiter, those laborers or inhabitants will be liars and thieves, even if they are old or decrepit. If **Mars** is in his place, the laborers will be thieves and liars, and those signified by Saturn will steal openly; they will be rogues and greater evildoers than simple thieves. If Mars or Saturn are direct, they will remain in the work; if they are not, they will depart from it, and the work will be hired out to better laborers or eventually to better managers.

### Chapter 4: Concerning the antiquity and novelty of things.

If you wish to know about those trees or about a building—whether they are ancient things or newly planted, or a building newly made—see if any planet is in the **Tenth House**. If so, the building will be not very ancient nor newly made; similarly with the trees, they will not be very old nor very young. 

If there is no planet there, see where the **Lord of the Tenth House** <note>Lord of the Tenth: The planet that rules the zodiac sign located on the cusp of the Tenth House.</note> is. If it aspects the Tenth House from where it is, or if it does not aspect it but aspects a planet that from its own place aspects the Tenth, the trees will be young and the buildings newly constructed, so that they are not ancient—especially if the Lord of the Tenth is oriental. If, however, it is occidental, the trees will be ancient and the buildings old. If it does not aspect the Tenth, nor is there any planet then that aspects it or sends its light to the Tenth, and it is occidental, the trees themselves will be very old and the building ancient.

Next, look similarly if you wish to know what will happen to those trees or the building from the Lord of the Tenth House. If it is direct—whether it is a **fortune** <note>fortune: A "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus, usually bringing positive results.</note> or an **infortune** <note>infortune: A "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars, usually bringing challenges.</note>—the trees and the building will remain in their current state. If, however, it is retrograde, the trees will be uprooted from that land, and the building likewise. If the Lord of the Tenth does not aspect the Tenth House and is not in the Eleventh, Third, Fifth, or Ninth from the Ascendant, the land will be without trees and without a building; it will either be uncultivated or poorly cultivated. 

To know whether there are seeds in it—namely wheat or other grains—if the time is suitable for this, look then at the **Lord of the Seventh House**. If it aspects the Seventh, there will be seed in it which the lord of the land hopes to harvest for his own benefit. If it does not aspect it, there will be no useful seeds there.

### Chapter 6: Whether the leasing of land or a house is profitable.

And if someone asks, wishing to lease land or a house—whether he is a laborer taking on land as a worker, or for a fixed rent each year as often happens, or a house to live in—and he wants to know if it is good for him to lease it, you shall give the first house and its lord to the one who leases the thing (the tenant), and the seventh house and its lord to the one who rents it out (the landlord). And you shall give the tenth house to the utility that may follow from that thing, and the fourth house to the final result that might follow from it. 

¶ If the lord of the ascendant <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</term> is in the ascendant or looks upon it by a trine or sextile aspect <note>trine or sextile: favorable geometric angles between planets, suggesting harmony</note>, or if a benefic planet <note>original: *fortuna*; usually Jupiter or Venus</note> is there (whether it has dignity there or not), or if the "Part of Fortune" is unhindered, it signifies that the tenant will lease that property hoping for good from it; he will not regret the lease and will find delight and joy in that arrangement. ¶ If, however, a malefic planet <note>original: *malus*; usually Saturn or Mars</note> is in the ascendant, one of two things will happen: either he will regret leasing it, or he will not lease it at all, or he seeks to lease it specifically to deceive the landlord. 

Then look at the seventh house for the one who is renting out the property. If the lord of the seventh is in it, or looks upon it by a trine or sextile aspect, or if a benefic planet is there and not badly hindered, the landlord will fulfill what is required for the tenant, keep his promise, and be useful to him. ¶ If, however, a malefic is there who is not the lord of the seventh, the landlord will not keep what he promised the tenant and will strive to deceive him and act fraudulently toward him. 

¶ Then look to the tenth house; if a benefic is in it or looks upon it by a trine or sextile aspect, the matter will be directed and brought to completion. ¶ If, however, a malefic is in it who is not the lord of the tenth, or looks upon it from an opposition or a square aspect <note>square aspect: a 90-degree angle, considered a position of tension or conflict</note>, that lease will not be completed, and it could be that a disagreement will arise because of the trees or the buildings existing on that land. 

¶ Then look to the fourth house and assign it to the end of the matter. If a benefic is there, or the lord of the fourth is there, or looks upon it from a trine or sextile aspect, the end of that matter will be good, useful, and praiseworthy. ¶ If, however, a malefic is there who is not the lord of the fourth, the end will be bad, and loss and inconvenience will follow for the tenant.

## Concerning the Fifth House.

### Chapter 1: Whether someone is going to have children by his wife or by another woman, or similarly asking about children in the same way.

When you are questioned by any man whether he is to have children by the wife he has or by another woman—or if a woman asks whether she will have children by the man she has or by another—take the "shadow" <note>original: *vmbram*; likely referring to the calculation of the astrological chart at the specific moment of the question</note> immediately. Arrange the figure according to the ascendant and the remaining houses, and look at the ascendant, its lord, and the moon. If you see the lord of the ascendant and the moon (or either of them) joined to the lord of the fifth, which is the house of children, say that he is to have children. Similarly, if the lord of the fifth is joined to the lord of the ascendant. ¶ And if

<column-break/>

you do not find them joined together, see if any planet "transfers light" <term>transfer of light: when a fast-moving planet connects two other planets by aspect in succession</term> between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the fifth, for this signifies children, though after a delay. If this is not the case, see if the lord of the ascendant or the moon is in the fifth house; if so, say he is to have children. 

¶ Similarly, if the lord of the fifth is in the ascendant, say he is to have children. If this is not the case, see if the lord of the ascendant (or the moon) and the lord of the fifth both join any planet that is "heavier" <note>heavier: a slower-moving planet, like Jupiter or Saturn</note> than them; for that planet will collect the light of both and will be the "receiver of the disposition" <note>receiver of the disposition: a planet that takes on the influence of others, indicating how the matter will resolve</note>. This planet will be the indicator of whether the children, if they are born, ought to live or not. 

And see if that planet is free from the hindrances I mentioned to you in the treatise on the hindrances of planets (that is, that it is not retrograde, "burnt" by the sun, or "falling" from the angles, etc.). If so, say those children will live. ¶ If, however, that heavier planet which receives the disposition is hindered (meaning it is moving backward, or hidden by the sun's rays, or falling away from the main corners of the chart or the ascendant, or besieged by malefic planets, or has any of the aforementioned hindrances), those children will not live long, nor will their father and mother be blessed by them. 

Then look at **Jupiter**, who naturally signifies children. If you find him in the ascendant, or in the 3rd, 5th, 9th, or 11th houses, free from all the aforementioned hindrances, say that the woman has either conceived or will conceive shortly—perhaps during the first intercourse or shortly after—so that it will be like a thing that is already seen as done or is in the making. 

¶ And if **Venus** is in the fifth house unhindered, or if there is another benefic planet there besides Jupiter or Venus that is unhindered, it signifies that the woman will become pregnant shortly. ¶ If, however, Jupiter is in the aforementioned places but hindered, say that the conception either does not happen, or if it has, it will not reach completion, but the woman will miscarry or suffer an abortion. 

¶ Similarly, if Venus is joined to **Saturn** or **Mars**, or is "under the rays" of the sun <note>under the rays: so close to the sun that its influence is weakened or hidden</note> moving toward a physical conjunction with the sun, the woman will not be pregnant. Even if a benefic planet is in the fifth (which might mean she could become pregnant soon), the birth will hardly be good. 

¶ If Saturn or Mars is in the fifth house, or another malefic, and especially the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>Tail of the Dragon: the South Node of the moon, traditionally associated with loss or "emptying"</note> which signifies "emptying," or if they look upon it from an opposition, it signifies that the woman will not be pregnant. Malefic planets are also seen to frustrate conception if they look upon the fifth house from a square aspect.

### Chapter 2: When the question about a child is general.

If, however, the question is general—meaning a man or woman asks if they will have children without specifying if it is with this woman or this man—look then at the ascendant and its lord. See if the lord of the ascendant is in the ascendant, or if a well-disposed benefic is there, or in the tenth, eleventh, or fifth houses. And if Jupiter is, as was said, in the third, fifth, ninth, or eleventh, the person will have children, though there will be some delay in this, but not a very great one. 

¶ If the lord of the ascendant is not in the fifth house (which is the house of children) but is in the fourth or the seventh, the matter will be directed and perfected. ¶ If, however, it is in the fifth, ninth, or eleventh, but is besieged by two malefics, or physically joined to one of the malefics that hinders it (namely Saturn or Mars), or if it is with the Tail of the Dragon, yet Jupiter is in one of the aforementioned places (third, fifth, ninth, or eleventh), that man or woman will have children, but the delay will be greater than mentioned above. 

¶ If, however, one of the malefics (Saturn or Mars) or the Tail of the Dragon is in the ascendant, or they look upon it from a square aspect or opposition, and the lord of the ascendant is hindered by retrograde motion, or by being burnt by the sun, or by being in its "fall" <note>fall: a position in the zodiac where a planet's power is greatly diminished</note>, or is in the second...

## Chapter Three: Whether a woman be pregnant.

Likewise, if someone is anxious to know whether a woman has conceived and carries a child in her womb or not: look to the lord of the ascendant <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the question is asked</term> and the Moon, or either of them, which signify the woman; and look to the fifth house and its lord, who are the signifiers of the conception. If you find the Moon in the fifth, or the lord of the fifth in the ascendant, free from "malifics" and other hindrances mentioned above, it signifies that the woman has conceived and has a child in her womb. Similarly, if the lord of the ascendant has committed its "disposition" to another planet in an angle, it is even more certain; and more certain still if the planet to whom the lord of the ascendant committed its power is "received" <term>reception: a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</term> or if it receives the lord of the ascendant itself. 

If, however, the planet to which the lord of the ascendant is joined is in a "cadent" house <term>cadent: houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) that "fall away" from the angles and are considered weak</term>, it signifies that the woman has conceived "pains"—that is, what appears to be a pregnancy is actually an illness rather than a child. And if it is a child, it will not come to a good end, especially if the ascendant is Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, or if there is a malific planet in any of the angles. This is even more certain if the Dragon's Tail <note>original: *cauda*; the South Node of the Moon</note> is there, for it signifies miscarriage above all other evils. But if the heavy planet to which the lord of the ascendant committed its power is in a good place relative to the ascendant, and is not joined with malifics but is free from hindrances, and the Moon is likewise safe, it signifies that the conception will come to a good end and the birth will not be frustrated. Likewise if the lord of the fifth—the signifier of children—is in the ascendant and free from the aforementioned hindrances: namely, that it is not re-

trograde, nor combust, nor joined with malifics—especially the Dragon's Tail by body, or other malifics by opposition or a square aspect <term>square aspect: a 90-degree angle between planets, indicating friction or conflict</term>—it signifies a conception. If it is hindered by any of the aforementioned, there will be no conception; and if there was one, it will be frustrated and destroyed.

## Chapter Four: Whether a woman be pregnant or not.

Sometimes women have cause to doubt whether they are pregnant or not; and also their husbands, desiring to have children but not knowing if it is so, are accustomed to ask about this so they may be made certain by an astrologer. Therefore, if a question is put to you by a woman about herself, whether she has conceived or not, and the question is about nothing else: look to the ascendant and its lord. See where the lord of the ascendant is; if it is in an angle and free from malifics and other hindrances, it signifies the woman is pregnant. Similarly, if the lord of the ascendant is in a "succedent" house <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> or even a cadent house, provided it is received by a planet existing in an angle. 

If, however, it is in a cadent house and is joined to a planet that does not receive it—or if it does receive it but that planet is retrograde, combust, or falling—it signifies the woman is not pregnant. Likewise if the Moon is hindered. But if the Moon is received by a planet that is free from the aforementioned hindrances, she will be pregnant. If the Moon is not received and the lord of the ascendant is hindered, she will not be pregnant. If the lord of the ascendant is in a good place and regards the ascendant with a favorable aspect, she will be pregnant. If a man asks about a woman with her consent, the judgment is the same. But if the man asks of his own accord and by himself, with the woman being ignorant of it, then under the same conditions you shall consider the seventh house and its lord, and you shall judge by the lord of the seventh just as you judged by the lord of the ascendant—though the Moon must never be overlooked.

## Chapter Five: Whether a woman who has conceived carries one or more in her womb.

If you are asked about a pregnant woman, or if anyone is anxious to know whether she carries one or several: look to the ascendant. See if the ascendant is Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces <note>these are "mutable" or "double-bodied" signs often associated with multiples</note>. Or, if the ascendant is one of the other signs but there are two "good" planets in it or in the fifth house, she has conceived twins. If the Dragon's Head is there with them, say that she carries more than two in her womb, and it is possible she carries four. 

And if there are no planets in the ascendant or the fifth: see if any of the planets aspect the ascendant or the fifth degree by degree—such that the aspect is no more than one degree before the line of the ascendant or two degrees behind it. For however many planets aspect it in this way, so many are the children conceived in the womb, even if all seven planets should aspect those degrees. And look at which ones aspect from a trine or sextile <term>trine and sextile: favorable aspects of 120 and 60 degrees respectively</term>; as many as do so will come to perfection <note>meaning a healthy birth</note>. But as many as aspect from a square or opposition <term>opposition: a 180-degree angle, usually signifying direct confrontation</term> will suffer harm. 

And if you find the Sun and Moon in one sign, provided the Moon moves toward the Sun and is not more than five degrees behind it or two degrees ahead of it, you shall judge the same if the Sun or Moon are in Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces. But if the ascendant is one of the fixed or movable signs, and the fifth house is likewise one of those signs, and the Sun and Moon are in fixed or movable signs, and there are not several planets in the ascendant or the fifth (or aspecting them as described), then know that the woman carries only one and not more.

### ¶ Chapter six: whether a woman carries a male or a female child.

And if it is asked whether a woman carries a male or a female child, look then to the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</term> and its Lord, and the fifth house and its Lord. See if they are in Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, or Aquarius; if so, it is a sign that she carries a male. If they are not, it appears she carries a female. However, if the Lord of the Ascendant is in a masculine sign and the Lord of the fifth is in a feminine sign—or the Lord of the fifth is in a masculine sign and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a feminine sign—then turn to the Moon, which participates in all matters. See if she is in a masculine sign and joined to a planet in a masculine sign; then she will testify for the one in the masculine sign. If she is in a feminine sign, she will testify for the one in the feminine sign, whether it be the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the fifth. Similarly, if the Moon is joined to a masculine planet, it testifies to the male; if joined to a feminine planet, it testifies to the female. Likewise, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the fifth is a masculine or feminine planet, the Moon will testify to the one whose position she resembles. And know that Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the Sun are always masculine, except occasionally in certain cases which do not apply here. Venus is always feminine, except occasionally in cases not applicable here. Mercury, however, is called masculine when he is "oriental" in the world <note>original: "orientalis in mundo"; meaning appearing in the east before the Sun rises</note> and rises in the morning before the Sun; when he is "occidental" and sets after the Sun in the evening, he is called feminine. Similarly, when he is joined to a masculine planet, he is masculine, and when joined to a feminine one, he is feminine.

->Concerning the sixth house.<-

### ¶ Chapter one: whether a sick person shall be freed from the illness that holds them or not.

If a question is put to you regarding a sick person, whether they shall be freed from the illness that holds them or not: first see who it is that asks—namely, is it the sick person themselves, or another asking on their behalf? Consider if it is appropriate for them to ask, and if they ask by the will of the sick person or by their own impulse. For if they ask by the will and permission of the sick person, the first house is given to both the asker and the patient. But if they ask of their own impulse, the first house is given to the asker, but the sick person is given the house that signifies their person: for example, if one asks for a brother, the first house is given to the asker and the third to the sick brother; if for a father, the first is given to the asker and the fourth to the father. Understand the significations of the houses in this way according to what was said above in the treatise on the twelve houses. You shall also consider the condition of the sick person: whether they are a layman, a cleric, or otherwise a member of a religious order, and whether they are among those who are placed above a doctor or those over whom a doctor is placed. For there have been many and diverse opinions on this. You must also look at the type of illness and its nature; for a new illness must be viewed differently than an old one. I shall tell you the conditions of the sick and their infirmities: which sick persons should be placed above the doctor and which should not, and in which cases; and how to judge based on diverse opinions if Jesus Christ our Lord grants me his grace in this part. For some gave the Ascendant to the doctor, the tenth house to the sick person, the seventh to the illness, and the fourth to the medicine; in this opinion were

<column-break/>

Zahel <note>Zahel: Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and physician whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology</note> and his followers. According to this, the doctor was placed "above" the sick person. Similarly, they placed the doctor above the sick person if the question was asked while the doctor was still ignorant of the case <note>meaning the doctor has not yet been consulted or diagnosed the patient</note>. But if the doctor already knows, or if another asks on the patient's behalf with their consent, regardless of their condition, then the first house is given to the sick person, the tenth to the doctor, the seventh to the illness, and the fourth to the medicine; in this case, the sick person is placed above the doctor. For instance, if someone of their own impulse asks about a sick King without his knowledge, the first house is given to the doctor and the tenth to the sick person, the seventh to the illness, and the fourth to the medicine. If they ask in the same way about a Pope or any other cleric, the first is given to the doctor, the ninth to the sick person, the seventh to the illness, and the third to the medicine. Now I will tell you the conditions of illnesses, for if you know their conditions, you can judge them better and more safely. And although medicine is said to have been invented for the wealthy and the great, nevertheless the common folk now rush toward medicine; nor is it a wonder, since they fall ill just as the great do and desire to be cured. As for calling an illness "chronic" or "ancient," I deem it chronic and old once it has lasted a year, because annual illnesses are never easily cured—rather, they are cured with great difficulty. I consider an illness "not ancient" if it has not yet reached a year. Therefore, if the illness is ancient (more than a year), whatever the condition of the patient, you must give the twelfth house to the illness. If it is a new illness (not yet a year), you must give it the seventh house if you give the first to the doctor, because the doctor is the enemy of the illness. And if you give the tenth to the sick person, you must give the fourth to the medicine, because although medicine cures the sick, it is nevertheless opposed to them <note>Medicine is "opposed" because it is often bitter or works against the body's current state to restore balance</note>, and opposition signifies enmity. Thus, medicine is the "enemy" of the illness, because in medicine are found things contrary to the nature of the disease, which do not nourish it but sometimes exterminate it. If you give the ninth house to the sick person, the third is given to the medicine. If you give the third to the sick person (as sometimes happens), the ninth is given to the medicine. And you must consider whether the illness is universal or particular; if universal, you must judge generally regarding the whole body; if particular, you must judge according to that member in which the illness thrives. But if you were to ask how the houses signifying doctors, illnesses, and medicines are differentiated when these houses ought to be equal or nearly the same: I believe well that a reason could be assigned to you, but it would be long to narrate, and not everything can be disputed everywhere. Thus it is necessary for us to hold to the sayings of the philosophers and know that they did not say this without cause, for a student must believe. Now I will arrange for you the method of judging whether a sick person will be freed or not. However, I want you first to know how to understand what Zahel and his followers said. When he said the Ascendant signifies the doctor, he said it for this reason: because the illness is signified by the seventh house, and the doctor is the enemy of the illness; since the first house is the enemy of the seventh, the first is rightly given to the doctor. In this, the doctor is signified by the first house; as the first house is fortunate, so shall the doctor's care benefit the patient, and as it is unfortunate, so shall his care harm them. And for this reason Zahel said the first house is given to the doctor. That which he said—that the tenth house is given to the sick person—he did for no other reason than that it is signified by the tenth whether the sick person...

If it is joined with the Lord of the sixth, it will be prolonged longer than it seems it ought to be. Yet, in the end, in that case, the patient will escape and be liberated. 

One must also consider whether the significator of the sickness is in any of the debilitated degrees <term>açemena: also called 'azemene' degrees, these were specific zodiac points believed to cause permanent physical lameness or disability</term> and is in the twelfth or eighth house and is aspected by any of the malefics; for this signifies that the patient will not be liberated from that sickness without some impediment remaining in the limb assigned to that sign where the debilitated degree was. Here, one must inquire from the patient or from someone else who can tell you the duration of the sickness: because if the sickness has lasted many years, the patient will not be quickly liberated.

### ¶ Chapter two: whether the sick person will escape.

**I**f any sick person asks you whether he will be liberated from his illness or not: look to the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon, who are the significators of the questioner. See if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the "angle" of the Ascendant or in the "angle" of the Midheaven <note>The "angles" (1st and 10th houses) are the strongest positions in a chart</note>; this signifies his liberation. Also, if he is in the seventh or fourth house and aspects the Ascendant, it signifies his liberation, unless he is impeded by malefics by a square aspect or by opposition, or is combust <term>Combust: A planet weakened by being too close to the Sun's heat</term>, or is with the Dragon’s Tail <term>Dragon's Tail: The South Node of the Moon, associated with loss or drainage</term> in the same minute or moving toward it—provided there are fewer than 15 minutes between him and the Tail—without an aspect from a fortune. For the aspect of a fortune breaks the malice of the Tail by helping the Lord of the Ascendant, even if it is a square aspect, whether with reception or not. But if it is from the opposition with reception, it similarly breaks that 

<column-break/>

malice, unless he is the Lord of the eighth house <note>The Eighth House is the house of death</note>; because then he does not help but harms, whether he be a fortune or a malefic who is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant or to whom the Lord of the Ascendant is joined. 

However, if the Lord of the Ascendant is impeded: look then to the Moon to see if she is free from malefics, is in an angle, and aspects the Ascendant. Look also at the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon—namely, the one through which you are working and which is stronger in signification—to see if it is above the earth <note>Planets "above the earth" are in the visible sky (houses 7 through 12)</note>; for this is a sign of escape, especially if it aspects the Ascendant or joins a planet that aspects the Ascendant and returns the light of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon to the Ascendant. Nor should the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon be joined to a planet existing below the earth; then it signifies liberation, unless poor care or poor guarding causes the opposite. For not only a sick person, but even a healthy one could treat himself badly if he wished, saying "I will act so that this astrologer lies" by doing the opposite of what he ought to do; nevertheless, once you have performed your office, let him who feels his own fault impute the damage to himself. 

But if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is below the earth—namely in the second, third, fourth, fifth, or sixth houses—and neither of them is joined to a planet existing above the earth, it signifies his death. If, however, the benefic planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined (which signifies the patient’s escape) is retrograde, it signifies a prolongation of the sickness; and it will be stronger and more prolonged if it is falling from an angle, yet he will be liberated afterward. If, however, that planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined, and to whom they commit their disposition, enters into combustion, it signifies the death of the patient. 

Furthermore, if the Lord of the Ascendant is the significator—that is, if he is so strong that the signification is attributed to him before it is attributed to the Moon—and he is joined to any malefic planet existing below the earth, it signifies his death. But if the Lord of the Ascendant is impeded as was said, so that he cannot be the significator of the patient, and the signification falls to the Moon: see also if she is above the earth. If she is joined to a malefic planet existing below the earth, it signifies the death of that patient. Similarly, if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, and he is fast in his course and is descending from his apogee toward the middle of his eccentricity, or from the greatest distance to his first station <note>these are technical descriptions of a planet's orbital speed and distance</note>—which happens to him when his argument is from 15 degrees to two signs and 15 degrees—then it signifies that the sick man will be liberated quickly and will quickly regain his bodily strength. 

And if you find the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant joined with Saturn, it signifies a prolongation of the sickness, even if the sickness is new; if it is an old sickness, it signifies its long duration. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is below the earth and the Moon is joined to a planet in the third, sixth, ninth, or twelfth houses—which is already falling from an angle—it signifies the death of the patient. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the eighth house and the Moon is otherwise impeded, or if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the eighth house and the Lord of the Ascendant is impeded, it signifies the death of that patient. 

However, I see this must be noted: if the Lord of the Ascendant is received <term>Reception: A relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting cooperation</term> by the Lord of the eighth house, and the Lord of the Ascendant himself does not receive the Lord of the eighth, it does not signify death; rather, it signifies a very fearsome sickness, but the patient will not perish except through error. But if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon receives the Lord of the eighth house, it signifies death.

If it does not happen then, it will be when the Lord of the eighth reaches the degree where the Lord of the Ascendant was at the hour of the inquiry. Or, if the Lord of the Ascendant is the ruler of the Lord of the eighth, it will be when it reaches the degree where the Lord of the eighth was at the hour of the inquiry. 

Similarly, if the Moon or any other planet transfers the power or light of the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the House of Death, and the Lord of the House of Death is strong or located in an angle, while the Lord of the Ascendant is "falling" from an angle <note>original: "cadens"; located in a weak house like the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th</note> or is in the position of its own "detriment" or "fall" <note>original: "dispositione domus sue vel exaltationis sue"; actually refers to the planet's essential dignity/debility</note>, it signifies death. But when it is not falling from an angle, even if it is in opposition to its house or exaltation, if it is received, it does not signify death. 

If the Lord of the eighth house is in the Ascendant, and both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are "afflicted" <term>Impediti: A planet is "impeded" or afflicted when it is poorly placed or in a harsh aspect with a malefic planet</term>, it signifies that the illness will increase greatly and the patient will be in danger of death; nevertheless, they will escape, though hardly, and only with good care and caution as was said before. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are afflicted, and the planet to which they committed their power is also afflicted, it signifies death. 

But if only the "receiver" of the power (which is the heavier planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or Moon joins) is afflicted, it signifies a prolongation of the illness. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant is "under the earth" <note>In the houses below the horizon (1st through 6th)</note> and is joined to the Lord of the eighth in the fourth house, or if it is above the earth and joined to the Lord of the eighth in the eighth house (or from the eighth), it signifies death if the Lord of the Ascendant receives the Lord of the eighth. If it does not receive it, even though the Lord of the eighth receives the Lord of the Ascendant, the illness will be very heavy and the patient will be in danger of death, but they will be freed with the help provided to them. 

If the Lord of the Ascendant does not "behold" <note>original: "aspererit" for "aspexerit"; to be in a geometric aspect with</note> the Lord of the eighth, nor the eighth behold it, but some planet transfers light between them, and the Lord of the Ascendant is falling away from the Ascendant while the Lord of the eighth is in one of the angles (for its strength in an angle is most terrible), it signifies the patient will die from that illness. 

¶ And Zael <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician</note> said that if the Lord of the Ascendant is "combust" <term>Combust: When a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden</term>—specifically, if it is one of the "superior" planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, or Mars</note> and is within 13 degrees before the Sun or 4 degrees after the Sun, or if it is one of the "inferior" planets <note>Venus or Mercury</note> and is within 3 degrees before the Sun or 14 degrees after it—it signifies death

for the patient, unless perhaps the Lord of the Ascendant is received; for then it signifies escape after despair, and perhaps the person will appear to be dead when they are not, and it is even possible that they might be believed dead and buried alive.

¶ And a certain man among the Cretans said that when the "Part of Sickness" <term>Lot of Sickness: A calculated mathematical point in a chart used to determine the nature of an ailment</term> is between the beginning of the Ascendant and the end of the fourth house, it signifies the cause of the illness is from something "discovered" or external. When it is from the beginning of the fifth to the end of the eighth, it signifies it is from a present cause. When it is from the beginning of the ninth to the end of the twelfth, it signifies a future cause. 

¶ Regarding the nature of the illness, whether it is lasting or not: look to the sixth house, which is the house of infirmities. See if it is a "fixed sign" <term>Fixed Sign: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius; signs that represent stability and persistence</term>; if so, the illness will be fixed and remain in its state and will not change into another. If it is a "movable sign" <term>Movable Sign: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs that represent change and action</term>, the illness will easily change into another. If it is a "common sign" <term>Common Sign: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces; signs that represent transition</term>, the illness will be relieved at one time and aggravated at another. 

¶ To know whether an illness is old or new: look at the Moon and see from which planet it has just "separated" <term>Separation: When two planets move away from a precise aspect or conjunction</term>. If it has separated from an "oriental" planet <note>A planet that rises before the Sun</note>, the illness is new. If it has separated from an "occidental" planet <note>A planet that sets after the Sun</note>, the illness is old. If you find the illness is old by the previously mentioned conditions, you shall consider the twelfth house; judge through it regarding the nature of the illness just as you judged the new illness previously through the Lord of the sixth house. 

Look similarly for the liberation from the illness: if the Moon is joined to an oriental planet, it signifies the illness could be quickly cured. If it is joined to an occidental planet, the illness will be cured slowly and with difficulty. If it is joined to no planet, move the Moon from the sign it is in to the next, and see which planet it joins first after leaving its current sign—whether it joins an oriental or occidental planet—and judge the speed or slowness of recovery accordingly. All these things will happen better and faster if a "fortune" <term>Fortune: A benefic planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</term> beholds the Lord of the Ascendant, provided the Lord of the Ascendant is not falling from the Ascendant or from an angle. 

See similarly that no "malefic" <term>Malefic: A planet that causes challenge or harm, usually Saturn or Mars</term> is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, whether bodily or by opposition or a square aspect <note>A 90-degree angle, considered difficult</note>; for such a planet afflicts him, and a man will either never be permitted to escape the illness, or if that malefic receives the Lord of the Ascendant, the patient will escape only with great difficulty. If it does not receive him, fear then that he will not escape; indeed, he will not be freed. 

Consider also the Moon: if it is "quietly" with a fast-moving planet and is itself fast in its course, it signifies the sick person will be quickly freed. If it is joined to a "retrograde" planet <term>Retrograde: A planet that appears to be moving backward in the sky, often signifying delays or reversals</term>, it signifies a prolongation and long duration of the illness. If it is joined to a slow-moving planet, it signifies prolongation and aggravation of the illness, such that the patient will hardly escape; indeed, it seems more likely that they will die than escape.

In this matter, physicians are sometimes deceived. When they predict a future crisis on a "critical day" according to medical theory <note>Traditional medicine used "critical days" based on fixed day counts, like the 7th or 14th day, while astrology adjusted these based on the Moon's actual speed</note>, the crisis happens differently than they say. This occurs because of the Moon's conjunction with the planets on those days, which is why physicians are held in low regard by laypeople for failing in their prognostications—though they are not truly to be blamed.

Add 90 degrees to that, and you will find the seventh day. Calculate those 90 degrees from the Moon's original degree; in whatever zodiac sign that number ends, the Moon will be at that degree. Or, you can calculate this using astronomical tables to find the same location. Then, see how and by whom the Moon is "aspected" <term>Aspect: A specific geometric angle between planets, thought to transmit their influence</term>. Judge the health or illness of the patient based on whether the aspects from the planets to the Moon are good or bad.

## Chapter 4: Whether an absent person is falling ill

If someone is anxious about someone who is absent, or anyone else, wanting to know whether they are sick or not, look at the status of the person asking and the person being asked about, and judge accordingly. That is, whether they ask about a brother, a father, a son, a servant, a wife, a partner, an enemy, a bishop, or another religious figure, a king, or another of their lords, or even a friend or a secret enemy. You must assign the first house <note>The Ascendant</note> to the person asking the question, and assign the house that represents the person being asked about to that person <note>Each relationship corresponds to a specific house: e.g., the 3rd for brothers, 4th for fathers, 10th for kings</note>. 

Then, look at the Ascendant and its Lord and give it to the asker; give the Lord of the house representing the subject and the Moon to the subject of the inquiry. If the Lord of the subject's house or the Moon is in an "angle" <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart</term> and is not hindered by a malefic planet, it signifies that they are healthy. The same applies if one of them is in a "succedent" house <term>Succedent: Houses (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th) that follow the angles and have moderate strength</term> and is free from malefics and the other hindrances mentioned above.

If, however, the Lord of the subject is in the sixth house, or if its Lord is joined physically or by opposition or a square aspect [to a malefic], it signifies that they are sick—whether it is in the sixth house of the inquiry itself, or in the sixth house relative to their own house <note>This uses a "derived" house system: for example, the 6th house from the 3rd house (a brother) would be the 8th house of the main chart</note>, or joined with its Lord. If these aforementioned hindrances are not present, say that they are not sick. 

Master G. <note>Likely referring to a medieval authority like Gerard of Cremona</note> said that if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are "void of course" <term>Void of Course: A period when the Moon or a planet makes no further major aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign</term>, you must see which of them has traveled through more degrees in the sign it is currently in, and move it into the next sign that follows. See then which planet it first joins: a "fortune" <note>A benefic planet</note> or a malefic. If it joins a fortune that "receives" it, it signifies recovery—unless that fortune is itself hindered by the aforementioned obstacles or is the Lord of the eighth house, for then death is feared for the sick person. This is especially true if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon has "received" the Lord of the eighth house. But if it has not received it, then it signifies an escape from the illness, almost as if after despair. It seems, however, that they should escape unless an error by the physician, the patient, or those standing by causes the contrary, as shown in the following example.

The inquiry of a certain sick person was [as follows]: the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the patient</term> was Virgo at 15 degrees; the tenth house was Gemini at 15 degrees; Mars was in Gemini at 17 degrees and 30 minutes; the Moon was in Taurus at 16 degrees and 25 minutes; Jupiter was in Taurus at 9 degrees and 15 minutes; the Sun was in Aries at 27 degrees and 30 minutes; Saturn was in Aries at 10 degrees and 15 minutes; Mercury was in Aries at 20 degrees and 50 minutes; and Venus was in Pisces at 5 degrees and 37 minutes. And [the master] said: "Look to the Ascendant, its Lord <term>Lord: The planet that rules the zodiac sign in which a house or another planet is located</term>, the Moon, the other planets, the angles, and the other houses." Mercury, who was the Lord of the Ascendant, was "void of course" <term>Void of Course: A planet that makes no further major aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign, often indicating a 'stalled' situation</term>—that is, joined to no one—and the Moon was similarly void of course, joined to no one.

Therefore, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, through the emptiness of their course, signified a prolongation of that illness and its heaviness. Whereupon he moved the Moon from the sign in which she was—namely, from Taurus to Gemini. He moved the Moon and not the Lord of the Ascendant because she had traveled through more degrees of the sign in which she was than Mercury, the Lord of the Ascendant, had of his own. And after she had entered Gemini, she was first joined to Venus (who was in Pisces) rather than to any other planet, and she committed her disposition <term>Disposition: The influence or 'power of attorney' one planet hands over to another through an aspect</term> to her. And Venus was joining Jupiter and received him from her own house—namely, Taurus—and Jupiter similarly received Venus from his own house, namely Pisces <note>This is 'Mutual Reception,' where each planet is in a sign ruled by the other, indicating high cooperation</note>. Nor did Jupiter commit the disposition to anyone who was not joined to Saturn; for he himself joins no planet except Saturn, who is heavier <term>Heavier: A planet with a slower orbit, such as Saturn or Jupiter, considered more 'weighted' in its influence</term> than he is, while all others join him because they are lighter than he. 

And that joining which Venus made with Jupiter through mutual reception signified that the sick man ought to be freed from that sickness. Nevertheless, the illness would be in a state of increase until the conjunction of Venus with Jupiter was perfected degree by degree, and she passed him by a single minute. And he saw that the sickness would be increasing for two days and nearly 15 hours, giving one day to each degree and two hours to every 20 minutes; for there were 2 degrees and 38 minutes until their perfect joining. From that point forward, the sick man began to be relieved. And he said that it was that sick man who asked about his own state, and his illness did not cease increasing until the conjunction of Venus with Jupiter was completed degree by degree; immediately when Venus was separated from Jupiter by one minute, the sick man began to be relieved, began to rest, and his pain was diminished.

And the same philosopher said that if Venus had been joined to Mars and not to Jupiter, the sick man would have died, unless Mars (who was the Lord of the fourth house) received Venus and she did not receive him. For if she received Mars, it would seem that the sick man received death and would die, since Mars signifies the matter of the question—namely, death. For when the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, either both or one of them, joins the Lord of the thing questioned, it perfects the matter of the inquiry, especially if reception intervenes. For the judgment of death is not entirely like the judgment of other things; for if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins the Lord of the eighth house <note>The house of death</note> without reception, it signifies death, unless the Lord of the eighth house receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, and the Lord of the Ascendant does not receive him, nor does the Moon. But if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon receives the Lord of the eighth, it signifies death whether the Lord of the eighth receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon or not. For death is not like other matters, because when it signifies death, it does not look to whether the thing is changed after it has happened or not; for no significator can change or destroy death after it has arrived in act. But other things change and are destroyed, sometimes even after they have been perfected. For when

<column-break/>

the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins the Lord of the thing questioned, or the Lord of the thing questioned joins the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies the effect of that thing. But although it may sometimes be perfected as I said to you above, if afterwards the Lord of the thing questioned joins a "malefic" <term>Malefic: A planet traditionally thought to bring misfortune, usually Saturn or Mars</term> hindering him to whom he committed the disposition, it destroys the matter after it has been perfected. In death, this cannot happen—that it be destroyed after it is perfected—because death itself dissolves every condition, and its sentence is such from which there can be no appeal. Regarding health or liberation, however, it is not so; for if some planet signifies the liberation of a sick man and is afterwards joined to a malefic planet who hinders him and commits its disposition to that malefic, the matter will be destroyed after it seemed certain that it should be perfected—that is, the liberation of the sick man. Wherefore, he who is seen to be liberated may die after it seemed he could escape; but he who is about to die cannot come back to life after death, whatever the receiver of the disposition may be seen to signify afterward.

¶ You shall also consider the Lord of the house signifying the sick person: in which part of the chart you find him—namely, in the first quarter, the second, the third, or the fourth—and judge by him. If you find him in the first quarter of the chart, it signifies that he asks about an illness that has already been. If he is in the second quarter, it signifies he asks about an illness that is now present. If, however, he is in the third quarter, it signifies he asks about a future illness or a relapse, for it signifies a recurring illness. And if he is in the last quarter, it signifies he asks about a chronic illness—that is, one which has been, is now, and will be or endure in the future. And this is all the more certain if he is joined with any of the Lords of the signs of any of those quarters in his own quarter.

### Chapter 5: Whether a servant shall be freed from
### servitude or not.

Whether he is liberated from sickness or not [having been discussed], it now remains to speak in this chapter about a servant: whether he shall be freed from servitude or not. This is not in vain, for servitude is compared to the most wicked sickness; for there is no sickness that could be called worse than that which always, everywhere, indifferently, and continuously afflicts. For there is no sickness that does not afflict with some interval or some rest, except for servitude; for in that, no interval or rest is found. Wherefore, if any question is moved to you for a servant—as if a servant should say simply, "See if I shall be freed from servitude or not"—then the first house gives [representation] to the servant, as do the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon likewise. The tenth house, however, gives [representation] to his master, whoever that master may be, even if he is otherwise a person of low status. 

Look then to the Lord of the Ascendant for the servant, and see if he is joined to the Lord of the tenth house, and if it is a perfect joining, whether it be physical or by aspect, of whatever kind the aspect may be, whether with reception or without reception. If the joining is complete degree by degree and minute by minute, say that he shall be freed from that servitude both easily and shortly. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is separated from the Lord of the tenth house by one minute or more, this signifies that he is already being freed from servitude. If what I told you regarding the Lord of the Ascendant is not the case, look then to the significatrix, namely the Moon, and judge according to what I told you about the Lord of the Ascendant.
