...power of my lord, in which I am, whether I shall depart from his power or not: look then to the lord of the ascendant <term>Ascendant: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question, representing the person asking</term> and see if he is cadent <term>Cadent: A planet in a house that does not touch the angles of the chart, often signifying weakness or a desire to leave</term> from an angle and does not aspect the ascendant; nor is he joined to a planet in an angle, nor one that aspects the ascendant; or if he is in the third or ninth house, or is joined to a planet in them, say that he shall be freed from that servitude and shall depart from the power of his master. But if it is not so for the lord of the ascendant, you shall judge the same regarding the Moon. If, however, the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in the ascendant, or in the tenth, fourth, or seventh house, or if any of them is joined to some planet in them, he shall not be freed—provided that the one to whom the lord of the ascendant or the Moon joins is direct <term>Direct: A planet moving forward through the zodiac; the opposite of retrograde</term>. If, however, he is retrograde, it signifies liberation, but with slowness and great labor, and with entanglement and delay. But if the lord of the ascendant is afflicted <term>Afflicted: A planet weakened by being in a difficult position or being "harmed" by a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</term> in the ascendant, or in the tenth, seventh, or fourth house, either by a bodily conjunction with some malefic planet, or by its opposition or square aspect; or if he enters into combustion <term>Combustion: When a planet is too close to the Sun, "burning up" its power and often signifying being hidden or destroyed</term>, he shall not be freed from that servitude except through death, which dissolves every snare with a grim solution.

### Chapter 6. Whether the master alienates the servant.

If a servant, sometimes hoping or perhaps fearing lest his lord sell him or alienate him in another way, asks: "Is my master, with whom I am, good for me, or is another to whom I am going better for me?" look then to the lord of the first house. If he is joined to some planet who receives him <term>Reception: A condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting a welcoming or supportive relationship</term> from the sign in which he is, by house or exaltation, or by two of the other minor dignities; and the lord of the seventh is not received—the one with whom he is and in whose power the servant resides is better for him. If, however, the lord of the seventh house is received, the one to whom he hopes to go is better for him. Furthermore, consider the lord of the ascendant and the Moon: see from whom either of them is separating, and see to whom they join. If they separate from a fortune <term>Fortune: A "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus that brings good luck</term> and join a malefic, the one with whom he is remains better. If, however, they separate from a malefic and join a fortune, the one to whom he intends to go is better for him. If both—namely the lord of the ascendant or the Moon—separate from a fortune and join a fortune, each will be good for him; but if the state of one fortune is better than the state of the other, judge according to that. If, however, they separate from a malefic and join a malefic, each will be bad for him, according to how each of them is disposed. And if you do not find that the lord of the ascendant or the Moon joins any planet—if both are void of course—look at the sign in which he is. Namely, if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon has greater dignity in that sign than in the seventh or in the second house—that is, by house, exaltation, term, triplicity, or face—the lord with whom he is will be better for him. If, however, he has greater dignity in the second or the seventh than in the ascending sign, the other lord is better for him than the first.

### Chapter 7. Concerning buying a servant, or any small animal, or a maidservant.

We have spoken of the servant, whether he is freed from servitude or not. It remains to be said in this chapter about buying a servant: and when I say "servant," you can understand the same for any small animal that is not ridden, which is signified by the sixth house. Hence, if someone is concerned about a servant and wishes to buy him, and puts the question to you whether the purchase of that servant he intends to buy will be completed or not: look to the lord of the ascendant and the significator <term>Significator: The planet that represents a specific person or thing in an astrological chart</term> which is the Moon, who are the significators of the questioner; and see if they both, or one of them, are joined to the lord of the sixth house, or the lord of the sixth house to the lord of the ascendant; or if you find some planet that transfers light <term>Translation of Light: When a faster planet moves from a conjunction or aspect with one planet to another, "carrying" the influence between them</term> between the lord of the

<column-break/>

ascendant and the lord of the sixth: tell him that he will acquire the servant of whom he asks, or the animal about which he inquires and which is signified by the sixth house. If, however, you do not find the lord of the ascendant joined to the lord of the sixth, nor the Moon, nor vice-versa; nor do you find a planet that transfers light between them, he shall not acquire the servant or animal of which he spoke. If, however, the inquiry is about buying a maidservant, Sarcinator <note>original: "sarcinator"; likely a reference to a medieval astrological authority, sometimes identified with Leopold of Austria or a similar compiler</note> said that you ought then to place the twelfth house for the maidservant. Arafatellus <note>original: "arafatellus"; likely a Latinized version of an Arabic authority such as Al-Rijal (Haly Abenragel)</note>, however, gave the sixth house for both the maidservant and the servant. The intention of Arafatellus was that when mention was made of a maidservant simply, she was part of the category of servants. The intention of Sarcinator, however, was as if the maidservant were the wife of a servant whom someone intended to buy; for if the sixth house signifies the servant, its opposite signifies the wife of the servant, which is the twelfth; and thus he spoke well of both. Hence, if a question is made about a maidservant as she is of the class of servants, you can give her the sixth just as for a servant. If, however, she is asked about as the wife of a servant about whom the question is made, you can give her the twelfth. You can also give that twelfth for another reason, namely when someone seeks a maidservant from another: the first house is given to the seeker; the seventh is given to the one from whom she is sought; the sixth from the seventh—which is the twelfth from the first—is given to the maidservant of the one from whom she is sought; and even in that same manner you could give the twelfth to a servant. For if a question is made to you about a maidservant and it is an absolute question as I told you above in the liberation of a servant, then you shall give her the sixth. If, however, it is a question about a maidservant as the wife of a servant, then you shall give her the twelfth. And if you find in the first condition the lord of the ascendant or the Moon joining with the lord of the sixth, or the lord of the sixth with the lord of the ascendant, say that he will obtain the maidservant of whom he speaks. If you find in the second condition the lord of the ascendant or the Moon joining with the lord of the twelfth, or the lord of the twelfth with them, judge that same thing. If some planet transfers light between them, it will signify the obtaining of her just as I told you regarding the servant.

### Chapter 8. Whether the master acquires the goods of the servant or maidservant.

In this chapter, it remains to say whether the goods of a servant will come into the hands of his master or not. For a certain servant of a certain man had died, and he whose servant he was asked whether he would obtain the remains <term>Remains: The estate or left-over property of the deceased</term> of that servant. See if such a question is made to you: you must then look to the lord of the ascendant and the Moon, and see if they both, or either of them, join the lord of the seventh house, which has the significance of the servant's substance; for it is the second from the sixth <term>Second from the Sixth: In "derivative houses," the 2nd house from any given house represents the wealth or resources of the person represented by that house</term>, which signifies servants, and the seventh is their substance. Say then that the master will acquire the sought-after substance, namely that which was his servant's. Say the same if the lord of the seventh is joined to the lord of the first house. Similarly, if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in the seventh, or if the lord of the seventh is in the ascendant or even in the second; but that is not so certain, for if the lord of the second were then afflicted, or if the lord of the seventh received him but the lord of the second did not receive him, the master could suffer loss in his own substance for the sake of recovering the servant's substance. Likewise, if some planet transfers light between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the seventh, the master will obtain the substance of the servant through the hands of someone who involves himself in it.

...and the Moon, which are the significators <term>Significator: A planet that represents a person or thing in an astrological chart</term> of the seeker <note>Latin: *querentis*</note> and the seventh house and its lord <term>Lord: The planet that rules a specific zodiac sign or house</term>, which are the significators of the person sought <note>Latin: *quesiti*</note>. For a woman can just as well ask about a man as a man about a woman. And see how and in what way they aspect each other.

If indeed the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is joined bodily <term>Bodily conjunction: When two planets occupy the same degree of the zodiac</term> to the lord of the seventh: if it is a man who asks, he shall obtain the woman; if it is a woman who asks, she shall obtain the man, and the matrimony shall be completed. If, however, they aspect each other from a trine <term>Trine: An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</term> or a sextile <term>Sextile: An aspect of 60 degrees, considered helpful</term> aspect, the matrimony shall be completed, whether that aspect or bodily conjunction is with reception <term>Reception: A supportive relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</term> or without reception. 

But if the aspect is from an opposition <term>Opposition: An aspect of 180 degrees, usually signifying conflict</term>, it shall not be completed unless reception intervenes; otherwise, there is no hope for it. If it is without reception, there may be hope that it is completed and it may be firmly believed to be so, yet it shall not be finished—unless by chance it happens, as sometimes occurs, that those who have the matter in hand (and are able to do it) are such friends of the seeker that they bring about the union; then perhaps the matter might be completed, even for the man. 

In the same way, if the lord of the seventh is joined to the lord of the ascendant by the aforementioned conjunctions. Similarly, if the lord of the seventh is in the ascendant, the marriage shall be completed with ease and without difficulty; and the desire will be more on the part of the woman than the man, if the man is the seeker. If the woman is the seeker, it will be more the desire of the man than the woman. 

But if the significators do not aspect each other, but there is some planet that transfers the light <term>Translation of Light: When a faster-moving planet moves from an aspect with one significator to an aspect with the other, "connecting" them</term> between them, the matter will be done through the hands of those who involve themselves in that business. And see of which house that planet is the lord which transfers the light between them, because the matter will be done through the person signified by that house. If it is a masculine planet, it will be a man; if feminine, a woman. 

Then look for the planet that transfers the light or the disposition <note>Latin: *dispositionem*</note> between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the seventh <gloss>that is, they commit the disposition</gloss> to the lord of the ascendant or the Moon and the lord of the seventh. If it is free from impediments—meaning it is not retrograde, nor combust <term>Combust: Weakened by being too close to the Sun</term>, nor falling from the angles or from the ascendant; nor besieged by malefic planets <term>Malefics: Mars or Saturn, traditionally seen as bringing difficulty</term>, nor in their opposition or square aspect without reception—if it is so, say that the matter shall be completed and shall last. 

If the receiver of the disposition or the translator of light is a fortunate planet <term>Fortuna: A lucky planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</term> and is free from the aforementioned impediments, the marriage will last in a good, tranquil, useful, and kind state. But if it is a malefic, even if found free from the aforementioned impediments, and even if it signifies the perfection of the marriage and its durability, nevertheless there will be many contentions, many altercations, and many quarrels between them, though not always. And those whisperings will come more from the side of the person whose significator was the malefic planet, whether the man or the woman. And perhaps a divorce <note>Latin: *divortium*</note> will be celebrated between them by reason of those whisperings. 

But if that receiver of the disposition or translator of light is an unfortunate and malefic planet, the matter will be destroyed after it was believed and thought to be settled; and it will be destroyed with a bad destruction so that ill-will, contentions, and enmities shall arise from it. If, however, it is a fortunate planet but is hindered by the aforementioned impediments or any one of them, understand that in any case the matter will not be completed even after it was thought to be settled; but enmities and contentions will not arise from it. And if they do arise, they will not be lasting; rather, both parties will perhaps depart from the proposal plainly and by common will.

And if that planet which transfers the light between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 7th is naturally malefic, there will be detriment and destruction from the part of those who involve themselves in that matter and who seem to want to complete it.

### Chapter 3. How they will behave together.

Although I have touched upon something for you above regarding how the husband and wife will behave toward each other if the marriage is completed, I will nevertheless tell you more about that same thing, nor is it a matter that seems to me should be diminished. 

And it is that you should look to see if the lord of the ascendant joins the lord of the seventh, or the lord of the seventh to the lord of the ascendant, by a trine aspect and with reception: they will always live together while they both last in a good and peaceful state and in concord that will not be disturbed in any way; and one will always want what the other wants. 

If, however, the conjunction is by a trine aspect without reception, or by a sextile with reception, it will be almost the same thing; yet there will sometimes be some slight contentions or altercations between them, but neither will care about them nor hold them in their heart. 

If, however, the conjunction is by a sextile aspect without reception, or by a square with reception, it also signifies concord and a good state between them; but there will many times be discords and contentions between them, but they will not be long-lasting. And if the Moon is joined to a planet in whose house she is, or in whose exaltation <term>Exaltation: A sign where a planet is particularly strong and honored</term>, it will be that same thing...

If indeed the aspect is from an opposition <note>original: *aspectus ex oppositione*; an angle of 180 degrees</note>, it signifies a multitude of discords and contention between them, often enduring for a long time, and they shall very rarely be well together. And if they are joined bodily <term>Bodily conjunction: When two planets are in the exact same degree of the zodiac</term> in one sign so that there are fewer degrees between them than the quantity of the orb <term>Orb: The range of influence surrounding a planet's exact position</term> of the one of them—specifically the one that has the smaller orb. 

After this, look at the lord of the ascendant <note>The planet ruling the sign currently rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the lord of the seventh <note>The planet ruling the house of marriage/partnerships</note>: which of them is heavier <term>Heavier: A "ponderous" planet is one that moves more slowly through the zodiac, like Saturn or Jupiter, often indicating greater power or seniority</term> or is located in an angle <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart</term>. If the Sun is afflicted <term>Afflicted: A planet "impedited" or weakened by a difficult aspect from a "malefic" planet like Mars or Saturn</term>, the man’s state shall be worsened. If, however, Venus is afflicted, the woman’s state shall be hindered and worsened. But if the Moon is afflicted, it signifies hindrance and worsening for both the man and the woman; even if they both commonly wish to rejoice and be well together, they shall not be able to, and both will be largely unfortunate. Similarly, if the Moon is afflicted and aspects the ascendant, or if a malefic <note>A planet like Mars or Saturn</note> is in the ascendant, there shall be contentions and discords between them arising from the seeker’s side. The occasion for contention and discord will be caused by the significators of that house ruled by the malefic planet in the ascendant or seventh; for example, if it is the lord of the second house, the cause will be wealth; if it is the lord of the third, it will be because of brothers; and understand the same for all other houses according to their specific nature.

### Chapter four: regarding whether a woman is corrupted, or a virgin, or has a lover, or another whom she loves besides her husband (if she is married) or besides her lover (if she has one).

If perhaps someone wishing to enter into marriage with a certain woman suspects she is not a virgin—perhaps because some have spoken ill of her, as often happens, sometimes due to envy, sometimes to disturb the marriage so it is not completed, or perhaps some man who sought an unchaste act from her which she refused, and he wishes to be certain of this—and he comes to you to move the question of whether that woman is a virgin or not: you shall then consider the ascendant and its lord, and the significatress, which is the Moon. In this case, the seeker <note>the man</note> does not have a house or a planet for his significator <note>Because the question is focused entirely on the woman's condition</note>. See if both are in angles and fixed signs <term>Fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; they represent stability and unchanging states</term>. If so, say that the woman is a virgin, such that there is no vice of corruption in her. If anything bad is said of her, the one who said it should not be believed, for they all lie; no uncleanness can be found in her, nor was she even tempted by anyone. But if the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are in fixed signs, but the angles are moveable signs <term>Moveable signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; they represent change and movement</term>, she was tempted but did not accept the advances of the tempter. If, however, the Moon is joined to Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, or the Sun, either bodily or by aspect within five degrees or less, she is being tempted by someone who bears the appearance of that planet to which she is joined. But if the Moon is joined to Venus or Mercury, she is being tempted by some woman on behalf of some man, yet she does not care for it nor will she agree to the words 

<column-break/>

of that person, but rather makes a mockery of that temptress. If indeed the Moon is separated from the aforementioned planets by three minutes <note>A very small unit of astrological measurement</note>, the woman was once with a temptress or other tempters, but they have ceased that temptation. If, however, the angles are fixed signs and the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are in moveable or common signs <term>Common signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces; they represent transition</term>—though common signs are of less import than moveable—she was tempted and is still being tempted; at one time she endured what the temptress women said to her, yet she did not yield to them, but perseveres in her virginity. 

But if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in moveable signs, or if both are in common signs and the Moon is joined with any of the aforementioned masculine planets, some man who bears the appearance of that planet has already embraced and kissed her, and has touched the private parts of the woman, and even placed his genitals near hers. It went so far that he believed he had known her <note>had sex with her</note>, and she was deceived so that her virginity expired; yet she did not believe she had lost it, because she did not complete that shameful act on her part. What was done here was the cause of a bad example. Such things are accustomed to happen when men have much domestic intimacy with women or frequent them often, or sometimes at great banquets, or by going to gardens, or when women go to festivals far away or remote from their cities and families. 

But if the Moon was then with the Head of the Dragon <term>Head of the Dragon: The North Node of the moon, usually considered increasing or beneficial</term>, the matter was one of touch but not of perfection <note>completion of the sex act</note>, and she did not lose her virginity for that reason. If, however, the Tail of the Dragon <term>Tail of the Dragon: The South Node of the moon, associated with loss, corruption, or "decreasing"</term> was in the place of the Head, let her be judged as having been guilty in the past, guilty now, and not free from crime in the future. The same can be said of Mars if he is in the place of the Head, except that Mars does not impose as much malice upon a woman as the Tail imposes. 

If indeed the Moon is joined to Venus under the aforementioned conditions of signs and angles, it does not appear that she completed the act, but it was not for lack of her trying; and it appears to be something else regarding her: for she seems to love girls and to rub herself with them and commit sodomy with them, completing her shame against nature. And if the Moon is afflicted in the last face <term>Face: A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> of Gemini, the woman has already corrupted herself with her own hands and took her own virginity. If, however, it is afflicted in the last term <term>Term: An irregular subdivision of a sign ruled by a specific planet</term> of the said sign, it signifies that the woman perseveres in that malice. 

And if the ascendant is a moveable or common sign, or the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are in moveable or common signs, the woman's virginity has already been taken earnestly and with her consent; and even if it were not with her consent, she is nevertheless devirginated. And if the ascendant is a fixed sign and the lord of the ascendant is in a fixed sign, even if the Moon is in a moveable or common sign—or if the Moon is in a fixed sign even if the lord of the ascendant is in a moveable sign or the ascendant is a moveable or common sign—nevertheless the woman has not lost her virginity. It could be, perhaps, that someone by violence brought his genitals near the private parts of the woman and ejaculated there, yet did not corrupt her.

### Chapter five: if a woman acts with someone other than her husband.

If someone, touched by the jealousy of a wife <note>meaning: "jealousy regarding his wife"</note>, comes to you to move a question about this, doubting lest she do evil with another: look in this case at the ascendant and its lord, and the Moon, and the planet from which she is separating, who are the significators <term>Significator: The planet or house representing a specific person in the chart</term> of the inquirer; and the seventh house and its lord, and the planet to which the Moon is joined, which are the significators of the woman. And see to whom the Moon or the lord of the seventh is joined; for if the lord of the seventh and the Moon are joined to the lord of the ascendant, whether with reception <term>Reception: When a planet is in a sign ruled by another planet, indicating a cooperative relationship</term> or without reception—provided it is not joined to another by a closer aspect or conjunction—say the woman is to be blamed in nothing, whatever is said of her.

And if indeed the lord of the seventh or the Moon (or either of them) joins the lord of the triplicity of the ascendant—second or third—or if any of them joins the lord of the seventh and the lord of the seventh or the Moon separates from the lord of the ascendant, it appears the woman has another whom she loves besides her husband. If, however, you find the lord of the seventh void of course <term>Void of course: When a planet makes no further major aspects before leaving its current sign, often indicating that "nothing will come" of the matter</term>, the woman has no lover, nor is she to be blamed.

If you find the lord of the seventh or the Moon (or both) separated from another planet besides the lord of the ascendant, and that separation was not more than three degrees, the woman loved another besides him but afterwards left him. If indeed the lord of the seventh is with the Head of the Dragon <note>original: *capite draconis*; the North Node of the Moon, generally considered an increasing or positive influence</note> without the conjunction of another, say the woman is not to be blamed. If indeed it is with the Tail <note>original: *cauda*; the South Node of the Moon, generally considered a decreasing or malefic influence</note> without another's conjunction, she appears blameworthy, and could be blamed in the past, now, and in the future.

Then look if the lord of the seventh or the Moon is joined to any with Mars, and the Head of the Dragon is there: it appears the woman has a lover whom she loves and who "uses" her. And if the Tail is with Mars and with the lord of the seventh or the Moon joined thus as I said, it diminishes the malice; and although the woman perhaps loves someone who bears the image of Mars <note>e.g., a soldier or someone with a fiery temperament</note>, he has not yet joined her under his yoke. And if Mars is with the lord of the seventh or with the Moon in one sign, joined without the Tail, the woman has a lover in her region, not very far from her house.

# Chapter Seven: If someone wishes to take a "corrupted" woman as his wife.

And if someone wishes to take a "corrupted" <note>A term used in this period to describe a woman who is not a virgin</note> woman as a wife—perhaps because it is said of her that she already has children—as sometimes happens when widows or other corrupted women act secretly with someone, conceive, give birth, and have the children raised in secret, or cast them off to hospitals or other religious places, and there is sometimes a murmur that this is the case. Therefore, some fear to take such wives because of the infamy, or perhaps for another reason, and they come to you to ask whether that woman has a son. Zael <note>Zael Ben Briz, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were widely translated into Latin</note> said that you must look at Venus: if she is in Aquarius or Leo and Mercury is with her, the woman has never given birth nor conceived. If, however, Venus and Mercury are both in Taurus or Scorpio, he said that the woman has a son. Similarly, if Mars, Venus, and the Moon—or even just one of them—is with Mars in Gemini, Virgo, or Pisces, the woman has a son. But if the aforementioned planets are in Sagittarius, they signify the woman’s sterility, past, present, and future; and if it is found that she has given birth until now, that son will die and will not remain after her. And if Saturn and Mars are in Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, the woman will be saddened because of that son; he was born from a lover <note>original: *amasio*</note>, not from her husband, nor did she keep faith with her husband. But if Jupiter and Venus are in the aforementioned signs—namely Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn—that son or that conception is from her own husband without the mixing of malice.

# Chapter Eight: Whether a woman who has left or been expelled from the home will return or not.

A certain chapter is subordinated to the one above, such that it can rightly be included under it. It concerns what very often happens: when men expel women from the house, sometimes with cause and sometimes without; or women depart from their husbands' houses voluntarily, either with cause or out of fear that their husbands might beat them, or for any other occasion. And if a woman should come to you who has gone out from the house in which she lived with her husband (or perhaps with a lover) and asks you whether she will return to the house or not: look then to the lord of the seventh house, which is the ascendant of the woman in this case—since the seventh house is given to the expelled person—and see if he looks at the ascendant in such a way that no other planet looks at the ascendant as well as he does. If so, say that the woman will return to the house from which she went out. Understand the same regarding the Moon. If the lord of the seventh house does not aspect the ascendant, but aspects another planet that is not hindered and which aspects the ascendant, the woman will return to the house through the intervention of some person who will involve themselves in the matter and reconcile her with her husband. But if none of these occur, look then at the Sun, who is naturally the significator of the husband, and Venus, who is naturally the significatrix of the woman. And if the Sun is then above the earth and Venus aspects the ascendant with a favorable aspect—namely a trine or sextile—the woman will return to the sought-after house with ease

# Chapter Nine: Concerning a lawsuit or controversy between parties; who will prevail, who will lose, or if they will settle before the trial or not.

If someone wishes to be certain about a lawsuit or controversy that is occurring between people, or is prepared to occur—which of the parties ought to prevail—and moves this question to you: look at the ascendant at the hour in which you were questioned by him who made the inquiry, and its lord and significatrix—namely the Moon—for the seeker; and look at the seventh house and its lord for the adversary. If a "light" planet performs the function of a "heavy" one and does not receive him, but the heavy one receives the light one, it signifies that the recipient wants to agree, even if the light one does not want to and will not stand by him; and even more so if it is a trine or sextile aspect. And if they are joined bodily in one sign so that their conjunction is not hindered by anything—whether with reception or without—they will agree even without the intervention of another. If, however, it is **Mars**, the judge will be false, full of wrath, unfaithful, not loving justice, and one who moves and changes quickly from purpose to purpose, so that the final error will be worse than the first, and they will repent having chosen such a judge. If it is the **Sun**, he will be a judge of good spirit, yet he will allow himself to be drawn by the prayers of friends and will lean toward them and give them his ear and the hope of doing what they wish; in the end, however, he will judge rightly. And if **Venus** is there, he will be a just judge and of good reputation, but he will not be very deep in the law; nevertheless, he will judge in good faith. And if **Mercury** is in the tenth, the judge will be of good and sharp wit, quickly seeing the heart of the matter; but he will judge according to how he applies to the planets: if to **benefics** <term>Benefics: "Good-doing" planets, specifically Jupiter and Venus, which bring harmony</term>, he judges justly; if to **malefics** <term>Malefics: "Evil-doing" planets, specifically Saturn and Mars, which bring difficulty</term>, he judges unjustly; if to none, he will judge according to the evidence he finds. And in all the above-mentioned events, the **lord of the ascendant** and the **lord of the seventh** and the other aforementioned significators are considered without the participation of the **Moon**; although she is naturally a participant in all things, her influence is somewhat diminished here. If, however, the Moon is in the tenth, the judge will be light and unstable, judging as it seems to him at the moment, not considering much what the law is, nor caring what he judges, nor what is said of his judgment, whether good or bad.

There is also a certain **secret consideration** which I never remember finding in the sayings of the ancients; yet I have experienced it and found it to be true. Namely, you should consider the position of the lord of the ascendant and the position of the lord of the **second house** and subtract the smaller from the larger; and what remains will be the "residue" of the lord of the first and the lord of the second. Then consider the position of the lord of the seventh and the position of the lord of the **eighth house** and subtract the smaller from the larger; and what remains will be the "residue" of the lord of the seventh and the lord of the eighth. Take those two residues and subtract the smaller from the larger, and keep that third residue. Then take the position of the lord of the **ninth house** and the position of the lord of the **twelfth house** and subtract the smaller from the larger; and what remains will be the signifying part of the 9th and 12th lords. Take that and the third residue and subtract the smaller from the larger; what remains will be the part signifying the help and strength of the seeker or the thing sought. Add to this the degree of the ascending sign and project it from the ascendant as you do for the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: A specific mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and success</term> if it be by day; if, however, it be by night, project it from the **nadir** <note>The point directly opposite the ascendant</note>. See in whose house, or exaltation, or term, or triplicity that number ends; for the planet who is the lord of that place, and is stronger and more powerful in it, will be the sought-after helper for the one whose significator he aspects most closely, minute by minute; or whoever is closer to that place, provided he has some **dignity** <term>Dignity: A position of strength for a planet, such as being in its own zodiac sign</term> in it that makes him stronger; and more so if this is with **reception** <note>A condition where planets "host" each other, showing mutual support</note>. But if both those residues are equal, the signification will be in the ascendant by day, and in the nadir by night. And when you have worked this, always prefer the lord; if he is impeded, work through the lord of the exaltation. If he is impeded, work through the lord of the term. If he is impeded, work finally through the lord of the triplicity. For the planet in whose place that "part" falls,

### Chapter 10. On Buying and Selling.

If anyone wishing to buy something should move a question to you about buying that thing—whether he is to obtain that thing or not: look then to the lord of the ascendant, who is the significator of the seeker <note>The buyer</note>, and similarly the Moon, who is not to be omitted. Look to the lord of the seventh house, who is the significator of the seller, and of the thing sold absolutely, unless the thing to be bought is specifically determined. And see if the lord of the ascendant or the Moon are joined with the lord of the seventh, or the lord of the seventh with the lord of the ascendant; the seeker will obtain the thing he asks about without great delay or invention, and the completion of the purchase or sale will come from the side of the one whose significator is **lighter** <term>Lighter: A planet that moves faster through the zodiac (like the Moon or Mercury), indicating the party who takes the initiative</term>. For example, if the lord of the ascendant is lighter, it will come from the seeker; if the lord of the seventh is lighter, it will come from the seller. If, however, the aforementioned significators are not joined by any conjunction or aspect, see if the Moon or another planet **transfers the light** <term>Transfer of Light: When a fast planet connects two slower planets, acting as a go-between or broker</term> between them. If so, it signifies that some person will intercede in that matter, and the thing will be completed in that way. Even if the translation of light were made from one planet to the seven planets, as long as it brings the light back to the lord of the ascendant or at least to the ascendant itself, it will complete the matter of the question.

If the question is specific, see what the asker inquires about. If he asks about buying a servant or any of those things signified by the house of servants <note>The 6th house, though the text here is slightly ambiguous</note>, give the seeker the [house] of the thing sought. If he asks about a horse, or an ox, or any of those things signified by the **twelfth house**, give the seeker the twelfth of the thing sought. If he asks about buying a city, or a village, or a castle, the first [house] is given to the seeker and the **fourth house** to the thing sought. Thus you can understand any saleable thing through the house by which it is signified.

Then see: if the lord of the seventh is in the first, the seller will press the buyer to buy that thing, and the will of the seller will be greater than that of the buyer. If the lord of the first is in the seventh, the buyer will press the seller to sell that thing, and the will of the buyer will be greater than that of the seller. Also look if any of the good planets are in the first—that is, Jupiter or Venus—the purchase will be completed without labor, without entanglement, and without delay, nor will the buyer strive to deceive the seller. If the Sun is there and is not in the company of any [malefic] planet, it will be the same. And if Mercury or the Moon are there and neither is in aspect to any malefic, it signifies the same as the Sun. If, however, any of the good planets are in the seventh, it signifies goodness on the part of the seller, just as I told you of the first for the buyer. If any of the malefics are there, it signifies malice on the part of the seller, just as I told you on the part of the buyer. Then look if the Moon is separated from any planet and is...

# Chapter 11. Whether a thief or another who flees may be found or not: or if they return of their own will.

**I**f anyone has fled from another, such as when a male or female servant or another servant flees; or if perhaps there was someone who was a guest and took something from him and fled; or perhaps it is a wife who similarly flees, and [the seeker] wants to find that person or thing and brings a question to you whether they may be found or not, and to which direction they fled: look at the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the person asking (the querent).</term> and its lord, and the Sun, and give these to the seeker. Give the **seventh house** and its lord to the one who fled, along with the Moon, which naturally signifies every fleeing thing because of her swift speed and motion. Then see if the lord of the first house joins in any way with the lord of the seventh, or if the lord of the first is in the seventh; this signifies that he will find him if he truly wishes to pursue him and studies well in searching for him. And if the lord of the seventh is joined to the lord of the first, or if the lord of the seventh is in the first, or if he is joined with a **retrograde planet**, it does not appear that the seeker needs to labor much in finding the one who fled: for one of two things will happen: either he will return of his own will and spontaneous motion, or the seeker will find him before he gets very far from the house where he stays. Similarly, look at the Moon, which signifies the fugitive: if she is separated at that time from the lord of the first and joined immediately to the lord of the seventh, it signifies that someone who knows news of the fugitive will come to the seeker and tell him where the one who fled is. And if the Moon is separated from the lord of the seventh and joined to the lord of the first, the fugitive will repent having fled, but will be afraid to return; therefore he will send word to the seeker to secure a promise of safety, and so he will return without further investigation by the seeker. Next, see if the lord of the seventh is joined to any malevolent planet <term>Malevolents: Usually Mars or Saturn, associated with hardship or obstruction.</term> in an **angle** <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, where planets are most active.</term>: or if a malevolent is joined to him, it signifies that the fugitive will be captured if the seeker pursues him well. But if both the lord of the seventh and the malevolent who hinders him are not in an angle, but only one of them is in an angle, the fugitive will not be caught such that he is put in prison, but he will be found and detained without being locked up. If, however, the lord of the first house aspects <term>Aspect: A specific geometric angle between planets that allows them to "see" or influence each other.</term> that malevolent which hinders the lord of the seventh, the seeker will find the fugitive detained by someone to whom he must give money before they will hand the fugitive over. Similarly, if a malevolent is in the **ninth house**, it signifies a hindrance to the fugitive on his journey and that he will be captured. But if a benefic <term>Fortuna: A "fortune" or benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus, associated with protection.</term> is in the ninth, the fugitive will not be caught, nor can he be caught unless that benefic is greatly hindered. Then look to see if the Sun and Moon are joined to the lord of the seventh or aspect him from any position—or at least one of them: for then the fugitive will not be able to hide himself so as not to be found. It is the same if the lord of the seventh enters into combustion or is already combust: it signifies the fugitive will be found even though he has 

<column-break/>

hidden himself. And if the lord of the first or any of the malevolents aspects him then, he will be captured and led away bound. If, however, the lord of the seventh is joined to any benefic by body or aspect, whether it is under the Sun's rays or not, the fugitive will be captured if he is found, except in one way: that is, if that benefic is retrograde or combust or entering under the Sun’s rays; for then it cannot defend him from being caught. Next, look to see if the lord of the seventh is joined with a **stationary planet**, in whichever station it may be—either the first or the second—and if it is in an angle or following an angle; this signifies that the fugitive does not know how to flee and knows not which direction to take, whether to flee or not; and so he will stay in one place until he is found and caught. Consider capture only when a planet is stationary; for if it is in its first station, then the seeker will catch the fugitive, or someone else will catch him and hand him over. But if it is in the second station, the fugitive will be caught, perhaps on the road while fleeing, and will be imprisoned and bound, but he will flee again from that prison or from those chains, so that it appears he escapes and is not caught again. And if that planet to which the lord of the seventh is joined is **direct**, Zahel said the fugitive will be caught but not returned to prison; he will simply be returned to the seeker or the one searching for him, and will not be imprisoned for this. Furthermore, if the Moon is increasing in light and speed <note>original: *numero*, referring to the Moon's daily motion.</note>, he will be pursued for a long time before being caught, and his capture or discovery will be much prolonged. But if she is decreasing in light and speed, he will be found more quickly and with less labor. 

To know toward which direction the fugitive goes, look at the significator of the fugitive, which is the Moon: and see where she is then. If she is in the Ascendant or between the Ascendant and the fourth house, it signifies he will flee toward the **East**. If in the first house exactly, directly East. If in the second, toward the East but inclining toward the **North**. If in the third, inclining even more toward the North. If, however, the Moon is in the tenth house, it signifies he will flee toward the **South**. If in the eleventh, toward the South but inclining toward the East; if in the twelfth, inclining more toward the East. If she is in the seventh house, it signifies the fugitive goes toward the **West**. If in the eighth, toward the West inclining toward the South. If in the ninth, inclining more toward the South. And if she is in the fourth house, it signifies the fugitive goes toward the **North**. If in the fifth, toward the North inclining toward the West. If in the sixth, inclining more toward the West. And you may also add or subtract something by your own skill according to whether you see the Moon or the lord of the seventh in an eastern, southern, western, or northern sign or quarter. 

If the one who fled is a thief, and the asker either follows or wishes to pursue him as a thief, the judgment will be the same in all things as for other fugitives; with the added detail that if the planet with which the lord of the seventh is joined enters into combustion then, it signifies the thief will die at the time of his capture, if he is caught. And if the planet with which the lord of the seventh joins as it enters combustion is also joined to a malevolent, it signifies the thief will be found in such a way that it will not be useful to the one who finds him; for he will find him dead, perhaps by a "bad death"; he might find him hanged, or decapitated, or burned, or perhaps his body will be mutilated. For if **Mars** is in the seventh house and the lord of the seventh is hindered in the tenth, he will be hanged. If, however, the Moon is under the Sun's rays and is otherwise hindered by Mars, he will be burned. And if Mars is in the Ascendant while hindering the lord of the seventh or the Moon, he will be decapitated. But if it is **Saturn** who hinders the lord of the seventh or the Moon and is below the earth, he will be drowned and suffocated in water.

### Chapter 12. On theft: whether it is found again or the seeker attains it or not.

**I**f anyone comes to you about a theft committed, [asking] whether he may recover the things taken by theft or not, and you wish to look into that matter for him: look at the first house <note>The "First House" or Ascendant represents the person asking the question.</note> of the hour of the question and its lord and the significatrix, namely the Moon, who are the significators of the one asking. And look at the seventh house and its lord for the thief, since the thief is signified by the lord of the seventh. If indeed you find him in the seventh, it signifies that the questioner could find the thief if he wishes to inquire well and to work and study in this, that is, so that he finds him. If however you wish to know whether he finds the stolen thing again, look at the second house from the Ascendant. If its lord is joined to the lord of the eighth house and "receives" <note>Reception: A relationship where one planet is in a sign governed by another, indicating cooperation or support.</note> it—which has the significance of the thief's substance—the seeker will obtain the stolen thing or [payment] from the thief's goods so that he satisfies himself for the theft committed. Say the same regarding the lord of the first if it is joined to the lord of the eighth and receives it. If, however, the lord of the second from the Ascendant—which signifies the substance of the questioner and even the stolen thing itself—is combust <term>Combust: A planet is "combust" when it is very close to the Sun, which was thought to "burn up" its power and hide the matter it represents.</term>, it signifies that the thief has sold off <note>original: "distrarit," likely a contraction for *distraxerit*.</note>, consumed, dissipated, and destroyed the stolen thing. Thus, although the seeker finds the thief, he will not find the theft or the stolen thing. If the lord of the second has emerged from combustion, the seeker will find part of the theft but will not find the whole, and scarcely or never will he find more than half of the theft. Then look if the lord of the seventh house was in the first or was joined to the lord of the first: the thief will repent of having stolen that thing and will return it to the one to whom it belonged. Then look if the lord of the first was joined to any planet existing in the tenth house, in the first, or at least in the seventh: for if it were so, the questioner will find the thief even without the greatest inquiry. And if the lord of the first was joined to a planet "falling from an angle" <term>Cadent: Planets in houses 3, 6, 9, or 12, which are considered weaker and often signify things that are hidden or far away.</term> which does not "behold" or aspect the Ascendant, it signifies that the thief has already left that land and distanced himself from it so much that there is no hope in finding him. But if that falling planet to which the lord of the first is joined aspects the Ascendant, it signifies the finding of the thief as if after despair, and with custody and great inquiry. Furthermore, if you find the lord of the seventh combust and the lord of the first aspects him, it signifies the finding of the thief when he did not believe he would be found. Similarly, if the Moon transfers light between the lord of the first and the lord of the seventh, it signifies the finding of the thief. And if the lord of the first does not aspect him and he is "under the rays" <note>original: "sub radijs," a state similar to combustion but less severe, where the planet is still hidden by the Sun's light.</note>, namely the significator of the thief, he will be found nonetheless, but not so easily. If, however, the lord of the first and the lord of the second were both joined

to the lord of the tenth, the power or the magistrate <note>original: "potestas siue rector."</note> will compel the thief to return the stolen thing to the questioner or to the owner; or the thief will return it for fear lest he be led before the power or magistrate of that land in which he was detained. ## Chapter 13. Whether a lost thing is found.

If someone asks you at any time simply about a lost or stolen thing—and perhaps they mention it as a theft, and perhaps not, but says, "Look concerning a certain thing of mine which I lost, whether I shall find it again or not"—and you wish to look for him whether it was stolen or not, or lost otherwise: you must then look at the lord <note>The "lord" is the planet that rules a specific zodiac sign or house in the chart.</note> of the first house and the significator of the Moon. And if both are joined to the lord of the second house from the ascendant, who is the significator of property <note>original: "substantie"; meaning one's wealth or material goods.</note>, it signifies the discovery of the lost thing quickly and with little labor. But if only one of them—that is, the lord of the first house or the Moon—is joined to the lord of the second, it signifies the discovery of the taken thing, but not as easily as when both aspect. But if neither of them is joined to the lord of the second, nor aspects him, see then if any planet transfers the light from one of them to the other; this similarly signifies that he will find the thing about which he asks. And if there is no planet which transfers light between them, but there is one who is heavier <note>A "heavier" planet is one that moves more slowly through the zodiac, like Saturn or Jupiter.</note> than the lord of the first and the lord of the second, to whom both are joined and he himself receives the light of both, it signifies the discovery of the sought thing. Similarly, even if the lord of the second is in the second house (which has custody over property) or aspects it by a trine or sextile aspect <note>Trines (120 degrees) and sextiles (60 degrees) are considered "harmonious" or helpful alignments between planets.</note>, it signifies the discovery of the lost thing, but with delay, entanglement, care, and the anxiety of the seeker. And if you do not find the lord of the second in the second house, but another planet is in the second and the lord of the second is joined to it (or it to him), it signifies the discovery of the sought thing, whether that conjunction be by body or by aspect. But if the lord of the second is not in the second house, nor is there a planet there which he aspects, nor does he aspect by a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies the loss of the sought thing and that he will not recover it. Furthermore, if you find the lord of the eighth house from the ascendant joined to the lord of the seventh, he will not recover the lost thing; because it signifies that he who has it (whether he be the thief or another to whom the thing itself came) has appropriated it for himself. And say the same if the lord of the seventh is joined to the lord of the second, or he to him, without the conjunction of the lord of the ascendant or the Moon; because if the lord of the first or the Moon aspects them while they are thus joined to each other, it signifies the rediscovery of the sought thing, although with litigation and controversy. And if the lord of the eighth is joined to the lord of the second, it signifies that the seeker will recover the lost thing; because the conjunction of the lord of the eighth signifies that the property of the thief (or of him who has the seeker's thing) will pass into the property of the questioner and become his as it was before. And if there be a dispute over it, the seeker will prevail and recover. And if he does not recover the same thing...

<column-break/>

...he will recover from the goods of the thief or other adversary as much as his thing was worth, and he will be satisfied for the lost thing; this is especially and most safely true if the lord of the first house then aspects the lord of the eighth or second. And if the lord of the tenth house then aspects them, it signifies that the power, or a judge, or a ruler will take those things and they will come into his hands, and he will give hope from there that whatever seems to him to be done will be done. But if the lord of the eighth house is then joined to the lord of the tenth house, it signifies that the thief or adversary will give money to the power or ruler so that he himself does not harm him, but rather is a help to him. Then look and see: if the lord of the second is not joined to the lord of the first, nor to the lord of the eighth, it signifies that the thing about which the inquiry is made is utterly lost; and that he will not recover it henceforth, indeed he will count it as almost nothing. Then look if the lord of the second is joined with the lord of the third, or with the lord of the ninth, or with any planet existing in them, or is himself in them; it signifies that he who stole the thing or property, or he to whom it came, has carried it out of that land to another. Then look if the Sun and Moon are both under the earth at the hour of the question, or at the hour when the thing was taken; it signifies that the thing will not be recovered by any means, nor can it be recovered; nor will the thief be known, nor the lost thing known, nor known who had it. Then look if the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are both in the ascendant, and the Sun aspects them by a trine or sextile aspect; it signifies that the thing about which he asks will be found again on the first day in which it was taken or lost. But if the Sun aspects by a fourth aspect <note>original: "ex quarto aspectu"; a square aspect, or 90 degrees, usually considered stressful.</note>, it will be found in that week. But if it aspects by opposition <note>A 180-degree alignment.</note>, it will be found in that month and return to its lord. Understand the same concerning any thing, in whatever way it was lost or taken.

## Chapter 14. Whether the thief or the one having the lost thing is of the household, or of what conditions he might be.

If the seeker suspects whether the thief or he who has the sought thing is of the household, or of what status he might be, and wants to know that from you: see if the Sun and the Moon both simultaneously aspect the ascendant, or if the lord of the ascendant is in the ascendant, or is bodily joined to anyone, or with the lord of the seventh; or if the Sun and Moon are in their own houses; or if they are in the houses of the lord of the ascendant and aspect the ascendant or its lord; or if the lord of the ascendant is remote from the degree of the cusp of the ascendant, and another planet is with him in the same sign so that it is closer to the degree of the ascendant: this signifies that the thief or he who has the lost thing is from the members of the household. But if it is not from both luminaries as I told you, but only from one of them, he will not be from the members of the household but will be a domestic servant and born in that house in which the thing was lost or stolen. And if the Sun and Moon are in their triplicities <note>original: "triplicitatibus"; groups of three signs associated with the four elements (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note>, the thief will be from those who belong to the lord of the thing by kinship but does not live in the house with him. But if the luminaries are in their terms or faces <note>original: "terminis vel faciebus"; "Terms" and "Faces" (or decans) are essential dignities, specific small subdivisions of a zodiac sign that grant a planet strength.</note>, the thief will not be from the inhabitants of the house, but is a familiar to the inhabitants of the house—and more familiar to others than to the lord of the house, yet he is known to him; and he associates with them frequently so that it is believed he is a kinsman of the household. But if the luminaries aspect the ascendant and do not aspect the seventh house, the thief had not entered that house at any time before, but then entered for the first time when the sought property was stolen. But if any of the luminaries were in a common sign <note>original: "signo communi"; also known as mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which suggest change or double nature.</note>, it signifies that the thief had already entered that house another time.

...but not for the purpose of stealing: and those of the house knew when that thief entered at that time. If, however, the <term>significator</term> <note>The planet representing the person or object in question.</note> of the thief, which is the lord of the seventh house from the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The "ascendant" or first house represents the victim; the seventh house, being opposite, represents the thief.</note>, is in the third house from the first (which is the ninth house from the seventh), it signifies that the thief is not from that land, but from another land far from there. But if the significator of the robber is in the twelfth house from the ascendant (which is the sixth house from his own house), the robber will be his own servant. And if he is in the ninth house from the seventh (which is the third from the ascendant), the robber was a religious person <note>Likely a monk or cleric.</note>. And if he is in the fourth house from the ascendant (which is the tenth from the seventh), he was someone holding royal offices. And if he is in the eleventh house (which is the fifth from the seventh), he was from the inner circle of the king, or a person of power, or another such magnate—namely, those who are close to the kingdom. And if he is in any of his own houses <note>A zodiac sign that the planet rules.</note>, he will be a man who used to have his own means, but now is in need and is ashamed to labor for profit. And if he is in his <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet’s influence is most powerful and noble.</note>, it signifies that the robber is a noble; but because of poverty, he is compelled to steal because he blushes to beg or to work in another way to acquire what he needs. And if he is in any of the lesser dignities—namely, the <term>term</term>, <term>triplicity</term>, or <term>face</term> <note>These are technical subdivisions of the zodiac signs that indicate a person of lower social status or someone less well-known.</note>—he will not be very well known in that city, but he will be known in the region where he lives or in the neighborhood. 

¶ After you know whether he is of the family of the seeker or of the inhabitants of his house, <term>Zahel</term> <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were widely used in the Middle Ages.</note> says that if the **Sun** is the significator of the robber, it will be the father of the seeker. If, however, the **Moon** is the significator, it will be the mother of the seeker. And if it is **Venus**, it will be his wife. And if it is **Saturn**, it will be his grandfather or a stranger. And if it is **Jupiter**, he will be more noble than everyone else in the house, and someone of whom no suspicion was held. And if it is **Mars**, it will be his son or daughter or his brother. And if it is **Mercury**, he will be from among his close friends. 

¶ Then Zahel said that if the significator of the robber is a "pilgrim" <note>A planet in a sign where it has no particular strength or dignity.</note>, you should look at the **Part of Fortune**; if it is free from "evils" <note>Unfavorable planetary alignments with Mars or Saturn.</note>, that thief has stolen nothing before this time. Similarly, if the lord of the ascendant is free from evils. And if **Mars** is separated from the lord of the seventh house, he has not been involved in a theft from them before this. Then he says that if **Saturn** aspects the Moon or the ascendant, that thief has stolen with cunning and ingenuity. And if **Jupiter** is the significator of the robber, he did not enter to steal, but entered for the sake of some other business, and the theft happened to him, and so he stole. And he said if **Mars** is the significator of the robber, he does not commit the theft until he has pierced the house, or dug through the wall of the house in which the wealth was kept, or broken the locks or doors, or found a key. And if **Venus** is the significator, it signifies friendship and security, and also his boldness among them while he entered in this manner, taking on the image and likeness of a visiting friend, and thus he stole from them. And if **Mercury** is the significator, the thief entered the house with ingenuity and cunning or some art. And he said that if the **Sun** and **Moon** aspect the ascendant, the thief will be from the inhabitants of the house. And if the significator of the thief is a "fortune" <note>A lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>, he will be a free man; and if it is an "evil" <note>A planet like Mars or Saturn.</note>, he will be a servant. 

### ¶ On the age of the thief. 

And he said if **Venus** is the significatrix of the thief, it will be a young man or a girl, and **Mercury** is of a younger age than Venus. And if **Mars** is the significator of the robber, he will be a young man who has reached the peak of youth—more so than Saturn, that is, younger. **Jupiter**, however, is older than Mars. And if it is **Saturn**, he will be a decrepit old man. If, however, he is <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the Sun.</note>, he will be of a mature age. And if the **Moon** is the significatrix and she is at the beginning of the month, he will be young. And if she is in the middle of the month, he will be of middle age—that is, a full-grown man. And if she is at the end of the month, he will be an old man. If, however, the **Sun** is the significator and is between the ascendant and the <term>midheaven</term> <note>The highest point in the sky.</note>, the thief will be of a youthful age; and so you shall not cease to increase the age until you reach the

<column-break/>

angle of the earth <note>The fourth house, representing the lowest point of the chart and the end of life.</note>: for this place is the end of life.

### ¶ Chapter Fifteen: On the location of the theft.

**A**nd if you are asked, or you wish to know for yourself in what place the stolen property is deposited or hidden, consider then the **fourth house**, which signifies all hidden things, and see what sign the fourth house is in. Because if it is **Aries**, **Leo**, or **Sagittarius**, the theft will be hidden in a stable or in a high place where animals stay. If it is Aries, it will be in a place of small domestic animals that are eaten, such as sheep, pigs, and the like. If it is Leo, in a place of biting domestic animals that are not eaten, such as dogs; or of wild animals staying as if domestic, such as wolves, lions, and the like. If it is Sagittarius, it will be in a place of animals that people ride, such as in a horse stable. 

¶ And if it is **Taurus**, **Virgo**, or **Capricorn**, it will be in a horse stable or in another place where large animals stay that are eaten and slaughtered, such as oxen and the like. And if it is Virgo or Capricorn, it will be in a place where horses, donkeys, mules, or camels stay, and the like, which are not slaughtered or not eaten. And Virgo can also signify granaries, especially those that are underground, like pits; or near the ground, such as vats, chests, and the like in which grain is stored. And similarly, Capricorn signifies a place for goats or sheep together, and the like. 

¶ And if it is **Gemini**, **Libra**, or **Aquarius**, it will be in a house. If it is Gemini, it will be in a wall or the partition of a house. And if the place of the fourth house is Libra, the stolen thing will be near the roof of the house. And if it is Aquarius, it will be next to the door or above the door of the house or the gate, in higher places. 

¶ And if it is **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, or **Pisces**, the place of the theft will be near water. If it is Cancer, it will be near a well or a pond or cisterns. If it is Scorpio, it will be near a place where foul water stays or is thrown out. If it is Pisces, it will be a place that remains almost always soaked. 

¶ Furthermore, Zahel said that if you find the theft is in a house and you wish to know the specific location, look at the house; look at the lord of the fourth house and the planet that is there. If it is **Saturn**, it will be in the latrine of the houses, in a dirtier and deeper place. And if it is **Jupiter**, it signifies a place of woods or gardens. And **Mars** signifies the kitchen and the place of fire. And the **Sun** signifies the main hall of the house and the place where the master of the house sits. **Venus**, however, signifies the place where the woman sits. And **Mercury** the place of a decorated building and of books; or a place of grain, and especially so in Virgo. And if it is the **Moon**, it will be inside a well or cistern or a washroom. And Zahel said that when "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets.</note> are in the fourth house from the ascendant, the theft will be in a clean and beautiful place, and it has already been entrusted to someone noble. And if "evils" <note>Malefic planets.</note> are there, it will be in a horrific and stinking place, and it has already been entrusted to someone ignoble.

### ¶ On the number of stolen things, whether they are one or many.

**A**nd if you wish to know whether that thing which was stolen is one or many: Zahel said that you must look at the signs that are between the **Moon** and **Mercury**, whether they are even or odd. For if they are even, that theft is a thing made of several things which are joined together, or they are more than one thing. If, however, there are odd signs between them, it will be one thing.

**A**nd if it should happen sometimes, as occurs when a man is accused of being a thief, or is captured or otherwise detained on the occasion that someone says he is a thief, and you wish to know whether he is to be blamed or not: if he is to you...

Even if she is in an angle but is "impeded" <note>Afflicted by a bad aspect from a malic planet.</note>, it signifies the falsehood of what is charged against him.

And if you wish to know whether he has stolen anything besides that instance of which he is accused: see which of the <term>significators</term> is stronger—namely the lord of the ascendant or the Moon. For in such a case, the first house is given to the suspect; see which of them is stronger and observe if it is separated from any malic planet. And if it was not separated from a malic, but was separated from the lord of the <term>second house</term> (which is the house of substance/possessions), whether that lord be a fortune or a malic, it signifies that he has already stolen something on another occasion. If the lord of the second was a fortune, he did not persist in thievery; but if it was a malic, he did persist in thievery. 

If, however, it was separated from the fortunes, whether it is joined to fortunes or not, he has never stolen anything until now—unless that fortune is the lord of the second house from the ascendant, for then it signifies that he has already stolen something at some time; and even more strongly if the lord of the ascendant, after separation from the lord of the second, is joined to some malic.

### Chapter Seventeen: What kind of things were stolen.

**I**f you wish to know what kind of things were stolen: observe the ascendant and the Moon, and see where she is—namely, in what sign and in what degree of that sign—and see in the <term>term</term> <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note> of which planet that degree falls. 

If it is in the term of Saturn, and he is in the ascendant or in the tenth house in an earthy sign, the object will be among those pertaining to the preparation of the earth, which are made of iron, such as plowshares, hoes, movers, two-pronged mattocks, and the like. If Saturn is in the seventh or fourth house, they will be other iron tools with which they perform heavy works, such as the cutting of stones and the like; or it will be an iron club, or any of the aforementioned items weighted with lead; or it will be lead itself, or copper, and the like. Similarly, if he is falling from the ascendant and from the other angles. And if the Sun or Moon aspects him, then they will be

But if Saturn is in Gemini, the object will be of various materials and kinds; yet it will not seem to be a precious thing unless another planet aspects Saturn. For if Jupiter aspects him from the first or tenth house, it signifies that a part of those stolen things is gold, while others are cheap things. And if Jupiter is in the seventh or fourth house and aspects Saturn, a part of the stolen things will be silver, and others will be cheap things of little value. 

If, however, the degree in which the Moon is found is in the term of Jupiter, one must then see how and in what way he aspects her. If any of them aspect her from the seventh or fourth house, it will be silver or an object made of silver. 

But if Venus aspects Jupiter by any aspect, and Jupiter is in her term, they will be very precious things such as pearls and other precious stones. If, however, Jupiter is in Taurus or another earthy sign, it signifies that the stolen thing is a costly and noble garment. If he is in Gemini or another airy sign, the object will be an animal, such as a horse, mule, ox, and the like. And if Jupiter is in Cancer or some watery sign, it will be a thing taken from the water, like a pearl and the like. 

And <term>Zael</term> <note>original: "çabel"; referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and physician whose works were standard textbooks in the Middle Ages.</note> said that if the Moon is in the term of Mars, the thing itself has passed through fire or has touched fire in some way. If the Moon aspects Venus, it has already been worked with dye. If the Moon is in the term of Venus in Aries or its <term>triplicity</term> <note>The group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, it will be gold or silver. If it is in Taurus and its triplicity, or in Cancer and its triplicity, it will be a garment adorned with gold, or *albonasij*, which is a kind of precious silk garment woven with various colors and different patterns. 

And he said that you shall know the goodness and beauty of the thing from the placement of Venus in the signs. If she is in Gemini and its triplicity, the thing will not be of animal substance. And he said that if Venus has emerged from under the Sun's rays, the thing will be new. If she is retrograde, or at the end of her course, or diminished in number, it will be an old and already worn thing.

Similarly, say in what sign the Moon is; if she is in Aries, it signifies that the stolen thing is among those things worn on the head; for if they are weapons, they will be helmets of steel or painted leather. If Mercury does not aspect her, they will be items of decorated leather in which figures are similarly painted. There is a consideration among some modern practitioners regarding what kind of things are lost or stolen, for each of them is not sought from a single house, but from different ones according to the variety of the things. For there were some, as he says, who wanted to show that every stolen thing should be sought from the <term>tenth house</term> <note>In astrology, different 'houses' or segments of the sky represent different areas of life (money, family, etc.).</note>; but it is not so: for the thing is sought according to what it signifies by the houses. 

He said that if the thing was stolen from someone's household goods, it is sought from the second house. And if it was his brother or sister or another of his kinsmen, it is sought from the third. And if it was the father or grandfather or father-in-law, it is sought from the fourth. And if it was a son or another delightful thing, such as women's sashes or belts or something similar, it is sought from the fifth. And if it was weapons or mail or similar things, or some small animal, it is sought from the sixth. And if it was a wife or a mistress, it is sought from the seventh. And if it was a dowry or dowry-substance or a deposited item, it is sought from the eighth. And if it was a cleric or a religious person, it is sought from the ninth. And if it was the king's tax or that of some community, it is sought from the eleventh. And if it was a large animal or someone imprisoned, it is sought from the twelfth. If, however, they were coins or books or grain or oil or similar things, they are sought from the tenth; and this is done specifically from the aforementioned houses and their lords. Likewise, however, any thing, if it is from the goods of the <term>querent</term> <note>The person asking the question.</note>, can be sought from the second house and its lord.

### Chapter Eighteen: The Figure of the Thief.

**A**lbumasar <note>A famous 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to European astrology.</note> made a long discussion of this which was said above regarding the quality of stolen things; but I do not place much weight on it: that which was said above through the chapter is enough; and I have added what seemed to me ought to be added, so that it might sufficiently serve you, since there is not such great utility in it: but rather a certain reputation so that one may be seen to know something.

<column-break/>

Therefore, to avoid excessive wordiness, it seemed better to me to speak of what can be said regarding the form of the thief and his quality: and that is that you should look at the seventh house, which has the significance of the thief; and see which planet's <term>face</term> <note>original: "facies"; also known as a decan, a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign.</note> is the degree of the seventh house, for through it one can know the form or quality of the thief. 

Since if it is the sign of the thief: the first face of Aries signifies that the thief is a man of brown color and well-dressed when he stole, in garments belonging rather to a white color than to another. And if it is the third face of it, it signifies that the thief has a pale color and has red or nearly red hair.

And if it is the first face of Gemini, it signifies that the thief was accustomed to carry a rod or staff in his hand and had a young attendant with him. And if it is the second face of Gemini, it signifies that the thief knows how to play the pipe and use musical instruments, and had one with him who is a hunchback. And if it is the third face of it, it signifies that it was one man and one woman who stole.

And if it is the third face of it, it signifies that the thief is a man who often carries a small rod in his hand and has an ugly face and always seems almost sad. 

And if it is the first face of Virgo, it signifies that the thief who stole is a certain girl who seems to be good, of whom no one suspects anything evil. And if it is the second face of Scorpio, it signifies that there were one man and one woman, needy and poorly dressed. And if it is the third face of it, it signifies that the thief is one who walks bent over his knees, nor does he stand well upon them.
