### Chapter 19. On entering into partnership between people and their participation.

**I**f anyone, wishing to enter into a partnership with another, asks you whether it will be useful for him or not, and raises a question to you about this, and you wish to satisfy him therein: at the hour of the question, you shall give the <term>first house</term> <note>The first house represents the "querent," the person asking the question.</note> to him who asks or desires the partnership; make the Moon also a participant of both parties. From the <term>tenth house</term> <note>The tenth house traditionally signifies the success, profit, or "action" of a venture.</note>, however, he will be able to know what will come to him from that partnership which he intends to contract. To what end the partnership will arrive, you shall know from the fourth house and from the planet to which the Moon is then joined; although the Moon is more on the side of the asker than on the side of the one asked about, nevertheless the planet to which she then joins signifies for both, but less for the asker than for that person with whom he intends to enter the partnership; the planet, however, from which she then separates or is separated, acts for the asker more than it acts for the one asked about. And consider then the hour—that is, of the question—if the lord of the first, who is the significator of the asker, and the Moon should be in Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn without perfect <term>reception</term> <note>Reception is a favorable astrological condition where planets are in signs that they "rule" or "exalt," indicating mutual support.</note> from the house—that is, or from exaltation, or from two minor dignities together—it signifies that the partnership will be difficult and troubled, and afterwards it will be rectified and the partnership will last; but it will not be in truly good stability, nor will it be very useful or very profitable. If, however, they should be in Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, that partnership will be durable and constant; yet it will not be very profitable, and when they buy something they will not sell it quickly; rather, it will stay with them longer than is the proper custom. If, however, they should be in Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces, it signifies that the partnership will be useful, good, and profitable, and that he will frequently repeat his buying and his selling, and that he will sell his merchandise expeditiously and quickly; and there will be security and legality between them, and good spirit and good faith, nor will there be fraud between them. And if one [planet] is here and the other there—that is, of the first house or the Moon in a <term>movable sign</term> <note>Also known as "Cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), indicating change.</note> and the other in a fixed or common sign, or vice-versa, those things which I told you above will be, not entirely, but to a lesser degree. And if the "evil significators" [malefics] aspect—namely, the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the seventh—their partnership will be bad, and each will act with falsehood against the other and with deception, and one will not behave well toward the other. Therefore, look where the evil hindering significators are—namely, the lord of the first and the lord of the seventh—because for that reason discord will come between those partners, which is signified by that house in which the evil hindrances are located. What is signified through each house has already been repeated to you enough so that you can know it well. And see if any of the malefics are in the first, whether they hinder the lord of the first or the seventh or not: it signifies that the discord, fraud, deception, injury, and malice come from the side of the asker. If, however, there is any of the malefics in the seventh, then it signifies that it will come from the side of him with whom the asker intends to contract the partnership, or with whom he has contracted it, if the partnership has already been made; and the question was perhaps made as to what would become of the partnership already contracted. ¶ Furthermore, look similarly if the Moon is separated from one <term>fortune</term> <note>A "fortune" or "benefic" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus, indicating good luck.</note> and joined to another: they will begin the partnership well and will finish it similarly with affection, whether they profit or do not profit. If, however, she has been separated from a good planet and joined to an evil one, they will begin well and willingly, but they will finish it badly and with strife and discord, unless that evil planet is well-disposed and receives the Moon with perfect reception as I told you above. If, however, she was separated from some evil planet and joined to a good one, they will begin it poorly and unwillingly, but well...

### Chapter 20. When someone goes to find someone, whether he finds him or not.

If someone is about to set out to find someone and asks you whether he will find them or not: if you wish to look into such a question, see what kind of person it is whom he intends to visit—whether it be a king, a prelate, another religious figure, or some other individual person.

If it is a **king**, see if the Lord of the **tenth house** is in the tenth, or the first, or the seventh, or the fourth; for this signifies that the king is in the place where the seeker intends to find him. If the Lord of the tenth house is in the **third house** and the journey is one day's travel (which is called a short journey), or if he is in the **ninth house** and the journey is many days (which is called a long journey), it signifies that he will find him on the road, provided that the Lord of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The first house, representing the person asking the question.</note> and the Lord of the tenth house are joined together. If, however, he is in the eleventh, second, fifth, or eighth, it signifies that he is not in the place the seeker intends, but he will not be so remote from that place that he cannot find him with some searching. If the Lord of the tenth house is in the **sixth** or **twelfth**, he will not find him, nor in the third or ninth without a <term>conjunction</term> or <term>aspect</term>.

If the person asked about is a **cleric** and is in the aforementioned places, he will find him just as was said of the king. If, however, it is another **lay individual**, look then to the **Lord of the seventh house**; if he is in the seventh, tenth, first, or fourth, he will find him in the place he believes, unless that planet is joined to a planet "falling from an angle," for then he will not find him immediately without first searching. If the Lord of the seventh is in the eighth, eleventh, second, or fifth, he will not find him in that place, but nearby, not very far from the estimated spot. If he is in the ninth, twelfth, third, or sixth, he will not find him in the place he believes, nor nearby, especially if the Lord of the seventh is in the sixth or twelfth. If, however, he is in the third or ninth, and the Lord of the seventh and the Lord of the third (or ninth) are joined together by body or aspect, it signifies he will find or encounter him on the road.

### Chapter 21. Concerning someone wanting to go into an army, or to war, or to start a conflict, whether a leader or anyone else, and whether they win or not.

<column-break/>

**W**hen there is a war between some parties, or it is expected that there will be one (as often happens), and one of them comes to you and wants to be certain of what might happen to him—whether he is a king, emperor, marquis, duke, count, or magistrate, or any other person, lay or clerical, who acts in a lay capacity and must lead an army (whether he be noble, common, or a rustic)—as long as he is the leader of the army or of one side of a war, he is called the **leader** of that army or war, whether he is acting for himself or appointed by another. And if he wishes to begin a war against someone or go into an army against another, and he asks you a question about these things (or someone else asks for him who is very concerned for his welfare):

If the person for whom the query is made is **not** an emperor or king, you shall give him the **Ascendant** and its Lord; see from which planet the Moon is separating, and give that also to the seeker. And give the **seventh house**, its Lord, and the planet to which the Moon is then joining to the **adversary**. 

If, however, he is an **emperor**, magistrate, or ruler, and asks about the affairs of the empire, kingdom, or city he rules, you shall give him the **tenth house** and give his enemy the **fourth house**. If he asks about his own private and personal affairs (not involving the state or city), give him the **first house** and the enemy the **seventh**, and judge for him as you would for any other individual person. If the Moon has not separated from anyone nor joined anyone, the question says that the Moon should not be used in that undertaking.

Furthermore: if the Lord of the first is joined to the Lord of the seventh (or vice versa) by a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note> with perfect <term>reception</term>—that is, one of them receives the other—it signifies that **peace** will be made between them before the battle. If, however, they are joined by a **square** aspect <note>A harsh 90-degree angle.</note> or **opposition** (even with reception), or by a trine or sextile without reception, they will not be reconciled unless they first fight or clash together. But after they have clashed or fought, they will settle between themselves, and the beginning of peace or settlement will come from the side whose significator is "lighter" <note>The planet that moves faster through the zodiac, such as the Moon or Mercury.</note>.

And you should know that the **Superior planets**—namely Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—are stronger in battles and wars than the **Inferior planets**—namely the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon—and are more stable and constant because of the slowness of their motions. This is because the Inferior planets apply themselves to the Superiors, not the Superiors to the Inferiors. Therefore, if you can, always act in your beginnings of battles or wars so that you have one of the Superior planets as your significator, as I have said elsewhere. However, if you cannot have a Superior, take one of the Inferiors as best you can; for it is better for you to have a "blessed" Inferior than an unfortunate or hindered Superior.

Afterward, consider (since you see they will be reconciled) if both significators—the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the seventh—are **direct** <note>Moving forward normally through the zodiac.</note>; the peace or concord they make together will be good and firm, especially if the aspect is a trine or sextile. If, however, both are **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward, which usually suggests delays, deception, or weakness.</note>, the peace will be fake and will not be good or lasting; rather, it will be with evil intent and craftiness, and each will strive to deceive the other. If one is direct and the other retrograde, the one whose significator is retrograde will strive to deceive the other and will proceed with evil intent and craftiness against the other. And see what house the deceiver is in relative to the one he tries to trick: for if he is in the second house from the first after they have made peace, and the other trusts him, he will take away his wealth. If he is in the third, he will first deceive him on account of a brother; for he will take his brother from him and hold him to extort something, or perhaps plot with the brother and cause him harm, or send him out of that region to his detriment. But whenever the conjunction between him and the falling planet is completed degree by degree, he is immediately weakened, and it is feared afterward that the questioner will succumb, even if at the beginning things went well for him; and the enemy will be strengthened, even if things went poorly for him at the beginning. 

You shall judge the same for the Lord of the Seventh as you judged for the Lord of the First: namely, if you find the Lord of the Seventh strong in an angle, even if he is joined to a planet falling from an angle (which signifies his impediment), he will nevertheless be strong then. If indeed they are **unfortunate** and weak, they will signify the contrary, for he will succumb on whose side they are located.

### Chapter twenty-four: what was the cause for which that war arose, whether just or unjust.

->If anyone should ask at any time, as is often<-

If he separates from the **fortunes**, or the fortunes separate from him, and he is joined to a **malefic**, or a malefic is joined to him, it signifies that the inquirer or the beginner moved himself for a just cause to begin that war, and that he uses justice and truth, and the adversary the opposites of these. And if Mars was separated from fortunes and joined to fortunes, it signifies that each side fosters a just cause, which rarely happens. If indeed he was separated from malefics and joined to malefics, it signifies that each side strives against justice and against truth.

### Chapter 25: Concerning the great or small size of armies.

If by chance any of the leaders of an army should doubt the army of his adversary, and should want to know from you whether it is large or small: and if you wish to look into this for him, look then to the position of the Moon by signs and degrees, and likewise Mercury; and subtract the Moon’s position from the position of Mercury; and see how many signs remain for you. If they are even, the army will be large; and the more signs that remain after that subtraction, the larger the army will be. And if they are odd, the army will be small; and the fewer they are, the smaller the army will be. If, however, the position of Mercury is not so great that you can subtract the position of the Moon from it, add twelve signs to it and afterward subtract the position of the Moon and do as has been said. And also see if on the western side—which is from the **angle of the earth** <note>the Imum Coeli or 4th house cusp</note> to the **tenth** [house]—there should be a greater quantity of planets than on the eastern side—which is from the angle of the tenth to the **fourth** on the eastern side—it signifies a greater quantity of people on the side of the adversary. If, however, there should be a greater quantity of them on the eastern side than on the western side, it signifies a decrease in the quantity of people on the side of the adversary; this, by the aforesaid reasoning, signifies his army to be large and on the side of the seeker.

### Chapter Twenty-Six: To know all the instruments and other things that pertain to war.

To know all the instruments that pertain to war, **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century astrologer</note> said that the **Ascendant** <note>the 1st house</note> signifies the one beginning the war and its cause; and that it is what stirred up the war; and whether he began it with force or by a lie. The first house signifies the one beginning the war, because the first thing that comes into a war is the beginner. The **second house** from the Ascendant signifies whether there is a war or not, and whether it is for profit or for loss; for that which comes into war after the beginners is the actual effect of fighting. And he said that the **third house** from the first signifies the weapons and with what 

<column-break/>

kinds of weapons there will be victory or success; and what types of weapons will not be necessary in the war itself; for the third thing that comes into war is weapons, because without them one could not fight in a good way. And the **fourth house** from the first signifies the place in which the war will be: whether it will be a field or mountainous; and whether it is on the seashore or next to a river; or if there are fruit trees or a grove; for the place is a thing so suited to war that without it, war could not happen. And the **fifth house** signifies the integrity, the advance, the audacity, and the laziness of the warriors; for integrity is a thing without which warriors would not fight well. And he said that the **sixth house** signifies the animals of the soldiers, what they might be—namely, whether horses, donkeys, mules, or camels—for the thing that is most useful to soldier-warriors are horses or other animals that carry them. And he said that the **seventh house** signifies the instruments with which they throw stones <note>catapults or siege engines</note>; and whether the war is with cunning or not; for it is a thing very useful to war, and he places it among other instruments or the aforementioned weapons. And he said that the **eighth house** signifies wounds, captures, and death, as well as the breaking of the conquered in flight; for these are the very acts of fighting into which wars are accustomed finally to come. And he said that the **ninth house** signifies the work of scouts and knowledge of the enemy’s affairs, and his rumors and cunnings; for this is a thing which a leader of war ought much to provide for—namely, so that he may know the enemy’s deeds and news that are with him, and how he himself is concerned about the facts of the war, and how he himself is cunning or ingenious. And he said that the **tenth house** signifies the custom or acts of the high commander and of the other commanders who are under his command; for you or someone else must see whether the King or leader is attentive and providing for those things that pertain to war or not, and whether he is cautious or astute in those things that belong to him. And he said that the **eleventh house** signifies their battle lines and their arrangement, how they advance upon the enemy; for this is a thing very much to be observed: so that he knows how to arrange his lines and his warriors and to instruct them how they should behave in the matter of war; and from this alone many have conquered their enemies. And he said that the **twelfth house** signifies the city and those who are besieged and attacked in it; for this is a thing which a fighting man must know, and from which he will be able to consider what he has to do and how he can prevail against his enemy.

### Chapter Twenty-Seven: How you ought to look at the significations of the twelve houses.

Although many things have been said above in this same chapter concerning those things that pertain to the fact of wars or contentions, yet I will still tell you certain useful things which do not seem to me should be omitted; nor should you believe that I wish to fail in the opinions stated above; because if you have looked well into what has been said, and understood them well, you will find nothing discordant. When, therefore, you have looked well—as has been said—at all the houses and you wish to know the signification of each of them: look for the one questioning or the one beginning [the war] at all the houses in the order written below, starting from the first. For the enemy, however, look from the **seventh house**, and make it the enemy's first; and make the eighth his second; and make the ninth his third; and the tenth his fourth; and the eleventh his fifth; the twelfth his sixth; the first his seventh; the second his eighth; the third his ninth; the fourth his tenth; the fifth his eleventh; the sixth his twelfth. Then look if there should be a **malefic** <note>a planet like Mars or Saturn</note> in the first house, or if it aspects it from a fourth aspect <note>a square</note> or from opposition; it signifies that the leader will not perform well and what must be done for the fact of war will not be done, nor will he be well concerned about those things; and this could be the cause why it does not turn out well for him in the war; unless that malefic is the lord of the Ascendant or at least of its exaltation <note>a sign where a planet's influence is strengthened</note>; and it also signifies that he does not have the right [on his side]; but rather...

And if the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>the South Node, considered diminishing and negative</note> is there, there will be many other vile animals for the fighting that are not well-trained. 

If, however, a **Fortune** is in the **seventh house** <note>the house of the enemy and siege engines</note> or its aforementioned aspects, it signifies that the instruments with which they throw stones <note>catapults or trebuchets</note> will be useful and well-performing the task for which they were assigned, and it signifies the goodness of the enemy. If, however, a **Fortune** or its aspect is in the **ninth house** <note>the house of long journeys and rumors</note>, it signifies that the enemy is well-disposed and that they have hope in certain rumors which they hold, and that those rumors are useful to them; and that they are a cunning person who strives to deceive the querent if they can. 

If a **Fortune** or its aforementioned aspects are in the **tenth house** <note>the house of authority and the leader</note>, it signifies that the querent, or he who is the superior or captain of his army, is wise and learned in such things as pertain to war, as are the others to whom any part of the war’s conduct is committed. If, however, a malefic is there, it signifies that the querent, or his lord, or the superior of his army, and the other leaders of the army to whom anything of the army’s deeds is committed, are all or for the most part men inept at carrying out such things.

If indeed a malefic or its aforementioned aspects are there, it signifies that they are poorly disposed and not fit for defense, and are not of one mind, and are timid and terrified. 

Do not forget one thing which I tell you now: because although I have not found it in the sayings of the philosophers, yet I have found through proven experience that whenever **Mars** is in the **twelfth house**, one must always fear **betrayal** <note>original: "proditione"</note>; and almost the same can be said of the **Tail of the Dragon**.

And if one is well-disposed and the other poorly, he whose significator was well-disposed shall prevail. ### Chapter Twenty-Eight: Whether there will be a battle between armies or not.

To know whether there will be a battle between armies or not: look then to the **first house** and its lord, and the **Moon**, and the **seventh house** and its lord; and see if they join bodily <note>in conjunction</note> in any of the **angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, since that signifies that there will be a battle between them. If, however, they are not joined bodily, see if they join by an **opposition** or **square aspect**; since that similarly signifies a future battle. 

And if none of these should be: look then if any planet **transfers light** <note>an astrological term where a faster planet moves from an aspect with one ruler to an aspect with the other, "linking" them</note> between them by opposition or square aspect; since that signifies a future battle if it is without **reception** <note>when one planet is in a sign where the other has dignity</note>. If, however, the heavier of them receives the one who transfers their light between them, it signifies that the battle will not be; and if there was one, they will be pacified either in the army itself or shortly after the army. 

And if it should be otherwise—namely, that the significators of the armies (the lord of the first and the lord of the seventh) are not joined anywhere, nor have they met each other, nor is there anyone who transfers light between them—as was said, it signifies that the battle will not be.

### ¶ Chapter twenty-one: Whether a city or castle, besieged or to be besieged, will be captured or not.

The ancient astrologers did not care much for 
this matter, which I wonder at, since it is a 
thing that very often passes through one's hands. 
But it could perhaps be that they did this 
because they considered the matter easy, 
and they assumed that anyone would 
know this, and for this reason they did 
not care to speak of it. I, however, shall 
join something here for you. **Zael** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr (c. 786–845 AD), a famous Persian Jewish astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology.</note> 
did say something about it, though I 
did not perceive his intention well. 
Therefore, if a question is put to you 
about some city or some castle, 
besieged or to be besieged, whether 
it is captured or not, and concerning 
that siege: look to the first house, 
which is for the querent, and the 
fourth, which has the significance 
of the city or besieged castle. 
And perhaps some of the moderns 
have said that the tenth house 
signifies the city; they were moved 
by this reason: that the fourth 
signifies the land of the querent, 
and by the same reason the tenth 
signifies the land of the enemy, not

<column-break/>

making a distinction between the land 
or the inheritance of estates and a 
city or castle. To me, however, it 
seemed that we ought to give the 
fourth house to the city or castle; 
because the fourth signifies the 
inheritance of the querent and his 
lands and houses, and the tenth

### Chapter 30. Whether someone has public or hidden enemies.

Fortunate things are more numerous than unfortunate ones, yet more unfortunate things seem to be seen; not because they are more in number, but because they are felt more acutely. Thus, there are some fortunate men, though no one knows why this is except perhaps the experts. Similarly, there are some unfortunate ones who do not know why this happens to them; for they serve others indifferently—though perhaps more to one than another—and harm no one, yet some (and sometimes many) are hostile to them. They would not know how to assign a cause for why they hate them, except perhaps that they are moved by envy because they see them as good and not malicious. Therefore, those people sometimes think on these things and consult an astrologer, asking whether they have enemies and why these contrary things happen to them, or not. When anyone brings you a question about whether they have enemies or not, know that if he asks about someone by name, whether this person...

Understand the same regarding those signified by the house in which a planet is located that opposes the lord of the first or the Moon; and all these are moved by envy rather than any other cause.

# Chapter 31. On the hunting of land and water, of birds and wild beasts.

The modes of hunting are two: one is on land and through the land; the other is in water and through the water. Hunting that is done on land is of two types: for wild beasts or for birds. Furthermore, both for beasts and for birds, it is subdivided: for it is either in the mountains or on flat land. If a question is put to you regarding land hunting and it is for wild beasts, if the **ascendant** is an earthy sign <note>The Earth signs are Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.</note> and determines that hunt, look then to the ascendant and its lord; look also to the **lord of the hour** <note>In medieval astrology, each hour of the day is ruled by a specific planet.</note>, for the lord of the hour has much to do in hunting, both on land and water. Look also if it is among the quadrupedal signs <note>Signs representing four-legged animals: Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius (the latter half), and Capricorn.</note>, for the same operates as an earthy sign in the hunting of beasts. Look also if your hunting is in the mountains; if the ascendant is then any of the fiery signs <note>Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius.</note>, it will be good. If it is on flat land and the ascendant is earthy or quadrupedal, it similarly signifies good as far as this is concerned. In the hunting of birds, whether they be land birds, or birds of the air or marshes, the airy signs <note>Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.</note> are to be applied. Then look to the **seventh house**, which has the significance of the prey <note>original: "venationem"; here referring to the object of the hunt.</note>, and its lord. See where it is, and see if they aspect each other from a trine <note>A harmonious 120-degree aspect.</note> or a fertile aspect <note>original: "fertili aspectu"; likely referring to a sextile (60 degrees).</note>; this signifies the obtaining of the prey without great labor and without much searching. It is even better if the first two <note>The Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon.</note> receive the lord of the seventh; for then it signifies the capture with ease and pleasantness. If they are joined by opposition or a square aspect, it signifies that whatever is obtained from the hunt will be acquired with much labor and great fatigue, and often after despair. But if they are not joined by any aspect nor by body <note>A physical conjunction.</note>, and there is someone who "transfers the light" <note>Translation of light: when a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, connecting their energies.</note> or the power of one—namely, from the lord of the seventh to the lord of the first—and the lord of the first does not then commit that disposition to another, it also signifies the obtaining of the hunt, although not much, but a modest amount. If, however, the lord of the first commits the disposition to another, or transfers some of his disposition to the lord of the seventh, it signifies that he will be on the verge of capturing the prey, yet he will not capture it; he will, however, take joy from those things which he sees of the hunt, such as the chase and similar things. If they are not joined together by conjunction or by aspect or through the translation of light, it signifies that

<column-break/>

nothing will be obtained from the hunt. If, however, you find that he is to obtain the prey, and the **seventh sign** is **Aries**, **Taurus**, the latter part of **Sagittarius**, or **Capricorn**, and the question was in the **hour of Jupiter**, and the lord of the hour was in the first or tenth house, he will obtain prey from the wild quadrupeds that run swiftly, such as stags, roe deer, hares, and the like. If, however, it is **Leo**, the hunt will be among wild quadrupeds that can injure, such as bears, wolves, foxes, wild boars, and the like. If the seventh house is among the "bad houses" <note>The 6th, 8th, or 12th houses.</note> and yet signifies the obtaining of the prey, look to see if the **fortunes** <note>The "Benefics": Jupiter and Venus.</note> are in it or aspect it, which signifies the capture with the safety of the hunter. But if the fortunes are not in it nor aspect it, it signifies great fatigue in that hunt and in its finding, and he will obtain little from it; and there is fear for that hunter lest some misfortune happen to him because of the hunt or from the prey itself to his person. And if **Saturn** is lord of the seventh or has another dignity there, and the question signifies obtaining the prey, or at the beginning of the journey to the hunt: he will obtain not much from the hunt, but there is fear lest someone in the hunt injure him, perhaps believing they are striking a beast, or in some other way. However, the matter will not be of very great injury; but if he should strike himself, it could be more serious. For that shedding of blood pertains to **Mars**, which is why it hinders less, because all blood shed in hunting pertains naturally to Mars; and therefore his malice is mitigated in this and he injures less. But if **Jupiter**, who is naturally the solver of all malices, then aspects Mars, the hunter will not be hindered, especially if Jupiter is the lord of the hour; or if the ascendant is **Sagittarius** or **Pisces**, he will hunt with the safety of his body and will obtain much prey, easily, with little labor and small fatigue, and swiftly. If the seventh sign is earthy or airy, and there is a fortune in it, even if the lord of the seventh is a fortune and the lord of the hour is likewise a fortune, he will still be safe and not injured in that hunt; he will entirely obtain from the hunt what he intends and expects. However, the wild beasts and birds he intends to hunt may sense him and his dogs or leopards <note>Hunting leopards (cheetahs) were used by medieval nobility for coursing.</note> or other animals with which he hunts from afar, and they will flee terrified by him so that he does not catch them; and he will seek with a strong and laborious search, yet no utility will follow from it—unless Jupiter, the breaker of malice, or **Mercury** is with the lord of the seventh or with that "malic" <note>Malefic planet.</note> who is lord of the hour. This does not prevent the hunter from being able to hunt well; for Mercury then takes the place of Mars in the cause of hunting in such a case.

# Chapter 32. On the multitude or paucity of the hunt.

If you wish to know the quantity of the hunt, whether the hunter may obtain much or little, look first to the hour of the interrogation or the setting out for the hunt. See the **tenth sign** of that figure <note>The 10th house or Midheaven.</note>; if it is **Aries** or **Scorpio**, or if you find **Mars** in it, and **Jupiter** or **Mercury** aspects him, and the ascendant is any of the houses of those two <note>The houses of Jupiter (Sagittarius/Pisces) or Mercury (Gemini/Virgo).</note>, and Mars is in the tenth. And if the ascendant is not one of their houses, but one of the two is the lord of the hour and aspects Mars with this, it signifies the obtaining of much prey, and he will find it in such great quantity that not only with instruments, but even with his own hands and without great labor, he will obtain it; unless **Saturn** then aspects Mars. For if he aspects him without the aspect of Jupiter, and that aspect is a square, or from any of the angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note>, or if he is in the tenth, or if he is...

If **Capricorn** or **Aquarius** <note>original: "capricornus vel aquarius"</note> occupies the **tenth house** <note>The 10th house in a chart represents the success or "prize" of an undertaking.</note>, the hunter will perhaps obtain very little. This is because such a position diminishes the hunt and brings labor, sadness, and distress upon the endeavor. For if **Jupiter** does not then aspect **Mars**, and Mars itself is in one of the locations signifying hunting—especially in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in an astrological chart.</note>—the hunter or the master of the hunt should fear physical injury and the escape of the game from his sight. He will find travel difficult during that hunt; and if he does catch anything, it will be small and bring him no joy. Indeed, he may even lose the game after it has been caught, particularly if the hunting takes place on land, whether on the plains or in the mountains.

### Chapter 33. On hunting in the water.

If your intention, or the intention of the one going out to hunt, is to fish—which is a type of hunting dedicated to **Mars** and falls under his rule—you should apply the same understanding to every place of fishing, regardless of the water: whether it be a river, lake, marsh, or any other place, provided it is a place for fishing. All these types of hunting are subordinate to the astrology of Mars. Look to see if the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question.</note> is a water sign, of which **Pisces** is the most useful; **Cancer** follows, and **Scorpio** is considered less effective than Cancer. In this case, Mars is not helpful, as he hinders hunting in the water. Therefore, if the **Moon** is then joined with Mars, or if the lord of the hour is Mars, do not go; you will catch nothing unless **Venus** is then in conjunction with the Moon. In this situation, Venus breaks the malice of Mars. For when the Moon—which holds great power over hunting—is joined with Mars in a water-based hunt, it signifies very little profit in fishing, or effectively none at all; and what is caught will be obtained with great difficulty and hardship, alongside obstacles for the hunters themselves.

It is different with **Saturn**; for he does not hinder the Moon in water hunting, just as Mars does not hinder her in land hunting. Indeed, if the Moon is joined with Saturn during a hunt, it multiplies the catch, unless Mars aspects her. However, if the Moon is joined by any aspect while she is in **Libra**, **Capricorn**, or **Aquarius**, there is a fear that the hunter or fisherman might suffer a shipwreck or otherwise be drowned <note>original: "suffoceť"</note>. If she is specifically in Capricorn or Aquarius, there is a fear he might fall into the water, but he will not drown. But if she is in Libra, it signifies he will be soaked by rains or by trees and grass wet with dew. This happens because Mars and Saturn are the enemies of Venus <note>Libra is ruled by Venus; the presence of her "enemies" Mars or Saturn there creates these specific difficulties.</note>. In my treatise on **elections** <note>The branch of astrology used to choose the most auspicious time for an event.</note>, I shall tell you other things from the sayings of the ancients regarding the practice of hunting, whether by water, in the mountains, or on the plains.

### Chapter 34. Whether an exile, one expelled, or one banished shall return to his land or not.

Sometimes people are expelled from the houses or cities where they live, or they depart from them for other reasons. They may wish to know if they are destined to return to the home or the land where they used to dwell, and they consult an astrologer on this matter. It is necessary, therefore, for you to know the circumstances of the person asking you, for one can be away from home or land for many reasons: one might be an **expelled exile**, a **pilgrim**, a **fugitive**, one **banished**, an **absentee**, or one **deported**. If you are asked about any of these, see who is asking: is it the person himself, or someone else on his behalf? If it is someone else concerned for the person's welfare, see how they are related—whether it be a father, mother, brother, son, and so on. Assign the **first house** <note>The house representing the person asking the question (the querent).</note> to the one asking, and to the person being asked about, assign the house that 

<column-break/>

signifies them. Judge according to this: for if the lord of the house signifying the person being sought aspects the first house, or is located in the first house, or is joined to a planet that is in the first house, it signifies a return. This is also true if that planet is joined to another planet that does not aspect the first house, provided that second planet then joins a third planet that *does* aspect the first house and transmits its power and light to the first. This indicates his return. Apply this same logic to the Moon: if the question is about a brother, see if the lord of the **third house** aspects the first; if a father, the **fourth house**; if a son, the **fifth house**; and so on for the significations of all the houses.

If, however, the person asks for himself—that is, the traveler himself is the one asking—see whether he is absent by his own choice with the intent to return, as merchants often do, or those who go into government service or other administrations, or for the sake of profit or pleasure, or any other voluntary reason. Unless he is a pilgrim, the **eighth house** always represents the person asking; the **first house** is given to the land from which he departed. Even if he suspects something might happen to cause his expulsion, he is still called "absent" and not "expelled," even if something happens after his departure that makes him afraid to return. Thus, if the **lord of the eighth house** aspects the first house, or if the Moon does so from any aspect, it signifies his return. If the aspect is from an **angle** or a **trine** <note>A 120-degree aspect, considered very harmonious.</note>, his return will be swift. If it is from **succedent houses** <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses.</note> or a "fertile" aspect, his return will be somewhat delayed. If it is from **cadent houses** <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which are weaker.</note> or a **square aspect** <note>original: "quarto aspectu"; a 90-degree angle, suggesting tension.</note>, it will be much delayed. If it is from an **opposition**, it will be delayed even further and the return postponed.

For a **pilgrim**, the **twelfth house** is given because of the anger, sadness, and tribulations that happen to one on a pilgrimage; though some give him the **seventh house**. You may choose whichever seems more appropriate to signify the intent. If he is absent because he was violently expelled from the land, or fled, or is an exile, or left out of fear, or was banished or deported, or is a pilgrim—for a pilgrim is in a way compelled to go on his journey and cannot easily turn back—different rules apply. If the one asking was expelled, banished, or deported, or left out of fear of a ruler or an enemy, give the **seventh house** to his person (along with its lord and the Moon), and give the **first house** to the land from which he was expelled. If the lord of the seventh is in the first, or the Moon is there, it signifies his return. If neither is in the first, but one of them aspects the first, or is joined to the lord of the first who in turn aspects the first, it signifies his return. 

Even if the connection is made through a chain of planets, as was the view of **Messahala** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a famous Persian-Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note>, one planet relieves the other and returns its light to the first, completing the matter for the seeker. Though this may involve the intervention of several people, the matter can be accomplished through those signified by the houses of the intervening planets. If you find none of these conditions, it signifies he will not return. But if the person is absent and asks about his own property, give the first house to the person and the **fourth house** to his city or land and any of his immovable goods; for his other possessions, use the houses specifically assigned to them.

-># On the eighth house.<-

### Chapter 1: Concerning someone absent or who has set out elsewhere, whether they live or are dead.
**I**t is common for people to sometimes be absent from their home or land, and this happens for many and various reasons. For some absent themselves for the sake of a **pilgrimage**, others for **trade**, some for **pleasure**, some perhaps for the sake of some **governance**, others for the **exercise of arms**, and for many other reasons they distance themselves from their children or families, so that their kin have no news of them, nor is the truth known about them. If perhaps someone concerned for one of them wishes to know from you whether the one they are worried about is alive or not, and poses a question to you about him, and you wish to answer him: look then to who it is that asks, and see for whom they are asking—whether for a **father**, a **brother**, a **son**, a **servant**, a **wife**, a **husband**, a **religious person**, a **master**, a **friend**, or perhaps for someone who does not love the one who pretends to be their friend, and similar cases. You shall then give the **first house** <note>The Ascendant, representing the person asking the question.</note> to the seeker; but to the one being sought, you shall give the **house** which signifies him <note>For example, the 3rd house for a brother, the 4th for a father, the 10th for a master.</note> and the **Moon** likewise. See if you find that planet in the **fourth** or **eighth** house from its own house, or even from the house of the question; for then it signifies his death. Likewise, if it is in the **twelfth** from its own house with one of the **malefics** <note>original: "malorum" — referring to Saturn or Mars, planets traditionally associated with hardship.</note>, or if one of the malefics aspects it by a **fourth aspect** <term>square: an angle of 90 degrees, considered stressful</term> or by **opposition** <term>an angle of 180 degrees, indicating conflict</term>; and if the **Sun** is impeded or the **Moon** likewise, it signifies that he is dead. Nevertheless, **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician.</note> said that one must look to the lord of the **ascendant** and the **Moon**: if they are in the **fourth** from the ascendant, or in the **house of death** (which is the **eighth** from the ascendant), or if they are **combust** <note>original: "combusti" — when a planet is so close to the Sun that its light and power are hidden</note>, or in their **detriment** <note>original: "descensione" — a sign where the planet's power is weakened</note>, or with the lord of the house of death, it signifies death. And he said that if you do not find any of them disposed as has been said, look to the aspect of the **malefics** and the **fortunes** <note>original: "fortunae" — refers to "benefic" planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note> toward them. If the lord of the ascendant is **retrograde** in the fourth, or retrograde in the house of death, or separated from the lord of the house of death through retrogradation, look to see if it returns to the degree of combustion: he will be dead. Likewise, he said if the **Moon** joins a planet **under the earth** <note>The houses below the horizon in a chart (houses 1 through 6).</note>, he will be dead; if she joins a planet **above the earth**, he lives. Likewise, he said if you find the lord of the ascendant in the **twelfth** with malefics, or if the malefics aspect him, and either of the **luminaries** <note>The Sun or the Moon.</note> is impeded, you shall judge him dead. And he said if the malefics are also with the luminaries (which are the Sun and Moon) in one sign—that is, joined bodily without the aspect of the fortunes—it signifies death. And likewise, if the Moon is in the fourth with **Mars** and the fortunes do not aspect her, it signifies the same. And he said, know that what is **above the earth** signifies life, and what is **under the earth** signifies death. And he said when you find him **combust** under the rays and no fortune aspects him, and the Moon is under the earth, falling from the ascendant in the **third** or **sixth**, know that the one being asked about is dead—especially if it happens that he is in **Scorpio** and in the **third degree** of the same, impeded by **Saturn**, who naturally signifies death. You shall then verify the death of the one about whom the inquiry is made. I agree with this closely enough, except in the assignment of the houses; because he [Zahel] seems to want to give the **first house** to the absent person regardless of who is asking. To me, it seemed that the house which signifies the person's relationship should be given. However, it may have been a fault of the translator or the scribes; you, however, hold whichever way you wish, for when you have experimented once or many times, you will see which of these

<column-break/>

ways is more correct. For it is not my intention to disparage any worthy man, but to commend and approve whatever they have said, and to believe they spoke with a good conscience. But if the **significator** <note>The planet representing the absent person.</note> of the absent one is in the **sixth** from his own house, or in the **sixth** from the ascendant, or elsewhere joined with the lord of the sixth, or in its **square aspect** or **opposition** without **reception** <note>A condition where planets are in each other's signs, indicating mutual support.</note> and the aspect of an unimpeded fortune, it signifies that he is **ill**. If, however, he is seeking the conjunction of that addition mentioned before, it signifies he is about to become ill. But if he is escaping from a conjunction of the malefics by body or by any of the aforementioned aspects so that he is separated from them, or is escaping from combustion, it signifies he has escaped from sickness or from another impediment similar to sickness. You shall judge the severity or lightness of the sickness according to the conjunction he has passed, from which that significator has escaped. ¶ However, you must be careful not to judge him sick unless you first see whether he is then **sleeping**; nor judge him dead unless you first see whether he is then **drunk**; nor judge him wounded unless you first see whether he has then been **bled** <term>phlebotomy: the medical practice of opening a vein to balance the humors</term>, of which things you can have such knowledge: consider if the significator of the absent one is in the **sixth** but is not joined to the lord of the sixth nor to any malefic impeding him, and is joined to a strong and free fortune that is not impeded, or to one of the planets friendly to him that is fortunate, strong, and not impeded: it signifies he is not sick but rather **sleepy**; and not wounded but rather **bled**. Understand the same if he is in the **eighth** with the aforementioned conditions, for it signifies he is **drunk** and not dead.

### Chapter 2: Concerning the arrival of someone absent.
**V**ery often questions are put to astrologers about absent persons—whether they will return or not, and when they will return, which is a difficult matter; though those who ask do not believe that it is more labor to answer than to ask. Therefore, if you are asked about someone who is absent, whether he returns or not and when: look to the **lord of the house** by which the absent one is signified, as I told you above in the preceding chapter, and see if his significator is in the **ascendant** (whatever the journey may be), or in the **ninth** if it was a **long journey**, or in the **twelfth** if it was a **very long journey**, or in the **fifth** if it was a **moderate journey**, or in the **third** if it was a **short journey**. For a **short journey** is considered one day's travel; a **moderate** one I call from one day up to three; **long** from three up to sixty; and **very long** from sixty as far as one can go. Or if he joins with any planet which is in those houses to whom he commits his disposition, it signifies that the absent one will return. And if he is in the **seventh**, it signifies his arrival, but not quickly—rather his arrival is delayed; and it signifies that he is in the land to which he set out, and has not yet left it to return, though he is concerned about his arrival. But if he is in the **fourth**, it signifies a longer delay of his arrival than when he is in the seventh; yet he intends to return when he can, and will return unless he is impeded by some malefic in his own house. And if he is in the **third** or **ninth** and is joined to any planet in the **ascendant**, it signifies that the absent person is ready or is preparing himself immediately for the return. And if you find him in the **second** and he is joined to any planet in the **ninth house** or in the **tenth house**, it signifies that he is preparing for the return, nor will there be a great delay in his arrival. If, however, you find him **cadent** <note>In a house that does not aspect the ascendant, traditionally houses 3, 6, 9, or 12.</note> from the ascendant so that he does not aspect it, also...

Refers to Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician.</note>, however, as I told you in another chapter, gave the first house to the absent person.

Next, you must consider another thing about the absent person, because absence can happen in many and various ways, as was said in the preceding chapter. For there is the absent person who is an **exile**; there is the **traveler**; there is the **expelled**; there is the **banished**; there is the **deportee**; and there is the **fugitive**. Thus "absent" is a general term. 

However, "absent" is properly said of one who absented himself by his own spontaneous will, whether he went to a certain or determined place or not, provided he went with the purpose and intention of returning, as I said elsewhere. An **exile** is said to be one who left his land not knowing the cause, except perhaps led by some foolishness, or perhaps he goes wavering or inquiring if he can find a land better suited to him than the one he was in; perhaps he had not premeditated where he was going, nor did he absent himself with the mind to return or not to return, but goes like a wanderer. A **traveler** <note>Original: "Peregrinus." Often meaning a pilgrim.</note> is said to be one who absented himself by his own spontaneous will to set out for some place in the manner of a journey, whether in the serv-

<column-break/>

-ice of God, as if he wished to cross the sea to go to **Saint James** <note>Santiago de Compostela.</note> or **Saint Peter** <note>Rome.</note> and similar places. 

C An **expelled person** is said to be one who was driven out of the land in which he lived against his will by some enemy of his, or by someone stronger than him, or by some faction—as sometimes happens between parties in cities, castles, or other lands when one side expels the other. 

C A **banished person** is said to be one who is expelled because of some crime or for any other cause, such as when the authorities or the commune of the land in which he lived expelled him and banished him, and he does not dare return there even if he wishes to. 

C A **deportee** is said to be one who, by the commune of his land, was sent under guard for some reason to a certain place and cannot leave there without the permission of the guards or the garrison. 

C A **fugitive** is said to be one who, out of fear that some disaster might happen to him, fled from the land in which he lived; he fears to return to it, yet for this he has not been officially banished, but perhaps there are some who seek to harm him if he returns. 

Thus, all such people in any of the predicted cases are "absent." And if a question is asked about any of them—whether he will return to his land, whether by his own accord or by another—always give the person who absented himself spontaneously with the intention of returning the **eighth house** for his person, as I said, and the **first house** for his land (except for the traveler). To all other absent people, whether expelled, banished, fugitives, or travelers, give the **seventh house** for their person and the **first house** for their land, just as with the expelled, as was said in the other chapter.

### On the time of the absent person’s arrival.

To know the time of the absent person’s arrival, look at the cusp of the house in which he is located, if he is in any of the aforementioned houses. If he is not in one of them, see how many degrees he is distant from the planet to which he committed his disposition. In any of these, count degree by degree: for if it is a short journey, it signifies he may come within that many **days**; if it is a medium journey, it signifies he will come within that many **weeks**; if it is a long journey, it signifies he is to come within that many **months**; if it is a very long journey, it signifies he is to come within that many **years**.

## Chapter 3: Concerning the death of the interrogator.

Some people occasionally have doubts about the arrival of **death**, fearing it might overtake them before a time that seems naturally appropriate. Lest they be unable to properly arrange their affairs, they consult an astrologer on this matter so they can be certain. 

Therefore, if someone asks you a question about their own death, whether they ask it generally or for a specific time: look at the hour of his questioning and cast a figure for that question—specifically the first and tenth houses and the other houses and the locations of the planets by their degrees and minutes, and by their direct or retrograde motion, and according to their longitude and latitude. If he asks specifically, saying: "See if I shall die between now and one, two, or three years," or more or less as it seems to him he should ask: look to the **Lord of the First House** and the **Moon**. Use them in this matter and see where they are: whether in "angles," in "succedent" houses, or in "cadent" houses; whether they are in their own dignities, or are "peregrine" <note>Without essential dignity or strength.</note>, or are "void of course" <note>Making no further aspects before leaving their current sign.</note>, or joined to others. 

For if the Lord of the First is joined with one of the planets that are **fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus.</note> and commits its disposition to it, and that planet is strong so that it does not commit its disposition to another: look then to see if that good planet and fortune is the **Lord of the Eighth House**. For if it is not the Lord of the Eighth and is disposed as I have said, it signifies that he will not die.

### Chapter Four: On the time of death for one asking generally about death.

If the question is "absolute" <note>A general question with no specific timeframe.</note> and the person has not specified a timeframe but says: "See for me when I shall die," then observe the Lord of the First, the Moon, the Lord of the Eighth, and the planet to which the Lord of the First or the Moon is joined. Judge his death according to the distance in degrees existing between the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Eighth, or the planet to which he or the Moon is joined; for he will die within that many units of time. 

If the Lord of the First is in an **angle** <term>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, representing the strongest points of the chart.</term>, he will die within that many years. If he is in a **succedent house** <term>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses.</term>, within that many months. If he is in a **cadent house** <term>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, traditionally the weakest.</term>, within that many weeks <note>original: "ebdomadas".</note>. 

However, if it does not signify death, it signifies that he will live for as many years, months, or weeks as there are degrees in that distance—that is, however many degrees the Lord of the First is distant from the Lord of the Eighth or from the hindering malefic planet, so many will be the years, months, or weeks. Know this because in this case, you must watch the Lord of the First and the Moon more closely, for the Moon is the partner of the Lord of the First in this matter. Hence, the conjunction of the Lord of the First with the Lord of the Eighth, or with any hindering malefic and the Moon, is more to be feared; for

<column-break/>

the Lord of the First signifies the life and body of the person by his nature, not by accident. But if the Lord of the First has separated from the Lord of the Eighth, or the Lord of the Eighth from him, or from a malefic planet that was hindering him, it does not kill him, nor will it kill him for as many years (if it signifies years), or months (if it signifies months), or weeks (if it signifies weeks) as there are degrees between that separation and the next conjunction they will make together. 

The conjunction of the Moon with the Lord of the Eighth does not harm unless the Lord of the First also joins him, and she is stronger and freer from impediments than the Lord of the First. This does not happen with the Moon, because if the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Eighth or a malefic under the conditions stated above, the goodness of the Moon does not help the person or the seeker to escape, even though she has the greatest significance in other matters along with the Lord of the First.

### Chapter Five: Whether the wife or the husband shall die first.

If a man or woman asks you which of them will die first, look at the Lord of the First House and the Lord of the Seventh House <note>The house of marriage and partners.</note>. See which of them is first in misfortune, combustion, or "fall" <term>A sign where a planet's influence is weakened.</term>, or which will first experience any of the aforementioned hindrances and conditions. That person whose significator is so disposed is signified to die first.

### Chapter Six: By what kind of death the interrogator shall die.

And if he says to you, "See by what death I am to die," look at the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> and its Lord. If you find the Lord in the Eighth House and the Eighth House is in **Leo**, and its Lord is unfortunate or hindered, it signifies he will be torn by the teeth or claws of some beast, or will die by a beast in some other way. 

But if **Saturn** is joined with the Lord of the Eighth and hinders him from **Scorpio** or **Pisces**, he will fear death from the bite of a serpent or another poisonous animal. If he escapes this, he should fear suffocating in water. 

If **Mars** is joined with the Lord of the Eighth in the Eighth, Sixth, Fourth, or Twelfth house without reception, and is joined with the Lord of the First and hinders him, it announces he will perish by the sword or fire—but more likely by the sword. In other places, however, it will not leave him secure.

### Concerning the Ninth House.

#### Chapter One: On a journey or pilgrimage, whether it will be good or not; and if it occurs, whether it will be profitable or not.

If someone proposes to make a journey and has firmly decided to do so—or perhaps if there is only one person who proposed the journey and wants to know whether that journey will come to pass or not—and he asks you whether that journey will happen or not; and if it does not happen, what it is that will hinder it: then look at the **Lord of the First House** and the significatrix, which is the **Moon** (as both are significators of the querent). Look also at the **Ninth House** and its Lord, which has the power to signify a long journey or pilgrimage; the **Third House** signifies a short journey; the **Fifth**, a medium one; and the **Twelfth**, the longest journey of all. 

For if you find the Lord of the First in the Ninth, or the Moon, or if any of them are joined with the Lord of the Ninth—and even more strongly if it is in the Third, Fifth, Seventh, or Eleventh—the journey or pilgrimage will take place. The interrogator himself will be the reason the journey happens, and nothing external or foreign will occur to move him to the journey except his own spontaneous and voluntary motion. <margin>¶</margin> Then look at the Lord of the Ninth and see where he is; if he is in the First House, it signifies that news will come to him from the place where he intended to go, which will move him to that same place even faster than he was originally going to go. 

If, however, the Lord of the First or the significatrix (the Moon) is in the Ninth, such news will come to him that the man will almost never go. But if, in addition to the Lord of the Ninth being in the First, he is joined with the Lord of the First, certain things will happen such that he can in no way go, unless perhaps the interrogator wishes to act by his own natural will and choice. <margin>¶</margin> If the Lord of the Ninth is not in the First House joined to the Lord of the First, see if any planet "transfers light" <term>Translation of light: when a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, connecting their influences.</term> from one to the other; this signifies that the journey will happen. 

If there is no planet to transfer the light of the Lord of the First or of the Ninth from one to the other, then see if the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Ninth are both joined to some planet that is "heavier" <note>Moving more slowly through the zodiac.</note> than they are, and if that heavier planet beholds the Ninth House; this similarly signifies that the journey will happen. If the Lord of the First is not joined to the Lord of the Ninth, and there is no planet to transfer light between them, nor are they joined to a heavier planet that beholds the Ninth House, judge that the journey will not happen—

<column-break/>

—that journey about which he asks. Likewise, if the Lord of the First is in an "angle" <term>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful and active positions.</term> and is joined to some planet in the Third, it signifies that the journey will happen if it is free from malefics, as certain authorities have said, with whom **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician.</note> seems to agree. If it is joined to a planet in the Second House, it signifies the journey just as if it were in the Third, provided it is free from the aspects or conjunctions of malefics. If, however, the Lord of the First and the Moon are joined to some planet in an angle and are not in the aforementioned places—though they signify the journey as has been said—it signifies that the journey will not happen.

<margin>¶</margin> Nevertheless, you must consider this: if the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Ninth, and you see by that conjunction that the journey ought to take place, but you find any malefic in the First House that has no "dignity" <term>Essential dignity refers to a planet's strength based on its position in a specific sign (like being in its own 'home').</term> there and hinders them or one of them, then the journey will be nullified and will not happen. There will be some cause destroying it that happens to the querent, hindering his journey so that what he began does not occur. 

If that malefic is in the **Second House**, something will happen regarding his wealth or substance that disturbs the journey, or regarding a member of his household who is not a relative. If it is in the **Third**, it will happen because of a brother; if he has no brother, it will happen because of something signified by the Third House <note>Such as neighbors or short trips.</note>. <margin>¶</margin> And if it is in the **Fourth**, it will happen because of his father; if he has no father, it will happen because of something signified by the Fourth House, such as a matter of land. If it is in the **Fifth**, it will happen because of a son; if he has no son, it will happen because of something signified by the Fifth House <note>Such as pleasure or messengers.</note>. 

<margin>¶</margin> And if it is in the **Sixth**, it will happen because of illness or because of a servant, or a household matter, or any of the things signified by the Sixth House. If it is in the **Seventh**, it will be because of rumors coming to him from the land to which he wished to go, or because of the thing he intended to obtain, or because of a wife, or because of enemies or thieves. And **Zahel** said that if it beholds the "Ascendant" <note>The First House or the rising sign.</note>, he should fear being killed or something signified by the Seventh House. 

<margin>¶</margin> And if it is in the **Eighth**, it will happen to him because of death or something signified by the Eighth House. If it is in the **Ninth**, it will happen because of rumors he hears from the journey, or perhaps because the way is not safe, or something signified by the Ninth House. If it is in the **Tenth**, it will happen because of someone in authority over him who does not permit him to make his journey, such as a government power or his family, or something signified by the Tenth House. 

<margin>¶</margin> And if it is in the **Eleventh**, it will happen because of a friend or something signified by the Eleventh House. And if it is in the **Twelfth**, it will happen because of someone who feigns being a friend when he is not—indeed, he is a secret enemy—or something signified by the Twelfth House. 

If the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Ninth, and afterward is joined to a malefic by conjunction or from opposition or a square aspect, and that person has already set out on the journey, it signifies destruction that will occur to him after he has traveled. <margin>¶</margin> And **Zahel** said that the destruction will be according to the nature of that malefic's enmity: that is, if it is the Lord of the Sixth, it will be illness; if it is the Lord of the Fourth, it will be imprisonment or some sorrow; and if it is the Lord of the Eighth, it will be death. If it is the Lord of the Seventh or the Twelfth, it signifies destruction by thieves and enemies. And if it beholds the Ascendant, fear being killed. If from the Second House, it signifies the loss of wealth. Likewise, a square aspect to the Ascendant signifies harm to the body, and the other square aspect (the tenth) signifies loss of wealth. And he said that if you find the Lord of the Ascendant in the Seventh or Eighth, it signifies labor and hardship in travel, and especially if it is...

Nevertheless, if the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term> <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon, representing the person asking the question.</note> is in the eighth house and is not a malefic, and receives the Lord of the eighth house but is not received by it, it signifies that the traveler will take possession of the goods of others in the place to which he intends to go. <margin>¶</margin> Next, observe if the Lord of the first house is free from impediment—that is, from <term>retrogradation</term> <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky.</note>, "fall," <term>combustion</term> <note>Being so close to the Sun that the planet's power is "burned up."</note>, conjunction with malefics, or their "square" aspect or opposition—it signifies that the journey will be safe and easy, neither narrow nor laborious. Likewise, he said: know that the Ascendant signifies the pilgrimage; the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The 10th house, representing the traveler's business or success.</note> signifies his affairs; the seventh house from the Ascendant signifies the land to which he goes; and the fourth house from the Ascendant signifies the end of that matter. If, however, you find a "fortune" in the first house, you will see that the journey becomes good and useful, with the safety of both soul and body. If a "fortune" is in the 10th, it signifies that the merchandise or things he carries will be clearly profitable, if he brings trade goods with him. If a "fortune" is in the seventh, that land to which he intends to go will be good and useful for him, and he will rejoice and be glad in what he finds there; for he shall find what he desired to find. If, indeed, there is a "fortune" in the fourth, it signifies that his journey will end in a way that pleases him, and his will shall be well satisfied by what happens to him on that journey. If, however, you find any of the malefics in the aforesaid places, not having dignity in them, the journey will not be according to his will, but rather the opposite; for if it is in the first house, something horrible will happen to him on the road as he goes. If it is in the seventh, a horrible infirmity (that is, an illness or something similar) will happen to him in the land to which he intends to go. If it is in the tenth, there will happen a deterioration and loss of the things he carries. If it is in the fourth, distress and a lessening of things will happen to him, and the labor he sustained will be frustrating and useless.

## Chapter 2: For what purpose the traveler sets out, or for what cause the journey is made.

It is sometimes the custom for some to hide from the astrologer what they intend to seek, sometimes for the sake of testing him, and sometimes for the sake of hiding their intention, because they do not wish to reveal to anyone what they intend—and most often regarding journeys, lest perhaps others envy them, or perhaps for some other cause as it seems best to them. If, however, after the question is posed, you see that a journey is in the future and you wish to know toward whom the traveler intends to go: <margin>¶</margin> Look to the significator, which is the **Moon**, and see to whom she is joined; for that planet to which the **Moon** is joined signifies the person toward whom the traveler intends to go, or the cause for which the journey happens to him. If the **Moon** is joined to **Saturn**, he goes to low-born and ignoble persons, or to monks or other religious men wearing black garments, or to the old and decrepit, or to Jews. And if she is joined to **Jupiter**, his journey is to citizens, or to bishops, or secular religious men, or judges, or those learned in the law. And if she is joined to **Mars**, it signifies he goes to warriors, or to bellicose soldiers, or pirates, or highwaymen <note>original: "abscisores viarum"; literally "cutters of the roads."</note>. And if she is joined to the **Sun**, it signifies he goes to a 

<column-break/>

king or to some noble magnate, wealthy and honorable. And if she is joined to **Venus**, it signifies he goes to women or to others of the players <note>Actors or entertainers.</note> who perform womanly offices. And if she is joined to **Mercury**, it signifies he goes to philosophers, or writers, or other wise and lettered men, or to merchants, or masters of works <note>Architects or master craftsmen.</note>. If, however, the **Moon** is then <term>void of course</term> <note>original: "vacua cursu"; moving through a sign without making any further connections to planets.</note>, his journey will be for the purpose of finding a certain absent person who is known to him. <margin>¶</margin> If, with this, she was previously separated from **Saturn** (that is, if she were void of course), it signifies that his journey is because he is infested by creditors because of a guarantee <note>original: "manu levationem"; likely referring to acting as a surety or bondsman for someone else's debt.</note> he made for someone, or even because of his own debts, because he is not able to satisfy the creditors. If she was separated from **Jupiter**, it signifies his journey is caused by being separated, or wanting to separate himself, from some bishop or other prelate or judge, or from some noble citizen. And if she was separated from **Mars**, it signifies his journey is because he intends to separate himself from someone who is accustomed to leading armies, who is then in command of some army, or from some bellicose soldier, according to how you then see **Mars** in his dignity; for if **Mars** was then in his exaltation, he flees or intends to flee from a king. If in his house, from a duke. If in any of his minor dignities, from a bellicose soldier. If he is <term>peregrine</term> <note>A planet wandering in a sign where it has no special power or "dignity."</note>, he flees or wishes to flee from thieves or highwaymen. If she was separated from the **Sun**, it signifies he is separated from some king or a very noble magnate, or intends to separate himself from him, perhaps fearing him. And if she was separated from **Venus**, it signifies that his journey is because he is separated from some woman or intends to separate from her; or perhaps because he deceived her and made light of her in some way. If, however, she was separated from **Mercury**, it signifies that the journey or the flight which he has fled (or intends to flee) is to separate himself from some writer or other lettered man, or from some merchant. <margin>¶</margin> Likewise, look to which of the planets the **Moon** first joins if she were void of course: for if it is in its own house, the one to whom the traveler goes will be from that region; and if it is in its exaltation, he will be from outside the region, but he holds a lay dignity there, such as a power <note>A "podestà" or high-ranking civic official.</note> or similar. And if it is in its <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, it signifies he is a man from outside the region, but he dwells in it as if he were a citizen of that region or land. And if it is in its <term>term</term> <note>A specific segment of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet.</note>, he will be a man who dwells in that region and has his parents there. And if it is in its <term>face</term> <note>A ten-degree subdivision of a sign.</note>, he will be a foreigner, but now he dwells in that land or region and is held as a citizen. And if the Lord of the house in which the planet is found (to which the **Moon** is joined) "beholds" it <note>Forms an astrological aspect.</note>, the person to whom the traveler goes will be well-known in the region where he dwells. If, however, he does not behold it, he is not publicly known in that region or land where he then dwells. And if he does behold it, see with what aspect he beholds it, whether good or bad; for if he beholds it with a <term>trine</term> aspect <note>A harmonious 120-degree angle.</note>, he will be a man whom all his neighbors love and honor, and he is very pleasing to them. If he beholds it with a <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>A harmonious 60-degree angle.</note>, he will be beloved and honored in that land, but it will be somewhat less than the former. If that aspect is a <term>square</term> <note>A challenging 90-degree angle.</note>, he is not loved much, nor is he much hated; and some say good of him, yet there are more speaking ill than those who commend him. If indeed the aspect is an opposition, he will be a man of whom men commonly and unanimously speak ill, and almost all who have to communicate with him hate him and hold him as contentious and a whisperer <note>A spreader of rumors or a backbiter.</note>. If, however, it is a bodily conjunction <note>When two planets are in the exact same degree.</note>, it signifies he is a talkative man who meddles in many of his own and others' affairs, and by that meddling he strives to subtract money from men, and he does not look for any path <note>original: "vadum"; literally "ford" or "shallows."</note> except where he can acquire it in all ways, through right and wrong, and he is solicitous so that he may be able to wander <note>original: "erogare"; possibly meant to distribute or take away.</note> after the money of others. <margin>¶</margin> Likewise, look if you see that he makes the journey he proposed to make...
