### Chapter 3: How it will go for a traveler in the city they enter.

If any traveler or pilgrim wishes to know, when he enters any city or foreign land, what will happen to him there—or if you wish to know this for yourself—look at the **first house** at the moment he enters that land, or when the traveler asks the question. 

And see if the **Lord of the 2nd House**, which signifies the substance <note>In astrology, the second house relates to wealth, possessions, and the "substance" of a place.</note> of that city, is "direct" <note>Moving forward normally through the zodiac.</note>; he will return in no great length of time and will complete what he intends quite quickly. 

If, however, the planet is "stationary" <note>Appearing to stand still before changing direction.</note> in its second station, there will be a delay in his return; but nevertheless, he will complete the business for which he went. Yet, many contrary hindrances will strike his business, such that he will not believe himself able to complete it. 

If, however, it is stationary in its first station, he will believe he can complete what he intends, but in the end, he will not finish it, and he will return angry after some delay because he will have gained nothing; rather, he will have spent more than he gained. 

If it is "retrograde" <note>Appearing to move backward.</note>, he will depart quickly from that land and will not complete the thing for which he went, nor will he gain anything there, nor will any good come to him in it. 

If the Lord of the 2nd House is in the 1st, 10th, or 11th house, that journey and entry into that land will be useful, good, and profitable; he will rejoice and be glad for that reason. 

But if the Lord of the 2nd is in the 7th house, many contrary and horrible things will happen to him, and it will be necessary for him to litigate for that reason. For perhaps those with whom he has to do business will deny him the truth, especially if they are "malefic significators"—namely, if they are the Lords of the 7th house—and contentions, hardships, and many other things will strike him, which will disturb him and bring him grief and sadness. 

If the Lord of the 2nd is in the 3rd or 9th house from the **Ascendant**, it signifies the instability of the seeker and his movement within the land he entered, or that he will move from that land to another. He will not draw out a delay in it except a small one or almost none; and if he does delay there, it will not be by his own will, but rather against his will, as if he were forced to stay there. 

If it is in the 4th house and any of the malefics aspect it from a "square" aspect <note>An angle of 90 degrees, considered stressful.</note> or from opposition <note>An angle of 180 degrees.</note>, he will not travel further easily unless he is "received" with a good reception. 

<column-break/>

And if it is joined to it bodily <note>A "conjunction," where two planets are in the same degree.</note>, it does not seem that he will return further to his own home, and it seems that he is destined to die there. 

If, however, **Mars** is that malefic which hinders the Lord of the 2nd, and the **Moon** is joined to it (the Lord of the 2nd), or if she is joined with **Mercury** by a square aspect, or opposition, or by body, and then **Mars** aspects the **Moon**, horrible things will happen to him. He will fall into contention with certain evil people who use the things that belong to **Mars** and are signified by sight <note>Likely referring to weapons or violent tools.</note>; thus they will offend him and wound him with uncertain wounds. 

If the **Moon** is then in the 4th house and **Mars** aspects her from any aspect whatsoever, that seeker or traveler will die from it. If, however, she is in other "narrow" places <note>Difficult or weak astrological houses.</note>, he will not die from it; but if he is wounded, scars will appear in the places of the wounds. And if he survives entirely, traces of torture will remain in the places constricted by the tightness of the torment <note>This likely refers to being put in chains or stocks.</note>. 

If, however, when the **Moon** is in aspect with **Mars**, and **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, **Venus**, or **Mercury** (if he is good at that time) does not aspect her, that horrible thing will happen to the seeker or traveler according to the significance of that sign or house in which **Mars** is located. 

If, however, any of the aforementioned "fortunes" <note>Beneficial planets.</note> aspects the **Moon** at that time, then perhaps those horrible things we spoke of will not happen; or if they do happen, the seeker or traveler will be freed from them and will escape, and will find a remedy and an escape from all these things. 

But if none of the aforementioned fortunes aspect the **Moon**, it is feared then that those horrors are so depraved and so clinging to the traveler or seeker that he may die from them.

### Chapter 4: How it will go for a traveler on their journey or its occasion, whether a king or any other person.

Men are sometimes accustomed to ask, when they go on some journey or pilgrimage or some such thing, how they ought to believe or what will happen to them on that journey or because of it; or perhaps you wish to know for yourself how it should go for him. 

Look at the **Ascendant** at the hour of the question, if he asked, or his movement, if he did not ask, and verify all the houses from the 1st to the 12th. See the disposition of the significators of all the houses and their state; whichever of them you find well-disposed, judge good from that; and whichever of them you find ill-disposed, judge evil from that. 

Furthermore, you shall judge for him concerning his state according to another less detailed method: namely, you must look at the planets that are between the 1st and the 4th houses, and especially those which are in the **2nd house**. 

And if there is a malefic planet there which has no "house," "exaltation," "term," "triplicity," or "face" <note>These are the five "Essential Dignities" or strengths a planet can have in a specific sign.</note>, it signifies at least that damage will happen to him in those things which he left behind him. 

If he is a **king** or another great noble, that damage or detriment will be in his kingdom or duchy or county, and in those things which belong to him by kinship. 

If, however, the planet does not have any of the aforementioned dignities there, nor has a "face" there, it signifies damage to his things, both in great men and in common people. And especially if it is a common person who does not have a kingdom or city or castles, it signifies damage to the things he possesses and in the things of his house, both movable and otherwise; and it signifies detriment in any of his neighbors and blood-relations who love him. 

If that malefic which was in the 2nd house is **Mars**, that detriment will happen to him because of war or some other contention, or by the burning of fire, or the shedding of blood, or by the cutting off of roads, or the death of small animals or male or female servants, according to how **Mars** was then disposed to signify any of the aforesaid. 

If, however, it is **Saturn**, that horror or detriment will be by reason of shipwreck, or drowning, or ruin, or thieves...

where it is located. And if it is between the **first** and **tenth** houses, as 
Zahel says, that detriment or loss will happen on 
his return. If it is between the **seventh** and **tenth** houses, it happens during 
his departure. And if it is between the **first** and **fourth** houses beneath the earth, 
it relates to those things he acquired during his departure. If, however, it is

it seems that the one who translated this did not know the Arabic

would seem more appropriate that impediments should happen 
if there were a hindering malefic between the **first** and **fourth** houses 
during his departure from the land in which he was, going toward the deep 
until the middle of the journey. If it were between the **fourth** and **seventh**, 
they ought to happen from the middle of the journey until the land to 
which the traveler intended to go. And if it were between the **7th**, **8th**, and **10th**, 
it would happen to him on his return until the middle of the return 
journey, especially in those things he acquired. And if it were 
between the **tenth** and **first**, it would happen after the middle of the return 
journey back to his home or his land. ¶ Here must be placed 
the accidents according to each house and each 
planet: and so that you may know this more specifically, look for the 
**Fortunes** helping and the **malefics** hindering: and see in which 
houses they are: because in those proportions of the 
journey, their significations (of both the Fortunes and malefics) will happen. 
For if they are in the **first house**, they will happen at the beginning of the 
journey, a little outside the gate of the land from which he departs, or perhaps 
they will happen within the gate. If they are in the **second**, they will happen 
within the fifth part of the journey. If they are in the **third**, they will happen 
within the third part of the journey. If they are in the **fourth**, they 
will happen within the halfway point of the journey. If they are in the **fifth**, 
they will happen within the third part of the remaining journey after the 
first half. If they are in the **sixth**, they will happen after two 
parts of the remaining journey after the first half. If they are in the **seventh**, 
they will happen in the place to which the traveler is going. If they are in the **eighth**, 
they will happen in the departure from that place, or near the fifth part of 
the return journey from the place to which he returned. If 
they are in the **ninth**, they will happen in the third part of the return journey. 
If they are in the **tenth**, they will happen at the halfway point of the return 
journey. If they are in the **eleventh**, they will happen after the second 
part of the return journey. If they are in the **twelfth**, they will happen 
near the land to which the traveler returns. Then look 
to see in which of the aforementioned houses a **Fortune** is found: because 
there the traveler will rejoice and good things will happen to him; for example, if it is 
**Jupiter**, it will signify the gain of money; if it is **Venus**, he 
will rejoice with women and banquets and similar things.

If, however, **malefics** are found there, the opposite will happen to him: for

### ¶ Chapter 5: Toward which direction it is better to go.

Now, when a traveler or someone else asks, 
saying: "Toward which direction is it better for me to go?" 
Look at the figure <note>The astrological chart or "horoscope" cast for the moment of the question.</note> you have erected: and see in which quarter the 
**Fortunes** are, and which are most fit and better; and 
according to that, tell him where it is better to go: if in the **Eastern** quarter, toward the 
East; if in the **Southern**, toward the South; if in the **Western**, 
toward the West; if in the **Northern**, toward the 
North. And in whichever quarter there are more Fortunes 
and better disposed ones, it is better to go toward that direction. 
And say the same of the **infortunes** <note>Another term for malefics.</note>: that in whichever quarter 
there are more infortunes, it is worse to go toward that direction. 
And let him see what else might happen to that traveler: 
for if the **Lord of the First** <note>The planet ruling the person asking the question.</note> is joined with any of the 
significators of the question, he will meet that person on the road. If it is the **Lord of the 
Third**, he will meet a brother. If it is the **Lord of the Fourth**, he will meet 
a father. If it is in the **Fifth**, he will meet a son, if he has 
a brother or father, etc. And understand that same thing for 
all the significators of the houses. And if the significator of the 
brother is in the first, the brother will come to him. And if the **Lord of the 
First** is in the third, the traveler goes there to his brother. And say the same 
for all significators of the houses if the seeker 
has a brother or father, etc., while traveling. And always let it be 
your care to look at the **second** and **eighth** houses in journeys; according to that 
saying of **Ptolemy**: "Beware of infortunes in the eighth house and their 
aspects when departing on a journey, and in the second when returning." Because a malefic 
or infortune in the eighth signifies detriment in the 
gain of the land to which the traveler intends to go; and in the second, in the gain 
of the land to which the traveler intends to return. Therefore, you ought to 
place a **Fortune** in the eighth house in any journey, or 
make it so that some of them aspect <note>Forms a geometric relationship, like a trine or sextile, with that house.</note> it; and if you can place the 
**Head** <note>original: "caput"; the "Head of the Dragon" or North Node, considered beneficial.</note> with it, it will be better. And then beware of the **Tail**; and if it 
should happen that you could not avoid a malefic being there, 
place the **Tail** there and then beware of the **Head**. Understand that same thing 
regarding the **second house** when someone returns, just as I told you regarding 
the **eighth** when one goes: that no malefic be there, nor aspect it; 
and if you cannot avoid it aspecting, let its aspect be 
**trine** or at least **sextile** <note>Harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note>; and always place a Fortune there 
or make it so that it aspects it.

<meta>This page continues a technical manual on horary astrology—the practice of casting a chart to answer specific questions. While the previous page focused on the dangers of travel (thieves and animals), this page describes the refined methods used by master astrologers for choosing between multiple options, such as which person to marry or whether to change jobs or homes. It references specific historical figures to lend authority to these techniques.</meta>

Regarding **Sabbioneta of Cremona** <note>original: "de sabloneto cremonēsi"; likely referring to a specific school of thought or a scholar from the Italian town of Sabbioneta, near Cremona.</note>: many others used the first and seventh houses for all the matters mentioned above, yet they believed their judgments primarily relied on these two modes. **Bellonus of Pisa** <note>original: "Bellonus vō pisanus"; a known medieval astrological authority.</note> used all four angles for the matters above. **Brandeus**, the son of the aforementioned David, used a certain secret method of his own which he revealed to no one, and it served him well in his judgments.

I, however, without disparaging any of them—neither the ancients nor the moderns—have used the method I am telling you, and blessed be our Lord, the son of the Blessed Virgin. My judgments were sound and authentic because I used this method: and I advise you to use it as well. 

Specifically, if a question was put to me regarding any of the aforesaid things that involved multiple items of the same kind, I would safely take three things under one **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the person asking.</note> and judge them as if they were one. I used the **lords of triplicity** <note>term: triplicity; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water). Each triplicity has three planetary "lords" that rule it.</note> signifying the thing sought, and I judged based on them.

**For example:** suppose someone wanted to take a wife and had several women in mind. He would make his inquiry and phrase it thus: "I am in talks to take **Martha** as a wife, and also **Bertha** and **Juvenda**. See which of them is better or more useful for me, and if a marriage will be completed between me and any of them, and with which one it will be completed." 

Suppose the ascendant was **Aries**, which signifies the seeker, and **Libra** <note>The sign opposite Aries, ruling the seventh house of marriage.</note> was given to the woman. I would then look at the lords of the triplicity of Libra—namely **Saturn**, who is the first; **Mercury**, who is the second; and **Jupiter**, who is the third. Whichever of them I found in **conjunction** <note>An alignment where two planets appear in the same spot in the sky.</note> with **Mars** (which was the significator of the seeker), I would say that he would complete the marriage with that specific woman. 

And if Mars were joined with two of them, or with all of them, I would say that he would complete it with the one whose significator was closer to the conjunction of Mars. If all were equally joined to him, whether by body or by **aspect** <note>The geometric angles between planets, such as 60, 90, or 120 degrees.</note>, I would say he could complete it with any of them. But if one was joined to Mars by aspect and another by body <note>term: by body; a physical conjunction in the same degree, considered much stronger than a mere visual aspect.</note>, the one joined by body would be more worthy, and he would complete the marriage with her. 

You should understand the same for all other signified things; you shall judge the better and more useful one by that planet which is better, best positioned, and most fortunate. 

If, however, the question was about only one thing, you shall judge by the **lord of the seventh house** or by whichever house signifies the matter. And if he asks about several things—say, about three—then you will change the judgment: if there are four things, you will give the lord of the house signifying that matter to the first; the first lord of the triplicity to the second thing; the second lord of the triplicity to the third thing; and the third lord of the triplicity to the fourth thing. 

And if he asks again about five things of the same kind, you will again change the judgment and give the lord of the house to the first thing; the **lord of exaltation** <note>The planet that has its highest dignity or "strength" in a particular sign.</note> to the second thing; the first lord of the triplicity to the third; the second lord of the triplicity to the fourth; and the third lord of the triplicity to the fifth thing. 

If there is no exaltation for any planet there, you shall give (as was said) the lord of the house to the first thing, the first lord of the triplicity to the second, the second lord of the triplicity to the third, and the third lord to the fourth; and you shall give the **lord of the term** <note>A planet that rules a specific segment of degrees within a zodiac sign.</note> where the degree of the house signifying the thing sought falls to the fifth thing. 

Observe this method I have given you in every matter and every inquiry: such as if you are asked by someone who is in a certain land and things are not going well for him there, or if for another reason he wants to move from there to another, or from one house to another, or from one office to another, or from one craft to another, or any similar thing. 

And if he says to you: "See which of these is better for me, this or that," look at the state of the lord of the **first** and the lord of the **seventh**. If the lord of the first is in a better state than the lord of the seventh, then staying in that land, or that house where he is, or keeping that craft he holds, or practicing the 

<column-break/>

office he currently performs is better. If, however, the state of the lord of the seventh is better than the state of the lord of the first, then going to the land he wants, or moving to another house, or taking up the other craft is better and more useful for him. 

Likewise, observe whether, along with this, the **Moon** has separated from any **Fortune** <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> (whether it received her when she was joined to it or not), or from any malefic planet that was not hindered and which received her when she was joined to it; and if she has been joined to any malefic without full **reception** <note>A supportive relationship where one planet is in a sign or dignity ruled by the other.</note>, so that through that reception her state is improved: say that the land in which he is, or the house in which he dwells, or the craft he practices is better for him. 

But if she has separated from some malefic and has been joined to another malefic, then tell him to beware of that move. Speak similarly of the **Part of Fortune** <note>term: Part of Fortune; a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being.</note>: if the Fortunes are separating from it and malefics are joining it, predict evil; if malefics are separating from it and Fortunes are joining it, predict good—either way it will be good for him, whether he wants to do what he intends or not; but that thing whose significator is in a better state will be better for him. 

If, however, both significators are in a bad state, both options are bad for him; but the one whose significator is in a *less* bad state is the lesser evil for him. Speak similarly of the Moon and the Part of Fortune. 

If the state of the lord of the first is good, and the Moon has separated from a Fortune, and Fortunes have cast their aspect upon the Part of Fortune, say that the thing he is doing—or the house or land where he dwells—is the ultimate for him, such that it cannot be improved. If any of those things are missing, it will be less than this in proportion to what is missing from the aforementioned goods. 

If, however, the state of the lord of the seventh is bad, and the Moon is joined to malefics, and malefics aspect the Part of Fortune, it signifies that the thing he wants to do—or the house or land to which he wants to go or change—is so wretched for him that it cannot get any worse. If any of those conditions are missing, that malice will be less than this in proportion to the absence of any of those evils.

### Chapter Seven: Whether that land is better for him.

**Listen to Zael** <note>original: "Existe zabel"; likely an error for "Dixit Zael," referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were foundational in Latin translations.</note>: when someone asks you if the land I am in is better for me or the one to which I want to go, look at the Moon. If she has separated from a malefic, leaving will be better for him. If, however, she has separated from the Fortunes, staying will be better.

But **Zael** said: if he asks you, saying "Is it good for me if I go out for this business, or if I do that?", look at the lord of the ascendant and the Moon. If they have separated from malefics or are joined to Fortunes, command him to do what he wants. If, however, they have separated from Fortunes and are joined to malefics, let him not approach that work. 

If the state of the lord of the ascendant is good, staying will be better for him. If, however, the state of the lord of the seventh is better, going will be more useful for him. 

And if the Moon has separated from an **oriental** <note>A planet that rises before the Sun.</note> malefic that is **direct** <note>Moving forward, which is considered a position of strength.</note> and strong, and from a Fortune receiving her by **trine** or **sextile** <note>Favorable aspects of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note> aspect, and she has been joined to a hindered Fortune that does not receive her, it signifies that it is worse to do the thing he asks about than to leave it, even though it may seem good to do it. 

And if she has separated from a hindered and poorly disposed Fortune that does not receive her by a **square** <note>A challenging 90-degree aspect.</note> or by **opposition** <note>A stressful 180-degree aspect.</note>, and she has been joined to an oriental, direct, strong, and well-disposed malefic that receives her by a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies that it is worse to abandon the thing than to do it, even though doing it may not be "good" in an absolute sense. 

I say the same if she has separated from them as was said and is **void of course** <note>term: void of course; a period where the Moon makes no further aspects to other planets before changing signs, often indicating that "nothing will come of the matter."</note>, or if she is not separated but is joined to a Fortune. 

It seems to me that I have satisfied you regarding all these things. Nevertheless, if the significators of the things sought are so equal in strength or weakness that you cannot discern the truth through any of them, nor through the Moon similarly: then subtract the position of one significator from the position of the other significator, and to that remainder add the degrees of the ascending sign, and project it from the ascendant. See where that number falls, because according to that place, and according to the lord of 그 sign, and according to its state, you will be able to judge that matter.

### Chapter Eight: Concerning someone placed in prison or chains; what will happen to them regarding that prison—namely, whether they will be freed from that prison or not, and until when.

**W**hen someone who is imprisoned, or another person on their behalf, asks you whether they will be freed from that prison or not—and until when, without setting a specific time limit for the release: look to the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet that rules the sign on the eastern horizon.</note> and the **Moon**. If both are in **angles** <note>term: angles; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of an astrological chart, which are considered the most powerful and active positions.</note>, it signifies the detention of that captive and the prolongation of their imprisonment. Similarly, if the Lord of the 1st and the Lord of the 10th, as well as the Lord of the 7th and the Lord of the 4th, are in angles, it signifies their detention for that whole year. And if all four Lords of the said houses are not in those angles, but three of them or only two are, it likewise signifies their detention for that whole year. Furthermore, if only the Lord of the 1st is in an angle and the Moon is not in an angle, it signifies their detention and the prolongation of their imprisonment. Similarly, if the Lord of the 1st or the Moon is in a **fixed sign** <term>fixed sign; signs such as Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and duration.</term>, it signifies the prolongation of the prison. If they are in the first house, there will be such a prolongation. If they are in the tenth, their delay in prison will be longer: for if the first house signifies a day, the tenth will signify a **week** <note>original: "ebdomadam"</note>; what the first signifies as a week, the tenth will signify as a month; what the first signifies as a month, the tenth will signify as a year. And if it is in the seventh house: what would signify a day in the first, in the seventh will signify a week; what signifies a week in the first, in the seventh will signify a month; what signifies a month in the first, in the seventh will signify a year. If it is in the fourth house: what signifies hours in the first, in the fourth will signify a day; what signifies a day in the first, in the fourth signifies a week; what signifies a week in the first, in the fourth will signify a month; what signifies a month in the first, in the fourth will signify a year. And see if then the Lord of the **Twelfth House** <note>The house associated with imprisonment, hidden enemies, and suffering.</note> aspects the Lord of the 1st while that lord is in the fourth, or if the Moon does so; then distress and evil shall befall them in prison, such that because of that prison and that distress, one might doubt whether the prisoner will survive. And you should understand the same regarding the significator which is the Moon as was said regarding the Lord of the 1st. But if the Lord of the 3rd or the Lord of the 9th is the Lord of any angle—namely the 10th, 7th, or 4th—their exit from prison will be delayed; however, they shall escape afterward, and there will not be anyone who drags them from the prison, but they themselves shall break the locks or fetters and flee, or act in some other way so as to get out of the prison. If, however, the Lord of the 3rd or 9th is **lighter** <note>meaning a faster-moving planet, like Mercury or Venus.</note> than the Lord of the 1st, such that one of them is joined to it, it signifies that someone, even without the prisoner's request, will work on their behalf and act so that they are freed. And keep this always in mind: that when the Moon is joined to the Lord of any angle, unless something else assists as has been said, it judges a delay in the exit from prison.

Afterward, consider whether you see that the prisoner is about to leave the prison. If there is a malefic planet <note>Specifically Mars or Saturn.</note> in the **fourth house** which does not have its domicile or exaltation there, nor two of its minor dignities, and if it is direct in its motion, it signifies a misfortune that will happen to him after his exit from the prison. If it is **Mars**, he will be killed; if it is **Saturn**, he will be drowned—and perhaps he will be suffocated by that drowning—or they will beat him with clubs, or he will fall into wells or be thrown down, such that he could die from that fall, or his body will be broken. This will happen to him according to the significance of the sign in which that malefic planet is located.

But if the **Lord of the first house** is then entering **combustion** <note>term: combustion; the state of a planet being so close to the Sun (within approx. 8.5 degrees) that its influence is "burnt up" and hidden by the Sun's rays.</note>, such that it is already covered by the rays of the sun, it signifies that the prisoner about whom the question is asked is dead, or is sick with a fatal illness. I say this if a malefic is in the fourth house which has no dignity in it, as was said. If, however, the Lord of the first has passed through combustion from one minute up to one degree, it signifies that he is sick or about to be sick with a dangerous illness; nevertheless, there is hope for recovery from that illness. If he has passed further—that is, if he is separated from the body of the sun by more than one degree up to five full degrees—it signifies that he is sick or about to be sick with a very strong illness, but he will be healed. If he has been separated from the degree of the sun until he is distant from it by twelve full degrees, it signifies that he is sick, or can be sick, with an illness that is not very strong or dangerous. If he has been separated from it by more than twelve degrees until his appearance from under the sun's rays, it signifies that he was sick, but has already escaped from that sickness and is healed. You may understand the same thing regarding any absent person whose status is unknown: when you find their **significator** <note>The planet representing the person in the chart.</note> in such a state, you may judge them in this way.

And **Zahel** <note>The 9th-century Jewish astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr, a primary source for medieval astrology.</note> said that the further you see that malefic planet in the angle from the degree of the sun, the lighter his illness will be and the faster he will be healed. If, however, the Lord of the first is so disposed—namely, joined to the **Lord of the eighth house** <note>The house of death.</note> or with the Lord of the fourth—the prisoner or absent person will die from that illness. If, however, you do not find him to be sick but only incarcerated, and he is joined to **Saturn** bodily, or aspects it by opposition or a square aspect without perfect **reception** <note>term: reception; a cooperative relationship between planets where one "accepts" the other into its own zodiacal territory.</note>, it signifies an impediment to the body of the prisoner as well as a decrease and detriment to his wealth. If Saturn is then impeded, even if it receives the significator of the prisoner, it will still impede him, but not as severely as if it did not receive him. If **Mars** is in the place of Saturn, it signifies that he will be afflicted with strong affliction, and that his imprisonment will be made heavier, and he will be beaten more than usual. And look to the significatrix,

which is the **Moon**. If you find her impeded, misfortunes and obstacles will happen to him in prison which will come from an unknown or hidden cause; some naturally, and some by accident, even without the work of the guard or those who keep him imprisoned—unless the Lord of the house in which the Moon is then located aspects her. For if the Lord of her house aspects her, it diminishes that malice and alleviates it. Look also if **Mars** is in the **twelfth house** <note>The house of secret enemies and confinement.</note>; for it signifies the death of the prisoner before he exits from that prison, and the master of the prison will be the cause of that death. The same thing is to be said regarding the **Tail** <note>term: Tail; the South Node of the Moon (Cauda Draconis), generally considered a point of decrease or misfortune.</note>. For if it is so, he who resists him so that he is not freed from prison is moved by a just cause, and makes him stay in chains lest his exit cause him harm; therefore, fearing this, he strives so that he does not exit until he is first reconciled with him, and he is not found to act in a malicious way against him. But if they aspect each other by **opposition** or a **square aspect**, it does not appear that he who resists his release uses justice; rather, he seeks him with persistence, injustice, and the greatest perseverance, seeking that he be given over to his fortune, believing he can extort something from him and asserting that he has a right that the prisoner should be handed over to him. And look to the house of the prison, which is the **fourth**, if the prison is not very heavy (meaning tolerable); but if it is intolerable and unusual (meaning very heavy), it is signified by the **twelfth**. If you find the **Dragon’s Tail** there, it signifies an emptied prison and that the person asked about has already left the prison—unless the Lord of the first or the Moon is found in it, because the Tail always signifies emptying and decrease.

### Chapter Nine: Whether those things which appear in dreams have any significance or not, and when they signify something and when they have no significance.

**I**t is customary for things to appear in dreams that sometimes terrify men, yet some things sometimes make them rejoice. Sometimes horrible things appear which are beyond nature; sometimes things appear which seem natural. Sometimes things appear which afterward happen just as they were seen in the dreams, or nearly as they were seen. Sometimes nothing comes of all those things which are seen; sometimes they have some effect, and sometimes none. Sometimes men remember those things they see while dreaming, and sometimes they forget them and do not remember them at all. Hence, men—not knowing the difficulty of judging dreams and being unable to know their significance according to how they afterward occur—often ask an **astrologer** to tell them the truth of what their dream is meant to signify. Therefore, although we cannot answer them exactly as they intend, it is necessary that you say what can be said concerning dreams. If, therefore, someone comes to you to move a question about what he dreamed, or reports a dream to you and wants to know whether it signifies anything or not—and if it does signify, what it signifies: look to the hour of the question or the report, and the **ascendant**...

### Chapter 10. Concerning a bishopric, or an abbacy, or a cardinalate, or any other clerical dignity, whether an order or a religion, whose intent the seeker asks whether it may be obtained or not.

Although it may seem dishonorable to seek after religious dignities when divine gifts ought to be waited for from above, nevertheless there are many today who indifferently seek clerical dignities such as the papacy, the cardinalate, an archbishopric, a bishopric, abbacies, priories, and other dignities and clerical orders—both friars and others who are called secular clerics. Therefore, if anyone desiring to reach any of the aforementioned should come to you to be moved upon this question—whether he is to be promoted to the dignity or office he desires—you shall first consider what sign is on the **eastern line** <note>the Ascendant</note>, and see if the **Lord of Lords** <note>likely referring to the Almuten or the primary planetary ruler of the chart</note> or the Moon—that is, both of them or one of them, namely the one stronger than the Moon—is the **Lord of the Ninth**, which here signifies the matter sought. And if the Lord of the Ninth is in the ninth house or **aspects** it, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought, though with its own labor and ingenuity or study. If, however, neither of them is joined to the Lord of the Ninth, nor he with them, look then to see if either the Lord of the First or the Moon is in the ninth, for it signifies the attainment of that which the questioner intends, provided that the one among them in the ninth is not **impeded**—that is, that it is not **retrograde** or **combust** <note>A planet is "combust" when it is too close to the Sun, which was thought to weaken its power.</note>, nor does any of the malefics aspect it from a **fourth aspect** [square] or from **opposition** without perfect **reception** <note>original: "receptio"; a condition where a planet is in the sign or dignity of another planet, which "receives" it like a guest.</note>, for then it signifies the loss of the matter, even after it seemed it ought to be completed. If, however, the Lord of the Ninth is in the first house, whether the Lord of the First aspects it or the Moon or not, whatever the disposition of the Lord of the First or the Moon may be, or if the Lord of the Ninth is joined to the Lord of the First—that is, he becomes lighter than it and joins to it—it signifies the attainment of the thing sought without doubt, even without the petition of the seeker. But if the Lord of the Ninth is not in the first, nor joined to the Lord of the First, but is joined to **Jupiter** or even the **Sun** by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect, and Jupiter or the Sun is then in the first house, it signifies the attainment of that matter with little labor. If, moreover, that pre-conjunction is with reception and the aforementioned aspects, the thing sought will come to him from unexpected sources—namely, by grace while he is sitting in his own house. If, however, the aspect is a **square**, it will not come to him so easily, even if it is with reception; and it will happen because the reception intervened, even if the receiver who is in the first house has no power there; and even more, if the Lord of the Ninth receives the Lord of the First or the Moon, from whatever place that reception may be (even if from a **cadent house** <note>Houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, traditionally considered the weakest positions in a chart.</note>), it signifies the completion of the matter sought. If, however, it is not...

Look if any of the planets transfers light between the **Lord of the First** <note>The planet ruling the sign on the eastern horizon (the Ascendant), representing the person asking the question.</note> and the **Lord of the Ninth** <note>The planet ruling the ninth house, which governs the specific matter being asked about here.</note>, for this signifies the attainment of the matter. This is because the matter is mediated by a great messenger or intermediary, unless the planet to which the "translator" gives the light is more powerful. If the one who receives the light from the lighter planet commits its disposition <note>term: disposition; the "authority" or "management" of a planet's influence in a chart</note> to another, it signifies a loss, and afterwards they will believe the matter is being completed. But if the Lord of the First is not joined to the Lord of the Ninth, but seeks it out and joins it before any other planet cuts off their light, it signifies the perfection of the matter through persistence and urgent effort.

And if none of these things I have told you occur, but there is a **translation of light** <note>term: translation of light; when a fast-moving planet like the Moon separates from one planet and applies to another, "carrying" the influence between them</note> through many planets from one to another, the matter will eventually be completed, but not without great complication, entanglement, quarreling, attention, many words, involvements, and threats from both sides, accompanied by much noise and discord.

However, if the Lord of the First is joined to a **malefic** <note>term: malefic; a "bad-acting" planet, usually Saturn or Mars, thought to bring difficulty</note> that does not "receive" him, and that malefic is not the Lord of the Ninth, nor has it committed its disposition to any planet that receives the Lord of the First or the Moon, then the sought-after matter will not be completed. But if that malefic planet commits its disposition to a **fortune** <note>term: fortune; a "good-acting" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</note> that is in a good place relative to the Ascendant, it will complete the matter. The prediction regarding malefics is that they do not complete a matter unless they "receive" the other planet; but if there is reception, they complete it, though not easily. 

And know this: whichever other planet signifies the effect of a matter, if it is in an **angle** <note>term: angle; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful and active positions in a chart</note>, it hastens the matter. If it is in a **succedent house** <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses, which are moderate in power.</note>, it delays them. If, however, it is in a **cadent house** <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, considered the weakest positions.</note>, it postpones them, although it may complete them later—except for certain cases which are not relevant here. You should understand these and similar things that are said here.

Look also if any malefic planet regards the Lord of the First or the Moon by a **square aspect** <note>An angle of 90 degrees, considered stressful.</note> or by **opposition** <note>An angle of 180 degrees, the most difficult aspect.</note> without reception. Unless it then commits its disposition, it will impede the seeker or the Moon. The seeker will become angry and troubled with the person who involved themselves in handling that matter, will become an enemy to them, and it will be clear that they are not working faithfully. If, however, the aspect is a **trine** <note>120 degrees; harmonious.</note> or a **sextile** <note>60 degrees; helpful.</note>, the seeker will not be angry with them, even if they do not complete the matter.

If both the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Ninth commit their dispositions to some planet by any aspect that is neither impeded nor turns **retrograde** <note>term: retrograde; when a planet appears to move backward, signifying delays or reversals</note> before it leaves the sign in which it is, it signifies the fulfillment of the matter. If the Moon is "received" from the place where she is and is free from malefics and all other impediments, it signifies the attainment of the sought-after matter, and that the seeker will have many helpers to complete what they intend. 

If the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Ninth are joined together to some planet, and neither of them is impeded, and the Moon commits her disposition to one of them, it signifies the matter will be entirely completed. But if there is an impediment, it will not. And this happens not only in this case, but in any matter: when the Lord of the First joins the Lord of the sought-after matter and the Moon commits her disposition to one of them, the matter is fully completed. If the Moon does not commit her disposition to one of them, but is received by some planet and they are joined together as was said, it signifies the completion of the matter, though more slowly.

Say the same if the Lord of the Ninth joins the Lord of the Fourth, and the Lord of the Fourth joins the Lord of the First: it signifies the matter will be completed according to the inquiry and without great labor. If the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Fourth, and the Lord of the Fourth is joined to the Lord of the Ninth, it also signifies the completion of the sought-after matter, yet with maximum labor, hardship, slowness, and complication, so that the seeker will despair of completing it, though it will be completed in the end. 

Once you know the matter is attained and you wish to know something else regarding the outcomes, you shall judge it by the ninth house, according to what you find below in the judgment of travel <note>original: "perege"; likely referring to the section on journeys</note> and by the tenth house: namely, whether they will attain it or not, and what ought to happen to them from it. In all these things, follow those footsteps, for everything will be explained more broadly there.

## Chapter 11. Regarding a letter or rumor that will come, and whether the news in the letter is good or not.

There are sometimes certain business dealings in various places about which the truth is unknown to some, and they desire

<column-break/>

to know something about it. They might ask an astrologer, saying: "When will we know news of such business?" or perhaps expecting that another letter will come to them from some part, they ask, "When will such a letter arrive?" 

Look then at the **First** and **Second houses**, and see if **Mercury** <note>The planet of communication and messages.</note> is in the First or in the Second, so near the end of the Second that it seeks to enter the "belly" of the First <note>A figurative term for the start of the house.</note>—that is, within one or two degrees in the Second house, coming toward the First. Or, if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the First, or the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Moon's house, or vice versa. Or if Mercury is the Lord of the First, as seen by the "pack-bearer" <note>original: "sarcinatori"; possibly a specific technical term for the querent or the person delivering the question.</note>, it signifies the arrival of the letter or rumor concerning the matter sought. 

And it is said that if Mercury is not in the First, the hour when the letter or rumor arrives will be the hour in which Mercury enters the Ascendant. If the Moon joins Mercury, it will come at the hour they join, or the hour the Moon reaches the Ascendant. And if this is not the case, look at the significators: if the Moon receives light or nature from Mercury in the degree of the Ascendant or from its Lord, the time of the letter or rumor's arrival will be when the Moon reaches the Lord of the Ascendant or the Ascendant itself, as the same wise man shows.

->¶ If you wish to know when the letter was written.<-

And if you wish to know how long ago that letter was written, or how long ago the messenger who carries the rumor began their journey: look from which planet the Moon is separating, and see by how many degrees she has distanced herself from it. See if she is in an **angle**, and if the planet from which she is separated is likewise in an angle; this signifies that it has been that many **months**. If they are in a **succedent house**, it signifies **weeks**. If they are in a **cadent house**, it signifies that many **days**. 

And if you wish to know when it will arrive: see to which planet the Moon is joining, and how many degrees are between her and the one she joins. According to that number, assign months, weeks, or days, using the same distributions mentioned before.

## Chapter 12. If someone is ignorant of to whom a letter is sent and what their status is.

Sometimes one is ignorant of to whom a letter or rumor is being sent, and is afraid to open the writings or the letter. Look at the Ascendant at the hour of that inquiry and see to what planet the Moon is joining; for by her conjunction with the planets, you will be able to know the nature of the person to whom the letter is sent.

If the Moon joins **Saturn**, it is sent to an old man, or a Jew, or a religious person wearing black or dark-ish clothes, or a common person like a farmer or someone similar. 

But if she joins **Jupiter**, it is sent to a noble or a high religious official like a bishop and similar people, or a judge, or a great, wealthy, and famous merchant. 

And if she is joined to **Mars**, it is sent to some leader of an army or some warlike soldier. 

And if she is joined to the **Sun**, it is sent to a king or some magnate of those suited for a kingdom, or another famous man. 

And if she is joined to **Venus**, it is sent to a famous woman, or a beautiful one, or a lover. 

And if she is joined to **Mercury**, it is sent to someone skilled in writing and documents, or a judge who is not very famous, or a merchant, or a young man. 

You can also know the rank of the persons through the Moon's location. For the more she is in a greater and stronger place, the more it signifies the higher status of the persons. For instance, if she is in her **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's influence is heightened.</note> and in an **angle**, it signifies the highest status of the aforementioned persons. If in exaltation but not in an angle, it will be something just below that. If in her **house** <note>The sign a planet rules.</note> and in an angle, it will be a bit lower again. If in her house but not in an angle, lower still. **Triplicity** is much lower than being in its house; a **Term** is lower than triplicity; and a **Face** is lower than a term <note>These are "essential dignities," levels of planetary strength.</note>. And if she is not in any of her dignities, the person will be of low status.

# Chapter 13. What a letter may contain, whether good or evil.

Great lords and nobles are sometimes accustomed to wanting to take some form of revenge upon others. However, to avoid infamy, they sometimes send them to other people who might carry out that revenge, giving these messengers their letters or epistles, telling them to go to certain places and certain men so that they might be provided for—sometimes as a reward for service, and sometimes for other reasons. And it is sometimes contained in these letters that those carrying the letters should be rewarded for their service; at other times, that they should be punished for their misdeeds by others, such as being hanged, beheaded, or mutilated, and the like. If anyone, doubting whether a letter contains something sinister, asks to be informed by an astrologer about what is contained in the letter, look at the point of the hour of the interrogation <note>The "point of the hour" refers to the Ascendant, the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the question is asked.</note> and see where **Mercury** is, who is the general significator <note>term: significator; the planet that represents a specific person or topic in a chart</note> of all writings.

See from which planet he separates <note>term: separation; when a faster planet moves away from an aspect with a slower one, indicating a past event or existing condition</note>; for the meaning of the letter belongs to him alone, and the **Moon** does not participate with him in this except very rarely. Rather, the Moon herself signifies rumors, and especially those without writing, while writings are given to Mercury. If he separates from a **Fortune** <note>term: Fortune; a benefic or "lucky" planet, specifically Jupiter or Venus</note>, the letter contains good, and that the person will be rewarded for the service he performed. If, however, he separates from a **Malefic** <note>term: Malefic; a "bad-acting" planet, specifically Saturn or Mars</note>, the letter contains evil.

Then see if Mercury is in the **Ascendant** <note>The First House, representing the person asking the question.</note>, or if that malefic from which he separates signifies evil to the person of the seeker. If he is in the **Second House**, it signifies harm to his substance <note>Wealth or personal possessions.</note>. If he is in the **Third**, it signifies evil for a brother or those things signified by the third house, and so on for the rest. If he is in the **Fourth**, it signifies evil for his superior, his father, etc. If he is in the **Fifth**, it signifies evil for a son, etc. If he is in the **Sixth**, it signifies evil for a servant, etc. If he is in the **Seventh**, it signifies evil for a wife, etc. If in the **Eight**, it has no certain signification except that sometimes it could signify consumption or death. Nor is it necessary in the **Ninth**. In the **Tenth**, <unclear>illegible</unclear>. But if he is in the **Eleventh**, it signifies evil for a friend, etc. And if he is in the **Twelfth**, it signifies the loss of horses and oxen.

And if the Moon is then afflicted <note>term: afflicted; hindered by a bad relationship with a malefic planet</note> and is in **Aries**, it signifies his deception or cutting. If she is in **Taurus**, it signifies his beheading—especially if she is joined to **Mars**. If she is in **Gemini**, it signifies the cutting off of hands. If she is in **Cancer**, **Leo**, **Virgo**, or **Libra**, it signifies a beating. If she is in **Scorpio**, it signifies harm to the genitals. If she is in **Sagittarius**, **Capricorn**, or **Aquarius**, it signifies his imprisonment. And if she is in **Pisces**, it signifies the cutting off of his feet. If, however, the Moon is free and safe from affliction, there will be safety for all the significators of that house in which she resides.

->What the letter responds.<-

If the letter is about something other than the predicted matters, such as when one expects a response to be made to him, and you wish to know whether a response will be made to the pleasure of the sender: then look to see if **Mercury** or the **Moon**—for the Moon has a place here—are both joined to Fortunes. If so, the letter will respond to the pleasure of the sender. If, however, one of them is joined to a Fortune and the other is not, it will respond to him in part, but not according to his will. But if both are **void of course** <note>term: void of course; when a planet makes no further aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign, indicating "nothing will come of it."</note>, nothing will respond to him. And it seemed to **Zael** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician whose works were foundational to Western medieval astrology.</note> that you ought to judge the response of the letter by the second conjunction rather than the first.

->Whether a letter is sealed or not.<-

And if you wish to know the truth of any letter that is desired, and you wish to know whether it has been obtained or not: look at the Moon. If she is in conjunction with Mercury so that she is distant from him by one degree or less, it signifies that the letter is already obtained but is not yet

<column-break/>

sealed; however, it will be sealed. But if the Moon is then separated from Mercury by 59 minutes or less, it signifies that the letter is already sealed. If, however, you find Mercury joined to the **Sun** or separated from him up to the limit of three degrees or less, it signifies it is obtained and that it will be sealed; but if he has passed him by 3 degrees, it will neither be sealed nor is it obtained.

->From whom the letter comes or to whom it is sent.<-

And if you wish to know from whom a letter comes or is sent, look at Mercury. If you find he has passed the Sun or the Lord of the Tenth <note>The house of kings and high authorities.</note> or the Tenth house itself by 15 minutes or less, it signifies that the letter comes from a king or from a great noble of those, namely, who are fit for a kingdom. If, however, Mercury is joined to any of the aforementioned, it signifies the letter was sent to a king or a great noble aforementioned.

# Chapter 14. On rumors, whether they are true or not: and when they are entirely true, and when they are entirely false, and when they are part true and part false.

It seemed to some that the chapter on rumors should be placed among the chapters of the **Twelfth House**, and they held this consideration because rumors are for the most part found to be different than they were reported; and when truth is believed to be in them, a lie is found instead, though sometimes they are true. To me, however, it seems that the chapter on rumors should be placed under the **Ninth House**, because for the most part they come from afar, and one does not know immediately upon hearing them whether it is as they say or not. And this signifies that yet another new event might be expected from a distant place, which confirms in a way a journey and a long distance. You, however, may take whichever of these you wish.

When you are questioned about any rumor, whether it be true or false—or you hear the rumor yourself and wish to inquire into its truth—look at the **Ascendant** at the hour of the interrogation or the announcement of the rumor, or at the **Moon**. See which of them is stronger and work through that one. For that one is stronger which is in an **Angle** <note>term: Angle; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> and free from malefics. If, however, neither of them is in the angles, see if the Ascendant is a **fixed sign** <note>term: fixed sign; Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and endurance.</note> and the other angles as well; for if it is so, it signifies the truth of the rumors, unless the Lord of the First or the Moon or the other of them are joined with **Saturn** or **Mars** without reception <note>term: reception; when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting, suggesting cooperation.</note> or are with the **Tail** <note>term: Tail; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of decrease or misfortune.</note>.

Next, consider whatever the Ascendant may be: if **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, **Venus**, or the **Head of the Dragon** <note>term: Head of the Dragon; the North Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of increase or good fortune.</note> is there, it signifies the truth of the rumors. If none of these is in the first house, consider the **Third**. And if you do not find any in the third, consider the **Fifth**. And if you do not find any in the fifth, consider the **Ninth**. And if in any of these places you find any of the aforementioned planets which are truth-tellers, it signifies the truth of the rumors, even if the planet is solitary, provided it is not so afflicted. Nevertheless, the Sun, on account of his own brilliance, does not have as much signification over rumors as the other Fortunes do; for his role is to show a certainty that is not easily found in rumors.

If, however, you do not find any of the said planets in any of the predicted places, you are not certain whether the rumors are true or not. See if you find **Saturn** or **Mars** in any of the predicted places, or the Tail; it signifies the falsehood of the rumors, even if they are solitary. Consider furthermore, as I said, if the Lord of the First is in an angle free from malefics and is not joined with any planet that is falling from an angle <note>term: cadent; falling away from an angle, indicating weakness.</note>, it signifies the truth of the rumors. And if it is not so regarding the Lord of the First as I told you with the premises, you shall consider the Moon; if you find her in an angle and free, and she is not joined to a planet falling from an angle, it signifies the truth of the rumors, and even more strongly if she is received. Likewise, if the Lord of the First is in a succeeding angle <note>term: succedent; the houses following the angles (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th), which have moderate strength.</note> or even in a cadent house, and the Moon is with some planet that is in an angle and if a Fortu...

If, however, that malefic <note>original: "malus"; in astrology, the "malefics" are typically Mars and Saturn, planets associated with challenge or hardship</note> planet to which the lord of the first <note>term: lord of the first; the planet that rules the zodiac sign on the cusp of the first house, representing the person asking the question</note> is joined is neither retrograde <note>term: retrograde; the apparent backward motion of a planet, often signaling delays or reversals</note> nor combust <note>term: combust; when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden</note> and has "received" him <note>term: reception; a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting cooperation</note>, the rumors will be true. If a benefic planet <note>original: "fortuna"; typically Jupiter or Venus, planets associated with luck and success</note> is in an angle and the lord of the first joins it, or the one who joins it receives him and is not hindered, know then that all those rumors are entirely true; you need not seek or consider anything else but that alone. This is especially and primarily true if the planet to which the lord is joined is in the 10th house <note>the 10th house represents the highest point of the sky, associated with public truth and visibility</note>, for then they will be true from every side and in all their parts without any reduction—indeed, perhaps there will be more to those rumors than is even being said. 

¶ Understand the same regarding the Moon as I have told you regarding the lord of the first. You shall also see if the lord of the first or the Moon is joined to any planet that is in an angle and has committed its disposition to it; this signifies the truth of the rumors. And see if the planet to which the lord of the first or the Moon commits its disposition is in the 1st house; in that case, those rumors had already been heard and something of them had been said in that land before you heard them or before the question was put to you as to whether they were true or not. And if it is in the 4th house, nothing has yet sounded in that land regarding those rumors; rather, they were still in secret. And if it is in the 7th house, those rumors have already been named almost publicly. And if it is in the 10th house, even if you perhaps did not know those rumors, they are already openly divulged, and the truth of them is known among the people of that region.

### ¶ When rumors are not true.

If the lord of the first or the Moon is in an angle and is joined to a planet that is falling from an angle <note>cadent</note>, the rumors will be false, unless that falling planet is a benefic and receives the lord or the Moon; in that case, something was said about them so that it seemed to be so. If it is a benefic and receives him or the Moon, it signifies the truth of the rumors, though they may not be entirely true, as has been said. And if that falling planet does not receive the lord of the first or the Moon—or if it is a malefic, whether it receives the lord of the first or the Moon or not—the rumors will be false, even if something is said of them, and nothing will come of them in reality. 

If the lord of the first or the Moon itself is joined to a malefic planet which is hindered <note>meaning retrograde or combust</note>, it signifies that the rumors are false and that they will quickly be suppressed. But if that malefic is not hindered and receives the lord of the first or the Moon, it signifies some degree of truth in the rumors, though they are not entirely true. 

¶ However, Zahel <note>Zahel is the Latinized name for Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were central to medieval European practice</note> said that you ought to look at the lord of the ascendant and the Moon, and see which of them is stronger, and by that one you should judge the matter of the rumors. Thus, his intention was not to place weight except on one of them. ¶ To me, however, it seems that if we can use both lords—namely, the lord of the first and the Moon—we should do so; yet it does not seem to me that we should abandon his footsteps. 

¶ You should also look to see whether the angles are in movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; these signs represent change and instability</note>; for as far as this is concerned, they signify the rumors to be false. For just as when the angles are in fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> they signify the truth of the rumors, so when they are in movable signs they signify the falsehood of the rumors. And the rumors will be more truly lying if the lord of the first or the Moon is joined with any malefic through conjunction or aspect, unless perhaps it is received with a perfect reception <note>by house or exaltation</note>; and even with this, there will be little truth in those rumors. But if that malefic is retrograde, the rumors will be false, whether he himself or the lord of the first or the Moon is in an angle or outside an angle—whichever of them is with him then—and whether the angles are in fixed signs or not, and whether he is received or 

<column-break/>

not, the rumors will nonetheless be false. 

¶ And Zahel said that if the Moon is hindered in an angle and is joined to any malefic planet that does not receive her, the rumors will be false. And see if the lord of the first or the Moon, or either of them, is joined to any hindered planet—that is, retrograde or combust—or even a non-retrograde one which, since it does not receive, signifies the falsehood of the rumors, even if it is said by everyone indifferently that those rumors are true and it is believed by everyone to be so. 

However, you must see or consider the nature of the rumors you have heard or about which a question has been put to you. For if they are about things signified by and involving weapons and fire and the shedding of blood and the cutting off of roads and the like, and **Mars** is there as the lord who signifies that. And if it is about the destruction of a house or a castle or a city and similar things, and the **Tail** <note>term: the Tail; also known as Cauda Draconis or the South Node of the Moon, usually a point of loss or destruction</note> is there, it signifies that the rumors have some weight. And if it is about drowning or a fall from a great height, and **Saturn** or even the Tail is there, it signifies that very same thing. And understand this regarding the significations of every planet, and more strongly if there are signs in those houses that agree with those natures.

### ¶ Concerning the Tenth House.

### ¶ The first chapter regarding a kingdom, or empire, or dukedom, or earldom, or any other lay dignity, whereby the questioner has hope or confidence of attaining it: whether they will attain what they intend or not.

**M**en are sometimes accustomed to desire dignities or kingdoms—namely, dukedoms or earldoms or other lay dignities or offices or bailiwicks <note>term: bailiwick (baylia); an area of administrative jurisdiction or the office of a bailiff</note>. Whence they ask an astrologer whether they are to attain what they intend or not. And if any question is put to you regarding any of the aforesaid—whether it be an empire, a kingdom, a dukedom, a governorship, a judgeship, a senate seat, or any other office or dignity, whether great or small; even the guardianship of some castle or some city gate, provided it comes by way of an office or bailiwick—the first house is given to the seeker, and the tenth house is given to the kingdom, office, dignity, or bailiwick. 

Look then to the lord of the first and the Moon: if both are joined to the Sun or to the lord of the tenth <note>the planet ruling the sign on the 10th house cusp</note>, which has the signification of the dignity or office—or even if only one of them is, and that lord of the tenth aspects the tenth house or is in it—it signifies that the seeker will have what he intends. But it will not be for free; rather, it will be necessary for him to labor and study and inquire by all means possible so that he may attain what is sought. 

If, however, neither of them is joined to the lord of the tenth, but the lord of the first or the Moon is in the tenth, he will attain what he intends, provided the lord of the first or the Moon are not hindered—that is, that they are not combust, and that the planet is not retrograde, and that malefic planets do not aspect it by opposition or the fourth aspect <note>term: fourth aspect; a square aspect (90 degrees), considered a point of friction or difficulty</note> without reception. For then it signifies the dissolution of the matter, even if it seemed direct and as though it ought to be completed. 

If, however, the lord of the tenth is in the first, whether the lord of the first or the Moon aspects him or not, and whatever the lord of the first may be then—or if the lord of the tenth is joined to the lord of the first house so that it goes to its conjunction (that is, the lord of the tenth is the lighter planet)—it signifies without a doubt the attainment of the empire, kingdom, magistracy, lay dignity, office, or bailiwick without any petition of his own, or his own labor, or any importunity. And if the lord of the tenth is not in the first, nor joined to the lord of the first, but is joined to **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or the **Sun** by aspect (without an opposition to the Sun, for in others the opposition does not hinder as it does with the Sun), and that planet to which the lord of the tenth is joined is in the first house, he will attain the sought-after thing with ease.
