<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for astrological interrogations concerning the Tenth House, which governs social status, power, and high-ranking offices. It focuses on whether a seeker will obtain a desired position or "magistracy" based on the relationships between the planets representing the seeker (the first house) and the goal (the tenth house).</meta>

If indeed the Moon and Mars or Saturn <note>original: "marti vel saturno"; the two traditional "malefic" or challenging planets</note> are in the first house, and the Ascendant <note>term: Ascendant; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the seeker</note> is in a house or exaltation <note>term: exaltation; a sign where a planet's influence is particularly strengthened</note> belonging to them, and they are oriental <note>term: oriental; appearing in the sky before the Sun rises</note> and moving in direct motion, and neither is in opposition to the other, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought. However, this may involve complex entanglements, much petitioning, or persistence—though sometimes with little or no trouble at all. And it seemed to Messahala <note>original: "Messahala"; Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a prominent Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer</note> that whether a malefic planet "receives" <note>term: reception; a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting cooperation</note> the other or not, the matter will be completed. If the aspect <note>term: aspect; the geometric angle between planets that determines how they interact</note> is a trine or a sextile <note>note: trines (120°) and sextiles (60°) are considered harmonious and helpful aspects</note>, and a benefic planet <note>original: "fortuna"; a "fortune" or lucky planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</note> is in the first house, the seeker will obtain their request without even having to ask. 

If there is a square or opposition <note>note: these are challenging aspects of 90° or 180°</note>, or if the planet is a malefic but in a trine or sextile aspect, the goal will still be reached, but with more gentleness. If it is in opposition and is an infortune <note>a malefic planet</note>, the goal will be reached though with harshness and delay. All these things hold true whether the planet in the first house or the Moon has "testimony" <note>astrological evidence or strength</note> there or not. Furthermore, the Moon is related to the tenth house. Messahala also said that if the Lord of the Tenth <note>term: Lord of the Tenth; the planet that rules the sign on the cusp of the tenth house, representing the office or honor sought</note> receives the Lord of the First or the Moon, from whatever place that reception occurs, the matter will be completed with goodness, stability, utility, and profit. 

If none of these things I have told you occur, see if there is any planet that "transfers light" <note>term: translation of light; when a faster-moving planet connects two slower planets by forming an aspect with each in succession</note> between the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Tenth. If so, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought, though not through the seeker themselves, but through the intervention and help of an intermediary who manages the matter until it is finished. It will be completed unless the one who receives the power <note>original: "dispositionem"</note> of the other joins with a third party to whom he then commits that power; for that signifies the dissolution of the matter just when it was thought to be settled. But if he does not commit the power to anyone else, and is not retrograde or combust, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought. 

Similarly, if the Lord of the Tenth does not seek a conjunction with the Lord of the First, but the Lord of the First seeks a conjunction with the Lord of the Tenth and joins with it before any other planet cuts off their connection, the matter will be accomplished—but not without the petition and the persistent, urgent pressure of the seeker. Likewise, if the Lord of the Tenth does not join the Lord of the First, nor the First to the Tenth, and neither joins with a benefic planet, but instead joins with a malefic, and that malefic joins another malefic, and that second malefic joins a benefic, and that benefic finally joins the Lord of the Tenth—or if that final planet joins the Lord of the First—it signifies the attainment of the thing sought. However, this will happen through many intermediaries and various different people. You can identify these people through the houses ruled by those planets through which the connection is made, link by link, until the connection reaches the significator of the thing sought, or the Lord of the First or Tenth, as was said, even if that connection passes through all seven planets. 

Messahala said the same thing occurs in a conjunction by body <note>term: conjunction by body; when two planets are at the same degree of the zodiac, literally standing together</note>. He also said that if there is no conjunction between the Lord of the Midheaven <note>the tenth house</note> and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, and there is no planet transferring light between them, you must look at which planet is stronger. If it does not join the Lord of the Midheaven but joins another, provided it is stronger in an "angle" <note>term: angle; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful areas of a chart</note> or a strong place, it completes the thing sought, whether it receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon or not. He said that if the planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins is a malefic, but it receives him, the matter will be completed. If it is a malefic and is not the Lord of the Midheaven, and does not receive the Lord of the Ascendant, and that malefic does not commit its power to another planet, then the matter will not be completed, because that malefic destroys the matter. But if that malefic commits its power to another malefic, and that second malefic receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, the thing sought will be completed. If that malefic commits its power to a benefic planet in a strong place, it will be completed. Also, look if any planet mentioned is in the first or tenth house: if it is a benefic, it signifies the comple-

<column-break/>

-tion of the matter, whether it receives the significator or not, and the seeker will profit and increase their knowledge for that reason. If, however, it is a malefic and receives the Lord of the First or the Moon, the matter will be completed; but if it does not receive them, it will not. If the house or exaltation of that malefic planet is the tenth house and the malefic itself is in it, the matter will also be completed, whether that malefic receives the Lord of the First or the Moon or not. This is just as if a benefic were in the tenth house and the Lord of the First or the Moon aspected it: the matter would be completed whether that benefic received the Lord of the First or the Moon or not, and whether it had dignity in the tenth house or not. 

And you should know this: whichever planet is the significator of a matter, if it is in an angle, it hastens the effect; in a "succedent" house <note>houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which follow the angles</note>, it delays; in a "cadent" house <note>houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, which fall away from the angles</note>, it postpones, though it may eventually complete the matter. And see if a malefic aspects the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon from an opposition or a square aspect without reception; for unless it then commits its power to another, the seeker will be hindered and troubled by the one who interfered by disparaging the matter, and the seeker will not believe that person to be working faithfully; it is even possible that enemies will be made from this. If the aspect is a trine or sextile, the seeker will not be angry with them nor blame them, even if the matter is not completed. 

If the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Tenth commit their power to any planet from any aspect, whether with or without reception, and whether it be a benefic or a malefic—provided it is not retrograde, nor combust, nor cadent, and does not leave the sign it is in before the conjunction of those two (the Lord of the First and Tenth) with it is completed—and if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the First or Tenth, the seeker will obtain what they asked for. But if there is a "collection of light" <note>term: collection of light; when two planets do not aspect each other but both aspect a third, slower-moving planet</note> or power of the Lord of the First and Tenth as I described, but the Moon does not aspect either of those two, but instead aspects another planet that receives her by house, exaltation, or two other "dignities" <note>term: dignities; the various signs and degrees where a planet has strength or "rights"</note>, and she is not otherwise hindered (meaning she is free from "fall" <note>the sign opposite a planet's exaltation</note> and combustion, and not besieged by malefics, nor in opposition or square to them without reception), this signifies the attainment of the thing sought. It also shows that many people will help the seeker to complete the matter they request. 

Almost all the wise masters of astrological judgments agree that when the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Thing Sought are joined together, and the Moon commits her power to one of them, the thing sought is completed entirely. If she does not commit power to either of them, but the Moon is joined to a planet that does not receive her, and that planet aspects the house of the thing sought or aspects the house of the Lord [of the First], it signifies that the seeker will obtain a portion of what they asked for, though not the whole, if the matter is something that can be divided. 

And Zahel <note>original: "zahel"; Sahl ibn Bishr (c. 786–845 AD), a Jewish philosopher and astrologer</note> said that when the Lord of the Ascendant receives the power of the Moon, the petition for a "kingdom" <note>meaning high office or great power</note> will be easier; that is, he will obtain it more easily. If, however, the planet to which the Moon or the Lord of the First commits power is hindered—that is, if it is retrograde, combust, cadent, or besieged by two malefics, or in opposition or square to them without reception—it signifies the matter will not be completed. 

Next, look if the Lord of the First House is joined to the Lord of the Fourth House, and the Lord of the Fourth is joined to the Lord of the First; the thing sought will be completed for the seeker without great labor. If, however, the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Fourth, and the Lord of the Fourth is then joined to the Lord of the Tenth, the thing sought will be completed, but only with such great labor, hardship, entanglement, and delay that the seeker will despair of ever being able to finish what they intended; yet, in the end, it will be completed for them.

### ### Where his magistracy will be.

After you have seen that the seeker is to obtain the dignity, office, or magistracy sought, look at the Lord of the First and see if it is in its own house...

And if it is so, know that he will obtain that magistracy <note>term: magistracy; a high-ranking public office or position of authority</note> or that dignity in the land where he lives. And if the planet is in its exaltation <note>term: exaltation; a specific sign of the zodiac where a planet's influence is at its highest potential</note>, he will obtain a magistracy to which other magistracies and other offices are subordinate. That dignity will either encompass other dignities within itself or have others beneath it, whether he obtains this in his own land or in a foreign one—though it does not seem it should be very far from his own land. If, however, the planet is in its triplicity <note>term: triplicity; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</note>, it appears that he is to obtain a great office or magistracy outside the land in which he lives, and far from it, perhaps more than a day's journey away.

And if it is in its term <note>term: term; a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note>, he will not acquire a great office; rather, it will be lower than those mentioned above. It may happen that this comes to him because of kinship <note>original: "consanguineitatis"</note> between himself and the one who is commissioned to grant that office. Or perhaps one of his kinsmen named him to the person responsible for giving the office, and for that reason, he will be chosen and established over that kingdom or office. Or perhaps he will choose one of his kinsmen for some office and commit it to him.

And if the planet is in its face <note>term: face; the smallest subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</note>, this will happen to him because of his own mastery or his wisdom, and that office will be lower than the ones mentioned above. If, however, the planet has no dignity in the place where it is located, that dignity will be given to him in a land where few or almost no one knows him, and that office, dignity, or bailiwick <note>original: "baylia"; a legal or administrative jurisdiction</note> will be much lower than those described. 

And if the Lord of the First <note>term: Lord of the First; the planet ruling the Ascendant, representing the person asking the question</note> and the Lord of the Tenth <note>term: Lord of the Tenth; the planet ruling the house of career and status, representing the office itself</note> are the same planet—which can happen with Jupiter and Mercury—and it is received by another planet somewhere, and the Moon is joined to it from one of the angles <note>term: angles; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of an astrological chart</note>, it signifies the attainment of the thing sought. 

If, however, the Moon is not joined to the Lord of the First, but is joined to another who receives her, and the Lord of the First is himself received, and neither of them is falling away from an angle nor from the Ascendant, he will obtain from the kingdom a portion of those things he sought (if the matter is divisible), but not the whole.

### ¶ When the thing sought will not be obtained.

If the Moon is impeded <note>term: impeded; weakened by a harsh aspect from a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</note> and the Lord of the First is not received, and neither of them is in the house of the thing sought, the seeker will not obtain what he asked for. It appears the cause for not obtaining it is that he seeks a thing that is not suitable for him. 

If, however, the Lord of the First or the Moon does not aspect the Lord of the Tenth, and the Lord of the Tenth does not aspect either of them, and the angles are fixed signs <note>term: fixed signs; Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability or stagnation</note>, and there is none of the aforementioned aspects signifying the completion of the matter, then look to where the Sun is and where Venus is. See if both aspect the Tenth House and if both are received; for if it is so, it signifies the completion of the matter, and that the seeker will acquire the kingdom or magistracy in which he has trust. It will be useful and profitable for him, and he will acquire much money from it. 

If, however, both are not received but only one of them, see if the Moon then aspects the one who was not received; if so, the thing sought will be perfected, because the Moon commits her disposition and her strength to the one she joins. 

Look also at the Moon: if she aspects the degree of the Tenth House, or even if the Lord of the First aspects the degree of the Tenth House, or if one of them is in it, or if the Lord of the Tenth House is in that very degree of the Ascendant, it signifies that the choice has already been made, and news of that election will quickly reach him. 

And Messahala and Zahel <note>original: "messahala [et] zahel"; Masha'allah and Sahl ibn Bishr, two highly influential 8th and 9th-century astrologers</note> said that if the Moon is joined to the light of the Lord of the Midheaven <note>term: Midheaven; the cusp of the Tenth House, the highest point in the chart</note>, or passes over him so that she is north of him while passing through his rays, or is joined to his body and aspects the Midheaven, he will obtain it. If the Lord of the house in which the Moon is located receives her and both aspect the Tenth, he will obtain the request. And if the Moon is in some sign in which there is the light of some planet, but she does not join to that body before she leaves the sign she is in, the matter will not be perfected—unless the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Tenth (or of another thing sought) are both in a place where they have

<column-break/>

dignity and aspect the Tenth House or the place of the thing sought. 

And Zahel said that the "overcoming" of the Moon and the Lord of the Midheaven signifies a lessening of the matter in the works of the ancients if the receiver of the Moon's disposition is impeded; this then signifies detriment to the work. And he said that if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Midheaven, it will aid the pursuit. 

But if the receiver and the Lords of the Midheaven strike their strength and disposition against a planet that receives them and has strength in its place and in the matter, but does not aspect the Midheaven, the matter will not be perfected in the way he seeks. And he said that when the significator <note>term: significator; the planet representing a person or object in the chart</note> is "inimical" <note>original: "inimicat[ur]"; acting as an enemy or being poorly placed</note> to its own house, it signifies hardship and entanglement in the petition of the matter. 

Enmity toward its house in this case means being in the twelfth, second, sixth, or eighth house from its own house. And if the Lord of the thing sought aspects it from the seventh house, it signifies that he will not obtain the request; however, it does not totally prohibit it from happening. Rather, it is possible the thing sought may be completed, but if it is perfected, it will be with litigation, controversy, and contention.

### ¶ Chapter Two: Whether he will be praised or blamed on account of the kingdom, office, or magistracy.

After you have learned that the seeker is to obtain the Kingdom or whatever else he intends to acquire, and you wish to know what will happen to him in that kingdom, office, or magistracy, look at the Lord of the First and its location. See how it is disposed, for it must signify what will happen to the seeker from his kingdom or magistracy. 

If you find the Lord of the First in the Tenth, not further than three degrees before the degree of the Tenth House, or at most twelve degrees behind it; or if a benefic planet <note>original: "fortuna"; a lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> is there and not impeded; or if it aspects that place (namely the Tenth) three degrees before and five behind, or at most seven: understand the same if a benefic is not impeded or aspects as has been said of the Tenth. And understand the same of the Eleventh House. This signifies that he will acquire honor and praise from that office or kingdom, provided he is not badly impeded by the aforementioned hindrances—especially if the Dragon's Head <note>term: Dragon's Head; the North Node of the Moon, considered increasing and beneficial</note> is there. But if the Dragon's Tail <note>term: Dragon's Tail; the South Node of the Moon, considered decreasing or challenging</note> is there, it will diminish a third part of that honor. 

If, however, it is in the Eleventh House, it will be less than this, yet his kingdom will go well for him and good things will be said of him. If indeed it is in the First, he will be praised and good will be spoken of him; yet some will strive to speak evil, though they will not make their malice public. If it is in other places and well-disposed, he will retire from his kingdom or office neither with very great honor nor with reproach, but as governors commonly retire from their administrations—provided that malefic planets <note>original: "infortune"; "unfortunes" like Saturn or Mars</note> are not poorly disposed in the aforementioned places. 

If, however, a malefic is in the First or the Tenth and is poorly disposed and has no dignity there, or aspects the Tenth or First as described, and especially if it is retrograde <note>term: retrograde; appearing to move backward in the sky, usually a sign of weakness or reversal</note> or in its fall <note>term: fall; a sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</note>—and even more so if the Dragon's Head is there—it signifies the seeker will be blamed for that reason. 

And if the Lord of the Fourth aspects him and is a malefic by a fourth aspect <note>term: square aspect; a 90-degree angle, typically representing obstacles</note> or by opposition, it signifies that he will be seized and detained for that reason, though without being placed in prison. And if the Lord of the Twelfth aspects him under the conditions mentioned above, he will be imprisoned. And if the Lord of the Eighth also aspects him in the aforesaid manner, he will be confined in prison and it is feared he might die for that reason. And if the Dragon's Tail is there, it will diminish a third part of that blame. 

If a free benefic is in the Second House, it signifies he will acquire wealth for that reason, and profit and good will follow. Or if benefics aspect as was said of the other houses—and it is even better if the Part of Fortune <note>term: Part of Fortune; a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</note> is there. If it is elsewhere, similarly...

### Chapter Three: Again on the same subject and its conclusion.

**A**gain, consider if you find the Lord of the First House <note>term: Lord of the First; the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the horizon, representing the person asking the question</note> in a good place and well-disposed, for it likewise signifies a good end. 
And if it is in the tenth, eleventh, first, or fifth house and not hindered <note>original: "non impeditus"; meaning not negatively affected by difficult planets</note>, whether it is received <note>term: reception; a cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note> or not, or whether it is with the Part of Fortune <note>term: Part of Fortune; a calculated point in a chart representing success and prosperity</note> or not. 
But if it is in the second, third, ninth, or seventh, or even in the fourth—though in the fourth it stays more 

<column-break/>

weakly than in any of the above-mentioned places—and is well-disposed and in no other way hindered, his end will be mediocre, but it will not be something to be abhorred or blamed. 
If, however, it is hindered in any of the five aforementioned places, it signifies hindrance and evil. 
But if it is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, it signifies that he will be deposed from his kingdom or magistracy shamefully and with reproach and disgrace. 
But in the sixth and twelfth houses, it signifies a more serious disgrace than in the eighth, unless the planet is received; for then it signifies that a second-in-command <note>original: "secūdū"</note> or ruler will hinder him and rise up against him to his disgrace—and all the more strongly if the Head is there. 
And if the Tail is there, he will be weak; however, if the planet is received, he will not be hindered; and if it is hindered, he will be freed from that hindrance without great insistence or entanglement. 

And if the planet is not received and is in the three aforementioned houses and is otherwise hindered, something will happen to him after he is deposed that will be a greater loss and greater disgrace than the deposition from his magistracy. 
And if the Lord of the Twelfth House is joined to the Lord of the First House and does not receive him, it signifies that he who was deposed will be bound in chains and disgraced. 
And his disgrace and reproach will be signified much more strongly if that conjunction <note>term: conjunction; when two planets appear at the same point in the sky</note> is in any of the four angles <note>term: angles; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of an astrological chart</note>. 
The tenth house is the most disgraceful of all; for just as it signifies greater honor than the other houses, so if it turns to the opposite, it signifies a bad reputation. For it signifies that he will be put in chains publicly before everyone who wishes to see him, and all who wish to mock him will be able to do so. 

If, however, the conjunction is in the first house, it signifies that he will be bound and there will be a rumor of it, but not as great as when it is in the tenth. 
If the conjunction is in the seventh, it will be his own subjects over whom he was leader or ruler who will put him in prison or chains. 
If the conjunction is in the fourth, he will be put in chains or prison, but there will not be a great public outcry from it. 

If, in addition to this, the Lord of the First House is in a cadent house <note>term: cadent; houses that "fall away" from the angles (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) and are considered weaker</note> and is above the earth <note>note: above the horizon in the chart</note>, even if it is joined with the Lord of the Twelfth, he will not be imprisoned in that land where he was ruler or leader or bailiff or officer; rather, he will be led to another place and imprisoned there. 
But if it is below the earth, he will be bound on the road while being led to his place of detention. 

If, however, the Lord of the First House, once it has separated from the Lord of the Twelfth, makes its first conjunction with the Lord of the Eighth House, it signifies that he will die in that prison. 
But if the Lord of the First is joined to the Lord of the Tenth after it has separated from the Lord of the Twelfth and before it joins another, it signifies that after he has been imprisoned, he will be freed from prison and given another kingdom or office. 
And understand the same if the Lord of the First is joined to Mars; for it signifies that those same things will happen to him that happen when joined to the Lord of the Twelfth—and even more strongly, for Mars signifies scourging and the striking of weapons and the shedding of blood, and sometimes death, which the Lord of the Twelfth does not do. 

And if Mars is not joined bodily with the Lord of the First, but by opposition or by a square aspect, and happens to be the Lord of the Second or Eighth, it signifies that same thing which was said above.

If indeed it is Mars, as I said, that hindrance will be from shackles hurting and tightening around the legs or arms or both with skinning; and he will suffer from irons and be tightened with iron bonds, and perhaps be struck by swords and iron-tipped clubs. If, however, it is...

### Chapter four: when he shall enter into his kingdom
#### or office and shall begin to command or order, what
#### will happen to him in the office.

**A**nd if you wish to know what will happen to him in that kingdom or office: see when he himself enters that office or kingdom, or his own position. And that is the hour of his entry when he is placed in his seat or begins to command, or rather to order and arrange the affairs of the kingdom or office by way of governing the office. If that beginning was by day: look at the lord of the first <note>original: "dominum prime"; the planet that rules the sign on the eastern horizon (the Ascendant) at the moment of taking office</note> and the Sun: if the lord of the first is poorly disposed and the Sun is anywhere then with Saturn, or if it aspects him poorly from a fourth aspect <note>term: fourth aspect; a 90-degree "square" angle, considered stressful or challenging in astrology</note> or from an opposition <note>term: opposition; an 180-degree angle, suggesting direct conflict</note> without perfect reception <note>term: reception; a condition where planets "host" each other in their respective zodiac signs, mitigating negative effects</note>, it signifies his deposition, and there will be a swift removal from that kingdom or office. If, however, you find the lord of the first and the Sun in aspect or conjunction with the "fortunes" <note>term: fortunes; the benefic planets Jupiter and Venus, which bring good luck</note> and they are in the first or tenth or eleventh or fifth [houses], and they are with this in a fixed sign <note>term: fixed sign; signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius that represent stability and endurance</note>, it signifies that the kingdom or office of that person will endure and be prolonged, and he will delight in it: and those things which he desires will happen to him, and he will rejoice and be glad because of them. But if the lord of the first and the Sun are in a bodily conjunction or even in an aspect with Mars without perfect reception as I said, and [Mars] is north of the Sun, or if Mars is in the tenth and the Sun is in the first and the ascending sign is a movable sign <note>term: movable sign; signs like Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn that indicate change or swift action</note>, it signifies that someone will rise up against him from among those whom he has to rule, and will strive to resist him in his kingdom or office; and that king or official will fear that he cannot prevail against him or depose him from his office or rule: and he doubts whether he might be killed or die in another way before he completes his office. If, however, any of the aforesaid things are missing—that is, if Mars is not in the tenth, or the Sun is not in the first, or the ascending sign is not movable—it signifies that that person will not rise up against him: and if he does rise up, he will not be able to prevail against him and will fall. ## Chapter 6: Whether he will remain in this kingdom or office or be removed from it.

And sometimes a person already in an office or governance will ask you, saying: "See if I shall remain in this kingdom or governance or not." Consider the **lord of the first** <note>the planet ruling the person asking</note> and the **lord of the tenth** <note>the planet ruling the office</note> and see if they are joined together by physical conjunction or by any aspect. Look to see if the heavier of them, who is called the **receiver of the disposition** <note>original: "receptor disponis"; the planet that "takes on" the influence of another</note>, is in an angle other than the fourth; if so, tell him that he will not be removed from that office or governance before the due time. 

If, however, that receiver of the disposition is below the earth <note>in the houses beneath the horizon</note> in what is called the "left of the ascendant," it signifies that he will depart from that kingdom or office, but he shall return to it again; and this is more certain if that receiver is **received** <note>meaning the planets are in each other's signs of power</note> in the place where it is at that time, for then it signifies that the return will be swift and honorable. You may say the same thing if the lord of the first is joined to the lord of the third or the ninth, or to a planet in them, and after separating from them it is joined to a planet in an angle other than the fourth: the more this is true, the more his exit from governance will be good, secure, and useful. 

If, however, they are separated from each other so that their contact is already complete and one has passed the other, it signifies a departure from his governance. And if any of them—or the significator, which is the Moon—commits its disposition to any planet in any of the angles except the fourth, and that planet is slow in its course, he will not be removed from that kingdom or governance until that receiver becomes retrograde or enters under the Sun's rays, or until it exits the sign in which it is; that will be the limit of his removal from his governance. 

If, however, the lord of the first is joined to any planet that is in the sign opposite to its exaltation <note>meaning the planet is in its "Fall," a position of weakness</note>, that ruler will behave in that governance in a bad way, so that death is feared for him for that reason. If, moreover, the lord of the house opposite the exaltation of the first lord is joined to him, the men of that kingdom will bear **false testimony** against him, and that falsehood will be believed by those ignorant of the truth, and that belief will remain in their hearts for a long time. But if the lord of the tenth is joined to the lord of the house opposite its exaltation, his kingdom or the land he has to rule will suffer great detriment and depression. 

Furthermore, if the Moon is joined to the lord of the tenth and he is in the tenth, that king or ruler will not be deposed from his governance. And if the lord of the first or the Moon is joined to the lord of the tenth (or either of them), and the lord of the tenth is heavier than them and is in a place well-positioned from the ascendant—namely in the tenth, eleventh, or fifth—and is free from impediments, even if he does not aspect the tenth house itself, he will nevertheless be appointed over another governance.

### Caplm. 7. What the king or ruler will do with the wealth he has gained by reason of his rule.

**I**t happens sometimes to those who come into wealth or profit by reason of a kingdom, government, or office, that they must spend it, sometimes willingly and sometimes against their will. Therefore, if you wish to know on what he is likely to spend it—whether he asks the question himself or another who is interested asks—you must look at it in a different way than in other questions. In this case, you must look at the **Lord of the Second House** <note>original: "oñs sede dom⁹"; the second house traditionally governs personal finances and possessions</note> and see whether it is a **fortune** or an **infortune** <note>a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</note>. 

If it is a fortune and it is **Jupiter**, he will spend it on good works pleasing to God and men: building churches, making peace, founding hospitals or hermitages, and helping the needy with alms and the like. If it is the **Sun**, he will spend it on royal matters of the great and noble, and on things regarding the temporal honor of laymen, or building houses, castles, or towers, and such things that relate to worldly pomp; and also in giving to others out of vainglory and the like. If it is **Venus**, he will spend it on sexual pleasures <note>original: "vsu venereo"</note>, giving to women and performers <note>original: "histriōibus"</note>, on clothing, feasts, eating, and drinking by way of squandering it, and in the exercise of lust. And if Venus is then **elevated** over Saturn—that is, if she is north of him—it signifies that he will shamefully spend part of his money indulging in that foul and horrendous **sodomitical vice** <note>astrologers of this era often linked specific planetary configurations to what they considered deviant behaviors</note>. 

And if it is **Mercury**, he will spend it on things from which he expects profit, such as marketable goods and in buying and selling things that turn over quickly; his whole intention will be on profit, and he will make most of his expenditures by way of trade. And if it is the **Moon**, and she is in her light <note>increasing in visibility</note> or **void of course**, he will spend that substance to no personal benefit and will dissipate it, not knowing how or on what, until he has consumed it by way of squandering. If she is not void of course, he will spend it according to the nature of the planet to which the Moon is joined. 

But if it is **Saturn**, he will spend it unjustly and will always fear that this way of spending will be harmful to him; he will be distressed about it and will strive to spend to the harm of others, as if to be dreaded <note>original: "venerandi"</note>, and it will go badly for those with whom he deals and with whom he involves himself. And if it is **Mars**, he will spend it on every crime and on unjust and evil work, such as wars, stirrings of rumors, causing arson, bloodshed, fornications, and in the service of a friend by way of making war and the like.

### Caplm. 8. Concerning someone who is cast out of his kingdom or office, or an absent king: whether he returns to his kingdom or office or not.

**I**f anyone has been cast out from a kingdom, government, or secular office, as sometimes happens; or if any king or duke has absented himself from his kingdom or duchy, as such men are sometimes accustomed to travel far away; and a question is put to you as to whether the absent king returns to his kingdom, or the duke to his duchy, or the one removed from government to his government, or the official to his office, or not: look into this chapter as I tell you. 

If someone asks on behalf of a king whether he returns to his kingdom, or for a duke... that is, when a king or duke is absent, or if someone cast out from an office or government asks for himself, always give him the **First House** <note>the Ascendant</note>—that is, to the king and duke as well as to the one cast out. ### Chapter 9. Whether a kingdom or rule will endure or not: and for how long.

It has been said in the preceding sections whether someone is about to attain a kingdom or not, and whether an absent king is to return to his kingdom or not; the same applies to other leaders or officials cast out from their offices, whether they return to them or not. Now we must discuss if a kingdom or something similar will endure, and for how long. From the moment you have determined the hour of entry into the kingdom—either when he first received it, or when he was confirmed in it—or the hour of the question being asked, you will be able to know the time of its durability in that kingdom or office. You can also know what ought to happen to him there, and how he will be perceived by his subjects, how he will be honored by them, and what kind of memory will remain of him regarding the things he did while standing in that rule. Furthermore, you will see how it will go for him against his enemies or the enemies of his kingdom, what kind of victory he will have over them, and how he will preserve the goods of his kingdom and acquire the goods of his enemies and such things. 

In this, one must look at the **Lords of the Part** <note>the 'Lot of Fortune' or other calculated points</note> and the **Lord of the 10th house**. See if both have suffered the misfortune of **combustion** <note>being so close to the Sun that their power is 'burned up' or hidden</note> in the ascending sign <note>the 1st house</note> that was present at the hour of enthronement, confirmation, or the question. If this occurs there, or in the 10th, 7th, or 4th houses, within three degrees before the line of any of the aforementioned houses or five degrees behind, it signifies that he will then be deposed from his kingdom or rule. Understand the same regarding the planet that was in the first house at the aforementioned hour, if it had any significance over the kingdom or office as described in the chapter before this one. If the Lord of the First, the planet existing within it, or the Lord of the 10th do not show what has been said, and if no planet was joined in the first house at the hour of his confirmation or enthronement into the kingdom which might signify something about the rule, then look to see if there is any planet in the 10th house that has some significance over the kingdom—namely, one that has some **dignity** <note>essential power based on its zodiacal position</note> in the 10th; you may judge the same from that. 

Similarly, when **Mars** or **Saturn** <note>the malefic planets</note> reaches that degree or that minute in which the aforementioned planet was then located—and even more strongly if one of them, namely Mars or Saturn, turns retrograde in that same degree—it then signifies removal without a doubt. You can say the same if the planet that was the Lord of the 4th house <note>representing the end of matters</note> at the entry of the kingdom or its confirmation was retrograde, combust, or in the 10th house, provided the 10th house was the **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet's influence is extremely heightened</note> of some planet. If, however, the Lord of the 10th house was not the exaltation of any planet but was rather the **fall** <note>the sign opposite the exaltation, where a planet is weakened</note> of someone, you shall judge the same by the planet that was the Lord if it aspects <note>forms a specific angular relationship with</note> it—namely, the one whose fall is in the 10th house at the entry of the kingdom—and that planet shall be the significator of the king when he began his reign. If you do not find in any of the aforementioned places—the 1st, 10th, 7th, or 4th—a planet or any planets disposed as I have said, and the entry into the kingdom or office was by day: look at whether the **Sun** is joined to any planet, namely to Saturn or Mars, and look at the degree

This cannot be avoided, and he will be removed shortly, or at least before his year of kingdom or office is completed.

### Whether he will reign in the second year.

Wherever you find that he is to remain in the kingdom for one year, see when that year will be completed. Its completion will be when the **Sun** returns to the exact point <note>the exact degree, minute, and second of the zodiac</note> in which it was when the king or ruler rose—that is, when he entered that regime and assumed its lordship or magistracy. For the year will then be complete when he has circled 360 full degrees. Then the second year will begin when he starts to enter that same minute which he was entering when he began his kingdom or regime. For example: if the Sun was at the beginning of the first minute of the degree of **Taurus**, and had already passed 4 seconds of that minute when the Sun has circled the entire zodiac and arrived at the 4th second of the first minute of the degree of Taurus, then the year will be complete. And when it touches the fifth second of the fifth degree <note>this seems to be a clarifying example of progress</note> of Taurus, then another year will begin, and that will be the second year after the first. Therefore, calculate the positions of the planets for that hour and that minute of the hour, and verify the twelve **cusps** <note>the starting points of the astrological houses</note>—the first, the tenth, and the other houses. Then you will be able to know whether he is to remain in that kingdom in the second year or not, and what ought to happen to him in the second year. Do the same for the other years if you see that he is to remain longer in the kingdom.

### Concerning the third year.

For if he is well-disposed and free from the impediment of malefics, it signifies that he will stay for another year. Understand it thus in every revolution: for whenever the Lord of the Ascendant of the revolution is free from the impediment of malefics, it signifies that he will remain in that regime for another year. If, however, the **Moon** is joined to a planet that receives her, see if that receiver is free from malefics. ## On the eleventh house.
### Chapter one: on the confidence or hope that someone has regarding any matter.

Since hope is one of those things in which all humans rejoice and which causes them to take delight, it is no wonder if men have hope in possessing the things they desire. Because of this, men sometimes hope to have things that are possible to have, and sometimes things that are impossible to have—and they see clearly that it is impossible for them to have them; nevertheless, they desire them anyway. Therefore, if anyone puts a question to you about something they hope to have, see if it is impossible; if so, do not involve yourself in that judgment. 

If, however, it is about possible things, look at the <term>ascendant</term>—the sign of the hour of the question, which is called the first house—and its lord, as well as the Moon and the lord of the eleventh house. See if the lord of the first or the Moon is joined to the lord of the eleventh, or if the lord of the eleventh is joined to the lord of the first "corporeally" <note>by a physical meeting in the same degree of the zodiac</note>; this signifies that he has obtained the thing in which he has confidence. If the connection is by an "aspect" <note>a geometric angle</note>, see what kind of aspect it is: for if it is a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> without <term>reception</term> <note>a cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note>, he will obtain it easily. If, however, it is with reception, he will obtain it very easily. If it 

<column-break/>

is a <term>square</term> with reception, he will obtain it, but not very easily—though not with great difficulty. And if it is without reception, or if it is an <term>opposition</term> with reception, he will obtain it with difficulty. And if it is an opposition without reception, he will obtain it with even greater difficulty, and only after despair. 

If the lord of the eleventh house is in the first, tenth, seventh, or fourth house, and the Moon is joined to him by known aspects, or is joined to any planet that "receives" her, he will obtain the thing he hopes for according to his wish, unless the Moon commits her disposition to another who is badly disposed. For if the Moon commits her disposition to any planet and that planet is in Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces <note>the "mutable" or "double-bodied" signs</note>, it signifies that the seeker will obtain something of the thing he hopes for, but not so much that his mind is satisfied; however, he will obtain it with little labor. 

If, however, the planet is in Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn <note>the "cardinal" signs</note>, he will obtain it; but what is obtained will be meager and come with labor and the greatest difficulty. But if it is in Taurus, Leo, or Aquarius <note>the "fixed" signs</note>, he will obtain in full what he intends and without great labor. If it is in Scorpio, he will obtain it, but not entirely and with labor—unless it is then received by Mars, for if it is received, he will obtain it as in the other cases. 

And if the one to whom the Moon has committed her disposition is "hindered" <note>afflicted by bad planets or positions</note>, it signifies that the matter will almost reach an effect and will be as if it were happening—it will be fully believed to be happening, and perhaps he will obtain it—yet it will be destroyed after it is obtained or after it is thought to be settled. And if he is not hindered, but is in conjunction with some planet that receives him, it signifies the obtaining of the thing even more perfectly than the questioner would believe. The same thing will happen to him if the lord of the first house is joined to any planet that receives him.

### Chapter two: whether the person he speaks of is a friend of the seeker or not; or if he will become a friend or not.

There are some people who sometimes pretend to be friends of others, or wish to say that they want to become their friends; those who wish to be certain of this consult an astrologer to see whether it is so or not. Therefore, if someone moved by this question comes to you: look at the first house and its lord, and the Moon, and the lord of the eleventh house, just as was said in the preceding chapter. See if the lord of the first or the Moon joins with the lord of the eleventh corporeally, or by a trine or sextile aspect. If the lord of the eleventh is joined to the lord of the first, it signifies that he is a friend, and he who said he wants to become a friend will become one, and they will be joined together in true and stable friendship. 

And if it is with reception, their friendship will endure forever, even unto their successors. And if the lord of the fifth house <note>the house of children</note> then aspects any of the aforementioned by an aspect of friendship, the friendship will endure even with the children and other descendants. And if it is without reception, or from a square aspect with reception, that friendship will last a long time but will not extend to the future generation. And if it is from an opposition (whether with or without reception) or from a square without reception, that friendship will be full of whispering, contrariety, and worsening; each will be contrary to the other, nor will they be friendly in a good way, nor will their friendship be durable; and the opposition will devastate the friendship more than the square aspect.

If someone asks you about something he does not wish to reveal to you, but says to you: "See if I shall obtain the thing I hope to obtain or not," you must then consider the lord of the first house and the significator, which is the Moon. If they are both joined to the fortunes, and they to them, and the fortune is in the angles, or if one is in an angle...

# ON THE TWELFTH HOUSE.

## Chapter one: regarding a prize placed in some location, which of the horses or other animals, whether rational or irrational, will reach it first.

If ever someone comes to you with a desire and a question concerning a <term>prize</term> <note>original: "bravio," a trophy or reward in a contest</note>, asking which horse or other animal will win it or reach it first: you must look into this matter not as you look into other things, but differently. This is because the twelfth house represents the animal running for the prize; the <term>planetary hour</term> represents the prize itself; and the Lord of the Hour similarly represents the animal. Therefore, you must see where the Lord of the Hour of the question is at that time. If it is in the first house, the animal of the person who is first will arrive. If it is not his own, but belongs to another, and he wishes to be certain of this, the judgment shall be that it will arrive before all other animals. This is stronger and more certain if the Lord of the First and the Lord of the Hour are the same; that animal will far outpace the others. If the Lord of the Hour is in the tenth, it will come second; if in the eleventh, third; if in the seventh, fourth; if in the fifth, fifth; if in the ninth, sixth; if in the third, seventh; if in the sixth, eighth; if in the eighth, ninth; if in the fourth, tenth; if in the second, eleventh or equivalent to the last; and if it is in the twelfth, it will be the last or its equivalent. If there are more than twelve—which rarely happens—judge them by the aspects the running animals have to the fourth or twelfth house.

As for the safety of the person riding the horse or other animal, look similarly at him and the Lord of the Hour. If the Lord is in its own house or its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet's influence is especially powerful</note>, it will save his body from hindrance, unless the Lord of the Eighth <note>the house of death and injury</note> aspects him, which then signifies a hindrance without the breaking of limbs. If, however, it is in its <term>term</term>, <term>triplicity</term>, or <term>face</term> <note>these are minor astrological dignities</note> and free from harmful planets, it will likewise save him. If it is in its <term>fall</term> <note>a sign where a planet is weakened</note>, it signifies a fall from the horse, but he will be hindered in a bad way. And if it is in its <term>detriment</term>, it signifies both a fall and it is possible that the horse also falls with him. And if then any of the <term>malifics</term> <note>harmful planets, like Saturn or Mars</note> aspects him from opposition, or is joined to him bodily or by a square aspect, he will break some member of his body. And if that malific who hinders him is in Aries, it will hurt his head; if in Taurus, it will hurt the neck or adjacent parts; if in Gemini, the shoulder, arms, or hands; if in Cancer, it will hurt around the chest; if in Leo, it will hurt the back; if in Virgo, it will hurt around the navel; if in Libra, it will hurt around the hips; if in Scorpio, it will hurt around the private parts; if in Sagittarius, it will hurt around the thighs; if in Capricorn, it will hurt around the knees; if in Aquarius, it will hurt around the shins; if in Pisces, it will hurt around the feet. But if the Lord of the First is in the eighth with a malific or is otherwise hindered, or if with this the Lord of the Eighth is hindered, or

<column-break/>

the Moon is hindered, it signifies death from that fall.

## Chapter second: when someone who does not have an animal among those running for a prize asks which animal will win.

If perhaps someone is anxious who does not have a horse or animal among the animals or horses running for a prize, and asks which of the horses or other animals running for the prize will win it: you can see through this which animal may win, its color, age, quality, and reputation. For this, you must look at the Lord of the Hour with a most true instrument <note>likely an astrolabe or quadrant</note> so that it does not deceive you. If you find it in the first, tenth, or eleventh house, or if you find another planet in any of the aforementioned places, you can tell him that the horse or other animal of the color signified by that planet will win the prize. Do not prefer the eleventh to the tenth, nor the tenth to the first, but the first over the tenth, and the tenth over the eleventh. Once the color of the animal is known, you will know the winner. Then, once you have seen which animal ought to win, look to see if its <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing the animal</note> is in its own house; if so, the animal will be noble, like a <term>destrier</term> <note>original: "dextrariū," a high-bred warhorse</note> certainly famous among other horses. If it is in its exaltation, it will be more famous and more renowned, a high-bred animal that has long been accustomed to defeating other animals. If it is in its triplicity, it will be much less than this, and the animal will not be very renowned or high-bred. If it is in its term, it will be lower still and little-known. If it is in its face, it will be an animal of little notice, or perhaps a stranger from another land that is unknown in that land. If it is in none of these places, it is an unknown animal of no great value, like a <term>rouncey</term> <note>original: "roncinus," an ordinary all-purpose horse</note> or similar. And if the animal's significator is in its fall, it will be vicious and full of faults, though perhaps many are not known. If it is in its detriment, it will be even more vicious, and its faults will be well-known.

## Whether the animal winning the prize is long-lived or not.

If you wish to know if the winning animal is long-lived or not: look at the planet that signifies that animal. If it is <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the Sun</note>, it signifies a young animal; if it is <term>occidental</term> <note>setting after the Sun</note>, it will be long-lived; and whether it is before the Sun or after, whatever it signifies will follow immediately.

## Chapter third: what quality the owner of the animal is.

And if you wish to know the quality of the owner of the animal, <term>Gabel</term> <note>likely referring to the astrologer Sahl ibn Bishr, known as Zahel or Zael</note> said that if the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is the house of the Sun, the owner will be a king; it seems to me he would be greater than all those whose animals are running. If it is from the houses of Saturn, the animal will be long-lived but not high-bred, unless Saturn is then in an angle or in an excellent place from the ascendant. If it is from the houses of Jupiter, it will belong to some famous and noble man who has familiarity with nobles and magnates, or perhaps he could be a bishop or a great judge. If it is from the houses of Mars, it will belong to some warlike knight or a bearer of arms, or perhaps some duke. And the philosopher also said that if it is from the houses of Venus or Mercury, it will belong to some magnate or noble, or a woman, or a scribe, or a wise or literate man. If it is the house of the Moon, it will belong to some sailor or some merchant who entered it in the race so that it might increase in fame so he could sell it better.

It happens sometimes that someone, because of threats made against him, or because of something he has committed, or for whatever reason, falls into fear; and concerning—

If that lord is in the first, tenth, seventh, or fourth house <note>these are the "angles," the strongest points of a chart</note> and is free from Mars and from their hindrances, say that the threats will be false and the fear he has will be empty, and that he will not fall into any danger from those things he fears. 

However, if the lord of the first house is in houses "falling" from the <term>ascendant</term> <note>known as cadent houses, which are traditionally considered weak or unstable</note>—which are the second, sixth, eighth, and twelfth—then those threats have already been made openly and are widely known. Understand this same logic for any matter that is doubted.

### Chapter 5: On the diversity of many things about which a question is sometimes made at the same time.

Many times people come to an astrologer indiscreetly, asking him about many and diverse things, 

<column-break/>

and they believe that it is as easy to answer as it is to ask; they think that all things can be answered together as easily as one, when the reality is quite different. Therefore, when you do not have a specific <term>ascendant</term> for each matter, you must take the most general thing for the seeker, which is the Moon; and the other planets must signify the things sought. 

Hence, you must consider the number of things asked: if those things are six or fewer, you can judge them according to the conjunctions the Moon makes with the six planets. For the nature of the first thing is found through the nature of the planet to which the Moon first joins after the question is asked. See the disposition of that planet, and according to how it is disposed, you shall judge the outcome of that matter. For if it is well-disposed in a strong place, such as in the angles or in the houses succeeding the angles, and in its own "dignities" <note>signs where the planet has the most power, like its 'Home' or 'Exaltation'</note>, and free from the hindrances I have often named to you, the outcome of that matter will be good. If, however, the contrary of what I have said is true, the outcome will also be the contrary. 

Next, see to which planet the Moon joins again after it has separated from the first one, and see what its disposition is; according to that, judge the second matter. Afterward, look to which planet the Moon joins again after separating from the second, and judge the third matter according to the disposition of the third planet it joins. Then look to the fourth it joins after separating from the third, and judge the fourth matter according to its disposition. Then see to which it joins first after its separation from the fourth, and according to its disposition judge the fifth matter. Then see to which it joins after separation from the fifth, and judge the sixth matter according to its disposition. Understand the same regarding an "aspect" as you do for a physical "conjunction." 

And if those matters or questions are more than six, judge afterward by the lords of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</note> of the houses in which the planets were when the Moon was joined to them, whether by body or by aspect. For example: the Moon was joined to Mars in the first conjunction it made after the question was asked, and Mars was in Virgo. Now, since you have completed the count of six planets, you must now judge the seventh matter according to the first lord of the triplicity of Virgo, which is Venus. It made a second conjunction with Saturn after it separated from Mars, which was in Cancer; now you must judge the eighth matter according to the first lord of the triplicity of Cancer, which is Venus <note>the text here seems to list Venus for both, though triplicity rulers vary by day/night</note>. In the third conjunction after separation from Saturn, the Moon was joined to Mercury, which was in Libra; now you must judge the ninth matter according to the first lord of the triplicity of Libra, which is Saturn. And after separation from Mercury, the Moon was joined to Jupiter, which was in Sagittarius; now you must judge the tenth matter according to the disposition of the Sun, which is the first lord of the triplicity of Sagittarius. 

After you have completed the first lords of the triplicities, if there are more than ten matters, judge again by the second lords of the triplicities just as you judged by the first. And if the matters still exceed this, judge again by the third lords of the triplicities as you did for the first and second. And if the matters still exceed these for you—which has never happened to me—judge according to the lords of the angles. And if they still exceed those, judge according to the lords of the triplicities of the angles.

Similarly, if asked about any matter whether it be true or not: look to the lord of the first and the Moon; if they are well-disposed, that thing will be true in its nature. And if that thing is gold, see if the Sun is well-disposed; if so, it will be true gold; if not, it will be false. If it is silver: look to the Moon; if she is well-disposed, the silver will be true; if she is ill-disposed, it will be false. If someone asks about several things—namely two or three—regarding which of them might be better, more useful, or more truthful, whether they are rumors or something else, such as which of two or more things he might obtain: look to the <term>lord of the first house</term> <note>the planet ruling the sign on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</note> and the Moon. If indeed the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is hindered and in a cadent house, nothing of those things named to you will come to pass.

### Chapter 6: When someone is invited to a banquet, whether one should go or not, and what foods will be there.

**B**anquets are held at times in certain places and regions more than in others, as the Italians are very often accustomed to do—especially the people of Romagna, and above all others, the knights of Ravenna. They invite many to these banquets who do not go willingly, and also to weddings and other great gatherings. Therefore, people sometimes wish to be assured by an astrologer whether they should go to that banquet or gathering or not, and they may put this question to you. Or perhaps you yourself are invited to that banquet and wish to know whether you should go or not. 

Look to the sign that is then <term>ascending</term>; and see if the Moon is in it alone, joined to no one, for then it signifies that you can go to the banquet, and there will not be much fuss made over formalities, nor will you or the seeker be looked down upon. And if the Moon is in the <term>tenth house</term> <note>the house of social status and career</note>, almost the same will happen, except that you (or whoever asks) will be held in greater honor. In the seventh house, its significance is less than in the first. In the fourth house, it is less than in the seventh; in all other places, the significance is lower than this. According to how much weaker one house is than another, so much more will the person who goes to that gathering be disdained.

And if the Moon is joined to any planet and is in the first house, see to whom she is joined. For if she is joined with **Saturn**, it signifies that at the banquet the food will be tasteless, unclean, poorly prepared, and not well served or organized. The seasoned dishes and sauces there will not taste as they naturally should, nor will the one going to the feast enjoy those foods or sauces; he will regret going. Therefore, it is better not to go to such a banquet. 

If, however, she is joined with **Jupiter**, you can go to the banquet safely, for you will feast well there. There will be good-tasting and sweet foods, they will be delightful, and there will be dishes made with rice and similar things. You will be honored there such that few will be honored more than you—or perhaps no one at all. 

If she is joined with **Mars**, do not go to those nuptials or that banquet, for the food there will not be fit for the palate and will taste bitter; moreover, it is feared there may be brawls and discord among the guests. 

If she is joined with the **Sun**, you can go if you wish. For there will be good-tasting foods made with arugula or mustard or <term>verjuice</term> <note>original: "agresta"; a tart juice made from unripe grapes</note> and similar things that taste good to the palate, served and laid out with care. 

If she is joined with **Venus**, go safely, for it signi-

<column-break/>

fies that there will be delightful and good-tasting foods. There will likewise be cheerfulness, games, and many delights. Various kinds of foods and different drinks will be multiplied there. There will be things there that will please you or anyone going to the banquet, and in which you will take delight; a great part of the food will be rich and very fatty. 

And if she is joined with **Mercury**, it signifies that you can certainly go, for there will be many and diverse kinds of food, drinks, and mixtures thereof, having a sharp taste to the palate. People there will speak good words—namely, words of wisdom—and they will tell the deeds of the ancients. They will say many new things there and recite things both heard and unheard of, both credible and incredible. Likewise, there will be a gathering of many men. 

It should be known generally that if the Moon is joined to **Saturn** from a water sign by a <term>trine or sextile aspect</term> <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, they will eat <term>tarts</term> <note>original: "turtas"</note>. If he aspects her from a <term>quartile or opposition</term> <note>challenging angles of 90 or 180 degrees</note>, it signifies they will eat cold meats such as <term>aspics</term> <note>original: "sulfia"; chilled meat jellies</note> and the like. If the Moon is in **Libra**, it signifies the eating of legumes. If she is in **Gemini** or **Aquarius**, it signifies the eating of poultry. If **Jupiter** aspects her, it signifies the eating of delicate foods. If **Mars** aspects her, it signifies the eating of hot and roasted foods. And if the **Sun** then aspects Mars, it signifies that a part of those meats will be burnt. The other planets do not hinder her. 

And if the Moon is outside the Ascendant and is in the tenth house, the banquet will be similar to when she is in the first, but more renowned. If she is in the seventh, it will be less than this. If she is in the fourth, it will be even less. In the other houses, it will be lower still, as each is less strong than the other.

### Chapter 7: Whether the banquet consists of one dish or many.

**I** shall show you whether one kind of food is eaten at the banquet or many. Look then at which sign is found on the eastern line <note>the Ascendant</note>. If it is a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius; signs representing stability</note> and its lord is in a fixed sign, and the Moon likewise, they will dine content with one kind of food. If, however, the lord of the first is in a <term>common sign</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces; signs representing change or duality</note>, they will have another food—that is, a second course—but somewhat less than the first. If, along with this, the Moon is in a common sign, the second dish will be different from the first or it will be doubled. 

If the Ascendant is a common sign and its lord and the Moon are in fixed signs, they will have two dishes. If the lord of the first and the Moon are in common signs, they will have three dishes. If they are in <term>movable signs</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs representing action and quick change</note>, they will have something after those three dishes. If the Ascendant is a movable sign and the lord of the first and the Moon are in a fixed or common sign, they will have three dishes and something else after those three. And if the lord of the first is in a movable sign, each of the diners will have four different dishes and something after those four. And if with this the Moon is in a movable sign, they will have five kinds of dishes and something else after them. And if with this the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note> and its lord are in movable signs, they will have many kinds of dishes—perhaps six or more—not counting the fruits of trees and similar things which are not counted among the formal courses of a banquet.

### Chapter 8: To know the reason why the banquet was held.

**V**ile and envious people—whose hearts do not allow them to do well—are sometimes accustomed to speak as if by way of reproach when someone, out of the nobility of his heart or perhaps for some other reason, holds a banquet, asking: "Why is he doing this?" And perhaps you wish to know the reason for yourself, or someone else has asked you about this. Look at the Ascendant at the hour of the beginning of the banquet or of the questioning...

<meta>This page continues the specific "interrogations" or astrological inquiries regarding social gatherings. While the previous page discussed choosing between various options, this page focuses entirely on the nature, quality, and outcomes of attending a banquet or feast.</meta>

Regarding the invitation or when you are called to a banquet: observe from which of the planets the Moon is separating and to which of them she is joining. For if she is separating from one of the <term>malefics</term> <note>original: "infortunarum"; refers to Mars or Saturn, planets believed to bring difficulty</note> and is not joining with any other, but is <term>void of course</term> <note>original: "vacua cursu"; when the Moon makes no further astrological aspects before leaving its current sign</note>, that banquet will not take place for some clearly apparent reason; rather, the host does this led as if by a certain lack of spirit <note>original: "insipiditate"</note>. 

If, however, the Moon is joined to <term>benefics</term> <note>original: "fortuna"; refers to Jupiter or Venus, planets believed to bring good luck</note> by an <term>opposition</term> <note>an aspect of 180 degrees</note> or <term>square aspect</term> <note>an aspect of 90 degrees</note>, the host held the banquet for such a reason that he could not avoid it—such as the occasion of a wedding, or because someone came to his house such that he could not, without reproach, fail to provide a feast, or similar reasons. 

If, however, the aspect was from a <term>trine</term> <note>an aspect of 120 degrees</note> or <term>sextile</term> <note>an aspect of 60 degrees</note>, the host held the banquet for the sake of his own honor and so that he might be happy and rejoice with those feasting; or perhaps because someone else had hosted him, and he wished to return the favor, or similar things.

### ¶ How long the banquet is likely to last.

If you wish to know how long the banquet will endure: look to the planet to which the Moon is then joined. If that planet is in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of the chart</note> and in a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, that banquet will be finished in a single sitting. Or, if it is finished in a <term>mutable sign</term> <note>original: "signo communi"; Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, there will be two sittings. And if it is in a <term>succedent house</term> <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> in a mutable sign, it will not be finished in two sittings. And if it is in a <term>cadent house</term> <note>the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses</note> and in a <term>cardinal sign</term> <note>original: "signo mobili"; Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> or even a mutable one, the banquet will last for two days or more.

### ¶ When the guests will have quarreled.

And if the planet to which the Moon is joined is the <term>lord of its house</term> <note>the planet that rules the sign where the Moon is located</note>, some of those at the banquet will quarrel together; nevertheless, the banquet will not be abandoned, and they shall eat.

### ¶ When the food is placed at the banquet.

To know how the food is brought to the banquet: you should look to the <term>lord of the hour</term> <note>the planet ruling the specific hour of the day or night</note> at the beginning of the banquet, or of the inquiry, or of the start of the journey when one goes there. If he is found in the first or tenth house, everything will be prepared well and in an orderly fashion according to the conditions of health mentioned above, and the things to be served will be placed on the dish before the guests sit down. And if he is in the 7th or 4th house, they will sit down first, and the seating area will be filled with diners before the courses are served.

### ¶ When one must be careful of the banquet foods.

And if you or another person going to the banquet should doubt whether there are foods there that ought to be avoided: look to see if the Moon is then in Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn in <term>conjunction</term> or aspect with any of the malefics—unless Saturn or Mars aspects her from Capricorn. For in that case, herbs should not be eaten, neither cooked nor raw; nor should you eat legumes when she is in Libra, nor even in Virgo, if any of the malefics aspects her or is bodily joined to her. 

And <term>Sahl</term> <note>original: "Zahel"; refers to Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and mathematician</note> said that if the Moon is in Scorpio with the <term>Dragon's Tail</term> <note>original: "cauda"; the South Node of the Moon, often associated with loss or purging</note>, do not eat fat. And if she is in Leo or Sagittarius, do not eat the meat of wild animals. And if she is in Pisces, do not eat trout or other salted fish. And you should understand all these things to apply when the Moon is in the aforementioned signs in square or opposite aspects to the malefics without <term>reception</term> <note>a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note>.

### Chapter nine: which houses signify the banquet, its cause, and similar things.

<column-break/>

And Sahl said that the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> signifies the cause of the banquet. He said that if the ascendant of the banquet is any of the houses of Venus, the cause will be a wedding. And if it is from the houses of Mercury, it will be on account of a son. And if it is from the houses of Jupiter, it will be on account of a friend. 

The second house from the ascendant signifies the drinking vessels and the household furnishings. Hence, if the second house is a mutable sign, their vessel will be colored. And if Mars is then in the second house, that vessel will be made with bronze. And if Venus is in it, there is silver in it. And if it is Jupiter, there will be silver and gold. And if it is Saturn, it will be a wooden or earthen vessel. And if a benefic is in the second house, it will signify the beauty of the house’s ornaments. And if a benefic has <term>dignity</term> <note>astrological standing or power</note> there in the second, those ornaments will be the host's own. If, however, the planet is <term>peregrine</term> <note>lacking any essential dignity; a "foreigner" in that part of the zodiac</note>, he will have those things on loan. 

The third house signifies the guests: if a benefic is there, they will be people of good character. If, however, Saturn is there, they will be base. If Mars is there, there will be whisperings, or they will be bellicose men or highwaymen and the like. 

The fourth house signifies the location of the banquet: if a benefic is there, it will be a beautiful, suitable, and decent place. If, however, a malefic is there, it will be an unsuitable, ugly, or foul-smelling place. And Sahl said that if it is a mutable sign, the place of the banquet will be in a portico. And if the Sun or Jupiter is there, their banquet will be in the cloister of the house or in the south. 

The fifth house signifies their cups. If the fifth sign is fixed, they will drink from a single type of drink. If it is a mutable sign, they will drink various drinks. And if Jupiter or Mercury is in it, their drinks will be sweet and flavorful. If, however, Mars is there, the drink tastes of sharpness. And if Mars is hindered by Saturn, the drink will be vinegary. And if the Sun is there, it will be harsh or somewhat bitter. And if Venus is there, it will be very sweet or otherwise pleasant to the taste. If, however, the Moon is there, the drink will be flavorless. 

The sixth house signifies the servants of the banquet: if a benefic is there, the servants will be capable and decent. If, however, an evil planet is there, they will be incapable and dirty, not knowing how to serve. 

The seventh house signifies the cooks and butchers <note>original: "carneparios"</note>: if a benefic is there, they will be capable; if a malefic is there, they will be incapable. 

The eighth house signifies the <term>seneschals</term> <note>stewards or masters of ceremonies</note>. 

The ninth house signifies those who set and carry the courses onto the dish. If benefics are in these houses, they will be fit for this and will know how to do it well. If, however, evil planets are there, they will not be up to the task. 

The tenth house signifies the universal goodness of the banquet and the cheerfulness which the guests will have together. And if a benefic is there, the banquet will be decent and laudable, and the guests will rejoice and be happy together. And if a malefic is there, the banquet will be unseemly, so that the guests will be hateful to the host and among themselves. 

The eleventh house signifies whether the host and the guests are friends. 

The twelfth house signifies the expense which he will have from the banquet. If, indeed, an evil planet is in it, the host will be sad within himself and will grieve over the providing of that banquet. 

And whenever you find a benefic in any of the aforesaid places and it is strengthened, it signifies an increase of good. And if an evil planet is weakened in any of the aforesaid places, it signifies an increase of malice.
