...[if] all things were well-disposed, as he said, because where the Moon is chosen, from there ten things will come to the begun matter for a better and more orderly state. If they were not well-disposed, it will diminish something of the good, but they will not be able to destroy the good established by a well-chosen matter. And if the **election** <term>election: the act of choosing a specific time to act based on planetary positions</term> was bad and poorly disposed, it will increase the evil and it will happen more quickly.

And Haly <note>Haly Abenragel, a 10th-century Arab court astrologer</note> said that the most patient way to increase the good is to adapt the place of the "lord of the fourth part of the year" in every election, just as was said regarding the place of **conjunction** <term>conjunction: the New Moon</term> or **prevention** <term>prevention: the Full Moon immediately preceding the event</term>. He said, however, that the adaptation of the place of conjunction or prevention in this work is more appropriate than the adaptation of the lord of the fourth of the year, and the adaptation of the lord of the 4th is more powerful than the adaptation of the "lord of the soul." He said that we can adapt all of them, which would not be bad.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a leading Persian astrologer of the 9th century</note> indeed said that when the lord of the election is the lord of the Moon's sign in the "revolution of the year," or the lord of the year's **ascendant** is fortunate at the hour of the election, and the revolution signifies an increase in honor, you shall begin, and the end of the begun matter will be praiseworthy. And he said when the lord of the year's ascendant is not witnessed in any place of the "luminaries" <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term> nor in the midheaven, the things begun will be vile, meager, and subtle.

Atabari <note>Omar Tiberiades, a Persian-Jewish astrologer</note> indeed said—as Haly recites—that when the place of conjunction or prevention and their lords are in some praiseworthy place, the matter will be fixed—that is, the thing then begun will be durable and firm. And similarly, if someone is born in that same hour, or ordained, or appointed to any leadership, office, or dignity, the matter will be firm and durable. And he said that those places were praiseworthy at the hour of the beginning of things.

And the ancients took testimony in the adaptation of the thing to be done from the "lords of the triplicity" <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> of the sign in which the Moon was at the hour of conjunction or prevention, saying that they themselves are the guardians of things—both of the person beginning or doing the thing and of the thing to be done or begun. If they are "received" <term>reception: a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term> at the hour of the beginning or election, they will signify good; if, on the contrary, they will signify evil.

And they said that it increases the good if the ascendant of the election is a fortunate sign in the revolution of the year: and let there be a "fortune" <term>fortune: a beneficial planet, like Jupiter or Venus</term> that makes that sign fortunate in the first or tenth house, or let it be in the eleventh or fifth, or at least in the second; or let it be in the house that signifies the matter for which we are choosing, so that it turns out well for the one wanting to do it. And let the "significators" <term>significator: a planet representing a specific person or object in a chart</term> of the matter we are beginning be in places concordant with the aforesaid significators, namely the houses of the triplicity mentioned before; and let the significators be strong at the hour of the election or beginning.

And Haly said that it is among the "fortitudes" of the planets that they should be ascending toward the north; and it is sometimes necessary that a planet be ascending in the south, and it has strength, as when the Moon is increasing in light and number <note>The Moon is "increasing in number" when its daily motion is faster than its average speed</note>, it is stronger ascending in the south than if it were then ascending in the north. And let the Moon be in the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful houses in a chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th)</term> increased in light and number in matters we wish to be increased; in contrary matters, let it be the opposite.

And he said let the significators be moving toward "fortunes" and away from "malifics" <term>malifics: harmful planets, specifically Saturn and Mars</term>. Indeed, let the Moon and the significator of the thing to be done or begun—in every matter we wish to be made public—be above the earth; and in every matter we wish to be hidden, let the Moon and the significators be under the earth. And let the lord of the ascendant and other significators as much as possible be "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note>; and the planet toward whose conjunction the Moon goes should be a fortune, for that surely signifies a good end to the begun matter and what will become of it.

And Alchindi <note>Al-Kindi, known as the 'Philosopher of the Arabs'</note> said when the Sun and Moon look upon each other with an "aspect of friendship" <term>aspect of friendship: the trine or sextile angles, considered harmonious</term>, it signifies the strength and goodness of any begun matter; even more strongly if the Moon is in the third degree of Taurus <note>The Moon's degree of "exaltation," where it is considered most powerful</note>: for then it signifies the ultimate goodness of the thing we wish to begin or do, even if other significators

<column-break/>

were not well-disposed, provided they are not "besieged" by two malifics without reception.

And Messahali <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari, a 10th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer</note> said that planets are said to be strong when they are "western" from the Moon, just as they are when they are "oriental" from the Sun: since the Moon rules in the night just as the Sun rules in the day.

Atabari, however, said when we cannot adapt the Moon and the ascendant, let us adapt one of them: for if it be a daytime election, let us adapt the ascendant, especially if the Moon is under the earth; if it be a nighttime election, let us adapt the Moon, especially if she is above the earth. And he said that if we can delay our election from day to night or night to day, it must be considered which of them is better to adapt—namely the Moon or the ascendant—and do from them what seems better to us.

And Haly said that the Moon being under the earth by day and above the earth by night is good and increases the strength of the ascendant. And if it is necessary for us to choose for someone and we cannot adapt the Moon, let us place Jupiter or Venus in the first or tenth house: for these will adapt the matter with a great adaptation. And someone said that they will make it last a long time.

Others, however, said that the adaptation of the Moon is to be preferred in all things we wish to last a long time, such as the building of cities or houses, the celebration of marriages, and similar things. When the Moon is weak, she must be removed from the angles; and if we cannot remove her from the angles, let her not "look at" <note>form an aspect with</note> the ascendant, nor its lord, nor the house of the matter being chosen, nor its lord, nor even the planet that signifies the thing being chosen. And if she cannot be removed from all the aforesaid aspects, let her at least be removed from those from which she can be removed.

And Alchindi said if we cannot adapt all the significators and we can adapt the Moon, it will be good. Nevertheless, it does not promise us that the matter will not be destroyed. Therefore, if the lord of the "house of signification" of the thing we want to do or begin can be adapted, it is better for the matter so that it may endure or come to the end we desire. And it will be considered less of a burden to astrologers if they have not adapted the Moon and the lord of the first house (which signify the person of the seeker or the beginner), for in observing the person of the seeker or beginner, the lord of the first and the Moon are to be adapted. However, men do not consider what happens except concerning the *matter* itself, and they look forward to its outcome, not caring about the state of the person.

If, however, the Moon is slow in course—namely similar to the course of Saturn, which is to say she moves less than 12 degrees in one day—it signifies difficulty and slowness. Indeed, if that building we intend to make, or what ought to begin, or what one intends by beginning to raise above the earth [is started then], and the Moon is slow in course and other significators are under the earth, that building will never be raised; and if it is raised, it will happen most slowly; but it will not be raised in that entire age in which it was begun.

And if you cannot make the Moon fortunate as you wish in your matter, and there is something that makes her unfortunate and you cannot avoid that impediment, place that which impedes her as the "Lord of the First," because the first house does not impede itself nor the Moon to its own detriment. And if you can place [the Moon] in the first, it will be better, and let her be free from the impediments mentioned elsewhere. And if you cannot place it in the first, place it in some other praiseworthy place, such as in the tenth, eleventh, or fifth; and if it were possible that [the Lord of the First] should "receive" the Moon, it would utterly break all its malice. For the Moon and other significators being in a praiseworthy state increases the good and diminishes the evil; and their being in an evil state increases the evil and diminishes the good. And you should beware of the conjunction of malifics with the Moon or with other significators, or their square aspect <note>original: "quarto aspectu"</note> or opposition without reception, provided they are not impeded; for from a trine or sextile aspect...

They are not so harmful as long as they are otherwise "free"; rather, when they receive an aspect from the Moon or a **sextile aspect** <term>sextile aspect: an angle of 60 degrees between planets, considered harmonious</term>, they themselves are made "free" for good fortune. And always place your **significators** <term>significators: the planets that represent the person or the goal of the election</term> as strongly as you can, and guard them and the Moon from the "impediments" of the malefic planets as best you know how. See that they are not ill-placed in the locations from which they signify the things we intend to do or begin, nor should they look upon those locations from a **fourth aspect** <term>fourth aspect: also called a "square," an angle of 90 degrees that causes tension</term> or from **opposition** <term>opposition: an angle of 180 degrees, indicating conflict</term>.

And Haly <note>Haly Abenragel, a 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> said: guard against an **eclipse**, and especially if there is an eclipse in the sign where a "luminary" <note>the Sun or the Moon</note> was at the hour of the birth of the person for whom we are making the election. And he said the Moon should not be "under the rays" <term>under the rays: a planet so close to the Sun that its light and power are "burned up" or hidden</term>, and she must be removed entirely from every impediment. Nor should the significator be joined to the Sun, nor the Sun to it. One must also guard against the fourth aspect of the Sun and its opposition; however, if there is "reception" between them, it will be slightly easier. And he said that opposition always gives rise to quarrels and contrarieties. 

Let the malefic planets <note>traditionally Mars and Saturn</note> not be in the "angles" <term>angles: the most powerful houses in a chart—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</term>, and specifically in the **ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> or in the "declining" houses. This is especially true if the malefics are the lords of the houses signifying evil, which are the sixth, eighth, and twelfth <note>houses associated with illness, death, and secret enemies</note>; for then they will signify exactly what those houses signify.

And he said that the Ascendant should not be a sign in which its lord is about to enter **combustion** <term>combustion: a state of extreme weakness caused by being within 8.5 degrees of the Sun</term> in that year; nor should the Ascendant be a sign that was impeded in the "revolution of the year." Nor should the Moon be slow in her course for any matter which we wish to be done quickly, because a slow Moon postpones and delays it, unless there are many other significators.

And he said that one should avoid **moveable signs** <term>moveable signs: also known as "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which favor change and movement</term> in every matter where we desire stability and durability; and in the same way, avoid **fixed signs** <term>fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius, which favor permanence</term> in every matter we wish to pass quickly. **Common signs** <term>common signs: also known as "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces)</term> are for everything you wish to happen exactly as the matter itself requires; a secret renders whatever is in them difficult.

And he said: take care that none of the **fixed stars** which are of the nature of the malefics are in the same degree as the Ascendant, or the "Midheaven," or the house of the matter being chosen. On this point, I have found all the sages who have mentioned them to agree: that they are "cursed." One of these is at the 14th degree of Aries and another at the 15th degree of the same; one is at the 10th of Taurus and another at the 20th; one is at the 18th degree of Gemini; one is at the 8th degree of Cancer and another at the 18th; one is at the 26th degree of Leo; one is at the 8th degree of Virgo and another at the 16th; one is at the 16th degree of Libra; one is at the 7th degree of Scorpio, and in the 9th degree of the same there are two; one is in Sagittarius at the 20th degree and another at the 22nd; one is in Capricorn at the 28th degree and another in the other <note>likely referring to a neighboring degree</note>; one is at the 10th degree of Aquarius; one is at the 5th degree of Pisces.

I highly praise that you do all the things he told you should be done, and that you avoid all the things he told you to avoid, if it can be done; however, it seems to me that a man could almost never do it so perfectly. You, therefore, as I have told you elsewhere, do what good you *can* do, and avoid what evil you *can* avoid; for there will be no peace on earth that is not possible, even if it is not as much as the one receiving it desires.

And Al-Kindi <note>a 9th-century philosopher and "Philosopher of the Arabs"</note> said that it is bad for the "angles" to be remote. Haly, however, praised the angles being remote. But Al-Kindi’s intention was when that "remoteness" occurs by receding from the angles—that is, if one sign were the ninth house, or the twelfth, or the third, or the sixth. If the sign that was the ninth house was also the tenth, or the twelfth was the first, or the third was the fourth, or the sixth was the seventh, that remoteness would be bad because it moves toward the "cadent" houses <note>the weakest houses in a chart</note>. Others, however, understood "remoteness" to mean moving toward the angles—that is, if one sign was the tenth house and that same sign was the eleventh; or the first was the second; or the fourth was the fifth; or the seventh was the eighth. That remoteness would not be bad, because it is done by going *toward* the angles. And Haly praised this remoteness 

<column-break/>

in matters for which we desire durability. 

And Haly said to beware lest the lord of the Ascendant, or the lord of the house signifying the matter we are choosing, or even the planet signifying the matter itself, or the lord of the sign in which the Moon is located, or the planet to which the Moon is joined (if she is joined to any), be in the "second [house] from the Sun" <note>original: "scda a sole"</note>. And when planets are "occidental" <term>occidental: setting in the west after the Sun, usually making them weaker in certain types of astrology</term>, they should not be so close to the Sun that they fall in the second house from it, unless it be Venus or Mercury, for they do not have the prerogative to be very far from the Sun. This signifies the vileness, slowness, and failure of the matter. 

The three "superior" planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>, when they are far from the Sun by two entire signs and are occidental until the completion of the third sign, are said to be in their "old age" <note>original: "senio"</note>, which is a certain impediment to them in elections; this is especially true in matters we intend to finish quickly, for they delay the matter, but they do not prohibit it from happening, though it will not be so swift.

And Haly said that if it is necessary for us to choose something, and we have one of those laudable hours that does not harm the "great ones," let the Moon be joined to Mars or Saturn, provided that the matter we wish to choose is among the things signified by the "fortunes" <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>. For example: if it is a secular dignity or a magistracy or similar things signified by the Sun; or if it is for substance or the accumulation of money signified by Jupiter; or if it is women's affairs and games or other things signified by Venus; or writings or trade or merchandise signified by Mercury and the like. For then those malefic planets cannot prevent the matter from being done and perfected, although they may mix in something of their natural malice. They impede only slightly when they have "reception" <term>reception: when planets are in each other's signs, creating a hospitable relationship</term>, or not at all, because then they are made to be only slightly malicious. When they are "wild" and "horrible" <note>meaning they have no dignity or reception</note>, they impede more, yet they will not be able to turn the matter away from being done. 

If, however, the matter we wish to choose is something we want to be hidden, and the Sun aspects the Ascendant or its lord, and the Sun is good, and the Moon aspects Mercury, and they aspect each other with a laudable aspect—that matter will not be concealed nor hidden, but will be made public. And if someone begins a flight then, they will be captured. And if the aspect of the Sun to the Ascendant, its lord, or the Moon is bad (such as a square or opposition), that matter will be detected in a vile and reprehensible way. And if the significators of the matter are "above the earth," the matter will also be detected, and more strongly if they are in the Midheaven. 

When the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is "under the rays" of the Sun, or the Sun and Moon are "falling" from the Ascendant and not looking at each other, or the Moon and the significators of the matter we are choosing are "under the earth" (especially in the fourth house), it signifies that the matter will be hidden and not detected. And if the lord of the Ascendant is Mars or Saturn or any other unfortunate planet, evil and contrariety will follow the person hiding from that concealment; this is even stronger if the luminaries are impeded. If, however, the luminaries are free, that evil will not harm them.

And Haly also said that all these things mentioned—both the laudable and the unlaudable—are not to be considered except after the adaptation of the "roots" <note>the 'radices' or base charts, such as a birth chart or the chart of a year's beginning</note> named above. And he said when the "fortunes" dominate in the aforementioned roots, one should not worry about these contrary things, even if they are malefic. And he said when the fortunes are strong and dominant in an election, we ought to look only at those things we see will be praiseworthy. And he said when things are laudable, it will multiply the good fortune and the good. If, however, the "roots" are bad, the things that follow, even if they are laudable, do not change or take away that malice, but rather increase it.

And he says that if it is necessary for us to begin something and the evil influences are present, the subsequent factors must be adapted to that beginning; for they reduce the evil somewhat, even if they do not remove it entirely. And he said that one must beware lest the subsequent factors be evil: as if someone were to ask an **astrologer** <term>astrologer: original Latin: "astrologus"; in the medieval sense, this includes what we now call an astronomer</term> to choose a good hour for doing something, but it was a matter he does not wish to reveal to the astrologer. It is necessary for the astrologer to be certain which planet or sign signifies the matter he intends. Therefore, he must then adapt the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the election</term> and its **lord** <term>lord: the planet that "rules" or has the most influence over a specific zodiac sign</term>, both **luminaries** <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term>, and the **fourth house** <term>fourth house: in elections, the fourth house represents the "end of the matter" or final outcome</term> and its lord, so that he may guard the body and soul of the undertaking and the end of the matter, whether it completes the thing he intends to do or not. In the deeds of men, we must adapt **masculine signs** and perform their deeds likewise, if we can, in masculine and diurnal hours. And also, the sign signifying the people must be adapted, and similarly, the planet signifying the people is to be adapted, as I have told you. And the planet that signifies that region or province or city for which you are choosing must be adapted—which is a very difficult thing to know, namely, which planet rules that city or land. Nor can you know this except through deep investigation, unless perhaps you have the hour of the foundation of that land, which very rarely happens. However, you could more easily obtain its signification through an interrogation. But if you do not have the hour of foundation or a question, consider the customs of the people of that land and their life, and consider what has usually happened to them in great and difficult business concerning victories and setbacks; and according to how you see the planets ruling in those events, whether they were good or bad, according to that you will be able to determine its **significator** <term>significator: the planet that represents the person, place, or object in the chart</term> from among the planets. You shall also consider the customs of those citizens, what they are like: for if they are good and honest, and are men of good life and gladly profiting from honest gains—or at least not from shameful ones—and who gladly spend and live honorably, even though perhaps lustfulness might abound in them, nevertheless it is a sign that **Jupiter** is their significator. Therefore you can adapt him in their elections when you do not have a question. The question, however, is an easy matter, and through it you easily have the significator of the city and its citizens, provided it is made by one whom it concerns, such as a ruler or a manager appointed for this purpose, and the like. But if they are greedy, thieves, and wretched, and their customs are base and mean, eager to profit from others from any source whatsoever, not considering whether it is from the lawful or the unlawful, it is a sign that **Saturn** is their significator. If, however, they are pompous men, affecting dominance and desiring to be praised, of an honorable

<column-break/>

and praiseworthy life and of suitable expenses, it is a sign that the **Sun** is their significator. But if they are warlike men, robbers, contentious, and spirited evildoers, furious, proud, profiting from any source and snatching things by right or wrong, and avoiding spending because they are tight-fisted, and practicing shameful customs and vices, it is a sign that **Mars** is their significator. If, however, they are ingenious men, wise, literate, deep in the sciences, of good spending habits, of good customs, not envious, not greedy, merchants of moderate trade, despising money, not intent on profit, it is a sign that **Mercury** is their significator. If, however, they are men of comfort, play, dancing, eating, drinking, and users of musical instruments, and despising greed through every kind of comfort, it is a sign that **Venus** is their significatrix. If, however, they are unfaithful, changeable, wandering, unstable—wanting now this, now that—and users of small-scale trade, it is a sign that the **Moon** is their significatrix.
¶ We can also adapt any planet to various things: for we can adapt **Saturn** to the aforementioned things, and we can also adapt him for those wishing to **dye in a black color**, since he himself naturally signifies blackness; and he is to be placed so that he looks upon the Ascendant and its lord with a favorable **aspect** <term>aspect: the geometric angle between planets, indicating how their energies combine</term>. And also let the Moon be in an aspect of friendship with him, or at least the lord of the house in which she is; or let her be in the house of Saturn, not "falling" from the Ascendant or the tenth house. However, it is better that she looks upon Saturn with a good aspect. Similarly, we can adapt **Jupiter** to the aforementioned things and many others, and especially for those wishing to dye in a **citrine color** <note>a yellow-orange or lemon-like hue</note>, since he naturally signifies that, and he is to be placed as was said of Saturn. We can also adapt **Mars** to the aforementioned and to many other things, and especially for those wishing to dye in a **red color**, since he naturally signifies that color; and he is to be adapted as was said of Jupiter. Mars can also be adapted for **servants** because of his falsity, since servants use it much. We can further adapt the **Sun** to the above-mentioned and to certain other things, and especially for dyers wishing to dye in a **mixed color** which shares in the mixture of many and various colors. We can similarly adapt **Venus** to all the aforementioned and to many other things, and especially for those wishing to **whiten** something, since she naturally signifies whiteness. We can indeed adapt **Mercury** to all the things named above and to certain other things similarly, and especially for those wishing to dye a color that is like **indigo** or **purple** or **semi-purple**, and for composing all other mixed and varied colors. We can similarly adapt the **Moon** to all the things already said above and many other things, and especially for those wishing to dye in a **glaucous** <note>a dull green or bluish-gray color</note> or **callo** <note>possibly a pale or skin-toned color</note> color; similarly for all colors of little durability. And just as one planet can be adapted to many and diverse things, so also one **house** can be adapted to many and diverse things. And many houses can sometimes be adapted to one and the same thing, such as the **second house** being adapted to **substance** <term>substance: personal property, wealth, or material assets</term>, and the **sixth house** is similarly adapted to substance because it signifies servants (who are part of one's substance) and smaller animals (which are part of one's substance); and the **twelfth house** similarly signifies larger animals which are part of one's substance. And understand this in the same way concerning all the houses, as was said in the treatise on the twelve houses. And also many planets can be adapted to one thing, as when we wish to choose an hour for a servant or a **Slavonian** <term>Slavonian: Latin: "Sclavonum"; the root of the word "slave." In the medieval period, many captives sold in Mediterranean markets were of Slavic origin</term> being bought, since he himself is counted among the servants; we can adapt to each of them...

## Chapter Twelve: On the Weakening of Planets.

Just as planets must sometimes be adapted, so must some of them sometimes be weakened, as I remember touching upon above, according as it is necessary to weaken them for the thing we wish to do. For if we wish to go out against enemies, it is necessary to weaken the seventh house and its lord as much as we can, and to strengthen the lord of the first house. If, however, we wish to go out hunting, we must weaken the seventh house and its lord, and we must weaken the Moon—but do not **afflict** <term>afflict: original: "infortunare"; to place a planet in a harsh relationship with the "malefic" planets Mars or Saturn</term> her, unless perhaps the lord of the first house or the lord of the sixth house afflicts her, because the sixth house has significance over the aforementioned animals with which we hunt; yet there are some who say she should be afflicted. If indeed we wish to pursue a thief or a distant fugitive, we must weaken the Moon and even afflict her, especially if we can make it so that the lord of the first house is the one who afflicts her, for then it signifies that he shall not escape from the hands of the one pursuing him. The Moon is sometimes weakened but not afflicted when we give **medicines** <term>original: "farmaca"; specifically purgatives or herbal remedies meant to cleanse the body</term>; for she should then be placed in Scorpio so that the humors may run through all the parts in which the medicine is fit to exercise its power and what pertains to it. We must then beware of the "infortunes"—namely Mars and Saturn. For Saturn could constipate the medicine, and Mars could sharpen it so much that it leads even to the discharge of blood, and perhaps wounds the intestines, from which **dysentery** <note>original: "dissinteria"</note> might be generated, which could be the cause of death for the one who took the medicine. Thus, the Moon should not be afflicted in these matters, but only weakened; and the lord of the first house should be made fortunate and strengthened. In this, our ancient sages seem to disagree.

## Chapter Thirteen: On Particulars Pertaining to Elections.

After a general mention has been made in the preceding sections regarding facts pertaining to universal elections, it seems appropriate to descend to particulars, so that those things which were said generally may be better known in detail. Nor is it necessary for us to call back to memory in the particulars what has already been said in the universals, for that would prolong the work too much and generate boredom for the readers; instead, I shall only subjoin what pertains to the specific fact or chapter. Yet one cannot pass through with such a "dry foot" <note>An idiom meaning to pass through quickly without getting involved in details</note> that something of the aforesaid is not occasionally touched upon; nevertheless, I shall proceed by the easiest path I can for the reader. I will not entangle myself by saying everything that could be observed by the wise in elections, although some say that they always avoided **combust hours** <term>combust: when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden</term> in every matter. I, however, praise anyone who can adapt all contingencies; but as I remember telling you elsewhere, it seems a certain impossibility to be able to adapt everything, and if we wished to look into everything so precisely, so many hours would become "fearful" <note>meaning astrologically dangerous or unusable</note> that we would make very few and rare elections. You, however, follow those things I have told you.

<column-break/>

### On the Hours of Diminution.

And the Egyptians avoided certain hours of certain days of every month which are called the days of the **hours of diminution** <note>These were specific times considered naturally unlucky or "hollow" for starting new ventures</note>. If someone could observe these, it would be good; but if they cannot be observed, it is not a matter as dangerous as some have sometimes believed. I will make a table of them for you so that you can know which they are if you wish to avoid them. Do not wonder if no mention is made here of many things that seem to occur in this work of elections—namely, concerning the preservation of the figures, their arrangement, their rising or setting, and similar things—for all these, if you remember well, have been said elsewhere. For here nothing is said except for the specific "useful selections," just as in the **Philosophers' Dispensatory** <note>original: "antidotario philosophorum"; likely a reference to a well-known medical or alchemical compendium</note> only the useful selections of their books are mentioned.

## Chapter Fourteen: What Must Be Considered at the Start of Elections for Those Whose Birth Charts We Know.

In the elections mentioned above, those things were stated which ought to be considered universally; next, we must see those things which are to be seen first and most principally in particular cases. The ancients said that there are principally three things in elections. The first, they said, is to consider which of the planets is strongest in the **root of the nativity** <term>root of the nativity: the original birth chart of the person for whom the election is being made</term> or the **question** <term>question: a "horary" chart cast for the moment a question is asked</term>, and that planet should be placed in the **angles** <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, which are the most powerful positions</term> or in their **succedents** <term>succedents: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow the angles</term> if possible. It should be free from the "evils" <note>Mars and Saturn</note> and from other impediments, and it should be strong and fortunate, and placed above the earth, made lucky by a fortunate influence. If that planet is itself a **fortune** <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, it will be better; but if it is an "evil" one, let it be removed from the angle, because it would become so harsh in its operations that it could impede the matter, so that it would not happen, and it would seem that the same planet was more likely a cause of destruction. Nor should it be placed in a **cadent** house <term>cadent: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered the weakest</term>, because its virtue would not be strong enough to complete the matter; thus it should be placed in a succedent house, and so its virtue and power will be suitable for our business. 

One must also adapt the lord of the sign in which the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing luck and prosperity</term> was at the hour of birth or the question; similarly also the lord of the **revolution** <term>revolution: a "Solar Return" chart or the yearly update of a birth chart</term> of the birth or question if possible; and the Part of Fortune of the year's revolution and its lord, and the lord of the second sign from the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> of the revolution itself, and the lord of the hour of the election, who is called the **Lord of the Orb** by some. 

The second thing is that the Ascendant of the election and its tenth house be free from the infortunes and their prohibiting aspects. It is praised if some "fortune" is in it or aspects it by a **trine** or **sextile** <term>original: "fertili aspectu"; sextile</term> aspect. It is also praised that the Ascendant of the election be the same as the first house of the birth chart or question, or its tenth, or at least its eleventh, provided it is then free and was free in the birth or question; and there is greater impediment if it is not free in the election than in the birth. If this cannot be done, the sign in which the Part of Fortune was in the birth or question should be set as the Ascendant of the election, or the second sign from the Ascendant of the birth or question, provided it is free. If any of these cannot be done, as often happens, adapt the Ascendant of the election as best fits your search and the other things I told you. And if you cannot adapt what you want, adapt what you can, so that your election may be of value to the one for whom you choose. One could also choose in another way that would not be rejected: namely, that you set as the Ascendant of the election the sign that signified the matter for which you are choosing in the birth or question, provided it was free from the "evils" and their aspects—unless that "evil" one causing the impediment was the lord of the Ascendant sign of the birth or question, for then he does not impede himself. And one must beware above all other avoidable things that the Ascendant of the election is not the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house of the birth or question. And if you can...

## Chapter 15: Whether the matter proposed in a 
## question should be completed or not when an election is made for it.

->As has been said elsewhere, several wise men, when<-
->they wished to choose for someone but did not have their<-
nativity so that they could know if the matter of the question could be completed or not, would take a "question" for any matter to be started. If they saw that it ought to be completed, they would see whether it would be useful or not; and according to that question, they would choose just as they would choose based on a nativity. One of these was **Al-Khayyat** <note>original: "alchalat"; likely Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer and student of Mashallah</note>, and he would not choose for anyone in any other way. It seemed that their opinion was sound so that their elections would be perfect and secure. But it did not seem as useful as choosing for anyone who wanted an election for a matter they wished to begin. However, it was good to choose based on the nativity or the question. Yet, sometimes hasty elections occur for which we cannot judge questions or see their end according to the judgments; and yet it is necessary for the **astrologer** to choose for the one who consults him. I have already told you above that you can choose for anyone wishing to begin something, and your election will be useful to them as I showed you elsewhere, if I remember well. It is also true that through the nativity or the question we can know the end of the matter started or to be started, which does not happen through just any election. Nevertheless, we should always hope they are useful since we choose what seems best to us; for, as I have already told you, a good election can be of benefit, but it can do very little harm. Nor have I ever found that **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational authority on Western astrology</note>, who was the best astrologer, forbade an astrologer from choosing without the aforementioned nativities or questions. It was the intention of the **philosophers** <note>In this context, "philosophers" usually refers to learned astrologers and scientists of antiquity</note> that the evils signified by the nativity or the question could be removed by a good election; and if they are not removed entirely, they can be greatly diminished and lightened. 

There were similarly certain others who held that we should not choose except for those whose nativities we knew; but those people are few, and elections would benefit few if that were the case. For they said that the nativity is a natural thing, but an interrogation is not; rather, it is a non-natural thing. But even though an interrogation is not a natural thing, it is nonetheless very close to it. Just as the cause of a legal appeal is so close to the principal cause that he who later wins in the cause of the appeal is made stronger in the judgment of the matter already decided. 

There is also another way of choosing, and through it one can know whether a matter will be completed after an interrogation has been made: as if the Ascendant of the question were fortunate, or the Ascendant of the **conjunction** <term>conjunction: when two planets occupy the same degree of the zodiac</term> or the preceding...

If, however, it was unfortunate, it signifies an impediment that prevents the matter from being finished. But if a **nativity** <term>nativity: a birth chart based on the exact moment of a person's birth</term> or an interrogation is available, the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon; it represents the beginning and the "self" in a chart</term> of the election should be placed in the Ascendant of the nativity or the question, or in the sign signifying the matter we wish to begin, provided it is fortunate.

If that is fortunate, or its Lord, or the sign signifying that matter at that hour—and whichever of those you find most fortunate—make that the Ascendant of the election for the matter chosen. This applies both to those whose nativities are known or whose questions are held, as well as to others: this will similarly signify the outcome of the matter.

There is also another way to choose for those whose nativities are unknown and whose questions are not held: but this method is difficult since we do not know everything that happens to a person. But if some **great accident** <note>original: "magnum accidens"; here meaning a major life-altering event</note> of someone were manifest to you, you could know how you ought to choose for them in the beginnings of their affairs. This is even stronger, better, and more secure if that accident was the first major thing to happen to them, whether that accident was good or bad. "Good" accidents include **dignities** <term>dignity: a high office, title, or position of honor</term>, or some great magistracy, or similar things that were not customary for them. The greater that dignity was, the more its Ascendant will be like the Ascendant of the nativity of the person for whom you wish to choose. Likewise, the greater the evil was, the more its Ascendant will be in harmony with that accident.

But if that accident was evil, that Ascendant must be avoided in his elections, just as it should be adopted if the accident was good. Its contrary should be taken: namely the seventh sign from the Ascendant of that evil accident; from there you can choose for him if you do not have his nativity or question. An "evil accident" is said to occur when some great misfortune happens to him, such as an adversity that was not customary for him—like a very large loss of his possessions, a sickness, a shipwreck, a head injury, or similar things. Therefore, one must know the Ascendant of those accidents and preserve it just like the Ascendant of a nativity or question, if it can be known. If it cannot be done, do as I told you: otherwise, adapt what you can adapt so that your election may benefit the one for whom you choose.

And in this same way, we can consider when a certain planet is fortunate and strong, or a certain sign is fortunate, and pleasing and useful things happen to someone: it means that planet or sign has power in the "root" of his nativity. And when some sign or planet is unfortunate and brings him adversity, then that sign or planet has power in the root of his nativity. Similarly, if this happens to a Great Man—one of those, that is, who are fit for a kingdom—it signifies the power of those planets in the root of his nativity. You can say the same of any climate or region when some great, horrible thing happens to it, or even to a city, castle, or any building of long durability. When some sign or planet is impeded, it is a sign that it has power in the beginning of that building. Therefore, you can use that for its Ascendant in your elections. Or when great good things happen to it, you can do the same with that same sign and that

<column-break/>

same planet being strong and fortunate. The same applies to all movements of the citizens of any city or region: look to which sign or which planet they are likened, and you can give that to them as their **significator** <term>significator: the planet or sign that represents a specific person or thing in a chart</term>. This can even take place in individual and private matters.

### Chapter 16: When that which has been begun should be believed to reach completion.

When we begin something, and the Lord of the first house, the Moon, and the Lord of the matter we are beginning are in **angles** <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, which are the most powerful and active areas</term> or in their **succedent** <term>succedent: the houses following the angles (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th); they provide stability</term> houses, free from impediments and fortunate—or at least the planet signifying the matter we are beginning is so—it is a sign of success. If the matter is meant to be durable, such as the construction of a city or castle, or the building of a house, the planting of a tree, or similar things, and they are in a **trine or sextile aspect** <term>trine/sextile: beneficial geometric angles (120 or 60 degrees) that allow energy to flow easily</term> with the Sun by day, or even in the fourth house with reception, or with the Moon by night, or in aspect with those who are the lords of the houses in which they reside: it is a sign that the matter will be completed, reach a good end, and endure for a long time. Therefore, in such cases, you should always place the significators in **fixed signs** <term>fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; they represent stability and permanence</term> and in angles or succedent houses, strong and fortunate as best as you can.

In matters that we wish to finish quickly and which cannot last long, one places the significators in **cadent** <term>cadent: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses; they are considered the weakest and represent moving away or fading</term> houses from the angles, provided they are not otherwise impeded. These include unions, the strengthening of women, and their betrothals, for which we desire a quick end and brief duration. And if the Ascendant is a **movable sign** <term>movable sign: also called "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn); they represent initiation and rapid change</term>, it will be better, provided its Lord is not impeded.

For the speed and slowness of things are considered according to what the nature of each thing requires, just like size and smallness. For if a thing ought to be completed in one hour, and its nature requires this, but it takes four or five hours to finish, slowness is attributed to that thing; because it should have been finished quickly, it was finished slowly. For example, someone who invited others to a meal should have prepared the food in the third hour, but delayed preparing it until the fourth hour; in this way, the matter was delayed because it was not ready at the proper hour. Similarly, if someone should have gone to a certain place on that day, but delayed going until the following day, that journey was delayed because it was not on the appointed day. This is just like size. For "smallness" is considered in relation to its subject: there is a "large" ant and a "small" horse.

The same applies to speed: as when someone should go to someone who promised to give him a horse after one year, and he went to him before half a year or even before the year was up; in this way, he hurried to go where he ought to go because he arrived before the proper and appointed time. Understand this regarding all haste or speed, whether that speed or slowness be annual or momentary. And thus it can be said of various things according to different considerations and different relations, since according to the same year, the same month, the same day, and the same hour—according to any same time—slowness and speed can be judged.

The significations of all times are taken from the signs and planets, from the places in which they are, and from their natures. For **slow planets** signify slowness, and especially **retrograde** <term>retrograde: when a planet appears to move backward in the sky, usually signaling delays or reversals</term> or even **stationary** <term>stationary: when a planet appears to stand still before changing direction</term> ones, and most especially in the first station and when they are slow. "Light" <note>meaning fast-moving</note> planets signify speed according to the state of their motion, especially when they are **direct** <note>moving forward</note> and even more so when they are increased in number <note>speeding up</note>. From the signs, we take the signification of time: for **fixed signs** signify slowness and the stretching out of time; **common signs** <term>common signs: also known as "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces); they represent transition and a mix of qualities</term> signify a medium amount of time; and **movable signs** signify speed. And...

Also, signs of direct ascension <term>direct ascension: signs that take longer to rise over the horizon (Cancer through Sagittarius in the northern hemisphere), often associated with slower results</term> assist slowness, while signs of crooked ascension <term>crooked ascension: signs that rise quickly (Capricorn through Gemini), associated with speed</term> assist speed, as do the planets placed within them. Other factors similarly assist speed; fire signs do so even more sharply. Water signs, however, increase slowness, and earth signs even more than water signs. Angles <term>angles: the four most powerful houses in a chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th), representing active points of life</term> similarly assist speed. Cadent houses <term>cadent houses: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, often representing delay, illness, or things moving out of view</term> assist slowness, while succedent houses <term>succedent houses: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which "follow" the angles</term> seem to assist speed only moderately. 

Therefore, if one of those signs is rising, or if it is the house signifying the matter to be begun, or if one of the aforementioned planets is in one of those places, each will help or hinder according to the nature of the sign or the place in the speed or slowness where it may be. For example, if a fast planet is in a place, sign, or house signifying speed, it will assist that speed and the matter will be done more quickly. If, however, it is in a sign or house signifying slowness, it will lessen some of that slowness. If it is in a house or sign signifying speed, it will lessen some of that speed. If they are occidental <term>occidental: setting after the Sun in the evening</term>, they assist slowness and lessen speed. 

And Haly <note>original: "haly"; referring to Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century court astrologer whose work "On the Judgments of the Stars" was a standard textbook</note> said that the meaning is taken from the places of the signs according to which houses they are in. For he said that the Ascendant and the tenth house signify speed in days and hours; the seventh signifies slowness (that is, lesser speed, such as a month or a week); and the fourth signifies even lesser speed, because in place of months it could signify years. Succedent houses signify the same as their angles, but they delay the matter a bit more. Cadent houses signify slowness. And he said those things that are above the earth generally signify a more certain speed than those existing below the earth. And he said that the eastern quarter, which is from the Midheaven <term>Midheaven: the 10th house, the highest point in the sky at any given moment</term> to the Ascendant, signifies speed; the southern quarter, from the tenth to the seventh, signifies moderate speed; the western quarter, from the tenth to the fourth <note>The text likely refers to the arc spanning the western side of the sky</note>, designates moderate slowness; and the northern quarter, from the fourth to the first, signifies slowness. And he said whenever it happens that a sign signifying speed is in a quarter signifying speed, and if it is a moveable sign <term>moveable sign: also known as "Cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which initiate change and motion</term> as the Ascendant or the tenth house, this will be the fastest speed we can have from the signs.

### Chapter 17: From which planets the significance of time is taken.

The planets from which we take the significance of speed are the lord of the matter and the planet that joins with any of them, or the one that transfers the disposition from one to another, and the luminaries <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term>, and the planet to which the Moon is joined. And whichever of the predicted planets has more dignities <term>dignities: the essential strength or "rights" of a planet based on its position in the zodiac</term> or strengths in the Ascendant and in the 10th house of the matter—or at least in the house of the matter—from that one we take the significance of the time of the event we wish to know. 

And Haly said that the fastest speed and the slowest slowness of any matter in its kind and its being is signified by the planets according to their speed. And he said that the planets signifying the time in which a matter begun ought to be perfected (whether that significance is good or not) will give their indication when their state changes from strength to weakness or vice versa. And he said that the weakest change a planet can make is when it is in one quarter of the circle and moves from that into another, such as from the east to the west, or if it was below the earth and moves above the earth, or descends

<column-break/>

from the higher to the lower parts. And he said that their change is strong, such as if an oriental planet becomes occidental or vice versa, or if it moves from one sign to another—especially if it is a change from a sign in which it has dignity to another in which it has no dignity, or vice versa. 

Likewise, to know the time of a matter begun or to be begun—when it will happen or when it will end—you must take the number of degrees between the planet that is the Almuten <term>Almuten: the planet with the most combined strength (dignity) over a specific degree of the zodiac</term> over the place signifying that matter, and another planet that similarly has significance over the same matter. However many those degrees are, if the planet is one of those signifying hours, there will be that many hours until the end, durability, or perfection of that matter. If it signifies days, it will be that many days; if it signifies months, it will be that many months; if it signifies years, it will be that many years, according to the nature of the place, the nature of the significator, and the nature of the matter itself, insofar as it can be done or finished in hours, days, months, or years. 

For example: Let us suppose that Mercury is the significator of time and is at the 9th degree of Pisces, and Jupiter is at the 16th degree of Cancer, toward whose conjunction Mercury is now moving. There are 7 degrees until the completion of their conjunction. Now, since Mercury is one of the light planets <term>light planets: the fast-moving celestial bodies, namely the Moon, Mercury, and Venus</term> that signify haste, the matter now signifies hours, or in a matter that is not very fast, days. Therefore, if it is a matter of haste, the thing will be done within 7 hours. If it is something that ought to take a long time and is one of those matters of lesser speed that take weeks, it will be done within 7 days, or until the hour in which Mercury is in the 16th degree of Pisces, so that it directly aspects the degree where Jupiter was when the matter was begun or the question was asked, if its arrival at that degree occurs after 7 days. And if it were a matter that expects months, it would be done in that many months. And if it were among those expecting years, it would be done in that many years. 

Understand the same for all things according to the quantity of the distance in degrees existing between the significators; that will be the hour of perfection or the occurrence of the matter questioned or begun. And if there were a greater quantity of degrees between the significators, it would similarly happen according to that many hours, days, months, or years, according to its nature and relation to that matter. And if there were such a quantity that signs could be made from it <note>One "sign" equals 30 degrees</note>, the matter would happen in as many hours, days, months, or years as the signs resulting from those degrees, with fractions according to the number of degrees in the incomplete sign. 

For example, if there were 180 degrees between the significator planet (whatever that significator may be) and the planet it is joined to, from which 6 signs result, it signifies that the effect, durability, or completion of this matter will be in 6 hours if it is a matter done in hours as its nature requires. If it is one of those done in days, it will be done in 6 days. If it is one of those done in weeks, it will be done in 6 weeks. If it is one of those done in months, it will be done in 6 months. If it is one of those done in years, it will be done in 6 years—and perhaps a fraction might fall among them, but not one that leads into error. And so understand all distances of numbers of all degrees or signs, estimating all proportions as they occur to you. 

Likewise, if the significator planet of the matter is joined to another planet, or another is joined to it, and there is mutual reception <term>mutual reception: a condition where two planets are in each other's zodiacal signs, signifying cooperation and a positive outcome</term> between them, their years are to be considered. For instance, if it is in the angles and by the authority of the significator—that is, the one which has greater strength or power in the matter among those heavy planets <term>heavy planets: slow-moving planets, specifically Saturn and Jupiter</term> that signify years—you will consider the greater years <term>greater years: a traditional planetary period (e.g., Saturn's greater years are 57) used for long-term predictions</term> of the significator, and say that the matter will last for that many years. # Chapter 18. On fixed, common, and movable signs.

Abel <note>possibly a reference to a specific authority or a corruption of an Arabic name like Abu Ma'shar</note> indeed placed great emphasis on the signs and placed great meanings in them, and not in vain. These things are to be referred to the significators when they are in them, and to the Moon; to her above all other significators because she is the significatrix of all things, as is said elsewhere. Even if all other significators were left out, she is always to be considered, except that the lord of the hour <term>lord of the hour: the planet ruling the specific planetary hour of the day</term> preserves its place as I told you. 

For the said wise man said: fixed signs are suitable for every work where stability and the prolongation of time is <meta>catchword: sought</meta>

sought, and what its author wants to be durable and good. It is useful to build in them, and to celebrate weddings with a sacred betrothal in movable signs. 

If a woman is dismissed by her husband while in them <note>fixed signs</note>, she will not return to him quickly, unless many testimonies of the fortunes are multiplied in those signs. He who is bound <note>imprisoned</note> in them will have his imprisonment prolonged. He who is dragged into a lawsuit in them cannot be quickly pacified. Leases and wages, however, are useful in them. It is good to build and lay foundations. 

He said that Scorpio is the lightest of all the fixed signs; Leo is the most fixed; Aquarius is the slowest and worst; and Taurus is the most level.

# Chapter 19. On common signs.

He said common signs <term>common signs: also known as "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which represent transition</term> are useful for partnership and participation, and whatever work is done in them will often be repeated. Buying—that is, things we want to remain for a long time in the hands of the buyers—and celebrating weddings will not be useful in them, and there will be trickery and deception in them. He to whom something is objected in them will escape and be healed of that which is objected to him. He who is incarcerated in them is only signified to be in fear because of the smallness of his appearance and his exit, and he who goes out of prison returns to it. If a fugitive is captured in them, he returns to his flight a second time. 

He who goes to a judge in them will have no firm sentence or judgment, nor should anyone go in a ship in them because they will be changed from one to another for a poor reason. When something is permitted in them, it will be dissolved and not completed. A sick person in them is healed and then suffers a relapse. Therefore, whatever happens to a man in them, whether good or bad, is doubled upon him. If someone dies in them, then another will die soon after him in that place due to the change. 

Cutting, washing, shaving, and the refining of gold and silver are suitable in them, as is sending boys to their letters <note>starting an education</term>. The same author said: if you wish to begin anything in them from those things I told you, then place the Moon in the house signifying the matter you intend to do, and join her with a fortune as she recedes in that sign. 

He said that the signs of the day are stronger for a daytime operation; set the Ascendant to a diurnal sign or the sign signifying your matter. He said the air signs are suitable for hunting on land and sea, such as Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. The signs of kings are suitable for kings, such as Aries and Leo. Signs having voices <term>signs having voices: "vocal" or "human" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Aquarius), thought to be good for communication</term> are suitable for singers and those wanting to use musical instruments. Fire signs are suitable for every matter you wish to work with fire. Equinoctial signs are suitable for all equality and every measure, and every matter in which truth and the balance flourish, such as the scales and measures and weights of justice. 

Movable signs <term>movable signs: "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which mark the start of seasons</term>—and these are those in which the night and day begin to change—are suitable for those who wish to change from one thing to another or from place to place. He said: consider for every work you wish to begin what the nature of that sign is from the spheres, and join the Moon and the lord of the Ascendant with that substance. The root of that nature and its virtue is that hour, namely the hour of the inception. 

Consider the Sun in the deeds of lords, magnates, princes, and governors of cities and officials, as is said elsewhere. And in the deeds of the generous and those making great expenses, take consideration of him. In the deeds of farmers and villages, consider Saturn. In the deeds of generals and lords of armies and battles, consider Mars. In the deeds of scribes, painters, money-changers or bankers, pearl-merchants, and even merchants, consider <note>The text cuts off here, but would logically conclude with Mercury.</note>

### Chapter twenty concerning mobile signs
<term>mobile signs: Also known as cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn), these signs mark the start of the four seasons and represent initiative, change, and rapid movement.</term>

And know: mobile signs signify a festive mobility of things; nothing is durable in them, nor is the time of things done prolonged when the Moon and the significator <term>significator: the planet that represents the person or the specific matter at hand in an astrological chart</term> are in them. However, they are suitable for those who wish to sow, or to confirm a woman and betroth her; all these things benefit in them. Likewise, they are good for buying and selling merchandise, and for those things which quickly change from one hand to another. If anyone should fall ill then, they will be liberated and the illness will end quickly. If any dispute is begun then, it will not be prolonged. If anyone flees then, they will return quickly. If anyone promises something to another, they will not keep the promise. It will also be good and useful to travel in them. Rumors that sound then will be false, and dreams in them have no significance. Nor is it good to begin treating any sick person then—if the illness is such that it can be delayed—while the Moon is in a mobile sign. Nor should a tree be planted then whose durability we desire, nor should a stake be fixed, nor a building built, nor any foundation laid. Do not do or begin anything for which we desire durability or prolongation; but whatever thing you desire speed for, begin under them. Those are faster which have greater "tortuosity" and greater mobility, such as Aries and Cancer; but Libra and Capricorn are stronger and more temperate. 

And Zabel <note>original: "Zabel", referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology</note> said: prepare the Moon as best you can, and never place it in the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment an event begins; it represents the "head" or beginning of the matter</term> of any beginning, especially of any journey. For that signifies that some infirmity in the body or something equivalent to infirmity will happen to the traveler, unless the lord of the Ascendant or a "fortune" <term>fortune: a beneficial planet, typically Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring luck and protection</term> aspects the degree of the Ascendant. For when a planet "aspects" <term>aspect: the specific geometric angle between planets, through which they are said to "see" and influence each other</term> the Ascendant and its own house, it is like a man who guards his own home: because everyone who is inside fears him, and whoever is outside fears to go there; but if it does not aspect it, it will be the opposite. 

And if the lord of the first [house] is a malific <term>malific: a planet traditionally associated with hardship or destruction, usually Saturn or Mars</term>, make that aspect happen through a trine or sextile <term>trine/sextile: harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees that allow even difficult planets to work together more constructively</term>. Beware of placing the Moon in an "angle" <term>angle: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses—the four most powerful and active positions in a chart</term> when malifics aspect it or the lord of the Ascendant, unless perhaps it receives it from a trine or sextile aspect. Do not place the Moon in an angle unless it is "free" <term>free: unimpeded by harsh contact with difficult planets</term>; but place the fortunes and the Part of Fortune <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated point in a chart used to determine prosperity and physical well-being</term> in the angles. And act in all ways, if you ever can, so that the Moon aspects the Part of Fortune or is joined to it bodily <note>original: "iungatur ei corporaliter", meaning a conjunction where two bodies occupy the same degree of space</note>, though this can rarely happen. And if you cannot prevent the Part of Fortune from falling away from the Ascendant, make it so the lord of the Ascendant aspects it or is joined to it, as I told you about the Moon. And strive, if you can, to place the lord of the Ascendant with the Part of Fortune, for this signifies greater profit on a journey and greater utility. And beware of placing the Moon in the second, sixth, eighth, or twelfth [houses], for it is harmful <note>original: "bochorũ bile", likely a corruption of "abhorribile" (abhorrent) or "prohibibile" (forbidden)</note> and to be feared. 

Zabel said: if you can do so, strive to place the Ascendant, its lord, and the Moon in signs of "direct ascension" <term>direct ascension: signs that rise slowly and steadily (Cancer through Sagittarius), associated with smoother progress</term>, for it signifies ease and progress; do not place them in "tortuous" signs <term>tortuous signs: signs that rise quickly and at a slant (Capricorn through Gemini), often associated with complications</term>. For he said they signify involvement, hardship, and slowness. For the Ascendant and the fourth [house] signify what may happen from that election. Look therefore at the fortunes and malifics from their 

<column-break/>

places and their strength and weakness, and speak according to what you find regarding the strength or weakness of the beginning or end of the matter. And Dorotheus <note>original: "dorothius", referring to Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrologer whose work on "elections" was widely translated</note> said: when you find the Moon impeded and the matter is such that it cannot be delayed, do not give the Moon a part in the Ascendant, but make it "fall away" from it, and place a fortune there, along with the Part of Fortune and its lord. And by no means place the Moon in the Ascendant for journeys, whether it is impeded or not.

### Here begins the second treatise on those things which seem to pertain to particular elections.

### Chapter one, which is a preamble to the particular elections of the houses.

<image-desc>Historiated woodcut initial 'L' showing a scholar or teacher seated at a high desk or lectern, gesturing toward two students or figures standing before him. The scene is framed within the decorative structure of the letter L.</image-desc>

**A**lthough enough has been said above concerning those things that generally pertain to elections, what has been said does not seem perfectly sufficient for those who wish to use elections, unless they arrive at those things which look toward particular elections. From now on, these things will be like an example or collection of the aforementioned. Nor does it seem possible to descend into particular elections without touching upon some of the premises. It was said above that we ought to adapt certain things which are fundamental <note>original: "radicales", meaning at the root or base of the chart</note> in elections as much as seems possible, although it is impossible to always be able to adapt everything when we wish. 

These [fundamentals] are: the first [house] and its lord; the fourth [house] and its lord; the Moon and the lord of the sign in which she is placed; the Sun and the lord of the sign in which he is placed; also the Part of Fortune and the lord of the house in which it falls in the election; also the house signifying the matter for which one chooses, and its lord, and the planet which naturally signifies that matter, and the lord of the sign in which it is located. All these are to be adapted according to the words of the wise at the beginning of any election, so that the election is secure on all sides—as has been told to you, man, even if it will never be [entirely] possible. And I have already pointed out many times: you cannot adapt everything you wish; adapt what you can. 

And Haly <note>original: "haly", referring to the 11th-century astrologer Haly Abenragel</note> said that none of the significators should be weakened at the beginning of any matter we wish to start, especially if it was strong in the "nativity" <term>nativity: the original birth chart of the person for whom the election is being made</term>—if the nativity of the one for whom you choose is known—or if a "question" <term>question: refers to horary astrology, where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</term> is held, or in the "revolution of that year" <term>revolution: a solar return chart, cast for the person's birthday for that specific year</term>. And perhaps it will be necessary for us sometimes to weaken one of the said significators in some cases, such as weakening the Moon when going out to hunt, or in the investigation of a thief or another fugitive; and also [to weaken] the planet to which she joins herself, and to strengthen the one from which she separates. 

And there will be twelve chapters in this treatise, according to the number of the twelve houses, to which other chapters will be subordinated. It will not be surprising if some of the things named above are mentioned in them, since there are certain things with a "univocal" voice <note>univocal: using one term to mean one specific thing</note> that have "equivocal" meanings <note>equivocal: using one term to mean multiple different things</note>; and also sometimes a planet is placed in one spot for one meaning and in another spot for another. 

The first chapter is on the first house and its significance; the second on the second and its significance; the third on the third and its significance; the fourth on the fourth and its significance; the fifth on the fifth and its significance; the sixth on the sixth and its significance; the seventh on the seventh and its significance; the eighth on the eighth and its significance; the ninth on the ninth and its significance; the tenth on the tenth and its significance; the eleventh on the eleventh and its significance; the twelfth on the twelfth and its significance.
