## Concerning the First House.

### Chapter one: on the nursing of children.
**I**f anyone wishes to hand over a child to a nurse so that she may suckle him: it is necessary that when the <term>nurse</term><note>Latin: *nutrix*</note> first begins to nurse, the Moon should be joined to Venus bodily <note>meaning in the same degree of the zodiac</note>: and if this cannot be, let it be joined to her by a "trine" or "sextile" aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note> with "reception" from Taurus or Libra. And if Venus is "descending" in her <term>eccentric</term> or <term>epicycle</term> <note>technical terms for the paths planets were thought to take to explain their varying speeds and distances</note>, it will be even better. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer whose works were foundational in Europe</note> said that it is necessary that the matters of the father's "root" <note>the original birth chart</note> be adapted: you, however, adapt what you can from those roots; and if you cannot adapt all the roots, at least adapt those which involve Venus and the Moon.

### Chapter second: on the weaning of children from milk.
**W**hen you wish to withdraw a child from milk <note>weaning</note>, place the Moon as far from the Sun as you possibly can—namely, from 90 degrees up to 167. And **Haly** said that it seemed to some that the Moon should not be in any of the houses of Venus <note>Taurus or Libra</note> during this work, because they feared that the child's mother would not be able to pull him away from her breasts. And someone said that when we separate the suckling child from the nurse, if the Moon is in *Marchasa* (which is the twelfth <term>Lunar Mansion</term> <note>one of 28 segments of the moon's monthly path</note> and is located in Libra), the child will no longer care for milk. And others have said that the Moon and the "Lord of the Ascendant" <note>the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> should be in the signs of "sowing" <note>Latin: *sementum*, likely referring to Earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn</note>, because this signifies that the child will crave the eating of grains and herbs. And if it is in Leo, he will crave the eating of meat. And if it is in Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, he will crave the eating of fish. And if it is in other signs, he will generally eat those things which are given to him to eat.

### Chapter third: on the cutting of the nails of the hands and feet.
**W**hen you wish to cut the nails of the hands or feet, let the Moon be in a "succedent" angle <note>houses 2, 5, 8, or 11, which follow the main corners of a chart</note>: and if she cannot be placed in a succedent one, let her be placed in an "angle" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>; for the "cadent" houses <note>3, 6, 9, 12</note> are to be avoided. And let the Moon be increasing in light and in her daily travel: nor should she be in Gemini, especially if any of the "malefics" <note>unlucky planets</note>—Mars or Saturn—look upon her from a square aspect or from an opposition. For if Saturn looks upon her, it is to be feared that they will not grow back properly: or if they do grow back, they may grow back as "rinhoini" <note>likely *paronychia* or painful hangnails/infections</note>. If, however, Mars looks upon her from one of those aspects, it is feared that the flesh of the fingers may be cut, from which discomfort and pain follow: and perhaps that pain might increase so much that an <term>aposteme</term> <note>an abscess or swelling</note> or something similar results. And **Haly** said that she should not be in Gemini nor in Sagittarius, nor joined to their Lords: but let her be in Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, or Libra; but place her outside of the **Combust Way** <note>Latin: *viam combustam*; a specifically unlucky stretch of the zodiac</note> and see that she is not hindered in those signs. In the cutting of the toenails, one must specifically beware of Gemini, Pisces, the Combust Way, and the hindrance of the malefics.

### Chapter fourth: on the cutting of hair and the shaving of the beard.
**W**hen you wish to cut hair or shave a beard, let the Moon be in "common" signs <note>also called mutable signs: Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> except for Gemini. And **Haly** said there was a certain person who did not recommend Virgo, nor did he condemn Libra, Aries, Taurus, or Capricorn, nor did he assign a reason why: I, however, do not speak ill of Aries for the cutting of hair or beard—but for the shaving of the head and beard, I do. And he said that when the Moon and the Ascendant are in the signs of sowing, the hair and bristles will regrow and grow back more quickly. And he said that one must beware of the hindrance of Saturn and Mars then, lest perhaps "dandruff" <note>Latin: *furfures*</note> should form in the hair.

<column-break/>

### Chapter fifth: on the circumcision of boys.
**I**t has seemed to some that this chapter should be included under the Sixth House <note>the house of illness and surgery</note> because it seemed to them to be a kind of infirmity: to me, however, it seems it should be included under the First House: because it is one of the first "accidents" <note>events or qualities</note> of the body: just as it usually happens on the seventh day after birth to the body of the newborn: however, under whichever house it is included, the power remains in the hour of its "election." Therefore, when you wish to choose a time for someone to be circumcised, place the Moon joined to Jupiter by a trine or sextile aspect, or by a square aspect but with "reception": and let the Moon herself be to the north of Venus: and beware that Saturn does not look upon the Lord of the First House, or the Moon, or Venus from a square or opposition, or even upon the Ascendant itself: because this signifies the putrefaction <note>infection or rotting</note> of that incision: and let the Lord of the sign in which the Moon is be northern if it can be done: and the Moon moving toward an angle: and beware of Mars, let him not be in any angle: but let him be in a cadent house: if you cannot put him in a cadent house, beware that the Ascendant is not Scorpio, nor should the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant be in it.

## Concerning the Second House.

### Chapter first: on lending or receiving.
**I**n the significations of the Second House <note>the house of money and assets</note>, we cannot descend to particulars in the beginning without first setting forth other things that seem universal regarding life—namely, those things which pertain to substance or profit or anything from which profit is expected. It is indeed necessary for us in this matter to adapt the Lord of the Second House and the planet in whose house he resides: Jupiter must also always be adapted in every election that regards substance naturally, as has been said elsewhere. And **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century astrologer</note> said if you want to choose an hour for the receiving and lending of money, let the Moon be in Leo (except in its first <term>term</term> <note>a specific sub-division of a sign</note>), or in Scorpio or Sagittarius, and let the Moon not be in the first degree of any of them: nor should she be in Gemini, nor should the first term of any of them be the Ascendant: because these things signify good for the receiver and a gain for the giver: however, let the Moon be in "restitution" in Aquarius or Pisces, so that the Moon is decreasing in light: and let Jupiter and Venus be ascending to their "greater longitude," or let one of them look upon the Ascendant or the Moon or its Lord, or at least let one of them look upon them: nor should any of them be hindered if it can be done: at the very least, save what you can from them: and let Mercury be "clean" (who signifies coins naturally) from the hindrances of the malefics, and let the Moon be specifically free from the hindrances of Mars: because when the Moon in such a matter is hindered by Mars, it signifies contention, strife, distress, and denial in the recovery or restitution of the money or the loan. When, however, she is hindered by Saturn, it signifies entanglement, prolongation, fatigue, and much destruction in its recovery or restitution.

### Chapter second: on profit that should always remain with the one for whom you choose.
**I**f, however, the intention of the one for whom you choose is to make a profit that should always remain in his possession so that he does not hand it over further to another, let the Ascendant of the hour of election be a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius—signs known for stability</note>, and let the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the Second House be in fixed signs, free from hindrances, and let the angles not be "remote" <note>meaning the planets should be near the house cusps</note>. If, however, the election is for the profit of a thing that is to be sold or in another way alienated or turned over, let the Ascendant be a **mobile** or **common** sign: a mobile sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> is better for this: let the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon be in mobile or common signs: and let them be free from hindrances and let the angles be remote if it can be done: and in each of these cases, always adapt whatever you can from the "radical" things <note>the birth chart</note>. If, however, the intention of him who profits is to keep the thing acquired so that he may use it when he wishes, adapt the first house and its Lord.

### Chapter 2. On partnership and participation for the purpose of utility and profit.

**W**hen any two people wish to enter into a partnership and participation between themselves for their mutual benefit and profit, and you wish to choose a suitable hour for them: choose a suitable Ascendant and its Lord, and the Moon as well as the Lord of the sign in which she is located, if possible. Or at least let the Ascendant be a common sign and the Moon be in a common sign other than Gemini; and let the Lord of the sign in which the Moon is located be in a common sign or in Leo. For Leo, because of the goodness of the Sun, and the Sun itself, are considered suitable for partnership. Since the intention is to profit, place the Moon clean from all impediments of the malifics, and especially from a conjunction, opposition, or square aspect with them; let her be joined to the <term>fortunes</term><note>the "good" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>. And if she is in Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces with reception, it will be good. If, however, there is no reception, Sagittarius or Pisces are not praised, for reception signifies their profit. And if you cannot place her in the aforementioned signs, place her in Taurus and beware of the southern signs, except for those mentioned; and in these, let it be with reception. Of all of them, Libra is judged the worst because of the <term>Via Combusta</term><note>The "Burnt Path," a section of the zodiac (roughly the end of Libra and start of Scorpio) considered unlucky</note> existing in it, which signifies a bad illness in these matters. Let the Moon be increasing in light and in her daily travel; let her be received by a trine or sextile aspect, for this signifies that their separation will be good and with goodwill. For the square aspect and the opposition signify litigation and quarreling at their separation. If you cannot arrange all these things, arrange those that you can: namely, after the arrangement of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, look to the fourth and eleventh houses and their Lords, and the <term>Part of Fortune</term><note>a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note>, even if the wise men have not mentioned them. If you cannot arrange all these, arrange the Moon and the Part of Fortune, because it is necessary in this matter, or at least arrange the Moon.

### Chapter 3. On choosing hours for war or for conquering enemies.

**W**hen you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to go to war or to conquer enemies, arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, and likewise the Moon and her Lord. Weaken the seventh house <note>which represents the enemy</note> and its Lord, as well as the eighth house and its Lord. Make the Ascendant one of the houses of Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn; the houses of Mars are stronger than all of them, and Scorpio is mightier than Aries. Hence, if you can suitably place Scorpio in the Ascendant, place Mars strong and "fortunate" <note>well-placed and supported by good planets</note>. And although some seem to disagree about placing him in the Ascendant when he is the Lord of the Ascendant, it will nevertheless be very good if you can place another "fortune" <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> in the Ascendant with him. Arrange Jupiter by placing him in the second house, or the first, or the eleventh, to help the soldiers or

auxiliaries of the one beginning the war. Weaken Venus, who is the mistress of the seventh house, representing the enemy; and weaken Mercury for his helpers; place them in the first or second house, or place them <term>retrograde</term><note>appearing to move backward in the sky, a sign of weakness</note> or <term>combust</term><note>so close to the Sun that their power is "burned up"</note> or "falling" from the <term>angles</term><note>the four most powerful houses: 1, 4, 7, and 10</note> and away from any aspect of friendship (the 7th or 8th). If, however, the Ascendant is Aries, let Mars likewise be the Lord of the Ascendant, strong and fortunate. And weaken Venus, the Lady of the 7th, as was said. But if you cannot place one of the houses of Mars in the Ascendant, place one of the other houses—namely of Jupiter or Saturn—and place the planet whose house is the Ascendant in a fortunate and strong position, such as the 1st, 10th, or 11th house. Strengthen the Lord of the second and his helpers by likewise placing him in the Ascendant, or the 10th, or the 11th, or the 12th, fortunate and strong. Weaken the 7th house and its Lord, and the 8th and its Lord, by every means you can. Afflict them with misfortune as much as possible, and ensure that the planet that afflicts them (or at least one of them) is the Lord of the Ascendant, or at least the Lord of the 2nd, for that will be good. Beware of placing Mars in the Ascendant unless he is the Lord of the Ascendant; instead, make him aspect the Ascendant or its Lord from a trine or sextile aspect, for that will be good, provided he is not impeded. If he is impeded, apply all the "fortunes" that prevent him from reaching the Ascendant. And beware that you do not place the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the second house in an impeded state, nor place either of them in the 7th or 8th houses, for that is the worst; it signifies that they will be conquered. Likewise, beware of the 4th house, lest the Lord of the Ascendant join with a planet that is "falling" or in its <term>detriment</term><note>a sign where a planet is weakest</note>, unless perhaps that falling planet "receives" him. And if you cannot place the Lord of the seventh house in the Ascendant or in the second, make him join the Lord of the Ascendant, so that he goes toward him and the Lord of the Ascendant goes toward him; let their conjunction be such that the Lord of the 7th does not receive the Lord of the Ascendant, whether he himself is received or not. Let the Lord of the Ascendant be moving toward an angle in one of his dignities, elevated above the Lords of the 7th and 10th. It is also good for the Lord of the Ascendant to "transfer" light over the Lord of the 7th, whether he is a fortune or an infortune; let the Lord of the Ascendant be above the earth, and the Lord of the 7th be below the earth. And **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer whose works were translated into Latin</note> said: if you make them join in an angle, war will break out between them. ¶ And Haly <note>original: "haly"; referring to Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer whose works were foundational to European astrology</note> said that it should be hateful to those who are fighting to begin a war in the hours they call **combust** <note>original: "combuste"; literally "burned" hours, considered highly unlucky in medieval astrology</note>, regarding which I have made you prepare the "stars of war"—namely **Mars** and **Mercury**—as well as the **Moon** and the lord of its house. Therefore, look to the arrangement of the hours; do not be negligent in this nor allow it to be forgotten. And he said: know that when you have wisely led both armies to war as I told you, victory will be achieved by the one who was born at night, in whose **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> Mars had a part, because Mars is the lord of wars and to him wars are committed. And he said that perhaps they will make peace or abandon the war if the "exit to war" for both sides was made under the influence of the **benefics** <note>original: "boni"; the "good" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>.

## Concerning the consideration of the yearly revolution of the army captain.

Even if it is necessary to know the birth chart of the king or the captain of the army, one must look at his **revolution** <note>original: "reuolutione’"; a solar return chart calculated for the individual's birthday each year to predict that year's events</note>. If it signifies victory over his enemies for him in that year, without a doubt his side will win. If, however, it signifies humility for him in that year, there will be regret and another must be substituted in his place.

### Chapter 4: On the discovery of the combust hours.

You can find the **combust hours** <term>combust hours: specific periods of time calculated from the New Moon that are considered spiritually "burnt" or dangerous for new ventures</term> in this way. Consider the hour of the last **conjunction** <note>the New Moon</note> of the Sun and Moon and its minute, and begin from 그 minute and count up to 12 completed hours, because those 12 hours are "combust," during which things are to be feared according to what Haly said. For if anyone begins a war then, and especially in the first four of those hours, the loss of the battle and the destruction of body and soul is feared for him, even if he has otherwise made a good "election" for the start of the fighting. In this, many ignorant people are deceived, not knowing where that deception comes from, because they do not consider those combust hours. In the remaining eight hours, danger is imminent, but not as final. And after these 12 combust hours, there are 72 hours that are **incombust** <note>safe/not burned</note> in which men can conduct their business. And after those 72 safe hours, there are 12 combust ones. And after those 12 combust ones, there are 72 safe ones. Thus, by calculating from the minute of the conjunction to the hour and minute in which you are, you can know whether that hour in which you wish to begin the war is combust or safe. And if the adversaries begin to fight in those combust hours, that same misfortune will happen to them, nor will it be held against those against whom the battle was started. But because of the impossibility of arranging all the aforementioned things perfectly every time, and because men sometimes cannot wait so long, all their "elections" are assigned to the work of the astrologer to do what he can, since he cannot always do everything he wishes. Therefore, when you choose for the aforementioned tasks, ensure you place the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> in one of the houses of the superior planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, or Saturn</note>. If they are so disposed or so suited that the house of one of them should be used for the Ascendant, place **Leo** as the Ascendant and make the **Sun** fortunate and strong. Weaken **Saturn** as much as you ever can by placing him, for example, **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward, a sign of weakness</note> or combust, or in Leo or Cancer or Aries; let him not look upon his own house, nor any planet that returns his light to it. And weaken **Jupiter**, the signifier of the helpers of the opposing side, and make **Mercury** strong, the signifier of the helpers of the side for which you are choosing. And if you can arrange **Mars** so that you have him on your side, that is indeed good; if not, act so that the enemy does not have him on their side. Let him not be in the 7th or 8th house, nor let him aspect any of them nor any of their lords. Always weaken the 7th and 8th houses and their lords. Understand the same regarding Saturn and Jupiter. Always take care to fortify the Ascendant and the 2nd house and their lords. For as **the Philosopher** <note>Aristotle</note> testifies, a multitude cannot be killed where there is no victory against a multitude; therefore, against a multitude, an "election" is weak, and one does not clearly feel its help. Let the side for which you choose be equal to the other, or if it is smaller, let it be for a fifth part or a four-

<column-break/>

-th or a third, since beyond that it is excessive and you make the side you favor doubtful. And beware lest you place the **Moon** on the side of the enemies; and if she is the signifier—that is, if the Ascendant were **Capricorn**—weaken her to your best ability and fortify Saturn as much as you ever can so that your side may prevail. And it seemed to some of the ancients that the **superior planets** <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> when retrograde are stronger than the **inferiors** <note>Venus, Mercury, and Moon</note> when moving direct, but it is not simply so. Rather, if the superiors are retrograde near their "second station," they will be stronger than the inferiors moving direct when they are near their "first station." If, however, you cannot arrange the aforementioned things as I told you, delay your "election" until you can arrange them. If the one who consults you does not wish to delay, do not choose for him, lest perhaps you fall into disgrace through no fault of your own; let him do as seems possible to him. Perhaps it will be that his **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> is so strong that he prevails; and it is possible that what happens to him is what seems more likely, which is no wonder.

### Chapter 5: On the giving of banners or great flags or pennons.

Because it has seemed to some that this chapter should be placed before the preceding one, because the giving of **banners** <note>original: "vexilla"</note> is among the things preparatory to battle. To others, it seemed that the other should precede and this follow, because although the giving of banners is a sign of preparing for battle, it does not actually cause the battle; for men can carry banners and fight, or carry them and not fight. To fight, however, only happens if there is a battle; but I make no issue of this. The shaking of banners or other signs for battle is threefold: for it is either the giving or the confirming of the banner of the King, or of another nobleman below the King, or of a city or another community. And if several are found under alternating jurisdiction—that is, if the King wishes to give or establish his own banner—it is necessary that he gives it from his own hand or commits it to another who gives it in his name. And the "giving" and the "confirmation" differ from one another. For **Giving** is when a banner is newly given to one who was not accustomed to having it. **Confirmation** is when he confirms it for the one who has it then or to whom it has already been given. Therefore, if someone wants you to choose an auspicious hour for this: arrange the **10th house** <note>the house of kingship and high office</note> and its lord, and place the Moon in **Scorpio** joined to Mars with a "friendly" aspect, with a conjunction or aspect of some **Fortune** <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>. Let Mars be free from his own fortunes—that is, strong and not impeded. And if you cannot place the Moon in Scorpio, place her in **Aries**; but Scorpio is more praised, and let it be near the end of the lunar month if possible, provided the Moon remains safe. And if Scorpio could be the 10th house with the Moon in it, and the Sun in **Aquarius** in the region where Aquarius was then the 1st house and Saturn was safe, it would be good; if, however, Capricorn were the 1st house, it would not be as safe. If indeed it is the banner of another nobleman below the King and he is the lord of the war, it will be good for the Moon to be in Scorpio when it is chosen for him, because of the strength of Mars in that sign. Let the Ascendant be Scorpio as was said, and let the Moon herself be free and joined to Mars in a laudable aspect. If, however, it is the banner of some city or community or a nobleman who is not the lord of the war—that is, it is not his own personal war but he is acting on behalf of another—let the Moon be in the houses of **Jupiter** <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, pure and fortunate, and strong and free from all impediment. Let Jupiter also be fortunate, strong, and free from all impediment. Let the Moon not be in **Cancer** then, nor in the house of any "Fortune." This applies when he expects a determined battle and the giving of those banners, even if perhaps the battle follows later after that "shaking" <note>the ritual waving of the flag</note> which they sometimes practiced.

### Chapter Six: On buying arms, or war horses, or other instruments pertaining to war.

Just as it seems to some that the logic of the banners should precede the departure to war, so it seems to them that the buying of arms should precede the giving of the banners. But because fighting is the most powerful part of battle or war, it has seemed to others that those two things ought to come first and this third thing follow; unless you wish to arrange a time for someone wishing to buy arms, whether buying defensive or offensive weapons. Defensive arms include all things such as **mail** <note>original: "lorice"</note>, shields, helmets, and the like; or horses with that intention and cause alone, that they may be present for that purpose. Or if someone wishes to have the aforementioned arms made, or painted, or arranged in another way: you shall arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, as well as the Moon and the Lord of the house in which she is located. Place Mars freely in any of his **dignities** <note>signs where the planet has more power, like Aries, Scorpio, or Capricorn</note>, and let the Moon be joined to him by an aspect of friendship. At that time, the Moon should not be increased in light, but in the waning of her light, in her final **scotomity** <note>original: "discotomitate"; referring to the dark phase of the Moon</note> or near it, provided she is not **under the rays** <note>too close to the Sun to be seen</note> nor going toward **combustion** <note>the most unlucky position, within 8.5 degrees of the Sun</note>. And if you cannot make it so that the Moon increases in light, keep her from the aspect of Mars and from a physical conjunction with him; and let her otherwise be free from impediments. And if you cannot arrange all these things, at least arrange Mars as has been said: and place him free and fortunate—that is, both lucky and strong.

### On the purchase of horses.

In the purchase of horses, however, you can place a **common sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> on the Ascendant, and let the Moon be in **Taurus** or **Leo**. Let the planet to which the Ascendant is directly joined be fortunate; for this signifies that the horse will increase in size and value. If, however, the planet of the Ascendant is **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, the horse will decrease in size, although perhaps it may increase in value. If it is **direct** and descending, it will decrease in value, though perhaps it may increase in size. But if it is retrograde and descending, it will decrease in both. Understand the same for all other horses.

### Chapter Seven: On the reconciliation of enemies or those who have waged war against each other.

Since mention has been made of war and of those things which regard war in the preceding chapters, it seemed altogether appropriate that a discussion of concord or the reconciliation of enemies should follow immediately after what has been said about war and the fighting of enemies. When you wish to choose a time for someone wishing to be reconciled with his enemies, arrange the Ascendant and its Lord: place it fortunate and strong. Also the Moon, if you can, and the Lord of the house in which she is located. Weaken the Seventh House and its Lord; nevertheless, make that Lord fortunate even though you weaken him, and make it so that he joins the Lord of the Ascendant by a **trine or sextile aspect** <note>favorable angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, or at least that he regards the Ascendant from that same aspect. And Haly <note>Haly Abenragel</note> said: let the Lord of the **Twelfth House** <note>the house of hidden enemies and secret plots</note> be weak and **cadent** <note>falling away from the powerful angles of the chart</note>. And he said if that 12th House itself is impeded, it will be good; and the 12th and its Lord should be treated just like the Seventh

<column-break/>

and its Lords: that the Lord of the **Eleventh House** <note>the house of friends and allies</note> and its Lord should be arranged. And he said let the Lord of the Ascendant be in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th House, the highest point in the sky</note> or hold toward it, and let it be as strong as can be; likewise the planet in whose house it is located, and let it be in the best possible strength and fortune. If, however, the Lord of the 12th is among those planets who are friends to the Lord of the Ascendant, it will be better. And he said if the degree of the Ascendant and the degree of the 12th are of equal strength, this will be the best that can be in the arrangement of the houses. And he said if he who makes peace is a king, those things which were commemorated at the beginning of this chapter should be arranged: and let the Lord of the Ascendant be passing over the Lord of the 12th. If the signs from which the **significators** <note>the planets representing the people involved</note> are taken are **fixed** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; signifying stability</note> or of **direct ascension**, it will be better. If, however, the concord is made through the hands of legates or through letters, **Mercury** must be arranged. But if it is through actions and words in person, **Jupiter** and the Lord of the Ascendant should be arranged in signs of direct ascension, and the Lords of the Seventh and 12th in signs of **tortuous ascension** <note>signs that take less time to rise, often associated with difficulty or haste</note>. And he said it should be arranged if the intention of the one for whom you are choosing is to deceive the adversary by proceeding craftily: then let the Moon be in Aries, or Taurus, or Gemini, or Scorpio, or Sagittarius, or Capricorn, or Pisces. Let the Moon be joined to one of the **benefics** <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, or let one of them be in the Ascendant; and let the Lord of the Ascendant not be cadent from an angle, but let it regard the Ascendant with an aspect of friendship, and be in an aspect of fortune: it is necessary that the Lord of the 12th be weak.

### Chapter Eight: On choosing the hour for expelling or casting out a phantom or some evil spirit, which is called by some a devil, which is hindering or infesting some place or house, or from some person, or to destroy an oracle of idols or similar things.

If anyone wishes to cast out or expel a phantom or some harmful spirit from any place or house, which is called by some a devil, or any harmful or terrible thing infesting the inhabitant of that place; or if there is a disturbance in some person which is entirely demonic; and you wish to provide some medicine or perform some **exorcism** <note>original: "exorcidimuz"</note> or the like: and you wish to choose a suitable hour for this: arrange the Ascendant and its Lord. Beware that the Ascendant is not **Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius**; nor should the Moon be in any of those signs. Let the Ascendant be whatever else you wish and its Lord free, and let the Moon be in any of them joined to some benefic; let it not be impeded. In the destruction of houses in which idols are worshipped, or in which any prayer is made that is not divine, it is sufficient for you to weaken and make unfortunate the planet **Venus**.

### Chapter Nine: On the buying generally of all things, both movable and immovable, under which can be included the aforementioned chapter on the buying of animals.

...and things subordinate to it. Whence if anyone wishes to buy some thing and wishes that you choose a suitable hour for doing this: arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, and the Moon also, and place her in the First or Tenth House. If you can do this, let the First and Tenth be a **feminine sign**; the Tenth is more praised in this case than the First, or let it be in the Eleventh. Let the Lord of the house in which the Moon is located be safe and free from impediments. Let the Lord of the Ascendant be decreasing in number so that it travels in one day less than its mean course; and let **Mercury** and the Lord of the Tenth be safe and free from impediments. And Haly said if the Moon is with Mercury, it will be useful; and if Mercury is also decreasing in his course, it will be good. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is increasing in number and in **direct signs**, it is bad for the buyer. ### Chapter Ten: On buying seeds for fields or gardens, etc., such as grain, barley, beans, winter wheat, cabbage, and the like.

When someone wishes to buy any seed to be sown, from which utility and multiplication are expected, and wishes to choose for himself a suitable hour for this, let him arrange the **Ascendant** and its **Lord** <note>the planet ruling the sign on the horizon</note>. Let such an election be in the fourth quarter of the lunar month; and let the Moon be increased in number <note>likely referring to its daily motion or age</note> if it can be; let it also be in the tortuous signs which are said to be **augmenting**; and in any of the **masculine quarters** <note>sections of the zodiac chart traditionally categorized by gender</note>, because those also tend to augment, which are from the **tenth house** even to the Ascendant, and from the **fourth house** to the **seventh**; and let the Lord of the first also be in some of those places; let the **tenth house** and its Lord be free from the impediments of the "malefics" <note>the planets Mars and Saturn, traditionally seen as bringing bad luck</note>. C And Haly said: let the Moon also be with **Mercury**, and let Mercury be "oriental" <note>rising before the sun</note> and swift in his motion and free; which opinion I greatly approve of if it can be entirely observed; but if it cannot be observed, let it at least be observed that the Moon is arranged.

### Chapter Eleven: On the receiving and lending of money.

This chapter seems also to be the chapter on the **accommodation of money** <note>lending/loans</note>; wherefore it is necessary for him who chooses to use certain of these things which are used in that chapter. Therefore, if anyone wishes to receive a loan, it is required that you choose for him a suitable hour: arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, and place the Moon in **Leo**, **Libra**, **Scorpio**, **Sagittarius**, or **Aquarius**; and let it be **diminished in light** <note>waning</note> and in **aspect** to **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or **Mercury**. Let the Ascendant be any of the aforementioned signs, and let the Lord of the first house and the Lord of the **seventh house** <note>representing the lender</note> be free from impediments; and if it can be, let them be in agreement or "receiving" one another in some of their **dignities** <note>astrological strengths</note>, whether great or small. C And Haly said that some people hated the **hour of Mars** and the **hour of the Sun** for this matter.

### Chapter Twelve: On the hunting of land and water, of birds, wild beasts, and fish.

As has been said elsewhere, there are two modes of hunting: one on land and through the land; the other in the water and through the water. That which is on land is divided: for either it is in the mountains and through the mountains, or it is on the land and through flat land. That

<column-break/>

which is in the water and through the water is divided: for it is either in the sea, or in rivers, or in lakes, or in valleys, or in streams. Also, hunting which is done on land is either for wild beasts or for birds. Also, that for wild beasts is either for harmful beasts that bite or claw, such as **bears, wolves, foxes**, and the like; or it is for other beasts sharing with domestic ones in **rumination** <note>chewing the cud</note> or the splitting of hooves, such as **hares, roe deer, stags, boars**, and the like. Also, that which is for birds is either for **birds of the air**, such as **eagles, falcons, goshawks, hawks, kites**, and the like that live by prey; or for **doves, magpies** <note>original: "agatias"</note>, **cranes, large starlings, starlings, blackbirds, sparrows, quails**, and similar; or it is for **terrestrial birds**, such as **pheasants, partridges, terns** <note>original: "sterne"</note>, **quails**, and similar; or it is for **marsh birds** living in and near the water, such as **geese, swans, ducks, cormorants** <note>original: "mergones"</note>, and similar. That hunting which is done in the water is either with a **hook**, or with **nets**, or with other ingenious instruments placed in the water, such as **fish-traps** <note>original: "nasse"</note>, **conical nets** <note>original: "cuculli"</note>, **specialized traps** <note>original: "mermeili"</note>, and the like. C Therefore, if you wish to go out to hunt, or wish to choose a suitable hour for someone else wishing to go out: arrange the **Ascendant** and its Lord. Let the **seventh house** <note>which represents the "other" or the prey</note>, or at least the Ascendant, be of the nature of the species of hunting which the hunter intends to hunt; yet it is better that the seventh house be of that nature than the first. For if the hunting is through the mountains and for harmful beasts, let the Ascendant be a **fiery sign**, of which the best is the last half of **Leo**, and also **Sagittarius**; but this one [Sagittarius] is after Leo, and **Aries** is below Sagittarius; and let the Lord of the Ascendant be fortunate and strong, and similarly the Lord of the **sixth house** <note>the house governing small animals, including hunting dogs and hawks</note>. But if the hunting is for other ruminating or cloven-hoofed beasts, let the Ascendant be any of the **quadruped signs** <note>signs depicted as four-legged animals: Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, Capricorn</note> or other **earthy signs**. And if you cannot have it thus, have whatever you can from the other quadrupeds; but the aforementioned are better than the others if they can be had. C But if the hunting is for **birds of the air**, whether in the mountains or on flat land, let the Ascendant be any of the **airy signs** <note>Gemini, Libra, Aquarius</note>; let the Lord of the Ascendant also be fortunate and strong in a **common** or airy sign, and the Lord of the sixth similarly, or at least one of them. If indeed it is for **terrestrial birds**, let the Ascendant be an airy sign and the Lord of the Ascendant in an earthy sign, and the Lord of the sixth also in an airy sign, or let both be in an airy sign if you cannot do better. If the hunting is for **marsh birds**, let the Ascendant be an airy sign and its Lord in a **watery sign** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces</note>; or let the Ascendant be a watery sign and its Lord in an airy or earthy sign, and similarly the Lord of the sixth if it can be done. If this cannot be done, let the Ascendant and its Lord, or one of them, be in an airy sign. And do not forget to always arrange the **sixth house** and its Lord as best you are able. ### Chapter seven on the hiring or leasing
### of houses or lands or vineyards or their fruits
### or of other things which are leased and hired.

**I**f you wish to choose an hour for someone to hire a certain thing or lease it for a fixed price and a fixed return, or for a certain portion of the gathered fruits: or to receive from that thing what is appropriate, you shall arrange the **ascendant** <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the "election"</note> and its lord; also the **Moon** and the lord of the sign in which she resides. For the ascendant and its lord signify the person who hires the thing, while the seventh house and its lord signify the person who leases it out. The tenth house signifies that which is given for the hire <note>the rent or payment</note>; the fourth house, however, signifies the property itself and what will become of the lease and what will follow from it for both parties. See, therefore, which of the aforesaid places are fortunate and which are unfortunate. For if the ascendant and its lord are fortunate, it signifies good for the hirer, and he will be a true and legal producer and will keep those things which he promised to the lessor. But if he is unfortunate and bad, it will be the opposite. If, however, the seventh house and its lord are fortunate, it signifies that the lessor will keep those things which he promised to the hirer and will be legal and of good faith. But if he is bad and unfortunate, he will lie to his partner and will not keep his promises and will be fraudulent toward him. If indeed both significators are fortunate and good, each will keep faith with the other and both will be legal. If both are bad and unfortunate, each of them will strive to deceive the other and will be fraudulent toward him. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> said that the planet to which the Moon is joined signifies the one who leases, and the one from which she separates signifies the one who hires; yet he believed, as I do, that this is considered if the leasing was first moved by the lessor; but if the hirer moved it first, it will be the opposite. The lord of the sign in which the Moon resides signifies the end of the matter. And **Athabari** <note>Al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: let us arrange **Jupiter** and **Saturn** and place them so they look upon each other with a praiseworthy **aspect** <note>the geometric angle between planets</note>. And he said this so that the promises of the lessor and the hirer might be kept and be firm. And **Haly** said that in a lease the ascendant and its lord should be arranged, and if possible coming to an **angle** <note>the four strongest points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> in an earthy sign, and the Moon similarly, or let her be in an angle of the earth. The planet, however, from which the Moon separates should be free and in some of its own **dignities** <note>signs where a planet has specific strength, like its "home" sign</note>, because it signifies the land. And he said that the lord of the seventh should be fortunate and in agreement with the lord of the ascendant: and do this as best you can. The planet, however, whose conjunction the Moon seeks should be in agreement with the planet from which she separates. And he said that the seventh house and its lord and the planet to which the Moon is joined signify the lessor; and the ascendant and its lord and the planet from which the Moon separates signify the hirer and signify the mastery of both; and the fourth house and its lord signify the land. And he said that in the beginning of choosing land, you should use this same election.

### Chapter eight on the production of rivers
### or canals and similar things.

<column-break/>

**W**hen someone wishes to produce a river or a canal or other waters and you wish to choose for him an hour suitable for this, arrange the ascendant and its lord, also the Moon and the lord of the sign in which she resides: also arrange **Saturn** so that he is in the east: and to the lord and the ascendant let him be eastern, free from impediments, in an angle, and in some of his own dignities: and let the Moon be beneath the earth in the 3rd or 5th house in an earthy sign. And if she is above the earth, let her be in the 10th or 11th house. And **Haly** said that it is good for Saturn to be in the 11th house, provided that the Moon is not joined to him by body <note>meaning a physical conjunction</note>. You shall also arrange **Jupiter**, and let there be no misfortune in the 10th house. And **Alchindi** <note>Al-Kindi, the 9th-century "Philosopher of the Arabs"</note> said: let the Moon be in the first quarter from the Sun, fortunate and increased in light and number: and let her be in an angle of the first (that is, the ascendant) or the tenth or the fourth, and let the angles not be remote: and let the ascendant be a fortunate watery sign with strong fortune. The **Part of Fortune** <note>a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note> must also be arranged: and the lord of the conjunction or prevention <note>the New or Full Moon</note> which was before the election itself, and the other things that were said in the leasing of land: but if you cannot arrange all these, arrange those which you can: also let it be the aspect of the Moon especially: you shall also arrange the lord of the ascendant and the Part of Fortune.

### Chapter nine on the plantations of trees
### and fig groves.

**T**he methods of planting trees or shrubs are several: for they are either planted or "fixed" <note>original: "figunr̄"; refers to planting cuttings or stakes</note>. Likewise, among trees, some are planted with roots or clumps, such as figs, olives, apples, almonds, walnuts, and the like. Others are planted without roots and are said to be fixed, such as poplars, willows, and the like. Others are called shrubs, such as vines, wild olives, and the like. And of those to be planted, some are fixed at times, and of those to be fixed, some are at times planted: and any of these methods can be called "planting." When you wish to choose an hour for someone to plant trees or shrubs or to fix fig groves, begin with the **Moon** and place her in **Taurus** joined to **Venus** in whatever way is possible. And if you cannot place the Moon in Taurus, place her in **Aquarius**, but Aquarius is below Taurus. If you cannot do this, place her in **Leo**, though Leo is below Aquarius. If you cannot do this again, place her in **Pisces** or in **Virgo**: but these are below Leo, provided that she is aspected by some planet from a watery sign when she is in Leo: but above all others, Taurus is to be preferred. And let Saturn be in the first house, direct <note>moving forward</note>, or in the 11th or 5th or 2nd, in some of his own dignities or strengths, or let him have one of the aforesaid signs there. And if you cannot place him in the first house, place Jupiter there, looking upon Saturn; or wherever Jupiter may be, make him look upon Saturn with an aspect of friendship <note>like a sextile or trine</note>, and let he himself be in a place in which he has some "testimony" <note>astrological support or dignity</note>. And if neither of those can be placed in the first, place the Moon there, or place her in the 10th or 11th, or at least in the 5th or 3rd; and never place her "impeded" <note>afflicted by bad aspects</note> in plantings and sowings. And beware not to give **Mars** any part in plantings or sowings, except as in buildings: and make the Moon fall away from him, and the lord of the sign in which she resides, and the Part of Fortune likewise: and arrange the lord of the exaltation of the ascendant if you can do so: for it is not bad if he is preferred to the lord of the house in this. And **Alchalat** <note>likely Al-Khayyat, a 9th-century astrologer</note> said: let the lord of the Moon's house be looking upon her from a watery sign. And if the ascendant is not a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius—signs associated with stability</note>, let the lord of the ascendant and the Moon be eastern and ascending, or at least one of them. For if the lord of the ascendant is eastern and is ascending toward his **apogee** <note>his highest or furthest point</note> or his longest distance, it signifies that the tree which is then planted will grow quickly. If he is ascending but not eastern, it signifies that the tree grows quickly but will be slow to bear fruit: and this does not hurt in non-fruiting trees. And if he is eastern, descending from his apogee or toward a nearer distance...

And **Haly** said that someone once said the Moon should be placed in Cancer because Cancer is the house of the Moon; and the Moon is of faster motion than the other planets, which should signify the speed of the dogs. This same thing seems to be said regarding the instruction and training <note>original: "cognastructione"; likely a scribal error for "constructione" or "instructione"</note> for hunting.

### Chapter 16. On the purchase of birds with which we hunt other birds.

If one wishes to choose an hour for someone wanting to buy a **falcon**, a **goshawk**, a **sparrowhawk**, or similar birds with which men hunt other birds, prepare the Ascendant and its lord and place the Moon in Gemini, Libra, Aquarius, or in the first half of Capricorn; for the philosophers have said that the hawk is located there. The third house and its lord must also be prepared in every purchase of any hunting bird and other birds, whether domestic or wild. You shall prepare those same things in the instruction or training of the birds themselves so they may learn to hunt, and in the training of dogs that hunt birds, such as **scent-hounds** <term>brachī sensu: hounds that track by scent rather than sight</term> and similar types.

### Chapter 17. On the physician’s approach to the sick.

If a physician is called to a sick person, he shall first consider whether there can be a delay in going to him or not. If indeed he cannot interpose a delay so that a start could be waited for, let the beginning of his journey to the person be in the name of the Most High. If, however, a choice of time can be waited for, place the Ascendant and the tenth house in any of the **rational signs** <note>human signs: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, and Aquarius</note> if it can be done. And if this cannot be done, let at least the Ascendant be a rational sign; and let one of the **fortunes** <note>beneficial planets: Jupiter or Venus</note> be in it, another in the 10th, another in the 7th, and the other of them in the 4th, if it can be done, or at least let the said angles be aspected by the fortunes. If this cannot be done, let the said angles be free from the **malefics** <note>unfavorable planets: Saturn or Mars</note> and their aspects, unless **Mars** should be involved in the business of a wound or the opening of veins <note>bloodletting</note> or other useful shedding of blood.

For a fortune in the first sign signifies that the physician will be useful to the sick person. In the 10th sign, it signifies that the sick person will be obedient to the physician. In the 7th sign, it signifies that the sickness will be alleviated not only by the medicine but also by the very presence of the physician. In the 4th, however, it signifies that the medicine will benefit him. And say the opposite concerning the malefics in the aforementioned places. Also place a fortune, and especially **Jupiter**, if you can do so, or the **Part of Fortune** <note>a mathematical point in the chart representing luck and prosperity</note> unimpeded in the second house, because this has to signify the profit of the physician; or let it be joined to the lord of the eighth or eleventh house, and this similarly signifies the profit of the physician.

And if the lord of the second house or the lord of the first does not receive either of them, beware lest it be joined by opposition or a square aspect. And see also that none of the evil planets are impeded in the 9th house so that they have no testimony there; for it signifies that the physician will not acquire honor from that sick person, but rather he will acquire infamy or disgrace, with cause or without cause. If, however, a fortune is there, it signifies that he will acquire praise therefrom, both with cause and without cause; and even more strongly if that fortune has testimony there, provided it is not impeded. In surgical medicine, however, **Mars** is of less hindrance. And in whatever medicine they make

one should place Jupiter in the sixth house or at least in the 7th, but the 6th is better; because he who then administers medicine to the sick person will benefit him.

## On the seventh house and those things which pertain to it.

### Chapter 1. On marriage.

When anyone wishes to complete a union, or if you wish to celebrate a marriage or nuptials: choose a suitable hour for yourself to do this. The wise men have said: prepare the Ascendant and its lord, the Moon also and the lord of the sign in which it is; and let the Ascendant be a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> and similarly the Moon in a fixed sign. The wise men said the best of these were Taurus and Leo. But **Cahel** <note>likely Al-Khayyat, a 9th-century astrologer</note> did not praise Leo absolutely; for he said the marriage would be benevolent and that there would be firmness of affection and concord between them, but they will not care to increase their substance <note>wealth</note>, but rather they will care to destroy it in turn, unless the Moon, when it is in Leo, is joined to the Sun by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, for that breaks all malice; a **square** aspect <note>90 degrees</note> greatly diminishes it.

Scorpio and Aquarius are to be avoided, and especially for the man, because they are malicious and the houses of the malefics. Thus they have a tendency to harm the man. For a woman, however, they are not so malicious. For the Ascendant and its lord and the Sun and the planet from which the Moon separates <note>the previous aspect</note>, if the man seeks the marriage, must be the man's significators. The **seventh house** and its lord and **Venus** and the planet to which the Moon is joined signify the woman. The tenth house and its lord signify what shall happen between them; the fourth house and its lord signify the end and the virtue of the man and the woman. And **Cahel** said that it seemed to some that the fourth signifies the dowry. Another confirmed it.

And **Haly** said if the significators of the man and woman are in a masculine sign, it will be good for the man from the woman, better than for her from him. And if they are in a feminine sign, it will be good for the woman from the man, better than for him from her. And if the significator of the man is in a masculine sign and the woman's in a feminine, it will be good for both. If however the man’s is in a feminine sign and the woman’s in a masculine, it signifies that the union will not be well joined, nor will they rejoice well together, and they will be burdensome and hateful to one another. **Haly** said some take the significator of the one beginning the matter from the planet from which the Moon separates, and the other from the planet to which she joins; from which it does not seem to me I should dissent. And they give the Moon as the significator of both, and they give Mercury similarly. And he said the Moon should not be placed in a **rational sign** <note>human sign</note> because it signifies the "talkativeness" <note>original: "linguositatem"; suggests a nagging or overly vocal nature</note> of the woman.

And **Haly** said if anyone wishes to buy a female captive, the choice shall be the same; and if he wished to lie with her, it should be the same. And **Haly** said in the purchase of other female captives this is not considered, but rather what was said in the first chapter on servants. And **Cahel** said that Scorpio and Aquarius are useful for women and less malicious than for the man, and that the first half of Taurus is better than the last; and that the first half of Gemini is worse than the last; and that Aries and Cancer are bad. And he said that **Virgo** is not useful for a marriage <note>perhaps due to its association with virginity or being "barren"</note>, though for "corrupted" women <note>those who are not virgins</note> it is so. Libra is bad, and so is the end of Scorpio; for they say that a partnership from that time will be of little duration. The beginning of Scorpio is less bad for a woman. Sagittarius is bad, and the first half of Capricorn; the last half is less bad. And he said the 4th house and Pisces are bad, nor is there any utility in them, even when Venus aspects the malefics.

If however you wish to improve the choice for a union, place Venus in any of the houses of a fortune, received, or at least joined to them in their **terms** <note>specific degrees of a sign ruled by a planet</note>. And if she is in the house of any malefic, let her be separated from him and let Jupiter be elevated above her, or let Venus be joined to him by a trine or sextile aspect, though the trine is better; and especially if it is from the **water triplicity** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>. Let the Moon also be free from the impediments of the malefics, increased in light and number <note>waxing and moving fast</note>. Let Venus also always be in one of her dignities or in a place in which she rejoices, or at least in her own **chariot** <term>arz: a planet in its own dignity or a specific favorable position</term>; or let her be joined to Jupiter or Mercury, and let Mercury be fortunate and strong. And always beware of the conjunction of the malefics with the Moon by condition...

If a mill is built in a house to be turned by beasts or by mechanical tools, which is called a *posterna* <note>original: "posternã"; likely referring to a treadmill or a specific type of concealed mill mechanism</note>, let the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of work</note> be a fixed sign, whether it is an aquatic or earthy sign. If, however, it is a mill that is turned by the wind, as is accustomed to be done in certain places, let the Ascendant be an airy sign and the Moon be in the aforementioned signs, or in the Ascendant, or in the tenth or eleventh houses. ¶ And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arabic astrologer</note> said: beware lest the Moon be in Cancer or Capricorn; similarly, Gemini and Sagittarius are to be avoided because of the great inequality of days and nights when the Sun is in them. In every construction of a mill, let the Moon always be in her mean course, or a little faster if possible. If you cannot place the Moon in the aforementioned signs or use those Ascendants, but the Moon and the Ascendant are in other signs, Haly says that if it is with a favorable aspect of a **Fortune** <note>a "Fortune" is a beneficial planet, namely Jupiter or Venus</note>, it will be good; nevertheless, if it is with a favorable aspect of a Fortune, it will be better. The beginning of a ship-mill <note>original: "molēdini naualis"; a mill built on a floating vessel to utilize river currents</note> is when its builder begins to construct the first boat. The beginnings of other mills, however, are when the masterworks that constitute the substance of the mill begin to be built. And if it is a mill that requires a water-race, make the digging of the race begin when the other aforementioned beginning occurs. Do not by chance believe or doubt that anything contrary, superfluous, or diminished might be found in the judgments or elections of astronomy; always judge each chapter according to what you find decreed by the wise men, and do not care for what might be said elsewhere. You will not be able to err, but will always judge and choose rightly.

## Concerning the fifth house.

### Chapter one: on the reconciliation of a son with his father.

**J**ust as a father disagrees with a son, so a son sometimes by his own impulse disagrees with his father. Thus, if a father comes to you wishing to be reconciled with his son, so that an apt hour may be chosen for this, you shall arrange the Lord of his Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the sign in which she is; also arrange the **fifth house** <note>traditionally the house representing children</note> and its Lord, who signifies the son. Make it so that the Lord of the fifth joins the Lord of the first with an aspect of friendship <note>a sextile or trine aspect</note>. And if it is with **reception** <note>a condition where two planets are in each other's signs, strengthening their bond</note>, it will be better. Let the Lord of the first be in the first, tenth, or eleventh house, and let the Moon then aspect the Lord of the first and the Lord of the fifth, or one of them, so that their reconciliation may be lasting.

### Chapter two: on the sending of legates or messengers.

**I**f anyone wishes to send a messenger or a legate to any person, you shall consider the Moon in this matter above all other significators. Make her join the planet signifying the person to whom he is sent by a trine or harmonious aspect; and if you can, make that person "receive" the Moon, or at least the Lord of the first house. For example, if he sends to a king, make her join the Sun or the Lord of the tenth house; and let the Sun or the Lord of the tenth be the one to whom the Moon is joined in the first, tenth, or eleventh house. If you cannot place him in any of those places, place him in the ninth, fifth, or third, though this will be of modest utility. And beware when you send to or go to a king lest the Moon be in Aquarius or Pisces. If he sends to other nobles, or magnates, or judges, or the Pope, or Cardinals, or bishops, or other religious men, let the Moon be joined to Jupiter by the aforementioned aspects in an **angle** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the strongest</note> or in a good place from the Ascendant. If he sends to warlike men, let her be joined to Mars, but let that conjunction not be from an angle, nor let Mars himself be in an angle, but let him be in the houses following an angle. And if he sends to old men, or Jews, or farmers and the like, let her be joined to Saturn by the said aspects, and let Saturn be in a good state in a house succeeding an angle. And if he sends to a woman, let her be joined to Venus.

<column-break/>

And if he sends to a wise man, or scribes, or merchants, or to youths from the fourteenth year until the twentieth, let her be joined to Mercury; and beware lest Mercury then be afflicted <note>original: "impeditus"; hindered by bad aspects or being too close to the Sun</note>, nor any of the planets to which the Moon is joined.

### Chapter three: on the putting on of new clothes or the cutting of them.

**I**t has seemed to some wise men that this chapter belongs to the **first house** <note>the house of the self and the physical body</note>, since it appears to be among the things pertaining to the first. To me, however, it seems appropriate—though there is no great force in this—that it can pertain to the **fifth house** because the fifth house signifies pleasures and joys, and men delight in new clothes and rejoice in them just as in other delightful things. Therefore, when you wish to choose an hour for someone to buy, or cut, or make, or put on a new garment, arrange the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon, and place them in **moveable signs** <note>Cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note>, and let the Ascendant be a moveable sign. Let the Moon therefore be in Aries, excepting the seven degrees that are after the eighth until the end of the 15th degree of the same Aries, and excepting the 22nd and 23rd degrees of the same. Or let her be in Cancer, excepting its first six degrees and its last three. Or let her be in the first half of Libra. Or let her be in the first 18 degrees of Virgo, or in the first 19 degrees of Sagittarius, or in the first 20 degrees of Pisces. And the wise men said that **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> are not to be praised, except in garments pertaining to war. Therefore, you should not avoid the first 20 degrees of Taurus, because it is the house of Venus which signifies delights, and the Moon is exalted in it. But all unanimously blasphemed Leo. Whence **Ptolemy** in the *Centiloquium* <note>a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms attributed to Claudius Ptolemy</note> says: to make or handle new garments while the Moon is in Leo is dangerous. I do not dissent from them, unless perhaps the Sun aspects the Moon by a trine or harmonious aspect; and wherever you find her received with perfect reception, you shall not blaspheme her. If you can arrange her as stated, it is well; if not, place her outside of Leo, outside of Capricorn, and outside of the **combust way** <note>a section of the zodiac, roughly from late Libra to early Scorpio, considered unlucky</note>; nor ever place her anywhere afflicted, but free. ¶ And Haly said: arrange the second house and its Lord, especially in the purchase of clothes, and let the Moon be increasing in light. If you cannot arrange all these things, arrange the Moon for the putting on of new clothes and their making, and place the Sun in the **Midheaven** <note>the 10th house, representing the highest point of the sky</note>. For this signifies that the garment will be clear and beautiful. And if you can arrange nothing else, make sure the Moon is not afflicted, nor in Leo without reception as was said, and that the Sun is in the Midheaven. ¶ Certain foolish sophists were accustomed sometimes to ask why food does not harm, nor is it prohibited when the Moon is in Leo, since it enters the body, yet garments are prohibited which do not enter the body. To whom it can be answered thus: that food is potentially of the nature of the body; once received and transmitted into the stomach, its potentiality—through the motions of the bodies—is led into act by the collective and governing virtue of the body and is made into the substance of the body; for from the nourishment and the one nourished, one thing is made, just as from the food and the eater. Whence the body must naturally defend, guard, and retain it by the aforementioned virtue, nor can it oppose or hinder it. Garments, however, are "accidental" <note>in the Aristotelian sense: external and non-essential to the biological nature of the being</note> and do not have to defend the body naturally, nor nature itself; they have what they have only accidentally, since a person could live without garments, but not without food. And although garments contribute to the well-being of the body, they do not contribute to its being, nor are they of its substance. The superior bodies <note>the planets</note> work upon the putting on of new clothes solely through their motions, but in food it is not so; for although they work upon the consumption of food through their motions, they do not work without the benefit of nature operating intrinsically by transforming...

## ¶ Chapter 10: On sowing seeds which we intend to bear fruit in the same or the second year.

When you wish to choose an hour for sowing seeds <note>original: "feminibus," a common scribal/OCR error for "seminibus"</note>, it is necessary that in every sowing the **Ascendant** be a **movable** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn—signs of action</note> or **common** sign, and the Lord of the Ascendant should be in a movable sign if possible. As I told you regarding planting, begin with the **Moon** and work through her, for her power in sowing is to be preferred over the powers of all other planets. **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century court astrologer</note> said let the Moon be in movable signs; therefore, she should be placed in a movable or common sign that is of the earth or suitable for seed. But if she is in **Aries**, it is necessary that a planet from an **aquatic sign** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> aspects her, lest the planted seed dry out. Haly praised **Cancer** and **Capricorn**, but he praised **Virgo** above all other earthy signs for sowing, both for seeds that bear fruit in the same year and for those that fruit in the second year—such as those sown when they are planted, like cabbage, emmer <note>original: "zea"</note>, and the like—and for when they fruit in the same year they are planted. **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and physician</note> wished and said that the Ascendant should be a common sign and its Lord in a movable sign, aspecting the Lord of its own house, and it should be free from the **Malefics** <note>Mars and Saturn</note>. For if the Malefics aspect it, the seed will encounter an impediment. Let the Moon be increased in light <note>waxing</note> and in number <note>moving faster than her average daily speed</note>; for if she is under the sun's rays <note>combust</note> or decreasing in number, it signifies that the seed will be diminished and only a little will grow from it. Because of this, **Taurus** is praised, but it makes the form and quantity of what is sown sparse; therefore, one must cast more seed than is customary, though not exceeding reason. It is estimated that the last half of **Sagittarius** is useful in sowings, and **Pisces** is also praised. If indeed it is the seed of trees—as sometimes people sow to later transplant the trees that grow from those seeds more orderly—let the Moon be in **Taurus**. However, if you cannot fit all the aforementioned conditions, place the Moon in **Virgo**, free from impediments, and you have prepared the hour for sowing.

## ¶ Chapter 11: On the beginning of the cultivation of inheritances.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to begin cultivating an inheritance that he has taken up or which another has left to him: prepare the **Ascendant**, its Lord, the Moon, and the planet in whose house she resides, so that all are **received** <note>a condition where a planet is in a sign ruled by another</note>, and the planet that receives any of them should be in an **Angle** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or a **Succedent** <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> house, free from impediments. If all these cannot be done, let at least the Moon be received by a strong and fortunate planet, and let her be in a good house. Do this if you can, so that a **Fortune** <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> free from impediments is in the **second house** <note>the house of wealth and resources</note>. **Al-Kindi** <note>9th-century philosopher known as "the Philosopher of the Arabs"</note> said: let the lady of the **Part of Fortune** and of every conjunction or prevention <note>the New or Full Moon preceding the event</note> be in some Angle, or moving toward one; and let the Lord of the sign in which the Moon is be a Fortune. If all these are lacking, at the very least ensure the Moon is in the Ascendant or in a good house, and that she is received.

## ¶ Chapter 12: On the construction of ships or galleys.

<column-break/>

There are three types of ship construction; all others are subordinate to these. For it is either the construction of a **galley** or an *epibatis* <note>original: "egpolletis," likely referring to a specialized warship or boarding vessel</note> for attacking enemies; or it is the construction of a **great ship** for transport; or it is a ship for other common navigations, such as for minor merchants and the like. When someone wishes to build a galley or another ship for speed, for attacking enemies, or for riding the sea in some other fast manner: prepare the **Ascendant** and its Lord, the Moon, and the planet in whose house she resides. Place them in the Ascendant, the **tenth**, or the **eleventh** house. Let the Ascendant be a **fixed sign**, and if possible, let the other Angles also be fixed signs. Prepare the **fourth house** and its Lord, since it naturally signifies the ship itself. If you can, make it an **aquatic sign**, or at least place its Lord in an aquatic sign, free from impediment and joined to some Fortune. See if the planet from which the Moon separates is strong and fast. If you cannot place the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon in the tenth house, place a strong Fortune there—one having strong dignity in that place—and let it be **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note> and fast in its course. By all means, let the Lord of the **seventh house** <note>representing the enemy</note> be weak and slow in its course. If, however, it is a ship for transport, let the Moon be at her **mean course** <note>her average speed</note> according to the things mentioned above; so that she does not travel more in one day than her mean course. Even if she travels three or four minutes less in a day, it will not be bad, for fear that she might be damaged by excessive speed. If it is one of the other aforementioned ships, prepare them as stated, but it does not matter whether the Moon is fast or not, provided she is not very slow—that is, she should not move less than 31 minutes more than her [minimum] daily course. Strive to prepare the Lord of the **conjunction** or **prevention** <note>the preceding New or Full Moon</note> to the best of your ability, for this is good. When the Moon has separated from another planet, ensure she joins with a Fortune. If the Lord of the Ascendant is not in an Angle, make sure he is moving toward one. **Haly** said that some affirmed it is good if the Moon is in **Taurus** or **Gemini**. He also said to beware of the aspect of **Mars** with the Moon, or with the Lord of the Ascendant, or with the Lord of the fourth house in the construction of ships. Haly said it is poor if the Moon is above the earth <note>in the visible hemisphere</note>. He said these same things should be prepared for the launching of ships into the water and for their purchase. You, however, prepare all that you can; always take care to prepare the Moon. When the **mast** <note>original: "arbor," literally "tree"</note> is erected in the ship, then you must especially prepare the **tenth house** and its Lord, and the Moon should likewise be placed there.

## ¶ Chapter 13: On the construction of a mill.

One kind is built on ships; another is built on a balance, so that it is raised or lowered at the will of its operator, and this is called a **pendulum mill**. Another is built fixed, so that it is neither lowered nor raised, but remains firm, and this is called a **transverse mill**. Another is built in an inhabited house to be turned by some animal or with some stable instrument, and this is called a **postern mill** <note>likely a treadmill or indoor animal-driven mill</note>. Another is built in high places to be turned by the wind, and this is called a **wind mill**. Their elections are to be varied according to these different methods of building. Thus, if someone wishes to build any of the aforementioned mills and comes to you to choose a suitable hour: if it is a mill on **ships**, let the Ascendant be the last half of **Pisces** or the last part of **Virgo**. If it is a mill suspended on a balance or on ships, which is called a **pendulum**, let the Ascendant be the first half of **Aries** or the first half of **Libra**, because both of these signify equality. If indeed it is a **fixed mill** that is not raised or lowered, which is called a transverse mill...
