Similarly, **Jupiter** should be prepared, which naturally signifies "natural substance" <note>original: "substābam naturaliter," likely meaning one's inherent wealth or physical constitution</note> acquired through honest means, so that an expanded utility might be preserved and drawn into the state of the person receiving the increase, becoming habitual. When Jupiter has given some increase already acquired, or has sent it to someone, one must prepare the **fifth house** and its lord, along with Jupiter; and let the **Moon** in both cases be falling away from the **Ascendant** and its lord. Also consider the Moon's relation to the planet in whose house she resides, and similarly the **second house** and its lord, the **Part of Fortune**, the **Part of Substance**, and the **fifth house** and their lords. And if it can be done, let the second and fifth houses be in **common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces—signs that allow for change and growth</note>, of which **Sagittarius** and **Pisces** are the best; **Virgo** is below these, and **Gemini** is below Virgo. One must also beware lest **Saturn** behold the Moon, the Ascendant, its lord, the Part of Fortune, or the Part of Substance without "reception" <note>an astrological relationship where planets "host" each other</note>; and let the lord of the Ascendant be elevated above the seventh house of all. If you cannot do all these things, at least prepare the Moon and the seat of the house, and Jupiter in a "reception of increases"; or in a nativity <note>a birth chart</note>, the Moon and the lord of the fifth house, and Jupiter or the Part of Fortune.

<margin>About the sixth house.</margin>

### Chapter 1: On treating the sick.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to heal a sick person, look to see if the illness is universal throughout the whole body, or if it is particular to a specific part—namely, a special limb like the eye or the ear, or some other "official" limb <note>a functional or instrumental part of the body</note> such as the arm, hand, or similar. If the illness is in the whole body, let the **Ascendant** be one of the **human signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note>, of which **Libra** is most praised. For the Ascendant signifies the whole body unless a limb is specifically identified. But if the illness is in a specific one of the twelve parts of the human body named below—which are the head, neck, arms, shoulders, chest, back, belly, genitals, hips, knees, shins, and feet—<term>Arthephius said</term> <note>Arthephius was a medieval alchemical and astrological authority</note> let the Ascendant be that sign to which the sick limb is assigned. Also, let the lord of the first house be free from impediments, and let the planet signifying that limb be safe and free; and the Moon must be prepared. And <term>Haly said</term> <note>referring to Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> one must beware lest the Moon be in opposition to the lord of the "falling" house <note>the 6th or 12th houses</note> or the eighth house. If that planet is a "fortune" <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> and in a trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, it is not to be feared. But if it is a "malefic" <note>Saturn or Mars</note> and the lord of the falling or eighth house, let the Moon not be in any aspect with it. If you cannot avoid her being in aspect with one of them, let it be in trine or sextile and not from any other, nor in a bodily conjunction, nor should the Moon be descending. And **Messahala** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari, a prominent 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer</note> said that the Moon should be in the sign assigned to the limb that is sick when it is being treated. Understand this to apply to pharmacy, anointing, or applying plasters, but **not** for surgery where the limb is touched with iron or fire or similar; according to that saying of **Ptolemy** in the *Centiloquium*: touching a limb with iron while the Moon is in the sign assigned to that limb is dangerous.

### Chapter 2: On taking medicine on the occasion of some illness.

When you wish to choose an hour for a sick person to take some medicine for the purpose of expelling an illness—such as migraines, toothache, spasms, belly pain, and similar—which are treated through ointments, plasters, or the application of cupping glasses <note>original: "em cuffarū," likely *cupparum*</note> or sponges and the like, <term>Zahel said</term> <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century astrologer</note> let the Ascendant be **Libra** or **Scorpio** and the Moon in it joined to the "fortunes." Let none of the "malefics" be placed in the "angle" of the Moon; if she cannot be kept from the aspects of the malefics, let it be by a trine or sextile aspect. She should not be "besieged" <note>trapped between two malefic planets</note> or hindered by the rays of the two malefics, nor be "combust" <note>too close to the Sun</note> or moving toward combustion. Rather, let her be free and unhindered, for if she is not free, the medicine brings pain and hindrance to the sick person.

### Chapter 3: On universal care to be applied to the head.

<column-break/>

If you wish to choose an hour for any medicine applied universally to the head, or for any humor descending from the head—such as vomiting, gargles, and the like—let the Ascendant be **Aries** and the Moon in it or in **Taurus**; and let her be joined to any of the "fortunes" while she is diminished in light. And **Zahel** said: beware of the fourth aspect <note>a square aspect</note> of the Sun or its opposition in Aries, specifically because of the Sun's heat.

### Chapter 4: When you wish to apply care to the nostrils.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to treat the nostrils with ointments or other things—such as sneezing powders or suffumigations and the like—place **Cancer**, **Leo**, or **Virgo** as the Ascendant; let the Moon be in the Ascendant joined with one of the "fortunes." Beware of the conjunction of any "infortune" <note>malefic planet</note> with her, and let her not be joined to any planet hindered by retrograde motion, combustion, "fall" <note>a position of weakness</note>, or by any other way.

### Chapter 5: When you wish to treat the eyes.

For the eyes—as if there were a spot, blister, ulcer, "nail" <note>likely a pterygium, a growth on the eye</note>, ophthalmia, or anything that must be removed by surgery, any other instrument, or by medicines—let this be when the Moon is increasing in light and in number <note>moving faster than average</note>, and joined to a "fortune." And **Zahel** said: beware of her conjunction with **Mars** when she is increasing in light and number. Let **Jupiter** be above the earth in the Ascendant—namely, the first, eleventh, or ninth house. If you cannot place him in these locations, let him behold the Ascendant from a trine or sextile aspect, or at least from a fourth <note>square</note>, provided he is not himself hindered. And beware lest she or the Ascendant be in **earthly signs** <note>Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn</note>. If you can avoid the conjunction of the Moon with Mars, postpone your work until she is separated from him and leave off all eye treatments then; however, at the end of the month, it is less harmful. Yet **Zahel** said the "wise ones" <note>the ancient authorities</note> agree on the hindrance of Mars in the head; and they said that for everything cured by iron or fire, the Moon should **not** be in the sign signifying the limb being treated, nor in a **movable** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> or **common** sign. They said that when she is ill-disposed with Mars or Saturn, if any part of the body is cut or pierced, it putrefies. They also said that in all these things, one must beware of the Moon's conjunction [with the Sun] and its "prevention" <note>the time just before the new moon</note> until she passes the Sun by at least 12 degrees.

### Chapter 6: On the special care of any other official limb.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to treat any other part of the body: If the illness is in the **neck**, let the Ascendant be **Taurus** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **shoulders, arms, or hands**, let the Ascendant be **Gemini** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **chest**, let the Ascendant be **Cancer** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **back or spine**, let the Ascendant be **Leo** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **belly, navel, or adjacent parts**, let the Ascendant be **Virgo** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **genitals**, let the Ascendant be **Libra** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **hip**, let the Ascendant be **Scorpio** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **thigh**, let the Ascendant be **Sagittarius** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **knees**, let the Ascendant be **Capricorn** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **shins**, let the Ascendant be **Aquarius** and the Moon in it. If it is in the **feet**, let the Ascendant be **Pisces** and the Moon in it. And always understand that the lord of the Ascendant must be safe and free from impediments if it can be done in any way. If it cannot be done, always place **Jupiter** in the **sixth house**; this will be no less effective than the instructions above. And **Messahala** said: in every treatment, look to the location of the infirmity in the body. If it is in the head, throat, shoulders, arms, or hands, treat it when the Moon is in **Aries, Taurus, or Gemini**, which are the superior parts. And if it is in the chest, back, belly, or navel...

And if it is in the knees, the shins, or the feet, treat it when the Moon is in **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**, or **Pisces**, which is the lowest part. And if it is from the chest down to the lower part of the feet, it should be treated when the Moon is between the Midheaven and the Angle of the Earth, which is the "sunken" or lowest part of the circle. However, always keep this in memory: do not touch a limb with iron or fire <note>referring to surgery or cautery</note> while the Moon is in the zodiac sign assigned to that limb; but in other medicines and cures, such as drugs, ointments, poultices, and the like, you may treat it safely.

### Chapter Seven: Regarding medicines performed through surgery.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone you intend to heal through surgery, let the Moon be increasing in light and number; let her also be made fortunate by **Jupiter** or **Venus**. And **Alchafat** <note>a medieval spelling of an Arabic astrological authority, likely Al-Kaffat</note> said one must beware of every hindrance from **Mars**: for he said that the Moon is more hindered by Mars when she is in the increase of her light, and less when she is in her decrease; conversely, in her decrease, she is more hindered by **Saturn** and less when she is in her increase. And it is seen that the Moon should be in a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius—signs that favor stability</note>, and she should not behold the sign signifying the limb being treated with iron by any aspect; nor should the lord of the Ascendant be in that sign, nor should that sign be the Ascendant, nor the lord of the Ascendant. Nor is the Moon falling <note>in a cadent house</note> good; rather, let the lord of the Ascendant be in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven. And follow the same method in the treatment of the eyes for an abscess, a blemish, or whiteness <note>likely cataracts or corneal scarring</note>; and adapt the sign and the planet signifying that limb. I recommend this opinion if it can be followed; but if it cannot be followed entirely, let it be followed at least in that part which can be observed: especially that the Moon and the lord of the Ascendant (or at least the Moon) be adapted so that she is not in the sign assigned to that limb, nor in conjunction or aspect with any of the "malifics" <note>Saturn or Mars</note>.

### Chapter Eight: On choosing the hour for one wishing to perform phlebotomy <note>bloodletting</note>.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wishing to perform phlebotomy <term>phlebotomy: the surgical opening of a vein to withdraw blood for health reasons</term>, adapt the Ascendant and its lord so that the Ascendant is not **Gemini**, nor is the Moon in it. And beware lest Mars or Saturn be in the Ascendant; nor should the Moon be in opposition to either of them. However, let her be joined to Mars by a **trine** or **sextile** <note>original: "fertili aspectu," referring to favorable 120-degree or 60-degree angles</note> in this work, provided that her aspect to him is not from **Taurus**, so that she is in none of these, nor is Mars ascending in the north or in the circle of his apogee. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arabic astrologer</note> said that the lord of the house of the Moon should be beholding her with a praiseworthy aspect. And he said some have said to beware of **Taurus** and **Leo** in this work; and it is testified that the signs of these two are not to be feared, especially if a "fortune" is in them. Nevertheless, I have found that the bodily conjunction of the Moon with **Jupiter** is prohibited in the letting of blood through phlebotomy; and I find other wise men who speak of phlebotomy of the arm <note>original: "brachy," from the Greek brachion</note>. And some have said that if it is necessary to let a small amount of blood,

<column-break/>

let the Moon be in **Libra** or **Scorpio**. I, however, recommend the first half of Libra; and if **Mars** <note>original: "mare," likely a slip for "mars"</note> beholds the Moon with a praiseworthy aspect, I recommend the last half of Scorpio. And the wise men hated the **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note> because they prohibited the conjunction of the Moon with **Mercury** or with **Saturn**; and they hated **Virgo**, **Capricorn**, and **Pisces**; and they would place the Moon in the waning of her light. And those same wise men said that the **second house** from the house of the Moon would not be unfortunate; all these things they said were to be avoided unless the aspect of the "fortunes" <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> was present. And there it is seen that all of **Aries** and the first half of **Libra**, as I said, are praiseworthy, even if they are movable. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that Mars is a "fortune" in this work, except in those things pertaining to blood, the opening of veins, and the letting of blood through cupping glasses <note>original: "ventosas"</note> or in treating the sick; this is true when the Moon is in the waning of her light and joined to him by an aspect of friendship. And **Alchindi** <note>Al-Kindi, a 9th-century philosopher and astrologer</note> said it is necessary for the Moon to be in an **Air** or **Fire** sign, and their lords as well. Nor should any limb be touched when the Moon and the lord of the Ascendant are in the sign of that limb. They also praised that the lord of the Midheaven should be a "fortune" beholding the Moon or the lord of the Ascendant, and that the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon should be in the **fourth house**, because those things of the Air are better after the "prevention" <note>likely referring to the syzygy or the previous New Moon</note>. And they said bloodletting at the start of the month is more to be praised, which I say applies to those who need phlebotomy from the age of 45 onwards. One must also beware of the presence of the lord of the **eighth house** <note>the house of death</note> with the Moon. And one must beware lest the Moon be under the rays of the Sun <note>within 17 degrees of the Sun</note> or in "combust degrees" <note>certain degrees of the zodiac considered weakened or dangerous</note>.

### Chapter Nine: On giving purgative medicines and bowel movements.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wishing to take medicine by mouth to induce a bowel movement, adapt the Ascendant and its lord if you can; if they cannot be adapted, place the Moon in the last half of **Libra** or the first half of **Scorpio**; and let the planet in whose house she resides—whether it be **Venus** or **Mars**—be free from hindrance, fortunate, and strong. And if you can place any of these two signs [in the Ascendant], it will be good. Similarly, place the Ascendant in one of the **southern signs** and let its lord be safe. Likewise, if the Moon cannot be placed in Libra or Scorpio as I said, let her at least be in some of those southern signs. And if the purgation is for a sickness of a specific limb, let the Moon be in the sign signifying that limb. And if it is for the beginning of these signs, then let that medicine [be taken when] the Moon or the Ascendant is in a **Fire sign**. And if you wish to cool the body, let the Moon or the Ascendant be in a **Water sign**. And if you wish to dry, let them be in an **Earth sign**. And if you wish to moisten, let them be in an **Air sign**. And one must beware lest the Moon or the Ascendant be in **ruminant signs** <note>zodiac signs representing animals that chew the cud: Aries, Taurus, the last half of Sagittarius, and Capricorn</note>, especially the Moon; for these signify nausea and vomiting: **Capricorn** is worse than the others; **Aries** is below it; **Taurus** is below Aries; and the last part of **Sagittarius** is below Taurus. Let the Moon also be descending toward the south. And **Haly** said that someone remarked only Capricorn among the ruminants is hateful. And the ancient wise men prohibited the Moon from every aspect of **Mars** and **Saturn**; for Saturn constipates and restricts the medicine, while Mars sharpens it and makes it lead even to the discharge of blood. Understand this same thing for any laxative medicine, whether it be an electuary <note>a medicinal paste made with honey or syrup</note> or a decoction, except that it does not matter what the Ascendant is as long as it, its lord, and the place of the Moon are fortunate. And one must beware lest the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon be in the **eighth house** or joined to its lord.

### Chapter 10. On giving medicines that induce vomiting.

And if you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to take a medicine that provokes vomiting, you must then use the **ruminating signs** <note>original: "signis ruminantibibus"—the "cud-chewing" signs (Aries, Taurus, and Capricorn), which astrologically favor the upward movement of the stomach</note>. Then the **Moon** should be placed in the **Ascendant** <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> or ascending in one of those signs if it can be done. Among them all, **Taurus** is most to be chosen because of the Moon's dignity within it; it is especially strong if she is then within three degrees of her **exaltation** <note>the specific point in a sign where a planet's influence is most powerful; for the Moon, this is 3 degrees of Taurus</note>. And if the vomiting is necessary for a specific ailment of a particular limb, let the Moon be fortunate in the sign assigned to that limb; that is, let it be strong and well-adapted as best as can be managed. **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arabic astrologer whose "Book of the Skilled in the Judgments of the Stars" was a standard medieval textbook</note> says that if the **Lord of the Ascendant** is moving toward its own exaltation, it will be good.

### Chapter 11. On sneezing, gargling, and similar medicines given as potions.

If you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to take a **sternutatory** <note>a substance that causes sneezing to clear the head</note> or a gargle or an emetic or anything similar, Haly says the person who wants to use any of these should place the **Ascendant**, the **Moon**, and the **Significator** <note>the planet representing the matter at hand</note> in a ruminating sign, following all the rules given for purgative medicines. And **Athabari** <note>Al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian scholar and astrologer</note> says let the Moon be increasing in light and speed, with the Ascendant in an "increasing" part of the circle. However, Athabari also says let the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant be in **Cancer**, **Leo**, or **Virgo**.

### Chapter 12. Regarding entering baths or anointing with "annora" or "philothrum."

When you wish to choose an hour for someone to enter the baths or to be anointed with **annora** <note>a depilatory paste made of lime and arsenic used to remove body hair</note>, which is an ointment for pulling out hair—which some call **philothrum** and others call **leonaption**—place the Moon in **Aries** or **Scorpio**, joined to **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, or **Venus** by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, or by a **conjunction** <note>original: "iunctionem corporalem," meaning the two planets are in the same degree</note>. Do not place her joined to anyone bodily, nor in aspect to **Saturn** <note>Saturn is associated with decay and delays</note>. If she is not in those signs, let her be in **Cancer** or **Leo**. One must beware then that she is not in **Taurus**, **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, **Capricorn**, or **Aquarius**. If, however, the person entering the bath or steam-room does not intend to use the *annora*, they may do so in whatever sign they wish; nor is it forbidden to use baths or *annora* if the Moon is "under the sun's rays" <note>hidden by the Sun's light, usually considered a weakness</note>. And **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer</note> says that for anointing with *annora*, the Moon should not be placed in **hairy signs**, which are **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, the last part of **Sagittarius**, and **Capricorn**.

### Chapter 13. On the purchase of captives, servants, and the like.

If you wish to choose an hour to buy a captive, a servant, or a slave—as is customary in some places—and you want to choose a fit hour: you shall adapt the **Ascendant** and its **Lord**, and also the **Moon**. Place the Moon in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; signs that indicate stability and endurance</note>, except for **Scorpio**, or in signs of **direct ascension** or **domestic** signs. These signify that the servant or person bought will be patient and enduring, and will honor his master. Adapt the **Sixth House** <note>the astrological house associated with servants and small animals</note> and its Lord, and make it join with the Lord of the Ascendant by a trine or sextile aspect if you can, with **reception** <note>a condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other, facilitating cooperation</note>, or with the Moon, or with the Lord of the house in which the Moon is located. If you can make it join with all the aforesaid or with two of them, it is better than with one alone. Indeed, the wise ones praise having the Moon in **Taurus** or in the last half of **Sagittarius**. They similarly praise having the Moon and the Ascendant in **human signs** <note>signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and the first half of Sagittarius</note> or even in others, but not without the influence of the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets</note>, excepting **Aries**, **Leo**, **Scorpio**, **Capricorn**, and **Pisces**. And beware lest the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Moon, or the Lord of the Sixth House be in any of the aforesaid forbidden signs. For **Aries** signifies that the servant or person bought will be negligent, and will not care for his master's profit but will rejoice in his loss. **Leo** signifies that the servant or person bought will be

<column-break/>

proud and inglorious, a thief, greedy, and a miser, but not for his master's benefit. **Scorpio** signifies him to be deceitful, a wrongdoer, and an accuser. **Capricorn** signifies him to be a destroyer and a bringer of loss to his master. **Pisces** signifies a servant or person bought who is impetuous, who will judge against his master and think to ruin him, and who will disparage him in all ways possible and speak evil of him; nor will such servants be obedient to their masters. And if there is any of the "malefics" <note>unlucky planets like Mars or Saturn</note> in the Sixth House or elsewhere underground <note>below the horizon</note> that aspects the Sixth, it signifies that the person bought or the servant is unfaithful and malicious. If, however, the Lord of the Sixth is in **Sagittarius**, it signifies that he who is being sold is not truly a servant nor in a state of servitude, but is free.

### Chapter 14. On the liberation of the incarcerated or captives, or the manumission of servants.

When your intention is to choose an hour for the liberation of captives, or for those incarcerated, or for the **manumission** <note>the formal act of freeing a slave</note> of servants, adapt the **Ascendant**, its **Lord**, and the **Moon**. For the Ascendant, its Lord, and the planet from which the Moon is separating signify the one who liberates or manumits. The **Seventh House**, its Lord, and the planet to which the Moon is joining signify the one who is being liberated or manumitted. The **Tenth House** and its Lord signify the one who causes the liberation or manumission to happen, or through whose intervention it occurs. The **Fourth House** signifies what will become of each of them as a result of that liberation or manumission. Consider then whether the Moon is fortunate or unfortunate. For if she is fortunate, see in which house she is: for if she is in the **First**, it signifies good for the one manumitting. If she is in the **Tenth**, it will be good for the mediator. If she is in the **Seventh**, it will be good for the one liberated or manumitted. If she is in the **Fourth**, the end of the matter will be good for each of them. But if she is unfortunate and is in the First, it signifies it will go badly for the one manumitting. If in the Tenth, it signifies it will go badly for the one who caused the manumission or liberation. If in the Seventh, it signifies it will go badly for the liberated or manumitted person; for it signifies their return to prison or servitude. If she is in the Fourth, it signifies it will go badly for all the aforementioned from that liberation or manumission. And **Zahel** says let the Moon be increasing in light and number, touched by the fortunes; and let that fortune to which she joins be **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note> and similarly increasing. If it is thus, it signifies that good will happen to him and he will be healthy. In the waning of the Moon, however, it signifies that evils and pains will happen to him, which will not cease until he dies. And he says that in the increase of the number <note>the Moon's daily speed</note> it signifies the finding of substance <note>wealth</note>. And he says similarly that the **Sun** and the **Tenth House** should be free from malefics; for if they are impeded, the one who liberates or manumits will find some hindrance. And **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrologer</note> says: beware lest the Moon be in the **Twelfth House**. And he says let the hour of liberation be when the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> aspect each other by a trine or sextile aspect, so that there is affection between servant and master and one finds good in the other. For a **square** aspect <note>90 degrees, indicating tension</note> is middling; but an **opposition** signifies that if the Moon is impeded, it would have been better for the servant to remain in servitude than to have liberty. Therefore, place the Moon in fixed signs as was said above.

### Chapter 15. On the purchase of animals, both those for riding and others.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to buy any animal, let the **Ascendant** and the **Moon** be in a sign signifying that animal or one that is very close to that species. And let the Moon be made fortunate by one of the planets; and if it can be done so that the **Lord of that sign** fortifies her, it will be better. Even when she is not "received," so long as she is in a praiseworthy aspect with some fortune that is not impeded, then it will be good. If she is received, it does not matter whether the one receiving her is a "fortune" or a "malefic"; nor is anything then to be feared. Hence, if it is an ox or a horse or another large animal, whether it is for riding or not...

Since it is in the intention of nature to preserve, it does not hinder that process.

### Chapter four: On generating or conceiving a son or daughter.

**Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arabic astrologer</note> said: when you wish to choose an hour for joining with your wife to generate a male son, let the **Ascendant** <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and its **Lord**, and the **Lord of the House of Children** <note>the 5th House of a zodiac chart, which governs offspring</note>, be in masculine signs or in the masculine part of the circle (which is the right-hand side) at the hour of conjunction. You should not place any planet in the Ascendant at that hour, nor in the sign of children, unless it is a masculine planet. And if you wish for the child to be female, let these significators be in feminine signs and in the feminine part of the circle (which is the left). If you cannot do this and these significators are diverse—that is, some are in masculine signs and some in feminine—let the **Lord of the Hour** participate with the planet that received the **disposition of the Moon**. Judge from those that have more "testimonies" <note>astrological factors or points of evidence</note> in masculine or feminine signs, and the conception will be according to this. 

**Al-haly** <note>likely a reference to the same Haly, or a specific commentary</note> spoke even more at length than **Zabel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and physician</note> on this; for he said that in this election, the Ascendant should be a masculine sign of direct ascension. The boundaries <note>original: "fines," referring to the 'Terms,' a specific subdivision of zodiac signs</note> should be narrow and not remote. Let the **Lord of the Ascendant** be in the Ascendant, the **Midheaven**, or the **Eleventh House**. The planet that first reaches the degree of the Ascendant by its motion should be a **Fortune** <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus, which brings good luck</note>. 

He also said it is known from what has been promised that both **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> must necessarily be prepared in these matters, and it is especially necessary to prepare the **Lord of the Time**. Let no **Infortune** <note>a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</note> be in any angle, but let the Fortunes be free and strong. He also said we should turn our attention to the Lord of the Ascendant and beware of any planet that might hinder the ninth month, for birth is often seen to occur then. Likewise, if possible, it is praiseworthy to take precautions for the seventh and tenth months, for birth sometimes happens in those as well. In these places, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Luminaries should be fortunate and strong. 

Care must be taken that the **Lord of the Sixth or Eighth House** <note>the houses of illness and death</note>, if it is an Infortune, does not combine with any significator in any way. Generally, all things said to be unfavorable in the books of nativities <note>books on birth charts</note> should be avoided, and those things approved in them should be looked upon as the roots of the election. 

**Alchafat** <note>likely Al-Khafaji or another Arabic authority</note> said the best thing is for the Moon to be in the Ascendant in **trine aspect** <note>an angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</note> to the Sun. He also said: beware of the **Burned Path** <note>original: "via combusta," a section of the zodiac (late Libra to early Scorpio) considered unlucky</note>. We should also prepare **Venus**, for if Venus is hindered, the *allara* <note>original: "allara," likely a corruption of an Arabic term; the text glosses it as "the woman or the womb"</note>—that is, the woman or the womb—is corrupted. If the Moon is corrupted, the seed is corrupted. Also prepare the **Fifth House** and its Lord. Some also approve of this being done in odd-numbered hours—that is, the first, third, or fifth. If it happens that the Ascendant and the Moon are in **Libra** (which is a rational sign), it will be good if it and its Lord are then free. Then **Cancer** (the sign of many children) will be at the Midheaven. Let the remaining significators be in masculine signs, and she will become pregnant and conceive a male. 

We should also apply our effort to things pertaining to her—that is, we shall judge whether her womb is healthy or infirm in any way for the physician. For the circular significators perfect things according to how the subject matter itself is able to receive them. This is the discourse of Haly on generation and corruption. But since it would be very difficult to prepare everything so precisely as they have stated, it seems to me that you should at least prepare the Ascendant, the Moon, and its Lord at the time of the union of the man and woman. Place **Jupiter** in the degree of the **Tenth House** if you can, for this signifies that the woman 

<column-break/>

will conceive at the first intercourse she has then—unless perhaps she were a virgin, who might not be able to conceive at the first lying-together, but then can conceive at the second. If you cannot place Jupiter in the degree of the Tenth House, place him in the Tenth or Eleventh in such a degree that he aspects the Ascendant degree for degree. Or place him in the **Fifth House** so that he aspects the Ascendant, the Moon, or the Lord of the Fifth with a praiseworthy aspect. Or place the **Lord of the First House** and the Moon in the Fifth, or one of them so that it is two degrees above the line of the Fifth House, or at most three, or fifteen degrees below it at most. For this signifies the woman will then conceive. The **Part of Children** <note>a specific mathematical point in a chart</note> also signifies masculinity if it is masculine or in a masculine place, and femininity in a feminine one. And if there are as many masculine significators as feminine, they can signify one of two things: either one or more males and the same number of females, or a hermaphrodite.

### Chapter five: On extracting a miscarriage from a woman.

As it often happens, if a fetus has died in the mother's womb and you wish to choose an hour to extract it—whether by way of surgery, pharmacy, industry, or whatever way it may be—let the **Ascendant** be a feminine sign of direct ascension. Let the **Moon** also be waning in light, if possible, and let it be six degrees or more beyond the line of the Tenth House, descending toward the **Seventh House**. Let some **Fortune** aspect the Moon from a trine, sextile, or square aspect, whether the Moon is "received" <note>an astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note> or not. And if **Mars** then aspects it from nearby with reception, it will be good; they say it will not be bad without reception as long as the Moon is in a feminine sign and the Ascendant is a feminine sign of direct ascension, as was said. Care must be taken that the Ascendant is not a "crooked" sign <note>signs like Pisces or Aries that rise at an angle</note>, nor should the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon be in one of them.

### Chapter six: On handing a child over to disciplines.

This chapter seems like it should be contained under the **House of Mastery** <note>the 10th House, governing careers</note>, but because it mentions only the discipline of the child, it is better placed under the **Fifth House**, which signifies children. When you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to hand their child over to any discipline, doctrine, or for learning any instruction or mastery—whether it be numbers, measurement, song, astronomy, or any skillful art—let the Ascendant be one of the **houses of Mercury** (of which **Gemini** is best). Let the Moon be free from impediments and joined to **Mercury** by a trine or sextile aspect. Let Mercury be safe and free from impediments, and let the **Oriental Ascendant** <note>Mercury appearing in the east before the Sun</note> be direct, fortunate, and strong. Let the Lord of the house in which Mercury is located be free and safe. Let the Moon also be increasing in light and speed, for this signifies quickness in learning; if it is slow or waning, it signifies slowness in learning. **Zabel** said: let the Lords of the Houses aspect them. If you cannot do all these things, prepare the Moon as best you can and prepare Mercury so that it is not retrograde, nor under the rays of the Sun, nor in its first station; let it be occidental from the Sun or even oriental, provided it is moving direct.

### Chapter 7. On giving or receiving gifts.

In this matter—that is, *enchenia* <note>original: "enchenijs," from Greek 'enkaínia,' meaning dedications or ceremonial gifts</note>—two things are considered: the giving and the receiving. Just as people receive gifts, they also sometimes give them; the whole thing is called an *enchenium*. For just as one who receives is called a "host," the one who provides is also humbly called a "host." When someone wishes to receive a gift from another, then the **First House** and its Lord must be prepared, along with the Moon and the Lord of the sign in which she is located. The **Second House** and its Lord must also be prepared so that the gift turns to the benefit of the receiver. The **Part of Fortune** and its Lord should also be prepared so that this utility may be increased.

$\P$ ...as much as you can: and set the **Moon** <note>In astrology, the Moon represents the flow of events and the physical body of the prey</note> to be slow in its course. If the Lord of the Fourth afflicts her, it can be tolerated; let her not be afflicted by others, but let her be weakened in whatever other way she can be. I say this for the safety of the hunter, because he always has something to do with her, as I said: her weakening always benefits the hunter, but her "affliction" does not always, unless it comes from the aforementioned significators. However, the affliction of the Lord of the Seventh always works for the hunter and is to his utility and favor. And beware that the Lord of the Eighth, Seventh, or Twelfth does not afflict her. And if you still cannot do these things, coordinate the Lord of the First for the protection of the body, and the Third for the animals and instruments of the hunt. $\P$ If again you cannot manage these, because sometimes they cannot wait—and hunts mostly happen by day and few by night, except for great hunts of the waters and the use of snares for harmful four-footed animals and the like—at the very least coordinate the Lord of the Hour and weaken the Moon for the one wishing to go out to hunt as described, and it will be effective, though perhaps not as much as the hunter desires.

### $\P$ Chapter 13: On the election for games with dice or those played in other ways for the sake of profit.

When someone wishes to go out to play at **dice** <note>original: *taxillis*</note> or any other game from which his intention is to profit, it seemed to some of the ancient wise men that the Ascendant should be a **Movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs of action and change</note> and that **Fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> are not useful. $\P$ And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arabic astrologer</note> said that it is clear from their words that **common signs** are between the two—that is, neither very useful nor very useless. Thus, if the Ascendant is a common sign and its Lord is in a good state, it signifies good. If, however, he is in a bad state, it signifies evil. It is necessary that the Lord of the Ascendant be well-disposed and in a good state, while the Lord of the Seventh <note>representing the opponent</note> should be weak and hindered. And if it can be done, let the Lord of the Eighth <note>the house of the opponent's money</note> be in the Second house <note>the player's own money house</note>...

Let the **Moon** be separating from a **benefic** <note>original: *fortuna*; a lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> and joining another benefic, and let her be above the earth <note>above the horizon</note> and in the **house** <note>original: *pea*; likely a contraction for *penta* or *plaga*, referring to the astrological sector</note> of the one who intends to play; let her be fortunate and strong. If, however, she is **malefic** <note>original: *infortunata*; afflicted by planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, it is to be feared that she will oppose the one who holds his breast against her. Let her be in the eastern part if he seeks another to play. If he is the one being challenged, let her be in his breast in the western part. Whomever you choose to play for the sake of winning, let his face and breast always be turned toward the **Moon**. And if all these things cannot be done, let at least a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs associated with initiation and action</note> be rising when he goes out to play, and the Moon be in his breast while he plays. Again, if all these cannot be done, let the face and breast of the player be toward the Moon, and it shall be effective.

## ¶ Chapter Fourteen: How something may be perceived of what is said or discussed among those speaking secretly.

If you see some people speaking secretly apart from others, and you suspect their counsel might be harmful to you or another, and you wish to perceive something of it, consider the **first** and **seventh houses**, and their Lords. The first house, its Lord, and the planet from which the Moon separates belong to the one who first began to speak about the matter they are discussing. The seventh house, its Lord, and the planet to which the Moon joins belong to the one who is being spoken to. He among them who holds his face toward the south will be the one beginning; he who holds his face toward the east or north will be the other. The **tenth house** and its Lord signify the one or ones who run between them, or others whom the matter being settled most concerns. 

If there is a joining, a contention, or a war between them, the tenth house and its Lord will signify the victory, and he whom the Lord of the tenth most "beholds" <note>aspects or looks upon favorably</note> will be the victor. Indeed, the **fourth house**, its Lord, and the planet in whose house the Moon is found will signify the end toward which they are negotiating; but the planet in whose house the Moon resides will be stronger in its signification than the Lord of the fourth house. 

Therefore, look then to the Lord of the tenth, and see how he relates to the significators—namely, the Lords of the first or seventh. For if he is more favorable to the Lord of the first than the Lord of the seventh, he who began the talk will prevail. If he is more favorable to the Lord of the seventh than the Lord of the first, the one against whom the talk was started will prevail. You shall perceive this from the significators mentioned above. After this, see if the Lord of the first is among the **truthful planets**; if so, he who began the matter (or for whom it was begun) acts with truth and legality. If he is among the **liars** <note>original: *falsidicis*; planets prone to deception, often Mercury when afflicted</note>, he uses lies and falsehood. The same is to be said of the Lord of the seventh. If the Lord of the tenth is among the truthful planets, he who runs the business or handles the negotiation will use truth and legality toward the one to whom he is favorable; and vice versa if he is among the liars. And if the Lord of the fourth house or the planet to which the Moon joins is truthful, the matter being discussed will end with truth and legality; if it is among the liars, it will end with lies, fraud, and falsehood. Likewise, look to the planet signifying the completion of the matter, to which the Moon joins after its perfection. For if it is joined to a good planet, or even to a malefic that is not hindered and is "receiving" the Moon, then the one who prevails will follow with utility and good. If it is joined to an evil planet not receiving it, or to a hindered benefic, loss will follow. You may consider the same for other things whose end you desire to know.

## ¶ Chapter Fifteen: When you wish to seek a fugitive.

<column-break/>

When someone wishes to pursue or investigate a **fugitive**, or some lowly person, or even his servant, it is necessary to place the Moon "impedited" <note>afflicted or weakened</note> in the same degree as the **Sun**, provided there are more than 16 minutes between them <note>The Moon is "combust" or burnt up by the Sun's power, symbolizing the fugitive being overwhelmed</note>. This should not be in Aries or Leo; rather, let it be in the last half of Libra or the first of Scorpio, or with the **Head or Tail of the Dragon** <note>the Lunar Nodes</note>—specifically less than 12 degrees before or 7 degrees after. If it cannot be placed thus, place it in the **Ascendant** according to *Athabarus*; or let it be in conjunction, opposition, or a square aspect, or in a trine or sextile aspect without "reception," and let it be hindered by them. Or let it be three days before a lunar eclipse, or one day after. 

If there is an eclipse on those days, and the Sun is free and clear of vices and the hindrances of the malefics, and if any of the benefics are in the tenth house—especially 5 degrees before the midheaven line or 3 degrees after it—then as much as the Moon is hindered, so much more will the fugitive (or anyone you wish to hinder) be hindered. This applies especially to the aforementioned types, for the Moon naturally signifies them, as well as all common people.

## ¶ Chapter Sixteen: When the intention of the pursuer is to harm the one who flees.

This chapter can be subordinated to the one mentioned above, which treats those comprised under it—namely, the fugitive. But it differs in this: that one treats the investigation of the fugitive, while this one treats how one can harm a fugitive. Regarding this, **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> said: if the intention of the pursuer is to harm the fugitive (that is, to injure him in his person), let the Moon be in her **fall** <note>the sign where a planet's power is most weakened</note> and in her debility as described in the preceding chapter, and likewise the **twelfth house** and its Lord. If his intention is not to harm him personally, but only to catch or detain him, let the Moon be joined to a malefic and hindered, but do not place her or the planet she joins in the fourth house. Let the Lord of the first be joined with the Lord of the seventh. Care must be taken that the Moon is not joined to any planet in the twelfth house, which signifies that the fugitive will not be caught; or if he is caught, he will escape from the hands of the pursuer or the one who took him.

## ¶ Chapter Seventeen: When someone wishes to inquire of a thief, a detainee, or anyone else suspected of some crime or matter.

If someone wishes to inquire something of a **thief** or anyone else—to make him manifest what he is being questioned about, or whether he is guilty of that which he is suspected—place the Moon in **Libra**, and likewise the planet to which she joins. **Haly** said that **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> praised this opinion. He said that everything he [Albumasar] mentioned should be done after the fitting of the "electional roots" <note>the primary astrological conditions</note> and those things that follow them. He said to beware of all things he called avoidable, and to use those things spoken of above. He also said that the seventh house signifies all things predicted of thieves and fugitives, just as the twelfth signifies animals (namely, the larger ones). He said we must adapt the seventh house and its Lord for these matters, just as we adapt the twelfth house and its Lord in the purchase of animals, according to its significance.

## ¶ Of the Eighth House.
## ¶ Chapter One: On the election for the return of an absent person.

In this chapter, a remembrance is made concerning **return**. It seems to some that this chapter should be included under the **tenth house**, since it immediately follows the ninth house (which signifies travel), and not under the **eighth house**, which precedes the ninth—since a return does not happen before a journey. But because the eighth is assigned to the absent person, and a return does not happen except by an absent...

...rightly considered and received from the eighth house and not from the tenth, and also because the second house, which precedes the third, is fitting and should be regarded in the matter of the return. ¶ When you wish to choose a suitable hour for the **return** <note>original: *reuersionez*; the act of coming back from a journey</note> of someone absent, you must arrange the second house and its **Lord** <note>the planet that rules the zodiac sign on the threshold of that house</note> according to that saying of **Ptolemy** in the *Centiloquy*: "beware of misfortune in the eighth house for those departing on a journey, and in the second house for those returning." However, the return upon entry is differentiated according to the status of the persons. For if it is the return of a citizen or an inhabitant of a place who is subject to another as the lord of that land, his entry is signified when he crosses the threshold of the door of his own house, or another place where he lives, or where his subjects show him reverence. But the entry of a **king or prince** or another magnate who rules and dominates that city or land is when he enters the gates of the city, castle, or other land over which he presides as lord. If, however, he later goes outside that land and returns to it, **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, a famous 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> said that we need not be anxious about his return—that is, to know what things should happen to him from the hour of his return until he goes out from that land again, as great men and others are accustomed to do. For that return is like the **revolution of the years of the nativity** <note>original: *reuolutio annoz natiuitatis*; what we now call a "Solar Return" or a birthday chart for the year</note>: for if the birth chart was good and the revolution is good, it will increase the good. But if the revolution is bad, it will diminish the good signified by the birth, though not by much. And if the birth was bad and the revolution is bad, it will increase the evil. And if the revolution is good, it will diminish the evil, albeit slightly. Similarly, it happens in the return from the aforementioned journeys: if the first entry was good and the return is good, it will increase the good. And if it was bad, it will diminish something of the good. And if the entry was bad and the return is bad, it will increase the evil. And if it is good, it will diminish something of the evil; and this will last until he goes out of the land another time, for then that significance will expire, just as the significance of a revolution year expires when another revolution year turns. It seemed to some that we ought to consider the entry of a traveler into the cities through which they pass; yet a traveler has nothing to do in the cities he enters except as in other parts of the way through which he goes.

### ¶ Chapter 2: On the arrangement of the election for inheritances.

When you wish to choose an hour for the arrangement of any **inheritance** <note>original: *hereditatũ*; the acquisition of ancestral property or estates</note>, Haly said that one must place the eighth house in one of the houses of **Jupiter or Venus** <note>the "benefics" or lucky planets</note>, free and fortunate, and let its Lord be free and fortunate, and in a succeeding **angle** <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses, which follow the powerful "corner" houses</note> of which the second is best. Let both it and its Lord be free from the presence of the **malefics** <note>Mars and Saturn</note> and their opposition or **square aspect** <note>original: *4. aspectu*; an astrological angle of 90 degrees, considered stressful</note>, unless that malefic which would impede it were the Lord of the eighth house or of his exaltation, or held two of the minor dignities in it and were himself free from impediments. It would also be good if the degree of the eighth house fell in the **term** <note>a specific subsection of a zodiac sign</note> of the fortunes, Jupiter or Venus; and let the Moon be free and fortunate and aspect the eighth house or its Lord with a **trine or sextile aspect** <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>. You shall therefore arrange the first house and its Lord and all other things you can of those considered in elections. And if all these cannot be arranged, at least arrange the first and the eighth and their Lords, as well as the Moon and the Lord of the house in which she is; or at least arrange the eighth and its Lord and the Moon, lest you forget this.

### ¶ Chapter 3: On making a testament or codicils.

Because someone may wish to make a **will** <note>original: *testm / testamentum*</note> or **codicils** <note>legal additions to a will</note>, or to ordain any other last will, and wants you to choose a suitable hour for doing so: place the Moon decreasing in number and increasing in light, for this signifies that the will will be completed and changed, but it will remain firm as the testator ordained it. It is also praised that the Moon and the Lord of the **Ascendant** <note>the rising sign</note>, or one of them, be joined to **Saturn** out of friendship <note>in a favorable aspect</note>,

<column-break/>

for this signifies the perfect completion of the matter, and that it will not change after it has once been perfected, neither while the testator is living nor after his death. And **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician</note> said that it signifies the prolongation of the testator's life even after the will is made. You may say the same if the Moon were joined to Venus as was said of Saturn, and let the rising sign be a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius; signs associated with stability</note> and the Moon similarly in a fixed sign; for if it were a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> or the Moon were in a movable sign, it signifies that the will will be changed and will not remain firm. One must also beware lest the Moon be joined to a planet existing **under the rays** <note>original: *sub radijs*; "combust" or too close to the Sun, which weakens a planet's power</note>, nor should she be joined to **Mars** by body <note>conjunction</note> or by opposition or square aspect; nor should Mars himself be in the Ascendant, nor aspect it or its Lord with an aspect of enmity; for this signifies that the will will be changed and will not remain firm, and that the life of the testator will be shortened and he will not escape that sickness; and that the will of the testator will not be fulfilled—rather, the heirs and executors will strive to steal what was judged, and each will strive to extort for his own benefit, whatever survivors they may be, even if they are religious men.

## ¶ On the Ninth House.

### ¶ Chapter 1: On the entry into any city or other place.

Although in this chapter no mention is made of the ninth house, nevertheless it contains many things under it, for it has to signify local motion for both those who move from afar and others. Whence, if you wish to choose for someone a suitable hour for this—whatever the entry may be, whether into a city or another land, or whether it be the entry to inhabit some house in which he had not been accustomed to live for a long time—arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, and also the Moon and the Lord of the house in which she is, and let her be increasing in light. Arrange also the second house and its Lord, the arrangement of which is that he be in the Ascendant, free from impediments, fortunate, and strong. And Zahel said: place therefore a **fortune** <note>a benefic planet</note> so that it is above the earth in the ninth, tenth, or eleventh house, and never place it under the earth in the fourth, fifth, or sixth house. For he said it is horrible in pilgrimage and in work that you perish in a foreign region, whether the planet be a fortune or a malefic. And let the Lord of the house of the second house be entirely above the earth; it is not praised that he be under the earth, unless the thing you seek in that region is something a person wishes to hide until it is completed. And he said: let the Moon be with the Sun, so that there are between them from 12 to 15 degrees, and it will be better when she recedes from the Sun, for when she is near departing from "under the rays" by 3 degrees, she is fortunate. This is praised in all concealment; however, it is more useful if only the Ascendant, the tenth, or the eleventh be fortunate, and if the Moon were similarly joined and fortunate, it will be better. And beware that you do not place her under the earth or joined to a planet existing under the earth which is a malefic, or unfortunate, or impeded. And let the rising sign be a fixed sign; let the Lord of the tenth be free from impediments and from malefics, and let him not aspect the eleventh with an aspect of enmity; let the fourth sign also be fixed if it can be done. And if the Moon cannot be arranged, let her be **cadent** <note>falling away</note> from the Ascendant; let some of the fortunes be aspecting the 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, or one of them—the fourth is better than the tenth. And if with this you can place **Jupiter** in the second house, it will be the ultimate [success], for he naturally signifies gain and the increase of things. And if the intention of the one who enters the land or place is to depart afterward from there with prosperity and profit, let the Lord of the seventh house be oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note> and increasing in number; and if with this the Moon were increasing in number and the planet to which she is joined, it will be better. And Haly said one must beware lest... <note>original: *Et dixit q detestabilius esset...*; text repeats and continues</note> he said it would be most detestable if he committed his disposition to any of the Lords from any of those places, and all the more so if this were in any of the aforementioned places in the **revolution of the year of the world** <note>mundane astrology; the chart for the spring equinox</note> or of the nativity of the one for whom you are choosing; for that would be very detestable. But if you cannot arrange all these things, arrange the Ascendant and the second house and their Lords, and the Moon and the planet to which she is joined. And if again you cannot...

## Chapter Two: On the general beginning of journeys not pertaining to wars.

In this chapter, we must treat the journeys that occur daily to men, except that it does not treat journeys pertaining to wars. And although journeys differ from one another, all are made either by land or by water. Hence, if it is a journey by land, let the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of the journey</note> be an earthy sign <note>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</note>. If indeed it is by water, let the Ascendant be a watery sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>; and let the **Moon** be in the 11th house, moving toward the 10th, and never place her under the earth. But if you cannot avoid this, place her in the 3rd or 5th house, clean of "evils" <note>Malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> and free from impediment. And if the journey is by land, one must beware lest the Moon be joined to **Mars** by body <note>a conjunction, where planets are in the same degree</note> or by any aspect, unless perhaps by a trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note> with perfect **reception** <note>A state where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is looking at, creating a "hospitable" relationship</note>; unless Mars itself is in some "house of the journey" <note>the 3rd or 9th houses</note> and does not look upon the Ascendant or its Lord, nor is he himself the Lord of the Ascendant or of the 3rd, 5th, or 9th houses; for then he does not impede his own house if he looks upon it with a praiseworthy aspect. If however the journey is by water, let the Ascendant be a watery sign: and beware of **Saturn** in the water unless **Jupiter** looks upon him, who can break his malice, just as I told you regarding Mars on land, using all the stated methods and conditions. And **Cahel** <note>Another reference to Sahl ibn Bishr</note> said: beware of Saturn, lest he be in a watery sign; let him not be situated in the Ascendant of the departure or with the Moon. And if you cannot avoid it, let the Moon be joined to him along with a **fortune** <note>a benefic planet</note> or in a trine or sextile aspect, or from an "angle" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the strongest points in a chart</note>, so that it may take away the malices of Saturn and protect from shipwreck or impediment and heavy storms. You must also adapt the Moon and the Lord of the house in which she is found in all journeys, both by land and by water; since she, above all others, holds the primary meaning in them, except perhaps for the **Lord of the Hour** <note>The planet ruling the specific planetary hour of the day</note> in the matter at hand—this applies to short and medium journeys as well as to long, longer, and longest journeys. Also adapt the Lord of the Hour at the beginning of any journey from which utility or profit is hoped. In all meanings of journeys, adapt the Ascendant to the place from which the traveler departs; and adapt the Lord to the protection of his things. Whence **Messahala** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari, an 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer</note> said: if an **infortune** <note>a "bad" planet</note> is in the second house and has no "testimony" there <note>astrological support from other planets</note>, it signifies that an impediment will happen to the things he leaves behind. If it is **Mars**, it signifies contentions, or wars, or fires, or the shedding of blood, according as he is disposed toward this. If it is **Saturn**, it signifies impediment by thieves or drownings and similar things as was said above. The seventh house, however, is adapted to the place to which he goes; the eighth to the profit he intends to make there; the tenth and its Lord to the accidents that ought to happen to him on the way; the fourth and its Lord you shall adapt to the end of that journey. And you must adapt all the "angles" if you can, and especially the seventh; and place the Moon increasing in light and number <note>waxing and moving faster than its average speed</note>, and let her not be "falling" <note>in a weak house</note>. Also, let the Lord of the first and the Lords of the house in which the Moon is located be "free from combustion" <note>original: *egressi de cōbustione*; not so close to the Sun that their power is overwhelmed</note>; and let them be in

<column-break/>

**angles** or in their **succedent** houses <note>The houses immediately following the angles: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th</note>. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> said: the increase of the Moon signifies that the traveler will quickly arrive at the place he intends to go. He also praised it if **Mercury** has come out of combustion and is joined to some fortune, especially in the journeys of those wishing to go for the sake of buying or selling; for Mercury, as is said elsewhere, signifies things and goods and especially the trade of merchants. If, however, the journey is for different purposes, join the Moon to the planet signifying that specific matter, or let her be in its house: as, if it were a journey to a **king**, let her be joined to the **Sun** or at least to the Lord of the 10th house by a trine or sextile aspect; and if it is with reception, it will be better. And let the Sun be in a good place, namely in the 1st, 10th, or 11th; for if it is thus, his journey will be useful and fruitful; in other places, it will be otherwise. For if he is in the 3rd, 5th, or 9th, it signifies that the journey will be of little utility and great labor. If he is in the 7th or 4th, it signifies a lack of utility and labor, namely with greater delay. Beware, however, not to place the Moon, in the journey of someone wishing to go to a king, in **Aquarius**; because the king will not care for him, because Aquarius is opposite to **Leo** (which is the house of the Sun, which naturally signifies kings). Nor should you place her in **Pisces**; for the king would not wish to see him; indeed, he will turn his face away from him; because **Aries** is among the signs that have significance over kings, and Pisces is the 12th sign from Aries, which signifies detriment and sorrow. And if the traveler for whom you are choosing is going to warriors or bellicose soldiers, place the Moon joined to Mars by a trine or sextile aspect; and let both be in good condition. And **Cahel** said: beware of his conjunction from an angle and from a square aspect <note>original: *4. aspectu*; an aspect of 90 degrees, often considered difficult</note> and from an opposition, and let Mars be in the houses following an angle. If indeed his journey is to **bishops** or to religious men of whatever sect they may be, or to noble men or soldiers who are not bellicose and are at peace (not then living after the manner of warriors using arms), or to judges, or doctors of laws, or decrees, or similar persons, place the Moon joined to **Jupiter** by body or by a trine or sextile aspect, or at least a square with reception from some angle or other good place from the Ascendant. And if his journey is to **long-lived old men**, or to **Jews**, or to ignoble or vile persons, or to someone who will not yield to the words of others and wants whatever he himself says or does to be held as authentic, whether it be good or evil—such as was that tyrant **Ezzelino da Romano** <note>original: *ecilinus deromano*; Ezzelino III da Romano (1194–1259), a notorious northern Italian ruler used here as a contemporary or recent example of a stubborn, "Saturnine" personality</note> who is at least 45 years of age—place the Moon joined to Saturn by a trine or sextile aspect; and let Saturn be in a good state and free from impediment and in the succedent houses of the angles, and especially in the 5th or 11th. And let whichever planet the Moon is joined to be free from impediments; because its impediment signifies the failure of the matter for which the journey is made. And if his journey is to **women** of whatever condition they may be, let the Moon be joined to **Venus** by a trine or sextile aspect; and let Venus be in a masculine sign; and if you can place her in the angles or in the succedent houses of the angles, and especially in the 5th, it will be good. And if his journey is to **learned men** beyond those mentioned before, or to writers or merchants, let the Moon be joined to **Mercury** by a trine or sextile aspect; and let Mercury be in a good state, free from faults <note>original: *mādīs*; likely a scribal error or abbreviation for "faults" or "maladies"</note> and from impediments. For **Cahel** said: whenever the planet to which the Moon is joined, or the planet which is in opposition to the Ascendant or the 7th house, is slow, or retrograde, or impeded, it signifies entanglement and difficulty in those very ways. And **Haly** said that if the Lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant, or if the Moon is joined to a retrograde planet receiving her, that which he goes for will meet him on the road. And **Alchabicius** <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer</note> said the journey should be deferred as long as the Moon is in the 2nd or 3rd **face** <note>A ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of **Libra**. And he said that the indication of a journey is given to the **Moon**, and its condition has significance especially over every beginning, and for this reason, it is stronger. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century court astrologer from Tunisia</note> said if the birth chart of the traveler is known, or if it is his habit that the **Ascendant** of the journey be his birth house or the house of the question <note>The house in a birth chart or horary chart related to the specific topic</note>, and if the **Moon** is increased in light or in its daily motion, or if it is in a **Fortune** <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the 9th or 3rd houses. And if the **Moon** is impeded, we cannot delay the journey; let the **Moon** be falling away from the **Ascendant**, and likewise the planet that impedes it, and let us arrange the entry and be careful in it. And **Athabari** <note>Al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said whoever desires a swift and prosperous return should place **Venus** and **Jupiter** both in the 4th house from the **Sun** and the **Moon**; that is, that one of them be in the 10th from the **Sun** and in the 4th from the **Moon**, or vice versa; and let the **Moon** be between two **Fortunes**, separated from one and joined to the other. And he said that the **Moon** should be increased in light and motion. And he said that likewise, if the **Sun** is in opposition to the **Fortunes**, it signifies speed of return; and the **Infortunes** <note>Malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> cause the return to be delayed and impede with the greatest obstruction. And he said if a **Fortune** is with them, prosperity will follow. And he said that when the **Moon** is in the fourth house, it signifies a long delay; and this is according to the nature and quality of the journey. And **Zahel** <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century authority on elections</note> said that you should not place the birth **Ascendant** and its **Lord** falling from the **Ascendant** of the departure. And he said let the **Ascendant** of the departure be the 10th house from the birth or question **Ascendant**, if you seek a kingdom. And if you seek business, let it be the 11th from it, which is the sign for every thing you seek. And he said place that sign as its **Ascendant**, and let the **Moon** be in an **Angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful</note> or in a house following an **Angle**; and if it is fortunate, let it be aspecting the **Ascendant**. If indeed it is impeded, make it fall away from the **Ascendant**. And he said let the **Lord of the Ascendant** and the **Lord** of the **Moon's** house be in an **Angle**, and the **Moon** should precede the **Lord** of its own house. And beware lest you place the **Moon** with the **Malefics**, or in their square aspect or opposition. And he said that you should never place it in the 4th house; but if you must place it "under the earth," place it in the 5th house and fortunate: for it will shorten the labor of the journey and increase its profit; and it will lead more to the safety of the traveler's body. And he said that you should not place it in the **Ascendant**, because she herself is hostile to the **Ascendant** and hostile to the traveler, as is said elsewhere; nor place her in the 2nd house, for it signifies the taking away of substance and its diminution; and the **Sun** is friendly to the **Ascendant**. Wherefore if the **Moon** is in the **Ascendant**, the traveler's weakness in his body is feared, or labor similar to sickness or equivalent to it. And never place it in the 6th house, because sickness is feared for him; nor in the 8th, because death is feared for him unless God turns it away; and this is more powerful if she herself receives any **Lord** of those houses. And **Zahel** said that in riding the sea <note>Traveling by ship</note> you should not place the **Luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> impeded; because if they are free and fortunate, they signify safety and prosperity. If, however, they are impeded, it signifies death or the loss of the traveler. And he said do not ride the sea during the new moon <note>original: "interlunio"</note>, because this is a horrible thing. And he said if you ride the sea for the sake of business, arrange **Mercury** and the **Moon**; and let one of them be aspecting **Jupiter** from **Cancer** or **Pisces**. And he said that **Scorpio** is horrible in sea travel because of the place of **Mars** and its hostility; and always fear the bounds of the **Malefics** in travel, both at sea and on land. It is also to be feared to travel by land or water when the **Moon** is in the last half of **Libra**, unless **Venus** beholds it with a favorable aspect and she is of good condition, or **Saturn** beholds them with a favorable aspect in land journeys, and he is oriental and direct in his own house or exaltation

<column-break/>

or in his two minor dignities. And **Zahel** said if you seek a kingdom in that region, arrange the midheaven <note>The 10th house, representing career and public authority</note> and its **Lord** with the **Lord** of the 2nd house from the **Ascendant** and the **Moon**. Understand the same for a governorship and any office and any lay dignity. And if a governor goes to any land for the sake of his office or another duty and arranges the aforementioned, it will be useful to him. And **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> said look at the place of the **Moon** in the signs for travel by water: if it is in the first face <note>A 10-degree section of a sign, also called a decan</note> of **Aries**, it signifies the ease of the thing for which the journey is made, whether the planets aspect it or not. If it is less, there will be an impediment from the sea. If, however, **Saturn** aspects it, he will impede him and cause him shipwreck. And in the second face of **Gemini**, it signifies delay, but after this, it will be resolved. In **Cancer**, however, safety from every impediment. In **Leo**, indeed, he says there is impediment, and more so if a **Malefic** aspects it. In **Virgo**, he says prosperity and delay and return. In **Libra**, when it has passed the 10th degree, you shall not travel by land or sea. In **Scorpio**, it says sadness. In **Sagittarius**, say that before the journey is completed, he shall return. In **Capricorn**, at the beginning, a little good. In **Aquarius**, say delay and safety, yet let it not be a journey to a king. In **Pisces**, it says impediment and distress. And he said if a **Malefic** aspects it, it will increase the impediment. If indeed a **Fortune** aspects it, the impediment will be diminished and the good will be strengthened.

### Chapter Three: On the instruction of singing, both in music and in other things.

This chapter could be included under both the 9th and 10th houses, but it seems more appropriate to me that it be included under the 9th rather than the 10th: because the 9th house signifies rather ecclesiastical songs and those which singers use in temples and other religious places. For the 10th signifies songs which are made by laypeople and the joyful who delight in secular and lay singing and games. Wherefore if anyone wishes to be taught to sing and wishes to choose for himself a suitable hour for this, place the **Ascendant** in one of the rational signs or the 10th house, and arrange **Mercury** first and principally for church singing, and **Venus** secondarily. In secular and lay singing, however, arrange **Venus** principally and **Mercury** secondarily; but for a musical instrument, arrange whichever of them is powerful; and let the **Ascendant** be **Libra** or **Taurus**, or at least **Pisces** for delightful singing, or **Gemini** or **Virgo** for church singing. Also, let the **Moon** in any singing be in **Cancer**, **Taurus**, or **Pisces**, separated from **Mercury** and going to a conjunction with **Venus**, if it can be done. Let **Venus** also be in some of her dignities. Say the same for **Mercury**: let **Mercury** also be joined to **Venus** by body or by a sextile aspect if you can do this; unless one of those three—**Venus**, **Mercury**, or the **Moon**—is falling, unless by chance it were in the 9th house, for that is not a blasphemy <note>Meaning it is not a negative placement here</note> provided it is fortunate otherwise; and let that one be stronger which is in the 9th, because it signifies the goodness of the thing which he whom you are choosing for wishes to begin. And if you wish that there be a perfect singer whom no one exceeds in song, let **Mercury** be direct, joined to **Venus** retrograde in her house or exaltation, or in two of the minor dignities of either of them. If, however, their conjunction is outside those places, your work will be below this. Say the same in birth charts regarding singing and the composition of melodies: and whatever the **Ascendant** may be, if its **Lord** is in the 9th or 10th, it will be praiseworthy, provided it is fortunate and strong. And one of the ancients said if there is an election for the sound of musical instruments, such as the lyre or the symphony <note>A medieval term for various instruments, often a hurdy-gurdy or a type of organ</note> or similar things, let the **Moon** be in **Capricorn**...
