...and the **lord** <note>The planet that rules a specific zodiac sign or house</note> who can be commended in the beginning of any matter.

## Concerning the Tenth House.

### Chapter One: On the election of kings and nobles, or magnates and the wealthy.

It has been shown in the preceding sections regarding those things that pertain to the **elections** <note>The astrological practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an endeavor</note> of the 9th house; now, however, we must speak of those things which are seen to pertain to the 10th house. Hence, when you wish to elect for someone a king or a duke or similar figures regarding those things which pertain to a kingdom or a dukedom, or to their affairs, or that which is done for them, adapt the 10th house and its **lord**, and the **Sun**; and let the **Sun** not be joined with any **Infortune** <note>A "malefic" planet, specifically Saturn or Mars, believed to cause difficulty</note>, nor should the **Moon** be; nor let the **Sun** be going toward a conjunction with **Mars** or **Saturn**, nor to their **square aspect** <note>original: "4. aspectū"; an astrological angle of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note> or **opposition**. And if it receives them, let it not even be to their **trine aspect** <note>A harmonious 120-degree angle</note> or **sextile** <note>original: "fertili"; a harmonious 60-degree angle</note> without **reception** <note>A condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it aspects, creating a "hospitable" relationship</note>: but place the **Sun** in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, where planets are most powerful</note> or in a **succeedent house** <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> following an angle, or let it be in **Leo** not falling away nor otherwise impeded. And if it is not in **Leo**, let it be then with that planet in whose house or **exaltation** it resides, by a **trine** or **sextile aspect**. And if you cannot avoid a **square aspect**, let it be with **reception**; but you shall avoid the **opposition** in every way, whether with **reception** or without **reception**, just as you avoid its aspect with **Infortunes**. As for the **trine** or **sextile** without **reception**: let it be in a **masculine sign** and in a **masculine quarter** <note>The divisions of the sky traditionally classified by gender in medieval astrology</note> if it can be done; let it also be in a sign in which it has some **dignity** <note>Essential strength based on the planet's position in the zodiac</note> if it can be done. Consider also if in that year there was or will be an **eclipse** of either luminary, and you shall avoid that sign in which it was or is meant to be. Let both **luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> be in the **terms** <note>Small subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> of **Fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, specifically Jupiter or Venus</note>, helping each other by aspect from a **trine** or **sextile** if it can be done; and the **lords** of those **terms** should be in their own **dignities**, aspecting the **luminaries** or at least one of them. And by as much as you better adapt the **luminaries**, or make them stronger or more fortunate, by so much more will it be good for the matter for which you are electing; and the less you adapt them, the more the matter will fall below what you desire. You must, however, beware lest the **conjunction** or **prevention** <note>The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the event</note> which occurred before the election itself be unfortunate; for if it was so, the election should not be made for the aforesaid persons except fifteen days after the said **conjunction** or **prevention**, or more if you can avoid it, even if the election otherwise appears fortunate. If indeed you can avoid this, your election will be more secure and better and more fortunate.

### Chapter Two: On promotion to a kingdom or dukedom, or other dignity pertaining to a kingdom or dukedom, or any other.

If someone consults you wishing to be promoted to a kingdom or dukedom or anything similar, so that you may choose for him a convenient hour for this: place the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> in **Leo**; and let the **Sun** then be in **Taurus**, in the 10th house from the **Ascendant**; let the **Moon** also be in the 1st house, joined to **Venus**, **Jupiter**, or **Mercury**, they being fortunate and strong both in the election and in the reception of the dignity.

### Chapter Three: On the enthronement of a kingdom or dukedom or other dignity, or the ascending of that seat.

<column-break/>

When you wish to choose the hour for the enthronement of a kingdom, so that they may ascend that seat or place, or for a dukedom or any other dignity: place **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, associated with stability</note> on the **angles**, and especially the 1st and the 4th; and let the **lord** of the 10th be free from impediment; and let the **lord** of the **Ascendant** be in the **Ascendant**, or the 10th, or the 11th, or the 5th, and be **received**; let also the **lord** of the 10th receive the **lord** of the house in which he is located by a **trine** or **sextile aspect**; let the **lord** of the 4th also be free in the aspect of a **Fortune**. And if you cannot do this, make sure the **Moon** is **received**. And if you cannot place the **lord** of the 4th free and strong, prohibit him from aspecting the **Ascendant** or its **lord**, and make sure some of the **Fortunes** aspect the 4th and the 10th, or at least one of them, if you can do that.

## Concerning dignity pertaining to war.

If, however, it is a dignity that pertains to war, such as the leadership of an army and the like: place the **Ascendant** in **Aries** or **Scorpio** <note>Signs ruled by Mars, the planet of war</note> and place **Mars** fortunate and strong, and make sure he aspects the **Ascendant** with a laudable aspect, and the **trine** will be better than the others. And if the **Ascendant** is in any of the houses of other planets, let it be aspecting **Mars**, the **lord** of the **Ascendant**, with a **trine aspect**, and let him be free from impediments; and let the **Ascendant** be a **fixed sign** or at least a **common sign** <note>Also known as mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>. In elections meant to endure for a long time, **fixed signs** are better; **common signs** are below **fixed**; **movable signs** <note>Also known as cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> are below **common**. And in any election for any dignity, place the **Moon** so that it is **received**, or at least joined to the **Sun** by a **trine** or **sextile aspect**, or at least by a **square** with **reception**; let also the **Sun** be joined to **Jupiter** in **Sagittarius**, **Pisces**, **Aries**, **Cancer**, or **Leo** by a **trine** or **sextile aspect** if it can be done. And if you cannot adapt all these things, as often happens, adapt those that you can; but your work will not be so perfect. For not all things can be observed in the elections of a king and of all their sons and other dukes in all established matters.

If, however, it is a dignity or office through which the property of others is committed to someone for distribution—such as **chamberlains**, **stewards** <note>original: "massarij"</note> of some community, namely a city or a castle, or humble officers, or the **stipendiaries** <note>Paid soldiers or officials</note> of magnates—you shall similarly adapt the **lord** [of the 10th] and its **lord** with the adaptation of the 1st and its **lord**, as well as the **Moon**. And if your election is for some **scribe**: adapt **Mercury** after the adaptation of the aforesaid things, so that **Mercury** aspects the **Ascendant** with a laudable aspect; for this signifies that he will be faithful and legal in the matters committed to him, and that it will be useful to him.

### Chapter Four: When someone wishes to go and live with a king or duke or power, or with such a person, or to set out with them.

If there is someone wishing to go to a king or duke or prince or power or another magnate to stay or set out with him, and he consults you to choose for him a convenient hour for this: whatever **Ascendant** you have placed, let **Jupiter** be in it, and make him join with the **lord** of the 10th if you can; for this will signify that the king will be agreeable and affable and that things will turn out well for him from the king. And if you make them join by a **trine** or **sextile aspect**, it will be good, or even by a **square** with **reception**. And if you cannot do this, place **Jupiter** in the 9th; for this will signify that the traveler will find in that journey good and useful things from which he will rejoice and see things pleasing to himself; and it will be all the better if **Jupiter** is safe and free from impediments. And you shall avoid placing him in the 4th; because although the 4th signifies the end of a matter, nevertheless in this case it is to be avoided that you place him in it; and make sure he aspects the **Moon** herself from the 10th if **Jupiter** himself is in the 1st, or from the 7th if he himself is in the 9th. Beware of the 6th and the 12th <note>Houses traditionally associated with illness, service, and hidden enemies</note>; but if you cannot avoid this, it will be less horrible in such a case than in others. And if you cannot do this, let **Venus** testify to him from the 1st, or from the 7th, or from the 10th.

...or from the fourth house, with or without **reception** <note>A condition where a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it aspects, like a guest in a friend's house</note>; or from the sixth or third houses with reception. And beware of **Saturn** and **Mars**, lest either of them be in the first house or in any of the **angles** <note>The powerful 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart</note>. And take care that the **Moon** is not **impeded** <note>Afflicted by a bad aspect or position</note>, especially by the misfortune of **combustion** <note>Being too close to the Sun, which "burns" a planet's power</note>; nor should she be with the **Tail** <note>The South Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with loss or "draining" energy</note> or any of the **malefics** <note>Saturn or Mars</note> or those planets that cause hindrance. For when this occurs, it signifies that there will be no profit in that journey; indeed, it is feared the traveler may not return. Even if it were a different kind of journey, the same is feared. And if he is sickly, it is feared he may die; if he goes to **battle** <note>original: "p̅liū" for "proelium"</note>, then he will fall or perhaps be killed. To tell you the truth briefly, it would be a great and even miraculous thing if he escaped the aforementioned dangers.

### Chapter Five: When someone wishes to oppose a king, a duke, or anyone similar.

It happens sometimes that someone wishes to harbor enmity against a king, a duke, or some great noble from among those suited for the realm, or their sons who are to succeed them in dignity or inheritance. Place the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the election</note> in one of the houses of **Jupiter** or **Mars**; let the **Lord of the Ascendant** be strong and **fortunate** <note>Well-placed and receiving good aspects</note> and free from hindrances. Let the **Lord of the Seventh House** <note>Representing the opponent or enemy</note> be impeded, unfortunate, and weak in a malignant place relative to the Ascendant—the worst of which are the **Sixth** and **Twelfth houses**. Let him not behold any of the **Fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</note>, nor let them behold him, nor any of the **luminaries** <note>The Sun or the Moon</note>.

### Chapter Six: On reconciliation with a king, a duke, or similar persons.

Sometimes a person is at odds with a king, a duke, or their sons, and wishes the king to be reconciled with him, asking you to choose an hour suited for this. When you wish to choose this for him, set the **Ascendant** as it may be, but make it and its **Lord** impeded, unfortunate, and weak. Let the **Moon** also be impeded and let the planet from which she separates be diminishing in light and number. Conversely, let the **Seventh House** be fortunate and strong, and likewise its **Lord** fortunate and strong, as well as the planet to which the Moon is joining. Let the **Lord of the Seventh** be in a good place relative to the Ascendant, free from evils and hindrances; for this signifies the strength of the matter you seek.

### Chapter Seven: On the deprivation of any dignity.

It happens sometimes that one who has promoted someone to a **dignity** <note>A high office, rank, or position of honor</note> strives and wishes to remove him from that dignity because of someone else, as sometimes happens; or another person strives to do the same. Whether it is the one who promoted him or another who asks you to choose a suited hour for this task, you must consider whether his intention is to remove him out of hatred or out of favor. For if it is out of hatred, the **Moon** must be placed unfortunate and weak by **combustion** or some other great hindrance; let her be diminished in light and number, placing her in the **Sixth** or **Twelfth** house. Let her be in a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> in the house or **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note> of Jupiter, Venus, the Sun, or Mercury, while these planets themselves are unfortunate and weak. However, the **Ascendant** and its **Lord** should be fortunate and strong. If, however, his intention is to remove him out of favor—that is, to restore him so that he might obtain a greater place or be promoted to a greater dignity—let the **Moon** be in **Virgo**, **Sagittarius**, or **Pisces**, or at least in **Gemini**, but she shall be below the others. Let her and the **Lord of the Ascendant** be increasing in light and number, and let the Ascendant be in the north. Let the **Moon** also be in the house or exaltation of one of the **Fortunes**, that Fortune being herself fortunate and strong. Let the **Lord of the Tenth** be strong if it is a **secular dignity**, or the **Lord of the Ninth** if it is a **clerical dignity**. Nor is this contrary to what is said elsewhere—that the **Moon** is the significator of the business when the Lord of the Ascendant is failing—for here it is understood that the Ascendant is free and its Lord safe and fortunate. Because of this, the Lord of the Ascendant will be the significator as far as the significance pertains to the Ascendant and its Lord, but the **Moon** will be the significator of the matter you intend to arrange; and she has her own specific significance separate from the significance of the Lord of the Ascen-

<column-break/>

-dant, and so understand this in similar cases.

### Chapter Eight: On instruction in morals.

If someone wishes to be taught moral dogmas and asks you to choose a time suited for this, when he has requested it, make the **Ascendant** **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, the first half of **Sagittarius**, or **Aquarius** <note>These were known as the "human signs," thought to favor intellectual and social pursuits</note>. Let it be fortunate, and the **Moon** in one of the suited signs. Let the **Lord of the Tenth** be in the Tenth, its Lord being of the same nature as the Lord of the Ascendant, or at least in friendship with it. Let the **Moon** also be joined to **Mercury** by body <note>Conjunction</note> or by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect. Let **Mercury** be safe and free from hindrances, fortunate and strong. And if you can make him behold the Lord of the Ascendant with an aspect of friendship, it will be good. Let the **Moon** also be in her **apogee** <note>The point where the Moon is farthest from Earth, considered more stable in some traditions</note> or moving toward it, not descending from it. You shall also adapt the **Ninth House** and its Lord if you can do so in any way. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer whose "Book of the Skilled" was a standard text</note> said that in the instruction of writing, the **Tenth House** must be adapted with all these things, since it signifies scripture. And know that scripture is both a science and a craft; and he said let us include the "ways" in this chapter.

### Chapter Nine: On instruction in fighting, battling, or competing.

If you wish to choose an hour for someone wanting to be taught how to battle, fight, or compete, set the **Ascendant** in **Aries**, **Leo**, or **Sagittarius**. Place **Mars** strong and fortunate, and let the **Moon** be fortunate and strong. It will be better if she is in **Taurus**, provided she is fortunate otherwise. And beware of placing her in **Scorpio** or **Capricorn**, especially in the instruction of military combat. Let the **Lord of the Ascendant** also be in his **exaltation** and in a strong place. Beware lest he or the **Moon** be **cadent** <note>Falling away</note> from an angle or the Ascendant. If you cannot do this, place the **Moon** and the **Lord of the Ascendant**, or one of them, in the **Tenth** or moving toward it. And **Haly** said that some say the **Moon** should be in **Gemini**.

### Chapter Ten: On instruction in swimming.

If someone wishing to be taught how to swim asks you to choose a time suited for it, make the **Ascendant** **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, or **Pisces** <note>The water signs</note>. Let the **Lord of the Ascendant** be in the angle of the **Tenth** or moving toward it, not more than 15 degrees from it; let him be fortunate and strong. Let the **Moon** also be in one of her **dignities**, among which **Cancer** holds the principal place; **Taurus** is below Cancer, and the other dignities are below Taurus. Let the Ascendant itself be in the north; and if it can be done, let the Moon be in her apogee, moving toward the proper length at the contact of the **epicycle** line with the **eccentric** line <note>Technical terms from Ptolemaic astronomy describing the Moon's complex orbit</note>.

### Chapter Eleven: On the general instruction of all works.

If your election is general for works that men are generally accustomed to use, such as the **work of smiths** and the like, whatever Ascendant you set, adapt the **Tenth** and its Lord, and the **Moon** likewise. Place the planet that naturally signifies the work someone intends to begin in a fortunate and strong position. For example, if it is a heavy and laborious or long-lasting work, such as the **cultivation of lands** or **waterworks**, or things made near water such as **bridges**, **mills**, and the like, you shall adapt **Jupiter**. And if it is a work pertaining to **judges** or **arbitrators** wishing to judge justly and the like, you shall adapt **Jupiter**. If it is the work of a **smith** or a **butcher** and the like, you shall adapt **Mars**. If it is the work of a **goldsmith** or **money-changer** and the like, you shall adapt the **Sun**. If it is the work of **ornaments for women**, adapt **Venus** and place **Mercury** joined with her likewise, and with others by body or aspect, fortunate and strong; for he has participation in all these things. And if it is the work of **painers** or **writers** or those forming **images** or...

## Concerning the Eleventh House.

### Chapter One: Concerning those things for which we have hope or confidence, and attaining praise and good reputation.

This chapter seems as though it could be included under the Tenth House, because it concerns things through which good fame is acquired—which follows from hope first held. However, it seems more appropriate to include it under the Eleventh. Therefore, when you wish to do this, set the **Ascendant** <note>The "first house," representing the person starting the endeavor</note> in **Sagittarius** or **Pisces** <note>Signs ruled by Jupiter, the planet of growth and success</note> or at least **Cancer**; but Cancer will be inferior to Sagittarius and Pisces. You shall prepare **Jupiter** as best as you can, and also prepare the **eleventh house** and its lord with all your might. If you can place Jupiter in the 11th, it will be very useful for your matter. If you cannot place Jupiter in the 11th, place him in the 1st. If you again cannot do this, see that he aspects either of them with a laudable aspect; and place him fortunate, strong, and free from **impediments** <note>Negative influences like "bad" aspects from Saturn or Mars</note>. If you can place the Lord of the 1st house in the 11th, or the Lord of the 11th in the 1st, it will be praiseworthy. Let the **Sun** be in the 10th house free from impediments if possible, or in the 1st, provided he does not hinder Jupiter or the Lord of the 1st or the Lord of the 11th. Let the Moon also be joined to him by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>original: "trino vel fertili aspectu"; sextiles were often called "fertile" because they facilitate growth</note> or at least by a **square** with reception, and let her be free, fortunate, and strong. Let her also be separated from Jupiter so that she joins the Sun or the Lord of the 1st or the 11th if possible, and it will be better; that fame and praise will be more widely spread and will fall upon the ears of men and into their praises. Whatever of the **significators** <note>The planets that represent the specific people or goals involved</note> you can prepare, it will be better, and especially if you can make the **luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> aspect one another, or the Lord of the 1st with the Lord of the 11th by a trine or sextile aspect, or at least by a square with reception. If you can make them look at each other mutually, it will be better.

If you cannot do this, see that Venus joins with the Moon and with the Lord of the 11th. Let the Lord of the 11th be looking on with a laudable aspect; and if he aspects its Lord or the Moon, it will be better.

### On the twelfth house.

#### Chapter one: on the racing of horses or other animals, whether rational or other types, running for a prize.

When someone wishes to make a **horse** or another animal run for a **prize** or for some other cause of acquiring or winning it, and you wish to choose a suitable hour for this: adapt for him the **Ascendant** and its **Lord**, and the **Moon** also, and the **Lord** of the house in which she is located, and similarly the planet to which she joins if you can—namely the **Part of Fortune** and its **Lord**. For if you place the **Lord of the Hour** in the **First** house, as I said, it will come in **first**; if in the **Tenth**, **second**; if in the **Eleventh**, **third**; if in the **Seventh**, **fourth**; if in the **Fifth**, **fifth**; if in the **Ninth**, **sixth**;

If, however, there are more than twelve animals, the others will come in a mixed order, following the primary significations. And if you cannot adapt all these things, adapt the **Lord of the Hour**, the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon**. #### Chapter two: on the purchase of larger animals, both horses and others, for riding or taming.

When you wish to choose an hour for someone to **buy** an animal, or for **riding** or **taming** it, adapt the **Ascendant**, its **Lord**, and the **Moon**. Place her joined to some **benefic** <note>original: "fortuna"; a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> that is moving **direct** and is **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, ascending in the circle of its **apogee** <note>original: "augis"; its highest point of power</note> if you can, or at least moving direct. Beware lest that benefic or the **Moon** be joined to a **malefic** by body or by aspect, because it sends fears into the animal; so that if it is a **purchase**, it threatens loss and that he will not get a good deal from it. If it is for **riding** or **taming**, he will not follow through with what he intends, because the animal will shy away; and all the more so if a hindering malefic is in the **Twelfth** house. Nevertheless, see if the riding is for a horse or other animal already tamed: for such, set the **Ascendant** of the purchase in a **common sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and let the **Moon** be in **Taurus** or **Leo**. Also make her join a planet that is moving **direct** and is in the **North** and **ascending**, or at least in the **South** as long as it is ascending; for this signifies that the animal will increase in price and in body. For if it is **retrograde**, it signifies that the animal will increase in price but not as much, and it will decrease in body. And if it is moving **direct but descending**, whether it is in the **North** or the **South**, it signifies that it will increase in body but decrease in price. Similarly, if it is in the **South** and **descending**, it signifies that it will decrease in both price and body, and even more so if it is in the South. ¶ If indeed the animal is **untamed**, set the **Ascendant** in a **common sign**, and let the **Moon** be in a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> joined to one of the **benefics** according to the conditions mentioned above concerning ascending, descending, direction, and retrogradation. ¶ Yet it must be considered that if someone wishes to buy any animal—namely a **horse**, **ox**, **donkey**, or **camel**—for the sake of **profit** or improvement, if the **Moon** is between the beginning of **Cancer** and the end of **Sagittarius**, he will not profit from it easily; for he will buy dear and sell cheap. If, however, he buys while she is between the beginning of **Capricorn** and the end of **Gemini**, the opposite will happen: for he will buy cheap and sell dear. And this occurs not only with the aforementioned animals but indeed with any thing that someone buys at that time. This must not be overlooked: that the **benefics** always provide and increase the good and diminish the evil; while the **malefics**, on the contrary, increase the evil and diminish the good—each one according to its own nature and according to its interest in helping or harming, increasing or diminishing.

# Here begins the treatise on the revolutions of the years of the world. And first, it presents the prologue.

<image-desc>A large square woodcut initial 'Q' containing intricate floral and vine-like scrollwork in a style typical of early modern printed books.</image-desc>Since after the treatise on **elections** <note>The practice of choosing the best time to start an undertaking</note> nothing is more suitable than to subsequently treat the **revolutions of the years of the world**, it is worthily a subject of discussion and a special treatise should be produced about them. But first it must be briefly seen what a "revolution" is. A revolution of a year is the circular course of the **Sun** from one minute of any degree of any sign until its return to that same point; though it might perhaps be defined differently as it has seemed to some. And that consideration has two modes: namely, according to the revolution of the years of **nativities** <note>Individual birth charts, commonly called "Solar Returns" today</note> or other beginnings. For the **revolution of the year of the world** is from the entry of the Sun into the first minute of **Aries** <note>The vernal equinox, marking the start of the astrological year</note> until it revolves circularly, passes through the whole **zodiac**, and returns to the same point. But the revolution of the year of a nativity, or of other principles or of another beginning, is from the minute in which the Sun was in the nativity of some newborn until it revolves and circularly passes through the whole zodiac and returns to that same point; and so it must be seen concerning all other revolutions. Indeed, a revolution is very useful among other things; for its signs are higher than others, just as the effort required to find its certainty is more intense and complex. For through the revolution of the years of the world, it is known what will happen in that year regarding good or evil—such as whether the year will be tranquil or turbulent, and whether there will be future wars or not in the year which is revolving. Similarly, it is to be said of peace; and what the state of the kingdom or princes, of wealth or of the great men will be in the future. Similarly also of the common people and the lowly, the religious and universal things; and if it is of universal things, how they differ generally according to the customs of men. Likewise, it shows what will happen to all earthly crops—whether abundance or scarcity is to be expected from them, and whether their future price will be low, moderate, or high, as will be said in the chapter on parts in its proper place. For through the revolution of nativities, the accidents of any person born are known for that year. Hence, when you wish to know the signs of the revolutions of the years, both of the world and of nativities, you shall observe this order according to what I hand down to you; nor should this book be neglected by you, but it is necessary for you to know it and have it in your mind above all others. For there is great industry in knowing and understanding it well, so that by distinguishing the times you may harmonize the writings; lest perhaps you believe all times are the same in it, for they are not if you well consider those things which occur to you to be considered. Because even if you find it said somewhere that such a thing signifies such an event or signifies a multitude of such things, and in that same chapter you find it signifies a scarcity of the same thing, do not take it as a contradiction but distinguish so that they agree: because one intention will be general, the other will be particular; and the particular overrides the general <note>original: "spale derogat gñali"; a principle that a specific rule takes precedence over a general one</note>. It happens, however, sometimes that it speaks of overriding according to latitude, according to easternness or westernness, or according to **direction** <note>moving forward through the zodiac</note> or **retrogradation** <note>appearing to move backward</note> and the like. For these accidents change the significations, and because of this, the chapters do not contradict each other. ¶ When you wish to know the revolution of the year of the world, at what hour the Sun enters the first minute of the sign of **Aries**—namely, from the first section of the same minute up to the 4th or at most the 5th second of it. And when you have found this with the most certain inquiry, you shall equate the planets and houses to that hour and to the 

<column-break/>

minute of that same hour. You shall find the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> as accurately as you can: and construct the 12 houses by their degrees and minutes to the minute of that hour, as you seek it better and more certainly. You shall similarly equate all the planets to the same minute of that hour; and having found their locations most certainly by degrees and minutes and likewise the seconds of each of them, lest you fall into any error. And you shall also consider their qualities: namely, how they are disposed and in which houses and in which signs they are. And which of them are **direct**, and which **retrograde**, and which **stationary**; and which are fast in their course and which are slow; and whether any of them are northern or southern among themselves or from the path of the Sun <note>The ecliptic</note>. For when a planet is northern to another, it is said to go "over" it, whether it be of the superior or inferior planets; he who is northern to the other is said to go over him. Similarly, if they are southern, the one that is less southern is said to go over the one that is more southern. And how one of them **regards** <note>aspects</note> another or how it is regarded by it; and how one casts its rays upon the body or the rays of another; and how they regard the **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful points in a chart</note>; since a good aspect signifies good; a bad one, however, the contrary. And when you have done this, you will similarly see what sign is the Ascendant; since then you will be able to take the **Lord of the Year** and the signification of the whole of the common people from the **Lord of the Ascendant** sign, provided nothing else prevents that which pertains to the Lord of the Ascendant from the lordship of the year. Nevertheless, do not believe that the Lord of the Ascendant of the revolution will always be the Lord of the Year absolutely—as some seem to want to say so they might finish more easily—but you shall take him as I shall tell you below.

### Chapter 1: How the Lord of the Year is found.

**A**fter you have been certified to the hair <note>to the highest precision</note> concerning the time of the Sun's entry into **Aries** as was said, and concerning the Ascendant of that entry and all the other houses and the locations of the planets: see which planet is the Lord of the Ascendant; and how it is disposed and where it is. For if it is **direct** and free from **combustion** <note>Being too close to the Sun, which "burns" up a planet's power</note> and is in the Ascendant—three degrees before the line or four after—do not seek another, for it will be the **Lord of the Year** or the revolution; and it is the significator of the common people, and nothing else can take that lordship from it. If, however, it is retrograde or combust, it can no longer be the Lord of the Year or the revolution; for the power of a retrograde or combust planet is annihilated, unless for some very great cause which very rarely happens. Seek then the Lord from the **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet is particularly honored and strong</note>. For if there is an exaltation of some planet in the Ascendant sign, seek the ruler from that; for if it is in the degree of the Ascendant, or three degrees before or four after, it will be the Lord of the Year or the revolution, and the significator of the common people, if it is free from the aforementioned impediments. If indeed it is impeded, as I said of the Lord of the Ascendant, it will not be the Lord of the Year or the revolution. If there is no exaltation of any planet, or if there is one but the Lord of the exaltation cannot be the Lord of the Year: seek then the ruler from the **Sun** if the revolution is by day, or from the **Moon** if it is by night; for the luminary which holds authority, if it has any dignity in the Ascendant, will be the Lord of the Year or the revolution. But if again the luminary which holds authority cannot be the Lord of the Year, seek then the significator from the **Lord of the Term** <note>Specific degrees within a sign assigned to a planet</note>; if it is in the Ascendant—three degrees before the line or four after—and is free, it will be the Lord of the Year. And if again the Lord of the Term cannot be the Lord of the Year, seek then the ruler from the **Lord of the Triplicity** <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element</note> in the same manner I told you for the others. And if it is none of these things which I told you—neither the Lord of the house, nor of the exaltation of the Ascendant, nor of the Term, nor of the Triplicity, nor the luminary which holds authority (namely the Sun by day and the Moon by night): seek then the ruler of the year or the revolution...

It details the precise astronomical observations required and establishes a hierarchical method for determining the "Lord of the Year."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "revolutions" (astrological returns) from the previous page, beginning mid-word with the conclusion of the previous sentence. ...of the revolution from the lord of the tenth: see if the lord of the tenth house is in the tenth, or three degrees before [the cusp], or four degrees behind, and is not **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually seen as a sign of weakness or delay</note> or **combust** <note>Being so close to the Sun that its influence is "burnt up" or hidden</note>; if so, he shall be the Lord of the Year or the revolution, and the significator of the common people and the peasants. If, however, the lord of the tenth house is retrograde or combust or otherwise impeded so that he cannot be the significator, then seek the ruler from the lord of the **exaltation** <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note> of the tenth house—if there is an exaltation of any planet there. If that planet is in the tenth, free from the aforementioned impediments, and is at least three degrees before the line of the tenth house or four degrees behind it, he shall be the Lord of the Year and the significator of the common people.

But if there is no exaltation of any planet, or if there is one but the lord of the exaltation cannot be the Lord of the Year, then seek it from the **luminary** <note>The Sun or the Moon</note> which has authority; for if it is there and holds any dignity in that place, it shall be the Lord of the Year. If, again, the luminary which has authority cannot be the Lord of the Year, then seek the ruler from the lord of the **term** <note>term: a specific subdivision of an astrological sign governed by a particular planet</note> of the degree of the tenth house. If he is in the degree of the tenth house, or three degrees before or four behind, and is free from impediments, he shall be the Lord of the Year and the significator of the common people.

If, again, the lord of the term cannot be the Lord of the Year, then seek the ruler from the lord of the **triplicity** <note>triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</note> of the tenth house. If he is on the line of the tenth house, or three degrees before or four after, he shall be the Lord of the Year and the significator of the common people or the peasants. If you cannot find a significator from the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> or from the tenth, seek him through that same method which I told you for the first and the tenth, starting from the seventh house. And if you cannot have him from the seventh, seek him by that same method from the fourth. And if you still cannot have him from the fourth, seek him by that same method from the 11th. And if you still cannot have him from the 11th, seek him by that same method from the 9th. And if you still cannot have him from the 9th, seek him by that same method from the 5th. And if you still cannot have him from the 5th, finally seek him from the third, always beginning with the lord of the house; then from the lord of the exaltation; afterward from the luminary which has authority; then from the lord of the term; and lastly from the lord of the triplicity.

And it was the custom of one of the ancients that you can do this same thing through the lord of the **face** <note>A ten-degree subdivision of a sign, also known as a decan</note>. And whatever planet you find in any of the aforementioned places after the failure of the previously mentioned significators for the lordship of the year—if he has any dignity there, even if he has only the face there, and is free from impediments as was said of the others—he shall be the Lord of the Year or the revolution. And if there are multiple planets in any of the aforementioned places, the one who is more powerful or the <term>almutem</term> <note>original: "almuten"—the planet that holds the most combined dignity or "fortitude" at a specific point in the zodiac</note> by the multitude of strengths in that place shall be the Lord of the Year or the revolution. And if they are equal in strength, the one who is closer to the line [of the house cusp] shall be preferred. And if they are **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, the one who is closer to the Sun shall excel the other. And if both are equally distant from the Moon or the Sun, then the one who will change more quickly from the degree in which he is located is to be preferred. 

And if any of the aforementioned planets aspects any of the named houses by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note> within two degrees before or three after, and holds any dignity there, he shall be the Lord of the Year after you have found nothing among the other aforementioned rules. And if there is a house of the Ascendant or an exaltation of some luminary and it aspects the Ascendant by a trine or sextile aspect within 3 degrees before or 3 after, or if it is in the second house from the Ascendant, it shall be the Lord of the Year. If this is not the case, look to the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of its exaltation; and see if the luminary which has authority is in the house of either of them and aspects it by a trine or sextile aspect, and is not falling away from the Ascendant and is in a strong place, for it shall be the Lord of the Year. And some prefer the luminary which has authority to the <term>almutem</term> planet. However, I do not see the reason why that should be preferred...

<column-break/>

...always preferring the Ascendant, the 10th, and then the other houses in this order: 10th, 7th, 4th, 11th, 9th, 5th, 3rd, as was said. And if neither of the luminaries is in any of the aforementioned places, see if the planet in whose house the luminary of authority is located is in any of those places; for he shall be the Lord of the Year or the revolution, whether he has dignity there or not. Now, if this again is not the case, look to the lord of the hour of that revolution; if he is in any of the aforementioned places, he shall be the Lord of the Year or the revolution, and the significator of the common people or the peasants.

And always understand regarding any significator: if he is on the line of the house in which he is, or three degrees before or 4 behind, always preferring the lord of the house [over] the lord of the exaltation, and the lord of the exaltation [over] the lord of the term, and the lord of the term [over] the lord of the triplicity. For the lord of the house has 5 strengths; the lord of the exaltation has 4 strengths; the lord of the term has 3 strengths; the lord of the triplicity has 3 strengths. And although the lord of the term here has as many strengths as the lord of the triplicity, nevertheless those [the house and exaltation lords] are preferred because of their excellence. 

Now, if this again is not the case, know the locations of all the signs in which the luminaries are; and the location of the sign in which the luminary of authority is, and put it in the count with the other significators. For if all the significators fail for the lord of the revolution, that one will be the <unclear>ruler</unclear> who is most powerful by the multitude of strengths and will take the place of the Lord of the Year, at least until the lord of the Ascendant or the 10th is directed, if he was retrograde, or escapes if he was combust. Now, if none of these things happen, then the disposition returns to the luminary that has authority. And if the revolution is at night and the Moon is under the rays of the Sun, then the Sun shall take its place.

**Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said, and it seems to me reasonable to agree through investigation, that the significations of the lord of the term, the lord of the triplicity, and the lord of the hour are to be considered in two places only: namely, in the 1st and in the 10th house. And some might perhaps believe that he was contradicting himself. For he says elsewhere that their significations are considered in all the aforementioned places, but it is not so. Where he says they are to be considered in the 1st and 10th, he meant by their own nature. Where he says they are considered in all other places, he meant by accident: that is, they are testimonies of good or evil, and thus both [views] are to be followed.

Furthermore, if the lord of the term or triplicity or hour is in the Ascendant or in the 10th, and the lord of the Ascendant or 10th is in the degree of his exaltation, or one degree before or one behind, and he cannot be the significator, and any of those [other lords] holds the lordship of the year, he adds to himself from the signification of the first lord: that is, the lord of the triplicity will have a third part, the lord of the term will have a fifth, and the lord of the hour a seventh, according to how strong they are. In other places, however, this does not happen to them; rather, it diminishes their strength in them.

And although I have named for you the places and houses from which the Lord of the Year or the revolution can be known, I want you to know that they are not equal in strength. For the Ascendant and the 10th exceed the other houses in strength; the seventh is below the tenth; the fourth is below the seventh; the eleventh is below the fourth; the ninth is below the eleventh; the fifth is below the ninth; the third is below the fifth. Therefore, according to the house from which the Lord of the Year was taken, according to that house the significations will be stronger or weaker in 그 year, or that half-year, or that quarter, in the regions over which that revolution occurs. Therefore, it will be necessary for you to consider according to the part of the climate in which you are, or of which the revolution occurs. For there can be a revolution which is not a full year, such as when the year revolves by half-years or by quarters.

It remains, therefore, that the testimonies which create significations in these places are four: the first of which is the lord of the house; the second is the lord of the exaltation; the third is the luminary which has authority; the fourth is the <term>almutem</term> planet in the place from which the revolution is taken, by the nature and position of the circle at that hour in which the year revolves. After which you will not be able to work through...

You shall also see, after it seems to you that you have found the lord of the year, if he is in the house of another planet and is joined to it by a favorable **aspect** <note>The geometric angle between two planets, such as a trine or sextile</note> when it gives him its virtue; then that planet becomes the lord of the year if it is in an excellent place from the ascendant: even more strongly if some luminary regards them, or one of them, or the lord of the house in which the luminary is placed. And the **Sun** could also be the lord of the year since it is the receiver and gatherer of the lights or strengths of the planets—for instance, if the revolution occurs at night and the planet which ought to be the lord of the year is nocturnal and is **under the Sun's rays** <note>When a planet is so close to the Sun that its light is obscured, weakening its effect</note>. And if all the aforementioned are lacking, the governance or lordship of the year reverts to the lord of the ascendant, whatever its condition may be and in whatever place it is found. And since it might be difficult for you to always observe everything that has been said, I will shorten the rules for you a little: and I will summarize for you the considerations and modes by which you ought to find the significator or lord of the year or the revolution. And there are 12 modes and 54 considerations.

The **first** of the modes is that you look to the lords of the houses from which the lord of the year is sought. The **second** is that you look to the lords of their exaltations. The **third**, that you look to the luminary that has authority. The **fourth**, that you look to the lords of their **terms** <note>term: Terms; specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign governed by different planets</note>. The **fifth**, that you look to the lords of their **triplicities** <note>term: Triplicities; the four groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water)</note>. The **sixth**, that you look to the **almuten** over those places. The **seventh**, that you look to the lord of the **hour** of the revolution. The **eighth**, that you look to the planet in whose house the luminary with authority is placed. The **ninth**, that you look to see if any of the planets **aspects** the ascendant. The **tenth**, that you see whether the ascendant of the revolution is the house or exaltation of any of the luminaries and that luminary aspects it. The **eleventh**, that you see if the luminary that has authority is in the house of the lord of the ascendant or the lord of its exaltation. The **twelfth**, that you look to the lord of the house in which the planet resides in whose house the luminary with authority was placed, to see what its condition is. Finally, other modes could be had, but these are the primary and most important.

### Chapter 2. On finding the significator of the king.

Having spoken of the significator of the common people or the peasants, it remains for you yet to find the **significator of the king**, since it is very opportune to consider him as well in the revolutions of the years of the world. You can find him in this manner: Look to the lord of the **tenth house** <note>The house of status, career, and rulers</note> of the chart of the revolution of the year to see whether it is free from **combustion** <note>Being too close to the Sun</note>, **retrogradation** <note>Moving backwards</note>, fall, and other aforementioned impediments. If it is so, and it is in the cusp of the 10th house or three degrees before or five after, he shall be the significator of the king without doubt; work through him and do not seek another. If, however, you find him impeded by any of the aforementioned impediments, he shall no longer be the significator. Seek then the significator from the lord of the exaltation of the sign of the tenth house, if there is an exaltation of any planet there; if he is free (as I said regarding the lord of the house) and is in the cusp of the tenth house or three degrees before or four after, he shall be the significator of the king. If, however, he is impeded, he shall not be his significator. Seek then the significator from the **Sun**, who, if he is free and safe as I said regarding the others, and is in the cusp of the tenth house or 3 degrees before or 5 behind, he shall be the significator of the king. If, however, it is not so, he shall no longer be the significator. Seek him then from the planet that is **almuten** in the sign of the tenth house by the multitude of its dignities. If he is in the cusp of the tenth house or 3 degrees before or 5 after, free and safe, he shall be the significator of the king. If, however, he is...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for identifying planetary rulers in a revolution (solar return) chart. If [the planet] is hindered, it cannot be the **significator** <note>The planet chosen to represent a specific person or matter in an astrological chart</note>. ¶ **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer whose works were vital to medieval European science</note> indeed proposed the Sun for the lord of **exaltation** <note>A specific sign where a planet is thought to have its highest and most beneficial power</note>. If, however, you do not find any of these, then seek the significator from the planet that was on the **cusp** <note>The starting border of an astrological house</note> of the **tenth house** <note>The house governing kingship, status, and public authority</note>, or three degrees before or four degrees after, provided it is otherwise free and possesses some **dignity** <note>Astrological strength gained by being in a favorable sign or position</note> there; for that planet itself shall be the significator of the king. If, however, it is hindered, it shall not be the significator of the king. If it does not have dignity there, but is on the cusp or two degrees before or three after, or if it is the lord of the house in which the **Lot of Kingship** <note>A mathematical point in a chart calculated from the positions of the planets to signify royal fortune</note> falls, and if it is free and safe from the aforementioned hindrances, it shall be the significator of the king.

¶ And if this still is not found, Albumasar says that if the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the chart, also called the tenth house</note> is the house of the Sun <note>The sign of Leo</note>, and the Sun is on its cusp, neither removed nor falling away, the Sun itself shall be the significator of the king; and similarly when it is in the **ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and received by Mars, and Leo is in the Midheaven, because the ascendant then is Scorpio. ¶ And he said that if the Midheaven is Aries and the Sun is on its cusp according to the proper order, and Mars is "falling" <note>In a weak or inactive house</note> from it, the Sun itself shall be the significator of the king; and if it looks upon Mars, Mars shall participate in the signification. ¶ And he said if Mars is strong and in a good state in its own place, and the Sun is joined to it, Mars shall be the significator of the king—and more worthily so if it is in Capricorn and the Sun is joined to it from the Midheaven. ¶ And he said that if its **fall** <note>The sign where a planet is weakest; for the Sun, this is Libra</note> occurs in the Midheaven or in an **angle** <note>The powerful 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> from the ascendant, and it casts its rays toward it, the Sun shall be more worthy of the signification. And similarly, when the Sun is in an angle of the Midheaven or other places looking upon the Midheaven with aspects of friendship, and is the lord of the Midheaven, it shall be more worthy of the signification.

### Chapter 2. When the Lord of the Year becomes the significator of the king.

¶ But if you do not find it as I have told you, then if the planet is the lord of the house or of the exaltation of the **Lord of the Year** <note>The planet ruling the entire year's forecast</note>, and it looks upon it from any **aspect** <note>A specific geometric angle between planets, like a square or trine</note> except opposition, that planet shall be the Lord of the Year or the significator: the significator of the common people and the king. ¶ And if this still is not found, see if the Lord of the Year is joined with the lord of the 10th house or with the lord of its exaltation from such a place that the lord of the 10th "receives" <note>A term for a supportive relationship between planets in each other's signs</note> it; for then it commits the management of the outcome to the Lord of the Year as significator of the king. Also, if the lord of the 10th house is in the house or exaltation of the Lord of the Year, so that the lord of the 10th receives from it and commits the management to the Lord of the Year: for the Lord of the Year would not become the significator of the king unless the lord of the 10th committed its management to it. 

¶ And if this again is not found, see if the Sun is the Lord of the Year, and if it has some dignity in the 10th, or if the lord of the 10th is **under the sunbeams** <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen, which usually weakens a planet</note>—whether it has escaped **combustion** <note>The most intense state of being hidden by the Sun's light</note> or not—provided it does not appear from under the rays, the Sun shall be the significator of the king, especially in the region where this occurs. 

¶ And Albumasar said if the Sun commits its management to the ascendant and has some testimony in the Midheaven, the lord of the ascendant shall be the significator of the king. ¶ And he said that if the Midheaven is one of the houses of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> or his sign of exaltation <note>Libra</note>, and Saturn is on its cusp and free from combustion, Saturn shall be the significator of the king. ¶ And he said that if the Sun has no testimony in the Midheaven, look to the lord of the Midheaven and the lord of its exaltation: whichever of them is stronger, with more testimonies and in a better state, with more collection and reception of the lights of the planets and a better position relative to the Midheaven, that one shall be the significator of the king. ¶ And if the lord of the Midheaven, the lord of its exaltation, and the Sun are all "falling" from the aspects and are in a bad state, and you find none of the above, see if any planet looks upon any of the aforementioned significators that do not look upon the 10th, while it itself looks upon the 10th: so that it carries its light to it. For this will strengthen it regarding the king's management, and he whose light is thus carried to the 10th of that revolution becomes the significator of the king. But if you find none of these, return then to the Lord of the Year, the lord of the 10th, and the Sun...

<column-break/>

...and whichever of them you find stronger or less weak, or better disposed or less poorly, or in a better place from the 10th or a less bad one, set this one as the significator of the king. ¶ And Albumasar said when the Sun is the lord of the ascendant, the Midheaven will be Taurus. ¶ And if Venus is under its rays, the Sun will be the significator of the king because the lord of the Midheaven <note>Venus rules Taurus</note> is under the rays. ¶ If, however, Venus has emerged from under the rays into its own light, she herself will be more worthy of the signification; she will be, for instance, in the ascendant or in a house from which she looks upon the 10th, and all the better if she is in her own house or exaltation. And he said when Venus is at the end of an **angle** <note>The strongest points of the chart</note> and "beats" her strength into the Sun—which cannot happen except when there is a **conjunction** <note>When two planets are at the same degree</note>—if Venus is at the end of the angle and beats her strength into the Sun, then the Sun shall be the significator of the king. ¶ And he said the angles of the planets are the totality of their calculation of truth or certainty; and this is taken from the diameters of their **epicycles** <note>original: "circulorum eorum brevium," literally "their small circles"; the small circles used in Ptolemaic astronomy to explain planetary orbits</note>.

### Chapter 3. How the lord of the ascendant is the Lord of the Year, from which is known the state of the king, his helpers, the common people, and certain men, both religious and secular.

¶ Having found the significator of the year (or the revolution) and the significator of the king, it remains to find the significators of other diverse persons, and from where they look upon the significators of the king. You cannot know this, as Albumasar says, except from Saturn, the Sun, the 10th house, and its significator. For if you see these four well-disposed, announce entirely and on all sides that the king’s state is good. If, however, you find them hindered, announce entirely the opposite. But if you find one free and the other hindered, judge according to what you see of the hindrance or freedom. But Saturn is of greater significance than any of them, both for good and for evil, except for the significator of the king; and the significations of the Sun are beneath the significations of Saturn, and the significations of the lord of the 10th are beneath those of the Sun in this case.

### How to look upon the king's soldiers.

¶ And it is said that you ought to look upon the king’s **soldiers** <note>original: "militibus," which could refer to knights or military forces</note> from the **eleventh house** <note>The house of allies and supporters</note> and its lord; hence if you see the 11th suitable and its lord well-disposed, along with Mars, announce that the state of the king’s soldiers is also good. If, however, you see it unsuitable and its lord hindered, along with Mars, announce the opposite of what was said. If, however, the lord of the 11th or Mars is hindered while the other is free, announce their state as mediocre.

### How to look upon the wealthy and the great men who are beneath the king.

¶ The state of the wealthy and the **magnates** <note>High-ranking nobles or influential figures</note> who are beneath the king: you should take this from **Jupiter** and include the lord of the house in which he resides; if you find him strong and well-disposed, announce their state as good. If, however, you find him poorly disposed, announce the contrary.

### How to look upon bishops and other secular clerics.

¶ For **bishops** and other **secular clerics** <note>Clergy who live in the world rather than in a monastery, such as parish priests</note>, and for **popes**, **cardinals**, and even **legists** <note>Experts in civil law</note>, **decretists** <note>Experts in canon (church) law</note>, and counselors: you shall look to Jupiter, the lord of his house, and the **ninth house** <note>The house governing religion, law, and wisdom</note> and its lord. If you find them free and well-disposed, announce their state as good. If, however, you find one strong and another weak, you shall announce a mediocrity according to the weakness or strength you find.

### How to look upon the king’s soldiers, his helpers, and those who bear arms.

¶ For these and the king’s helpers and the **armbearers** <note>Squire-like figures or soldiers</note> for the sake of profiting from war: you shall look to **Mars**; if you find him well-disposed, announce their state as good. If, however, you find him poorly disposed, announce the contrary.

### ¶ How to look at [the fate of] those in regular religious orders.

Regarding the religious who serve God according to a rule (*regulares*) <note>Monks and nuns who lived according to a specific "Rule," such as the Rule of St. Benedict</note> and those who are appointed to this service: do not believe this refers to just anyone wearing a religious hood, but to those who have dedicated themselves and their possessions to God. Among these, you should count monks—especially those wearing black robes—and the elderly, the decrepit, and those who live by heavy, lowly labor, such as fullers <note>Workers who cleaned and thickened cloth</note> or diggers and the like. You shall look to **Saturn** for these; if you find him free, fortunate (meaning strong), announce that it will be a good year for the aforementioned people. If, however, you find him to the contrary, announce the contrary.

### ¶ How to look at [the fate of] women.

The state of women you shall take from **Venus** and her position. If you find her well-disposed, announce that it will be good for women, and especially for young girls. If, however, you find her ill-disposed, you shall announce the contrary.

### ¶ How to look at [the fate of] merchants and traders, etc.

The state of merchants, traders, painters, scribes, judges, wise men, teachers—especially those of the *quadrivium* <note>The four "mathematical" liberal arts: Arithmetic, Geometry, Music, and Astronomy</note>—as well as boys, adolescents, and the like, you shall take from **Mercury**. If you find him free and well-disposed, announce that their state will be good; if you find him hindered, judge the opposite. However, the state of merchants varies from the others: for their state is looked at through the Lord of the Year, the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart</note> and its lord, the Moon, and Jupiter, just as it is through Mercury. But Mercury and Jupiter prevail over the others in signifying merchants.

### ¶ How to look at [the fate of] the lowly and the common people.

For the lowly, the common people, and sailors of smaller ships, look to the **Moon**. If you find her free and well-disposed, announce that their state will be good; if she is hindered, announce the opposite. In all the cases mentioned above, involve the Lord of the Year and the lord of the "house" in which you find the **significator** <note>The specific planet chosen to represent the person or group you are asking about</note> whose fate you seek. Mix them together and see how they are positioned and how they are "joined" <note>An astrological aspect or connection between planets</note>. For if all are free and fortunate—that is, the planet naturally signifying the matter, the planet in whose house it resides, and the Lord of the Year—judge it to be good in every way for the subject you seek. If all are safe but one is hindered, judge more good than bad. If they are hindered but one is safe, judge more bad than good. According to whether their freedom or hindrance is greater or lesser, and according to the Ascendant at that time, you shall judge the increase or decrease of good or evil. For if the Ascendant or the **Midheaven** <note>The tenth house, representing the highest point in the sky and matters of status</note> is one of the houses of the planet naturally signifying the subject—for example, if you seek the significance of Saturn and the Ascendant or Midheaven is Capricorn or Aquarius; or if you seek the significance of Jupiter and the Ascendant or Midheaven is Sagittarius or Pisces; or if you seek the significance of Mercury and it is Gemini or Virgo—[the effect is strengthened]. In the case of Venus and the Moon, it is different: if the significance of Venus is sought, do not consider the Ascendant or the Midheaven, but rather the seventh and fourth houses. For if the seventh or fourth house is Taurus or Libra, it will harm or benefit just as the Ascendant or Midheaven harms or benefits in the cases of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury. And if the seventh or fourth is Cancer [for the Moon], this is because of the femininity of those planets and those places. In the case of Mars, the Ascendant and Midheaven are considered because of his masculinity, but the seventh and fourth are also considered because of his nocturnal nature.

### ¶ Chapter 4: What the Lord of the Year or the Revolution signifies in the places where it falls at the hour of the revolution.

When you have found the Lord of the Year (or the revolution) and the significator of the king and the others whose significators are considered in revolutions, you must consider in this chapter those things which appear

<column-break/>

possible to happen in that revolution. But first, concerning the universal accidents of the year (besides the fertility of the earth and similar things, which will be discussed elsewhere in their own place and time): ¶ Look, therefore, in which place in the chart you have cast the Lord of the Year fell at the hour the year began. For if it fell in the Ascendant or in a place of friendship to the Ascendant, it signifies good, joy, and tranquility for the people of that **climate** <note>A geographical zone or region defined by its latitude</note> and region, according to the nature of the house into which it fell, as is said elsewhere. If, however, it fell in a place of enmity to the Ascendant, it will signify hindrance, hardship, and friction—and all the more strongly if the Lord of the Year is an "enemy" to the lord of the Ascendant. For if it falls in the sixth house, which is one of the houses inimical to the Ascendant, illnesses will happen to the bodies of the people of that region, and loss among small animals that are not ridden <note>Likely referring to sheep, pigs, or poultry rather than horses</note>, especially if that house is a sign signifying such a subject. If it falls in the seventh house, hardships, rumors, and wars will happen. If it falls in the twelfth, enmities and betrayals will happen to them; and all these will happen according to the nature and substance of the sign in which the significator is placed. And this applies not only to the lord of the Ascendant, but also to the lord of the **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet is thought to have particularly high honor</note>, the **term** <note>A small division of a zodiac sign</note>, the **triplicity** <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water)</note>, and all other significators of the revolution. But the significance of these others will be secondary to the significance of the lord of the Ascendant, whether their meanings are good or evil. Evil significations will be even stronger if the Lord of the Year happens to be **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually considered a sign of weakness or corruption</note>, though this happens very rarely. Yet, there could be such a poor arrangement of the planets that the Lord of the Year is necessarily retrograde; in that case, it needs the support of another planet to lift it up and return its light to the Ascendant, or there must be a "return of light" from planet to planet until a planet is found that returns its light to the Ascendant or the Midheaven (if it is the significator of the king).

### ¶ Chapter 5: On the knowledge of events that are to come in the year and in which parts they should happen.

Although it is very difficult to see in which parts, regions, and climates the events of the revolution or the year should occur, it seems appropriate to me to know what can be learned from it. I will tell you certain things through which you may perceive something by God's will; for I cannot explain everything to you fully because of the great confusion of cities and regions. For ancient cities, towns, castles, and other dwellings equivalent to cities in the climates—whether newly established or old—are [distributed] by the arrival of the Lord. 12345. <note>original: "12345." - This appears to be a list or a sequence of categories</note> as I have found recited by certain ancient wise men. Among these, **Messahala** the Indian <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a Persian Jewish astrologer who was a founding father of Baghdad and a major source for medieval astrology</note> said there are 12 [regions] exceeding others in magnitude. Of these, in the first climate, two are assigned to **Saturn**. In the second, two are assigned to **Jupiter**. In the third, two are assigned to **Mars**. In the fourth, two are assigned to the **Sun**. In the fifth, one is assigned to **Venus**. In the sixth, two are assigned to **Mercury**. In the seventh, one is assigned to the **Moon**. ¶ Then, when you wish to know the events that are to come in the region where you are, from the revolution or year you are considering, you shall note the Ascendant according to the "ascensions" <note>The time it takes for a sign to rise over the horizon at a specific latitude</note> of the city or region where you are. See how far it extends to the west; for that significance will extend as long as the Ascendant does not undergo an alteration—that is, it expires after passing five degrees, giving 53 **miles** to each degree. Some ancient wise men measured by a mile of 4,000 cubits (using an equal cubit). The significance will extend as far as the nature of the Ascendant allows.

### Chapter Six: How the Earth is divided into two primary divisions.

<image-desc>Decorative initial N at the start of the chapter.</image-desc>For the Earth is divided into two primary divisions: one of which consists of the eastern quarter and the southern quarter, because the heat in which they agree associates them and makes one share the nature of the other. The second consists of the western quarter and the northern quarter, because the coldness in which they agree associates them and makes one share the nature of the other.

### Chapter Seven: How it is divided according to three other secondary divisions.

<image-desc>Decorative initial I at the start of the chapter.</image-desc>Furthermore, the Earth is subdivided into three other secondary divisions: namely the upper, the middle, and the lower. These three divisions are assigned to the three superior planets: namely Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—and to these rather than others, because greater significations descend from them than from the others. For although the other planets participate with them, their power is far greater and stronger than the power of the inferior planets <note>The "inferior" planets are those between the Earth and the Sun: Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</note>. 

Now, the first division—namely the upper, which is the northern part, comprising the seventh climate <note>A "climate" in ancient geography was a latitudinal band of the Earth</note> and whatever part of the Earth is inhabited beyond the climates determined by the ancients toward the North Pole—is attributed to **Saturn**, in which the **Moon** participates. This is evident through these facts: because of the slowness of Saturn and his darkness, and the thickness of the air in those parts and the vapors of those lands, the masses of people inhabiting those regions are of little knowledge and little intellect, and they are forgetful; nevertheless, they are greedy, yet mercy reigns in them. 

However, if it should occasionally happen that one of them applies himself to knowledge, he will greatly exceed others—such as that most reverend predecessor, Albumasar Tricas <note>original: "albumasar tricas"; likely referring to the Persian astronomer Abu Ma'shar</note>, who, although he studied in Athens, was nevertheless a Latin, as he himself professes in the treatise *Agiget*. And certain others are found, though they are rare, such as Michael Scot <note>A famous 13th-century mathematician and scholar</note> of my own time, and another younger man, namely Albert the German <note>Albertus Magnus, the famous theologian and scientist</note> of the Order of Preachers. That the Moon participates with Saturn is evident because of their persistence and fury, which happens to them because of the influence of the Moon and her instability, sudden change, and alteration, and because of their yellow, white, and red colors...

### Chapter Eight: How the Earth is divided into seven other divisions.

Once again, those two and those three divisions <note>Referring to the previous chapter's divisions of the world</note> are subdivided into another seven divisions according to the number of the seven planets; these are called "climates" <term>climata: latitudinal bands of the Earth used by ancient geographers to calculate the length of the longest day</term> which are assigned to the seven planets in this way. For the first climate is assigned to Saturn, who is higher and further above than the other planets and slower than the rest. The second climate is assigned to Jupiter, who follows immediately after Saturn in slowness and succeeds him in the order of the celestial spheres. The third is assigned to Mars, who follows immediately after Jupiter and succeeds him both in slowness and in the order of the spheres. The fourth is assigned to the Sun, who follows Mars in the order of the spheres. The fifth is assigned to Venus, who follows the Sun in the order of the spheres. The sixth is assigned to Mercury, who follows Venus in the order of the spheres. The seventh and final climate is assigned to the Moon, who follows Mercury in the order of the spheres, because she is lower than the other planets and faster than the rest. Thus, each planet exerts more influence over the climate assigned to it than over the others, although each of them has something to do with every climate, sometimes more and sometimes less.

Similarly, the signs of the zodiac rule over regions and impress their influence upon them, each according to its nature: for the fiery signs impress more upon hot regions, the earthy upon dry ones, the airy upon humid ones, and the watery upon cold ones. This is because the signs do not signify parts of the world by their location or position, but by their nature. Therefore, if a region ruled by a fiery sign is already hot, that significance will occur more strongly in a cold region: for in a cold region it tempers the coldness, and that which it moistens in a humid region, it tempers with dryness in a dry one, and vice-versa. 

Just as Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius—which are the first triplicity <note>original: "triplicitas"; a group of three signs belonging to the same element</note>—bring heat to the eastern parts, in the northern parts they temper the coldness, because they are fiery and are eastern signs. Thus, if any of those signs is the ascendant, it will strengthen the significance and increase it; and the eastern wind is hot and dry. And just as Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn—which are the second triplicity—bring dryness to the southern parts, in the western parts they temper the humidity, because they are earthy and are southern signs. Thus, if the angle of the tenth house <note>The Midheaven or peak of the chart</note> consists of those signs, it will strengthen the significance and increase it; and the southern wind is hot and humid. And just as Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius—which are the third triplicity—bring moisture to the western parts, in the southern part they temper the dryness, because they are airy and are western signs. Thus, if the angle of the seventh house <note>The Descendant or western horizon</note> consists of those signs, it will strengthen the significance and increase it; and the western wind is cold and humid. And just as Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces—which are the fourth triplicity—bring cold to the northern parts, in the eastern parts they temper the heat, because they are watery and are northern signs. Thus, if the angle of the fourth house <note>The Imum Coeli or bottom of the chart</note> consists of those signs, it will strengthen the significance and increase it; and the northern wind is cold and dry. 

The planets also assist in this: for if a significance is in the north and Saturn rules that significance, he will assist it and make it appear more clearly—and all the more strongly if Mercury is with him and it

### Another division of the earth.

And after these two, these three, and these seven divisions, the earth is again subdivided into another twelve divisions according to the number of the twelve signs, and according to the passage of degrees from east to west. For Aries is assigned to the first climate; thus Mars, who is the ruler of the house of Aries <note>In traditional astrology, Mars "owns" or rules the sign of Aries</note>, governs the significations of that climate from east to west. For Jupiter, to whom the first term of Aries belongs, governs the significations of the revolution of the first climate from the beginning of the habitable earth on the eastern side toward the west for 318 miles. And after him, Saturn for 212 miles. From there, the governance returns to Jupiter and to the others until it reaches the end of the habitable region toward the west. 

And Taurus is assigned to the southern half of the second climate; its significance is governed by Venus, since she is the lady of Taurus from east to west.
