However, if the climate should not be of such great length that the significations of the planets can be extended to the number of miles, it could be completed just as was said, it does not matter. Wherefore you ought to look at the arrangement and state of the planets in the revolutions of the years, whether of births or of the beginnings of the world <note>Referring to both natal horoscopes and mundane astrology, which predicts global events based on the year's beginning</note>; and see if the state of the lord of the sign is good; because it signifies a good state for the climate generally according to the part it presides over; and look similarly at the state of the planets present in the terms. For if they agree in one state, it will signify that the signification of the revolution will appear more, whether in good or in evil: as if the state of the lord of the sign and the state of the lord of the term were both good, it signifies complete good in the region over which the lord of the term presides. But if the state of both were evil, it signifies that complete evil will appear in the region over which the lord of the term presides.

### ¶ Chapter 9. How one must observe the state of the Sun in the revolution of the year if it occurs by day.

Observe also in the revolution of the world's year <note>original: *revolutiõe anni mudi*; this refers to the "Solar Ingress" chart cast for the moment the Sun enters the first degree of Aries</note>—if the revolution occurs during the day—the state of the Sun and its disposer, whether it is eclipsed in that year or not. Observe the aspects of the planets toward it, namely the "fortunes" <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> and the "evils" <note>the malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, for the fortunes signify good, while the evils conversely signify evil. For if the Sun is fortified and well-situated, it signifies exaltation and the occurrence of great things in a day revolution. Observe also the state of the lord of the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the chart</term> and whether it is free from the aforementioned impediments or not; for if it is free, it brings goodness and tranquility to the land belonging to the sign that was rising then, and to the citizens of that region and the people signified by that planet. 

But if it is impeded, it brings hindrance, detriment, and evil which will befall the inhabitants of that region and those signified by the planet that is the lord of the Ascendant of the revolution. Their condition is disposed according to the nature of the sign ruling that region which is signified by that sign: for example, when the Ascendant is Libra and Venus, its mistress, is "falling" from the Ascendant or from the angles <note>falling: located in a weak house; angles: the four most powerful houses of a chart</note>, or is impeded, or retrograde, or "combust" <term>combust: a planet weakened by being too close to the Sun</term>, or besieged by two evils, or unfortunate in some other way, it signifies that destructions, infirmities, and sorrows will happen in Arabia and to those living in it, and to all who are signified by Libra or by Venus. And if the Ascendant is Leo and the Sun is impeded, it signifies that the aforementioned hindrances will happen to those of Babylon and to all who are signified by Leo and the Sun. But if the Ascendant is Cancer and the Moon is hindered by the aforementioned impediments, it signifies that the aforementioned hindrances will happen to the Romans and to all who are signified by Cancer and the Moon. And you should understand this in the same way for any sign and any planet according to its own significations.

### ¶ Chapter ten. How one must observe the state of the Moon if the revolution occurs by night.

If, however, the revolution occurs at night, then observe the Moon just as you observe the Sun in a day revolution: if she is the mistress of the revolution or the disposition and is in Cancer, you shall observe her alone. But if she is outside of Cancer, then look to the lord of the house in which she is located: if you find it strong and fortunate in a powerful location or by the aspect of "fortunes" to it, it signifies good for the citizens of that region. If, however, you find it weak and unfortunate for the reasons mentioned above, it signifies an evil state and a bad disposition for the citizens or inhabitants of that region and their detriment. Speak similarly regarding the lord of the Ascendant of the revolution: for if it is in a good state, it signifies good for the aforementioned citizens; if, however, it is in a bad state, it signifies their detriment. 

And know that the Moon in a night revolution, when she is fortunate and powerful, increasing in light and in number <note>meaning a waxing moon with increasing daily motion</note>, signifies exaltation and the advancement of some great matter toward a good end. Observe similarly if the luminary of the time—and especially the nocturnal one <note>the Moon</note>—is joined to Saturn by body or by aspect: for if it is joined to him by body or by any aspect without "perfect reception" <term>reception: a stabilizing relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting</term>, it will increase his malice; and this is more powerful if the Moon is joined to him while her light is decreasing. But if she is then separating from him, and especially while her light is increasing, she will diminish that malice and will not inflict such great detriment. 

You shall also see where the "evil" planet causing the hindrance is located and of which house it is the lord: for the harm will come from the matter signified by that house. For example, if it is in the second house, the cause will arise from substance <note>wealth or possessions</note> or from those things signified by the second house. If it is in the third, the cause will arise from brothers, or from short journeys, or from those things signified by the third house. If it is in the fourth, the cause will arise from fathers or inheritances, or from those things signified by the fourth house. If it is in the

And if it is in the sixth, the cause will arise from infirmities, or male or female servants, or from those things signified by the sixth house. If it is in the seventh, the cause will arise from wives, or partners, or enemies, or from any of the causes signified by the seventh house. If it is in the eighth, the cause will arise from death, or from those who inherit from the dead, or from those things signified by the eighth house. And if it is in the ninth, the cause will arise from religion or religious people, or long journeys, or the pursuit of things pertaining to the future eternal life, or any of those things signified by the ninth house.

Chapter 11. What each of the seven planets signifies when in the Ascendant at the time of the year's revolution.

### ¶ Concerning Saturn in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of Saturn riding a chariot pulled by two winged dragons. Saturn is depicted as an elderly man with a long beard, wearing a draped cloak and holding a scythe. Above him in the sky is the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄).</image-desc>

You shall also observe the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> at the hour of the revolution to see which of the planets is within it. For if Saturn is there, and is not himself the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies detriment to the region subject to that revolution; this may manifest as pestilences, such as lingering illnesses, famines, and highly destructive winds—especially if Saturn is moving "direct" <note>Moving forward through the zodiac from our perspective.</note> and particularly in the Airy signs <note>Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>. If, however, he is retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward, often weakening or internalizing a planet's influence.</note>, he predicts winds but will not permit them to grow strong, though they will still be harmful to those they strike. But if Saturn himself is the Lord of the Ascendant, the aforementioned evils will be mitigated and will not cause as much harm.

### ¶ Concerning what Jupiter signifies in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of Jupiter riding a chariot pulled by two eagles. Jupiter is depicted as a majestic king wearing a crown and holding a scepter. Above him in the sky is the astrological symbol for Jupiter (♃).</image-desc>

If, however, Jupiter is in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution, it signifies a general goodness in the disposition of that year or revolution. There will be peace, security, and more goodwill among the men of that region than usual. It will be well for the wealthy and the great nobles; their goods will increase, and they will prosper and im-

<column-break/>

-prove their business. And if Jupiter is then the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of its exaltation <note>Jupiter is "exalted" or highly honored in the sign of Cancer.</note>, or if he and the Lord of the sign are in a good state through any aspect—especially a trine or sextile <note>Harmonious 120-degree or 60-degree angles.</note>—or through a physical conjunction, there will be love between the king of that region and his subjects, and even the common country-folk will find goodness and things that please them from him.

### ¶ Concerning what Mars signifies in the Ascendant.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of Mars riding a chariot pulled by two galloping horses. Mars is depicted as a warrior in full plate armor, holding a raised sword in his right hand and a shield in his left. Above him in the sky is the astrological symbol for Mars (♂).</image-desc>

If, however, Mars is in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution, and he is free, fortunate, and strong, it signifies that an earthquake will occur in that region. If he is in an Oriental sign <note>The "eastern" signs, associated with the first quarter of the year/Spring.</note>, it signifies this will happen in the first quarter of that revolution. If he is in a Southern sign <note>Associated with the second quarter/Summer.</note>, it signifies it will happen in the second quarter. If indeed he is in an Occidental sign <note>Associated with the third quarter/Autumn.</note>, it signifies it will happen in the third quarter. And if he is in a Northern sign <note>Associated with the final quarter/Winter.</note>, it signifies it will happen in the final quarter of the revolution. It also signifies a scarcity of rain and a lack of war. If indeed he is hindered and in a bad state, say the opposite: in place of good, say evil, and in place of evil, say worse—except regarding rain, for his power is not exhausted in that. If he is on the cusp of the Tenth House, or within 15 minutes <note>A minute is 1/60th of a degree.</note> before or after it, or within one degree after it, it signifies that the king or presiding official of that region will capture or imprison many of his subjects. If he is between 15 and 30 minutes beyond it, or from one to three degrees after it, he will capture a smaller quantity of them. If he is from 30 minutes to one full degree beyond, or three to five degrees after, he will capture even fewer. If he is from one to two degrees beyond, or five to ten degrees after, he will capture very few indeed. If he is from two to five degrees beyond, or from ten up to 25 degrees after—provided the house is not too remote—he will imprison almost none, or perhaps just a few. And though he may imprison them, he will not kill or mutilate them, except for a few; however, he will torture them. If, however, Mars at the hour of the revolution is on the cusp of the Fourth House, or in the other degrees or places opposite to those mentioned above, he will kill those whom he captures, according to the quantity, proportion, and manner described for when Mars was in the Tenth, and according to the degrees opposite to those. If he is in the First or Seventh house in similar places and degrees, he will mutilate some of them according to the aforementioned quantity and proportion.

### ¶ Concerning what the Sun signifies in the Ascendant.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of Sol (the Sun) riding a chariot pulled by four horses. Sol is depicted as a young man with a crown of radiant light rays, holding a globe in his left hand and a scepter in his right. Above him in the sky is the astrological symbol for the Sun (☉).</image-desc>

If, however, the Sun is in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution, free from malefic planets and other hindrances, and is furthermore the Lord of the Year <note>The planet with the most dignity at the time of the Solar Ingress.</note>, it signifies goodness for all, especially for the great ones and the nobles; it signifies their joy, an increase in wealth, and the perfection of affairs. If he is "received" <term>reception: a supportive relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term>, it signifies the removal of evil. If he is not in the Ascendant at the hour of the revolution, but is elsewhere in a good place and free from hindrances, it signifies the same, but to a lesser degree. If, however, he is hindered, it signifies their detriment and the arising of those evils I mentioned to you.

### On what Venus in the ascendant signifies.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personification of Venus, depicted as a crowned woman seated and holding a mirror. To her right is the astrological symbol for Venus ♀.</image-desc>

**I**f, however, **Venus** is in the ascendant at the hour of the revolution, and she is free <note>original: "libera"; meaning she is not afflicted by "malefic" planets like Mars or Saturn.</note>, fortunate, and strong, she signifies joy, cheerfulness, and dancing. She indicates a diminishing of wars, the marriage of young women, and young men devoted to the pursuits of pleasure <term>the worship of Venus: a poetic way of describing romantic and sexual pursuits</term>. She also signifies a good disposition among the Arabs <note>Medieval European astrology was deeply rooted in Arabic scholarship, and texts often specifically forecasted the state of Islamic nations.</note> and that they will be well-off; this is even better if she is with the lord of the house or the exaltation of the sign in which she resides. But if she is hindered, she signifies the opposite of the aforementioned things.

### On what Mercury in the ascendant signifies.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personification of Mercury, depicted as a man with a winged hat (petasos) holding a caduceus. To his right is the astrological symbol for Mercury ☿.</image-desc>

**I**f indeed **Mercury** is in the ascendant at the hour of the revolution, is in aspect with the "fortunes" <note>The "fortunate" planets are typically Jupiter and Venus.</note>, and is free from impediments, fortunate, and strong—or if he himself is the Lord of the Year—he signifies that things will be well. He portends a good disposition and utility for wise judges, physicians, merchants, and scribes, as well as for children. This is even better if he is then with the lord of the house or the exaltation of the sign in which he resides. If, however, he is hindered, he signifies the opposite of those things I have told you.

### On what the Moon in the ascendant signifies.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personification of the Moon (Luna), depicted as a woman with a bow and arrow (Diana) and a crescent moon. To her right is the astrological symbol for the Moon ☽.</image-desc>

**B**ut if the **Moon** is in the ascendant at the hour of the revolution, or is in the house of the Lord of the Year or of the revolution, and is joined to it by body <note>meaning a "conjunction," where two objects appear in the same spot in the sky.</note> or by aspect (except for the opposition), and is otherwise free from impediments, she signifies an abundance of water or rain. She portends an increase in rivers and streams and their flooding, an increase in cold, and a good disposition among men, who will rejoice in good things. If, however, she is hindered, the aforementioned things will be diminished or perhaps even brought to nothing.

### Chapter 12: On Saturn and Mars when they are hindered in the revolution if they are above the earth.

**Y**ou shall observe if, at the hour of the revolution, **Mars** and **Saturn** are above the earth <note>meaning they are above the horizon and thus visible in the sky.</note> and hindered, for this signifies a gravity or heaviness to the year or the revolution. This is even stronger if Mars "receives" Saturn <note>Reception is a technical relationship where one planet is in a zodiac sign ruled by the other.</note> and commits the disposition to him, for it will signify heavy and durable accidents. These signs or detriments will appear and be made manifest. They will signify, in fact, the detriment and weakness of the king or the presiding official, as well as the wealthy, the noble, and those great men who are fit for rule. Faith and religion will be diminished—indeed, almost annihilated—and religious men will suffer detriment. There will be many thieves and highwaymen or plunderers; wars and contentions will multiply, and there will be more brawls among men than usual. Even religious men will envy one another, especially those to whom pride and vainglory are suited. This is even more grave if Saturn is in the Tenth House <note>The Tenth House represents the government and those in power.</note>. The more these "evils" <note>original: "mali"; referring to the malefic planets Saturn and Mars.</note> are elevated above the earth, the more grave the accidents will be. And it will be even

<column-break/>

worse if the **Moon** is below the earth and commits her disposition to **Saturn** while he is above the earth, or if she is joined to him by opposition or a "square" aspect <note>A square aspect is a 90-degree angle, considered stressful in astrology.</note>. For then it signifies heavy detriments and great, horrible, and fearsome tribulations, such as the death of the king, the great men, the wealthy, or the nobles, or a change of the kingdom for the worse. This is even stronger if these "evils" are retrograde <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, western, or otherwise hindered. If, however, they are direct in motion or "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note> and not hindered, their significations will be more relaxed. If Mars does not commit his disposition to Saturn, the significations of Saturn will not be as intense, and the significations of Mars will be stronger, especially in contentions and wars. If Saturn commits his disposition to Mars, the significations of Mars will be more intense and those of Saturn will be diminished. If the "fortunes" <note>Venus and Jupiter</note> are above the earth, direct, fortunate, and strong, they signify the removal of evil and the increase of good. This is even stronger if **Jupiter** is thus disposed in any of his "dignities" <note>specific parts of the zodiac where a planet has more power</note> and is oriental; **Venus** is stronger when she is western, provided she is otherwise fortunate. For when a planet emerges from under the rays of the Sun <note>original: "sub radijs solis"; this refers to "combustion," where a planet is too close to the sun to be seen and is considered weakened.</note>, it is like a man who was sick and has been freed from illness; he begins to resume his strength and increases little by little until he returns to his former strength, provided the "evils" do not look upon him. For then he is like a sick man who undergoes a "crisis" <term>crisis: a medical turning point, often the moment when a fever breaks or the patient dies</term>, and though he seems to have escaped, he afterwards relapses. When a planet enters under the rays, it is like a man who was healthy and begins to grow sick, or one who was young and begins to grow old until his natural heat fails him.

### Chapter Thirteen: On the planets when they enter the degrees of their exaltations.

**O**bserve, therefore, if **Saturn** enters into Libra or is in it, and especially in its 21st degree; for then his virtue is increased and his significations are made greater. This is even stronger if he receives the disposition of other planets, especially the "evils"; for he will then signify changes and great, marvelous, and stupendous things, which are touched upon in the record of the "conjunction" which Mars and Saturn make at the beginning of Cancer. Observe also whether **Jupiter** enters into Cancer or is in it, especially in its 15th degree; for then his virtue is increased and his significations made greater. This is even stronger if he receives the disposition of any "fortune," for he will signify great things and changes that are marvelous, famous, and durable—yet toward the good. Observe similarly if **Mars** enters into Capricorn or is in it, especially in its 28th degree; for then his significations increase and grow greater. ### ¶ Chapter Fourteen: How the state of the region's nobles, magnates, and commoners or peasants should be considered.
You shall consider what their state will be in the annual revolution and concerning the events that will happen to them; specifically, how the king is obeyed by his subjects, what they seek from him, and in what manner they follow and obey. You shall also look at the citizens of that region and their powers, their rulers, or those set over them. You will look at the condition of each of the aforementioned according to the state of the region, which you can observe in this manner:

You will see in which house its **significator** <term>significator: the specific planet acting as a 'stand-in' for a person or group in the chart</term> is located, for its events will take their root or strength from the house in which it sits. According to the fortune or misfortune of that planet, you will see its impediments, its elevation, or its liberation. And if you see that adversities such as wars and lawsuits and the like ought to happen to him, you can see that the same should befall him through his significator and the strength or weakness of his enemies. 

You will see whether long or short journeys ought to happen to him in that revolution, which you can perceive through the **Lord of the Ninth** and the **Lord of the Third**. For through the Lord of the Ninth you will perceive pilgrimages or long journeys; through the Lord of the Third, short or nearby ones. You will see the Lord of the house of journeys for this revolution and its location: if it is well-disposed, in a fortunate place, and strong, and if it is **received** <term>reception: when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting, indicating cooperation</term> by the house it is in, it signifies that he will travel or go on pilgrimage at his departure for the sake of peace, wandering, or leisure. 

And if it is in its **station** <note>original: "statione"; the point where a planet appears to stop before changing direction</note>, either at or near the first station—specifically within degrees or less—it signifies slowness and laziness in that pilgrimage or journeying. And if it is **retrograde** <term>retrograde: the appearance of a planet moving backward in the sky, usually indicating delays or reversals</term> or stationary in its first station and is received, it signifies that he will travel but will return shortly. If, however, it is so without reception, it signifies that he will not complete his journey; rather, he will suffer loss in it, and anger or distress. 

Next, look at the Lord of the house of travel and see if the Lord of the house in which it sits is retrograde and looks upon its Lord from a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>Trine (120°) and sextile (60°) are harmonious alignments</note>; for this will signify that he is going for the purpose of ordering and disposing of his business and that of his subjects. If, however, it looks upon them from a **square** aspect <term>square: a 90° angle, indicating friction or conflict</term> or from opposition, it signifies that he is going for the purpose of fighting with his rebels and enemies. 

Then look at the significator of the king: if it is free from impediments and is also free from any of the planets that are naturally hostile to it, and that the Lord of the house of travel or pilgrimage is not in the house of illness <term>the sixth house</term> or the house of death <term>the eighth house</term>; for this signifies the protection and safety of his person on that pilgrimage or journey, just as his significator is safe and free from hindrances. And even if the king’s significator is found free from these things, if the Lord of the house of travel or pilgrimage is hindered, it signifies hindrance and sadness according to the meanings of the house in which it sits, whether the house of illness, the house of death, or any of the others. And if the Lord of the house of travel or

### ¶ Chapter Eleven: Why the king shall go on pilgrimage, if he is to go.
<note>The chapter numbering in the manuscript jumps from 14 to 11.</note>

To know the causes why he shall go on pilgrimage, if he must travel, you shall look at the Lord of the house of pilgrimage or travel and see in which house it is located; for some meaning of that house will be the cause of the journey or pilgrimage. 

For if it is in the **first house** <term>the first house: represents the physical body and the self</term>, either the planet itself or the significator of the king joined to the Lord of the first, the cause will be the safety of his person; and it seems rather that he will not travel but will be in tranquility and rest. But if there is another planet between it and the degree of the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>, whether it be lighter or heavier, see what its nature is. For if it is among those hostile to the king's significator, someone will come upon him seeking to deprive him of his kingdom or his dignity, and will strive with him to take his kingdom or dignity away. 

If, however, it is among his own associates, the person who comes will be such that the king or ruler will voluntarily hand over the kingdom or dignity to him and prefer him over himself. See also which house that planet rules; for from that place shall be chosen the one who is to come to do this. For example, if it is the Lord of the second house, he will be among those signified by the second house. If it is the Lord of the third, he will be among those signified by the third house. And understand the same for the meanings of the other houses; perhaps he will even build in the land to which he has gone. 

If the Lord of the ninth is in the second house or joined to its Lord, it signifies that he will go for the sake of gain—that is, to acquire money. If, however, it is in the third—which is the house of his enemies <note>The third house is the seventh house (enemies) relative to the ninth house</note>—it signifies that his departure will be for the sake of warring or making war; he will desire to travel and ride out, and he will multiply his journeys, even if he does not desire it with great longing if he is a traveler. 

And if it is in the fourth house or joined to its Lord, it signifies that his journey will be horrible and fearful if he has traveled. And because it is in the eighth house from its own house <note>The fourth house is the eighth house (death) when counting from the ninth house</note>, death is feared for him. And if any of the **malefics** <term>malefic planets: usually Saturn or Mars</term> then look upon it from a square aspect or opposition, or is bodily joined to it, or if a man transfers his disposition to it, he will hardly or never escape those dangers; yet he will not desire to go out or travel much, but rather desire to be in rest and tranquility. 

And if it is in the fifth or joined to the Lord of the fifth, his state is signified as praiseworthy; he will be in joy, dance, and delight. He will desire to have a son and will have one according to the gender of the sign in which **Mars** is, alongside the significators which are the Lord of the first, the Lord of the fifth, the **Moon**, the Lord of the house in which she sits, and **Jupiter**. It also signifies that he will build in the land to which he has set out and will intend to stay there a long time, yet he will rarely or never actually remain there. 

If it is in the sixth or joined to its Lord—that is, if it transfers its disposition—it signifies that he will be sick in that revolution. If it is in the seventh or joined to its Lord, it signifies some strength for his enemies who are hostile to him, not for the sake of the kingdom or dignity but for any other cause; he will also be intent on "venereal worship" <note>Lust or sexual pursuits</note> more than is proper. 

If it is in the eighth or joined to its Lord from any aspect without reception, death is feared for him in that revolution. And if the Lord of the eighth receives him, but he does not receive the Lord of the eighth, he will fear it even more. And if he receives the Lord of the eighth, but the Lord of the eighth does not receive him, he will fear it yet more, so that it will hardly or never happen but that he dies.

### Concerning the mutual reception of the planets.

**A**fter this, you should know which of the planets "receive" each other <note>original: "recepciant se inuicẽ"</note> and to which places of the figure they cast their rays; for in the regions subject to the signs to which the rays are cast, the meanings of those planets will have more efficacy and will leave more of an impression upon them than in other places.

### Which planets are friends to the lord of the Ascendant in the revolution.

**Y**ou should also know which planets are friends to the lord of the rising sign of the revolution, or which are enemies, and which of them he regards more or to which he commits his disposition. And see whether he regards the Ascendant with a praiseworthy aspect or one of enmity; for according to how they regard him or the Ascendant—whether good or evil—judgment will be made concerning their meanings to come in that revolution. The Master whom God willed said: know that both malefics, namely Saturn and Mars, when one of them is in an "angle" <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the strongest points in a chart</term> in the revolution of the year and is in earthly signs and is "direct" <term>direct: moving forward through the zodiac, rather than backward/retrograde</term>, it signifies the destruction of trees and the death of animals. And if Mars regards the significator of the king and is himself mixed with the light of Saturn, contentions and the shedding of blood will occur. And Masha'allah <note>original: "meffahala"; an 8th-century Jewish-Persian astrologer and astronomer</note> said if it is in a fiery sign, it signifies injuries and enmities. If indeed it is in an angle and regards the Ascendant, it signifies infirmities and blood and more serious things; and this in every land in which its light or opposition or square aspect falls. And he said that if it is "retrograde," <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward, usually seen as a negative or erratic omen</term> it signifies pestilence. And if it is in a sign that regards the Ascendant and is direct, it signifies infirmity and harm to crops. If it is retrograde, it will signify death, infirmity, and blood.

### Chapter Seventeen: Concerning those things which ought to happen to the king in the revolution of the year.

**B**y this you shall see if the king will travel in that year. Look at what the state of the lord of the house of pilgrimage is: namely, whether he is direct or free, or hindered; and whether he is in his own house or in another's; and if he was going from the sign in which he is toward one of his own houses and was joined to the lord of the house or the "exaltation" <term>exaltation: a sign where a planet's influence is especially harmonious and powerful</term> in which he was located. And see at what hour he is to enter his own house or at what hour he is to come to the place where the lord of the house or exaltation was when he was joined.

Look if the lord is retrograde <term>retrograde: an optical illusion where a planet appears to move backward in the sky; usually considered a weakening influence</term>; for if it is so, and if it has been "received," <note>original: "receptus"; mutual reception occurs when two planets are in each other's signs of power, allowing them to cooperate</note> it signifies that he will linger on his journey or his pilgrimage, but will return quickly relative to the length of the trip. But if it is retrograde and not received, it signifies that his journey will be difficult and tedious, and that obstacles will befall him during that journey or pilgrimage. 

If, however, it is slower in its course—specifically in its first "slowness" <note>original: "tarditate prima"; referring to the first station where a planet slows down before turning retrograde</note>—it signifies a long delay in that journey or pilgrimage, and that for various reasons he will be detained in the regions to which he has gone; there will even be fear for him during that pilgrimage. And Albumasar <note>Albumasar (787–886 AD) was a highly influential Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology</note> said: if it is in its second "slowness" <note>the second station where a planet slows before returning to direct motion</note>, he will return once the planet has become direct, and his pilgrimage will not be completed. 

If it is retrograde and the lord of its own house looks upon it from a square aspect <note>90 degrees</note> or from an opposition <note>180 degrees</note>, it signifies that his departure is for war against an enemy openly opposing him, and it appears he must be outside his own region. If, however, [the lord] looks upon it from a trine <note>120 degrees</note> or sextile <note>60 degrees</note> aspect, it appears he will go out against some of his own subjects who are becoming, or have already become, rebels. But if their bodies are joined <term>conjunction: when two planets occupy the same degree of the zodiac</term>, it appears he will reach the place of his intention. 

When you have examined this, look at the "significator of the region." If you find it free from the hindrance of the malefics <term>malefics: planets like Saturn and Mars that were thought to cause hardship</term>, and it is not joined to any planets that are naturally its enemies; and if the lord of the pilgrimage is free in an excellent place relative to the ascendant <note>the rising sign</note>, and is not in a place of enmity to the ascendant, nor found in the 6th or 8th houses <note>traditionally the houses of illness and death</note>, it signifies the safety and salvation of his body. 

If, however, his significator is free from the aforementioned hindrance, but the lord of the sign in which the lord of the house of pilgrimage is found is hindered, it signifies that an obstacle and his destruction will occur during the pilgrimage. Perhaps some infirmity will happen to him which is not of his own natural constitution, the nature of which should be judged according to the "substance" of the sign in which the lord of the house of pilgrimage is located. If the significator is hindered but the lord of the house of pilgrimage is free, he will suffer from the same sickness that usually afflicts him. 

You shall also see whether the significator of the region is aspected by any of the planets, and whether the one looking at it is a "fortune" <term>benefics: helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</term> or a "malefic." For if it is a malefic, it signifies enmity that will occur to the king in that year or revolution. You must then see if that malefic has any "dignity" <term>dignity: essential strength or rulership over a specific part of the zodiac</term> in the sign from which it aspects the king's significator; for if it has some dignity there, that enemy will be from the king's own land, according to the person signified by that dignity. For if it is the lord of the house, the enemy will be among the greater inhabitants of his land or his own domestics. 

If it is the exaltation <note>a high dignity</note>, the enemy will be from the more noble people of his kingdom, or from those who came from elsewhere and were appointed to certain positions of dignity in that kingdom, or perhaps those who acquired fortune and great riches there through the signified aspect, but who do not have hereditary power—those, that is, who are fit for the kingdom and royal dignities; they will be all the more noble if the aspect is the "second square." A bodily conjunction, however, signifies kinship through the women's side. If [the malefic] has no dignity there, the enemy will be from the king's own blood relations. If it is the triplicity <note>ruling a group of three signs</note> or the "term" <note>a specific small segment of a sign</note>, the enemy will be among the great citizens subject to the king. If the aspect is the "first square," it signifies the person is a son born of an illegitimate union. But if the aspect is from opposition, it will be an enemy openly opposing the king. If the aspect is sextile or trine, it signifies he is a relative or from the king's close kin.

## Chapter 18. On the joining of the two malefics, namely Saturn and Mars, with any planet in the degree of its exaltation, and what is signified thereby.

Albumasar said: look in the revolution of the year for the junction of the malefics, namely Saturn and Mars, to see whether they join with any planet that is in the degree of its exaltation <note>the specific degree where a planet is most powerful</note> by aspect—and it is worse if by square or opposition. For if it is Saturn, it signifies evil and destruction in the region assigned to that planet. 

If Saturn's aspect is from a "fixed sign" <note>signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability</note>, it will prolong that significance according to the number of degrees between their bodies into years, months, weeks, or days. For if the significance is something that should be completed within the year of the revolution, the number of degrees signifies months. If it exceeds that year, it will be extended to years. If it is from a "moveable sign" <note>signs like Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, which represent change</note>, it signifies days according to the number of degrees. And if it is not completed in that many days, it signifies weeks. If it is from a "common sign" <note>signs like Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, it will be weeks. And if it is not completed in that many weeks, it signifies months. 

But if Saturn does not aspect it directly, but some other planet "transfers the light" <note>original: "transtulerit... lumen"; when a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, carrying the influence between them</note> between them, it signifies the king's displeasure toward the people of that planet's region, or destruction and loss will come upon them from nations that are not from that region. If no planet transfers the light between them, but the rays of Saturn touch the rays of the planet in its exaltation, or the planet that is fit to transfer the light between them, sadness and grief will enter upon the people of that region which they ought not to fear; for the fear will be dissolved and will not result in action, by the will of God.

->Of the aspect of Mars to a planet in its exaltation.<-

If it is an aspect of Mars, just as I said regarding the aspect of Saturn—and worse if it is square or opposition—the aforementioned things will happen just as I said for Saturn, in a similar way and for similar reasons. It is even more severe, because Mars will fulfill the events he signifies through iron [weapons], fire, and the shedding of blood. 

You shall also look at the lord of the ninth house; if you find it in the third house, it signifies the king travels for the sake of religion, and the cause of his pilgrimage will be for his life and the world to come before the Creator, because this place [the 3rd house] signifies the same as the ninth in this regard, even though it is its "nadir" <note>the point directly opposite</note>. And Albumasar said: if you look into any house among these 12 houses, do not omit its aspect from other places; the significators of the opposites will be stronger, so that its significance is the same as the significance of the "nadir" sign of a planet, or its house or exaltation, because it then signifies what he said.

## Chapter 19. When the Sun and Moon join with any of the planets or separate from them, what they signify.

You shall consider the Sun and Moon and see how they are disposed: namely, whether they are joining <term>application: when a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</term> with any of the planets or separating from any of them; for the significations will be according to how you see either of them with the planets or separating from them, both by body [conjunction] and by aspect. And Albumasar said that the square aspect is strong, the sextile is weak, and the conjunction is heavy.

### Also concerning the king's accidents.

Also, look so that you may know what kind of accidents are to come to the king in the revolution you are seeking: whether the Moon is found in the seventh house or not. ### Also concerning the good or bad state of the king.

You should also look in the revolution of the year <note>the "revolution of the year" refers to a horoscope cast for the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to predict the year's events</note> at the state of the king through the Midheaven <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the sky at the moment of the chart, representing authority, status, and the king himself</term>, to see what is to come in that revolution. You can weigh this by the state of Saturn and the "Lord of the Year," and also through certain other planets as I shall explain to you. When the Lord of the 10th house is the "significator" <term>significator: the specific planet acting as the representative for a person or topic in a horoscope</term> of the king in the revolution of the year and is joined to Saturn—especially if it is "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun in the morning</note>—or if the significator of the king is joined to the Lord of the Year and commits its "disposition" <note>original: "dispositionem"; this refers to one planet handing over its influence or "power of management" to another</note> to him, and the Lord of the Year is joined to a planet located in the 8th house from the Ascendant of the revolution (which is the house signifying death in general), or to a planet in the 8th from the Ascendant by opposition <note>an aspect of 180 degrees</note> or a "quartile" aspect <note>a square aspect of 90 degrees</note>, it signifies the death of the king in that year or that revolution. 

Or, if the significator of the king is joined to that same Lord of the Year, and the Lord of the Year is joined to the Lord of the 8th or the 5th in any of the other houses—whether bodily <note>occupying the same degree</note> or by opposition or quartile aspect—it signifies his death. And it is more certain if the Lord of the house in which that conjunction occurs is a "malefic" <term>malefic: a planet traditionally associated with hardship, usually Saturn or Mars</term>. Similarly, if the significator of the king is in "combustion" <term>combustion: when a planet is so close to the Sun (within 8.5 degrees) that its power is said to be "burned up" or hidden</term>, it signifies the death of the king; and a man can hardly ever avoid this. 

If, however, Saturn is oriental, emerging from under the rays of the Sun, it will not hinder the king but will improve his state. If this conjunction is with a planet in the 3rd or 6th house, or elsewhere with the Lord of the 3rd or 6th, it signifies an infirmity coming to him in that revolution. And according to the meanings of the house in which the conjunction occurs and their circumstances, all things that are to come to him will happen. 

But if the significator of the king does not commit its disposition to the Lord of the Year or the revolution, danger does not loom, though fear does. This is to be understood for any king or kingdom according to its own climate and region. But if it is already passing through combustion by as many degrees as there are in its "orb" <note>the range of influence surrounding a planet</note>—that is, until it touches the 10th minute of the last degree of its combustion—it signifies that anger, sadness, and contention, as well as fear, will come to the king in that revolution. This is even stronger if a malefic aspects him; for if a malefic aspects him, it will cast doubt upon the king, and there will be fear for him and over him according to the substance and meaning of the house and sign in which the malefic is located. 

For example, if it is in the 2nd, it will be because of wealth <note>substance</note>. If it is in the 3rd, it will be because of brothers or travel. If it is in the 4th, it will be because of fathers or inheritances. If it is in the 5th, it will be because of children. If it is in the 6th, it will be because of illness. If it is in the 7th, it will be because of a wife. If it is in the 8th, it will be because of death. If it is in the 9th, it will be because of long journeys. If it is in the 10th, it will be because of the kingdom. If it is in the 11th, it will be because of helpers. If it is in the 12th, it will be because of hidden enemies. 

If, however, a "fortune" <term>fortune: a benefic or "lucky" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</term> aspects him, it will resolve all these things and turn them away from him. And so that you may know when these things ought to happen, see when the significator of the king joins with that malefic; for that will be the time of their arrival. Whether the significator joins it bodily, or by opposition, or by a quartile aspect, judge by whichever malefic hindrance arrives first. Or, when that hindering malefic comes to the 10th house of the revolution’s Ascendant, or at least to its Ascendant, unless a fortune then aspects the significator

### Chapter 20. Concerning the state of the king with his subjects.

You can know the state of the king with his subjects, and the state of the subjects with him, through the conjunction of their significators to one another, or through their aspect with "reception"; for among those significators, the one who receives the other commits his disposition to him. Thus, if the significator of the king commits his disposition to the significator of his subjects, the king will be benevolent and pleasant toward his peasants—more so than they are toward him. If the significator of the common people <note>original: "vulgi"</note> commits its disposition to the significator of the king, they will be obedient and more benevolent toward their king than he is toward them. If, however, each significator receives the other, the king will commit his disposition to his subjects and they to him; each will want what the other wants, and each will be pleasing to the other.

### Chapter 21. Concerning the king’s own and special state.

You can know the king's own and special state, according to the daily accidents that ought to happen to him in that revolution, through his significator: namely, by what you see of its daily disposition toward good or otherwise. For according to that, things will happen to him from day to day until the end of that revolution, just as it joins with fortunes or misfortunes, or as they reach the places where the malefics were at the hour of the revolution, or other places that were then hindered; for according to that, good or evil things, or liberation from them, will come to him.

### Chapter 22. What the significator of the king signifies in an angle of the house.

Albumasar says: when the significator of the king is in the angle of the Midheaven, it signifies the king's war. When it is in the Ascendant, it will "cut off" the state of men. If it is in the West <note>the 7th house</note> or in the "angle of the earth" <note>the 4th house, or IC, the lowest point of the chart</note>, his peasants will be destroyed. And he said: if the Lord of the Year or the significator of the king moves toward a malefic planet, or toward the light of a slow and malefic planet in an angle, fear for him whose significator it is—either destruction or death.

### Chapter 23. When the significator of the king or any other planet escapes from a hindrance and goes to its exaltation.

When the significator of the king has stood hindered before its "exaltation" <term>exaltation: a specific sign of the zodiac where a planet is thought to be exceptionally strong or "honored"</term> and has now escaped from that hindrance and is then joined to any fortune—and even better if that fortune receives it—and when it is separated from that fortune before it reaches the degree in which it is immediately exalted, and it is not then hindered by any malefic, it will then be in the greatest strength and the strongest testimony that can be. 

Look then where the "Part of Kingdom" <term>Part of Kingdom: a specific mathematical point in a horoscope used to predict the fate of a realm</term> falls; for if it falls in the place where the significator had been hindered, it signifies delays and hindrances coming to the king in his kingdom during that revolution. But if it falls in the place of its exaltation toward which it is then going, it signifies the increase and goodness of his kingdom without end and without any hindrance. 

As for those wishing to resist him, look at the opposite places; however, do not count the king's natural enemies among them, for if they are hindered, they will be obstructed and things will go badly for them. If they are not hindered, they will not be weakened at all in the things they wish to do against the king. And if the significator of the king is the significator of any of those significators and is the "Almuten" <term>Almuten: the planet with the most combined dignity and power over a specific point or house in the chart</term> over them, or if the Part of Kingdom falls upon him, and the Sun commits its disposition to the significator of the king, the king will rule in that revolution over all those things that are signified...

### Chapter 24. To know when a revolution lasts for the whole year, for half a year, and for a quarter of the year.

I have named all the parts of the revolution to you many times when I mentioned the Lord of the Year, so that it would not be in vain; for every Lord of the Year is called the Lord of the Revolution, but the reverse is not always true. For there is a Lord of the Year when, in any given year, only one revolution is required; and that is when a "fixed sign" <term>fixed sign: the signs of Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability</term> is ascending at the entry of the Sun into Aries. That revolution contains within itself all the quarters of that year; and thus, whoever is then the Lord of the Year will be the Lord of the whole year and of its entire revolution. 

But if a "common sign" <term>common sign: also known as mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which represent transition</term> is ascending, that revolution will not last except for half of that year—that is, until the entry of the Sun into Libra. Then it will be necessary for you to repeat the revolution, and whoever presides then will be the Lord of the Revolution until the end of the second half of the year. 

If indeed a "movable sign" <term>movable sign: also known as cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which represent change and new beginnings</term> is ascending, that revolution will not last except until the entry of the Sun into Cancer; then it will be necessary for you to calculate for all the quarters of the year. The lord of the first quarter will be the one who has dominion at the entry of the Sun into Aries. And he who presides over the dominion at its entry into Cancer will be the Lord of the Revolution for the second quarter. And he who presides at the entry of the Sun into Libra will be the lord of the third quarter. And he who presides at its entry into Capricorn will be the lord of the final quarter. Always in each of the aforesaid entries, you shall renew your judgment just as you did at the entry of the Sun into Aries. Always make the prince of the first revolution work with the lord of the second, and the lord of the second with the lord of the third, and the lord of the third with the lord of the fourth until you complete them all; for every prior lord will have a fourth part over the next. And thus, he who is Lord of the whole year will be the Lord of the Revolution; he who is lord of the half-year will be the Lord of the Revolution; and he who is lord of the quarter will be the Lord of the Revolution. However, it is not so for the Lord of the Year, for he is specifically called the "Lord of the Year" <note>original: "dominus anni"</note>.

### What the Lord of the Hour and the "Part of Fortune" signify in the revolution.

After you have set up all the aforesaid things in the order described, and have looked at everything that must be observed as I told you, you shall then consider the Lord of the Hour and the "Part of Fortune" <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</term>, and the Lord of the House in which it falls. If they are well-disposed, they will aid the Lord of the Year and the king's significator; if you find them well-disposed, they will increase their good fortune. If, however, you find them "hindered" <note>original: "impediti"; a planet is hindered if it is in a weak position or under a harsh influence from a planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, they will diminish their obstacles. But if they were hindered and you find them hindered, they will increase their <insert>bad</insert> fortune. If you find them well-disposed, you shall decrease from their goodness. 

And Albumasar <note>Albumasar refers to Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer whose works were fundamental to Western medieval astrology</note> said: know the conjunction of the planets with the Lord of the Year and with the king's significator, and their conjunction with the planets, and the separation and the coming together of them with each other in the houses and aspects. Understand their works through the "falls" of others, and mix with these the substances of the signs and whichever overcomes by "reception" <term>reception: when a planet is in a sign ruled by another planet, allowing them to cooperate</term> from its nature; know your significators, and know their "fall" from one another through diversity and allegation, and with reception and returning.

### Chapter 25. Concerning the knowledge of "accidents" that are to come in the climates at the hour of the revolution.

The "climates" <term>climates: the seven latitudinal zones of the known world in ancient geography, each believed to be ruled by a different planet</term> are divided by the planets as has been said elsewhere. Therefore, you must consider in the re-

<column-break/>

-volution of the year which climate each planet presides over and know its state. If you wish to know the "accidents" <note>original: "accidentia"; here meaning events or occurrences</note> that are to come in the climate over which a planet presides: for the final accidents of the climate will be according to the state of the planet that presides over it. The Lord of the Year, the lord of the ascending sign of the revolution, and the Lord of the Hour will participate with it. Therefore, each of them will provide help or harm to the lord of the climate according to its state, whether in good or in evil. 

But always keep in your memory what I told you above in the chapter on what the Lord of the Year signifies in the places where it falls, and how far the significance of each significator extends. You shall consider the "ascendant" <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> of the revolution according to the different "ascensions" <note>The time it takes for a sign to rise varies depending on the latitude of the region</note> of any given region. And if it should happen that one planet has significance over two climates, or rules one and participates in another, always place its significance over every region which it presides over; and thus you will be able to know the accidents that are to come in those regions, both final and particular, both for the king and for the common people. 

For if the significance for both the king and the region—whose year’s revolution is stronger—is in the 10th house, and some planet is in its own house and is otherwise "safe and free" <note>meaning free from negative astrological influences</note>, it signifies that the king will preside over all the Great Men of that region and will rule over them. And if there is no king in that region, these things will happen to whoever is the greatest within it. Do not err in your consideration of the significators of kings, for you must consider them according to regions and according to the climates over which their significations extend.

### Chapter 26. What the Lord of the Year and the king's significator signify when they are well-disposed in that revolution.

Look in the revolution of the year at the Lord of the Year and the king's significator, how they are disposed and what their state is. If you find them well-disposed and in a good state, free from hindrances, and in a place of friendship with the ascendant and the 10th house, and if they are in aspects with planets that are "received" by them—especially the Sun if the revolution is by day, or the Moon if it is by night—or if one of the "luminaries" <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term> is one of the aforesaid significators of the king (namely of the year), and the luminaries (or one of them) look upon the ascendant or its lord; if that luminary is free and in a good place from the ascendant, it signifies that those who dwell in that climate or region (as far as the significance of the Lord of the Year extends) will be in a good state. It signifies that prosperity, good, attainment, and strength will happen to them. 

And Albumasar said: it is even better if the luminary that holds authority commits its disposition to the lord of the ascendant. Then the nobles, the Great Men, and the wealthy—both those suited for the kingdom and others—shall be subject to the king of that climate or region. The citizens or inhabitants of that region will be in "tranquility and peace" <note>original: "tranquillitate atq; quiete"</note> and will grant them good. 

And if any of the planets should commit their disposition to the Lord of the Year through a conjunction or some good aspect, and he receives them, joy and gladness will likewise happen to them from all sides, according to the natures of the signs in which the planets are, and in whose houses the luminaries are—especially if they look upon them (or at least one of them) from a strong and good place. For it signifies then that in that climate or region there will be security, peace, and health in all things, both in property and in persons. They will turn their wills away from doing evil and will strive to do good and to preserve justice and faith without detriment or diminution.

### Also concerning the disposition of the Lord of the Year according to the place in which he resides in the revolution of the year.

Look also in the revolution of the year at the significator and the place in which he resides. If he is in a good state, and similarly the sign in which he is located is well-disposed, and if he himself is "fortunate" <note>positioned near "benefic" planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> and strong in the "term" <term>term: a specific sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</term> of a fortune and received by any of the fortunes, that reception signifies...

The same applies to the lord of the region associated with the zodiac sign where the "Lord of the Year" <term>Lord of the Year: the planet that rules the rising sign at the moment the Sun enters the sign of Aries</term> is found, as well as all its inhabitants; prosperity and good fortune will come to them.

When you find the lord <note>the ruling planet</note> of a city to be free of negative influences and well-aspected by "fortunes" <term>fortunes: benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus that bring good luck</term>, and you know which zodiac sign governs that city or region, you should predict joy, gladness, and success for its people and affairs. Therefore, consider which sign and which planet rule that city or region; however, if you find the opposite <note>meaning the planet is afflicted or in a bad position</note>, you must judge that the outcome will be negative.

### Chapter 27. What the Lord of the Year and other planets signify when they are "impeded" in a revolution.

Just as you examined the Lord of the Year, you must also consider him and the other planets when their meanings are contrary to these. In the "revolution" <term>revolution: the casting of an astrological chart for the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to predict the year's events</term>, observe the strength and power of the Lord of the Year and the other planets, for their effects depend on their positions at the exact moment of the revolution. For if the Lord is "impeded" <term>impeded: a planet's power is weakened or blocked by a bad position or a harsh aspect from a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</term> and is located in the "Ascendant" <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon, representing the physical body and general well-being</term>, the people themselves will suffer in their persons. 

If he is elsewhere outside the Ascendant, the harm will affect the "substance" <note>wealth and possessions</note> associated with that sign and the "houses" <term>houses: twelve divisions of the sky representing different areas of life, such as wealth, health, or career</term> in which he is impeded. For example, if he is in the second house, he will hinder wealth, and you should judge the other houses similarly according to their specific meanings. If a planet other than the Lord of the Year is impeded, it will negatively affect the significance of the sign and the house it rules. For instance, if Aries is the Ascendant, an impeded planet will first affect Taurus and then Libra; if Taurus is the Ascendant, it will first affect Gemini and then Virgo, and so on. 

The condition of the inhabitants of that region will decline; they will feel oppressed, cast down, and stripped of their status. This is even more severe if the Lord of the Year is in one of the "angles" <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</term>, particularly the fourth house, and is pressured by Mars or Saturn, especially if he is in the "terms" <term>term: a small subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet</term> of the "malefics" <term>malefics: planets that traditionally cause difficulty, specifically Saturn and Mars</term>. It is even worse if he is at the end of a sign, unless that end belongs to the "term" of the malefic planet that is pressuring him, which slightly lessens the harm. 

The misfortune is even stronger if the planet is "besieged" <term>besieged: positioned between two malefic planets</term> by two malefics, for then the evil and the blockage of those citizens are doubled. This is especially true if the "obsession" <note>the state of being caught between planets</note> happens by "bodily conjunction" <note>planets occupying the same degree of the zodiac</note>, which strips away profits and brings loss. If it happens by "opposition" <note>planets 180 degrees apart</note>, the damage is a quarter less. If it happens by "square aspect" <note>planets 90 degrees apart</note>, it is a third less. The famous astrologer Albumasar says that if Saturn blocks from the front and Mars from behind, the citizens will be taken captive, though few will be killed. But if Mars is in front and Saturn behind, many of those captives will be killed. If the "significator" <term>significator: the specific planet acting as the representative for a person or topic</term> is "combust" <term>combust: so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up" or hidden</term>, it signifies the destruction of property and people in that region and their exile due to intolerable suffering.

->Also concerning the same:<-

Know also that in the year's revolution, you must see which sign and planet rule over a city. If the sign is poorly placed and the planet is impeded, it signifies loss and the destruction of the city's property and people. Albumasar says to assign for every planet a plane-

### Chapter 28. On the knowledge of the significations of planets in the year's revolution, regarding the king's significator and others.

When the Sun is in the tenth house (representing authority) during the revolution—not more than 4 degrees before the "cusp" <note>the boundary of the house</note> and not more than 10 degrees after—and the "lord of the term" of the tenth house's degree is in that term or aspects his term from a good house, these two signify the kings and their affairs. If the Sun is then free from the "malefics" and the lord of the tenth house's term is in a strong position, the kings and nobles will be safe and their wealth protected. (This is especially true if they are in an "angle," though the fourth house is excluded here). 

However, if the Sun and the lord of the tenth house's term are hindered by the presence or "aspect" <note>the geometric angles planets make with each other</note> of malefics—especially if this pressure comes from the angles of the chart—the kings and nobles will suffer and their condition will worsen. If the eleventh house (governing allies) and its lord are safe and free from malefics, the soldiers and the king's helpers will be protected. But if they are impeded, they will suffer loss. Albumasar says that Mercury represents scribes, merchants, astronomers, teachers, and scholars; if Mercury is well-placed, they will prosper. Jupiter represents counselors and leaders; if he is safe, they will be protected. Similarly, Venus represents women.

### Chapter 29. On the state of the king, his wealth, and the state of his soldiers or helpers.

Observe whether the king's significator forms a "friendly aspect" <note>angles of 60 or 120 degrees</note> with the "Part of Fortune" <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</term>. If it does, or if it is physically joined to it, the king will be fortunate, especially if his significator is also the Lord of the tenth house. Then, examine the eleventh house and its lord to judge the condition of his soldiers and his treasury; if you find them well-disposed, say that the state of the soldiers and the king's wealth is good and lucky.

->If the Lord of the Year is the king's significator.<-

When the Lord of the Year acts as the king's significator, look to the second house and its lord to determine his wealth, just as you would for common people. Albumasar advises looking at the "lords of triplicity" <term>lords of triplicity: three planets that rule a set of zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> for the sign where the king's significator is located. If all are well-placed, judge that the whole year will be good. If they are poorly placed, judge the opposite. If one is good and another bad, judge according to the parts of the year: the first lord rules the first third of the revolution, the second rules the middle, and the third rules the end. Always include the "lord of the term" <term>term: a small subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet</term> in your judgment.

->Concerning the common people and their wealth.<-

Similarly, judge the state of the common people through the Lord of the Year, and their wealth through the second house and its lord. Also, look to the "Part of Fortune"; if it is well-disposed, it signifies good; if poorly, it signifies loss.

### Also concerning the king's significator when Mars or Saturn is his significator.

When Mars or Saturn is the king's significator, but is not the lord of the Ascendant, nor of the tenth house, nor of any "exaltation" <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet's influence is exceptionally strong</term>, and it hinders any of these through its presence, opposition, or square aspect...

### ¶ When a "fortune" is in charge.

If the king’s significator <term>significator: the planet that represents a specific person or topic in a chart</term> is a "fortune" <term>fortune: a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus that brings good luck</term> and is located as I told you regarding the malefic ones, it signifies goodness, joy, and the cheerfulness of the citizens or inhabitants of the predicted parts according to its placement in any of them, unless it is impeded by retrogradation <term>retrogradation: when a planet appears to move backward, usually weakening its effect</term>, its "fall" <term>fall: a sign where a planet's influence is significantly weakened</term>, or its detriment <note>original: "difcensione"</note>; for if it is so, it will signify nothing good. And Albumasar <note>a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer and astronomer</note> said that if there is a bad aspect <term>aspect: the geometric angle between planets that determines their relationship</term> to the lord of the ascendant or the significator of "substance" <note>wealth and possessions</note>, there will be heaviness in the body; and from the second house in substance; from the third in brothers; from the fourth from the parents and bad relatives; from the fifth from journeys; and from the sixth from those things which come from his hand <note>subordinates or servants</note>; and from the sixth <note>likely referring to the health aspect of the house</note> from infirmity; from the seventh from women and war; from the eighth from the remains of the dead and apprehension. And if the eighth sign is "movable" or "common" <term>movable/common: types of zodiac signs—Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn (movable) or Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces (common)—that indicate changeability</term>, one shall fear for the king’s death if the king’s significator is one which bad lords <note>malefics</note> look upon. And if this aspect is from the eighth to the significator of the peasants, one shall fear for the peasants. And if there is one significator for both the king and the peasants, one shall fear for everyone, for death will overtake them. And if it is from the ninth, it concerns pilgrimages and religious men who seek justice. And if it is from the tenth, it concerns the king and his dominion. And if it is from the eleventh, it concerns friends. And from the twelfth, it concerns enemies. And he said likewise regarding good things when there is an aspect from a strong "fortune" even if the malefic planet has fallen. And he said to speak similarly in the "revolution of the years of births" <note>natal or birthday charts</note>.

### ¶ Chapter Thirty regarding the impediments of the "evils" <note>malefic planets</note> and their aspects, what they signify, and how the impediments and those causing them are recognized.

Look at the significators in the king's revolution, both of the common people and the peasants, and see whether they are aspected by the "evils" <note>malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> or not. If indeed the "evils" aspect them by opposition <term>opposition: an aspect where planets are 180 degrees apart, indicating direct conflict</term>, and those "evils" are themselves impeded, it signifies because of the enmity of the aspect that an impediment will come to the king and the peasants from the direction of enemies. And Albumasar said if it is a "fourth aspect" <term>fourth aspect: a square or 90-degree angle, representing challenges</term>, there will be an impediment from men who were unknown enemies. And he said that this aspect is "middle" <note>moderate</note> and does not make the enmity public. And if they aspect them from a "sextile aspect" <term>sextile: a 60-degree angle, usually a harmonious but weak aspect</term>, the impediment will come from certain people who are thought to be friends, yet it is not well-certain whether they are friends or not. But if they aspect them from a "trine aspect" <term>trine: a 120-degree angle, the most favorable and harmonious aspect</term>, the impediment will be from the direction of friends. And Albumasar said that if there is a bad aspect of such a figure from its locations, this is as was said regarding the significator of the peasants. And if it is to the significator of the king, it will fall upon the king. And he said one must look to see whether the peasants help the king, or the king helps the peasants. And this is known through the "complexion" <note>the specific combination of planetary influences</note> that exists between both significators and the "evils" impeding or aspecting them, and this is according to what their aspect is—whether it be trine, sextile, square, or opposition—and from which places, houses, or dignities <term>dignities: specific signs or degrees where a planet is said to have more power, like its 'throne'</term>. If a bad planet is impeding the significator of the king or the commoners and peasants in its own house,

the one from whom the impediment comes will be from that climate or region—namely, that which is signified by those testimonies. If it is in their house but not in the region, he will be from the king’s own household. And if it is in "exaltation" <term>exaltation: the sign where a planet's influence is most elevated or honored</term>, he will be noble and powerful among those who are fit for kingship. And if it is in "triplicity" <term>triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</term>, they will be from those who are not fit for kingship but are close to those in power. And if it is in the "term" <term>term: a small division of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet</term>, he will be from those mentioned above who are fit to be counts or marquises and the like. And if it is in the "face" <term>face: a ten-degree subdivision of a sign, the smallest of the primary dignities</term>, he will be of the nobler people. And if he is among the nobles who are below marquises, they are nevertheless magnanimous. If, however, he is not in any of the predicted dignities, he will not be high-born nor known in the region; and men will say that they do not know where he is from; and perhaps they will say he was born of an unknown father or from fornication, or that the "people" are his father <note>implying a commoner of obscure or illegitimate birth</note>. And Albumasar said that if the king's significator is in charge, the enemy will be from the same climate and the king will be too weak to prohibit or repel him. And he said if the peasants' significator is in charge, the enemy will not be from that climate or from his dominion. And he said the "Lord of the Year" <term>Lord of the Year: the planet ruling the rising sign at the start of the astrological year</term> is the significator of the year and the significator of the peasants. And he said the Moon is the significator of the peasants and the entirety of the common folk and is not "in charge"; for everyone who is "in charge" is a significator, but it does not work the other way around: for not every significator is "in charge."

### ¶ Chapter Thirty-One: what the retrogradation of the king’s significator, the Lord of the Year, or the peasants’ significator signifies.

If it should happen that the significator of the common folk is retrograde in the revolution of the year—though this happens very rarely—it could nevertheless happen as said elsewhere, and it would threaten a truly horrible evil. For the retrogradation of the king's significator signifies his weakness and his deposition; and it will be a great thing for him if he escapes being deposed from the kingdom, and if his kingdom escapes destruction in that year. Similarly, the retrogradation of the Lord of the Year will signify destruction and evil for the commoners and citizens of that region. You shall look at whose "term" each of them is in. For if it is retrograde in the term of some "misfortune" <term>misfortune: a malefic planet, usually Mars or Saturn</term>, and even more so if that term is in the house of some "evil" planet, this will be a far greater danger than if it were in the house or term of a "fortune." Likewise, if the lord of that term is himself impeded, for it will increase the malice again and multiply it. If, however, he is free, they will diminish the malice somewhat, though not much. If it is retrograde in the term of a "fortune," it will diminish that impediment, and even more so if it is also in the house of a "fortune"; and again even more if that "fortune" is well-disposed.

### ¶ Chapter Thirty-Two: what Mars and Saturn signify when they are poorly disposed in the revolution of the year.

When you calculate the revolution of the year, look to see if Mars is "stationary" <term>stationary: when a planet appears to stop in the sky before changing direction</term> in its first station, wanting to go retrograde, and joins with Saturn—whether Saturn is so disposed that he goes toward Mars while Mars stands still, or Mars goes toward him when he has turned retrograde. This signifies the severity and atrocity of men, such that there will be no one who wishes to stop his own evil if he can avoid doing so; piety will be cut off, nor will there be anyone who feels pity for another with good zeal; but evildoers, highwaymen, and robbers will abound; nor will a servant revere his master, nor even a religious man his superior. And it is even worse if Saturn is in Libra; and worse again if he is retrograde; and worse still if the Sun aspects him by opposition and Mars aspects the Sun and the Sun aspects him; and it will be even worse if Mars is "peregrine" <term>peregrine: a planet wandering in a sign where it has no special power or dignity, making it unpredictable or weak</term> while joining Saturn; and finally, it will be the ultimate evil above all others if the "revolution" occurs at sunset <note>original: "occasu solis"</note> or very near to it.
