### Chapter Thirty-Three: What follows when the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and other significators are impeded.

The Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of the year</term> and the Moon signify the affairs of the common people <note>original: "res vulgi"</note> in the revolution of the year. If they are impeded <term>impeded: weakened by a bad position or a "harsh" aspect from another planet</term> and are found in a place of enmity to the ascendant, they signify an impediment coming upon men in their persons and their affairs according to the degree of that enmity and the nature of the house in which they fall. For if they fall in the sixth house <note>the house of illness and service</note>, they signify infirmities and windy pains for men in 그 revolution. If they fall in the eighth house <note>the house of death</note>, they signify death, and this is more grave if the eighth house is a "human sign" <term>human sign: zodiac signs depicted as humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</term>. And if it falls in the twelfth house <note>the house of secret enemies and imprisonment</note>, it signifies enmities and betrayals according to the nature of the sign in which they are located. For example: if they are in Gemini, the cause will involve youths and adolescents. If they are in Virgo, the cause will be young women. If they are in Libra, the cause will be men of middle age. If they are in the first half of Sagittarius or in Aquarius, the cause will be adult males. If they are in Aries or Capricorn, the cause will be smaller animals <note>such as sheep or goats</note>. If they are in Taurus or in the latter half of Sagittarius, the cause will be larger animals and those that are ridden <note>such as horses or oxen</note>. And if it is in Leo, the cause will be wild, royal, and fierce beasts. And if they are in Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, the cause will be creatures that live in the water.

And if the Lord of the Exaltation <term>Exaltation: a specific sign where a planet's influence is most powerful</term> and the Moon are not impeded, and the ascending sign is the exaltation of some planet in the aforementioned places, it signifies the same as the Lord of the Ascendant. However, the significance of the Lord of the Ascendant and the significance or impediment of the Lord of the Term <term>Term: a small sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet</term> is below the significance of the Lord of the Exaltation. And the significance of the Lord of the Triplicity <term>Triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</term> will be below the significance of the Lord of the Term, provided any of them is impeded. And the impediment of the Lord of the Face <term>Face: also known as a Decan, a ten-degree segment of a sign</term> will be below the impediment of the Lord of the Triplicity. One must also observe how the predicted planets are aspected by the "fortunes" <term>fortunes: the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</term> or by the "infortunes" <term>infortunes: the malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</term>; for the fortunes diminish the evil (unless they themselves are impeded by combustion <term>combustion: being too close to the Sun, which weakens a planet</term> or retrogradation), while the evil ones increase it unless they are moving direct, well-disposed, and "receive" the impeded planets that are enemies to the ascendant. And Albumasar said that if the impediment comes from Mars, there will be choleric fever <note>fever caused by an excess of yellow bile</note> and sudden death. And if the impediment comes from Saturn, there will be fever from "black bile" <note>melancholy</note> and death.

### The chapters on wars are not placed here but are found in the *Book of Elections* <note>original: "libro de electionibus"</note>.

### Chapter Thirty-Four: When in the revolution of the year war is signified, by whom it will be made or provoked.

If you suspect whether there will be future battles or dissensions in the year you are revolving, and from where they are provoked and by whom, look into that matter according to the method handed down to us by the ancients, and especially by that most venerable predecessor of ours, Albumasar, who was useful, very astute, and bold in the revolutions of years and in all other parts of astronomy. You shall then cast a figure for the revolution of the year and establish the ascendant and the other houses and all the planets in the houses where they are found. Look at Mars and see from whom he is separating or from whom he was recently separated. And Albumasar said that the planet he separates from is the one who sends him and who provoked the war, even if that planet is a "fortune." Even if it is Jupiter, he will still be the provoker of war, but involving the persons signified by Jupiter—those of great power, and possibly of the rank of bishops and their sons. And if he is separated from Sa-

<column-break/>

-turn (since Saturn in such a case signifies kings), it appears that it is a king who has provoked the war, or it will be by the counsel of old or low-born men. And Albumasar said that there will be war when Mars commits his disposition to Saturn, and Saturn is joined with him and "receives" him <term>reception: an astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term>. And he said when Mars is separated from Jupiter and joined to Saturn without reception, know that he is the provoker of it, and he provokes it for the sake of justice because he is of the royal household. If, however, he is not separated from Jupiter and is joined to Saturn, the one who provokes the war will be of the low-born who are not fit for a kingdom nor great dignity. And when you see Mars separated from Saturn and joined to Jupiter, there will be no war; and if there is, it will not be among honorable men, nor Catholics, nor discreet men, nor bishops or their like. 

After you have seen the one from whom Mars separates (from whom it seems the war should be provoked) and the one to whom he is joined, and you see no reception, and their conjunction is in the same latitude, and it is a conjunction of Mars and Saturn: look at which of them is stronger in its own place. The one who "predominates" is stronger—that is, the one who "goes over" the other. One planet "goes over" another when it is more northern than the other, as was said above. And if Saturn is "over" the other, it signifies a weakness of the war. If, however, Mars is "over" Saturn, it signifies its strength. You may say the same if one of them receives the other. 

And Albumasar said that what you must first know in this chapter is what kind of strength the kingdom has and how great it is; then, you must know the duration of the kingdom's time. And when you know what concerns the kingdom and see its duration, look at the hour of destruction arising from the impediment of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, or from the one from whom Mars separates. And Albumasar said: know the destruction, and it comes from the destruction of these three planets, because they are the ones who provoke war. And if Mars is retrograde and the others are direct, a war will appear, but its appearance will not be finalized until Mars turns direct; then, indeed, its appearance will be finalized. And he said that if a war is provoked and Mars is "falling" <term>falling: located in a weak house, like the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th</term> from the ascendant of the year or is a "peregrine" <term>peregrine: a planet with no essential dignity or strength in its current sign</term>, the war will be weak. 

And Albumasar said: if you see the first "part" <term>part: a mathematical point in a chart, like the Arabic Parts</term> received by its own initial enemies, and it is opposite the first part or in its "fourth aspect" <note>a square aspect (90 degrees), usually signifying tension</note>, this will be the strength of the sword. If, however, the first part receives the second part, there will be no war. If indeed there is no reception and you see a war, and the first part is received, there will be no strength for those rising up; the stability of the people will remain with the first king, and their inclination will be toward him. And he said: look similarly at the second part; because "reception" is help, propitiation, and the strength of the one received. When, therefore, he does not receive, he will be a "peregrine," and there will be no trust in him, nor will there be strength.

### Chapter Eleven: Which of the planets signify wars in the revolution of the year and who is their disposer.

Albumasar said: Mars disposes wars and signifies the masters of armies and the heads of soldiers. If he is strong in an "angle" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, it signifies war; and if he is "falling" <note>in a weak house</note>, it does not. And he said the Moon is the "key" <note>original: "clauis"</note> to these things; if she is well-disposed, things will be well-disposed; if she is impeded, they will be impeded.

### Also on the same topic according to Albumasar.

In whatever "angle" of the ascendant Mars is located in a year, he will provoke war according to the quantity of his strength; and for this reason, they provoke war when he is in the "fourth aspect" <note>square</note> of Saturn and Jupiter. Then, when you see that Mars is the provoker of war, look in what place he has fallen from the ascendant; and you will see where the "Part of War" <term>Part of War: a specific calculated point used to predict conflict</term> has fallen, and which of the houses the Lord of that Part rules; and you will see if any of the "evils" <note>malefic planets</note> aspects that house...

...Mars <note>The OCR reads "marito," but the context of war suggests "Marte" (Mars), the planet of conflict.</note> or the "part of war" <term>part of war: a calculated mathematical point in a chart used to predict conflict</term> is in opposition or in a square aspect <term>square aspect: a harsh 90-degree angle between planets signifying tension</term>, or if they are in those signs, or if they aspect the sign that presides over that city or region in which the revolution of the year occurs; or if they aspect the significator of the king or another magnate who presides over that climate, city, or region from an opposition or square aspect, or are bodily joined to him: it signifies that whether that noble person wishes it or not, he shall have war with someone or some people in that revolution, and his enemies will achieve victory over him; or at the very least, sorrow, sadness, tribulation, and anguish will come upon him. And if the planet which was his significator is combust <term>combust: weakened by being too close to the Sun's heat</term>, it signifies the same, and there shall be fear for him; and if it is retrograde <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky, usually indicating weakness or reversal</term>, its figure signifies flight, the strength of enemies, and his own fall and dejection; similarly if it was first in a good place from the ascendant and then comes to a weak place.

### ¶ Also concerning the same: what follows when one of the malefics <term>malefics: "evil-doing" planets, specifically Saturn and Mars</term> presides.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, the 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said that when Mars presides over the signification of the year and is strong, there will be war with trickery and anxieties, and with plundering and violent killing. And when Saturn presides over the year or the quarter, there will be war through seductions and cunning, and through discipline and stratagems. And he said when one of the malefics presides over the year and another malefic is the lord of the quarter <note>original: "dñs quarte"</note>, there will be no doubt about wars in that same quarter. And similarly if a malefic aspects the lord of the year or the quarter from an opposition or square aspect; or if the lord of the quarter is in the seventh house <note>the house of open enemies</note> or is retrograde. And he said that if there is enmity toward the lord of the quarter, war will be in that same quarter; and similarly if there is enmity toward the lord of the month, it will be in that same month.

## ¶ Chapter Thirty-Six: When the revolution of the year signifies war; and if so, when it signifies victory, and when flight or defeat, and when peace or the ending of war.

After you see in the revolution that a future war is signified, look at the planet that signifies it. Because if it is direct <term>direct: moving forward in its usual orbit, a sign of strength</term> and in good condition, it does not permit the war to reach its end, and it will be stayed and annulled on the part of the king or the presiding official of the region in which you are, or in the region for which you seek that revolution of years; and it will signify peace and the extinction of war. See also how many planets aspect the significator and how many of them there are; for a multitude of planets aspecting him—and even more strongly if he has dignity <term>dignity: astrological "home turf" where a planet has more power</term> in the place where he is—will signify his strength and victory, and that he will be more helped than his adversaries, both by his own people and by foreigners. And if he is stationary in his second station <term>second station: the moment a planet stops moving backward to move forward again</term>, it signifies him as strong and powerful in war, as well as his followers. If however he is stationary in his first station <term>first station: the moment a planet stops moving forward to begin moving backward</term>, it signifies his strength at the beginning of the war, yet in the end he does not succeed well nor will he persevere. But if he is retrograde, it signifies his flight and ruin. And if it is the significator of the enemy or the one wishing to wage war with him, you shall judge by the aforementioned conditions just as I told you regarding the significator of your own kingdom, according to what you have observed. If however the significator is direct as I said and not impeded, it signifies either peace, or if there is war, it will signify victory. And if you wish to know on the part of which people or by whose aid his victory comes and the cause of the defeat of his enemies: look at which of the planets aspects him best and from the greatest dignity; for that one will be the significator of those who were the cause of his victory. For example, if it is the Sun or Saturn, it will be the king or another more noble person—though the Sun signifies younger men than Saturn. If it is Mars, it will be warlike soldiers. And if it is Jupiter, it will be noble and wise magnates.

<column-break/>

And if it is Mercury, it will be literate men, both noble and common. And if it is the Moon, it will be men who engage in trade, seafaring, and the like. And Albumasar said that if it is Venus, it will be the Arabs.

## ¶ Chapter Thirty-Seven: How a choice should be made for one wishing to go to war.

If someone wishes to go out to war because you have seen it coming in that revolution, and you wish to choose an hour for him to do this: look at the three superior planets <term>superior planets: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, which are further from the Sun than Earth is</term> to see whether they are retrograde or direct. If they are retrograde, Albumasar said the start of your hour for going to war should be when they turn direct. And if they are direct, then [the time is] when they begin to turn retrograde; and similarly when they begin to be combust; and if they were combust, when they begin to rise; and if they were occidental <term>occidental: setting in the west after the sun</term> when they become oriental <term>oriental: rising in the east before the sun</term>; and if they were oriental when they become occidental; or when they have changed from the signs in which they were—namely, the hour in which the planets signified war—for then the planet is said to "change its figure," and similarly then its substance or signification is changed. If however Mars is "received" <term>reception: a cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term> in the hour of the revolution—and even better if he is received by one of the "fortunes" <term>fortunes: the beneficial planets Jupiter and Venus</term> from a house or exaltation—the war will be extinguished in that year or that revolution. And if there is reception from the tenth house <note>the house of authority and government</note>, it signifies not only the extinction of war but also peace in that year.

## ¶ Chapter Thirty-Eight: By what kind of men or nations the war shall be waged.

When you see the figure of the revolution of the year cast and you find that a war is coming: look to which side Mars seems to give aid. For he will aid that side with whose significator he is in a friendly relationship and which he aspects most closely; consider also which side he is on, the east or the west, and from which side the planet from which he is separating is located. For he [the planet he separates from] is on the side of the ascendant <note>the person asking or the local ruler</note>, and the one he joins is on the opposite side. For from whichever side Mars is, if he is direct, the war on that side will be carried out by warlike and upright men who securely show their faces to the enemy and will not turn their backs. If indeed he is retrograde, it will be done by various men who want to be praised for things they do not do; they sometimes attribute to themselves what others do, and they say more than they perform, and they threaten more than they strike. These are the ones who cry for war with great insistence but are not stable in battle; instead, they then leave it on the shoulders of others and boast that they have done great things; they are plunderers like thieves and "cutters of the ways" <note>original: "abscisores viarum," meaning highwaymen or bandits</note>. And if Mars is stationary, the war will be strong, just as I told you above in another chapter when speaking of the station of the significator. Look similarly at Saturn, who, although he leads men to war heavily, nevertheless induces strong and terrible wars beyond all others, and great pestilential ones; for he too is seen in this matter to signify this from the side on which he is located. And Albumasar said that Saturn signifies a heaviness to the citizens of that same region in which he is, according to the amount of the substance of the sign in which he is and the bounds of his place; afterward you shall follow through the succession [of houses]: the ascendant, the house of substance <note>2nd house</note>, of brothers <note>3rd house</note>, etc., until the end of the twelve signs. And he said that when Saturn is retrograde, it will be just as I told you concerning Mars, but this is more grave. And these same chapters can be used in questions of wars, in the departure of hours to war, and in the bringing out of *carrocci* <note>original: "carociorum." A *carroccio* was a large, four-wheeled ceremonial chariot carrying a city's standard and an altar, used by medieval Italian city-states to rally troops in battle.</note> and banners. Do not believe that this chapter or anything else contradicts the others, but distinguish the times and harmonize the writings. And Albumasar said a retrograde planet signifies a mixing in affairs and a reversal and diversity; also war and victory for the lord of that same climate which belongs to that planet. And...

A stationary planet <term>stationary: a planet that appears to stand still in the sky before changing direction</term> signifies a desire for evil and the repetition of a matter that had already ceased, as well as killing. And if the aspect <term>aspect: the geometric relationship between two planets</term> signifies evil, it means strife, seductions, and cunning tricks.

### Chapter Thirty-Nine: Whether the captain of the adversaries is young or old.

If you wish to know the age of the captain or leader of the opposing side: look at the malefic planet that is hindering the situation; if it is not hindering, look at its location, and look at the location of the enemy's significator <term>significator: the planet that represents a specific person or event in a chart</term>. If both are oriental <term>oriental: rising before the sun; associated with youth or the beginning of a cycle</term>, they will be old. If one is oriental and the other occidental <term>occidental: setting after the sun; associated with ending or later life</term>, he will be of middle age, neither very young nor very old. However, a malefic signifies a younger person than the Lord of the Seventh House <note>The seventh house in an astrological chart traditionally represents open enemies and opponents.</note> if it is oriental, and an older person if it is occidental.

### Chapter Forty: When the significator of war is at peace with the Lord of the Year, and what follows from it.

Albumasar <note>Albumasar (787–886 AD) was a Persian astrologer whose writings were essential to medieval European science.</note> said that when the significator of war is at peace with the Lord of the Year <term>Lord of the Year: the planet ruling the sign rising at the start of the astrological year</term>, there will be good in that same year. And if it is at peace with the Lord of the half-year or with the Lord of the quarter-year, there will be good in that same half or quarter. And if it is at peace with the Lord of the month, there will be good in that month; if with the Lord of the day, in that day. By "at peace," I mean joined to it by "body" <term>conjunction: when two planets are at the same position</term> or by an aspect with "reception" <term>reception: when one planet is in a sign governed by the other, indicating cooperation</term>. And he said that when it is at peace with the Lord of the Profection <term>profection: a symbolic movement of the chart by one sign per year or month</term>, there will be good in the latter half of the month. Understand the same regarding the day and hour. And if the peacemaking occurs from the beginning of the sign up to its seventh degree and a half, the good will be in the first six months. And if it is from the seventh and a half degree up to the end of the 15th degree, the good will be from three months onward until the end of the half-year. And if it is from the 15th degree up to the 22nd degree and a half, it will be in the last six months of the year. And if it is from the 22nd and a half degree until the end of the sign, it will be from the ninth month onward until the end of the year. Understand the same for the month, day, and hour; in those times there will be security, and peoples will not attack men but will be at peace, nor will it be necessary to fear them.

### Chapter Forty-One: What the malefic planets signify when they are in human signs during the revolution.

Look in the revolution of the years and see if any of the planets are in "human signs"—namely Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, or Aquarius—and see whether that planet is slow in its course. Look similarly to see if another malefic joins it by body or by an opposition or square aspect <term>square aspect: a harsh 90-degree angle indicating conflict</term>, whether the one joining it is retrograde or direct. This signifies harm coming to humans; if it is retrograde <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward; usually a sign of weakness or disruption</term>, this will happen more quickly and with greater injury. And if the conjunction is in the "angles" <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the strongest parts of a chart</term>, it will be more severe and more cunning. If there is a malefic that aspects another, and the other (namely the retrograde one) which joins it is in the tenth house, it signifies a hindrance, weight, or evil that will then befall all men in any region, unless the planet that is the Lord of the sign presiding over a specific region works against it; it is more severe and powerful if the malefic that hinders is in the middle of heaven <term>midheaven: the highest point in the sky; the 10th house</term>.

<column-break/>

Those regions will be troubled for that reason. If, however, there is a malefic aspecting the seventh house and the retrograde planet joining it is in the fourth house, the beginning of the hindrance will be from everywhere and will extend from the north to the west. And if two malefics join, the hindrance will be more severe and appear more quickly; there will be heavy mortality among men. This is even more powerful if Saturn is the one doing the hindering, because he has a natural tendency to hinder the significations of the sign in which he is located. You should see, therefore, in what place the malefic falls in relation to the location of the other malefic (the slow one). For if they are joined in a "common sign" <term>common sign: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces; signs of transition</term>, or if the one joining the other joins from a common sign, it will determine that evil through death. But if it is in a "fixed" or "movable" sign, the end of the significance will follow the nature of whichever of the two malefics is stronger in the place where it is found. For if Mars is stronger, it will be determined through killing or through hot, pestilential infirmities, especially if it is prepared to join with the Lord of the Eighth House <note>The house of death.</note> or the Lord of the Sixth House <note>The house of illness.</note>, or with a planet that transfers light between itself and one of them. If, however, Saturn is stronger, it will end either through melancholic illnesses or pestilences, according as he is joined or prepared to be joined with any of those I mentioned regarding Mars. And Albumasar said: you shall combine the strength of death with it. These things happen more powerfully if their conjunction is in the angles. But if it is outside the angles, their significations will be diminished, there will not be as much hindrance, and things will improve. And Albumasar said the greatest destruction will be in the part where the hindering malefic is located. And he said: know therefore what sign the two malefics are in among the cities and provinces, for in those places the predicted evils will happen.

### Chapter 42: Concerning a thing that causes fear in the revolution of the year, and what the malefics in angles signify.

Sometimes certain horrible things appear in the revolution of the year which cause fear. Therefore, if you see any of these with the revolution of the year: see whether the thing that causes fear joins or aspects Saturn or Jupiter, since they are heavier than the rest; for they will weigh down that fear and it will be something to be doubted. This is even stronger if the aforementioned planets are hindered, and especially Saturn, who will signify long-lasting sorrows following from that fear, and even death. But if he does not aspect or join any of them, the peace will not be harmed. If, however, the significator of that evil is in an angle, it will signify a multitude of evil and its durability. And Albumasar said when it is "before an angle" <term>cadent: the houses moving away from the angles; weaker positions</term>, it will be slight and brief. And he said: look for help through the "dignities" <term>dignities: the essential strength of a planet based on its position in the zodiac</term> in this time, for they help toward both good and evil.

### Chapter 43: When the Lord of the sign in which the Lord of the Year is located aspects him, or when he does not aspect him, and what it signifies.

Look in the revolution at the planet in whose house the Lord of the Year is located, and see whether that planet aspects him with a trine or sextile aspect <term>trine/sextile: harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</term> and is not hindered; for if it is so, men will be in a good state, namely in peace, security, joy, and tranquility. But if it is not hindered but does not aspect him, or if it aspects him but is hindered, judge between the two. If it does not aspect him and is hindered, it signifies sadness, anxiety, fear, lawsuits, or contentions, and the total opposite of what it signified for good. And Albumasar said that this is according to the quantity of the "complexion of the substance" of the sign in which the significator is located: for if it is in the first house, it will be in persons; if it is in the second, it will be in substance <note>Wealth or possessions.</note>; and understand the same for the other houses.

## Chapter 44. Concerning the revolution of the year when it occurs at the setting of the sun.

We shall consider the revolution of the year <term>revolution of the year: the moment the Sun enters the sign of Aries, marking the astrological New Year</term> to see whether it falls at the setting of the sun. For Albumasar <note>Albumasar (787–886 AD) was a Persian astrologer whose work was foundational to Western medieval astrology.</note> said that when it is so, the Sun will commit its disposition to the Moon, which is the light-bearer of the night. Therefore, look at her and where her place is from the ascendant <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</term>; if she is fit to receive the disposition of the revolution, look to the lord of the sign in which she is then located. See how it is regarded by the planets and judge according to what you see: for if the fortunes <term>fortunes: beneficial planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</term> regard it, they signify good; but the evil ones <term>malefics: harmful planets, usually Saturn and Mars</term> signify evil. Also observe how the Moon is placed with Saturn—that is, in what aspect, whether trine or sextile <term>aspect: the geometric angle between planets; trines and sextiles are considered harmonious</term>—and whether Saturn receives her from his house or his exaltation or from two other dignities. For then Saturn will commit his disposition to her, or she will commit her disposition to Saturn. For if Saturn commits his disposition to her, she becomes stronger and will better dispose the events of that revolution. If, however, she commits her disposition to him, he will not dispose well over that revolution afterward, and if he does dispose, his disposition will be wicked. And Albumasar said to look at the increasing of her light and its lessening, and whether an eclipse is to come to her in 그해 <note>original: "in anno illo"</note>. And he said it is necessary that you look at the place of the eclipse and the degree of its completion, and in an eclipse of the sun, its degree and the place of conjunction, and the <term>Almuten: the planet with the most combined strength and dignity at a specific point in the zodiac</term> over these places, and how the planets looking upon it regard it. The Almuten is the planet that presides over the degree of conjunction or return due to its multitude of dignities or strengths.

## Chapter 45. When the lord of the ascendant is impeded in the revolution of the year, and what follows from it.

Look in the revolution of the year for the lord of the ascendant <term>lord of the ascendant: the planet that rules the sign rising on the horizon</term>; if you find it impeded <term>impeded: weakened or afflicted by a bad position or a harmful planet</term>, announce that an impediment is coming upon men in that year according to the nature of the sign of the ascendant. For example, if the ascending sign is formed in the image of a human, it will happen to them in their persons. If, however, the ascending sign is formed in the image of another animal, it will happen to animals formed in that image. And this will happen more severely in the land over which that sign presides and over which that planet presides. And Albumasar said that it will be more from the direction of the east and in the parts assigned to the planet which was the lord of the ascending sign than in others. For instance, if the ascendant is Libra and Venus is impeded, the land of Libra will suffer an impediment from winds and infirmities, and pains of the head and such like. And if the ascendant is Taurus, the land of Taurus will suffer impediment and loss from cold and snow and drought, with the destruction of the fruits of trees and impediment to oxen and fractures <note>original: "amfractibus," likely referring to broken limbs or difficult terrains</note> and similar things, according to the nature and disposition of each region, unless Mars works against it. And if the ascendant is Gemini and Mercury is impeded, the land of the Gemini will suffer from the blowing of winds and from the corruption of the air, and from pain of the head and the intestines, the tongue, and the lungs, and in the breathing passages of the body. And if the ascendant is Virgo, the land of Virgo will suffer from cold and drought and moderate sterility, and from pains of the chest in the regions of the heart, unless Jupiter works against it. And if the ascendant is Cancer and the Moon is impeded, the land of Cancer will suffer from rains and from pain of the eyes and thundering in the head, unless Saturn works against it. And if the ascendant is Leo and the Sun is impeded, the land of Leo will suffer from the heat of the air and from the flowing of rheum <term>rheum: a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, often associated with illness</term> and from sicknesses of the head and similar things, unless Saturn works against it with coldness and constriction. And if the ascendant is Scorpio and Mars is impeded, the land of Scorpio will be hindered by waters and poisonous 

<column-break/>

reptiles and from pains of the head and the arms, as well as the private parts and similar things. And if the ascendant is Aries, the land of Aries will be hindered by the heat of the air and from the flowing of rheum and from pain of the head and similar things, unless Venus works against it. And if the ascendant is Sagittarius and Jupiter is impeded, the land of Sagittarius will be hindered in its people in the first part of the year, and in the last part in animals that are ridden, with sicknesses of the head and legs and similar things. If, however, the ascendant is Pisces, the land of Pisces will be hindered by the flooding of waters and from sicknesses of the feet, such as gout <note>original: "podagre"</note> and similar things, unless Mercury works against it. And if the ascendant is Capricorn and Saturn is impeded, the land of Capricorn will then be hindered by cold and drought and sterility, and from pain of the knees and fractures, and of the head and feet and similar things, unless the Moon works against it. And if the ascendant is Aquarius and Saturn is impeded, the land of Aquarius will be hindered by humid winds and from sicknesses of the legs and the neck and the head, unless the Sun works against it. And if the lord of the ascendant of the revolution presides over other lands than those the sign itself presides over, they will share in the impediments with the lands of the ascending sign, although they may not be hindered as much as those which are specifically assigned to the sign. And if the ascending signs are safe and the planets are free, the lands subject to them will be saved according to the state of each. And Albumasar said: after you have looked at the ascendant, look at the second, third, fourth, fifth, and the rest of the houses and their lords, just as you looked at the first, through to the end of the signs. And he said: make the angles <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the most powerful points in a chart</term> and their lords more worthy, because they have work and strength above the other signs, which have the task of signifying the affairs of kings.

## Chapter 46. What follows from the conjunction of two malefics with the year or with the significator of the king.

Look in the revolution of the year for the conjunction <term>conjunction: when two planets appear in the same spot in the sky</term> of the lord of the year and the significators of the king with the infortunes <term>infortunes: another term for the malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</term>. For if the infortunes are joined with the lord of the year—whether they join with him or he with them—this signifies a gravity <note>meaning a hardship or serious burden</note> that will come upon the peasants or the common people; and this will happen in the land or region that belongs to the sign in which the infortunes are located. If, however, they are in different signs, it will happen in different regions according to what is assigned to those signs. But if the point of conjunction is with the significator of the king, it signifies that gravity will come upon the king from the regions mentioned above. And Albumasar said that victory is seen in the sublimation of the strength of the evil ones in their journey. And he said: let the testimony of Saturn and Jupiter be sought in this, according to what he revealed in the chapter on conjunctions.

### Also concerning the same.

Albumasar said when one of the two malefics is joined to the other, and they are in human signs <term>human signs: signs depicted as humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</term>—whether by body <note>conjunction</note> or by opposition or by a square aspect—they are joined together. If, however, one of those evils is Saturn and he is stronger than Mars, it will signify many and grave infirmities, and many shall die from them. If, however, it is Mars and he is stronger than Saturn, it will signify killings instead of the infirmities of Saturn. If, moreover, one is in a human sign and the other in another, each will send an impediment upon the things signified by the sign in which he is, yet it will be less. In this, it does not matter whether one or two are diurnal or nocturnal, or masculine or feminine. But if they are in "reception" <term>reception: a cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</term>, it will diminish their impediment according to the reception. And Albumasar said: those who fall ill in that same year, health or safety will be separated for them <note>meaning they may struggle to recover</note>, except for a few who will die. If, however, those malefics are themselves in reception, there will be less death and less killing. And Albumasar said: and they shall mix with one another.

# Chapter 47. How the state of the King and the common people should be observed in their bodies during the revolution of the year.

After you have examined what follows from the conjunction of the evil planets <term>malefics: usually Saturn or Mars, planets associated with challenge or hardship</term> with the Lord of the Year <term>Lord of the Year: the planet ruling the sign of the Ascendant at the moment of the Aries ingress</term> and with the King’s significator, it now remains to be said in this chapter how one should observe the state of the common people, the peasants, and the King in their physical persons. You shall observe the state of the common people or the peasants and the King in their persons from the Lord of the Year and from the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>. Look at what aspects <note>original: "aspectibus"; the geometric angles between planets</note> are in the Ascendant of the revolution: whether the "fortunes" <term>fortunes: beneficial planets, typically Jupiter and Venus</term> or the "evils" look upon it. For if the fortunes look upon the Ascendant and the Lord of the Year, they signify that the bodies of these people will be in good health in that revolution. It is even better if they also look upon the house of the Ascendant, and better still if they look upon the Moon, and most perfect of all if the Part of Fortune <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</term> is there and is observed by the fortunes.

If, however, the evil planets look upon the Ascendant, and there are no other indicators of health or well-placed planets—and the Part of Fortune does not judge the opposite of what I told you (that is, if it is not in a good place)—then announce evil. For example, if the evil planets hinder the Lord of the Year, the hindrance will be judged according to the nature of the hindering evil planet. For **Saturn** signifies hindrance arising from deceit, long distances, and death. **Mars**, however, signifies hindrance through iron, fire, and slaughter, whether in flight or otherwise. You shall observe the state of the King from the Sun, the tenth house <term>tenth house: the "Midheaven," traditionally representing the King, authority, and career</term> and its lordship, as well as from the Part of Fortune and its lord. If you find these well-disposed in a trine or sextile aspect <note>trine (120°) and sextile (60°) are harmonious alignments</note> with the fortunes, or in a square aspect <note>original: "in quarto"; a 90° angle, usually challenging</note> with "reception" <term>reception: when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting, creating a hospitable link</term>, or in physical conjunction with them, and the fortunes look upon the tenth house, judge health and safety for the King's body from all sides and in every way. If you find the opposite, you shall judge the opposite. And if you find the good state to be less than what I have described, you shall judge it to be less good. I believe the same should be said regarding an evil state. And if you wish to make Saturn a participant in the aforesaid matters, you will not err.

# Chapter 48. Which planets signify kings and kingdoms, and concerning the impediments of the four angles.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a preeminent Persian astrologer</note> speaks of kings and kingdoms. He says that whatever planet you find hindered in the four angles <term>angles: the four most powerful points of a chart—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, you should declare evil according to that planet's nature. Therefore, you must see where the Sun and Moon fall in the figure of the revolution. For if they fall in good places from the tenth house and in stronger positions, or in the tenth house itself, they signify general good for kings and a good disposition for kingdoms. The angles and their lords should also be observed. For if you find the angles and their lords to be fortunate—and make the Moon and the Part of Fortune participants—and you find them well-disposed (that is, fortunate and strong), then announce general good. If you find them ill-disposed, announce the opposite. If you find some of them well-disposed and others poorly, announce according to what you find: for you should announce good according to the significations of the well-disposed ones, and evil according to the significations of the ill-disposed ones.

# Also concerning the same, according to Albumasar.

Albumasar says the strongest of kings will be the king whose climate <term>climate: a geographical zone or region in ancient geography</term> and cities belong to the Lord of the Year, following the succession of the signs' strengths. Every birth that occurs under that same sign of the Lord of the Year will be more reliably good and of better order and dignity among men, unless that person's birth chart was hindered at its root <note>original: "in radice"; referring to the individual's original birth chart or 'radix'</note>. Therefore, you must look at the hour of the revolution to see if the Lord of the Year was the significator of the birth, the region, or the climate over which the king presides. For that king whose kingdom falls under the lord of the Lord of the Year will be stronger than other kings, and his kingdom will be better, more durable, and in a better state than other kingdoms. And those who are born in the cities or regions or that kingdom

<column-break/>

during that revolution, provided the Moon is fortunate and strong, will be more fortunate and famous, and will be held in higher regard than those born in other kingdoms—provided that the planet which is the significator of any of them is not hindered in their original birth chart. Even if the Part of Fortune is hindered, this <insert>the Lord of the Year</insert> will supply what was lacking on the part of the Part of Fortune. If, however, the significator of someone's birth is hindered, that person will not be so fortunate, yet they will be less unfortunate than the unfortunate people of other regions.

# Chapter 49. When the Moon or Mercury is the Lord of the Year or the significator of the king and is observed by the unfortunates, what follows from that; and concerning the Part of Fortune and its lord.

If it should happen that the Moon or Mercury is the Lord of the Year or the significator of the king, and any of the evil planets is with it and hinders it by aspect or conjunction, it will weaken and burden the year and the common people if it is the Lord of the Year. If it is the significator of the king, it will weaken and burden his state. This can neither be avoided nor prevented because of the weakness of the significator; it will not have enough strength to expel the hindrances brought upon it by the evil planet with which it is joined, unless the Part of Fortune and its lord work to the contrary, producing good because of their own disposition. If indeed they are hindered, they will not signify good, but rather the opposite, according to the nature of the sign in which they are located; for the hindrance will fall upon the things signified by that sign, and it will be said to be an enemy to the significator. Look then and see whether the significator of the king commits its disposition or its strength to the significator of the common people; for the disposition of the year or the king will be worse if the significator is hindered by an evil planet and is joined to a planet that is an enemy to the Ascendant, and vice versa.

# Chapter 50. On the commission of the disposition of the Lord of the Year to the significator of the king and what follows from it.

Albumasar says that if the Lord of the Year commits its disposition to the significator of the king in a quartile aspect <note>a square or 90° angle</note>, the king will look upon the peasants for a petition of wealth <note>meaning he will demand taxes or resources</note>, and for this reason, distress will come upon them. But if it is from a trine or sextile aspect, they will return their tribute without the pressure of distress falling upon the peasants. And he said that if the significator of the king commits its disposition to the Lord of the Year, the king will extract wealth in that same year. And he said if the lord of the 11th house <term>11th house: the house of hopes, friends, and the king's treasury</term> looks upon the significator of the king, this will happen with a favorable spirit.

# Chapter 51. On the conjunction of the Head of the Dragon with Saturn and the conjunction of the Tail with Mars and what follows from it.

Albumasar says the conjunction of the Head of the Dragon <term>Head of the Dragon: the North Node of the Moon, usually considered magnifying or beneficial</term> with Saturn signifies a hindrance of the substance <note>wealth or property</note> of the sign in which they are joined, just as an eclipse of the Sun and Moon signifies, unless the malice is broken by the aspects of the fortunes. Therefore, if Saturn is joined with the Head of the Dragon in **Aries**, it signifies hindrances to come in that revolution in those things and their like, unless Mars looks upon them from a trine or sextile aspect and is himself fortunate; there will also be harm in the affairs of kings unless the significator of the king or the lord of the 10th house works to the contrary. If, however, their conjunction is in **Leo**, there will be hindrance among the wild animals that live by prey, and it will harm kings somewhat, though not much. And if their conjunction is in the first half of **Sagittarius**, there will be hindrance among men. If, however, it is in the last [half] of it...

## Chapter 52. On the conjunction of Mars and Saturn with the Tail.

**M**ars indeed, when joined with the Tail <term>Tail: the South Node of the Moon, traditionally called the "Cauda Draconis," often associated with decrease or misfortune</term>, signifies destruction, killing, famine, and a multitude of evils. If the Tail is joined with Saturn, it signifies famine and a lack of good things in whatever sign it may be, as well as heavy destruction, cold, great fears, the destruction of harvests, and an excess of evil; this will occur in the region where the conjunction takes place.

## Chapter 53. On the conjunction of the two malefics, namely Saturn and Mars, with any planet in the degree of its exaltation, and what follows from it.

**A**lbumasar says: look in the revolution of the year <term>revolution: the astrological chart cast for the moment the sun enters Aries, used to predict the year's events</term> for the conjunction of the malefics <term>malefics: planets associated with hardship, specifically Saturn and Mars</term>, namely Saturn and Mars. See whether they join with any planet that is in the degree of its exaltation <term>exaltation: a sign where a planet is thought to be particularly powerful</term> through an aspect <term>aspect: a specific geometric angle between planets</term>, which is even worse if it is by a square or opposition <note>the square (90°) and opposition (180°) are considered "hard" or difficult aspects</note>. 

For if it is Saturn, it signifies evil and destruction in the region assigned to that planet. If Saturn’s aspect is from a fixed sign, that significance will be prolonged according to the number of degrees between their bodies, into years, months, weeks, or days. For if it is signified that it should be completed within the year which the revolution represents, the number of degrees will indicate months. But if the significance extends beyond that year or that revolution, it will be prolonged for us. If it is from a movable sign, it will signify days according to the number 

<column-break/>

of degrees. And if it is not completed in that many days, it will signify weeks. If it is from a common sign, it will be weeks. And if it is not completed in that many weeks, it will signify months. 

But if Saturn does not aspect it, but some planet transfers their light <term>transfer of light: when a faster planet moves from one planet to another, effectively carrying the influence or "message" between them</term> between them, it will signify the occurrence of unpleasant events for the people of that planet's region; or destruction and harm will come upon them from nations that were not from that region. But if no planet transfers the light between them, and the rays of Saturn touch the rays of a planet in its exaltation, or a planet suited to transfer the light between them, sadness and sorrow will come upon the people of that region, which they ought not to fear; for the fear will be dissolved and will not result in action, by the will of God. 

If it is from an aspect of Mars, just as was said regarding the aspect of Saturn—and worse if it is a square or opposition—the predicted things will happen just as I said of Saturn, in a similar way and for similar causes; and even more so because Mars will carry out the events he signifies through iron, fire, and the shedding of blood.

## Chapter 54. On the Lord of the Fourth if he is in the house of travel at the hour of the revolution, and what it signifies.

**S**hould there be people imprisoned <note>original: "incarcerati"</note> at the hour of the revolution in the city or region where you are, as sometimes happens, and you wish to know what will become of them in that revolution: look to the Lord of the Fourth <term>Lord of the Fourth: the planet ruling the 4th house, which represents the end of matters and hidden places like prisons</term> from the Ascendant, and see if he is in the Ninth house <term>Ninth house: the house of long-distance travel and foreign lands</term>. For if he is there, it signifies the "travel" of those who were in prisons in that city or region, and their exit from their prisons in that revolution. 

This will happen to them without the permission or will of the King, the power, or others who rule that region—unless the King's significator aspects the Lord of the Fourth with a third aspect <term>third aspect: a sextile (60 degrees), usually a friendly aspect</term>, for then it will be by his will. If, however, it is from a fourth aspect <term>fourth aspect: a square (90 degrees)</term> or opposition, then they will go out not only without his permission but even against his will and command. And if the King's significator or the presiding planet is in the Ninth and the Lord of the Fourth commits his disposition <term>commits his disposition: when a planet hands over its influence to the planet that rules the sign it occupies</term> to him, it signifies that the King himself or the ruler will lead the bound prisoners out of their cells by his own will. But if the Lord of the Ninth receives the disposition from the Lord of the Fourth in the Ninth, it signifies that an enemy of the King or the ruler will lead the incarcerated out of their prisons. Albumasar said: mix the conjunctions of the planets with one another and judge according to their mixture.

## Chapter 55. What it signifies when one of the planets commits its disposition to another in the revolution.

**Y**ou shall also see whether any of the planets commits its disposition to another in the mixture. For if the King’s significator commits his disposition to Saturn, religious people keeping their vows, as well as the old, the decrepit, and those engaged in heavy labors, will receive good from the King; and the King will spend on the buildings of religious orders and also on his own. If Saturn is then above the earth, the King will build a structure on the land. If he is beneath the earth, he will build canals, wells, and aqueducts and will populate lands—even more so if he is in the Ascendant near its end, or in the Third or Ninth houses—and he will be diligent in heavy works. 

If he commits it to Jupiter, two nobles, great men, famous skilled men, bishops, and the like will receive good from the King. If he commits it to Mars, bellicose soldiers, armor-bearers, leaders of armies, and commanders of wars will obtain good from the King; they will be honored by him, he will listen to them, and he will bring them close to himself.

### Chapter Fifty-Six: When any planet is the Lord of the Year, what it signifies in every sign and in every triplicity; and first concerning Saturn.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personified planet Saturn. He is depicted as an elderly bearded man sitting in a chariot pulled by two winged dragons or serpents. He holds a scythe in his right hand. To his right is the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄). A small circular emblem below the chariot shows a man working the earth with a spade.</image-desc>

Although **Saturn** is naturally "evil" <note>original: "malus"; in medieval astrology, Saturn was considered a 'Great Malefic,' associated with hardship and restriction</note>, yet by accident he can sometimes signify good and fortune. Likewise, a "fortunate" planet, although it naturally signifies good, can by accident sometimes signify evil. Therefore, a planet that is evil by its own nature signifies harm and hindrance; if it joins with another evil planet or looks upon it with any aspect <note>an "aspect" is a specific geometric angle between planets that determines their relationship</note>, and is itself hindered, it will hinder the other. However, if it is free from hindrances and well-disposed, whenever it relates via a **trine** or **sextile** aspect, it will not hinder but will signify an adaptation toward the good. Similarly, if a fortunate planet is hindered and weak, it weakens its own significance. Thus, if some hindered evil planet looks upon it, that planet will take on its malice and signify harm and hindrance, and the hindrance will be according to the nature of the evil planet obstructing that fortune. Therefore, after you have found the **Lord of the Year** and the signifier of the common people or peasants, if it is in **Aries**, **Leo**, or **Sagittarius** <note>these three signs make up the "Fire Triplicity"</note>, it signifies the appearance of things at which men will marvel in the cities and regions or lands which that sign rules. This will occur especially in eastern parts, and it will fall mostly upon the wealthy, the great, and the powerful who exceed the status of common nobles. This will be brought about by shrewd and ingenious men who hide their affairs and keep them silent. Signs and wondrous prodigies will be shown, and this will happen under the appearance of beautiful displays and hypocrisy. You will then see whether the one ruling the revolution is a fortune or a misfortune. If it is indeed a misfortune—namely Saturn—and he is free from hindrances and "fortunate" (meaning strong), it signifies that his subjects will be in a good state and well-disposed. But if he is hindered and in an evil state at the hour of the revolution, it signifies hindrance and a poor disposition for all his subjects and those under his dominion: whether they be the old wealthy, religious orders, Jews, farmers, or the elderly and infirm. Discords will arise among men, and 

<column-break/>

lies will abound, and they will blaspheme one another. And if Saturn is in a good state and well-disposed in the place where he then resides, he will signify patience, subtlety, and the investigation of matters both noble and common in that year. It also signifies that peasants will obey their lords or kings and humble themselves before them; and the empire, kingdom, or dominion of the region in which you have cast the year's revolution will be exalted, and its fame and name will increase. But if Saturn is in an evil state and his malice is diminished in that revolution, and **Jupiter** looks upon him from a trine or sextile aspect—being himself free, fortunate, and strong—he breaks the malice of Saturn and takes it away, nor does he allow it to harm or hinder. If the **Sun** looks upon him from a trine or sextile aspect, and is not falling away from the Ascendant or from an angle (except for the tenth), nor is otherwise unfortunate, he breaks three parts of Saturn's malice. If another fortunate planet, being itself fortunate and strong, looks upon him from the said aspects, or if Jupiter does so from a **square** <note>original: "quarto aspectu"; refers to a 90-degree angle, usually considered challenging but here acting as a check</note> aspect, it breaks and removes half of Saturn's malice. From other aspects, a fortunate planet diminishes Saturn's malice according to its own strength. If, however, no fortunate planet looks upon him to remove or diminish his malice, it signifies the death of the wealthy and the great, and their envy toward one another, along with accusations and negligence; it also signifies the hatred of the common people against them and their subjects. It further signifies death by way of water, and hindrance, fear, and death in the land or region signified by the sign in which he then resides. And if he is "oriental" in his light, direct in motion, swift in course, or in any of his dignities <note>specific degrees or signs where a planet has more power</note>, or in the dignity of another planet that is friendly to him—such as Jupiter and both the Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note>—and he joins with them and receives them, and is in a good house from the Ascendant, it signifies that men will apply themselves in that year or revolution to the management of heavy and laborious works. These include waterworks, the planting of trees, the gathering and raising of forests, the populating of lands and their cultivation, and the building of cities, castles, houses, or palaces and such things.

### Chapter Fifty-Eight: When Mars is joined to Saturn in the revolution and is in a good state, what it signifies.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration showing the personifications of the planets Saturn and Mars. They stand together in a chariot drawn by a horse. On the left, Saturn is depicted as an older man holding a scythe. On the right, Mars is depicted as a warrior in full armor. And if Saturn is the **Lord of the Year** or the revolution, and it is in a "good state" <note>original: "boni esse"; meaning it is positioned strongly in a sign where it has dignity or power</note>, and **Mars** is likewise, and it regards Saturn from a trine or sextile aspect, and each receives the other into its own house or its **exaltation** <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is most harmonious and powerful</note> or two other dignities; or if both are "received" by another single planet, it signifies that in that same year the wealth of the common people, the populace, or the peasants will increase, and their goods and reputation will be shared with the great and the wealthy. But if Mars regards Saturn or is physically joined to it while being in a "bad state" <note>original: "mali esse"; weakened or poorly positioned</note>, it signifies a decline in the status of the wealthy and great during that revolution in the regions associated with Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius, occurring shortly and without great delay. Those who live in the regions belonging to the sign in which both planets are located will fare poorly toward one another; there will be little piety and no mercy among them. 

And if their aspect is a trine or sextile, it signifies that gifts will come to the nobles, the wealthy, or the great who are in the regions of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius, and similarly they will rejoice and be glad because of the citizens who are in the division of the sign where Mars is located. Other inhabitants of those regions will also be in a good state, and pleasing things will come to them from those regions under the sign where Mars resides. However, if they are in **opposition** <note>180 degrees apart</note> or a square aspect without "reception" <note>When planets occupy each other's signs, softening a harsh aspect</note>, it signifies the opposite of what was said. For in place of gifts and other pleasantries, there will come evils, injuries, quarrels, demands, and strife between the wealthy or nobles and the great men of the regions in the division of the sign where Mars is, and the wealthy and great of the aforementioned regions. For they will rise up against them in wars and strive against them to expel them from their cities and regions, nor will they cease because of them; the roads between them will be cut off, and they will not allow goods to be carried from one region to another. The whole body of citizens in the regions under the sign of Mars will strive to harm and offend the citizens of the other aforementioned regions. 

And if Mars is physically joined with Saturn, it signifies war, the shedding of blood, and a multitude of fevers; it also signifies quartan and pestilential fevers in the eastern parts. It will signify trouble for young men, and war and mutual slaughter by the sword will fall among the wealthy and the great. And <term>Albumasar</term> <note>The Latinized name of Abu Ma'shar, a 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology</note> said it will bring hardship to the grain harvest and wine, and will multiply the supply of butter <note>original: "butiz"; likely referring to provisions or fat stores</note>. And he said that if Mars is near the ascendant of the year, there will be many wars, eye pains, and incurable infirmities; thunder will increase, and there will be

### Chapter 59: When the Sun is joined to Saturn in the revolution and both are in a good state.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration showing the personifications of the Sun and Saturn. On the left, Sol is depicted as a crowned king sitting on a throne. On the right, Saturn stands holding his scythe. Above them are their respective astrological symbols: ☉ for the Sun and ♄ for Saturn.</image-desc>

If Saturn is the Lord of the Year or the revolution, and the **Sun** is joined to it, and both are in a good state, it signifies that the wealthy or the great of that region will be occupied with seeking the kingdom and high, distinguished offices, looking toward the nobility or the great; and this will even be in a manner leaning toward the highest side of honesty and pleasantness. If, however, the aspect is a trine or sextile, gifts will come to those who are in the division of the sign where the Sun is. And <term>Albumasar</term> said it will bring good things and trade goods to those parts; and things will be brought from those matters signified by the Sun; the cheerfulness of men and their dignities will increase. But if the aspect is by opposition, in place of gifts there will come strife, war, and contradictions; nor will trade goods be carried from one of those regions to the other, and the opposite of what was said will occur; evil and terrible rumors will come in place of the former joyful ones. If indeed the aspect is a square, <term>Albumasar</term> said there will not be battles nor will wars multiply, but there will be quarrels and discord between the wealthy and the great.

### Chapter 60: When Venus is joined to Saturn in the revolution and they are in a good state.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration showing the personifications of the planets Venus and Saturn. On the left, Venus is depicted as a woman holding a large flower. On the right stands Saturn with his scythe. Above them are their respective astrological symbols: ♀ for Venus and ♄ for Saturn.</image-desc>

When Saturn is the Lord of the Year or the revolution and **Venus** is joined to it, it signifies the seeking of "Venerean" things, such as games, delights, songs, customs, objects of Venus's worship, and rivers in which men take delight; and peasants will mix with the wealthy from the start of the revolution, but their familiarity will not last. If Venus regards Saturn from a trine or sextile aspect, gifts and friendships will come to the wealthy who are in the division of the sign where Saturn is, from the citizens in the cities under the sign where Venus is; and pleasant things will come to them, including that which the power of Venus brings to them. And <term>Albumasar</term> said if she regards him from an opposition, there will be wars and strife in place of gifts and pleasant things, and the wealthy will go to war against these other wealthy men; what was being brought from those cities will be cut off, and resources will decrease in those parts. And he said it will shatter chance, and bad rumors will come, and a good state will be turned into evil, strife, grief, and sadness. And the root of all these things will be from women and because of women and Venerean matters; and men will be more honest than usual, especially if Saturn "receives" her and the revolution occurs at night. ### Chapter Sixty-One: Concerning Mercury when he is joined to Saturn in the revolution, and both are in a good state.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personification of Mercury seated in a chariot pulled by two roosters. Above the figure are the astrological symbols for Mercury (☿) and Saturn (♄). He holds a caduceus.</image-desc>

If, however, **Saturn** is the **Lord of the Year** <note>The planet that holds primary influence over the astrological chart cast for the year's beginning</note> or the **revolution** <note>original: "reuolutionis"; the start of the astrological year when the Sun enters Aries</note>, and **Mercury** is joined to him, it signifies that men—and especially the wealthy and the great—will be eager to acquire **simulations** <note>original: "simulationū"; here referring to the arts of rhetoric, representation, or persuasive speech</note> and eloquence, as well as philosophy, astronomy, medicine, and **dialectic** <note>The art of logical argument</note>. Similarly, anyone born under such a configuration will study these subjects, and will succeed and profit in them. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a highly influential Persian astrologer</note> said that there will be an appearance of such men at this time among the wealthy and the citizens of the regions in his division. And if Mercury regards him with a **trine or sextile aspect** <note>Harmonious geometric angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, every good thing will come upon the wealthy among them; they will bring goods for sale, and so on; and wealth will multiply there because of them. This will be praised in the cities under the division of Saturn and the sign in which he resides. For the most part, the aforementioned goods will be of a **mercurial** nature <note>Items associated with Mercury, such as books, tools, or trade goods</note>, and people will be firm and stable in their counsel. But if he regards him from an **opposition** <note>An angle of 180 degrees, usually indicating conflict</note>, there will be properties, conflict, and war in the place of gifts and domesticity. These wealthy men will move against those empires to attack them, fight them, and expel them from their own dwellings. Whatever good was being brought from them will be taken away; their substance will decrease in those parts, and wealth will be destroyed. Evil rumors will be heard; good will be hidden, and evil will appear from those cities. This is even stronger if Mercury is hindered by **malefics** <note>original: "infortuuis"; harmful planets like Mars or Saturn</note> or has any mixture with them. But if he is made fortunate by **benefics** <note>original: "fortunis"; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, he will hinder less, though he will not remove the obstacle of the opposition. When there is a **square aspect** <note>original: "aspectus quartus"; an angle of 90 degrees</note>, it will be less than this, and war will not appear; however, there will be a diversity of opinion between these wealthy or great men, and between the wealthy and the **peasants** <note>original: "rusticos"; common laborers or rural inhabitants</note>. And Albumasar said the cause of this matter will be a mercurial thing, just as he explained in the **Greater Book** <note>Referring to Albumasar's "Greater Introduction to Astrology"</note>, which he himself testifies. Understand this and keep it in your mind.

### Chapter Sixty-Two: Concerning the conjunction of the Moon with Saturn in the revolution, and both being in a good state.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the personification of Saturn seated in a chariot pulled by two dragons or winged serpents. Above the figure are the astrological symbols for Saturn (♄) and the Moon (☽).</image-desc>

If indeed Saturn is the Lord of the Year or the revolution, and the **Moon** is joined to him, there will be an appearance of legates, rumors, and spies, and the establishing of kingdoms. This will occur among the wealthy and the great as well as among the common people, for they will wish to be equal to the great in that revolution. And if the Moon then regards Saturn from a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies that there will come

<column-break/>

to the great or the nobles who are in the division of the sign where the Moon is, gifts and things in which they will rejoice. Goods for sale and physical wealth will be brought from those cities, and their riches will multiply because of them. And Albumasar said they will carry those things to the wealthy who are in the division of the sign where Saturn is, and they will mostly be **lunar things** <note>Items associated with the Moon, such as water-related goods, silver, or perishable foods</note>, and men will profit from **plantations** <note>original: "plā tatiōibus"; likely referring to agriculture or orchards</note>. And he said that if the aspect of the Moon and Saturn is from an opposition, it will be the contrary of what was said: for in the place of gifts and good things, there will be opposition and wars. These wealthy men—namely those in the division of the sign where the Moon is—will go toward the loss and weakening of the others. What was being brought from those parts to these will be taken away; wealth will be destroyed, and the ways of trade will be cut off. Evil rumors will rise and appear; good will be taken away and turned into evil. And if the aspect of the Moon to Saturn is a square, it will signify that war will not appear; nevertheless, there will be conflict between the wealthy, the great, and the peasants or commoners, and even among kinsmen, on account of lunar things.

### Chapter Sixty-Four: What Saturn signifies in each sign, and in each triplicity, and in each house, whether he is Lord of the Year or not.

When Saturn is Lord of the Year and is in **Aries** or its **triplicity** <note>A group of three signs of the same element; for Aries, these are the Fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>, it signifies a heaviness in the affairs of the great and the nobles who are in eastern parts, but especially in Aries.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a ram, representing the zodiac sign Aries.</image-desc>

Accordingly, when he is in Aries, it signifies a multitude of winds and the death of women of prayer or those pertaining to **religions** <note>original: "religiones"; likely referring to nuns or women in holy orders</note>. This will be in the parts of **Thozate** and **Alaroc** <note>Place names used in medieval astrological geography, often referring to regions in the East</note>. There will also be a scarcity of grain, wine, butter, and even ointments and fats. If indeed he is hindered, it signifies a multitude of thieves and the cutting off of roads, and many tribulations in that revolution. And if he is the sole **significator** <note>The planet that represents a specific person or event</note> and is **falling** <note>In a weak position in the horoscope</note> from the **ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> without regarding it, and is **direct** <note>Moving forward in the zodiac, not retrograde</note>, it signifies that distress and anguish will come upon the nobles. And Albumasar said if he is **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, he will destroy houses, substance, and their chests (of wealth); this is even more severe if he receives the **disposition of Mars** <note>Influenced by the planet Mars</note>, for then it signifies severe cold and the death of animals, along with what he said about wars and battles. But if he does not regard Mars, there will be a severe winter cold according to the nature of that region, and animals will die in it. And he said if he is not retrograde, it signifies that there will be contention among merchants, and plundering, and evil—and more strongly so if Mars regards him from an **angle** <note>A powerful position in the horoscope, like the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>. But if he regards him from a **falling house** <note>original: "cadenti"; a weak position</note>, it will lessen the hindrance; indeed, it almost entirely removes it. And **Messahala** <note>Māshā'allāh ibn Atharī (c. 740–815 AD), a prominent Jewish-Persian astrologer</note> said if he is direct in an angle, it signifies many rains and contentions of the wealthy; and more strongly so if he receives the lordship of Mars and his strength, for it signifies then that the peasants or commoners will contend with the king. And if he is retrograde, it will weigh heavily upon the being of men. And he said if he receives the disposition from Mars and the Moon together, it signifies severe cold, the death of animals, battles, and wars. Take note in the revolutions of the years of the world: if Saturn is in a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, he then signifies mortality and the penury and diminution of the things springing from the earth. But in **Leo**, it is stronger, harsher, and more lasting than in the others. In **Scorpio**, truly, it is less than in Leo. In **Taurus**, less than in Scorpio. In **Aquarius**...

### ¶ Chapter 64: Concerning Leo.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a lion walking to the left, representing the zodiac sign Leo.</image-desc>

If **Saturn** <note>original: "lito h̄"; the OCR likely misread the astrological symbol for Saturn ♄</note> is in **Leo** and his latitude is **Northern**, it signifies a multitude of rains and the corruption of the affairs of the great and the commoners alike, and the destruction of the gains of **merchants**. 

¶ And if he is **Oriental**, it signifies coming infirmities for peasants and low-born persons. 

¶ But if he is **Occidental**, it signifies pestilences and mortality that will come upon the land. 

¶ If indeed he is **retrograde**, it signifies hardships coming from accidents that will befall men; these will be prolonged and long-lasting. But if he is **direct** <note>original: "vltrectus"; meaning moving in his normal forward direction</note>, it signifies a lightness or relief from these things.

### ¶ Chapter 65: Concerning Sagittarius.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a centaur archer facing right, aiming a bow, representing the zodiac sign Sagittarius.</image-desc>

If he is in **Sagittarius** and his latitude is **Northern**, it signifies an abundance of water from springs and the cold of winter. 

¶ And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886), a famous Persian astrologer whose works were highly influential in Medieval Europe</note> said that if he is **Oriental**, it signifies the presence of the wealthy in their own regions. 

¶ And if he is **Occidental**, it signifies wars among noble men and magnates, and discords shall fall between them. 

¶ And if he is **retrograde**, it signifies hardship in the affairs and goods of men, and wars and battles among them. 

¶ And if he is **direct**, it signifies the prosperity of those traveling by land and by water.

If, however, he is in **Taurus** and its **triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; for Taurus, this is the Earth triplicity, including Virgo and Capricorn</note>, it signifies an impediment to the wealthy and the great. This will occur in southern parts, based on the observation of the sign in which **Saturn** is located, but especially in Taurus.
