### Chapter 68: On Virgo

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Virgo, depicted as a standing woman holding a branch in her right hand and a stalk of wheat in her left.</image-desc>

If indeed **Saturn** should be in **Virgo** and his **latitude** <note>The angular distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic</note> should be **northern**, it signifies the goodness of the winds and their sweetness and their strengthening in the times of harvests and of those bearing fruit. And if his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies a scarcity of rains and the drying up of spring waters. And if he should be **oriental** <note>Rising in the east before the sun</note>, it signifies that women who are pregnant in that year will miscarry because of the winds, and also because of sexual intercourse after pregnancy. But if he should be **occidental** <note>Setting in the west after the sun</note>, it signifies rapid fevers in that year, both terrible and trembling. And if he is **retrograde**, it signifies the fear of the king of that region regarding his enemies, lest they come into his territory against him. If indeed he should be **direct**, it signifies for that king the overcoming of his enemies and his own strength against them.

### Chapter 69: On Capricorn

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Capricorn, depicted as a sea-goat (a creature with the body of a goat and the tail of a fish).</image-desc>

Moreover, when he is in **Capricorn** and his latitude is **northern**, it signifies a good disposition of the air and a moderation of rains. And if his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies a darkness of the air in winter, and cloudiness and cold. And if he is **oriental**, it signifies evil for the great and the noble in that **revolution** <note>The astrological chart for the beginning of the year</note>, and their terror, and that they will not relate well with the peasants or common people; and that they will share poorly together. But if indeed he should be **occidental**, it signifies a multitude of locusts in the usual regions, and a great heat harming and devastating the harvests. Furthermore, if he should be **retrograde**, it signifies that the peasants or commoners will be mixed together and will be angry with one another. But if he should be **direct**, it signifies a good disposition for the wealthy and the great or noble; and that they will behave well toward everyone and among themselves; and that they will love justice and righteousness and gentleness, and will practice it.

### Chapter 70: On Gemini and its triplicity when Saturn is in it

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Gemini, depicted as two small children standing close together within a circular frame.</image-desc>

If indeed he should be in **Gemini** or its **triplicity** <note>A group of three signs of the same element; for Gemini, this includes Libra and Aquarius</note>, it signifies that whatever he has signified—whether it be good or evil—that sign will for the most part appear to those in the West. But if he should be in Gemini and is **direct in an angle** <note>The most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note>, it signifies the weight of northern winds and the cold of the winter of that year. And according to **Albumasar** <note>The Latinized name of Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astronomer and astrologer</note>, there will be loss and a decrease in birds, and illnesses from cold and dryness will happen to men in whatever mixture of hot and moist; and men will be

There will also be an impediment from these lightnings and fiery sparks occurring in the air under the stars. And if he should be **retrograde**, it signifies conflicts of kings and nobles and the great or the wealthy; and death will be feared over him in that year or in that revolution; for that reason, it signifies a coming earthquake in the same year. And if he should be **removed from an angle**, winds will be multiplied, both oriental and occidental. And Albumasar said it also signifies the severity of cold, and men will be in states of change. But if with this he should be **retrograde**, men will similarly be in motion <note>Possibly referring to travel or displacement</note>; and there will be illnesses from the winds and showers, dews and frost. If, however, he should be **falling** <note>original: "cadens", referring to a "cadent" house, which is astrologically weak</note> and not aspecting the **ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, and should be **direct**, these things will happen in the regions which are in the division of the sign in which Saturn then resides; and the winds will be multiplied from the southern division. But if he should be **direct**, these things will happen by fortune without weakness; and illnesses and dissolutions and fractures and plunderings will fall upon the citizens who are in the division of the predicted sign; and these things will happen more and more strongly to the peasants and commoners and low-born persons. And Albumasar said: if Saturn should be in an **earthly angle** and is the **Lord of the Year** <note>The planet that rules the chart for the year's beginning</note> in the said triplicity; or if he is not the Lord of the Year but receives the disposition of the Lord of the Ascendant of that revolution, it signifies that in the same year and in the predicted places many men will die from an earthquake. If, however, he receives the disposition of the Lord of the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the sky at the time of the chart</note>, it signifies wars and conflicts in the seeking of a kingdom or other dignity, or the lessening of the district of some city or land of a great man, which another will want to take from him by force. And he said it signifies a multitude of waters and the flooding of rivers and drownings; and also a multitude of snows; and harm to the grain harvest; and there will be a multitude of winds, and death is signified among men. And if his **latitude** should be **northern**, it signifies a violent blowing of the winds and darkness of the air and its corruption and the changing of its color to a <note>unclear: "latunẽ nẽ gredinis", possibly "nigredinem" (blackness) or "latitudinem" (breadth/density) of hail</note>; it also signifies earthquakes, and especially in the parts of the sign in which he himself resides. If, however, his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies the heat of the air and its dryness; also a scarcity of rains; and a multitude of pestiferous and mortal plagues. If, however, he is **oriental**, it signifies coming illnesses for the great men of the land of Babylon and for their king. If indeed he is **occidental**, it signifies dryness of the air and a scarcity of rains, and this if he is **direct**; for if he is **retrograde**, he will harm exceedingly.

And if his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies the goodness of the air and sweetness...

### Chapter Seventy-Two: On Aquarius when Saturn is in it

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting the zodiac sign Aquarius as a man standing in a landscape, pouring water from a large jar held in his hands.</image-desc>

If indeed **Saturn** should be in **Aquarius** and his **latitude** <note>The angular distance of a planet north or south of the path of the sun</note> should be **northern**, it signifies a multitude of rains and the severity of cold and frost. And if his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies a scarcity of the waters of springs and rivers. And if he should be **oriental**, it signifies a scarcity in the acquisition of inheritances and a scarcity of the wealth of the peasants. And if he should be **occidental**, it signifies a multitude of burning heat and strength. And if he should be **retrograde**, it signifies the severity of that same thing. And if he should be **direct**, it signifies the death of animals which men use for their utility <note>Livestock and work animals</note>.

### Chapter Seventy-Three: On Cancer and the Triplicity when Saturn is the Lord of the Revolution and is in it or its Triplicity

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Cancer, shown as a crab with large claws and several legs on each side.</image-desc>

If, however, **Saturn** should be the lord of the year and be in **Cancer** or in its **triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; for Cancer, these are the water signs: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>, **Albumasar** said that whatever he signifies, whether good or evil, will be in the northern part. But if he should be in Cancer, it signifies a multiplication of waters and rains and of the fish of those places, and a sudden upheaval of the earth. And if **Mars** does not **aspect** <note>Form a specific geometric angle with</note> him, the cold will be heavy, and locusts will multiply, and there will be illnesses in the lands that are in the division of the sign in which Saturn is, and the sign which is in its opposition or fourth aspect <note>A square or 90-degree angle</note>. And if he should be **retrograde**, death will be feared for the king of that region. If, however, **Mars** aspects him without the aspect of the **fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</note>, it signifies mortality in the aforementioned land, and evil and hindrance will multiply. If, however, he does not aspect the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, rains and dews and cold will multiply. But if he should be **direct**, the evil will be lessened, and all the more so if any of the fortunes aspect him, unless the **Moon** should then be in the first house, since that signifies a hindrance of misfortunes upon the kings and nobles of that region, and death. If, however, he should be **retrograde** and **Mars** aspects him, it signifies destruction and evil in the land of the aforementioned sign and its opposition and fourth aspect, and also locusts. And if he should be **falling** <note>Located in a weak house of the astrological chart</note>, not aspecting the ascendant, and should be **direct**, and Mars is falling from him, it signifies the security of men, and all the better if he has already passed the 15th degree of the sign; yet there will be illnesses in the land of that sign. And if he should be **retrograde** and Mars aspects him, and the fortunes are absent from him, tribulations and evils will happen to the low-born of those regions, and the cold will be heavy; waters and locusts will multiply. And Albumasar said there will be a hindrance in the water from shipwreck <column-break/> and from the breaking of ships, and those traveling upon the waters will perish; the animals of the water and things similar to these will die. He said that if he is well-disposed without the hindrance of the sign, let the good of those things I have said go forth, and the conversion of evil into good, and the fittingness in all their substances is his significance. And he said: look for the evil that will hinder him, which is **Mars** and the **Tail** <note>The South Node of the Moon, traditionally called the Dragon's Tail or Cauda Draconis</note> by conjunction, and Mars by opposition and by aspect. And he said the property of Saturn is over old wealthy men, Jews, religious people, farmers, the elderly, and the decrepit. For if he should be hindered at the hour of the revolution, judge destruction and hindrance. And if fortunate, judge fortune. And if his **latitude** should be **northern**, it signifies a scarcity of waters and a decrease of rivers and rains. And if his latitude should be **southern**, it signifies the occupation of men in their livelihoods and a scarcity in their acquisitions. And if he should be **oriental**, it signifies the corruption of the air and its darkness and a multitude of cold in its time. And if he should be **occidental**, it signifies a multitude of rains and their corruption and a hindrance of things from the winds. And if he should be **retrograde**, it signifies the strength of those things which have been said; and on account of that region which is in the division of the sign in which Saturn is, it will fall into reproach and very great disgrace, so that no greater evil could happen to it, and it will be compared almost to death. And **Messahala** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari, an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer</note> said there will be a very great war and a powerful death. And if he should be **direct**, it signifies a benevolent disposition of the air and the goodness of its temperament.

### Chapter 76: What Saturn signifies in each house in the revolution of years, whether of the world, of births, or of questions; whether he be the Lord of the Year or not.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting the astrological "Children of Saturn." In the center, Saturn is personified as an elderly bearded man wearing a floppy hat and holding a scythe. He sits in a chariot pulled by two winged dragons or serpents. In the upper right corner of the frame is the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄). Below the chariot wheels, various figures representing different occupations are shown: a man digging with a spade and several others engaged in manual labor or suffering, reflecting the planetary influence of Saturn over the peasantry and hard work.</image-desc>

When Saturn is in the **revolution** <note>the chart cast for the solar return or the beginning of the year</note>, or in a **nativity** <note>a birth chart</note>, or a **question** <note>a chart cast to answer a specific query</note>: In the **first house**, if it be the revolution of the year of the world, it signifies the sorrow of many men because of debt or because of lands. If it be a birth or its revolution or a question, it signifies the same for that person born or for the one asking the question. 

If, however, he should be in the **second house**, it signifies the disturbance of friends in that year, and men shall lose and suffer a decrease of their goods. 

If indeed he should be in the **third house**, it signifies quarrels and discords to come between brothers more than usual. 

And if he should be in the **fourth house**, it signifies the destruction of buildings, the depopulation of lands, the loss of crops and treasures, and danger from winds because of them, and death. 

And if he should be in the **fifth house**, it signifies more miscarriages in 그 year than usual, the loss of children and sorrows because of them, and contentions with messengers and ambassadors, and that they shall not perform their duties well in that year. 

And if he should be in the **sixth house**, it signifies the ill-will of male and female servants toward their masters and their disobedience, as well as many infirmities and harm to smaller animals. 

If indeed he should be in the **seventh house** and the sign be feminine and its lord be a feminine planet, it signifies the ill-will of women toward men and their disobedience. And if the sign be masculine or its lord be a masculine planet, it signifies the ill-will of men toward their wives, the fraud of partners, and the injury of enemies against absent enemies rather than openly, and tribulation because of lands, and for the most part, a detestable end to affairs. You should say the same if he is found thus in births or questions. 

And if he should be in the **eighth house**, it signifies lawsuits because of claims for inheritances or the remains of the dead and because of claims for ancient things, and sorrow because of death; and it signifies things whose pain, anguish, or sadness shall last a long time. 

But if he should be in the **ninth house**, it signifies a lessening of faith and the taking away of mercy and piety; and that certain hermits or religious people shall be changed from their religious orders and shall abandon them and take up evil counsels for themselves and others likewise; and certain men shall labor in vile and horrible things involving the property of others—such as those who pull the dead from their graves and strip them. It signifies sorrows, sadness, and anxieties to come upon those traveling on their pilgrimages and long delays for them. 

If indeed he should be in the **tenth house**, it signifies—in births or questions as well as in other revolutions—sorrow, sadness, attractions, and burdens on the part of the king or powers, and the complexity of prison. And **Albumasar** said that if the Sun is the lord of the tenth house, the king shall kill him in his prison. And

<column-break/>

if the Moon should be the mistress of the 10th house, it signifies the same as the Sun, unless she be joined to Saturn. 

And if the lord of the 10th house be **Jupiter**, the king shall kill him and do him injury without fault. 

And if the lord of the tenth house be **Mars**, he shall perish by his own fault. 

And if the lord of the 10th house be **Venus**, it signifies that prosperity, high status, joy, and profit shall follow from this tribulation, and the king shall repent having done this and shall confess that he did not do well and shall humble himself toward him. 

And if the lord of the 10th house be **Mercury**, he shall kill him out of injury or reason when he bears false witness against him. And if Mercury should **aspect** <note>be in a specific angular relationship with</note> Mars, he shall be struck with whips. And if Mercury should be with the Sun under his rays, the king shall use force against him and take away his substance, and then make a restoration of his goods to him. And know that this property belongs to Saturn in the 10th house among the other planets. 

And if he should be in the **11th house**, it signifies sorrow and sadness from friends and with friends, and a scarcity of profit in those things he hoped for and in which he had confidence for good, and involvement in difficult affairs and their hardness, and a multitude of confidence in false things which profit nothing. 

And if he should be in the **12th house**, it signifies impediments which happen on the part of the king or another ruler; it also signifies that he shall be captured by enemies, and there shall be cause for fear in all his affairs. And according to what I touched upon for you above, all these things can be considered in the revolutions of the years of the world, in the revolutions of births, in questions, and similar things in all chapters and in each one by itself. And as it is with Saturn, so it is with every other planet, both in good and in evil.

### Chapter 77: On the conjunction of Saturn and Mars in a revolution, and what it signifies.

Look also in the revolution—whether the revolution of the year be of the world or of a birth—if **Saturn** and **Mars** should be **conjoined** <note>occupying the same degree of the zodiac</note> in any of the 12 houses, for it signifies burdens and impediments according to the significations of the house in which they are conjoined. 

For if their conjunction should be in the **first house**, it signifies universal evil and impediment to come upon the peasants and the common people. 

If it should be in the **second house** from the **ascendant** <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the revolution, it signifies the destruction of wealth and of the houses themselves, and the rich and great men shall fall into the forgetfulness of the people and shall be regarded as almost nothing; and their household members and servants shall be exalted, as well as their soldiers, and they shall be proud against them and will not wish to obey them nor keep faith with them, except for a little, or rather almost none at all.

But if it should be in the **fourth house**, it signifies the destruction of buildings and dwellings or houses. 

If, however, it should be in the **fifth house**, it signifies destruction and impediment to fall upon children, and more miscarriages in that year than usual, and a change in the will of friends toward one another and even of persons who love one another; and in the place of love, weariness and ill-will shall fall between them. 

If indeed it should be in the **sixth house**, it signifies impediment and loss to fall upon the smaller and larger four-footed animals, especially those which men use, such as oxen, horses, donkeys, camels, and the like; and upon male and female servants and attendants; it also signifies infirmities. 

If indeed it should be in the **seventh house**, it signifies that quarrels, contentions, and discords shall fall, and likewise dissensions and many evils between partners and other associates, and even between husbands and wives, and enmities shall rise up between men against each other. 

If indeed it should be in the **eighth house**, it signifies that many men shall leave their...

## Chapter 78: What Jupiter signifies in the revolution in each sign and in each triplicity when he is the Lord of the Year, and in each house whether he is the Lord of the Year or not.

<image-desc>Woodcut depicting two figures in a chariot pulled by two eagles. The figure in front is holding the reins. The figure behind is crowned and holding a scepter, with the astrological symbol for Jupiter (♃) above them. To the left, a small figure stands holding a staff.</image-desc>

When Jupiter is the **Lord of the Year** <note>the planet ruling the sign on the ascendant of the year's start chart</note> and is in **Aries** or in its **triplicity** <term>a group of three signs belonging to the same element; for Aries, these are the Fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</term>, it signifies the appearance of religions in the eastern parts over which the sign in which he is located presides. Especially when he is in Aries, it signifies the appearance of [religious] sects, and the observation of divine precepts, justice, and good works in that **revolution** <note>the astrological chart for the year</note>. It also signifies a multitude of winds from the east, the cold of winter, and rains—though not destructive—as well as the flooding of rivers, the suitability of vineyards and trees, and that the granaries will be good. 

And if Jupiter is then of good condition and well-disposed, it signifies a multitude of resources for the wealthy of the regions over which he presides, and their goodness, joy, and cheerfulness, and a gathering of common people or peasants toward the rich, noble, and great. 

And **Albumasar** said if he is hindered or of evil condition, it signifies the opposite of those things which were said. And he said: know that

<column-break/>

the work in the matter of Jupiter and the **aspect** <note>the geometric relationship between planets</note> of the planets toward him is just like the work in the matter of Saturn equally. 

And he said: Jupiter is the significator of nobles, judges, bishops, consuls, religious men, and citizens of the various sects. And if he is hindered, everything that belongs to him will suffer detriment. And know that if he is in human signs <note>signs depicted as humans, like Gemini or Virgo</note> or fire signs, he will signify the delight of the wealthy and the smallness of their donations, the preservation of their orders, and their anxieties toward their relatives; also the destruction of the kingdom of **Babylon** and of the **Arabs**, a scarcity of resources, and curiosity. This will be upon the citizens of the cities that are in the division of the sign into which Jupiter has descended. There will be a practice of lying among the common people with the assent of evil or injuries, illnesses of the body, and the weakening of acquisitions.

### Chapter 79: Concerning his existence in Leo.

### Chapter 80: Concerning his existence in Sagittarius.

And if he is **direct** <note>moving forward</note>, it signifies a multitude of fish and of animals living in the waters and their safety.

### Chapter 81: What Jupiter signifies in each revolution of the year, both of the world and of nativities or questions, whether he be the Lord of the Year or not.

<image-desc>Woodcut of Jupiter in a chariot pulled by two eagles, holding a scepter, with the symbol ♃ clearly visible.</image-desc>

And when Jupiter is in the revolution, whether in a **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> or a **question** <note>a chart for a specific query</note>: if it is the revolution of the year of the world, it establishes in that year that men shall revere one another as is fitting for each according to his status. They shall preserve honesty, beauty, cleanliness, faith, and religion; and they shall spend the time in discipline and reason, and the end of their intention will be to labor in those things which pertain to salvation.

And it signifies the well-being of the wealthy, the magnates, and the nobles, and the usefulness of things in which men place their trust for good.

And if it should be in the **sixth**, it signifies good and profit in four-legged animals, and especially in the smaller ones, such as sheep and the like; and it signifies the safety of persons and a scarcity of infirmities, except in regions and places that are naturally sickly; nevertheless, in those places infirmities shall be diminished; and it signifies usefulness from male and female servants, and the obedience of attendants.

If however it should be in the **seventh**, it signifies usefulness, good, and joy on the part of women, and marriage or nuptials, and good on the part of partners and their fidelity; and it also signifies victory over those enemies in that region; and also for the native or the querent.

If truly it should be in the **eighth**, it signifies the removal of an evil and suspicious death universally in that region, if it be the revolution of the world's year. If, however, it be the revolution of a birth or a question, it signifies that there is evil for the native or the seeker that shall come to him because of enemies; and that he himself shall fall into their hands unless he guards himself well; and that gravity and hindrance shall follow from it; yet in the end it shall terminate in an endurable conclusion that will not be evil, but rather may in some way be praised.

And if it should be in the **ninth**, it signifies profitable journeys, especially long and useful ones in that year; and there shall be faith and honesty and good among men; and there shall be dreams, many of which are true; and the interpretation of dreams shall fall according to the nature of the planet which then separates from Jupiter, or from which Jupiter itself is separated, if it be separated from any; and according to the nature of those significators, the dreams in that revolution are to be explained; and this can also have a place in other dreams.

If truly it should be in the **tenth**, it signifies the accumulation of substances and their collection, and men shall desire to be praised, and they shall praise anyone worthy of praise according to their station, and honesty shall flourish among them.

If however it should be in the **eleventh**, it signifies praise and good fame on the part of friends, and that men shall rejoice; and they shall be in high spirits, and there shall be a good effect and progress in things in which men have confidence and from which they hope for good.

If indeed it should be in the **twelfth**, it signifies obstacles that occur on the part of servitude; and it signifies poverties and needs; and it signifies gravity that occurs on the part of servants and by their occasion; and also on the part of the servitude into which men fall; and they shall be saddened by the accidents that come to them by occasion of four-legged animals, and especially large animals such as horses, oxen, and the like.

<column-break/>

# Chapter 82. What Mars signifies when he is the
## lord of the year in each triplicity, and in each
## sign, and each house, whether he be the lord
## of the year or not.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the planetary deity Mars. Mars is depicted as a knight in full plate armor with a crested helmet, riding in a chariot drawn by two galloping horses. In his right hand, he brandishes a sword, and in his left, he holds a circular shield featuring the image of a scorpion. The astrological symbol for Mars (♂) is positioned above the horses. Below this scene is a separate woodcut showing a ram, the symbol for the zodiac sign Aries.</image-desc>

When Mars is the **Lord of the Year** and is in **Aries** or in its **triplicity** <note>The "Fiery Triplicity" includes Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>, it signifies strong winds and many various changes of the air in eastern parts; it also signifies pains of the eyes and a scarcity of rain; and it signifies war in those same parts and an abundance of provisions <note>original: "annone," referring to the grain supply</note>. It also signifies in those same parts, in the cities over which he rules and those in the division of Aries, that evil is to come, along with anger, injury, and strife.

It signifies victory in war for the leaders of those cities and the inhabitants of those regions over their enemies who come from other parts to those places for the sake of harming them; and their subjugation; and it signifies their army and their region in martial matters; and that fathers and the more nobly born <note>original: "ingenuiores"</note> shall teach and instruct their sons and other youths in wrestling and the exercise of wars.

And if Mars is then in a **good state**, it signifies to the citizens or the aforesaid inhabitants, or to their king, victory over their enemies; and that they shall obtain all things that are extended to them; and it signifies the greatness of his heart, and also that they will be quickly and swiftly changeable in will toward the undertaking of matters. It also signifies that the peasants and his subjects shall love and revere him and obey him, each according to his station.

And if Mars is the Lord of the Year and the Lord of the Ascendant, and is in a good state and not impeded <note>meaning the planet is not "afflicted" by negative aspects from other planets</note>: it signifies that in that same year there will be fertility and it will be a rainy year; and there shall be pestilences and earthquakes; and there shall be few men <note>original: "modicum ho:" likely "modicum hominum"</note>; and in the same year there shall be joy and gladness, and laborers and those who carry arms shall fight and find good; and there shall be war and contention near the king of that region.

**If however he be in an evil state**, it signifies a scarcity of success against his enemies, and that it will be enough for them if they can protect themselves from them; indeed, it shall rather seem that the enemies obtain or overcome them; and it signifies that the king will not be well established over the matters he ought to exercise—especially over noble, useful, and just matters—nor will he keep his secrets well; rather, he will make them known and will exercise his operations in martial matters more than in others.

**And if his latitude be Northern**, it signifies heat of the air and a scarcity of rain.
**If however his latitude be Southern**, it signifies thunders, lightning-flashes, and bolts of lightning.
**And if he be Oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note>, it signifies wars about to fall between the rich, the magnates, and the nobles.
**And if he be Occidental** <note>setting after the Sun</note>, it signifies disturbances and fears coming upon men.
**And if he be Retrograde**, it signifies infirmities of the eyes and of the whole human body.
**And if he be Direct**, it signifies a multitude of hypocrites who will appear in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they shall be... <meta>catchword: ravening wolves</meta>

### ¶ Chapter eighty-three: when Mars shall be in Leo.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of a lion (the zodiac sign Leo) facing toward the left.</image-desc>

If Mars should be in **Leo**, it signifies wars and contentions, and a scarcity of grain <note>original: "annone," referring to the yearly harvest or grain supply</note> in eastern parts. There shall be death among men, and especially among young men from 40 up to 50 years of age; among children, however, this shall be a sleep <note>original: "somnus"; likely a euphemism for death or a specific sleeping sickness</note>. And if its latitude should be northern, it signifies a scarcity of waters. If, however, its latitude should be southern, it signifies a multitude of waters in springs and rivers. And if it should be in the east <note>rising</note>, it signifies a hindrance to the animals which men use and the like. And if it should be in the west <note>setting</note>, it signifies a scarcity of fish and the death of animals living in the waters. And if it should be retrograde <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, it signifies a hindrance and burden that shall fall upon the wealthy and the great nobles. And if it should be direct <note>moving forward</note>, it signifies the blowing of western winds, and ships at sea shall be saved.

### ¶ Chapter eighty-four: when Mars shall be in Sagittarius.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Sagittarius, depicted as a centaur archer aiming a bow and arrow to the right.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in **Sagittarius**, it signifies a future war in western parts; and there shall be a scarcity of wine in those parts; and there shall be evil hindrance and death in the dwellings of those regions and among merchants. There shall be infirmities, coughs, and pains of the eyes; and there will be worms killing children and harming others as well. It signifies a scarcity of rains and shall generate cold in its proper seasons, so much so that for that reason trees, herbs, and grain shall be devastated; and bees shall suffer detriment in that revolution <note>the astrological cycle of the year</note>. If he <note>Mars</note> should be well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies good for the authors of wars, counselors, and those who carry arms for the sake of warring, and for warriors; also for those who seek injustice and those who cut off the roads <note>highwaymen</note>, as these people consider such things to be their own good. 

And **Albumasar** <note>a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer known in Europe as Albumasar</note> said that if Mars should be in the "human signs"—which are Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the last half of Sagittarius, and Aquarius—it signifies a multitude of wars and strife; and men shall rise up against their king in opposition to him. It also signifies sudden death, tertian fevers <note>fevers that return every three days</note>, and other strong and heavy fevers, as well as a multitude of infirmities. It also means many highwaymen, the shedding of human blood, conflagrations, and lightning. If, however, he should be ill-disposed, it signifies a malice in all the aforesaid things that is heavier, worse, and more harmful, unless **Jupiter** works against it. 

If his latitude should be northern, it signifies the goodness of the air and its beauty. And if his latitude should be southern, it signifies the profit of merchants and the beauty of their gain. And if he should be in the east, it signifies peace, quiet, and security; and there shall be few or no wars. And if he should be in the west, it signifies the salvation of trees and a multitude of fruits. And if he should be retrograde, it signifies coughs coming to men and pains in the back parts of the head. If, however, he should be direct, it signifies pestilences coming to the animals that dwell near the seashores.

<column-break/>

### ¶ Chapter eighty-five: concerning another wicked significance of Mars.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the god Mars as a king sitting in a horse-drawn chariot, holding a sword and a shield. The astrological symbol for Mars (♂) is shown in the upper right corner of the frame.</image-desc>

One must also observe in the revolution of the years of the world <note>the annual chart for the world</note> whether Mars is in **Gemini** or not. For if Mars should be in Gemini in the revolution of the year, and Gemini should be the **ninth house**, and the lower planets follow him, it signifies that the **Roman Church** shall take up the temporal sword <note>secular military or political power</note> in that year and shall exercise it; and there shall be the shedding of the blood of Christians, both the innocent and the guilty. 

When Mars shall be in the **first [house]** in the revolution of the year—whether he is the Lord of the Year or not—whenever there is a revolution, whether of the world or of a birth, it signifies a horror coming to men, whether to the native <note>the person born under the chart</note> or the querent <note>the person asking the astrologer a question</note> in that year: sadness, fear, contrarieties, and contentions. Men shall strive in taking away substance from one another; that is, things that do not belong to them, using ingenuity and craftiness without reason and without any praiseworthy manner. 

And if he should be in the **second [house]**, it signifies the taking away of things through injustice and without reason; and there shall be poverty and want, a cause inducing them to do this. Servants and ministers shall disturb their masters or those with whom they live or dwell. Some have wished to say that Mars in the second house is not to be blamed; they showed that it signifies trade, but I have not found this to be certain that I can remember. 

And if he should be in the **third [house]**, it signifies wrath, hatred, enmity, and opposition and contention falling between brothers and younger relatives by blood; for because of these things they shall kill one another on slight occasion; and this is more powerful if the third house should be **Capricorn** or **Aquarius**. 

And **Albumasar** said: if the third house should be from the houses of **Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, it signifies joy from brothers and sisters. And if it should be from the houses of **Jupiter** <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, it signifies a multitude of wealth and the acquisition of merchants. And if it should be from the houses of **Saturn** <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, it signifies the despoiling of the dead placed in tombs, the digging through of walls, and the taking of other things by way of robbery. It signifies the labor of men in gaining and extorting money from wherever they can by way of illicit lordship, by false testimonies, and by malicious and fraudulent words; and men shall suffer dangers and tribulations. 

And if it should be the house of the **Moon** <note>Cancer</note>, it signifies robberies and the digging through of walls so that for that reason things are stolen and snatched away through wickedness; and thieves shall be secure and bold in stealing; for they shall steal in the marketplace and in places of trade, not only in the night but even in the day. 

And if it should be the house of the **Sun** <note>Leo</note>, it signifies highwaymen, robberies, and plundering in villages, and sometimes in cities and other dwellings, and even in the inns of those hosting foreigners and pilgrims. 

And **Albumasar** said: know that this is the property of Mars among the other planets. And if he should be in the **fourth [house]**, it signifies death and destruction from sickness, and being cut down by the sword, and the shedding of blood and the suspicion of it; and these things shall end in the south from whatever part they look, and in the west; and the beginning of the principal tribulation shall be more from the north.

And if Mars is positioned in the fifth house <note>The fifth house traditionally governs children, pleasure, and procreation.</note>, it signifies fornications in that year, and that many children will be born from them, many of whom will be considered legitimate even though they are the product of adultery; their parents will gain little or nothing from them. The livelihood of the people for that year will be forthcoming. And if it is in the sixth house, it signifies hot diseases such as hot and dry fevers, which will be moved by corrupt blood and by bile <note>original: "colera," one of the four humors</note> coming upon people in that revolution of the year. It also signifies sorrows and sadness occurring on account of male and female servants and attendants, and for other reasons signified by the sixth house. And if it is in the seventh house, it signifies contentions, oppositions, and disturbances in all things, and loss for that reason; it also signifies trade conducted with fraud and deception, and sorrow and sadness therein. And if it is in the eighth house <note>The eighth house is the house of death and inheritance.</note>, it signifies the acquisition of the property of the dead among some people, and this is true both in the revolutions of births <note>individual birth charts</note> or questions, as well as in the revolutions of the years of the world; and justice shall be done for those acquiring them for that reason. Yet they shall lose them after their acquisition and fall into poverty and want. It also signifies the killing and mutilation or loss of limbs—namely the hands and feet—and they shall fall into great shame and a reproach that is most foul and blameworthy. And if it is in the ninth house <note>The ninth house governs religion and long journeys.</note>, it signifies a decline in the status of religious people; it also signifies a demand for horses and arms for the purpose of fighting and waging war; and men will seek out wars and desire to set up camp and go out in armies. It also signifies drinking, drunkenness, and a lack of restraint from dishonest and illicit acts; and men will be very unfaithful and liars, and they will strive to interpret dreams, but will interpret them falsely. And if it is in the tenth house <note>The tenth house governs kings, authority, and public life.</note>, it signifies tribulation coming to peasants and common people from the king or from the wealthy and powerful; it signifies wounds and blows of swords and floggings, and anguish from these things, and imprisonment, and a shortage or lack of food. It also signifies wars and contentions over things that do not belong to those who seek them, nor pertain to them. And if it is in the eleventh house, it signifies a scarcity of profit or progress in things where utility is hoped for, and that people will fall into the enmity of friends; it signifies a loss of wealth, and men will despair over things in which they had trust and hope. And if it is in the twelfth house <note>The twelfth house is associated with hidden enemies and prisons.</note>, it signifies cleverness in robbery and similar things, and laziness and delay in things that should and could be done. It signifies a loss of men’s wealth and signifies sorrow and sadness coming on account of large animals, both those that are ridden and those that are not—unless God turns it away.

### Chapter eighty-six: on what Mars signifies in Taurus.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Taurus, depicted as a bull facing right, emerging from behind a stylized architectural element or gate.</image-desc>

And if Mars is in **Taurus** or in its triplicity <note>The Earth Triplicity: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.</note>, the things it signifies will appear in southern regions and at sea, especially if it is in Taurus. For it then signifies strong winds to come and the destruction of crops that are in the places where they should be harvested; similarly, it signifies the destruction of trees, and this because of heat exceeding the proper and natural measure. It also signifies a multitude of clouds and mists, as well as rains, thunder, and lightning. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a famous Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to Western medieval astrology.</note> said it signifies the death of women and cows, and it signifies wars to come between the citizens of the East and the citizens of the West. It also signifies pain in the eyes, more in the left than the right, and more common in women than in men; nor will the cultivation of lands be very profitable, and there shall be a scarcity of grain. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies a multitude of rains and a goodness of herbs and utility from them. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies a multitude of northern winds. And if it is oriental <note>rising in the East before the sun</note>, it signifies peace to come in that revolution in the parts of Babylon and in western parts, and the security of those citizens. And if it is occidental <note>setting in the West after the sun</note>, it signifies a multitude of illnesses and death. And if it is retrograde, it signifies illnesses of children. And Albumasar said if it is direct, it signifies the hatred of women.

<column-break/>

### Chapter eighty-seven: on Mars when it shall be in Virgo.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Virgo, depicted as a winged female figure holding a branch or sheaf of grain in each hand.</image-desc>

And if Mars is in **Virgo**, it signifies battles and the shedding of blood in northern parts; it also signifies pains of the eyes and an abundance of grain, wine, and butter. And Albumasar said it also signifies mortality among women. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies impediments in the bodies of men, and women and harvests shall suffer damage. And if its latitude is southern, then it signifies the safety of women. And if it is oriental, it signifies the death of old men. And if occidental, it signifies the blowing of winds in the regions of Spain. And if it is retrograde, it signifies wars to come between men. And if it is direct, it signifies honesty and the well-being of the wealthy and great nobles.

### Chapter eighty-eight: on Mars in Capricorn.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Capricorn, depicted as a sea-goat (a goat with a curled fish tail) facing right.</image-desc>

And if Mars is in **Capricorn**, it signifies wars, looting, and the tribulation of death among young men; likewise, it signifies gusts of wind in eastern parts. It also signifies in those same parts rains and an increase of grain, butter, and ointment; and the aforementioned wars shall be between the citizens of the East and the citizens of the West. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies a multitude of snow at the proper and customary times. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies the heat of the air in its proper times and its darkness. And if it is oriental, it signifies the killing of the **Emperor of the Romans**. And this is more certain if the Moon is in the eighth house or joined to the Lord of the eighth, or if Mars itself is in an angle <note>One of the four pivotal houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th.</note> since the Moon is his natural indicator wherever she is joined to him. And it is even more certain if she is joined with him in the eighth house or if the Lord of the eighth house aspects her from an opposition or a square aspect. And even more certainly and infallibly so if there is mutual reception <note>An astrological condition where two planets are in each other's signs of dignity.</note> between them, or at least if the Moon receives the Lord of the eighth. Nor could Jupiter working alone prevent this; for only God could turn this away. And if Mars is occidental, it signifies pustules and also anthrax <note>original: "antraces," referring to carbuncles or skin ulcers</note> and the like falling upon the bodies of men. And if it is retrograde, it signifies a scarcity of grain. And if it is direct, it signifies an abundance of wine and oil.

### Chapter eighty-nine: on Gemini and its triplicity.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting the zodiac sign Gemini, shown as two winged figures (angels or youths) standing side-by-side.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in Gemini or in its triplicity <note>The Air triplicity consists of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>, it signifies that whatever it indicates, those events will occur in western regions. But if it is specifically in Gemini, it signifies obstacles falling upon people because of thunder and lightning; a scarcity of rain; and a severity of heat and its intensity. There will be wars, contentions, and robberies in northern parts. Their king will be exalted during the revolution <note>The "revolution of the year" refers to the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to cast a chart for the coming year.</note> of those regions; they shall have victory over their enemies; and there will be ear pains among children and outbreaks of carbuncles <note>original: "anthraculū," referring to inflamed, boil-like sores</note> and similar ailments. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies a multitude of rains. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies a scarcity of water in springs and rivers. And if it is oriental <note>Rising in the east before the sun.</note>, it signifies a multitude of pustules and sores on children. And if it is occidental <note>Setting in the west after the sun.</note>, it signifies an impediment to advocates <note>original: "pistillatoꝝ," likely a variant of "postulatorum," meaning legal petitioners or advocates.</note> and scribes, as well as to the judiciary and decurions <note>Local administrative officials in the Roman style.</note>, and their hiding or flight. And if it is retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky.</note>, it signifies dissension among religious people and diversity among their sects. And if it is direct, it signifies that men will reveal both their own secrets and those of others, nor will they keep them well.

### Chapter ninety: when Mars shall be in Libra.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a pair of balance scales, representing the zodiac sign Libra.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in Libra, it signifies winds to come, and infirmities and mortality in the cities or regions that fall under the division of Libra; and this will be more among men than among women. And Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a highly influential Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to European medieval astrology.</note> says: if Mars is there, it brings rains, winds, clouds, and mists. It also signifies that there will be infirmity and mortality in southern parts; there will be little wine, butter, and ointment; and thieves and those who lie in wait on the roads will multiply. There will be brawls and evils among men, and there will be fears, tremors, and terrors among them. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies lightning and flashes that will come and appear in that year or in that revolution. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies sicknesses in men on the left side of the body. And if it is oriental, it signifies future wars and contentions between the rich and the great. And if it is occidental, it signifies the safety of the rich, the great, the scribes of letters, and the wise. And if it is retrograde, it signifies stomach ailments for the rich, the great, the scribes, the judges, and the wise. And if it is direct, it signifies that the wills of the rich and the great or the nobles will differ among themselves.

### Chapter ninety-one: when Mars shall be in Aquarius.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the zodiac sign Aquarius, depicted as a man walking and pouring water from a large jug.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in Aquarius, it signifies hardships and tribulations coming to people in that revolution. Snow, rain, and cold will abound in their seasons; and grain, wine, and butter will be diminished in western parts and in the land called the "land of merchants" <note>original: "negodotatorum," a misspelling of "negotiatorum."</note>. It also signifies the death or

<column-break/>

change of the king or the ruler of that region in which you calculate the revolution of the year. And Albumasar said: if Venus then aspects <note>Forms a geometric relationship in the sky.</note> it while ascending through the north, it signifies a good spring; but wine will be scarce. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies a multitude of snow and cold in its proper seasons and in the accustomed regions, and locusts in their season. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies a darkening of the air and its thickness, as well as a severity of heat. And if it is oriental, it signifies the well-being of the rich, the great, and the nobles, and their joy and gladness; it also signifies a multitude of branches <note>Indicating lush growth in trees.</note>. And if it is retrograde, it signifies heavy falls <note>Of fruit or trees.</note>, and that obstacles will fall upon the trees for that reason. And if it is direct, it signifies an impediment to trees and a permitted falling upon them; and this is more powerful if the Head of the Dragon <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered a point of increase or intensification.</note> is there or in Gemini.

### Chapter ninety-two: on Mars in Cancer and its triplicity.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a crab, representing the zodiac sign Cancer.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in the revolution of the year in Cancer or its triplicity <note>The Water triplicity consists of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>: with Mars in Cancer, there will be the appearance of what it signifies in northern parts. But in Cancer specifically, it signifies shipwrecks coming suddenly from a strong and sudden blast of winds; it signifies brawl, contention, and war in western parts. Men will be burdened by the payment of taxes <note>original: "tributoz"</note>; and there will be fevers and other infirmities. There will be pains of the throat and chest; heat will be oppressive; and rain will diminish. And Albumasar says it will be a dangerous year, and there will be little ointment, butter, or fat. It also signifies the death of four-footed animals, but especially of horses. And if its latitude is northern, it signifies severe cold in its season and a scarcity of water from springs. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies coming winds and obstacles falling upon the trees. And if it is oriental, it signifies pestilences falling upon the animals of the fields. And if it is occidental, it signifies the care and concern of the common people or peasants and the populace regarding their own business. And if it is retrograde, it signifies wantonness; and that men will take delight and apply themselves to the cult of Venus and commit fornication and the like. And if it is direct, it signifies a good disposition of the air and its beauty and clarity.

### Chapter 93: on Mars in Scorpio.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a scorpion, representing the zodiac sign Scorpio.</image-desc>

And if Mars should be in Scorpio, it signifies a multitude of clouds, a severe cold in winter, and an intemperance of heat in summer, and a scarcity of grain for that reason, and also for the trees. There will be pains of the eyes, and robberies and highwaymen will multiply. Wars, pains, and other infirmities will arise among the youth. There will be a scarcity of wine, butter, and fat; and these things will happen more in northern parts. And if it is in Scorpio and its latitude is northern, it signifies a scarcity of water. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies a multitude of spring waters.

### Chapter 94: When Mars is in Pisces.

And if Mars should be in Pisces, it signifies a multitude of snow and rain, and there will be mortality in southern parts. More fish will be caught in that revolution than usual, but many kingdoms will suffer detriment; it also signifies the killing of kings, the great,

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of two fish swimming in opposite directions, representing the zodiac sign Pisces.</image-desc>

the wealthy, and the noble, and those who are fit for kingship. It also signifies a scarcity of the grain supply <note>original: "annone," referring to the state-regulated grain harvest and distribution</note> such that the market will suffer loss and decrease, and there will be much less than expected. People should hope for the best, but flying animals will suffer harm, such as flies, gadflies, and the like. And **Albumasar** says if Venus aspects <note>Forms a geometric relationship or "look" with</note> the ascendant of the year, death will dwell among humans and there will be pains of the eyes; thunders and lightnings will multiply. It will break the malice of the fruits of the earth, and they shall receive increase. And if its latitude <note>The planet's distance north or south of the ecliptic.</note> is northern, it signifies the goodness of the air and its beauty or purity. And if its latitude is southern, it signifies an abundance of locusts, but they will cause little hindrance. And if it is oriental, it signifies the killing of the wealthy and the great. And if it is occidental, it signifies infirmities falling upon male and female servants, and upon male and female attendants and persons of low status. And **Albumasar** says if it should be retrograde, it signifies safety and profit for merchants. And if it should be direct, it signifies the protection and safety of all small four-footed animals, and of male and female servants, attendants, and persons of low status. 

The wise men of this mastery—and especially that most reverend predecessor of ours, **Albumasar**—did not take care to record the latitudes of any but the three superior planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.</note>, since he did not find the truth as well-tested in the others as in those. Therefore, **Albumasar** says that he sometimes found error in the others, but in the superior planets in no way; wherefore he warns us to be intent upon the latitudes of the superior planets and not the inferior ones.

### Chapter 95: Regarding the Sun, when it is the Lord of the Year, and what it signifies.

When, however, the Sun is the Lord of the Year or of the revolution, and it is well-disposed <note>Ideally placed in its home sign or exalted.</note> and of good fortune—that is, strong and free from hindrance—it signifies the high

It also signifies utility and the profit of those who turn their faces away from things displeasing to God, and from injuries and dishonest things. It also signifies a good appearance for the great and noble, and for those to whom honor is owed by men. ### Chapter 96. What the Sun signifies in each house in the revolution of the years of births and the years of the world, and in births, whether it be the lord of the year or not.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting the personification of the Sun (Sol). A regal figure with a crown and radiant sun rays behind the head sits on an ornate throne, holding a scepter. To the left is a circular emblem showing a lion (Leo), and to the right is a circular emblem showing a ram (Aries).</image-desc>

**W**hen the Sun is in Aries, whether in the <term>revolution<note>The 'Solar Return' or 'Yearly Revolution'—the chart cast for the moment the Sun enters Aries (the new year) or returns to its birth position.</note></term> of a birth or a year of the world, in the first house, it signifies leadership, loftiness, and the greatness of the king or the person born; likewise, in the revolution of the years of the world, it signifies the state and increase of good for whichever year has been revolved, unless Saturn and Mars—or either of them—work against it and exist in a malicious state. ¶ And if it should be in the second house, it signifies a gathering among people and their becoming respectable; yet there will be some blemishes of the eyes. ¶ And in the third house, it signifies a change from one region to another, and that the king of 그 region will accomplish his affairs and those of his subjects for the better and in a good way; likewise, the person born will accomplish his affairs through the favor of the king. ¶ In the fourth house, however, it signifies praise among men, their loftiness, and honor; and things that had long remained hidden and had not appeared will come to light; it also signifies the discovery of treasures, or their accumulation or acquisition. ¶ In the fifth house, it signifies a change of status for many people because of children; and the person born will change his status because of his own son and will be respected by the people; and common people will respect the affairs of the wicked and honor them; there will also be joy because of gifts. ¶ In the sixth house, it signifies infirmities and losses because of servants and other things that are signified by the sixth house; and it signifies that peasants or the low-born will envy those greater than themselves; likewise for the person born. ¶ And in the seventh house, it signifies opposition that will happen to the common folk from the nobles, or the great, or the kings. The same things will likewise happen to the person born. ¶ In the eighth house, it signifies the depression of the wealthy and the great, or the nobles and the powerful, and their diminution, death, and reproach. ¶ In the ninth house, it signifies a good disposition of the minds of men toward themselves, and in thoughts pleasing to God and in those things which pertain to faith. ¶ In the tenth house, it signifies the honor of kings and their exaltation, glory, and progress. ¶ In the eleventh house, it signifies joy and gladness of men because of friends and mutual love among themselves, and concerning things in which there is a trust of good; likewise, this will happen to the person born from these things, and good from the great ones who are below the king. ¶ In the twelfth house, however, it signifies the diminution and depression of the wealthy and the noble great; also their death and the taking away of their dignities, and injuries to be brought upon them by the low-born; and it signifies oppositions that will happen to the person born from his enemies and also from others, and more from the base than from the great.

### Chapter 97. Concerning Venus when she is the lady of the year, what it signifies.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of Venus. She is depicted as a classical goddess in a chariot drawn by two birds (doves). Above her flies a small winged Cupid with a bow and arrow. To the left is a zodiac sign for Libra (scales) and to the right is the sign for Taurus (bull). The chariot wheels appear to contain astrological symbols.</image-desc>

**W**hen Venus is the <term>Lady of the Year<note>The planet ruling the astrological chart for the start of the year.</note></term> and she is good and well-disposed, it signifies a good condition and is a sign for women, both adults and girls, both those who have known men and virgins; likewise also for eunuchs. And if she is the Lady of the Year and the Lady of the Ascendant, and is free from impediments and from evils, it signifies a year of security and quietude; they will be fit for the king, and there will be good in honors, justice, generosity, righteousness, and peace. But if she is <term>received<note>original: "recepta"—a condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting hospitality or cooperation.</note></term>, peasants will find good from kings, the wealthy, and the great; and peasants will love their king and obey him; and marriages will multiply, and there will be joy and liveliness for women. But if she is hindered, it signifies little good in that year, and there will be earthquakes in various lands from which buildings will fall; and there will be war, though slight, and sadness for the king of that region; and these things will happen in the designated region and its climate. If indeed she is hindered at the hour of the revolution, it signifies an impediment and evil for all the aforesaid things. <margin>¶ And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous Persian astrologer.</note> said: if she is in human signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>, she will hinder whatever belongs to her among men. If she is in earthy signs, she will destroy whatever belongs to her from the substance of the earth. If she is in airy signs, she will destroy whatever belongs to her from the substance of the air. If she is in a watery sign, she will destroy whatever belongs to her from the substance of water. And he said: if she is in a place of evil fortune, turn your judgment around and speak of good in the place of evil, and justice in the place of injustice. And he said: look also at the planet hindering her, in what sign it may be, and combine it; and speak upon it according to what has been revealed to you regarding the matter of Saturn.</margin>

### Chapter One Hundred: Concerning Mercury; what it signifies when it is Lord of the Year.

<image-desc>Large woodcut illustration of Mercury as a winged deity riding in a chariot pulled by two roosters. He holds a caduceus. Above him are the astrological symbols for Mercury, Virgo, and Gemini.</image-desc>

When Mercury is the Lord of the Year or of the revolution of the year, and he is of good condition, well-disposed, and free from impediments, it signifies the well-being of merchants, wise men, scribes, those performing great works, arithmeticians, those who use numbers for the purpose of teaching, and geometers. It also signifies the well-being of children according to how he is joined with the planets. For if he is joined with a masculine planet, this will happen to males; if with a feminine one, this will happen to females; and it is even better if the lord of his house <term>receives<note>'Reception' occurs when one planet is in a sign ruled by another, creating a supportive relationship between them.</note></term> him. But if he is the Lord of the Year and the lord of the ascendant is free from impediments and any of the "fortunes" <note>The 'benefic' planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> should aspect him, men will find favor from the king; and everyone will find good from their masters; they will be heard by them and find honor, praise, and a good and laudable status from them; and the year will be useful for the said persons. If, however, he is impeded and not received, it signifies the opposite of what has been said: that men will find distress from kings and their masters and be oppressed by them; and the year will be the opposite for children, wise men, merchants, and the others mentioned before. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said: if, however, an "evil" planet <note>A 'malefic' planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note> aspects him along with this, it will destroy his essence in the place he mentioned. And he said: if the Moon is free from evils, rains and cold will be multiplied; and messengers will rejoice and find good; and it is even better and more worthy if she is received, for then they will find a place of dignity from the king and kings; and it will rain in its proper time when it is necessary. But if he is of bad condition and ill-disposed, it signifies hindrance and the ill-being of the aforementioned things and their bad disposition, each according to its subject. If, however, he is not joined to masculine and feminine planets together, it signifies that this will happen universally to boys and girls. And **Albumasar** said: whatever is his <note>Mercury's</note> will suffer detriment from this. Secondly, there will be an account of those things pertaining to him and regarding the human, earthy, airy, aquatic, and bestial figures <note>These are categories of zodiac signs; e.g., Gemini is 'human,' Taurus is 'bestial.'</note>; also the aspect of the "evils" and the "fortunes" toward him and his clothing, and so on. And he said there will be an account of all these things just as I have explained to you equally in the chapter on Saturn.

It is said by the wise man that whatever the revolution <note>original: "reuolutio"; the astrological chart cast for the start of the year.</note> of the year might be, or whoever its Lord <note>The "Lord of the Year" is the planet that rules the sign on the ascendant at the moment the Sun enters Aries.</note> might be, if it rains perceptibly on the eleventh day of June, it signifies that evil, loss, and hindrance will fall upon the fruits and the things growing from the earth, causing the destruction of a sixth part of them. And if the Lord of the hour of the ascending revolution is impeded, a fifth part of them will suffer loss. If, however, the Moon is then impeded, it will happen to a fourth part of them. But if the Lord of the ascending revolution is impeded, a third part of the aforementioned things will be destroyed. You shall also consider whether it rains in the sixth month, as October begins, or not; for if it rains in the manner of a downpour, he shall judge the future rains to be harmful. This will be even stronger and more harmful if a conjunction of the Sun and Moon, or their opposition, occurs on that day—and stronger still if the conjunction occurs in a "humid mansion" <note>One of the 28 Lunar Mansions associated with water signs or moisture.</note>.

### Chapter 103. What the Moon signifies in the revolution of the year of the world in each house, whether in a birth chart or in the revolution of a birth, whether she is the Lady of the Year or not.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the personification of the Moon (Luna). A crowned woman is seated on a throne, holding a crescent moon in her right hand and a circular mirror or shield in her left. She is flanked by celestial symbols: a sun on the left and a crescent moon on the right.</image-desc>

When the Moon is in the **first house** in the revolution of the year of the world—whether she is the Lady of the Year or not—she signifies swift changes for men during that revolution, from place to place, from one thing to another, and from one purpose to another. She signifies the successful outcome of matters in which men involve themselves; she signifies commands and dignities for those to whom they come. Men will also acquire good things from their elders, and those who have mothers will acquire good from them; men will also rejoice on account of women. And if it is a birth chart <note>original: "natiuitas"; a horoscope for the moment of a person's birth.</note>, good will happen to the one born. The same applies to his solar return revolution.

If, however, she is in the **second house**, it signifies grief and sadness which will happen to the one born because of his substance <note>Property or wealth.</note>; he will lose some of his goods in that revolution, and it will similarly diminish for the one born.

And if she is in the **third house**, it signifies that men will be friendly toward one another, especially in the lands that are within the division of the sign in which the Moon then resides. Similarly, it will happen among brothers: for their love will be increased. If there was enmity between them, it will diminish. Men will complete the things they begin and whose perfection they desire. They will also acquire good from the rich and the great, and dignities from kings, nobles, and the wealthy who are fit for the kingdom. There will be journeys and gatherings that are useful, unless Saturn or Mars works against this. You may say the same for a birth chart: that the person born will desire to be with nobles and the wealthy who are not slaves to money.

And if she is in the **fourth house**, and it is a daytime revolution, it signifies an evil beginning and hindrance, yet the end will be praiseworthy. If, however, it is a nighttime revolution, neither the beginning nor the end will be praised; the affairs of men will be diminished, and people will suffer loss unless Jupiter works against it. If it is a birth or a solar return, the same will happen to the one born. And if it is an "interrogation" <note>original: "interrogatio"; a branch of astrology (horary) where a chart is cast to answer a specific question.</note>, the questioner will be saddened for that reason or gladdened as was said regarding the daytime or nighttime revolution. Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "albumasar"; a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said: unless the question is about acquired treasure or a buried thing, because in this she is most excellent, for that thing will appear and be uncovered.

And if she is in the **fifth house**, it signifies the obtaining of children in that revolution. If it is a birth chart, it signifies a multitude of children. And if it is the revolution of a birth, it signifies the obtaining of a child in it

<column-break/>

if nature is fit to be able to do this. It signifies masculinity in a nighttime revolution, but if it is a daytime revolution, it signifies femininity. You should say this same thing in birth charts, their revolutions, and interrogations; nor will many horrible things appear. And Abu Ma'shar said it signifies the arrival of rumors from distant parts, at which men will rejoice, especially parents whose children are absent. He also said: if you wish to know what those rumors are, look to the planet from which the Moon is separating, for the rumors will be according to the nature of that planet. And if you wish to know whether those rumors are written on paper or if an envoy delivers them by mouth, look to the Moon and Mercury: if he joins with her or is separated from her. If she is separated from the Lord of the seventh house and joined to Mercury, the rumors will be written on paper. If indeed she is separated from Mercury or from his Lord, the envoy relates his rumors.

And if she is in the **sixth house**, Abu Ma'shar said it signifies strife and contention on the part of paternal uncles <note>original: "patruum"; specifically uncles on the father's side.</note>, and profit from four-footed animals, and health of the body.

And if she is in the **seventh house**, he said it signifies profit on the part of women and spouses, and benefit from them.

And if she is in the **eighth house**, he said it signifies death, consumption, and the deposition of a king or his death, and disturbance in works. For it signifies enchanters and enchantresses pretending they know such incantations so that they might extort something from others. Because of these incantations, some people, having been falsely judged, blaspheme astrologers. There will be evil thoughts in the hearts of men. If it is a birth chart, the person born will study these things. It signifies the same in the revolution of a birth.

And if she is in the **ninth house**, Abu Ma'shar said it signifies participation in journeys, evil thoughts, the changing from region to region, the beckoning of women, and knowledge of the administration of the kingdom and other matters. And he said if the ninth house itself is from the houses of Mercury, it signifies the wisdom of the stars <note>Astrology.</note>. And if it is from the houses of Venus, it signifies the sublimity of the sciences and of songs. And if it is from the houses of Mars, it signifies the mastery of instruments and the work of arms. And if it is from the houses of Jupiter, it signifies divine worship, knowledge of the law, and the leadership of judges. And if it is from the houses of Saturn, it signifies the science of alchemy and practice in it; for men will study this in that revolution. Similarly for the one born in whose birth chart or revolution the Moon is in the ninth house. And if she is fortunate and not impeded in the second or fourth houses, profit will follow from it; if not, then no. And if an "evil" <note>A malefic planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> is there, loss will follow. If that evil planet is impeded, the destruction of substance follows; it signifies many and diverse masteries. And if it is the house of the Sun <note>Leo.</note>, it signifies knowledge and foresight in all the subjects of the quadrivium <note>original: "quadruuialibus"; the four mathematical arts: arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.</note>. And if it is her own house <note>Cancer.</note>, it signifies universal knowledge of all things that are extracted from the waters or proceed from them. And he said that the Moon has these properties among the planets.
