### Chapter 109: On Cometary Stars

**Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian polymath.</note> said that there are nine types of cometary stars: the first is called the *Veru* (Spear); the second, *Cenaculum* (The Chamber); the third, *Partica* (The Pole); the fourth, *Miles* (The Soldier); the fifth is called *Ascone*; the sixth, *Matutina* (The Morning) or *Aurora* (The Dawn); the seventh, *Argentium* (The Silver); the eighth, *Rosea* (The Rosy); and the ninth, *Nigra* (The Black). And he said that the first four of these resemble stars, and all of them signify wars, terrors, and great events in the world. He said that one may know the future evil from their color and from the nature of the sign in which they first appeared. You will know when that evil will occur by its position: if it appears in the east or north and then moves toward the south, it will be soon; if it is in the west, it will be delayed.

That which is called **Veru** (The Spear) is horrible to look at and moves close to the sun; it appears during the day. When it appears, it signifies the change and lessening of the fruits of trees and the fruits of the earth, and the mortality of kings, the wealthy, and those who are heirs to a kingdom.

The one called **Cenaculum** (The Chamber) is similar to the color of Mars and has beneath it a ray like ash-colored smoke. When it appears, it signifies a scarcity—though not an extreme one—rather than a true famine; it also signifies wars in which religious people will involve themselves beyond what is appropriate for them.

The one called **Partica** (The Pole) has a thick ray as if it were dragging a pole behind it, and it is not very bright. When it appears, it signifies drought and a lack of water and grain. If it is joined with any of the planets, it signifies other things according to the nature and disposition of the planet it is bodily joined to. For instance, if it is joined with **Saturn**, there will be mortality, especially among the elderly, Jews, religious figures, and those who wear Saturnine clothes <note>Dark, heavy, or somber garments.</note>. 

If it is joined with **Jupiter**, its significations will appear among kings and magnates—always good or bad depending on whether Jupiter is well-disposed and strong, or unfortunate and weak. If it is joined with **Mars**, it signifies many wars, mortalities, the sword, the shedding of blood, and destruction by fire. It cannot appear with the **Sun**. If it is joined with **Venus**, it signifies drought and a great decrease of waters. If with **Mercury**, it signifies the death of youths, wise men, and scribes. If with the **Moon**, it signifies mortality falling among the common people and other lowly persons.

The one called **Miles** (The Soldier) is of the nature of Venus and is as large as the moon; it has a long ray and hair which it pours out behind it. When it appears, it travels through the twelve signs, and it signifies harm to kings, nobles, and magnates, and that men will rise up in the 

<column-break/>

world and want to change the laws and ancient things and introduce new ones. A worse danger will appear from the side toward which it extends its tail and hair.

The one called **Ascone** <note>Likely a corruption of the Greek 'Acontiae', meaning javelin-like.</note> is said to be of the nature of Mercury, and its color is blue. It appears small compared to other comets and has a long tail, extending its ray upward like a wing, holding its heads lower and bringing them together in one place. When it appears, it signifies the death of kings or magnates and nobles who are heirs to the kingdom—especially toward the part where it extends its tail or rays—and it signifies wars. 

And I saw this comet appear in the year of the Arabs 663 <note>Approx. 1265 AD.</note>, the year in which **Pope Alexander** died; and not long after, **King Manfred** was killed by a brother of the King of France named **Charles** <note>Charles of Anjou defeated Manfred at the Battle of Benevento in 1266.</note>. And again, not long after, **Conrad** <note>Conradin, the last Hohenstaufen heir, executed in 1268.</note> was killed by the same Charles in the kingdom of Apulia—this was in the year of the Arabs 665—and many dukes and many barons died with him. There were many wars and dissensions from the time of that comet's appearance, and they lasted a long time.

The one called **Matutina** (The Morning) or **Aurora** (The Dawn) is red and has a long tail, though shorter than *Ascone*, and is of the nature of Mars. When it appears in the east with its head depressed, it signifies wars and burnings of fire, pestilence, and famine in the land of Babylon, the lands of the Arabs and Persians, and drought and lack of water in Egypt; this will extend even to the western parts.

The one called **Argentium** (The Silver) has a ray like the height of purest silver, whose brightness exceeds that of all other stars at night. When it appears while **Jupiter** is in **Pisces** or **Cancer**, it signifies an abundance of grain and fruit in the regions where it appeared. If Jupiter is in **Scorpio**, these things will still happen, but with some difficulty.

The one called **Rosea** (The Rosy) is large and round, with a very thick appearance like a human face. Its color is between gold and silver. When it appears, it signifies the death of kings, magnates, the wealthy, and nobles, and the occurrence of great events and the emergence of ancient causes; however, things will change for the better.

The one called **Nigra** (The Black) is of the nature of Saturn and is of a similar color. When it appears, it signifies mortality, both natural death and death by the sword and beheading.

### Chapter 110: What the Dragon's Head and Tail signify in each house, whether in revolutions, births, or questions.

But if it is joined with an evil planet, it signifies an increase of evil, since its nature is to increase whatever it touches.

If it is in the **second house**, it signifies good fortune in wealth and its increase. The same is signified in a birth or question if it is in the second.

If it is in the **third house**, it signifies that the person born will be an interpreter of dreams and will be of good faith; there will be short journeys that are useful in that revolution, as well as acquisitions and profits.

If it is in the **fourth house**, and the fourth house is **Aries, Leo, Sagittarius, Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius**, it signifies an increase of good and profit from lands, vineyards, and other immovable things. But if the fourth house is **Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn, Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces**, it signifies loss and a decrease of income. If it is in the **fifth house**, it signifies fortune...

### Chapter 107: What the Tail signifies in the houses.

### Chapter 108: What the fixed stars signify in revolutions of years and nativities and what they work within them.

Having spoken of the revolutions of years and the 
meanings of the planets and the Dragon’s Head and its Tail, 
and what they signify in each house and in each sign: 
it remains now to speak of certain fixed stars that are 
found in each sign; some of which have the power to 
signify grave evil and impediment, while others have the power to 
signify good. This is a matter in which one must be very diligent, 
since upon them and from them depends much of the judgment of 
revolutions, nativities, questions, and elections. For the 
revolutions, nativities, questions, and the judgments themselves are 
often changed by them with a force far stronger than that of a 
planet; and in this, many excellent 
astrologers are often deceived: because they do not consider them in their judgments, but only the 
planets and <term>parts</term> <note>Specific calculated points in a chart, like the "Part of Fortune."</note>. And this is the reason why they are sometimes deceived and 
fail in those things which they judge, whether for good or for evil; 
and they are reproached and held in contempt, though they should not be reproached 
out of ignorance; nevertheless, I cannot excuse them for their 
sloth or negligence. But if you carefully consider them in 
your judgments of revolutions, nativities, and questions, you 
will not err, if God does not resist. When you approach 
any revolution, nativity, or question and have 
erected its figure, you shall consider all the houses from the first to 
the twelfth, and you will see whether any of the

and you shall judge good or evil according to the nature of those stars which 
you find there, which I shall describe to you. I will hand them down to you just

### Chapter 110. What fortunate fixed stars signify in births, questions, and the revolutions of years.

Having spoken of the misfortunes that descend from the fixed stars <term>Fixed Stars: Distant stars (unlike "wandering" planets) that were believed to exert specific influences based on their position</term> and the unfortunate ones upon the lower world, we must now speak of the fortunes that the fortunate fixed stars bestow upon the same. For just as some unfortunate stars are found in every sign, so too are found in each of them certain fortunate fixed stars that are the causes of success and greater fortune. 

Know, therefore, that in the 15th degree of Aries and its 6th minute, there is a certain star of the nature of Jupiter and Venus <note>original: "de natura iouis z veneris"; medieval astrologers categorized stars by which planets they most resembled in influence</note>, and its latitude is southern; its property is to be beneficial and to help. There is another in its 26th degree and 1st minute of the nature of Jupiter. 

In Taurus, there is one star in its first degree and 3rd minute. Another in its 8th degree and 7th minute. A third is in its 9th degree and 1st minute; all of these are of the nature of Venus. 

In Gemini, there is one star in its 19th degree and 2nd minute. And another in its 21st degree and 3rd minute, which are of the nature of Jupiter and are of the second magnitude <term>Magnitude: A measure of a star's brightness; second magnitude stars are bright, though not the brightest</term>. 

In Cancer, there is one star which is called "Good" in its 27th degree and 2nd minute. Another is in its 29th degree and 5th minute, and both are of the nature of Jupiter and work for good. 

In Leo, there is one star of the nature of Jupiter and Venus at its ninth degree and fourth minute, and it is called "Benevolent." 

In Virgo, there is a certain star in its 4th degree and seventh minute of the nature of Venus and the Moon. 

In Libra, there is a certain star of the nature of Jupiter and Venus in its 13th degree and 45th minute. And another in the 14th degree and 5th minute of the aforementioned nature; and both are south-

In Sagittarius, there is one star in its 10th degree and 15th minute which is called "Peaceful" <note>original: "pacifica"</note> and is of the nature of Venus. Another is in its 17th degree and 55th minute, and it is northern and of the nature of Jupiter. 

In Capricorn, there is one star in its 2nd degree and 3rd minute which is called "the Ox" <note>original: "bos"</note> and is of the nature of Jupiter. Another is in its 7th degree and 55th minute. In Aquarius, there is one star in its 15th degree and 55th minute, and it is of the nature of Jupiter. 

In Pisces, there is one star in its 7th degree and 11th minute, and it is of the nature of Jupiter itself.

### Chapter 112. On the varieties of customs.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a highly influential 9th-century Persian astrologer and astronomer</note> placed this chapter in his *Book of Revolutions*, which I do not think should be omitted, since I have followed in his footsteps in this matter, even though I have used longer speech than he did. And he said that in the sphere there are customs which do not resemble other customs. For he said that in a king there is a custom which does not resemble the custom of servants; and in servants there is a custom which does not resemble the custom of kings. And in a kingdom there is a custom which does not resemble the custom of nativities. And in nativities there is a custom which does not resemble the custom of interrogations <term>Interrogations: Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question</term>.

And if she is from the first dichotomy to the completion of her light <note>Full Moon</note>, it will be among those from the 30th year to the 45th. And if she is from the completion of her light to the third dichotomy <note>Last quarter</note>, it will be among those who have already begun to grow old from that point onward. And if she is in the fourth dichotomy, this will be among the elderly or aged women. And if this should happen to men, it would signify those ages in that same manner.

### On the meaning of the Lord of the Ascendant when it is combust 
### in the seventh [house] or the ascendant.

**A**nd if the Lord of the Ascendant should be combust in the seventh, it 
signifies wars, plundering, and disputes over fortresses between men. If, however, it should be combust in the first [house], its impediment will be less harmful. You should also look to the nature of the rising sign: for the impediment falls upon the things signified by that sign. For instance, if it is Aries or Capricorn, it will be among smaller animals <note>original: "animalibus minoribus," referring to sheep or goats</note>. If, however, it is Taurus or the latter part of Sagittarius, it will be among larger animals, and especially among oxen and similar creatures. And if it is Gemini, Libra, Aquarius, or the first part of Sagittarius, it will be among humans. And if it is Cancer or Pisces, it will be among aquatic animals which men use for their own benefit. If, however, it is Scorpio, it will be among venomous animals, both of the land and the water. And if it is Leo, it will be among wild animals that live by prey, such as lions, wolves, and apes. And if it is in Virgo, it will be among women, things growing from the earth, and young virgins. And know that if an afflicted planet is "received" <term>Reception: A dignifying relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term> by a strong planet that is not afflicted, that reception removes the malice and diminishes it. If, however, the malefic planets <note>Mars or Saturn</note> look upon it without a perfect reception, they increase the malice; and all the more strongly if the aspect <term>Aspect: The geometric angle between planets</term> should be a square or an opposition.

### Chapter 114: On the impediment sent by the Lord of the 
### Midheaven when it is afflicted in the revolution.

**A**fter you have looked at the Lord of the Ascendant of the 
revolution and seen its meanings, it remains for you to look 
at the meanings of the Lord of the Midheaven. For if it should be com-
bust in any of the angles <term>Angles: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful areas of a chart</term>, it signifies destruction

<column-break/>

that will occur to the king in that revolution: for instance, if it is combust in the first [house] and the Sun is the Lord of the First, it signifies wars or popular uprisings, or that subjects are going to kill the king in that revolution, or at the very least they will plot his downfall and betray him. Therefore, so that your judgment may benefit him and your discernment may be of value—and so that he may believe in the power of free will—you could turn away the evil that is coming according to the stars: advise him not to trust the common people nor to rely on them. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: when you wish to know in what manner he should fear, look at which of the planets gazes upon the Sun at the hour of the revolution. And if Mars gazes upon it or is bodily joined to it, it signifies the killing of the king, which will occur to him through the persuasion of the mob or common people, or by daylight robbers, murderers, and those who lie in wait on the roads to kill men for a price. If, however, Saturn gazes upon it or is bodily joined to it, a doubtful illness will be feared for the king, or perhaps that he will be poisoned. And know that if the Sun should "burn" the Lord of the Ascendant of the year, he should fear also what I have said in the same manner I described. And he said that whatever comes of this will be in his own region where he resides, and will not come from another land to him. But if the Lord of the Tenth is combust in the fourth or the seventh, these things will happen from causes coming from another land to the one in which he is: and it signifies that the aforesaid things will come according to what was said above. And he spoke again and told of evils (according to what I said in the chapter on the Sun) for the king and his peasants, except that in the chapter on the malefic planets you should look for this at the revolution of the year. And he said that if the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to a malefic in an angle—just as he said in the first chapter—and the aspect is from an opposition or a square <note>original: "quarto aspectu," the 90-degree square aspect</note>, this is more serious than a conjunction. And he said that if the Sun is the significator of the king and gazes upon Jupiter from an opposition in the revolution, he will be treated as an enemy through the nature of that same planet, and it will destroy him just as it does Jupiter <note>This likely refers to religious or legal authorities, represented by Jupiter, turning against the king</note>.

### On the meaning of Mars in the revolution.

**A**lbumasar said: know that when Mars is in Gemini at the hour of 
the revolution and is in the Midheaven, it signifies that in 
that revolution many men will be trained <note>original: "erudientur," which can mean educated or disciplined</note>. And if it is in the first or the seventh [house] as the ascendant, the hands of many will be cut off and many will be mutilated. And if it is in the fourth, that is, in the angle of the earth <note>The lowest point of the chart</note>, it signifies the cutting off of the hands and feet of many. And he said—and the son [of the author] says—this applies to the entry of two great kings into their reign. The same is said for the start of any magistracy or any other rule: it can be said that many evildoers will fall, who must be treated in this way. Know these things and do not consign them to oblivion.

### Chapter 115: How to know the evil or horrible things 
### at the hour of the revolution which are to come in that year.

**W**hen you wish to know the heavy and horrible events 
that are to come in the year you are forecasting: 
know that the accidents will be according to the disposition of the two 
malefics <term>Malefics: Saturn and Mars</term>. For if they are found in the upper circle, that is, in the northern half <note>original: "medietate septentrionali"</note> and that part being above the earth—and all the more strongly if they themselves are northern—they signify heaviness and horrors coming in that year. And the more they are elevated above the earth, and especially Saturn, the more their meaning will extend to distant and diverse regions. And Albumasar says: know that the state of the year will be heavy when two malefic planets are in the high circle where the pole is, in those images <note>Constellations</note> which, when they have gone to the end of the circle, will return, and they signify destructions. Therefore, when you see those two malefics at the hour of the revolu-

If both are retrograde—or at least one of them—Saturn is the source of greater harm. In such a case, he will signify things exceeding all bounds in malice, both in terms of fires and killings. Jupiter will not be able to break their malice unless, by chance, one of them is in Cancer in a trine <note>120-degree angle, considered harmonious</note> or sextile <note>60-degree angle, considered helpful</note> aspect to Jupiter, and Jupiter himself is in a good and well-disposed state. This will also signify a weakening of the state of the king of that region in which the year has turned, as well as of other magnates, the wealthy, and the noble. Kings and magnates will seek help from the common people; religion will be diminished; and piety will be taken away from men, nor will mercy be found among them. This will last until one of them—namely Saturn or Mars—reaches the degree that was the cusp of the Tenth House <note>The house of government and authority</note> at the hour of the revolution; or it will begin then and endure for a long time afterward, at least for one full transit of Mars through the zodiac. 

If, however, Saturn is then in Virgo and Mars commits his disposition to him from Gemini (as was said), and the Moon commits her disposition to Saturn while she is in Sagittarius, it will then signify the most horrible of horrors and the most pestilent of pestilences. It will signify the destruction of kingdoms and kings, and the transfer of certain kingdoms from some kings to others. Furthermore, when the Moon commits her disposition to Saturn, if she is joined to him or in a square or opposition aspect, and the Lord of the Sign in which she resides is impeded at the moment the conjunction with Saturn is perfected (degree by degree and minute by minute), it signifies many diverse types of obstacles coming in that revolution. 

And if the Moon suffered an eclipse in the revolution immediately preceding, or is due to suffer one in the immediate future, the evil will be prolonged for as many months as the hours the lunar eclipse lasted. But if she is hindered by the "fortunes" <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> and the Lord of the Sign in which she resides is hindered when the conjunction of the Moon and Saturn is perfected—whether by conjunction or aspect—that perfection of the conjunction signifies an increase in hindrance and destruction. 

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a highly influential Persian astrologer whose works were central to medieval European astrology</note> said: look to the Sun, its state, and its aspect toward the hindering evil planet, and to all the evil planets just as I told you concerning the Moon. Look also to the "perfection" and the Lord of the Perfection. Include the Part of Fortune and its Lord in this, and seek help through the dignities of the seven planets which provide aid and signify the timing. He also said that when the "significator" <note>The planet representing a specific person or topic</note> is in an "angle" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, where planets are most powerful</note>, it will prolong the evil, while in other places it will shorten it. Likewise, look to the Sun: if it suffered an eclipse in the preceding conjunction or will in the following one, the signified evil will be prolonged for as many years as the hours its eclipse lasted. 

He said that the Lord of the Course and the Perfection signifies what the "significator" has indicated of good or evil. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Division receive the Moon from Saturn in an excellent and strong place in the circle, it signifies the repelling of evil by the will of God, and the prohibition of the destruction of evil through its own good fortune. He said that similarly in nativities <note>birth charts</note>, when

He says the newborn will be wise and fortunate. He also said that the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets</note> dissolve the evil of the "strikers" <note>malefic planets</note> when they are strong in an opportune place and their testimony is direct. But if the Moon is, on the contrary, weakened, they will not prevail.

### When planets emerge from under the Sun's rays according to Albumasar.

->Albumasar said to take care whether the significator or any planet has emerged from "combustion" <note>being "burnt up" by the Sun's proximity</note>, and to see that no evil planet aspects it, for then it will be like a delicate child. If a "malefic" <note>original: "infortuna"</note> aspects it, it will destroy and finish it. ->See the state of the higher planets in the revolution of the year of the world, and specifically concerning Saturn.<-

**Y**ou shall look forward to the state of the higher planets in the revolution of the year of the world when you cast it. See where they fall in the circle, starting with Saturn. If he falls in the degree of his exaltation <note>Saturn is exalted in Libra</note> and is "received," disposing the influence of Venus, he will be the disposer and significator of a great matter. He will signify a great thing to come in that revolution, primarily in the **Roman Empire**. Secondarily, however, in the kingdom of **Babylon** <note>In medieval astrology, Babylon often represented the Middle East or specific Islamic caliphates</note>; and it will be a turn from detriment to good and to their utility. If it should be thus—though it happens very rarely—nevertheless, when it does occur, it signifies a maximum, almost exceeding measure, in the exaltation and increase of the kingdom or empire, and it will be a thing that lasts a long time. 

This can be perceived from the substance of the sign in which Venus is located, and from the "term" <note>a sub-division of a zodiac sign</note> of its location. If she is "occidental" <note>setting in the west</note> from the Sun, moving direct, and fortunate—meaning that she is entirely in a term of a fortune, free from impediments, and recently emerged from under the Sun's rays—it signifies that things must happen this way. Or, if another planet aspects Saturn and receives him by two dignities and commits its strength to him—and that planet is free, fortunate, strong, and well-disposed, of whom nothing bad is said—that planet will be a participant. If it is otherwise, the significance will be different: that is, may God avert it. 

**Y**ou shall also see if Jupiter falls in the degree of his exaltation <note>Jupiter is exalted in Cancer</note> and is fortunate, strong, and free from impediments; for it will signify the greatest changes coming in that revolution in that kingdom and empire, and for the good. This is even stronger and more complete if the Moon aspects him, and she herself is free and fortunate—that is, strong—and another planet receives him and commits its strength to him, being itself free from impediments; then that planet will be a participant. If it is otherwise, he will not keep the promise except according to how he himself is disposed.

### Concerning Mars.

**N**ext, look at Mars. If he falls in the degree of his exaltation <note>Mars is exalted in Capricorn</note>, it signifies great changes, but they will be less than those mentioned above. They will be of his own nature, such as wars, fiery burnings, the cutting off of roads <note>original: "abscisiones viarum" — likely highway robbery or blockades</note>, the shedding of blood, and similar things. This holds unless Saturn aspects him from a trine or sextile aspect, and Saturn himself is fortunate, strong, and free from impediments so that no evil is said of him; or if another planet aspects Mars, receives him, and commits its disposition to him, being itself free from impediments, fortunate, and strong.

### Concerning the other planets.

Nothing needs to be said about the Sun, because it is impossible for it to be in the degree of its exaltation <note>original: "exaltationis" — a specific sign where a planet's influence is most potent</note> in any revolution <note>The "revolution" is the astrological chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to the start of the year.</note>. Regarding the inferior planets, I have found nothing said by the ancient sages except what Albumasar said about Mercury: look at Mercury in the revolution; if it is in its exaltation with some planet that receives it and takes its disposition <note>original: "dispositionem" — the "handing over" of astrological influence or power</note> from it, it will be the lord of its own significance which I have stated by God's will, for it is fitting in the revolution of years and quarters to its exaltation. But when there is a planet in its exaltation that receives it, it will be similar to it. And he spoke of the state of the malefics <note>original: "maloz" (malorum) — "bad" planets, typically Saturn and Mars</note> in conjunction with that which is in its exaltation in the conjunction of malefics and their aspects, whichever planet is in the degree of its exaltation according to what has been revealed. And he said when the Moon is at peace with the Sun and is strong in its place in the nocturnal revolution, the Sun commits its lordship and governance to the Moon.

### Chapter 116. What they signify in the revolution of the year in which an eclipse of the Sun or Moon is due to occur.

When you examine the revolution of the world's year, see whether there will be an eclipse of the Sun or Moon in that year; for if no eclipse is to come, the judgment of the revolution will not change but will remain in its own state. But if one is to come, see in which sign its arrival is, and which planets rule the houses at the hour of the middle of the eclipse. Look then at the sign and its lord and see how it stands with the lordship of the ascendant <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the eclipse.</note> of the eclipse, and how it stands with the lord of the year or with the lord signifier, and how it stands with the royal signifier, and how they aspect each other and the other planets. Albumasar said that if some planet that was hindered <note>original: "ipediti" — weakened by its position or unfavorable connections</note> should aspect it at the time of the eclipse, and afterward the malefics aspect it, it will aggravate what it signifies and multiply the hindrance. This is even more severe if the royal signifier is the lord of the sign in which the eclipse occurred; for if it is so, and any of the malefics aspects it—and if that malefic is Mars—he will doubt the death of the king in that revolution. And if it were Saturn, he will fear a grave illness for him or another very serious accident. This will happen when the Sun comes to the degree that was at the cusp of the midheaven <note>The highest point in the sky at the time of the eclipse.</note> at the hour of the middle of the eclipse. And if the lord of the year is the ruler of the sign in which the coming eclipse will be, he will fear for the destruction of the common people and for their great hindrance, aside from death. And this will be when the Sun reaches the ascending degree of the middle of the eclipse; and this is if the ascendant of the eclipse is Gemini, Virgo, or Libra, or the first half of Sagittarius, or Aquarius, according to the type of people who are signified by the ascending sign—and according to other significations of the signs as I have explained to you above in the chapter on the hindrances that are sent to the lordship of the ascending sign of the revolution when it is hindered. And these significations will last according to the number we mentioned above: namely, if it is an eclipse of the Moon, every hour signifies one month. If, however, it is an eclipse of the Sun, every hour signifies one year. And Albumasar said after this, look at the part about which you fear from the place of the eclipse and the place of its lord, according to the substance of both signs. And he said: look at the flying stars <note>original: "stellas volantes" — likely referring to meteors or planetary movements near Mercury.</note> which are stars of Jupiter and always appear in the place of Mercury; if Mercury is in the east, they will be seen in the east; and if he is in the west, they will be seen in the west; and their departure will be the combustion <note>original: "combustio" — when a planet is so close to the Sun it becomes invisible and "burnt up."</note> of Mercury.

### Concerning the parts of the planets in the eclipse.

Albumasar said regarding the parts of the planets in an eclipse: if they are in the lower path, there will be evil in the part <column-break/> of Mars and Venus, which are south and north; and if they are in the upper path, there will be evil in the part of Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun. And he said after this: look in which sign they appear, and what the state of the lord of that sign is in its place, and what the aspect of the malefics and the fortunes <note>original: "fortunaz" (fortunarum) — "good" planets, typically Jupiter and Venus.</note> is toward the lord of the sign and the mansions. If it is in the sign of kings and the lord of the sign aspects from a strong place, it signifies that someone will emerge from that same region who will contend for the kingdom from among the king's household, and he will be famous. And he said if it is in the sign of the kingdom as I have said, and the lord of the sign does not aspect it, he will be from among the sons of the nobles and will be fit for the kingdom. And he said: judge all signs in this way. And he said: know that the signs of the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars signify the sons of kings; and the signs of Saturn signify those famous for antiquity; and the house of the Moon is within the house of the Sun; and the house of Mercury is within the house of Jupiter; and the house of Jupiter is within the house of Saturn; and their circuits are within the circles I have mentioned. And he said: Saturn in Aquarius is famous and refers to wise men, but in Capricorn he is evil. And he said: and the mansions in their rising do not signify anything except the state of the common people and the power of kings and magnates. Then you must consider the ascending sign or mansion and hold that ascendant and its planet to judge the aforementioned persons.

### How the hour may be distinguished.

Furthermore, Albumasar said: the knowledge of the hour in which this appears is found by counting from the ascendant of the eclipse or from the place of the eclipse to the ascendant of the middle of the eclipse, allowing one month for each sign. And he said: whenever you look at that sign in which either the ascendant or the middle of the eclipse shall be, this will happen without doubt, whether it be good or evil; or perhaps the thing itself will appear when it is faster at the entry of the Moon to the ascendant, especially in an eclipse that occurs in days of war, corruption, or change in the season and adversity.

<margin>Chapter 117. How one should proceed regarding the royal signifier and the peasants according to Albumasar.</margin>

Albumasar said that the significance of the Sun is over the state of the peasants; and knowing it will reveal the royal signifier to you and will disclose to you what may happen in his kingdom in that same year. And he said: know this from the reception of the planets with each other through their lights and the falls of those rays in the 12 houses and the circle; and what happens in those signs from the climates <note>Geographic zones.</note> and cities, so that their destruction or appreciation may be revealed to you through the rays of the hostile malefics, and through the rays of the good ones, and through the rays of the friendly malefics; and similarly through the rays of the friendly and hostile fortunes. Speak according to their friendship or hostility toward the houses. For the fortunes, when they are at peace with the houses, signify a multitude of good things—that is, when they aspect the locations from a trine or sextile <note>original: "fertili" — literally "fertile," used here for the 60-degree sextile aspect.</note> aspect; and when there are hostilities, they signify a scarcity of good—that is, when they aspect from a square <note>90-degree angle.</note> or from opposition. And similarly, when the malefics are hostile to the houses—that is, when they aspect from a square aspect or from opposition—they signify a multitude of evil. If, however, they are at peace with the houses—that is, if they aspect them from a trine or sextile aspect—they signify a scarcity of evil. And he said: then look at what is in each sign regarding the lands in the east and west; and whichever sign is hindered in the west signifies a hindrance from the lands that are in the east and west parts. And if it is hindered in the midheaven, it signifies hindrance in the lands that are in the east and west, and specifically toward the parts of the north and south—namely, in the part of Mars and Venus and in the land of the Ethiopians. And he said: and this is a marvelous model through which you contemplate the revolution of the year made in the 12 remaining days...

...with twelve days remaining in the month of Ramadan, which is a lunar month, in the 35th year of the Arabs, the year arrived at Scorpio. The ascendant <term>ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the calculation</term> was 15 degrees of Libra, the term <note>original: "terminus" — a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Jupiter, and the planets and their rays <note>original: "radij" — the angular relationships or "aspects" between planets</note> were as they appear in this figure.

And he <note>Likely referring to the astronomer Abu Ma'shar, often cited in these texts</note> said that if the revolution is calculated according to Benefaphar <note>original: "benefaphar" — a reference to the astrologer Ja'far (Abu Ma'shar)</note> at one equal hour and 12 minutes from the beginning of the night of the Sabbath <note>Saturday</note> which dawned on the 18th of the aforementioned month. And if the ascendant is calculated through the Toledan tables <note>original: "ascensiones toleti" — astronomical tables used for calculating celestial positions, based on the coordinates of Toledo, Spain</note> at 15 degrees of Libra, the planets are as I shall tell you. For Saturn was in Virgo at 27 degrees and 29 minutes. Jupiter was in Capricorn at 8 degrees and 16 minutes. Mars was in Leo at 13 degrees. The Sun was in the first degree of Aries. Venus was in Aries at almost 28 degrees. Mercury was in Aries at 19 degrees and 35 minutes. The Moon was in Scorpio at 18 degrees and 7 minutes. The North Node <note>original: "Caput" — the "Head of the Dragon"</note> was in Libra at 15 degrees and 33 minutes. And the South Node <note>original: "cauda" — the "Tail of the Dragon"</note> was in Aries at 15 degrees and 33 minutes. 

The year arrived at Scorpio, and the established angles—that is, the same signs—were determined by division and number in the revolution of the 35th year of the Arabs, with 12 days remaining. The Sun was in opposition to the ascendant, moving away from it, and the revolution occurred at night. The Moon was in its descent <note>original: "descenfione" — a place where a planet's influence is weakened</note> in the second sign. The "fortunes" <note>the beneficial planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> were absent from it, and it was joined to the "evils" <note>the harmful planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, though the Moon itself was the mistress of the midheaven <term>midheaven: the highest point in the sky at the time of the chart, relating to public life and status</term>. Venus and Mercury were in opposition to the ascendant, and Mars was in the 11th house in Leo, in reception <note>original: "receptus" — a condition where planets support one another by being in each other's signs</note>. Jupiter was in the fourth house in its descent, withholding the light of the Sun from Mars. Saturn was "falling" <note>original: "cadens" — located in a weak house</note> in Virgo, not received, in the 12th house. 

Mars was the lord of the house of the lord of the ascendant—namely, Aries—in which was Venus, who was the mistress of the ascendant and the mistress of the house of the Sun and Moon. Venus, who had the most testimony <note>astrological weight</note>, was the significator of the common people for the year. She was in an angle, in opposition to her own house, coming from the east to the angle of the west, and not received. 

The significator of the king was the Moon, because the revolution occurred at night and the authority belonged to her. She was the mistress of the midheaven and was joined to Saturn, who was falling in the 12th house; afterward, she was joined to Mars, who was retrograde in the 11th house. ### Also concerning the two parts in the revolution of the years of the world.

Albumasar <note>the Latinized name of Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> says: when you find two parts <note>referring to 'Arabic Parts' or 'Lots', calculated points in a chart used to predict specific topics</note> in one place or sign, those whose significator <term>significator: the planet representing a specific person or topic</term> is better disposed shall prevail. And he who is better disposed in this is said to be the one who better "beholds" (aspects) his part or is bodily joined to it. And Albumasar said this occurs when a part is joined to its lord in the water triplicity <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs sharing the same element—in this case, Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</term>, and their presence or conjunction is suitable in some sign and the triplicity from which the conjunction is changed, such as Gemini; the conjunction is changed from it and it will agree with its presence or conjunction in the circle of conjunction, or in two others outside that triplicity in Aquarius: with this, therefore, the citizens of this triplicity agree. And he said: and when Saturn is present and there is a conjunction in Scorpio, they will be strengthened. But if he [Saturn] receives the disposition of Mars in Scorpio, and it is in the midheaven and presides over the year; and if Mars is in the ascendant and presides with the commission of its disposition to Saturn in the midheaven in Scorpio, it will signify that the king shall perish in the eastern region and his kingdom shall pass away. And if it happens along with this that Venus is strong in her exaltation <term>exaltation: a sign where a planet's influence is especially powerful</term>, and the conjunction is in Scorpio, it signifies the strength of the Arabs and their petitioning in the kingdom.

### Another chapter on the revolution of the years of the world according to Albumasar.

In another account of the years of the world, look at the significator or lord of the year who is called the "significator of the peasants" <note>representing the common people</note>: and look at the Sun and the significator of the king. Also see if one of them has fallen into opposition with Mars, unless by chance Mars is very fortunate so that no evil is said of it—which rarely happens: for it signifies wars, terrors, and the shedding of blood. And if two of the aforementioned significators fall into opposition with Mars, they will signify a greater evil. And Albumasar said: the removal of the "evils" <note>malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> from an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> into the third or ninth house signifies war and a scarcity of religion <note>or religious observance</note> for both the king and the peasants. 

You must consider the Sun and its state: if it is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies a good disposition and adaptation of the land of Babylonia <note>this refers to the region of Mesopotamia/modern Iraq, then the center of the Abbasid Caliphate</note> and its citizens. If, however, it is impeded <term>impeded: 'afflicted' by a bad aspect from a malefic planet</term>, it signifies evil for them and their detriment and that of their king. The Sun also signifies—if it alone is impeded in the second, sixth, or twelfth houses, or is impeded anywhere by conjunction, aspect, or opposition from any of the "evils"—evil for the aforementioned king, namely, of Babylonia. 

You shall also see the disposition of the Moon: if it is free, fortunate, and strong, it signifies the strength of the Romans <note>referring to the Byzantine Empire, often called 'Rum' by Arabic sources</note> and their kings, and the weakness of their enemies. If, however, she [the Moon] alone is impeded in whatever place she may be, but especially in the aforementioned houses, it signifies an impediment and evil for them and their kings, and the strength of their enemies. 

But some might ask why the Sun signifies the king of Babylonia and the Moon signifies the king of the Romans, since that Roman kingdom is greater than any other, and the Sun is the greater light <note>making the assignment seem backwards to the reader</note>. To which it must be said that the Sun is the higher light, nor is it universally a "participant in things" like the Moon; and the kingdom of Babylonia existed before the Roman kingdom, nor is it a universal kingdom: for this reason the Sun was attributed to it as its significator. The Moon, however, because it is the universal light and a "participant in all things," was attributed as the significator of the kingdom and king of the Romans: because that kingdom is universal above all other kingdoms, to which all kings and all kingdoms then were subject. 

You shall also see the disposition of Saturn: if he is well-disposed and in conjunction with the "fortunes" [benefics], and especially from the ascendant, and is the lord of the year free from impediments, he will not hinder nor will he then be a malefic <term>malefic: a planet naturally inclined to cause harm</term>, and the impediment that he would naturally bring to these lower subjects will be removed. This is more strong if he is in Scorpio and Scorpio is the midheaven: because the ascendant will then be Aquarius and he [Saturn] will be the lord of the year: for it signifies the shedding of blood and other pestilences to come in that revolution, and it seems that this evil must occur when Saturn reaches his "term" <term>term: 'fines', a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet</term>. 

If, however, Mars beholds him from an opposition or a quartile aspect, he will increase the evil; but if it is a trine or sextile aspect with "reception" <term>reception: when one planet is in a sign ruled by another, creating a mutual agreement</term>, he will not bring so much, and the evil will be diminished.

And he said there will be poverty and tribulation among men, as well as heaviness and war; and there will be a scarcity of grain, and it will be in the sixth month because there are six degrees between them. And he said the cattle will thrive in that same year, and there will be little cold in their winter. You will also see at the hour of the revolution if Saturn is the significator of the common people, or the Lord of the Year, or the *almuten* over the Ascendant of the year, and Mars does not hinder him; and if the fortunes <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> are in the Ascendant and Mars is falling away from them and from the Ascendant; for this signifies the improvement of the affairs of the common people, and more strongly so if he is in an angle or in a high, good place from the Ascendant, receiving those fortunes. And Albumasar said that moist and watery planets in the Ascendant signify a cold year in that

<column-break/>

same city or region, as well as locusts and the fitness of cattle; and likewise when the fortunes descend in the Ascendant with the Sun. And he said the presence of the fall of the Lord of the Midheaven in the third house with Jupiter signifies the light-mindedness of the king and his dismissal from power.

These frequently occur in the work of astronomy, and from them, those who wish to follow revolutions can find very great utility. And Albumasar said that this is done in two ways. The first is when one planet is joined to another or is separated from it by a perceptible quantity; for then it acquires some signification of good or evil. For a planet signifies one thing when it is approaching and another when it is with it, and another when it recedes and is separated from it. For planets signify some things by nature, some by accident; some more, and some less; and some according to equality. If two planets have equal signification over one and the same thing, the one which is stronger is preferred—that is, the one which is stronger in nature, power, or dignity; or if one is diurnal and the other nocturnal; or if one is the *almuten* over the matter; or if one signifies the beginning and the other the end. In whatever way one is stronger or worthier, it is preferred. Just as you see in the extraction of the "Part of the Father," which the Sun and Saturn signify equally, since each of them has the role of signifying the father: it begins from the Sun by day because he is stronger than Saturn by day, for he signifies clarity and splendor and rejoices in them, while Saturn signifies obscurity and darkness and rejoices in those things which are contrary to the aforementioned. And you should understand the same for others, as will be said in its own time and place. The other way—that is, the second—the extraction of parts is done if there are two or three significators who signify one thing and the strength of one is equal to the strength of the other; or if one is worthier or stronger than the other. Albumasar said there will be a similarity in the signification, and for these reasons the extraction of parts was necessary. For the extraction of parts is the science of the distance <note>original: "longitudinis" — the longitudinal distance in degrees</note> between two significators who naturally signify one thing; and the effect of the "Part" is not well known through two significators unless a third is brought in—namely, that which naturally signifies the matter for which the part is extracted.

For when two <term>significators: planets or points that represent a specific person or topic in a chart</term> signify a matter, the span of longitude between them naturally depends on their positions. The one from which the count begins is called the first significator of that matter; the second is called the other; and these two are termed "immobile" <note>meaning their positions are the fixed starting and ending points for the measurement</note>. The third significator is the one from which the "projection" <term>projection: the process of measuring a distance and applying it to a new starting point</term> of the degrees of distance between the first natural significators begins. This third significator is the <term>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> or the lord of another "house" from which the projection of degrees begins, which is "mobile" <note>original: "mobilis" — changing based on the specific time of the chart</note>, as will be explained below in the appropriate place.

And for this reason, it is said: take the distance between this planet and that one, add it to the degree of the Ascendant, and project it from the Ascendant—or from such a place to such a place, or from such a planet to another—giving to each zodiac sign 30 equal degrees. Wherever the number ends, that is where the "Part" will be. This was done in two ways and for three reasons. One reason was to know what judgment should be made regarding the good or evil signified by the lord of the sign in which that Part falls, whether projected from the Ascendant or another place. The second reason was because the Ascendant signifies the bodies and the beginnings of all things. The projection from certain planets or other places was used because that same house or planet could be of the same nature or <term>complexion: the specific mixture of qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) in a planet or sign</term> as the location of the Part.

Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a highly influential 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that because the Ascendant is the "house of the circle" from which the longitude between the two natural significators is projected, and because it changes every hour, it is called the "third significator of mobile signification." They also use equal degrees for the Parts because the planets move upon the axis of the circle of signs <note>the ecliptic</note>, and the Ascendant is considered according to the degree of the circle of signs, and the degrees of the circle of signs are equal. Albumasar said it is therefore stated that a certain planet is in such a sign and such a degree, and the Ascendant is this or that degree of that sign. He said that the whole calculation is done through the equal degrees of the circle of signs. He said the degrees of the ascensions are from the degrees of the circle surrounding the circle of signs, and it moves the circle of signs and the other circles.

Albumasar said that the ancient Babylonians, Egyptians, and others used 97 Parts, as is found in their books. There are three modes of projecting the Parts: the first is the projection of the seven Parts of the seven planets; the second contains the Parts of the twelve houses; the third contains the Parts of all other things not mentioned or commemorated in the twelve houses, which are necessary Parts in certain places, both in "revolutions" <term>revolution: a chart cast for the Sun's return to a specific point, often the New Year</term> and in nativities <note>birth charts</note>. The Parts of the first mode are seven; of the second, twelve; of the third, ten. But first, we must speak of the Parts of the seven planets.

### Chapter Two: On the Parts of the seven planets and their 
### particular significations, and first on the Part of the 
### Moon, which is called the Part of Fortune.

Albumasar says: know that a Part is not extracted except from two significators that naturally signify the matter for which the Part is extracted. When two planets naturally signify a matter and agree—whether in their "diurnality" <term>diurnality: whether a planet is "of the day" (sect)</term> or in other qualities—the extraction of the Part must begin from the stronger one. As was said elsewhere regarding the Sun and Saturn, who are equal in the signification of the Part of the Father and in diurnality: nevertheless, the extraction of the Part of the Father begins from the Sun, because it is stronger for the reason assigned above. And if they are equal in the signification of the 

<column-break/>

projection, as was said, and one is diurnal and the other nocturnal, the extraction of the Part begins from the diurnal one during the day (because the day prevails over the night and is preferred to it). In the night, however, it begins from the nocturnal one because of its equality in signification with the diurnal one. This is how it is done in the extraction of the **Part of Fortune**, which is extracted from the "luminaries" <note>the Sun and Moon</note>.

The luminaries, as the ancients said, are of equal strength in "fortune." But because the Sun is the diurnal fortune, it starts from the Sun in the day; and because the Moon is nocturnal, it starts from her at night. This Part is placed before and preferred above all other Parts, just as the luminaries are preferred above all other stars. Thus, this Part will hold sway over all other Parts just as the luminaries held sway over all other stars. Similarly, the Sun is more splendid than the other stars; it is called the light of the day because the day is made by its rising, and by its setting the day is removed and it becomes night. It signifies natural life and the other things mentioned in the chapter on its significations. The Moon is the light of the night and the fortune signifying bodies and their affairs, as was said elsewhere in its own chapter.

I will give you an example of the extraction of the Part of Fortune: suppose the Sun is in the 12th degree of Taurus and the 5th minute, and the Moon is in the 12th degree of Virgo and the 5th minute, and the matter for which you wish to extract the Part of Fortune occurs during the day. You must subtract the position of the Sun from the position of the Moon, and there will remain 4 signs, 5 degrees, and 5 minutes. You then add this to the degree of the sign of the Ascendant and project from the beginning of that same sign through equal degrees, giving 30 degrees to each sign. Where the number ends, there shall be this Part.

In the night, it is the opposite: namely, you subtract the position of the Moon from the position of the Sun, add the degree of the Ascendant, and project from the Ascendant. Where the number ends, there shall be the Part of Fortune. If both luminaries are in the same degree, the Part of Fortune will be at the degree of the Ascendant and in the same minute. This Part signifies life, the body, and the soul; its strength, fortune, and liberty; profit, wealth, and poverty; the increase of silver; the "heaviness" or "lightness" <note>meaning high or low prices</note> of the market for saleable goods; praise, good fame, honors, and high status; good and evil; present and future; things hidden or manifest. It has signification over every matter; however, it does more for the wealthy and the great than for others, though it acts for every man according to the essence of each. If this Part and the luminaries are well-disposed in nativities or revolutions, it will be notably good. It is called the **Part of the Moon** and is the "Ascendant of the Moon," signifying good fortune. And Albumasar said...

...Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "Albumasar," the latinized name of the 9th-century Persian astrologer Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi</note> says that when the time that has passed from the hours of the day is multiplied by the parts of those hours (meaning, of that day) and the result is projected from the position of the Moon by equal degrees, it will fall upon the place of the <term>Lot of Fortune: a point in the chart representing physical well-being and prosperity</term> or near to that place. 

And if one <term>significator: a planet or point representing a specific topic</term> is stronger than another in the place of the calculation, the Part shall begin from the stronger one, both by day and by night. If, however, the significance arises from a zodiac sign and its planetary ruler, it shall begin more specifically from the ruler of the sign unto the degree of the sign itself, since the significance of the sign is strengthened by the significance of the planet. And if it happens that the sign itself is stronger in significance, it shall begin from the sign, and the <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> or another place in the circle to which it is brought shall be its partner. 

And this shall be discussed more broadly, clearly, and openly below in the account of the treatise on the twelve houses and the "things born of the earth" <note>original: "terrenascentium," referring to plants and crops</note>, according to what happens for each of those parts when they are treated individually, if God permits.

### Concerning the Lot of the Future, which is called the Lot of the Sun.

**A**fter the Lot of Fortune, which exceeds all other parts in strength and luck, we must next speak of the Lot of the Future, which is called the Lot of the Sun. This part immediately follows the Lot of Fortune in exceeding all other parts and prevailing over them—though some astrologers seem to care little for it, which does not seem right to me, as it is considered and extracted by the wise as a very useful thing. 

This part is extracted in the opposite way to the Lot of Fortune. For just as the Lot of Fortune is extracted by day from the Sun to the Moon, and by night from the Moon to the Sun, so the Lot of the Future is extracted by day from the Moon to the Sun, and by night from the Sun to the Moon. One then adds to this the degree that had risen at the Ascendant and projects it from the start of the ascending sign, giving 30 equal degrees to each sign; where the number ends, there shall this Part be. 

Indeed, the Parts of the <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term> are placed before the Parts of other planets. For although things that must be born are created through corruption, and things that must perish are destroyed through it—and this corruption happens through the movements of the planets—the operations that occur through the other planets are not as clearly apparent, nor so similar as those which appear to happen through the luminaries. 

And know that the property of the Lot of the Future is to signify the soul and the body (after the Lot of Fortune), as well as their being, faith, prophecy, religion, the worship of God, secrets, thoughts, intentions, hidden things, and everything that is absent; also courtesy, generosity, praise, good reputation, heat, and cold. 

And Abu Ma'shar said that the significations of the Lot of Fortune and the Lot of the Future appear more in every matter (whether absent or future) than in the present. It is also more evident at the beginnings of works and during the <term>revolutions: the return of a planet or the year to a starting point</term> of the years, both of the world and of individual births. And he said that the significations of the Lot of Fortune appear more during the day than the significations of the Lot of the Future, and the significations of the Lot of the Future appear more at night than those of the Lot of Fortune. 

Furthermore, its changes and alterations happen over time through the movement of the planets from sign to sign; births and deaths occur, and life is given to animals and other plants, and for the same reason, created things fail and are destroyed. Yet the luminaries work upon them more clearly and perceptibly than the other planets. These two Parts work more than all others, for both good and evil, and their significations are similar to the significations of the luminaries.

### Concerning the Heavy Lot, which is called the Lot of Saturn.

**T**he Lot of Saturn, which the wise used to call the "Heavy Lot" because of the grave and heavy

<column-break/>

matters signified by it, is taken by day from Saturn to the Lot of Fortune, and in the night the reverse; it is projected from the Ascendant, giving 30 equal degrees to each sign. Where its number and minutes fall, there shall this Part be. 

Its significations are these: for it signifies memory and the depth of talent and counsel, faith, religion, and restraint in these things, as well as constancy and durability. It also has the duty to signify a thing that had perished, or had gone astray, or had been stolen, or had fled, or had been submerged in the sea or a river, or had fallen into a well or similar place, or had died. It signifies the state of the dead: namely, by what death a person was born to die or is about to die. 

It also signifies the state of lands and crops and other things born of the earth; it particularly rules over inherited lands that are purchased. It signifies heavy buildings, especially those that are not raised high from the earth; also digging, the piling up of earth and carrying it high, the bringing forth of waters, and similar things. It also signifies avarice and the stinginess of the miserable who live miserably. It signifies praise and blame, old age and the time of life that causes one to grow old, and every person bound and imprisoned, or placed in a jail, and the liberation from jail or bonds.

### Concerning the Lot of Jupiter, which is called the Lot of Happiness.

**T**he Lot of Jupiter, which the philosophers called the Lot of Happiness and Help, is taken by day from the Lot of the Future (which signifies fortune) to Jupiter (who signifies happiness and help), and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. 

Its signification is over honor and the gaining of victories, help, happiness, and kindness; also the praiseworthy end of matters, the perfection of faith and its applications, and whatever concerns its essence; also belief in God, diligence in every good work, and the love of God and of His justice and of just judgment among men, and the building of <term>oratories: places of prayer or small chapels</term>. It signifies wisdom and the wise, and the high status of the wise; also confidence and hope, and all good things which men enjoy, and the sharing of good with one another.

### Concerning the Lot of Mars, which is called the Lot of Boldness.

**T**he Lot of Mars, which was called the Lot of Boldness by the ancients, is taken by day from Mars to the Lot of Fortune, and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. 

Its significations are these: it signifies the arrangement of armies, wars, and battles; integrity, sharpness of mind, boldness, strength, anticipation, and greatness of heart with impulse and haste. It also signifies lustful incests born of cunning and seductions.

### Concerning the Lot of Venus, which is called the Lot of Love and Concord.

**T**he Lot of Venus, which is called the Lot of Love and Concord, is taken by day from the Lot of Fortune to the Lot of the Future, and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. 

Its significations are these: it signifies pleasures, cravings, and desire in sexual matters and in the pursuit of them (both lawful and unlawful), and in those whom the lustful love and in whom they delight, and what the soul desires; also marriages and all things that look toward the utility of sexual union, and joy from games, and cheerfulness and delights.

### Concerning the Lot of Mercury, which is called the Lot of Poverty and Little Intellect.

**T**he Lot of Mercury, which is called the Lot of Poverty and Little Intellect, is taken by day from the Lot of the Future to the Part

...of Fortune: and at night it is projected from the Ascendant. And this here signifies poverty and a smallness of talent and intellect; it also signifies war, fear, hatred, intentions, injuries, and anger in the hour of injuries and enemies. It also signifies negotiations, buying, and selling, as well as thoughts, talents or cleverness, writings, numbers, and the pursuit of astronomy and diverse sciences. ¶ This is the method for extracting the Parts of the seven planets, and what has been said regarding them are their significations. Hence, if you extract any Part based on any of the predicted significators and project it into any chart, judge it according to what you see of its conjunction (or its ruler's conjunction) with the planets, or their aspects, whether they be good or bad. I do not wish to introduce the diversities of opinions among the ancients to you, because this is the more correct way followed by our most reverend predecessors: Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic founder of hermetic philosophy and astrology</note>, Guellius, and Albumasar <note>Abu Ma'shar, the 9th-century Persian astrologer</note>, who is called the "flower of the Latins" <note>original: "flos latinorum"; a title of high respect for Abu Ma'shar, whose works were fundamental to Latin medieval astrology</note> although he studied in Athens where study then flourished, and likewise their followers. Other significations of the Parts will be discussed below after this in their own place and in their own chapter, if God permits.

## Chapter Three: Concerning the Significations of the Parts of the Twelve Houses.

**H**aving spoken of the significations of the parts of the seven planets and their extraction, we must next speak of the significations of the parts of the twelve houses and their extraction likewise. The Parts mentioned above are those which are in themselves more useful and more necessary. And when it is noted in the place of any Part to "take from such a planet to such a planet" or "from such a place to such a place and project from the Ascendant," I say that you should always add the remainder between both places to that which is at the beginning of the sign from which it is projected, just as was given in the work on extracting the Lot of Fortune according to how others have extracted it. It does not seem to me that the diversities of opinions should be recited here; rather, one should apply the mind only to what is of greater utility. For the things signified by each house are not identical for everyone, but diverse, even though some have their beginning or origin from the same house. For example, regarding the significations of death, the end will not be the same for all, yet all signify death: for some die from infirmities in their beds or elsewhere; others from brief illnesses; others from long ones; some die from a sudden arrival of death; others by the sword; others by fire; some are suffocated; others drowned; others hanged; and men die in almost innumerable ways. And although the modes are not the same, nevertheless each of them is death. So it is also with the professions <term>magisterijs: occupations or masteries</term> which are signified by the tenth house, for a magistracy is one thing, a kingdom another, a government another, a dukedom another, an earldom another, and a blacksmith’s craft or a daughter <note>original: "filia," perhaps a scribal error for a trade or specific role</note> another. And although they are not all the same mode, nevertheless all have their origin from the thing signifying honors and dignity. And thus each of the significations of any house acts according to its own being and the nature of the house whose significations it was necessary to know. And many other parts will be found which would be tedious to relate; but you shall consider them as they come to your hand and by your own industry. Do not let what I say to you be a burden: if all things signified by the houses cannot be revealed at once and at the same time, others will explain to you so many and such great things that will suffice for you for the extraction of all the Parts of the houses. For once any upright person has seen the Part signifying a certain thing through one of the houses of the circle, he will be able by his own industry to know the Part and comprehend things which have not yet been explained to him.

<column-break/>

## Chapter 4: Concerning the Parts of the First House, namely the Ascendant, and concerning their Extraction and their Significations.

**N**ow concerning the extraction of the parts of the 12 houses: and first concerning the first house, namely the Ascendant, and the significations of its parts and their extraction. ¶ The first house, as was given above in the chapter on the 12 houses, signifies natural life. And I say "natural" for this reason: because due to a fall or some accident, the force of nature is often, indeed many times, overcome, as was said above in another chapter. Therefore, the Lot of Life and its extraction must be considered from this house, for through it the quality of the life of the person born is distinguished, and what their future state will be. And it is extracted from Jupiter and Saturn because of their altitude and long distance from the earth, and because of their motion, which is slower than all the other planets; for this reason, power is given to them over things in which we desire length and durability. And for the reason stated above, the Ascendant participates with them. And this Part is taken by day from Jupiter to Saturn, and at night it is projected from the Ascendant. And this Part is the significator of natural life and signifies the state of the body and its sustenance; if it is well-disposed, it signifies length of life and its continuity, the health of the body, and cheerfulness of the soul. But if it is hindered, it signifies a scarcity of life and its brevity, and an evil state of being with a multitude of diverse infirmities and with sorrow and sadness of the soul. ¶ Likewise, it will signify the state of men in the revolutions of the years, both for the years of births and the years of the world. ¶ Having spoken of the first part of the Ascendant, which is the Lot of Life, we must next speak of its second part, which is the Lot of Durability and Stability. This is the Lot of Confidence <term>pars fiducie: a lot representing self-assurance, stamina, and the strength of the life-force</term> of the Ascendant. Since there is no more noble or more worthy accident in this world, it was necessary that it be perfected by a more noble durability and stability; and it was necessary that this be from the compaction or complexion <term>complexione: the physical and spiritual "makeup" of a person</term> of the body and soul. This could not happen except through the stronger of the celestial bodies, and those are the Luminaries <term>luminaria: the Sun and the Moon</term>, whose parts are found to be stronger and more fortunate than the others, just as the Luminaries are stronger fortunes than the other fortunes, according to how their effects are felt more strongly and clearly than other effects; and they signify the parts of the body and the soul just as the Luminaries themselves do. Nor can durability happen or last in a living being without the compaction of the body and soul; just as they are made and endure through their complexion or union, so they are destroyed through their dissolution or separation. And this was the cause that moved the ancient sages to extract this part, and they calculated it from the Lot of Fortune as from a more dignified place in this way: the Lot of Durability, which is the Lot of Confidence of the Ascendant, is taken by day from the Lot of Fortune to the Lot of the Future <note>Lot of the Future: another name for the Lot of Spirit or the Lot of the Sun</note>; but at night it is projected from the Ascendant. ¶ And Albumasar said this part corresponds to the Lot of Venus; and certain other things are understood through this part that are not understood through other parts. And this Part signifies the beauty of the person born and their deformity; likewise their similarity to their parents. ¶ When this Part or its ruler is well-disposed in the birth of someone, the person born will be beautiful of body, beautiful of face, and surrounded on all sides in all parts of their body with beauty and health; and this will extend to their successors and endure until some misfortune resists them and hinders them. They will abound in goods, and all the more if the Lot of Fortune and the Lot of the Future are well-disposed; and even more so if their rulers are fortunate. For then they shall have that which they desire: there will be many and very great gains both in journeys or pilgrimages and in other places. But if this Part is hindered, it signifies deformity and a shameful form for the person born, and their body will be of a bad complexion and sickly.
