### Of the Extraction of the Parts

...circumvented by misfortunes: and if it is unfortunate, everything will fall into deterioration <note>original: "dērium," likely "deterius" or "delirium" in this context referring to a worsening state</note> according to the site and disposition of the aforementioned Parts and their significators. And perhaps these things will extend to their descendants until some good fortune is found among their significators in the nativity of any of them. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** <note>9th-century Persian astrologer Albumasar</note> said: if it should incline toward the significator of the father, the child will be similar and well-suited to the father; and if it should incline toward the significator of the mother, the child will be similar and well-suited to the mother. And he said: if you wish to know the durability of any thing—whether it be a nativity <note>a birth chart</note>, or an interrogation <note>a horary question</note>, or a revolution <note>a solar return chart</note>, or in any other way you wish to know its durability or its defect, whether the matter be known or unknown, manifest or hidden—look to this Part. If the Lord of the house, or of the exaltation, or of the two other dignities <note>the secondary astrological strengths like triplicity or term</note> of the sign in which the Part is located regards it, or if it is with the Lord of the Ascendant of that year, or with any of the Lords of the <term>Angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the strongest points in a chart</note>, and it is located in an Angle, it signifies the stability and durability of the matter; and it is greater and firmer when it is in the first or the tenth house. If, however, it is in a <term>Cadent</term> <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, considered weak or declining</note> house, it signifies its removal and destruction. If it is in a <term>Succedent</term> <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses</note> house, and more strongly if it is in the second or eighth, it signifies a durability of the matter that is always doubtful and fearful. If it is hindered in an Angle, it signifies durability with sadness and horror. But if a <term>Fortune</term> <note>A beneficial planet like Venus or Jupiter</note> is with it, or regards it by a trine or sextile aspect, or even by a square aspect with <term>Reception</term> <note>An astrological condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it aspects, facilitating a "handshake" between them</note>, and that Fortune is not hindered, there will be durability in the house, albeit with fear or suspicion. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** said: if it is in its recession, being fortunate, it will enjoy fortune according to its recession. But if it is hindered, it will be evil and horrible according to the quantity of its recession. And if it should be in any revolution as was said regarding that Part, this will be among men beyond what is customary, and they will be more stable, constant, and firm than usual. ¶ Having spoken of the first and second Parts of the Ascendant, we must now speak of its third Part, which is called the **Part of Reason and Sense**. And since a human being cannot truly exist without reason and sense, the wise men considered from whence they might extract the Part of Reason and Sense. Indeed, they saw that **Mercury** was naturally the significator of both: of thought, speech, and cognition; and **Mars** was the significator of heat and motion. They extracted from these two the Part which they called the **Part of Reason and Sense**; this can also be called the Part of Thought and Speech, which is taken by day from Mercury to Mars and by night the contrary, and is projected from the Ascendant. And they said that this Part has the significance of sense and reason; it also signifies science, thought, cognition, and speech. If this Part in someone's nativity is well-disposed and is with the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord of the house in which it sits, or if its Lord regards the Lord of the Ascendant in its own dignity—and if Mercury then regards the Part and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Parts by a trine or sextile aspect, or at least by a square with reception—that person, fortunate, strong, and unhindered, will be of a rational nature: knowing, speaking, thinking, and cognizant. And if Mars then regards the Ascendant or its Lord or the Lord of the Part, he will be naturally wise as I said, and will be of sharp wit, learning easily and retaining well those things he has learned, nor will he be forgetful. ¶ And if it should be in any revolution as was said regarding nativities, men in 그hat revolution will be of better wit and better intellect, and of better memory than they are accustomed to be. ¶ Having spoken of the first, second, and third Parts of the first house, it remains to speak of its fourth Part, which is called the **Part of Ysech** <note>original: "pars ysech"; likely a Latinization of the Arabic "al-Isah," often associated with the Lot of Life or Hyleg</note>, of which the ancients did not care

<column-break/>

to make much mention, because it is so intertwined with the others that none of them can exist without it, while it can well exist without the others. Indeed, they relate to it as matter relates to form; and the wise could have placed it first if they had wished, but they left it for the aforementioned reason: for it is the root of the others and is taken by day and night from the degree of the **Conjunction** or **Prevention** <note>The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth or event</note> that occurred before the nativity, question, or revolution, unto the degree of the Moon, and it is projected from the Ascendant. And this Part is called the **Root of Life**, because it universally encompasses the whole being of the native or the querent, or even of the revolution. If it is well-disposed, it signifies universally the well-being of the life of the native and his other subjects; if, however, it is poorly disposed, it signifies the opposite of the aforementioned.

## Chapter 5: Concerning the Parts of the Second House, their Extraction, and their Significations.

**A**fter having spoken above concerning the Parts of the first house, we must speak immediately concerning the Parts of the second house, which is called the **House of Substance**; for the first thing a human needs after birth is substance, and first life, and for this reason the significance of substance was given to the second house. Its first Part is called the **Part of Substance**, which is taken by day and night from the Lord of the house of substance unto the degree of the house of substance, and is projected from the Ascendant. And this Part signifies the sustenance of the lives of men and their very gain, and the other things which men use for their livelihood. If it is well-disposed and well-located, it signifies the well-being of the native and the querent, both in livelihood and in profit and similar things. If, however, it is hindered, it signifies the opposite of those things which were said. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** said: as for the other apparent species of fortune from substance—namely those which are treasured and saved—other significators of substance and fortune signify them. The same happens in revolutions. And the **Part of Poverty** is among the Parts of Mercury. ¶ The **Part of Usurers** <note>original: "Pars feneratoꝝ" (feneratorum), referring to moneylenders or those dealing in interest</note> is taken by day and night from Saturn to Mercury and is projected from the Ascendant. If it is fortunate and well-disposed, it signifies profit and the increase of substance by reason of usury and usurers. If, however, it is hindered and the Lord of substance is hindered, it signifies that the native will lose the greatest part of his substance by reason of usury and usurers and the like; and similarly the querent. The same thing happens in revolutions; for the substances of men will be disposed according to the disposition of the aforementioned Part. ¶ The **Part of Happiness** <note>original: "Pars beatitudinis"</note>, which elsewhere is called the **Part of Jupiter** and is called the **Part of Triumph and Victory**, is taken by day from Saturn to Jupiter and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. ¶ The fourth Part of the second house, which is called the **Part of Collection**, is taken by day from Mercury to Venus and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And this Part signifies lost things or half-dispersed things which someone sometimes finds on journeys, in the streets, fields, the seashore, or riverbanks, in the mountains, or by digging, or in another unthought-of way; or if it was a thing that had fallen or fled from someone, or if he had forgotten it, or it had departed from its master in another similar way or left his hands. If this Part is in an Angle and some Lord of its dignity in the sign where it sits, or any of the Luminaries <note>The Sun or the Moon</note>, is joined to it (unless it be <term>Combust</term> <note>Too close to the Sun, which weakens a planet's power</note>) or regards it by a trine or sextile aspect, the aforementioned things will come into the hands of the native or querent, and he will be fortunate in them; and he will find his things if they fell from him, or if he forgot them, or if they fled from him as was said of the things of others. And if the significators of the Part are good in the places where they are and have a root in the nativity...

The same will happen to men in revolutions <note>Solar returns, or the annual "birthday" chart of a person or the world</note> when the aforementioned things or significators are thus disposed.

### Chapter 6: Concerning the Parts of the Third House, their Extraction, and their Significance.

The Third House has three parts. ¶ The first is of **brothers** <note>original: "fratrum"</note> and is taken by day and night from Saturn to Jupiter and cast from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>. And the Lord of the house of this Part signifies the affairs of the brothers and their harmony. And if this Part falls in a sign of many children, the brothers will be many; specifically, the number of brothers is found by the number of signs between this Part and its Lord, giving one brother for each sign. ¶ The second Part, concerning the **number of brothers**, is taken from Mercury to Saturn and joined with it, and cast from the Ascendant: and if it falls in a sign of many children, there will be many brothers and sisters according to the number of signs and planets; and perhaps the number reaches the quantity of the planets' years—whether short, mean, or great; and planets aspecting <note>forming a geometric relationship with</note> it increase their years. And if this Part falls in a sign of few children, there will be few. ¶ The third Part is of the **death of brothers and sisters**: this is taken by day from the Sun to the degree of the Midheaven <note>original: "medij celi," the highest point in the chart</note> and increased; and it is cast from the Ascendant: and it signifies the cause of the death of brothers and sisters. When this Part reaches the significator of brothers and sisters, or vice versa, according to the <term>profection</term> <note>A technique that "advances" the chart by one sign per year</term> of the signs and the direction of the degrees, the brothers and sisters will suffer evil.

### Chapter 7: Concerning the Parts of the Fourth House, their Extraction, and their Significance.

Now we must speak of the Parts of the Fourth House: and first of the **Part of the Father**, which is taken by day from the Sun to Saturn, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. This Part is taken from these two planets because Saturn signifies antiquity and masculinity, and the Sun signifies natural heat, which is the cause of the life of living things; and fathers are older than their children and are the cause of their children. If, however, it happens that Saturn is "under the rays" of the Sun <note>original: "sub radijs solis," meaning the planet is so close to the Sun it is invisible and weakened</note>, then the Part of the Father is taken by day from the Sun to Jupiter, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. And **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "albumasar," a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that the Lord of the house of the father signifies the father's fortune, his substance <note>wealth</note>, and his labors. If the Part is in a good state, the father will be noble. And if its Lord is in a good state, he will be fortunate and long-lived. If, however, it is impeded or poorly placed, he will be hardworking, unfortunate, and short-lived. And the Lord says this governs the kingdom of the native, his honors, and his strengths. ¶ The second Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of the Death of the Father**, is taken by day from Saturn to Jupiter, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. This Part signifies the cause of the fathers' death; and whenever the profection of the year reaches this Part or its Lord, it signifies danger and horror for the father; likewise when one of them reaches the significator of the father. ¶ The third Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of Grandfathers**, is taken by day from the Lord of the house of the Sun to Saturn, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. If the Sun is in Leo, it is taken by day from the first degree of Leo to Saturn, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. And if it is in Capricorn or Aquarius, it is taken by day from the Sun to Saturn, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. You need not care then whether Saturn is under the rays of the Sun or not. This Part signifies the affairs of grandfathers. Whenever it is joined with the <term>fortunes</term> <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</term>, they will find the grandfather's good. And whenever it is joined with the <term>inflexible ones</term> <note>original: "malis," the malefic planets Saturn and Mars</note>, they will find the grandfather's dangers. ¶ The fourth Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of Parentage**, kinship, or nobility, is taken by day from Saturn to Mars, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascen-

<column-break/>

-dant; and they add from above the degrees which Saturn has traveled in the sign in which it is, and it is cast from the beginning of that same sign: and where it falls, there shall be this Part. And **Abu Ma'shar** said: after this, look if this Part is in an <term>Angle</term> <note>The most powerful houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note> and if any of the Lords of the dignities of the sign in which it is regards it—either the Sun, or the Lord of the Tenth House, or any of the Lords of the Angles—with an aspect of friendship <note>Trines or sextiles</note>, the native will be of noble progeny or honest parentage. If, however, the Part falls away from the Angles and is joined to the malefics, or if none of the Lords of the dignities of its sign or the Lords of the Angles regard it, he will be considered lowly in his parentage, kinship, or nobility. ¶ The fifth Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of Inheritances** or possessions, is taken by day and night from Saturn to the Moon and cast from the Ascendant. And **Abu Ma'shar** said that this Part relates to the Part of the King or the kingdom, or what kind of work the native will perform: when it is in a good state and well-located, and its Lord likewise, it will bring fortune to the native by reason of inheritances and by reason of the tilling of the earth and sowing, and he will acquire substance. If it is in a bad state and poorly located, it signifies grief, sadness, dejection, or evil and horror by reason of the aforementioned things. ¶ Likewise, there is another **Part of Inheritances** according to the sages of the Persians, and it is the sixth Part of the Fourth House: this Part is taken by day from Mercury to Jupiter, and in the night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. This Part is considered neither in the kingdom, nor in mastery, nor in the tilling of the earth, nor in seeds, but only in those things which are called inheritances. ¶ The seventh Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of Tilling the Earth**, is taken by day and night from Venus to Saturn and cast from the Ascendant: if it is fortunate and its Lord is fortunate, the native or the seeker will have good and utility from the cultivation of the earth, sowing, and planting; and he will be fortunate in them. The same will happen to men regarding the aforementioned things generally in the revolutions of the years of the world, and to natives in the revolutions of their births, if the aforementioned things are so disposed. If, however, they are impeded, the good of the aforementioned will not happen to them, but the contrary will follow. ¶ The eighth Part of the Fourth House according to **Al-Qabisi** <note>original: "Alphabicicū," referring to the 10th-century astrologer Alchabitius</note>, which is called the **Part of Nobility** of the native, and of that which is doubted—namely, whether one is the son of the father to whom he is attributed or of another—is taken by day from the degree of the Sun to the degree of its exaltation <note>19 degrees of Aries</note> and cast from the Ascendant. ¶ The ninth Part of the Fourth House, which is called the **Part of the Ends of Things**, is taken by day from Saturn to the Lord of the house of the <term>conjunction</term> <note>The New Moon occurring before the birth</term> if it was conjunctional, or to the Lord of the house of the <term>prevention</term> <note>The Full Moon occurring before the birth</term> if it was preventional, and cast from the Ascendant. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** said that if this Part and its Lord are in signs of direct ascension <note>Signs that take longer to rise, associated with ease</note> or are otherwise fortunate, the end of the native's or seeker's affairs will be of a good or praiseworthy state. If, however, they are in "crooked" signs <note>Signs that rise quickly, associated with difficulty</note> or are impeded, their ends will be evil. And if one of them is in a direct sign and the other in a crooked sign, the ends will be entangled, neither entirely good nor entirely evil. And **Abu Ma'shar** said after this that the matter returns to what the sign in which the Lord of that Part is located signifies.

### Chapter 8: Concerning the Parts of the Fifth House, their Extraction, and their Significance.

Here we must speak of the Parts of the Fifth House, and first of the **Part of Children**, which is taken by day from Jupiter to Saturn and by night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. For by this Part it is signified whether the native or seeker is to have children or not. And **Abu Ma'shar** said that if this Part or its Lord is in a sign of many children, he will have many children; and if it is in a sign of few children, he will have few children. And if it is in a sterile sign, he will have no children. If, however...

# Concerning the extraction of the Parts

If this Part signifies children and is fortunate and well-disposed, the children will live well. If, however, it is impeded <note>afflicted by difficult planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, it signifies that they will not live. And he said it also signifies the general state of the children, how they will behave toward their father, and how one might love or hate him. He also said that one takes the signs between this Part and its Lord <note>the planet that rules the sign where the Part is located</note>, and assigns a child to each sign. He noted that if there is a **common sign** <note>a "mutable" sign like Gemini or Virgo, which represents changeability</note> between them, the number of that sign is doubled, for two children are placed where only one was before. He said that if there is a planet between them, one child is counted for it, just as was said above regarding brothers.

¶ The **second Part** of the fifth house, which signifies the hour in which a child should be born, the number of children, and whether they are male or female, is taken by day and night from Mars to Jupiter and cast from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>. This is because the outcome of children is signified by Jupiter due to the heat and moisture of his nature, and also as a cause of growth; and by the significance of Mars over heat, and because of his motion, delight, and the natural desire for intercourse, which is stronger in men. And since a child cannot be made except through the intercourse of men and women and through natural heat and moisture, these are the reasons for extracting this Part from them.

¶ And **Hermes** said that if the first Part and the other significators <note>planets representing the matter</note> of children indicate offspring to the person born or the one asking, then this Part signifies their number. Because of this, when Jupiter reaches this Part or its location by body or by a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> <note>harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees</note> aspect—and even more strongly if there is <term>reception</term> <note>when planets are in each other's signs, indicating cooperation</note>—it signifies that he will beget a child in that same hour, if his age permits.

¶ And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said if it is in a masculine sign, his children will clearly be male; if it is in a feminine sign, they will mostly be female. He said if the significators indicate a multitude of children to the born or the seeker, look at this Part and its Lord and in what sign it sits: for this signifies that there will be children according to the number of the **minor, mean, or great years** <note>specific time periods assigned to each planet in ancient astrology</note> of the Lord of the Part. He also said that perhaps the planets aspecting it will increase the number according to their own years.

¶ The **third Part** of the fifth house, which signifies **male children**, is taken by day and night from the Moon to Jupiter and cast from the Ascendant.

¶ **Alchabicius** <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century astrologer</note> said it is taken by day from the Lord of the house of the Moon to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. This Part is extracted thus because the Moon signifies youth and those of minor age, who are stronger in generating from the time they can generate than the elderly; and the operations of nature ought to be more noble or powerful in that age than in others due to the proximity of birth. Furthermore, generating males is more noble than generating females, for males are active and females are passive, and action is more noble and worthy than passion. Since Jupiter is the significator of the outcome of children and their creation and growth, especially of males, the wise ones calculated this Part from them.

¶ **Theophilus** <note>Theophilus of Edessa, an 8th-century court astrologer</note> and certain other wise men were seen to wish to say something else. But **Albumasar** held the word of **Hermes** as more authentic. They likewise said that this Part assisted the fortune of the person born just like the **Part of Fortune**; nor was this disputed by the wise of that time.

¶ The **fourth Part** of the fifth house, which signifies **daughters**, according to Alchabicius, is taken by day and night from the Moon to Venus and cast from the Ascendant.

¶ The **fifth Part** of the fifth house, through which it is known whether a **conception** is male or female, is taken by day from the Lord of the house of the Moon and by night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. If it falls in a masculine sign, then the one born or the one being asked about will be male; if in a feminine sign, it will be female.

### Chapter 9: Concerning the parts of the sixth house, their extraction, and their significance.

<sig>EE</sig>

<column-break/>

The narration of the parts of the sixth house, and first concerning the **Part of Infirmities**, accidents, and inseparable vices, which is taken by day from Saturn to Mars and by night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant.

¶ The **second Part** of the sixth house, which is called the Part of Infirmities both separable and inseparable, is taken by day and night from Mercury to Mars and cast from the Ascendant.

¶ The **third Part** of the sixth house, which is called the **Part of Servants** according to Alchabicius and Theophilus, is taken by day from Mercury to the Moon and by night the reverse, and cast from the Ascendant. However, according to Hermes, whose opinion was held as more authentic by the wise, it is taken by day and night from Mercury to the Moon and cast from the Ascendant. This is because he and other wise men of those times considered servants, handmaids, and mostly attendants, followers, and messengers to be not very faithful and quickly changeable; and they attributed all these things and other matters of swift and rapid change to these lighter <note>faster-moving</note> planets. For this reason, they extracted this Part from them. If it is fortunate and well-disposed, and its Lord likewise, it signifies that the person born or seeking will have good from the aforementioned significations of the Part. If, however, they are impeded, it signifies the opposite. If the Part is well-disposed but its Lord is impeded, or vice-versa, it signifies that he will have good from them at first, but then the opposite will happen. And if this Part is in a sign of many children, he will have many servants and handmaids or other attendants. If it is in a sign of few children, he will have few servants. If it is in a **sterile sign**, he will lack them entirely. This same thing happens in the revolutions <note>annual charts</note> of those who have those Parts.

¶ **Theophilus** and certain others said that this Part is taken from Mercury to the **Part of Fortune**.

¶ **Albumasar** more highly praised the word of **Hermes**.

¶ The **fourth Part** of the sixth house, which is called the **Part of Captives** and the bound, is taken by day from the Lord of the house of the Sun to the Sun, and by night from the Lord of the house of the Moon to the Moon, and cast from the Ascendant. If it falls in a good place <note>a "good" house like the 1st, 10th, or 11th</note> from the Ascendant and is with one of the Fortunes <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, the seeker or the captive will be liberated from that captivity. But if it falls in a malignant place and with the Malefics <note>Saturn or Mars</note>, it signifies evil and horror for the captive or the bound; and perhaps it signifies the death of the captive, especially if the Lord of the tenth house aspects it.

¶ And **Albumasar** said if the Sun is in his own house by day, or the Moon by night, one of them will be the significator. He said after this, look at which of them is the significator, in what place of the circle it is, and from what it separates or to what it joins, and work according to this. Understand the same in revolutions.

### Chapter 10: Concerning the parts of the seventh house, their extraction, and their significance.

A discourse on the parts of the seventh house, and first concerning the **Part of Marriage of Men**, which is taken by day and night from Saturn to Venus and cast from the Ascendant. **Hermes** and other wise men extracted it from these two planets because Saturn signifies antiquity and durable things, and marriage ought to be among durable things. Saturn also has significance over masculinity, and Venus has significance over femininity; and masculinity ought to precede femininity by the nature of masculinity and action. If this Part is well-disposed and well-placed, it signifies a fitting and well-fortuned marriage, and that the person born or seeking will profit, and good will follow from the marriage.

...that marriage <note>original: "trimonio illo"</note>: and it also signifies that he will contract a marriage with a beautiful and decent woman. If, however, it is impeded <note>afflicted by difficult planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, it signifies that the union will be bad and harmful, and that loss, danger, and restlessness with adversities will follow from it. You will also see if Jupiter reaches this Part or aspects it with a praiseworthy <term>aspect</term> <note>A specific geometric angle between planets, like a trine or sextile</note>; for then the marriage will be praiseworthy if it was consummated at that hour. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "Albumasar," a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said when this Part is with the ruler of the sign in which it is located, or if the Sun and Moon aspect it and its ruler with a strong and praiseworthy aspect, it signifies that the <term>native</term> <note>The person for whom the horoscope is cast</note> or the <term>querent</term> <note>The person asking the astrological question</note> will be joined with someone from his own family or kin. You should understand this same thing regarding marriages that occur in <term>revolutions</term> <note>A solar return chart, cast for one's birthday to predict the year ahead</note> when the aforesaid Part or its Lord is disposed in the way that was described. ¶ **Abu Ma'shar** said the **second Part of marriage for men**, which **Vettius Valens** <note>original: "Uuellius," a 2nd-century Greek astrologer</note> described, is taken by day and night from the Sun to Venus and projected from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>. ¶ The **third Part of the seventh house** is the **Part of Cunning and Ingenuity of men toward women**, and it is similar to the Part of marriage for men according to Vettius Valens. ¶ The **fourth Part of the seventh house** is the **Part of Sexual Intercourse of men with women**; it is also similar to Vettius Valens's Part of marriage for men. ¶ The **fifth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Lust and Fornication of men**, is taken by day and night from Venus to Saturn and projected from the Ascendant; if it is in a good place, the marriage will be praiseworthy, and the man will succeed with whichever woman he desires. If, however, it is poorly located, the marriage will be blameworthy, and he will not be able to succeed with any of them. And **Abu Ma'shar** said if it is impeded in a sign signifying sexual intercourse, the man will be very lascivious in intercourse and a fornicator. If, however, it is fortunate, he will be a man of much intercourse, but his intercourse will be of a praiseworthy sort. And he spoke regarding the significance of the **Part of Lasciviousness and Fornication of men**: if the Lord of the Part of the Nuptials of Men, which **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of astrology</note> described, falls with the Part of Vettius Valens, or if the Lord of this Part aspects the Part of the Nuptials of Men, he will fornicate with a woman before he is joined in the manner of a marriage; and the matter will be made public after he has been a fornicator. ¶ The **sixth Part of the seventh house**, which is the **Part of Marriage for women**, **Hermes** said is similar to the cause of the marriage of men, and it is taken by day and night from Venus to Saturn and projected from the Ascendant. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** said that this Part corresponds to the Part of the Cultivation of the Earth. **Vettius Valens**, however, took it by day and night from the Sun to Mars and projected it from the Ascendant. **Hermes**, however, was more authentic than him. If this Part and its Lord are well-disposed and in a good state, they signify fortune for women through marriage. If, however, they are impeded, they signify sorrows, sadness, afflictions, or tribulations found because of marriage, and the woman will be lascivious. Likewise, **Vettius Valens** took it in another way—and he took it better—for he took it by day and night from the Moon to Mars and projected it from the Ascendant; and this method pleased **Abu Ma'shar** more: and this is the **seventh Part**. ¶ The **eighth Part of the seventh house** is called the **Part of Ingenuity and Cunning of women toward men**. **Hermes** said it is similar to the Part of marriage for women. ¶ The **ninth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Pleasure and Delight**, is taken by day and night from Venus to the degree and minute of the seventh house and projected from the Ascendant. ¶ The **tenth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Lasciviousness of women and their shame**, **Vettius Valens** said is similar to the Part of marriage for women, which is taken by day from Venus to Saturn and projected from the Ascendant. When this is in a good state and well-disposed, the woman will be pleased with her marriage and will praise it. If, however, it is in a bad state and poorly disposed, her marriage will displease her and she will blaspheme

<column-break/>

it, and she will be saddened and afflicted because of it, and she will strive in cunning and ingenuity for the deception of men. And if this Part is in a good state and well-located, or if it is in the signs of cunning and ingenuity—which are Leo, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Pisces—the woman will seduce whichever man she wishes. If, however, it is outside a sign of cunning and ingenuity, or if it is otherwise poorly located, she will not be able to seduce any of them. And regarding the significance of the **Part of Conjunction and Intercourse** of them: if it is impeded in a sign signifying intercourse, she will be a foul fornicatrix, evil and lascivious. If, however, it is fortunate in a sign signifying intercourse, she will have much pleasure in intercourse, yet in a fitting way. And regarding the significance of the **Part of Lasciviousness of women and their shame**: **Abu Ma'shar** said if the Part of marriage of women which **Hermes** described is with this Part which **Vettius Valens** described, and the Lord of this Part is with the Part of marriage, she will fornicate with a man and afterwards be joined to him. ¶ The **eleventh Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Religion and Honesty of the woman**, is taken by day and night from the Moon to Venus and projected from the Ascendant. And he said this is the **Part of Daughters**; if it falls in a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius—signs associated with stability</note>, or in the aspect of any of the Lords of the dignities of the sign in which it is, or with any fortune <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, the woman will be honest and religious, even if she is desiring of intercourse. If, however, malefic planets aspect it without <term>reception</term> <note>A condition where planets are in signs ruled by one another, indicating mutual support</note>, and it is in a <term>mobile sign</term> <note>A "cardinal" sign like Aries or Cancer, associated with change</note>, the woman will have excessive pleasure in the cause of intercourse, damaging herself through vice and inviting men to intercourse for any price; and she will be in every way a fornicatrix. ¶ The **twelfth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Marriage for men and women according to Hermes**, is taken from Venus to the degree and minute of the <term>Angle of Nuptials</term> <note>The cusp of the 7th house</note>—that is, the seventh—and projected from the Ascendant: if this is joined to the fortunes, the woman will marry and good things will be said of her marriage. If, however, it is in a bad state and poorly located, and joined to malifics or they aspect it without perfect reception, her marriage will be made public and she will fall into the reproach of the people. If, however, the Lord of the sign in which the Part is located is in a malignant place, and Venus is <term>under the rays</term> <note>Combust, or so close to the Sun that its power is weakened</note> of the Sun or impeded by Saturn, the woman will never marry but will lead her life in a foul way. ¶ The **thirteenth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Honor of Marriage**, is taken by day and night from the Sun to the Moon and projected from the Ascendant: if Jupiter aspects this with a praiseworthy aspect, or is joined to it bodily, and they are in a good state, and it is for a man, the man will marry a beautiful, honest, pleasing, and desirable woman. And **Abu Ma'shar** said this Part is used in this way because when the birth of a man signifies that he will marry, the cause of this thing is this: that one of the <term>luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and Moon</note> is hot and masculine, and the other is moist and feminine. And he said that through the conjunction of heat and masculinity with moisture and femininity, all generation occurs in this world; and for this reason, this Part was so named. ¶ The **fourteenth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Ingenuity and Ease of Marriage**, is taken by day and night from the Sun to the Moon and projected from the degree and minute of Venus: if it falls in a sign of cunning and is in a good state, fortunate, strong, and well-disposed, it signifies that he who has desired marriage will be completed with ease according to what he had devised. If, however, it is impeded and in a bad state, his marriage will be with hardship and affliction; and the man will never be able to reach that which he intended. ¶ The **fifteenth Part of the seventh house**, which is called the **Part of Fathers-in-law**, is taken by day and night from Saturn to Venus and projected from the Ascendant. ¶ And **Abu Ma'shar** said that this Part...

...agrees with the **Part of Marriage for Men** <note>original: "parti coniugij viroz"</note> which **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Hermeticism and astrology</note> discussed. And **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "Albumasar"</note> said that if this Part is in the Ascendant, or with its Lord in any <term>angle</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of a chart</note>, the native will be much given to contention. If the Part is fortunate, something evil and horrible will follow from the contention. But if this Part falls with the Lord of the Seventh House in the Ascendant, the person will be among those who plead cases before kings and judges.

### Chapter Eleven: Concerning the Parts of the Eighth House, their extraction, and their significations.

<margin>8 e</margin>
In this chapter, we must discuss the Parts of the **Eighth House** <note>The house governing death, inheritance, and shared resources</note>. There are five parts. The first is the **Part of Death**, which is extracted from three significators: it is taken by day and night from the Moon to the degree of the Eighth House, and to this is added the distance Saturn has traveled within the sign in which he resides, and it is projected from the beginning of that same sign. It is extracted in this way because the Moon is the significator of bodies, and the Eighth House is the significator of death which must destroy bodies; Saturn, moreover, signifies the end of things, as well as sorrow, sadness, weeping, lamentation, anguish, dissolution, and destruction—all of which follow from death. For this reason, the signification of the fact of death was given to these three indicators. If this Part and its Lord are free, in a good state, and well-placed, the native will die in his own bed a natural death. If, however, they are impeded and the <term>fortunes</term> <note>The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> do not aspect them (or at least one of them), the native will die a most foul death. If these aforesaid significators are so poorly disposed in any <term>revolution</term> <note>A solar return chart for the year</note> as described, many will die such a death in that year. ¶ The **second Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Killing Planet** <note>original: "planete interficientis," also known as the Anareta</note>, is taken by day from the Lord of the Ascendant to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part is extracted in this manner because the Lord of the Ascendant signifies the soul, and the Moon signifies the body (though sometimes one is put for the other). While the soul embraces the body, it signifies temperament, and they remain as long as they are in concord together; when they are divided, however, the body perishes, though the soul remains. Because of this, the Part was thus extracted by the wise. And Abu Ma'shar said that if the Moon alone aspects this Part and the Part itself is in a sign of "severed limbs" <note>Signs like Scorpio or others associated with physical damage</note> and is impeded, or if the Lord of the sign in which the Part resides or the Lords of the signs in which they reside impede one another, the person will die while suffering. If, however, they are not impeded and do not impede one another, the Moon will then be "mutilated," but the person will not die from it. ¶ The **third Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Year in which Death is Feared**, or affliction, destruction, impediment, or heavy burden, is taken by day from Saturn to the Lord of the House of the <term>Conjunction or Prevention</term> <note>The New Moon (Conjunction) or Full Moon (Prevention/Syzygy) immediately preceding the birth</note> which occurred before the birth, question, or revolution, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part is extracted thus because Saturn signifies cold, death, the end, and afflictions which lead to destruction, and the degree of the Conjunction or Prevention is similar; therefore, they calculated this Part from those two

<column-break/>

places. And Abu Ma'shar said this Part is related to the **Part of the End of Things**. He said when this Part and its Lord are impeded along with the Lord of the Ascendant, the native will suffer many infirmities and afflictions in both body and substance <note>Wealth or property</note>, and will many times approach the destruction of the body and the loss of substance. And whenever the year reaches this Part—whether through <term>profections</term> <note>A predictive technique where the chart is "advanced" by one sign per year</note> by which one sign is given for each year, or through <term>direction</term> <note>Primary directions, a calculation based on the rotation of the Earth</note> made by the degrees of ascension to the Ascendant or its Lord—the native will encounter dangers in his body and limbs from infirmities, and will find anguish and horrible things in his substance; he will also fear death from various quarters. ¶ The **fourth Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Heavy Place** <note>original: "loci ponderosi," often referring to burdens or chronic issues</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to Mars, and by night the reverse, and to this is added the distance Mercury has traveled in the sign where he resides, and it is projected from the beginning of that same sign. Abu Ma'shar said this Part is similar to the Part of Parentage. He said if this Part and the Lord of the Ascendant are impeded in anyone's birth, they will have an inseparable infirmity called <term>azamena</term> <note>A term derived from Arabic meaning a chronic physical defect or deformity</note> in the limb assigned to that sign in which the Part resides. He will be unfortunate in all his business, and will be so occupied and troubled by them that he cannot bring them to a good end. Whenever he does bring matters to a conclusion, whether for good or ill, they will be delayed and he will hardly be able to accomplish them. Abu Ma'shar also said when the year arrives from the Ascendant to this Part, or the Part arrives at the Ascendant or its Lord through profections or directions, the native's affairs will be burdened in 그 year; whatever he hoped for from his works will be delayed, and for that reason he will find sorrow, sadness, and afflictions. He shall begin nothing in that year that will be completed to his prosperity, but rather to his loss; he will find infirmities in the limb assigned to the sign where the year of the revolution reaches this Part. And if the <term>malifics</term> <note>The "bad" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> aspect it, anguish and ruin will find him. ¶ The **fifth Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of Riding, Heaviness, and Destruction** <note>original: "equitationis z grauitatis atqz destructionis"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to Mercury, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. If it happens that the Lord of the Ascendant is impeded with this Part in the <term>radix</term> <note>The original birth chart</note> of the birth, it signifies that the native will be in a state of evil and heaviness for his entire life. If he performs any work in which he has hope of good, he will find heaviness and evil from it, nor will his intentions follow. If the year of profection reaches them (meaning the year following the succession of signs), or through degrees of direction (as described in the treatise on births), the native will encounter an evil from which he will be liberated in that revolution. If he is liberated from it, he may fall into another perhaps no less heavy than the first. If the "fortunes" aspect the place from strong positions, they will alleviate the evil but not remove it entirely.

In this chapter we must speak of the Parts of the **Ninth House** <note>The house of long journeys, religion, philosophy, and dreams</note>, which are seven parts. First is the **Part of Pilgrimage** <note>original: "peregrinationis," also meaning travel or wandering</note>, which is taken by day and night from the Lord of the ninth sign to the degree of the Ninth House, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part signifies...

¶ The **second Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Travel and Pilgrimage in Water** <note>original: "ps itineris ac pegrinationis in aqua"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to the 15th degree of Cancer, and by night from the same [15 Cancer to Saturn], and is projected from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>. If this Part falls in <term>watery signs</term> <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note> along with <term>fortunes</term> <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</note>, the native will find goodness, utility, and profit from sea voyages and their practice, as well as gain and safety. And one of the ancients said: if Saturn is in the 15th degree of Cancer and that degree is the Ascendant, then look to the degrees of Saturn as the more significant indicators; therefore observe them and the aspect of those planets and act according to them.
¶ The **third Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Religion** <note>original: "ps religionis"</note>, is taken by day from the Moon to Mercury, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. If this Part and its Lord fall in the Ascendant, or with its Lord, or with the <term>Almuten</term> <note>The planet that has the most essential dignity or power over a specific point in the chart</note> over it, the native will be religious. And if the significators of the Part aspect the Part and the Lord of the Ascendant, it will be the same. If, however, the Part is impeded, none of the aforesaid will happen, but there will instead be a zeal for them.
¶ The **fourth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Prayer and Depth of Counsel** <note>original: "ps orationis ⁊ profunditatis cōfilij"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part signifies reason, consideration, and the scrutiny of deep matters: also the depth of praiseworthy philosophers and even the discovery of wisdom; and this is stronger if Saturn is above the earth by day, and even more so if he is <term>oriental</term> <note>A planet is oriental when it rises before the Sun</note> aspecting the Part and <term>receiving</term> <note>An astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note> it, or if the Moon is in an excellent place relative to the Ascendant.
¶ The **fifth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Wisdom and Patience** <note>original: "ps sapientie atq; patietie"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and is projected from Mercury. It is taken thus—as with the others—because Saturn signifies stability, philosophy, and depth in things, as well as scrutiny in speech and the lengthiness of thoughts; and Jupiter signifies wisdom, patience, and reason; and Mercury signifies writing, wisdom, and experience—therefore it was appropriate to extract it from them. If Saturn and Jupiter aspect this Part or are joined to it and both or either of them receive it, the native will be wise, patient, and rational. And if Mercury aspects it or is joined to it, he will be wise, of sharp and profound wit, and especially an expert or searcher of deep matters: and he will be swift in the discovery of all things discoverable.
¶ The **sixth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Histories and Knowledge of Rumors and Fables** <note>original: "pars hystoriar̄ ⁊ scientie rumorum ac fabulaz"</note>, is taken by day from the Sun to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "Albumasar," a Persian astrologer (787–886 AD) whose works were fundamental to medieval European astrology</note> said this Part corresponds to the Part of the Father. And he said that when Saturn is <term>under the rays</term> <note>A planet is "under the rays" when it is so close to the Sun that its light is obscured</note>: if this Part falls in an <term>angle</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the strongest points in a chart</note> in aspect to Mercury and Venus, and the Lord of the Ascendant aspects it, the native will retain ancient histories and the rumors of men: and he will be a creator of fables and beautiful narrations by which listeners are delighted, and they laugh and rejoice because of them. And Abu Ma'shar said: if it is otherwise, it will be an error.
¶ The **seventh Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Rumors, whether they be True or False** <note>original: "ps rumoz vtz sint veri vel falsi"</note>, is taken by day and night from Mercury to the Moon and projected from the Ascendant. Abu Ma'shar said this Part is similar to the Part of Servants. If it is in an angle or in a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> or directly ascending, the rumors will be true: and even more so if the Moon is joined to a truth-telling planet. Likewise, it is true if, with this, there is a truth-telling planet in the 8th, 2nd, 5th, or 9th house; if however it is otherwise, it will be the reverse.

### Chapter Thirteen: Concerning the Parts of the Tenth House, their signification, and their extraction.

<column-break/>

In this chapter, discourse must be made concerning the parts of the **Tenth House** <note>The house governing career, authority, kingship, and public reputation</note>: and first concerning the **Part of Nobility** <note>original: "parte nobilitatis"</note>, which is taken by day from the Sun in the 19th degree of Aries (which is the degree of his <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign and degree where a planet is thought to have its greatest power</note>), and by night from the Moon in the 3rd degree of Taurus (which is the degree of her exaltation), and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part is extracted in this way for this reason: because the Sun, who is the light of the day, is the significator of the native's life and his durability by day, and signifies the soul, honor, and loftiness, as well as exaltation, kingdom, and victory; and the Moon is the light of the night and signifies in the night what the Sun signifies in the day. Because of this, it is called the Part of Nobility, because it is extracted from the luminaries, which are the more noble bodies, and from the degrees of their exaltations. Indeed, through this Part, the nobility and high birth of the native is known: and whether he is the son of the one he is said to be or not. Through it, his honor, his exaltation, and his kingdom are known, as well as his loftiness and victory. If this Part falls in a good place, such as the Tenth House, or is with well-placed fortunes and is in a good state, it signifies that the native will come to honor, nobility, exaltation, riches, and the spreading of a good reputation—each according to his rank; so that if he is of those suited for a kingdom, he shall reach it. And if he is of others, he shall reach honors and dignities suitable to him and even transcend them. This same thing will happen if this Part is so disposed in the <term>revolution</term> <note>A chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to its birth position, used for annual predictions</note> of any person. If this Part falls in the aforesaid degrees and the birth is by day, Abu Ma'shar said that the signification of those degrees will be like the signification of the degree of the Ascendant. If the significators of this Part aspect it and are in good <term>complexions</term> <note>The specific mixture of planetary influences or "temperament"</note> with it, the native will be the son of the one to whom he is attributed; but if it is the reverse, he will not be his.
¶ The **second Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Kingdom** <note>original: "pars regni"</note>, is taken by day from Mars to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Abu Ma'shar said if this Part and its Lord are in a good state and are joined with the Lord of the Tenth and the Ascendant, the native will be a king or a leader, and will be among the wealthy who will receive his words and listen to them.
¶ The **third Part of the Tenth House** is called the **Part of Kingdom and of Kings and Administrators** <note>original: "pars regni atq; regum ⁊ dispositorum"</note>, and is taken by day from Mercury to Mars, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Part was extracted by them because the significance of giving, receiving, writing, prohibiting, attaining a consulship, reading, sending letters and receiving those sent, counting money, and the perspicacity of wit is given to Mercury. And the significance of fear and terror is given to Mars; therefore this Part was calculated from them. When this Part and its Lord are well-disposed, in a good state, and well-placed with the Lord of the Ascendant, the native will be of good wit, teachable, and rational, and a consulship will happen to him if he is suited for it: and he will be a scribe of kings, or a collector or guardian of their tax, or of the substances of great kings. And if he is suited for a kingdom or empire, he will obtain it, and the fame of his status will pass on high and be extended even to the ends of the earth. He will raise up some and exalt them beyond measure, and he will depose some powerful ones and push them down: and soldiers and the affairs of men shall pass through his hands.
¶ The **fourth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Kingdom, Victory, and Aid** <note>original: "pars regni ⁊ victorie atq; auxilij"</note>, is taken by day from the Sun to Saturn, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Abu Ma'shar said this Part corresponds to the Part of Fathers when Saturn is not...

### Chapter Eleven: Concerning the Parts of the Eighth House, their extraction, and their significations.

<margin>Note</margin>
In this chapter, we must speak of the parts of the Eighth House. There are five parts. First, the **Part of Death** <note>original: "parte mortis"</note>, which is extracted from three significators: it is taken by day and night from the Moon to the degree of the Eighth House, and to this is added the distance Saturn has traveled through the sign in which he resides, projected from the beginning of that same sign. It is extracted in this way because the Moon is the significator of the body, and the Eighth House is the significator of death, which must destroy the body; Saturn holds significance over the end of things, and over grief, sadness, weeping, lamentation, anguish, dissolution, and destruction—all of which follow from death. For this reason, the signification of death was given to these three indicators. If this part and its lord are free, in a good state, and well-disposed or located, the native will die in his own bed a natural death. However, if they are impeded and the <term>fortunes</term> <note>The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> (or at least one of them) do not aspect them, the native will die a most foul death. If these significators in any <term>revolution</term> <note>A solar return chart calculated for the year</note> are as poorly disposed as described, many will die such a death in that revolution.
¶ The **second Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Killing Planet** <note>original: "pars planete interficientis"</note>, is taken by day from the lord of the Ascendant to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This part is extracted in this manner: because the lord of the Ascendant signifies the soul and the Moon the body (though sometimes one is put for the other), the whole soul is joined to the body and signifies temperament and permanence while they are in harmony together; but when they are diverse, the body perishes, though the soul remains. This is why the wise extracted the part this way. Albumasar said that if the Moon alone aspects this part and it is in a <term>sign of cut-off members</term> <note>Certain zodiac signs historically associated with physical mutilation or loss of limbs</note> and impeded, or if the lord of the sign where the part is located and the lords of the signs they are in impede each other, the native will die in suffering. If they are not impeded, nor impede each other, the native will be mutilated in the limb assigned to the sign where the Moon then resides, but will not die from it.
¶ The **third Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Year in which Death is Feared** <note>original: "pars anni in quo timetur nato mors"</note>, or affliction, destruction, impediment, or heavy gravity, is taken by day from Saturn to the lord of the house of the <term>Syzygy</term> <note>The "conjunction or prevention"—the New or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth or question</note> that occurred before the birth, question, or revolution, and is projected from the Ascendant. This part is extracted here because Saturn is the significator of cold, death, the end, and affliction, which lead to destruction; the degree of the syzygy is similar, so they calculated this part from these two

<column-break/>

places. Albumasar said this part pertains to the Part of the End of Things. He said that when this part and its lord are with the lord of the Ascendant and are impeded, the native will suffer many infirmities and afflictions in body and substance; he will frequently approach the destruction of the body and the loss of wealth. Whenever the year reaches this part through <term>profections</term> <note>An ancient timing technique that moves the chart forward by one sign per year</note> (by which one sign is given to each year) or through <term>direction</term> <note>Primary directions, a complex calculation moving degrees of right ascension to the Ascendant</note> of the Ascendant or its lord, the native will encounter dangers in his body and limbs from infirmities, and will find anguish and horrible things in his substance; he will also fear death from various quarters. 
¶ The **fourth Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of the Heavy Place** <note>original: "pars loci ponderosi"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to Mars and by night the reverse, and there is added to it the distance Mercury has traveled through its sign, projected from the beginning of that sign. Albumasar said this part is similar to the previous one. He said that if this part and the lord of the Ascendant are impeded in anyone's birth, he will have an inseparable infirmity called <term>azamena</term> <note>A term for a chronic or incurable physical disability, deformity, or disease</note> in the limb assigned to the sign in which the part resides. He will be unfortunate in all his business, and will be so occupied and anxious in them that he cannot bring them to a good end. If he does finish them, whether for good or ill, they will be delayed and he will scarcely be able to do it. Albumasar said when the year moves from the Ascendant to this part, or the part moves to the Ascendant or its lord by profections or directions, the native's affairs will be burdened in that year; whatever he hopes for from his works will be delayed; he will find grief, sadness, and affliction because of it; and he will begin nothing in that year that will be completed to his prosperity, but rather to his loss. He will find infirmities in the limb assigned to the sign where the year of the revolution reaches this part. If the "males" <note>Malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> aspect it, they will find anguish and destruction.
¶ The **fifth Part of the Eighth House**, which is called the **Part of Occupation, Heaviness, and Destruction** <note>original: "pars occupationis et grauitatis atqꝫ destructio"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to Mercury and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. If it happens that the lord of the Ascendant is with this part and they are impeded at the root of the birth, it signifies that the native will be in evil and heaviness for the whole time of his life. If he works at something for which he has good hope, he will find heaviness and evil from it, and what he intends will not follow. If the year of profection reaches them or any one of them—the year determined by the succession of signs, giving one sign to each year, or by the degrees of direction as described in the treatise on births—when the degree is directed through the <term>terms</term> <note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by specific planets</note> to some place and the direction reaches that part, the native will find evil from which he will be liberated in that revolution. If he is liberated from it, he will fall into another no less heavy than the first. If the fortunes aspect the place from strong locations, they will alleviate the evil but not take it away entirely.

First, the **Part of Pilgrimage** <note>original: "parte peregrinationis"</note>, which is taken by day and night from the lord of the ninth sign to the degree of the Ninth House, and is projected from the Ascendant. And this part signifies...

Understand the same for the revolutions of the years: but if they are poorly disposed, say the opposite. ¶ The **second Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Journeying and Pilgrimage by Water** <note>original: "ps itineris ac pegrinatiōis in aqua"</note>, is taken by day from Saturn to the 15th degree of Cancer, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>. If this part falls in aquatic signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> with "fortunate" planets <note>traditionally Jupiter or Venus</note>, the native will see goodness, utility, and profit from sea voyages and their practice; likewise, he will find gain and safety. And a certain one of the ancients said if Saturn is in the 15th degree of Cancer and that degree is the Ascendant, then Saturn’s degrees will be the significators; therefore, look to them and to their aspect with the planets, and judge according to them. ¶ The **third Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Religion**, is taken by day from the Moon to Mercury, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And if this part and its lord fall in the Ascendant, or with its lord, or with the <term>Almuten</term> <note>the planet with the most essential dignity/power at a specific degree</note> over it, the native will be religious. And if the significators of the part aspect the part and the lord of the Ascendant, it will be the same. But if the part is impeded, none of the aforesaid will happen, but rather there will be a lack of them. ¶ The **fourth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Prayer and Depth of Counsel**, is taken by day from Saturn to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This same part signifies reason, consideration, and the scrutiny of deep matters: the depth of laudable counsels, and even the discovery of wisdom. This is stronger if Saturn is above the earth by day, and even more so if he is <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the Sun</note>, aspecting the part and receiving it, or if the Moon is in an excellent place from the Ascendant. ¶ The **fifth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Wisdom and Patience**, is taken by day from Saturn to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and is projected from Mercury. It is calculated this way for the reason that Saturn signifies stability, philosophy, and depth in things, as well as scrutiny in speech and the lengthiness of thoughts; Jupiter signifies wisdom, patience, and reason; and Mercury signifies writing, wisdom, and experiments. Therefore, this part was to be extracted from them. If Saturn and Jupiter aspect this part or are joined to it, and both or one of them "receives" it <note>a technical relationship where a planet occupies a sign ruled by another</note>, the native will be wise, patient, and rational. And if Mercury aspects it or is joined to it, he will be wise, of sharp and profound intellect, and a great expert or searcher of deep things; he will be swift in the discovery of all things that can be found. ¶ The **sixth Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Histories and the Knowledge of Rumors and Fables**, is taken by day from the Sun to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a highly influential Persian astrologer whose works were translated into Latin</note> said this part agrees with the Part of the Father. And he said when Saturn is "under the rays" <note>hidden by the Sun's light, making the planet weak</note>: if this part falls in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> in aspect to Mercury and Venus, and the lord of the Ascendant aspects it, the native will remember ancient histories and the rumors of men; he will be an inventor of fables and beautiful narrations in which listeners delight, laugh, and rejoice. And Albumasar said: if it is otherwise, there will be error. ¶ The **seventh Part of the Ninth House**, which is called the **Part of Rumors**, whether they be true or false, is taken by day and night from Mercury to the Moon and is projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said this part is similar to the Part of Servants. If it is in an angle or in a fixed sign, or rising directly, the rumors will be true: and even more so if the Moon is joined to a truth-telling planet. And it is even truer if, with this, the truth-telling planet is in the second, fifth, or ninth sign; but if it is otherwise, it will be the opposite.

### ¶ Chapter Thirteen: Concerning the Parts of the Tenth House, their signification, and their extraction.

<column-break/>

In this chapter, a discourse must be made concerning the parts of the Tenth House. First, concerning the **Part of Nobility** <note>original: "parte nobilitatis"</note>, which is taken by day from the Sun to the 19th degree of Aries (which is the degree of its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet's influence is especially powerful</note>), and by night from the Moon to the 3rd degree of Taurus (which is the degree of its exaltation), and it is projected from the Ascendant. This part is extracted in this way because the Sun, which is the luminary of the day, becomes the significator of the native's life and its durability by day, and signifies the soul, honor, and sublimity, as well as exaltation, kingdom, and victory. The Moon is the luminary of the night and signifies in the night what the Sun signifies in the day. For this reason, it is called the Part of Nobility, because it is extracted from the luminaries, which are the more noble bodies, and from the degrees of their exaltations. Indeed, through this part, the nobility and generosity of the native are known, and whether he is the son of the one he is said to be or not. Through it are known his honor, his exaltation, his kingdom, his sublimity, and his victory. If this part falls in a good place, such as the Tenth House, or is well-placed and in good condition with "fortunate" planets, it signifies that the native will come to honor, nobility, exaltation, riches, and the spreading of a good reputation—each according to his own degree. For instance, if he is of those suited for a kingdom, he will attain it. If he is of others, he will attain honors and dignities appropriate to himself, and even exceed them. This same thing happens if this part is so disposed in the "revolution" <note>the annual solar return chart</note> of anyone. If this part falls in the aforesaid degrees and it is a daytime birth, Albumasar said that the signification of those degrees will be like the signification of the degree of the Ascendant. If the significators of this part aspect it and are in good "complexions" <note>combinations of planetary influences</note> with it, the native will be the son of the one to whom he is attributed; but if it is the opposite, he will not be his son. ¶ The **second Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of the Kingdom**, is taken by day from Mars to the Moon, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said if this part and its lord are in good condition and are joined with the lord of the Tenth and the Ascendant, the native will be a king or a duke, and will be among the wealthy who will receive his words and listen to them. ¶ The **third Part of the Tenth House** is called the **Part of the Kingdom, Kings, and Administrators** <note>original: "pars regni atqꝫ regum ꝛ dispositoꝝm"</note>. It is taken by day from Mercury to Mars, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. This part was extracted by them because the signification of giving, receiving, writing, commanding, prohibiting, the affairs of the consulate, following, reading epistles, sending and receiving envoys, counting money, and the perceptiveness of genius is given to Mercury. And the signification of fear and terror is given to Mars. Therefore, this part was calculated from them. When this part and its lord are well-disposed, in good condition, and well-placed with the lord of the Ascendant, the native will be of good genius, teachable, and rational. Consulates will come to him if he is suited for them; he will be a scribe of kings, or a collector and guardian of their census, or of the substance of great kings. And if he is suited for a kingdom or an empire, he will obtain it, and the fame of his status will rise on high and extend to the ends of the earth. He will raise some up and exalt them beyond measure, and he will depose certain powerful ones and depress them; soldiers and the affairs of men will pass through his hands. ¶ The **fourth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Kingdom, Victory, and Aid**, is taken by day from the Sun to Saturn, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said this part agrees with the Part of Fathers when Saturn is not...
