# On the Exaltation of the Parts

...under the rays of the sun: when this has been well-disposed and in a good state, and especially when it is with the lord of the tenth house and with the lord of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, representing the individual self</note>, it signifies a kingdom for the native—provided they are among those fit for royal rule. It also signifies honor and exaltation for every person according to their own social standing, and such a person will expand their influence, be preferred for promotion, and prevail over those of their own kind. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a preeminent Persian astrologer whose works were foundational to Western medieval astrology</note> said that if it is in a sign in which the lord of the Ascendant or the lord of the tenth house has dignity, it will signify victory for the native over those who contend with him. The same occurs in <term>revolutions</term> <note>Yearly charts cast to predict events for the coming year</note> if this "gateway" is found further opposite.

¶ The **Fifth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of those who are suddenly elevated** <note>original: "ps illorum q̄ repente sublimant"</note>, is calculated by day from Saturn to the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>A mathematical point representing prosperity and well-being</note>, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And Albumasar said this Part is similar to the Part of Saturn: if it is found in someone’s birth chart, or at a time when it is in an excellent location relative to the Ascendant and the "Fortunes" <note>Beneficial planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</note>, that person will be suddenly raised up. And if the lord of the Ascendant is with it, or looks upon it with an aspect of friendship from a praiseworthy place, and is itself well-disposed, his height of status will increase. He will attain a kingdom very quickly and in the shortest time, so that men will marvel at it. And Albumasar said that by looking at this Part, one may know which man will be elevated and acquire a kingdom and honor. He also said that if this Part is "impeded" <note>Weakened by bad positioning or harsh planetary aspects</note>, the native will find earthly evil, obstacles, and horrors, suffering a sudden deposition from power. Understand the same for yearly revolutions: if that Part is in a good state and well-disposed, the native and others will suddenly acquire good in that year, but if it is impeded, they will be hindered in like manner.

¶ The **Sixth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Nobles and those known among men** (or the honored), is taken by day and night from Mercury to the Sun and is projected from the Ascendant. When this Part and its lord are in a good state and well-disposed, the native will be noble and honored among kings, nobles, the wealthy, and great magnates. And Albumasar said if it is with a planet that has great dignity in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the sky, signifying one's public life and career</note>, he will have a "principality" or leadership role by which he will be famous, just as one is named among the tribes of a city among his fellow citizens. If the contrary is true, the opposite will happen; understand the same for revolutions.

¶ The **Seventh Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Soldiers and Ministers**, Albumasar said is taken by day from Mars to Saturn and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And he said if this Part and its lord are joined to the lord of the Ascendant, the native will follow kings or be among their soldiers or ministers.

¶ The **Eighth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Kings and of the work the native performs**, is taken by day and night from Saturn to the Moon and is projected from the Ascendant. This is because Saturn signifies labor, adversity, necessity, poverty, and all laborious works—such as the building of houses, digging, working with iron and its extraction from the mine, and other hateful and tedious tasks, as he is the significator of toil and affliction. He is also the significator of the wealthy whose riches are "heavy" and burdensome. The Moon signifies labors and speed in affairs because of the velocity of her motion, and she is the significatrix of the common people. For this reason, the wise masters calculated this Part from these two. And Albumasar said this Part signifies a kingdom, honor, and magnificence: it shows what kind of work the native performs, what is best for him to do, and what mastery he will exercise; and whether or not he acquires gain from his mastery or kingdom. And he said if it is in Gemini or Virgo, or in signs of the arts and masteries, he will be elevated through the work of his hands which are necessary for the wealthy and by which they are adorned: he will be among the wealthy and magnates because of his skill and searching intellect. If the Part is favorably mixed with its significators, he will acquire a great quantity of things from his mastery. But he said if it is the opposite, he will be poor and unfortunate in his mastery, or he will acquire only the sustenance...

<column-break/>

...of his day: yet he will not be able to be weary, for if he is not weary, he will die of hunger, as there will be no one to offer him food. Understand the same in revolutions: for there are sometimes years in which the fortunate do not profit, and that is when that Part is poorly disposed in the revolution. And there are sometimes years in which the unfortunate gain, and that is when that Part is well-disposed.

¶ The **Ninth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Merchants and those who work with their hands**, is taken by day from Mercury to Venus and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And Albumasar said this Part is similar to the "Part of Gathering." This Part signifies ingenious men and craftsmen in their masteries—specifically those under Venus and Mercury, such as knowing how to work gold, silver, precious stones, and the like; and those who know how to trade, namely buying and selling precious and select merchandise of this kind, such as pearls, rings, and similar items. It also signifies those who know how to make beautiful garments and adorn them (especially those pertaining to women), and how to paint, write, mint coins, engrave seals, and other things pertaining to the nature of Mercury and Venus. If this Part and its lord are in a good state and well-disposed, and are joined to the lord of the Ascendant by conjunction or a "trine" or "sextile" aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees</note>, the native or the inquirer will be elevated by the works and trades of his hands; for he will produce beautiful instruments and beautiful operations that befit nobles, the wealthy, and magnates. If, however, it is the contrary, let him not involve himself in these things, for the opposite will happen to him. If this Part and its lord are well-disposed in any revolution, whether of individuals or of the world, the aforementioned craftsmen will profit from their businesses; if the contrary is true, the contrary will occur.

¶ The **Tenth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of the Business of Buying and Selling**, is taken by day from the "Part of the Future" <note>A specific lot often linked to expectations or Mercury</note> to the Part of Fortune, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said this Part is similar to the Part of Mercury. He said these Parts which concern business, when they are in aspect to Mercury and "received" by him <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, creating a hospitable relationship</note>, the native will be skilled in business: he will have the knowledge of buying and selling. When these are fortunate and well-disposed, they will profit him and he will gain from them. If they are in a bad state and poorly disposed, although he may know these trades, let him not involve himself in them, since it will result in the opposite of gain. The same is to be understood in the revolutions of both the world and of individual births.

¶ The **Eleventh Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Work and the thing that must necessarily be done**, is taken by day from the Sun to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said that when Saturn is "under the rays" <note>Too close to the sun to be seen, which was considered a state of weakness</note>, this Part is similar to the Part of Fathers. And he said when this Part is with the lord of the Ascendant, the native will be distinguished in his works because he will know them better than others; he will pant and be distressed in every thing he wishes to do, and he will intend to finish it hastily, always fearing he might not complete it until he sees it finished. Therefore, when someone wishes to work at something and wishes to know what will come of it, look at this Part: if it is in a good state, success is likely, especially if he has hastened to do it. If, however, it is with "malifics" <note>Mars or Saturn</note> or otherwise hindered, he will find evil, detriment, and horror if he proceeds for that reason; the more he hastens to do it, the worse and more horrible the outcome will be. This is valid not only in birth charts but also in <term>horary questions</term> <note>original: "qstionibus"; charts cast to answer a specific question</note> and in revolutions of the world and individuals.

¶ The **Twelfth Part of the Tenth House**, which is called the **Part of Mothers**, is taken by day from Venus to the Moon and by night...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Arabic Parts" or "Lots," transitioning from the domestic and maternal influences of the Tenth House into the social and communal sphere of the Eleventh House. ...the reverse, and project it from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, representing the self</note>. This part signifies the condition of **mothers**. If it is in a good state and well-disposed, it signifies that the mother is good. If, in the birth chart, it is in an aspect of <term>trine</term> <note>An angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</note> or <term>sextile</term> <note>An angle of 60 degrees, considered harmonious and helpful</note> with the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that the mother loves the child. If the Lord of the Tenth House <term>receives</term> <note>In astrology, "reception" occurs when one planet is in a sign where another has dignity, indicating a cooperative relationship</note> it—namely, if the Lord of the Ascendant does not receive the Lord of the Tenth or the Moon—it signifies that the mother loves the child, but he does not love the mother in the same way. If the Lord of the Ascendant receives the Lord of the Tenth, but the latter receives neither him nor the Moon, it signifies that the son loves the mother more than she loves him. If both receive each other, both will love each other. If neither receives the other, neither will love the other. The same is to be said in <term>Questions</term> <note>Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question</note> and <term>Revolutions</term> <note>Charts cast for the anniversary of a birth or the new year to predict annual trends</note> as in birth charts. The wise placed the Part of the Mother in the Tenth House because it is opposite the Fourth House, which signifies the father.

### Chapter 14: On the Parts of the Eleventh House, Their Extraction, and Their Significance.

In this chapter, we must discuss the Parts of the Eleventh House <note>The house governing friends, hopes, and social status</note>. First, we discuss the **Part of Excellence and Nobility**. **Albumasar said** that by day it is taken from the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>A mathematical point calculated from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant representing prosperity</note> to the Part of the Future <note>original: "ptem futuroz"; likely referring to the Part of Spirit, representing the soul's intent</note>, and by night the reverse, and it is projected from the Ascendant. He said this part is the Part of Stability and vocation under the influence of Venus. This part was extracted this way because, since it is noble, stable, and very useful, it had to be drawn from the two most noble and excellent parts: the Part of Fortune and the Part of the Future. When it is in a good state and well-disposed, located with <term>benefics</term> <note>The "fortunate" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>—and even better if it is in the Tenth or Eleventh House—and no <term>malefics</term> <note>The "unfortunate" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> hinder it, the native will excel over other men, being noble and fortunate. His fortune will endure, and he will be praiseworthy and in a good state. Albumasar said he will be among those whom people need because of his fortune, and whom men will revere; he will be like a prince among the tribes. He said his name will remain for ages for many years, and in every work he performs, he will see good, joy, and that which pleases him. If, however, it is the opposite, the reverse will happen. Understand this same principle in general questions and in others, such as revolutions. When this part is so disposed, good or the contrary will happen to each person according to their status.

**The Second Part of the 11th House** is the part signifying how the native (or a querent) will be loved by men, or how they will hate him. Albumasar said it is taken by day from the Part of Fortune to the Part of the Future, and by night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. He said this part belongs to the nature of Venus. If this part falls in the house, <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet's power is greatly increased</note>, or <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</note> of any benefic, and that benefic aspects the part, and it is not hindered by any malefic, he will be beloved by men, amiable, sweet, and pleasing in their eyes. If, however, it falls with malefics or in their harmful aspects, he will be hateful and burdensome to men, so much so that they cannot bear to see him; and for the most part, whatever he does or says will displease people, even when he says or does good.

**The Third Part of the 11th House** is called the **Part of those born among men and honored among them**, through whom people’s affairs and business are completed. It is taken by day from the Part of Fortune to the Sun, and by night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. If it is well-located—namely, received by the Sun, Venus, Mercury, or the Moon, these being benefics—or if they and the Lord of the Ascendant aspect it by trine or sextile, the native or querent will be honored by both the great and the 

<column-break/>

common people. They will love him and turn to him for their deeds, placing many things and much business in his hands to be completed or settled, and they will think very highly of him.

**The Fourth Part of the 11th House**, which is the **Part of Happiness and Success**, is taken by day from the Part of Fortune to Jupiter, and by night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. If it is with the Lord of the Ascendant, or aspects it with a trine or sextile (or at least a <term>square</term> <note>An angle of 90 degrees, usually considered tense but productive if there is "reception"</note> with reception), and is not otherwise hindered, it signifies that the native will be happy and successful in all things. He will obtain everything necessary for himself regarding temporal matters, and not only his own affairs but the affairs of others will succeed through his hands just as he wishes. Furthermore, if the benefics aspect this part, he will obtain whatever he wishes with such ease that nothing he desires will seem to be lacking. Albumasar said that perhaps he will even acquire more than he wanted, quite easily. If, however, it is not with the Lord of the Ascendant and does not aspect it, and the malefics aspect it instead, the opposite will occur. The same happens in questions and revolutions.

**The Fifth Part of the 11th House**, which is called the **Part of Concupiscence and Zeal** <note>original: "ps concupiſcentie atqȝ studij"</note> or appetite in the love of the world and temporal things, is taken by day from the Part of Fortune to the Part of the Future, and by night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. Albumasar said this part is similar to the Part of Venus. If it is in an excellent place in a birth chart, question, or revolution, that person will conquer his lusts and his desires. But he said if it is in a bad place, his lusts will conquer him; he will be zealous for and desirous of the world and its affection, and he will lose whatever he has in it.

**The Sixth Part of the 11th House**, which is called the **Part of Trust and Hope**, is taken by day from Saturn to Venus, and by night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. If this part and its Lord are in an excellent location—namely, fortunate and strong—in someone's birth chart or question, the native or querent will obtain everything he hopes for and in which he has trust. If, however, they are in a bad state and poorly located, he will not obtain from what he hoped for anything that profits him tangibly. The same happens in revolutions. For if they are in a good state and well-located, men will obtain enough of what they want in that revolution; but if they are hindered, the opposite will occur.

**The Seventh Part of the 11th House**, which is called the **Part of Friends**, is taken by day and night from the Moon to Mercury, and projected from the Ascendant. This part is taken thus because Mercury is "skin-changing" <note>original: "verſipellis"; meaning fickle or versatile</note> of various significations: at some times he signifies masculinity, at others femininity; in some, speed; in others, slowness; in some, heat; in others, cold; in some, fortune; in others, misfortune. He always inclines to the nature of the one he joins. The Moon likewise does the same because of her fast and quickly changing motion. Therefore, because the wills of men regarding friends change quickly and do not remain long in the same state, the wise extracted the Part of Friends from those two planets which are faster and more changeable than the others. When this part is in a good state and well-disposed, and its Lord is well-disposed and in <term>movable signs</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs associated with change and initiation</note>, the native or querent will have many friends. If they are fortunate, the friends will profit him and he them, and they will enjoy good things together. If they are received, he will be praiseworthy among them and beloved by them. If the opposite, judge accordingly.

**The Eighth Part of the 11th House**, which is called the **Part of Concord of Friends** and also of husband and wife and their discord, is taken by day and night from the Part of the Future to Mercury, and projected from the Ascendant. This part is among the most difficult of the parts...

### On the Extraction of the Parts

...to comprehend: since it is necessary to know the births of the native and of those who are considered his friends, or of a husband and wife, and to see if that part has fallen in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, representing the self</note> of the native’s birth, or of the one who is the lord without impediment from the <term>malefics</term> <note>The "unlucky" planets, Saturn and Mars, which were thought to cause difficulty</note>, or if it was in the sign that was the Ascendant of their births, or if it was in the 11th house, or joined with their lord, or joined with the lord of the Ascendant—and that being a good and well-disposed state, in aspect with the <term>benefics</term> <note>The "lucky" planets, Jupiter and Venus, which bring favor</note> and in a good place from the Ascendant, and not impeded by any of the evil ones—or if it was in the <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet’s influence is heightened and most dignified</note> of any of the planets, or as **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar (787–886 AD), a highly influential Persian astrologer whose works were the foundation of medieval European astrology</note> says, it was in concordant signs; for if it were so, they will diligently love each other along with his friends and his wife. But if it were in the sign of <term>detriment</term> <note>A sign opposite the one a planet naturally rules, where its power is weakened</note> of any of them, or in the sign of its <term>fall</term> <note>A sign opposite the planet's exaltation, where it is considered most powerless</note>, or in opposition to the Ascendant, or in signs that will be mutually inimical to them.

The **ninth part of the 11th house**, which is called the **Part of Fertility** and abundance of good in the house, is taken by day and night from the Moon to Mercury and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said this part is similar to the Part of Friends. And he said that if it and its lord are in a good <term>complexion</term> <note>The overall "temperament" or balance of planetary influences</note> with the Part of Fortune and the lord of the Ascendant, the native or the seeker will be generous in the house with all fertility; and if it be otherwise, he will be the opposite. If it is so disposed in a <term>Revolution</term> <note>An annual chart cast for the "birthday" of a person or a year to predict upcoming trends</note>, the same thing will happen.

The **tenth part of the 11th house**, which is called the **Part of Probity of Mind**, is taken by day from Mercury to the Sun, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. If it falls in a good place with any of the benefics, and especially with **Jupiter**, or if it aspects him, or the Sun aspects it from a <term>trine</term> <note>An angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</note> or fertile aspect, the native or seeker will be sweet and gentle and of a patient mind. And **Albumasar** said if this part and its lord fall in signs of probity, he will be of an honest mind; and if it falls with the malefics or in signs contrary to probity, it will be the opposite. Understand the same in Revolutions.

The **eleventh part of the 11th house**, which is called the **Part of Praise and Gratitude**, is taken by day from Jupiter to Venus, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. If it and its lord are of good essence and well-disposed, and the benefics aspect them or are joined to them—especially **Jupiter**—the native or seeker will be praiseworthy and pleasing above all things he might be, and will be praised for his works and benefit therefrom. If, however, they are ill-disposed or the malefics aspect them, he will not be praised for his works nor for his service; and not only will he not be praised or benefit from the services he has performed, but they will not even give him thanks for them; and it will be possible that for the services he has done, instead of a reward, they return reproach to him and he acquires ill-will thereby. The same will happen to men in Revolutions if this part and its lord are disposed as has been said.

The **twelfth part of the 11th house**, which is called the **Part of Necessity and Love of Things**, according to some, is taken by day and night from Venus to the house of brothers <note>The Third House, which governs siblings and immediate environment</note> and projected from the Ascendant; according to the **Egyptians**, it is taken by day from Mars to the house of brothers and projected from the Ascendant.

### Chapter 15: On the parts of the twelfth house and their extraction and their meanings.

Mention must be made in this chapter of the parts of the **12th house** <note>Traditionally the house of hidden enemies, prisons, and self-undoing</note>, and first of the **Part of Hidden Enemies**, which is taken by day and night from Saturn to Mars and projected from the Ascendant. The **second part of the 12th house**, according to **Hermes**, is taken by day and night from the Lord of the House of Enemies to the degree of the House of Enemies, and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said that both these parts ought to be examined; for if they are in opposition or in a <term>square</term> <note>An angle of 90 degrees, considered a point of tension or conflict</note> aspect to their lords or the lord of the Ascendant, the native or seeker will have many enemies; but if both are free from their lord and with the lord of the Ascendant, he will not easily have enemies. The same happens in Revolutions: for if they are ill-disposed as was said, men will be inimical to each other in

<column-break/>

that Revolution. The **third part of the 12th house**, which is called the **Part of Labor and Affliction**, is taken by day and night from the Part of things to come <note>original: "pte futuꝝ"; likely referring to the Part of Fata or Future Events</note> to the Part of Fortune, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said that this part is similar to the Part of Mercury; if it and its lord are of good essence and well-disposed, it signifies that the native or seeker will be fortunate in his labors and will gain from them, and it will be profitable for him. If, however, it is corrupted or joined with the lord of the Ascendant without <term>reception</term> <note>A condition where planets reside in signs ruled by each other, indicating a lack of cooperation here</note>, or if it is in its opposition or square aspect, he will be laborious all the time of his life; nor will his labors profit him, nor will he rejoice in his goods, nor will he gain from them, nor will his fortune be profitable to him.

### Chapter 16: In commemoration of certain parts according to Albumasar, of which mention was not made above, which is called the fifth difference.

In this chapter, mention must be made of certain other parts that were not distinctly noted above, which are **ten parts according to Albumasar**; they fall much into the work of the masters of this science when they wish to judge any birth, universal question, or any Revolution. The first of these is called the **Part of the Hyleg** <note>original: "ps ylez"; the Hyleg is the "giver of life," a point in the chart used to determine a person's lifespan and vital force</note>, and it is a matter that the ancient sages of this science observed greatly and found to be true. It is taken—whether it be a birth, a question, or a Revolution of the <term>conjunction</term> <note>The New Moon occurring before the birth</note>—from the degree of the conjunction; or if it be of the <term>prevention</term> <note>original: "preuentionis"; the Full Moon occurring before the birth</note>, from the degree of the prevention, both by day and night, to the Moon, and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said that this part is directed just as the Hyleg is directed. When its <term>direction</term> <note>An advanced predictive technique of moving planetary points through the zodiac to forecast the timing of events</note> or profection reaches the benefics, it signifies good; and when it reaches the malefics, it signifies evil and impediment and danger to the native or seeker, or to him for whom the revolution of the year is made, or even to any universal revolution. And this is the reason why many otherwise honest men are deceived: because they see many good things happen to someone that should not happen according to the Hyleg; for they considered only the Hyleg and did not care for the **Part of the Hyleg**. But you, do not neglect this, but always direct the Part of the Hyleg in births, questions, and Revolutions, and you will not err; for it has its own significations besides the others, which are of great efficacy.

The **second part** of the fifth category, which is called the **Part of the Magnitude of Bodies**, is taken by day from the Part of Fortune to Mars, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said when this part is with the lord of the Ascendant or with a planet that is in the Ascendant, or in the <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>The planet that rules the Hyleg, used by medieval astrologers to calculate the specific number of years a person would live</note> there is some dignity, and the planet is in its own dignity or in a <term>humid sign</term> <note>The water signs (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces), which were thought to produce more substantial or fleshy bodies</note>, the native will have large limbs. And he said if it be otherwise and it is with **Mercury** or **Mars**, or these planets dominate it, the native will be lean of body.

The **third part** of the fifth category, which is the **Part of Military Service and Boldness**, is taken by day from Saturn to the Moon, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. And **Albumasar** said this part is similar to the Part of Reason and depth of counsel, and the Part of the King, and to the work the native performs. When it is in a fertile aspect with **Mars** or **Jupiter** in the <term>animal signs</term> <note>Signs represented by creatures, like Aries (the Ram) or Leo (the Lion)</note>, it signifies that the native may be bold, a soldier, and a manager of animals, and he will be a swordsman playing with spears, arms, and swords.

The **fourth part** of the fifth category, which is called the **Part of Boldness, Strength, and Dominion**, is taken by day from the lord of the Ascendant to the Moon, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. When it is in a fertile aspect with **Mars** or **Jupiter**, or received in the houses of the malefics in strong signs, it signifies that its lord is spirited and strong in his body.

The **fifth part** of the fifth category, which is called the **Part of Cunning, Wit, Sharpness, and Discipline of all arts, and Memory**, and of the son, is taken by day from Mercury to the Part of things to come <note>original: "ptem futuꝝrum"</note>, and in the night the reverse, and projected from the Ascendant. And therefore...

The wise have understood this part as though it signifies all these things through **Mercury**; they are attributed to him and they refer to the soul and represent the future state of the soul’s matters, all these things proceeding from the authority of the soul. If the part is in a good state and well-disposed in the <term>nativity</term> <note>a birth chart</note> or conception along with Mercury, he signifies a good state, and the <term>native</term> <note>the person for whom the chart is cast</note> will be clever with a good craftiness, of sharp wit, teachable in many arts, and driven to learn all that he wishes. In whatever he studies, he will do so with less labor than others because he will well retain what he has learned, and all these things will be successful for him. But if they are <term>unfortunate</term> <note>afflicted by difficult planetary placements</note> and poorly disposed, he will be fit to learn, but it will not be useful to him; indeed, he will find evil and horror because of the aforementioned reasons. If, however, Mercury is joined to **Mars** by <term>conjunction</term> <note>planets sitting at the same degree</note> or <term>aspect</term> <note>specific geometric angles between planets</note>, and Mars has any testimony in the place where the part falls, it signifies that the native or the one being generated is a thief, a highwayman, and a very subtle robber who will know how to open doors and locks through craftiness and the subtleties of his wit without a key. But if there is a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note> with <term>reception</term> <note>a cooperative relationship where one planet is in the other's "home" sign</note>, he will know how to do all things, but he will not work them for an evil purpose. The same thing happens in <term>revolutions</term> <note>annual charts that forecast the year ahead</note>: for when this part is disposed as described, the aforementioned events will happen more in that revolution than is usual at other times. The **Sixth Part** of this division is sought, which is called the **Part of the Ingenuity of a Matter**, and whether it completes a thing fully, or destroys it, or delays it, or brings it to effect. In the day and night, it is taken from **Saturn** to **Mars** and projected from **Mercury**. This part is extracted from these three planets because the <term>malefics</term> <note>Saturn and Mars</note> have significance over destruction; although they sometimes hinder by a <term>quartile aspect</term> <note>a 90-degree angle of tension</note> or <term>opposition</term>, they nonetheless sometimes complete a matter, though perhaps with slowness and hardship. But when they hinder with evil, they destroy the matter; and if they do not destroy it, they will delay it unto desperation. Because Mercury has participation in affairs, this part is projected from him. If it is in a good state and well-disposed, free from evil—specifically from Mars during the day and from Saturn at night—it signifies the outcome of the matter. And if it is hindered by any of them as mentioned, it signifies its destruction, and they will not complete it. And if it is completed, it will not last. And **Albumasar** <note>the Persian astrologer Abu Ma'shar</note> said: this part operates in unknown matters and things whose nature is ignored. But if the matter is known, consider whether it pertains to substance, or contingency, or any other thing; you shall look at the matter itself from its own place, and this part will aid the <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing that specific topic</note> of those things. The **Seventh Part** of the fifth division is called the **Part of Necessity and Delay of Things**; it is taken in the day and in the night according to the Egyptians from Mars to the degree of the <term>House of Brothers</term> <note>the 3rd House</note> and projected from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the eastern horizon of the chart</note>. This part signifies the laziness and inertia of the native. If this part is so disposed in a revolution, it signifies that men will be such in that revolution. The **Eighth Part** of the fifth division, which like the previous one is called the **Part of Necessity and Delay of Things**, is taken in the day and night according to the parts from the Part of Delay to Mercury and projected from the Ascendant. And Albumasar said: both these parts are operative. If they are in a good state and well-disposed, they signify a native who is somewhat solicitous in carrying out his business. If, however, they are poorly disposed, joined with the malefics or any one of them—or if their <term>lord</term> <note>the planet ruling the sign where the Part sits</note> is with any of the malefics, and especially with Saturn—or if the part and its lord are with the lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that the native will be lazy and inert and will scarcely move to do anything, especially those things which are necessary for him, unless perhaps necessity forces him. Nor will he do anything of his own accord of those things which men work at for the sake of utility; nor will he allow himself to get involved in any trade or other lucrative matters for fear that he might lose for that reason; nor will he believe himself able to gain anything from elsewhere, and he will scarcely or never believe he can or knows how to live. And Albumasar said: if the lord of that evil part hinders the house...

<column-break/>

...of the lord of the **House of Substance** <note>the 2nd house, governing money and possessions</note>, the native will destroy his own reputation/wealth; he will not know how, or he will suffer much loss in it according to his own state. The same occurs in <term>interrogations</term> <note>horary astrology, where a chart is cast for a specific question</note> and in revolutions. For if that part is as described, men in that year or revolution will be lazier and more timid than usual. The **Ninth Part** of the fifth division, which is called the **Part of Retribution**, is taken in the day from Mars to the **Sun**, and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. If it is in a good state and well-disposed in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful</note>—especially in the first or tenth—or in the <term>succedent</term> houses of the angles—especially in the 11th or 5th—with the lord of the Ascendant in any of its <term>dignities</term> <note>signs or degrees where a planet has specific strength</note>, it signifies that the native will well reward those who have done well by him or who have shown him any service. But if it is in an evil state in the <term>cadent</term> houses from the angles—especially in the 6th or 12th—neither with the lord of the Ascendant nor in any of its dignities, it signifies that he will receive something for free from someone but will not repay the good deeds done for him. You may say the same in revolutions: if the part is so located, then men will act thus in that revolution. Understand the same in interrogations. The **Tenth Part** of the fifth division, which is called the **Part of Utility and Good Works**, is taken in the day from Mercury to Mars, and in the night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. And Albumasar said: this part is similar to the **Part of Reason and Sense**. If it is in a good state and well-disposed, fortunate and strong in an angle, it signifies that the native or the <term>querent</term> <note>the person asking the question</note> will be observant of utility and studious in good works, and abhorring vices, and utility and profit will happen to him for that reason. If, however, this part is in an angle but is hindered, he will be practicing and observant of utility and good works, but damage and evil will follow from them. And if it is outside the dignities of the lord of the Ascendant, he will be one who knows good things but does not practice them. If it is so disposed in revolutions, men in those revolutions will be so disposed and so acting. And Albumasar said: these are the publicized parts which the ancients recounted; and these operate in nativities and in many places in the revolutions of years and interrogations—that is, each of them in the places where they are necessary. And he said: know that in many matters and significations of the twelve houses, and interrogations, and <term>initiations</term> <note>charts for starting a new project</note>, and revolutions of years, there are parts of which we have made no mention here, because it is necessary that we speak of those parts in other books. And he said: what we have said concerning the significations of the parts in this book are collections of investigation, because the locations of these parts according to the signs in which they are, and the conjunctions of planets with them or their aspects toward them, change much of their significations into good or evil. And he said: we will recount the investigations of their significations in their places according to the signs in every book as it shall be necessary.

### Chapter 17 on the knowledge of certain extraordinary parts of which no mention has been made above.

**I**n this chapter, we must see concerning certain extraordinary parts of which no mention was made in the parts of the seven planets, nor in the parts of the twelve houses, nor in the commemoration of the ten parts of the fifth division. These are very useful parts, and in them he who wishes to be intent upon profit through revolutions can profit most. For through these parts, you will be able to weigh the utility, or the dearness <note>scarcity/high price</note>, or the mediocrity of the price of certain things born of the earth and of some other things to which men must for the most part have recourse for their food and their necessities, such as grain, wine, oil, and the like. You will also be able to see whether there will be an abundance or a scarcity of them...

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of astrological "Parts" or "Lots." You will likewise be able to know why it happens that a thing is sometimes abundant and yet expensive, or sometimes cheap. And why at other times it is not abundant—indeed, it is rare in quantity—and yet it is cheap, while at other times it is expensive. The abundance of a thing is signaled by the <term>aspect</term> <note>a specific geometric angle</note> of a <term>fortune</term> <note>a beneficial planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> to the Part itself, or to its <term>lord</term> <note>the planet that rules the zodiac sign where the Part is located</note>, as well as to the Moon or the "head of the corporal point." This is especially true if the fortune that aspects the Part, its lord, or the Moon, holds all the <term>dominion</term> <note>astrological authority or "dignity"</note> in the place where the Part falls. Scarcity or penury is signaled by the aspect of an <term>infortune</term> <note>a difficult planet like Saturn or Mars</note> to the Part, as well as a physical <term>conjunction</term> <note>when two bodies occupy the same degree of the zodiac</note>. 

You can weigh the fame or cheapness of a thing by the location of the lord of the house, or of its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet’s influence is strengthened</note>, or of the <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing the specific matter</note> in which the Part falls. If the significator is in its own house or exaltation, or is otherwise <term>fortunate</term> and strong, or is located in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of a chart</note>, it is all the more significant; if it is in a similar sign, it signifies the "heaviness" <note>high cost</note> of the price of that thing. If, however, one significator is fortunate and another is unfortunate, the state of that thing will change. But the lord of the exaltation is ranked below the lord of the house; the lord of the <term>term</term> and the lord of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>minor essential dignities</note> add or subtract something from the judgment. 

If, however, the significator is in the 12th house, in its <term>fall</term> <note>a sign where a planet’s influence is weakened</note>, or in its "decession," or falling from an angle—and even more so if it is in the 12th house or is <term>combust</term> <note>too close to the Sun, thus "burned up" and weakened</note>—it signifies cheapness and a low price for that thing. The weaker the significators are, the more it signifies the low value and cheapness of the item and the smallness of its price. If it is in a house <term>succeeding</term> an angle <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note>, and nothing else impedes it, it will neither be very burdensome nor much lightened in price. But if all the significators are fortunate and strong, that thing will be expensive and exceed the normal price, especially if they are in the 10th house, as I have said. If indeed they are unfortunate, weak, and poorly disposed, it signifies the ultimate cheapness of the thing and a very low price. 

Always take care to consider the significators of each thing, for each of them grants or takes away according to its own state. The significators are: the lord of the house of exaltation, the lord of the term, the lord of the triplicity of the planets from which you extracted the Part, and the planet which is the lord of the house from which you began the calculation of the Part. In all things, however, the lord of the house in which the Part falls should be prioritized above the others and judged most heavily; the others add or subtract as has been said. This is even more powerful if that lord is one of the planets from which the Part was originally calculated, as the Part is greatly strengthened by this.

## Chapter 18, in which is an example of the method for extracting certain parts.

Now I set before you examples of one Part as a model for all other extraordinary Parts; we begin with the **Part of Wheat**. When you wish to know the state of wheat in a <term>revolution</term> <note>a solar return chart, cast for the year</note>—namely, whether it will become cheap, or expensive, or have a mediocre price—subtract the position of the **Sun** from the position of **Mars**, and add to this the degree and minute of the **Ascendant**. Cast the resulting sum from the beginning of the Ascendant, giving 30 degrees to each sign; where the number ends, there will be the Part of Wheat. You will then consider how the lord of that sign is disposed; for the better it is disposed, the more wheat will be expensive, and the worse it is disposed, the more it will be cheap and of lower value. 

You will also see how the other significators I named to you are disposed; for those that are well-disposed will contribute to an increase in price and a scarcity of the item, and those that are poorly disposed will contribute to a low price and a greater abundance. According to this, you shall judge the others—each in its own place and its state of health, with the aforementioned aspects, and the Moon, or whatever other thing whose Part you seek. If the significator of the price of wheat (or any other thing) or the lord of the house in which the Part falls is impeded and in a bad state, but a "fortune" is well-fortuned and the Moon aspects the Part, it signifies that the wheat (or whatever else you seek) will be abundant and cheap. If, however, a "malefic" planet aspects it, the item will not be abundant, but it will still be cheap. And if its significator is fortunate, strong, and well-disposed, but a malefic aspects it, it signifies that the wheat or 

<column-break/>

To know in which regions the aforementioned events will happen: consider from which direction the lord of the Ascendant, or of the tenth, seventh, or fourth houses comes—whether in the eastern, southern, western, or northern part. ### ¶ On the Time when these things shall occur.
To know the time in which the significations of the predicted Parts ought to happen, and in which quarter that significance arrives: look at the Part you desire. If it falls in the Ascendant or between the Ascendant and the <term>fourth house</term> <note>the "angle" at the bottom of the chart</note>, its significance will happen in the first quarter of that year's revolution. If it is in the fourth house or between the fourth and the seventh, it happens in the second quarter. If it is in the seventh or between the seventh and tenth, it happens in the third quarter. But if it is in the tenth or between the tenth and the Ascendant, it happens in the final quarter of that time. The closer it is to an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the faster it will happen; the further it is from one, the slower.

And some Parts have four significators: the two from which it is extracted, the third to which it arrives, and the fourth from which it begins to project. A Part is harmonious when it is content with one significator when that significator aspects it...

However, the Part that has two significators <note>A planet that "rules" or "signifies" a specific point in the chart</note> strengthens it when both aspect <note>an "aspect" is a specific geometric angle between planets, like a trine or square</note> it; they give greater hope of fulfilling what the Part intends, especially if it is in a more dignified house of the lord where the Part falls. Or it might be knowledge concerning the Part of Servants or Attendants, where no specific significator aspects the Part, but Mercury (who naturally signifies servants and attendants) aspects it; but this will be below the full meaning of the Part's significator, and it will happen through someone who involves themselves in the matter, perhaps irregularly. If that unfortunate planet is **Saturn**, it will be an impediment from someone of great age. If it is **Jupiter**, the cause will be religious men or judges and others mediating between them. And if she is diminished in light, it will be because the matter is deteriorated and diminished.

at the hour of its elevation or enthronement: in the day, from the Sun to the 15th degree of the sign of Leo and projected from the degree of the Moon; in the night, however, it is taken from the degree of the Moon to the 15th degree of the sign of Cancer and projected from the degree of the Sun. ¶ There is also another Part of Kingship or Empire which is taken at the hour of its elevation: in the day, from the Sun to Saturn, and in the night the reverse, and it is projected from the Ascendant of the revolution of the year in which the king or emperor was elevated, or anyone else promoted to a lay dignity. ¶ And **Al-Qabisi** said that if Jupiter is in a <term>common sign</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and it is a daytime revolution, and Jupiter is falling from an angle, it is taken from Saturn to Jupiter and 30 degrees are added, then projected from the Ascendant of the revolution of the year in which the king rose. ¶ If, however, they are opposite one another and both are falling from the Ascendant, then half of the degrees between them are taken and projected from the Ascendant. And when you know in which sign or degree this is, save it; for this will be the place from which you will calculate the Part of the Palma. When you wish to prepare it, you shall prepare the Ascendant of the revolution of the year in which the king rose or was elected; after this, take from the planet oriental to the Sun (either Saturn or Jupiter in that year) to the degree of the first Part's equation which you saved, and project it from the Ascendant of the revolution; where it ends, that will be the place of the First Part. ¶ The Second Part is found when you look from the conjunction in which the kingdom or empire rose, to which sign or degree the profection of the year arrives from the number given to all (30 degrees for a year, a month, and the day) in which the king rose; that is the place of the equation of the Second Part; save that also. After this, take from the planet oriental to the Sun (namely Saturn and Jupiter) to the place of the Second Part's equation which you saved, and project it from the Ascendant of the revolution; where it ends, that is the place of the Second Part. These are the Parts that signify the strength of the king and his durability.

### ¶ Here begins the treatise on Nativities and their accidents, and other things that seem to pertain to those nativities generally and particularly. Preface.

Since the entire intention of astrology seems to be principally concerned with two things—namely, <term>nativities</term> <note>birth charts of individuals</note> and <term>revolutions</term>—and primarily with nativities, while other matters are secondary, it seems to me fitting and very appropriate to faithfully explain with my whole heart and mind that which the Divine Goodness has granted me. According to what my small knowledge can reveal for the utility of study, I shall follow in the footsteps of our predecessors: namely, **Ptolemy**, **Abu Ma'shar**, **Hermes**, **Al-Omar**, **Abu 'Ali**, **Al-Kindi**, **Zargis**, **Dorotheus**, and others who have studied generally and particularly for our benefit in this work.

<header>Concerning the Judgment of Nativities</header>

### An explanation of why this treatise was delayed until now

**L**et no one among those wishing to study wonder, nor let anyone arise as if envious, or speaking evil, or as a detractor, if the treatise on nativities <note>A "nativity" is a birth chart or the astrological study of a person's life based on their birth moment.</note> is placed after the other treatises mentioned above. For although birth precedes all the <term>accidents</term> <note>original: "accidentia." In medieval philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential qualities or events that happen to a person, such as their health, wealth, or character traits.</note> noted in other treatises, the study of nativities is found to be the weightiest and most difficult of all knowable things. Therefore, this treatise deserved to be placed after all the other aforementioned subjects. For it cannot be understood by the unrefined, nor by those just being introduced to the art, nor even by those somewhat educated, but only by the wise and the skilled. For this reason, it is placed after other treatises that can be understood by those with less knowledge. Here, however, it is not so: for no being contained within the circle of light <note>Likely referring to the solar system or the visible heavens.</note> is found to be more powerful than the treatise on nativities. For nativities are the work through which all the accidents of the newborn are known—those which ought to happen to him naturally from the hour of birth until the end of his life—and similarly what may be known of him even after his death.

### Chapter Two: That two things are principally required for the existence of every man.

**S**ince two things are mainly required for the existence of every human being, I believe it is appropriate in this chapter to speak first of the first, and second of the second—what each one is and in what way each is valid—as I have touched upon these things elsewhere. I shall mention how they differ so that the order of these things may be more rightly perceived, since it is from God: for whatever is from God is ordained. ¶ The beginning of the first principle, therefore, is the falling of the seed into the womb <note>original: "casus seminis" (OCR "feminis"). This refers to the moment of conception.</note>, from which the fetus is generated not suddenly, but over time. Hence, if that hour is known (which is accustomed to happen only in few cases), one will know through that beginning what shall be concerning that conception until the hour of its exit from the maternal womb. The accidents of that conception will be according to the disposition and the very being of the surrounding stars, which signify the accidents of the body until the soul is infused, and of both body and soul immediately after the soul is infused, as long as it remains in the womb. For from the moment the seed is placed in the womb, there happens to it location, variation, dilation, increase, the composition of members, and their natural division, and the nutritional adaptation of similar parts—about which a certainty cannot be had in the same way it can be had regarding a birth. For birth is entirely the "internal end," while the first cause is the "external end"; the operation, however, is the end both inside and out. For the beginning of birth is certain, while others waver. If the falling of the seed into the womb were the perfect beginning, then the beginning which is birth would seem superfluous. Nevertheless, the falling of the seed can be called an "imperfect beginning," as can other things that happen before birth. However, knowledge of it can be gained through reason, just as a business deal is renewed by a formal summons after the cause has begun. And although certain fictional people and those striving to detract from the truth say that the falling of the seed into the womb is the beginning of all the accidents of the newborn until the end of his life, this is manifestly against all truth and in harmony with falsehood. For the seed of man is not as they say: no part, whether whole or integral, can perfect any thing without the help of another. For imperfection does not contribute to nobility. One form cannot be in different materials among those things which have a connection to each other; one can be taken away without the other before they are joined. The falling of the seed is like the "path" toward the accidents of being born; the infusion [of the soul] is like the "gate"; birth is like the "entrance" to them. Moreover, it is superfluous that what can be had or done through one thing should be done through many. For it is not the intention of Nature, which is always intent on what is better, to hinder or involve itself in complications.

<column-break/>

### Concerning the second principle.

**T**he other principle—the second—regards the accidents of the newborn from the hour of his birth until the end of his life. These two principles differ in this: the first regards the accidents of the conceived child from the hour of the falling of the sperm until the hour of birth, and at that hour its disposition expires. The second, however—which is more effective, truer, and nobler than the first in the whole being of the newborn—is caused by the first as a "form" is caused by "matter." For this reason, it is considered nobler from the hour of birth until the end of life. Hence, the hour of birth is necessary to have for each and every thing that will come to the newborn. This beginning is said to be the most certain; birth is seen to be such a beginning that it encompasses all future accidents of the newborn, which does not happen in any of the others. It is a "perfect beginning" in that nothing is lacking in the number or composition of the limbs. In birth, identity, certainty, and one and the same cause are required—therefore, not diversity. In other things, a diversity of causes is found, and therefore a diversity of effects; for effects are diversified and multiplied according to how the causes are diversified and multiplied. To the completion of the child in the womb, many and diverse things are gathered into one before it is born; but once gathered, they are preserved through birth alone. This is properly the intention of Nature, which, as much as it is in itself, intends to propose things that are always worthier and better. Perfection contributes to nobility; for while the conceived child remains in the womb, it is "in motion," and that which is in motion is not at its goal or end, but is "on the way." It is in the operation of the imperfect, which is joined to motion. When, however, it is at the goal, it is in perfection; for the goal (or perfection) and the way (or motion) are contrary to each other. Hence, perfection takes away motion. For the child, while in the womb, is "on the way" until the membranes are broken in the natural order; then is the goal, for it is now perfect or complete, and it ceases to be "on the way" as a conception. ¶ Then the other principle begins—the second—which is the life of the man, in which he grows, is increased, diminished, and fails. Nor can a child be called "perfect" before the rational soul is present with it, since the soul is the "first perfection," and knowledge and virtue are the "second." In birth, both can be found, though perhaps not in every way or in a totally blessed manner. In the case of the seed, however, no perfection is found; the falling of the seed is an imperfect thing which lacks many things, and from the imperfect, the "perfect" cannot truly be named, because something is missing from it. And this principle is called the "being of man" because the newborn then begins to use the five natural bodily senses, which he could not use freely while in the womb. His growth and increase are clearly felt, and he also uses certain other accidents he did not use before, such as speaking, laughing, crying, and the like. ¶ The being of the newborn is also helped by the power of the stars, which have influence at the hour of birth over his qualities—though it may perhaps seem to some idle people that the stars do not help at all in making the newborn, which is far from the truth. For the stars help the conception in bringing it to completion, and after perfection, in leading it healthfully forth from the mother's womb. And just as they were involved in shaping him after the seed fell in the womb, so they help in nourishing him after birth. Since the truth of the matter is so, it is necessary for you to observe the state of the stars at the hour of the infant's exit from the womb, so that you may perceive the quality of the body and the soul of the newborn. You may do this through the <term>lords of the triplicity</term> <note>The three planets that rule a specific group of zodiac signs (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> of the Ascendant for nourishment, and through the <term>lords of the terms</term> <note>Specific degrees of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note> for direction; through this, you may naturally and truthfully proceed through the state of his life and all his being as long as he lives.

...be known: and to those things of which mention was made concerning the diversities of nativities; and I will do so below in its proper place and time, arriving by the path of nature and truth at the differing accidents. Whatever the state of the stars was at the hour of birth, and their dispositions, such will be all things for the newborn from his very birth until the end of his life. Since the state of the stars and their dispositions are to the state of the newborn and his dispositions like a container; and the state of the newborn and his dispositions are like the contents; and the contents are changed by the container. One disposition of the stars changes many dissimilarities: so that they seem in a way infinite, which for the most part happen by the implicit reason of the stars. The scrutiny of these matters seems to pertain to the natural philosopher <note>original: "naturalem." A scholar of the natural world and physics, rather than a purely mathematical astrologer.</note> rather than the astrologer; and therefore should be left to the natural philosophers; yet the astrologer cannot pass over this with such a "dry foot" <note>original: "sicco pede." A Latin idiom meaning to pass over a subject quickly or without getting one's feet wet.</note> without making some mention of them: since his intention could not easily be fully expressed; I will also speak to you of many things in their proper place and time.

### Chapter Three: How the state of the newborn is to be examined.

Now you must see by what method, according to each species of prognostication, the state of the newborn can be examined and clearly understood, so that the powers of the stars over these things can be narrated. By the natural path, as pertains to the mathematician <note>In the medieval period, "mathematicus" often specifically referred to an astrologer.</note>, the accidents of the newborn may be truly comprehended: and according to the figure of quantities we may arrive particularly and truly at the knowledge of that which we intend. And since particulars exist within universals according to the nature of both, these things will be seen later in their place and time. Nor does it seem appropriate here that a distinct discourse be held concerning every place in the chart: but concerning the lordship of dignities <note>original: "dignitatū dñio." Referring to the 'essential dignities' or the relative power a planet holds within specific signs.</note> and their grace in this matter, let what pertains to them and what is specific to them be said briefly in due order. According to the revolution of the *Allachir* <note>original: "Allachir." Likely a Latinization of an Arabic term (possibly *Al-Akhir*) referring to the planet that governs the length of life or the "prolongation" of time.</note>, which is the agent of the heavens and of the stars signifying the virtues of the nativities, let the accidents be distinguished in natural order, joined together step-by-step according to the successive significations of the houses. Thus, by subtle investigation, all things that are to come to the newborn in the whole time of his life, from the hour of birth until his final day, may be known more certainly. As for what should be investigated first among the aforementioned accidents: it seems to me most fitting in the inquiry of these accidents to place the instruction for finding the first degree of the nativity, the **Ascendant**, and then the rest in order as is fitting.

### Chapter 4: On the investigation of an unknown Ascendant degree.

In the resolution of a certain doubt that very often occurs, let your mind rest concerning the determination of an uncertain degree of someone's birth. Insofar as we can be made certain of it, it is appropriate that I set down a special chapter for you (as I remember saying above) according to the rules of the ancient wise men, and also what seems to me should be added, so that you may be truly certain concerning the degree of any rising sign for any birth. And since birth is the first accident that happens to the conceived child after its completion and the breaking of the *cotyledon* <note>original: "cottidionis." This refers to the placental attachments; the author is describing the physical separation of the baby from the mother.</note>, it is necessary for you to be made certain of the degree of the Ascendant so that you may avoid all error, and thus certify the newborn concerning all his accidents throughout his entire life. And I do not want you to think the discovery of this thing is merely through subtlety—it will be an inquiry even beyond what is found written in the books of the ancient wise men: not because they were ignorant of it, but because they left it to the industry of the wise.

<margin>
Concerning the
same [topic].
</margin>

But if the degree of the Ascendant of the birth—the degree of the sign which is on the eastern line—is found when the *cotyledon* is broken,

<column-break/>

the boy is then fitly born. He is not said to be born immediately when he begins to appear from the maternal womb, nor is he said to be born while he has not yet completely emerged from it: but he is said to be born when two parts of him have already appeared and the remaining third has stayed hidden, emerging naturally without a break in time. And if you have fixed the Ascendant at the moment when his last part emerges, no very perceptible error will fall into your work, nor one that perceptibly hinders. But if any impediment should occur that hinders the natural mode of being born when two parts have passed and the third remains to emerge—which you will be able to detect by the great industry of your judgment—you will have what was sought: for the degree which was then on the eastern line is called the Ascendant of that birth, provided the aforementioned observation regarding the child's appearance is kept.

### Method of finding the aforesaid degree.

<margin>
Concerning the
Degree.
</margin>

The method of intention for this profound matter, as the authority of our predecessors moves us, is as follows. You shall take the hour of the infant's exit from the maternal womb as you seek it best and most certainly with an **astrolabe** or any other instrument fit for this, such as a **quadrant** or a **horalogiū** <note>original: "horalogiū." An early mechanical device for telling time, such as a sundial or water clock.</note> or any other instrument by which hours are discerned. But with an astrolabe you can be more certain than with any other. Yet even with all this, you cannot be certain "to the fingernail" <note>original: "ad vnguem." A common Latin idiom for perfect precision.</note> without a scruple of doubt. Therefore, to remove every scruple of doubt and so that a certain and constructive reason may be had for this, even for one who has the hour of birth as close as you can be certified by yourself or by the report of others, or of midwives or the like—and so a certain and examined reason can be shown to you—you will equate the planets for that hour which is not fully certain. You will verify their places and the 12 <term>cusps</term> <note>The boundaries that divide the twelve 'houses' or life-areas of the astrological chart.</note>, and you will erect the figure according to the ascension of the region in which he was born. And you shall then take the degree of the <term>syzygy</term> <note>original: "cōiunctionis... vel puentionis." The author is referring to the New Moon or Full Moon that immediately preceded the birth.</note> nearest to that birth: the degree of the conjunction if the birth followed a New Moon, or the degree of the "prevention" if the birth followed a Full Moon—namely, the degree of that luminary [Sun or Moon] which was above the earth at the hour of that event. Then you shall look for the **Almuten** <note>The planet that has the most combined essential dignity (power) at a specific point in the zodiac.</note> in that degree by way of its house, or by exaltation, or term, or triplicity, or affinity of the Sun in the figure you have erected. But if all the aforesaid significators are powerless, hindered, and unfortunate, you shall then use the **Lord of the Face** <note>The planet ruling the 10-degree segment (decan) of the sign.</note>.

Concerning the
Ascendant.
</margin>

### Instruction for finding the aforesaid degree.

The instruction for this matter is this: you will see if the Lord of the House aspects the sought degree of conjunction or prevention, or is personally present in it; for the Lord of the House is to be preferred above all other significators. But if this is not the case, and the Lord of Exaltation aspects it, he shall be preferred over the Lord of the House and all other significators. But if neither of those aspects it nor is in it, and the Lord of Triplicity aspects it or is in it, you shall consider that one. If indeed he himself does not aspect it, you shall observe the Lord of the Term under the aforesaid conditions: yet do not judge according to this unless you have first seen the strengths of all of them. For you must observe the one who has more strengths in the aforesaid degree, except for what the work of another's aspect requires. But if all the aforesaid planets, or many of them, aspect the aforesaid degree equally, the one who has more dignities or strengths in it shall be called the <term>significator</term>. And if they are in different degrees or minutes and differ in number, you shall take the one whose number of degrees in the sign in which he is, is closer to the degree of the angle [the house cusp] if he is in an angle: or closer to the Sun if he is oriental [rising before the Sun]. But if it is not so, then see which of them was closer to the degree of the term in which he was, at the beginning or the end, and you shall prefer that one over them. But if all were equal in strength and dignity...

If the degree of the almuten planet is closer to the degree of the Ascendant's cusp than to the degree of any other angle, and the number of degrees it has traveled from the sign in which you find it is equal to the number of degrees of the rising sign found at the ambiguous birth—which you had previously found through your own consideration or the instruction of another—then that will be the sought-after Ascendant. A certain scholar <note>original: "C. Papiensis." The moment of conception.</note> in the womb is the degree of the Ascendant at birth, and vice versa.

## Chapter 5: On the narration of the division of nativities and some of their accidents.

<margin>Figure of Haly on the divisions!</margin> **T**hat most reverend predecessor of ours, Ptolemy, wishing to divide the <term>accidents</term> <note>original: "accidentia." In astrology, these are the events, characteristics, or "happenings" that befall a person.</note> of nativities according to the natural progress, took such a method of proceeding. For he said that whenever one wishes to divide them naturally, one finds what pertains to the execution of that work. He said that there are certain accidents which happen before birth and even after birth. Before birth: such as speaking of siblings, because it is possible that some were born before the birth itself from the same parents and some will be born after it. And there are some that happen at the very hour of birth; and these are not one and the same, but diverse. And he said that the accidents which happen to the newborn at the hour of birth, which the astrologer intends to know, are many and diverse—such as speaking of males and females, and whether the woman in labor will bear twins or multiple children or not, and of monstrous forms, and of those who did not grow. And he said concerning the accidents that happen after birth, one must speak of life, for which he gives a rule in two ways: one according to quantity, the other according to quality. For quantity does not vary except according to what is given by the <term>Hyleg</term> and <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>original: "vlez z alcocodē." Technical terms for the "Giver of Life" and the "Giver of Years" in a birth chart, used to calculate lifespan.</note>; for it is either long, short, or middling. Quality, however, varies according to the dispositions and directions of the lords of the <term>terms</term> <note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by specific planets.</note> of the birth chart in many ways: for some is good, some bad, some easy, some laborious, some generous, some stingy, some miserable, some greedy, some in good, some in evil; some chaste, some religious, some incestuous or lustful; some is in thieving and 

<column-break/>

squandering; some in gaining and preserving; some in dissipating and wasting; some in ruling; some in serving; some in praise; some in blame; and in many other almost innumerable ways, the qualities of the lives of the newborn vary according to the diverse accidents of men. These coincide from the diversities of the different movements of the super-celestial bodies and the uses and choices of men, as will be sufficiently said below in its proper place and time. Then we speak of the form and appearance of the newborn; then of the illnesses and impediments happening to the body; then of the qualities of the soul and its accidents; then of the fortunes and misfortunes of the newborn; likewise of his kingdom and exaltation and his greatness; then of his works; then of his marriage and the time spent with his spouse; then what may happen to him from his children, and of his familiarity with men, and of friends, and of his travels; and finally, to judge the manner of his death. And some of the wise men have followed his footsteps. I, however, proceeding not so much in a prior way but in a different way yet tending toward the same end, will follow the succession of the houses and their significations, beginning from the first up to the twelfth. I shall make mention to you of almost all things pertaining to the accidents of birth, so that the work of nativities may be rendered easier and you may more easily attain what you intend.

## Chapter 6: On the causation of the delays of those born in the maternal womb.

<margin>On the Cause of the delay in the womb</margin> **T**he delays of those conceived in maternal wombs are caused by the dispositions of the super-celestial bodies according to their three principal diversities, which are the greater, the middle, and the lesser, under which certain other intermediate ones are subordinated. For if you see the Moon in the upper part of its <term>epicycle</term> <note>In Ptolemaic astronomy, a small circle on which a planet moves, while the center of that circle moves around a larger circle.</note>, going from the east to the west at the hour of the falling of the seed into the womb (or at the hour of a question made after conception), it signifies that the delay of the infant in the womb is the greater, which consists of 288 days from the hour of the falling of the seed until the hour of birth. But if you find it in the lower part of the epicycle, going from the west to the east, it signifies that there was a middle delay which consists of 273 days; and this is if the Moon in the question was distant from the degree in which it was at the hour of the falling of the seed (or from the degree which was then the Ascendant) by 90 degrees only. If, however, it was distant by more or less, it signifies that the circular movements were not complete, and then there was some other middle delay between those—namely, between the greater and the middle. And if the Moon was in the degree of the Ascendant of the falling of the seed, it signifies that there was a lesser delay which consists of 258 days. If it was above the earth, distant from the east or from the west by more than 5 degrees, there will be some other intermediate delay in the womb between those—namely, between the middle and the lesser. But if the Moon was directly in opposition to the degree of the Ascendant at the hour of the falling of the seed, you could then err by one month. Since Haly said that to avoid that error, you ought to take the degrees that were between the western degree and the degree of the Moon and double them and divide by 24; and how many there are will be days, and what remains below 24 will be hours, since the Moon travels one degree in two equal hours according to its mean course. Therefore, add these days and these hours to the hours of the lesser delay, and what is collected will be the sought-after delay; then you will subtract this delay from the days of the birth and you will have what you intend. If, however, it was a leap year, add then 5 hours and 59 minutes; and with that which comes within the tables, equate the Moon; for the degree in which you then find it will be the place where it was at the hour of the falling of the seed. See, therefore, what degree was then the Ascendant, for that was the Ascendant at the hour of the falling of the seed. If the Moon was below the earth, tending from east to west, then you shall take what was between the rising degree and the Moon in degrees and minutes and divide by 24, as was said, and add to the middle delay, subtracting what was collected from the days and hours...
