# Concerning the account of the four differences or diversities of births.

It was stated above that there are four differences or diversities of births. Now, mention must be made of each of them individually. For as the ancient wise men testify: <margin>¶</margin> The first of these will be of those who are stillborn <note>original: "abortivorum"</note>, who are born as if dead or half-dead, or those whose life is not prolonged until they take any nourishment. <margin>¶</margin> The second indeed is of those who take nourishment, but life does not last in them long enough for any perceptible benefit to follow from it. <margin>¶</margin> For the third is of those who take nourishment and live for months or years, but do not exceed the years of childhood; and if they do not exceed them, they do not then reach a long life. <margin>¶</margin> The fourth, indeed, is of those who take nourishment and life lasts in them until they reach youth, and sometimes they reach old age. <margin>¶</margin> And subordinate to this is another category, namely, those who reach extreme old age and die of senescence; although this happens to few, my grandfather was one whom I saw die without any manifest cause, except that the vital spirits departed, leaving the corpse behind; for he was 120 years old, about whom I think it should be seen in the appropriate order of sustenance. <margin>¶</margin> And although I said I would reveal more elsewhere in this treatise and show my strengths, I want you to understand my word correctly. For birth is a very high and most subtle business requiring great understanding; hence I will not adopt the highest style lest it perhaps hinder you, nor a completely humble one lest you perhaps despise it; but a middle style, so that you may better follow what I intend, and do not think me not to have kept my promise to you.

## Part Two.
### Chapter One: How the four differences of births are to be seen in order.

Mention having been made above that there are four definitions of births according to the four diversities in the first part of this treatise—which precedes this one, to which this is subordinate—it now remains to speak of all of them in this second part in order. And first, of those whose life does not last in them long enough for them to take any nourishment. The science of this matter is that you should look at the degree of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> of any birth and its lord; also the lords of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: Fire, Earth, Air, or Water.</note> of the degree of the Ascendant and the other angles and their lords, and the degree of each of the <term>luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> and their lords. And <term>Aboali</term> <note>original: "Aboali," referring to the 9th-century Persian astrologer Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat.</note> said that you should look at the lords of the triplicity of the Sun, and likewise Jupiter and Venus, and the diurnal and nocturnal planets, according to whether the birth was by day or by night. Look also at the <term>Part of Fortune</term> and its lord; likewise the lord of the conjunction or prevention which was before the birth itself. Then you will look for the planet which was stronger than the others in the predicted places or in some of them, and you will see whether it is only one, or two, or three. If there is only one, and it is "falling" <note>positioned in a cadent house, which is considered a weak placement</note> from the Ascendant or from the angles, and some of the <term>malefics</term> <note>Harmful planets, usually Saturn or Mars.</note> are with it in the same degree hindering it, or if the degree of the Ascendant is hindered—namely, so that some of the malefics are in it without having "dignity" <note>astrological authority or strength</note> there, or it regards it by a square aspect or by opposition—it signifies that the newborn will die before taking any nourishment. You say the same if the degrees in which the luminaries are found are hindered.

<column-break/>

And <term>Ptolemy</term> <note>The famous 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian astronomer and astrologer.</note> indeed seemed to have felt something different from what other wise men felt, although not contrary. For it seemed to him that when the luminary which holds authority and the degree of the Ascendant are hindered, and the lords of the degrees in which the luminaries were found have retreated from the angles, the newborn will taste nothing until they die. And he said that the hour of this event will be when the luminaries reach a malefic. <margin>¶</margin> But other ancients said that when all three lords of the triplicity have retreated from the angles, and the luminaries and their lords have retreated, and the conjunction or prevention and its lord have retreated, then the newborn will taste nothing until they die; or the one born will not be human, or will be from those categories that are born with non-natural signs, such as those who have more limbs than they ought or lack them, or have them transposed, as I have seen many: some of whom lacked arms, some even hands, some feet, some legs; some had their knees backwards; some lacked eyes. And I saw one who had three arms, and another who had a breast in place of an arm, and another who did not have an anus; and there was a certain foolish lay <term>surgeon</term> <note>original: "cyrurgicus"</note> who wanted to fix him; he was so foolish that he pierced him below with a certain iron and so killed him. And there was likewise in my time a certain <term>monster</term> <note>original: "monstrū," used historically to mean a biological marvel or prodigy, often portending something.</note> which from the navel upward was two men, and from there only one; and another had one head and from there downward were two bodies. Or that newborn will be of those who are born with some brute beast, as sometimes happens with a monkey or a weasel or similar things, or a woman gives birth to a monstrous thing, or the newborn itself is a brute animal. For if it is so, and the aforesaid significators are all falling as was said, and some malefic hinders the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon or the <term>almuten</term> <note>The planet with the most combined "dignity" or power over a specific degree.</note> over the aforesaid places, or if the malefic itself is the almuten, it will be a fierce wild animal unwilling to associate with others, especially with humans, such as a wolf and the like. If indeed the benefics and malefics are present, and especially if Mercury has some dignity in these places, it will be of those that associate with humans, as <term>Asmar</term> <note>An unidentified astrological authority.</note> says, such as dogs and the like. And my mother, who seemed to be a sufficiently truthful woman, told me that in her time a certain woman gave birth to a cat.

# Concerning the second difference or definition.

The second difference or definition is that you look at the ascending degree and the other angles and their lords; also the degrees of the luminaries and their lords; and the lords of their triplicity according to whether the birth was by day or night; also the lords of the triplicity of the ascending degree; and the Part of Fortune and the conjunction or prevention which was before the birth itself; and the lords of the triplicity in which it fell; also Jupiter and Venus. And you should see the planet which was stronger in these places by a multitude of dignities, which is called the <term>almuten</term> <note>original: "almude-bit," a variant of almuten.</note>. If it is falling from the angles and some of the malefics are present with them, and there is some distance between the almuten and the malefic, it signifies that the newborn takes some nourishment for itself and lives until that almuten reaches the malefic, or the malefic reaches it by its body or by an aspect which first happens to it, degree by degree; for then it signifies that the newborn will perish after so many days or so many months or so many years. If the malefic is hindered in an angle and in a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius.</note>, there will be years according to the quantity of degrees of distance between the almuten and the malefic. If, however, it is in a <term>succedent house</term> <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses.</note> and in a <term>common sign</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces.</note>, there will be months. If indeed in a <term>cadent house</term> <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses.</note> and in a <term>movable sign</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn.</note>, there will be days. But if...

If [the malefic planet] is in an angle and in a mutable sign <note>original: "signo communi," referring to Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, it shall reduce a sixth part of those years. If, however, it is in a succedent house and a cardinal sign <note>original: "signo mobili," referring to Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>, it shall reduce a fourth part of those months. And if it is in a cadent house in a cardinal sign, it shall reduce a third part of those days. But if a benefic <note>original: "fortuna," referring to Jupiter or Venus</note> is in the place of the malefic and is in a cadent house in a mutable sign, it prolongs those days by a sixth part. And if all these, or most of them, fall away from the angles, the child will indeed taste food but will not be nourished. If, however, any of the lords of the triplicity <term>lords of the triplicity: planets that rule a group of three signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</term> of the ascendant are at the cusp of the ascending angle, or the tenth, second, or fifth houses, or if Jupiter or Venus is there and is free from impediments and from malefics, it signifies nourishment, but does not determine whether it will be long or short, except according to other testimonies that signify nourishment. And if the aforementioned significators are impeded, look to the lords of the triplicity of the Part of Fortune <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated point in the chart representing well-being and prosperity</term>, and judge according to their condition and according to how the Sun aspects that Part. Say the same of the lords of the triplicity of the conjunction or prevention <note>original: "iunctionis vel praeventionis," referring to the New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth</note>. It could also be said that if the Moon is besieged by two malefics, one of which is in the first house and the other in the seventh, the child's life will be short.

### ¶ If the time is to be known.

**If** the time and hour when these things ought to happen are to be known, the ascending degree must be directed to the body of the impeding malefic, or to its square aspect <note>original: "quartum aspectum," an angle of 90 degrees</note>, or to its opposition, giving one degree for a day, a month, or a year, according to whether they signified days, months, or years. And if the native has then passed one year, you shall consider afterward according to profections <term>profections: an ancient timing technique where a point in the chart moves forward by a specific amount over a set time</term>, giving thirty degrees to one year according to equal degrees: two degrees and thirty minutes for a month, and every five minutes for a day, and nearly every twelve seconds for an hour; and when the number is finished, then the native shall perish. And Aomar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: look also in that hour to certain benefics, if they are in angles or in their best places and dignities, or to the planet that is more worthy in the ascending degree and the Part of Fortune; because this signifies, according to the quantity of its strength or weakness, whether the life of the native will reach years, months, or days, according to the quantity of the gift of that planet from its minor years. And he said: perhaps it will be days, as Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> thinks. When the lords of the triplicity of the ascendant—the first, second, and third—fall away, it signifies that the child will not be nourished. And especially if Saturn is in an angle in nocturnal births, or Mars in diurnal ones. And the hour of death will be when the profection of any other year reaches the angles; because when a malefic is in an angle and the year comes to any of the angles where the light of the square aspect of the malefic is, if the native has not died in the first year, then it performs its work. And he said and thought in the *Book of Similitudes*: because if there are two Almutens <term>Almuten: the planet with the most combined essential dignity at a specific point</term>, or one of them is impeded, the native will die and the other cannot suffice. Similarly, if there are three and one of them is impeded, although the other two are strong, the child will last but his life will not be prolonged. Even if there are four and one or two are impeded and the others are useful, the child will remain longer but his life will not be prolonged. If three are impeded, even if the other is strong, the native will not live; and no strong benefic will aspect the significator of that birth, especially if the Moon is impeded and not received; but if she is free and received <note>original: "recepta," an astrological term where a planet is in a sign ruled by another planet that aspects it</note>, it signifies a prolong-

<column-break/>

ation of life in respect to its shortness.

### ¶ Concerning the third category or definition.

**The third** difference or definition is when the native has neither a Hyleg <term>Hyleg: the planet or point that acts as the "Giver of Life"</term> nor an Alcocoden <term>Alcocoden: the "Giver of Years" that determines the lifespan</term> from his birth, but the lords of the ascendant, the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note>, and the lords of the houses in which they are found are free from the aforementioned impediments—namely, retrogradation, combustion <note>being too close to the Sun</note>, bodily conjunction with malefics, and their square aspect or opposition. Even if the lords of the houses in which the malefics are found are falling from the angles or from the ascendant, or are impeded in the angles, it signifies the child's delay in the world and his nourishment, but his life will not be prolonged. And he will never become a man because he will not last beyond twelve years, but will die sooner according to the number of degrees between the lord of the ascendant and the angle from which they fell. And Tiberiadis <note>Omar Tiberiades, an 8th-century astrologer</note> said that when a birth is as we have described, we shall defer speaking of such a birth until the ascendant reaches one cycle, namely twelve years—one year for each sign—and this because of the fall of the significators. And he said that as often as the cycle of the ascendant reaches the bodies of the malefics, or the square aspect or opposition of any of them, there will be fear for him until the ascendant runs through one cycle. And he said that when it has passed one cycle, we shall direct for him from the ascendant one year for every degree by the ascensions of the region in which that birth occurred, until it reaches the malefics as was said in the other category.

### ¶ Concerning the fourth category or definition.

**The fourth** difference or definition is that the native should have a Hyleg and Alcocoden, and the aforementioned significators—namely, the ascending degree and its lord, and the lords of the triplicity of the ascending degree and of the other angles and their lords, and the degree of the luminaries and their lords, and Jupiter and Venus and the lords of the houses in which they are, and the diurnal and nocturnal planets according to whether the birth was by day or night, and the Part of Fortune and its lords, and likewise the lord of the conjunction or prevention that was before the birth, and the planet that was Almuten in these places—all should be free.

### ¶ On the finding of the Hyleg.

**The finding** of another thing is that you seek it in diurnal births from the Sun; if you find it in the 1st, 11th, or 10th house, it is fit to receive the Hyleg from it, whether it be in a masculine or feminine sign. If it is outside these places, in the 7th, 8th, or 9th house and in a masculine sign, it must be set as the Hyleg. And Aomar said: know that the Sun or the other places that serve as Hyleg cannot be Hyleg unless the lords of the houses, or of the exaltations, or of the triplicities, or of the terms, or of the faces <note>The five types of "Essential Dignity" or planetary strength</note> aspect them, according to what seemed to Aboali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a student of Mashallah</note> concerning the lordship of the faces. If the lords of any of these dignities do not aspect it, the Sun will not be fit for the Hyleg, nor will the lord of that dignity. Similarly, you shall pronounce concerning the Moon in the day and night, and concerning the Part of Fortune and the ascending degree, and also the degree of conjunction or prevention. Again, if the Sun is not fit to be the Hyleg, you shall take the Hyleg from the Moon; if you find her in an angle or in a succedent house and in a feminine sign, and any of the lords of the four aforementioned dignities aspects her, she is fit to be the Hyleg. If the birth was preventional <note>occurring after a Full Moon</note>, then the Hyleg must be sought from the Part of Fortune. If it was conjunctional <note>occurring after a New Moon</note>, seek it from the ascending degree, which will signify it if any of the aforementioned significators aspect it or the Moon, and it shall be preferred to the Part of Fortune when it is so. If, however, none of them aspect it, it shall not signify the Hyleg.

If [the previous significator] is not found, then you shall look to the ascending degree, and if not that, then to the Part of Fortune <note>original: "ptē fortune"</note>. If the Part of Fortune is in aspect with its own ruler or with the ascending degree of the birth, it shall be the Hyleg; if not, then it shall not. But if neither of those can be the Hyleg, then look to the degree of the Conjunction <note>the New Moon prior to birth</note> if the birth was conjunctional, or to the degree of the Prevention <note>the Full Moon prior to birth</note> if it was preventional. Aomar <note>likely Umar al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note>, however, seems to prefer that in this case one should look to the degree in which the Moon was at the hour of the Prevention. If, again, none of the aforementioned significators aspect those degrees, the effort is frustrated; the Hyleg will be absent and the child will have a short life <note>original: "puer vite," likely meaning a life of hours or days</note>. But if any of them aspect that degree, that planet shall be called the Alcocoden <term>Alcocoden: the "Giver of Years," a planet that determines the person's lifespan based on its relationship to the Hyleg</term> and the giver of years. And if all the aforementioned significators aspect the said degree—the lord of the house, the lord of the exaltation, the lord of the term, and the lord of the triplicity—then the one who is closest to the degree by aspect or by conjunction shall be the Alcocoden or giver of years, whether that aspect is direct or retrograde. If, however, all aspect it equally, then he who is stronger in his own place and holds equal dignity (meaning only one dignity) shall be called the Alcocoden. But if one of them holds more dignities than the others, he shall be called stronger than the rest and shall outweigh them all, provided he aspects the said degree; even if there is a smaller distance between the Hyleg degree and another of the aforementioned significators who holds only one dignity in the Hyleg degree.

### On the verification of the years and life of the native.

After you have done this and are certain of the Hyleg <term>Hyleg: the "Life-Giver," the primary point in a chart (usually the Sun, Moon, or Ascendant) that represents the native's vital force</term> and the Alcocoden, you will be able to determine the years of the native and his life: whether his future life will be long or short, healthy or dangerous, and concerning his good or bad accidents, as well as his prosperities and adversities. For the Hyleg holds the root of life, while the Alcocoden holds the number of his years. Because the state of life is taken from the Hyleg, but the granting of years is taken from the Alcocoden; yet neither of them is sufficient for giving life to the newborn without the other. For just as a man alone is not sufficient for generating, nor a woman alone sufficient for conceiving or bringing forth—for one cannot beget without the other—so the Hyleg gives formal life, and the Alcocoden gives it effectively.

### On the verification of the years of the native.

When you have received the years of the native and their number, you shall consider the disposition of the Hyleg and Alcocoden, and you will see how many years are attributed to the native. You will also see if the years are given to him by the Alcocoden or by another, as sometimes happens; if he has them through the Alcocoden, what you must do will be clear. If, however, fewer years are given, you will see whether the Alcocoden's years are equal to the minor, mean, major, or maximum years <note>astrologers assigned different "lengths" of years to planets based on their strength</note>, for it may come down to the very least or slightly less than the minor. And you will see at what point in the years the Hyleg reaches the body of the malefics <note>Mars or Saturn</note>, or the places where they were at the birth, or to their square aspect or opposition, or to the Dragon’s Tail <note>the South Node of the Moon, considered a point of depletion</note>, or the degree in which it was at birth, or to the square aspect of the place where the Moon was at birth, or to its opposition—assigning, for each degree, one year according to the degree of that region. And if a benefic <note>original: "fortuna," referring to Jupiter or Venus</note> does not cast its rays to the term <note>a specific division of a zodiac sign</note> where the Hyleg meets a hindering malefic, the native will die in that year, month, or day; specifically at the hour when the Hyleg reaches the said places or any of them. But if the said years are not equal to the years of the Alcocoden, nor to those of the Hyleg, and the Hyleg reaches a hindering malefic as was said, or the aforementioned places without the aspect of any benefic, it will weigh upon the native with a most powerful hindrance, so that when he despairs of himself so as not to be cast down, and he himself fears he might perish, he shall ultimately escape unless he perhaps perishes through an error. But if a benefic protects the Hyleg with its rays, the native will be oppressed

<column-break/>

then; but it will not be so doubtful for him at that time.

## Chapter Two: On the diversity of opinions regarding the Hyleg.

Because there is a diversity of opinion among the wise regarding the Hyleg, though not <unclear>unpleasant</unclear>; for it seemed to Ptolemy that the Hyleg should not be sought in the eighth house, because the Ascendant has no help in it, and it is a dark place that does not aspect the Ascendant. In the ninth house, however, it is otherwise, as it is of the triplicity of the Ascendant and of its own kind; and because the Sun rejoices in it and it is its foundation. If the Sun is in the ninth house in someone's birth and the lord of the year <note>original: "altas," likely meaning the Almuten or high ruler</note> is well-disposed, the native will have a good, honorable life of good duration. To Dorotheus, however, it seemed that the Hyleg should not be sought from the eighth nor the seventh house unless it is in masculine signs. And he said that if the Sun were in these two houses, it would not be fit to be the Hyleg in feminine signs, since its strength is weakened and feminized in them. And it seemed to him that the Sun should be Hyleg in nocturnal births in the place opposite those masculine signs. But Ptolemy made no mention of the gender of the signs, for which reason it seems fitting to me that you follow the opinion of Dorotheus if you can, for it is more secure; otherwise, the opinion of Ptolemy is not to be rejected. If, however, the Sun is not in masculine signs in the aforementioned places in diurnal births, it will not be fit to be the Hyleg; then you must seek the Hyleg from the Moon. If you find her in any of the angles or succedent houses, she will be fit to be the Hyleg, and you will not care about the gender of the signs, whether they be masculine or feminine; nevertheless, in the births of women, she will be more useful in a feminine sign, and in the births of men, in a masculine sign. And in this all agreed: that the Moon is fit to be the Hyleg in the third house, because she rejoices in it and it is her foundation; regarding the ninth house, however, there was diversity among them. For it seemed to Dorotheus not to be certain that the Moon could be the Hyleg in this place, because she is then impeded. To Ptolemy, however, it seemed that she could be the Hyleg in the ninth, but she must be in a feminine sign. And Aomar said that if the Moon is not in these places and the birth is conjunctional, the Hyleg should be sought from the degree of the Ascendant of the birth. If, however, it is preventional, it should be sought from the Part of Fortune, which is called the "Ascendant of the Moon"; the degree of the Ascendant is then placed second. And the wise men proposed the Part of Fortune in a preventional birth because the Moon is then at the fullness of all her light from the side we see of her, and she rules the whole night. In conjunctional births, however, one must begin from the Ascendant, because the Moon is then deprived of all her light. But if the Hyleg is sought from the Part of Fortune and it signifies it, and it is in the angles or in the houses following the angles, you shall not care whether it is in a masculine or feminine sign. If you seek it from the Ascendant in the birth and the Ascendant is not impeded, even if the Part of Fortune is not there, it shall be the Hyleg. And Aomar said you shall not care whether it is falling <note>cadent</note> from the angles or not, because the Ascendant itself is an angle. And he said there is nothing in it to be sought that one should fear concerning those other Hyleg locations regarding profit or lack of profit. It is possible for the aforementioned places to be in places of profit or lack of profit; for the Ascendant does not cease to be in profit. And he said if the Sun, Moon, Part of Fortune, or Ascendant do not agree as Hyleg, look to the Conjunction or Prevention that occurred before the birth; and whichever of them the Sun or Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant or another of the benefics aspects, and it is in an angle or succedent to an angle, it shall be the Hyleg; nor shall you care whether it is a masculine or feminine sign.

### On the Knowledge of the Alcocoden.

**A**nd when you have identified the Hyleg <term>Hyleg: the planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life," used to determine the native's vitality</term> and you wish to know the Alcocoden <term>Alcocoden: the "Giver of Years," a planet that determines the specific length of a person's life based on its strength and position</term>, because it is the "divider," you shall consider the four said significators: namely, the lord of the house in which the Hyleg is located, the lord of its exaltation, the lord of its term <note>The "terms" or "bounds" are specific degrees of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</note>, and the lord of its triplicity. Whichever of these you find to be in the greatest aspect to the Hyleg, establish it as the Alcocoden. Begin with the lord of the term; if you find it projecting its rays toward that term, set it as the Alcocoden. If you do not find it so, look then to the lord of the house and work with it as you did with the lord of the term; then look to the lord of the exaltation, and finally the lord of the triplicity. If you find none of these in aspect, you shall use the last lord, the lord of the face <note>original: "faciei," referring to the decans or 10-degree divisions of a sign</note>, even though its significance is weak. You should understand this applies if their dignity is the same and equal—that is, the dignity of each of them. If, however, all of them aspect the Hyleg equally, and one of them holds more than one dignity, the one who has two shall be preferred over the one having only one; and the one who has three shall be preferred over the one having two, and he shall be called the stronger. If they are all equally strong in dignities or testimony, the one who is in an angle <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the most powerful locations</note> or in a succedent house <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> shall be preferred. If all are in an angle or succedent house, the one closest to the cusp <note>the boundary or starting point of an astrological house</note> of the angle or succedent house is called the stronger. If they are equal in strength and dignity in the place of the Hyleg, and equal in their house position, the one in his own dignity is preferred over another who is a "pilgrim" <note>original: "peregrinus," a planet with no essential dignity in its current location</note> or who is in his minor dignity. If all are equal in all the aforementioned strengths, the one who is oriental <note>rising before the Sun in the morning</note> shall be preferred. And if all are oriental, prefer the one closest to the Sun, provided he is not "combust" <note>original: "combustus," meaning so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden</note> by either cosmic or heliacal rising. If the Sun is on the oriental line, it shall be preferred over the other significators. And if any of the planets are in the Ascendant or the tenth house, not distant from the line of the cusp by more than three degrees before or five degrees behind, make that planet the ruler with the Hyleg, whether it has dignity there or not; but if it has dignity there, it will be stronger than any located outside those places, even if their dignity is equal. Do not doubt this if it is equal; indeed, even if the one absent from those places has one or even two more dignities than the one present, the one present in those places shall be stronger, as I have said. However, if it has no dignity there, its participation will be weak and its peace barely profitable. And if any of these planets are oriental and in the "paths of the Sun" <note>original: "caminis solis"</note> or before its second station or within five days after it, and it can walk for seven days and has some dignity in the place of the Hyleg, and is otherwise well-disposed, the Hyleg and Alcocoden may be sought from it, unless the lord of the term of the Hyleg's degree stands in the way. It seemed to Ptolemy <note>original: "Ptholomeo"</note> that an aspect constitutes one strength of a planet in the Hyleg and Alcocoden; and that a planet having three dignities, even if it does not aspect, is stronger than one that has only one dignity and does aspect. He does not then contradict other philosophers who said that the one who has one dignity will be stronger if present in the aforementioned places, because he understood this to apply to those aspecting and not to those actually present in those places. And he said that the planet most worthy to rule is the one with the most dignities in the Ascendant, in the places of the Luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, in the Part of Fortune, or in the degree of the Conjunction or Prevention <note>the New or Full Moon</note> that occurred before the birth. And he said that if there is any planet that has dignity in three or four places, or at least in two, we shall establish it as the Almuten <note>original: "almutez," the winner of the most planetary dignities in a chart</note> over the birth.

### On the Knowledge of the Years of the Native.

**A**fter this, you shall look to the place of the Almuten itself to know the years of the native. If it is oriental and in an angle, and with this it is in its *Hayz* <note>original: "ayz," a condition of planetary strength based on gender and position relative to the horizon</note>—as a

<column-break/>

masculine planet in a masculine sign and above the earth, or a feminine planet in a feminine sign and below the earth—and it is in its other aforementioned dignities (house, exaltation, triplicity, term, and face), and it is in the Ascendant or the tenth house and in its *Hayz*, it shall then give its "Greater Years." <note>Each planet was assigned sets of Greater, Middle, and Minor years in antiquity; for example, Saturn's Greater Years are 57.</note> Aboali <note>likely Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century astrologer</note> said that if the Sun is the Hyleg and is in Aries or Leo, and none of the lords of its five dignities aspect it, the Sun itself shall be both Hyleg and Alcocoden. The same shall be true of the Moon when it is in Taurus or Cancer under the same conditions. Ptolemy said that if it is oriental and in a succedent house, especially the eleventh, and in any of its aforementioned dignities and free from impediments, it shall then give its "Middle Years." But if it is in cadent houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, considered the weakest</note>, even if it is otherwise free from impediments, it shall give its "Minor Years." If it is cadent and otherwise impeded—namely, retrograde, or in opposition to any of its own houses or its exaltation, or if it is a pilgrim or "besieged" by the two Malefics <note>Mars and Saturn</note>—it shall give months in place of those years, or perhaps weeks in place of months. And if it is combust along with any of the aforementioned impediments, it shall signify and give hours in place of those years, or at most it shall signify days. Alboali treated all the angles as equal in giving the Greater Years, all the succedents in giving the Middle Years, and the cadents in giving the Minor Years.

### How Planets Increase Years.

**A**fter you have recognized the Alcocoden, who is called the giver of years, see whether it is aspected by any of the planets or is bodily joined to one. You shall also see whether the one it is joined to or which aspects it is a Benefic <note>original: "fortuna," the "fortunes" Jupiter and Venus</note>, and by what aspect it views it. For if a Benefic aspects it by a trine or sextile aspect, and that Benefic is fortunate and strong, it shall add to the native's life its own "Minor Years" and as many months as there are in its "Middle Years." If, however, the Benefic does not "receive" <note>Reception is a technical term for when one planet is in a sign where another has dignity</note> the Alcocoden under the aforementioned conditions, it shall add its Minor Years and, furthermore, as many days as there are in its Greater Years. Say the same if it receives it by a square aspect or opposition. If, however, that Benefic is impeded, it shall add months according to the number of its Minor Years.

### How Planets Decrease Years.

**I**f the one who aspects the Alcocoden is a Malefic <note>original: "malus," the "infortunes" Saturn and Mars</note>, and it aspects it by a square aspect or by opposition or by bodily conjunction, it then diminishes the years according to the number of its Minor Years. If the Malefic is fortunate and strong, it diminishes only three parts <note>i.e., three-quarters</note> of its Minor Years. Mars is of greater harm than the other Malefics. Mercury is indeed "convertible"; for if it is with those who increase, it increases the years of the native according to the number of its Minor Years, but if it is with those who diminish, it diminishes by just as many.

### On the Head and Tail of the Dragon.

**R**egarding the Head of the Dragon <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, Al-Kindi <note>original: "alchindi," a 9th-century polymath</note> said that when it is with the Alcocoden within 12 degrees before or after, it diminishes the years by a fourth part; however, I have not proven this as far as I remember. The same is said of the Tail <note>the South Node</note>. It harms more when it is with the Moon than with any other significator. The years of the native are also clear in other ways, and from the virtue of the birth they properly give to the children of their descendants who shall live, just as the years vary through revolutions after birth; and you will find a saying about this below in the chapter on the father.

# On the direction of degrees to the planets to know the accidents of the native.

Once you have found the number of years of the native's life—which are signified by the *Alcocoden* <term>Alcocoden: The "Giver of Years," a planet that determines the length of life based on its strength at birth</term>—and you wish to know about the accidents <note>In astrology, "accidents" refers to specific events or life circumstances rather than chance mishaps.</note> of the native and their age, direct their *Hyleg* <term>Hyleg: The "Giver of Life," a point or planet in the birth chart used to determine vitality</term> to the rays of the malefic planets <note>The malefic planets are traditionally Saturn and Mars.</note>. Look for the square aspect, the opposition, and their physical conjunction in one sign; look also to their trine or sextile aspects. You shall give to each degree of distance between them—until the completion of their meeting—one year for every degree. To every 25 "thirds," give one month; to every minute, six days; to every ten seconds, one day; and to every 25 "thirds," one hour <note>These are subdivisions of a degree used for precise timing of future events.</note>. Observe when the *Hyleg* reaches the rays of the malefics, or the degrees where the malefics were at the hour of birth, or their rays. For if the significator, the *Hyleg*, or the *Alcocoden* was poorly placed at that time, the native’s misfortunes will be heavy and terrible things will occur.

For if the *Hyleg* reaches any malefic or any of the aforesaid places, it is to be feared—unless one of the benefic planets <note>The benefics are traditionally Jupiter and Venus.</note> casts its rays to that same spot. If that year is the final year of the native’s life given to them by the *Alcocoden*, the native will die in that year, in that month, on that day, and in that hour, by the kind of death signified by the "Giver of Years" at their birth; provided they live until that time—that is, if they are not overtaken by an accidental death, as often happens. This is even more certain and infallible if that malefic planet hinders the lord of the ascendant of the birth, the lord of the ascendant of the "revolution" <note>A "solar revolution" or solar return is a chart cast for the person's birthday each year.</note> of that year, and the lord of the "perfection" <note>An ancient timing technique that advances the ascendant by one sign per year.</note>, or if he and another malefic hinder all the aforesaid significators. There shall be only one remedy: if that malefic is at a greater or lesser latitude than the *Hyleg* so that they do not meet each other on a straight diameter <note>original: "recto dyametro," meaning a direct, degree-for-degree alignment in the sky's vertical and horizontal planes</note>, such that the deviation of one from the other is more than one degree; for then it would be a miraculous salvation. But if their deviation is as I have said, they shall not die except perhaps by the fault of those in error or by the force of nature; nevertheless, they shall be cast into a danger similar to death. You shall also employ the fixed stars that are of the nature of that hindering malefic in their latitudes, just as you employ the hindering malefic itself. And do not make your "direction" unless you have observed the latitudes of the planets and fixed stars as I have said.

In other years, when the *Hyleg* reaches the aforesaid places without the protection of the rays of any benefic, the native’s state will be burdened and all sorts of horrible but not necessarily perilous things will happen to them. But if a benefic casts its rays to that place, it will not be hindered, for the burden is removed. Whenever the *Hyleg* reaches the benefics, or the places where the benefics were, or the places where their rays were at the hour of someone’s birth without any malefic casting rays there, prosperous and even pleasing things will happen to them. If, however, a malefic casts its rays toward it, it will decrease that goodness, though not by much—increasing or decreasing according to how the malefic itself is disposed. Similarly, whenever the *Hyleg* reaches the malefics or their birth-positions without the rays of a benefic, sorrows and horrors will happen and their state will be worsened. But if a benefic casts its rays to those places, it will decrease the malice of that malefic according to how the benefic is disposed. For if the *Hyleg* reaches a hindering malefic from the hour of birth, or any of its aspects, and that malefic does not receive it with "perfect reception," and the malefic itself is hindered, it signifies the death of the native in that year, as is said elsewhere.

## Chapter Three: That all planets are givers of years, but they are not all simply preservers of them; rather, they are sometimes killers—some naturally, some by accident—similarly the Head and Tail.

<column-break/>

All planets are givers of years according to a triple and diverse order—including the Head and Tail of the Dragon <note>The Lunar Nodes: the points where the moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic.</note>—but they are not all simply guardians or preservers of them. Indeed, some of them are naturally "killers," namely Saturn, Mars, and the Head and Tail of the Dragon. And there are also certain other killers because of the aforesaid, not naturally but rather by accident; there are 13 such, so that there are 17 killers in total: the four natural ones mentioned, and these 13—some by accident, some by timing, and some by the names of the places.

For the Sun kills by physical conjunction, by the square aspect, and by opposition. The Moon similarly kills by physical conjunction with the Sun—whether she is the *Hyleg* or not—unless she is in the "furnace of the sun" <note>original: "camini solis," likely referring to being 'under the beams' or 'combust,' very close to the sun's position</note>, and when she is in its square aspect or in its opposition. The Moon also kills when she reaches the degree of the birth ascendant without a benefic aspect, if she was the *Hyleg* at birth and that degree is the ascendant of some solar revolution; then the native shall perish because it would be an enemy to the ascendant due to the diversity of their natures. For the Ascendant is friendly to the Sun and is of a hot and dry nature, while the Moon is an enemy to the Ascendant and friendly to its *nadir* <note>nadir: the point directly opposite, in this case the 7th house or western horizon</note>, that is, the seventh house; she is of a cold and nocturnal nature, and they are enemies to one another and distant.

The Head and Tail of the Dragon kill because of their constriction at the intersection of the circles when the *Hyleg* joins either of them in the birth or revolution, unless the benefics then aspect the degree of the *Hyleg*. And you should understand the same regarding the degree that was in the twelfth house at the hour of birth, or the sixth, or the eighth <note>The 6th, 8th, and 12th houses were traditionally considered "unfortunate" houses associated with illness, death, and hidden enemies.</note>. Similarly, the "Heart of the Bull" <note>Aldebaran</note> and the "Heart of the Scorpion" <note>Antares</note> act this way because of the excessive abundance of heat united in them. Mercury, however, when he is physically joined to any of the malefics, or in its square aspect, or in its opposition without perfect reception or without the aspect of any benefic, will kill if he is in the degree that was the ascendant at the hour of birth, or if he is joined to the *Hyleg* itself, or in its square or opposition; but with the benefics, he will not.

The *Hyleg* also kills if it is joined with the degree of the *nadir* of the birth ascendant. You can say the same of the Moon if she is joined with that degree; and what is more, if the planet whose degree you have directed to the *Hyleg* at the hour of birth was poorly disposed, it kills. Certain other degrees that you have directed to the *Hyleg* also kill.

Whence Aomar and Cuz said: when the direction is completed at the end of a sign with half the years of the minor, middle, or malefic *Alcocodens*, it kills. And he said: know that when the disposition changes from the *Hyleg* from the "term" of a malefic into the "term" of another malefic, at the very entry of that malefic, it kills. And he said: know that it seemed to Ptolemy <note>Ptholomeo: Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer/astrologer whose work 'Tetrabiblos' was the foundation of this science.</note> that the Moon should always be directed to the rays of the malefics and benefics to know the state of the body in health or sickness and the state of the mother. And the "Part of Fortune" <note>A calculated point in the chart representing prosperity.</note> to know the acquisitions of the native, namely their riches or poverty. And the Sun to know the state of the father or the kingdom. The Midheaven <term>Midheaven: The highest point in the chart, signifying career, reputation, and public life</term> to know the state of the kingdom and its mastery. And he said that it seemed to him that the direction of the degree of the Midheaven should be through the ascensions of the "right circle."

Again, he and all others saw that the degree of the ascendant should be directed—according to the divisions of the "terms" to the rays of the benefics and malefics—to know his state. If a benefic is seen and disposed there, it will signify in that division or disposition the health and safety of the body and its well-being, whatever his condition may be; and he will be of a greater and better state, and of a better complexion than his ancestors were. This will happen especially in kings, the wealthy, and the great, more than in the small, the poor, the low, or the middle-class. And it is all the better and...

### Chapter Four: On the science of directing the rays of the planets to the Hyleg.

When you wish to direct the degree of any planet to the Hyleg <term>Hyleg: The planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life" and determines vitality</term> so that you may know the life of the native and his state throughout the whole time of his life, along with his disposition and his accidents: see whether the Sun is the Hyleg, or the Moon, or which other of the planets or degrees. You must look at the disposition of the rays of the planets and their projection toward the Hyleg, and look at the place of the planet or the degree which is the Hyleg, and see in what place or in what degree it is by equal degrees and their minutes. When you have done this, see which of the planets projects its rays to it through whatever aspect it may be, whether by opposition, by equal degrees and their minutes, and reduce them into equal degrees by the ascensions of the region <note>Astrologers calculated timing based on how long it takes zodiac signs to rise over the horizon at a specific latitude</note>—and these are called the rays of that planet. Then we must look at what degree of that sign the planet itself is in, and reduce them to the degrees of the ascensions of that sign—these are called the degrees of the body of that planet. You will also find the Ascendant and the other houses through the degrees of the ascensions of that region. Many of the ancients worked in this manner, and especially those who followed the footsteps of Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrologer whose work influenced Persian and Arabic traditions</note>, who was one of the few experts who studied this work. Nor was this different from the opinion of Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the famous 2nd-century astronomer and astrologer</note>, although perhaps he may seem to see something diverse from it; but this was a easier method, and for this reason many of the ancients followed those footsteps. An example of this matter is as follows: let it be posited that the Hyleg is in the 17th degree of Leo, and the planet whose direction you intend to make is in the 28th degree of Pisces. The 17th degree of Leo, in which the Hyleg sits, is to be directed to the 28th of Virgo toward the rays of the aforesaid planet, whether it be a fortune or a malefic—provided that the fortune is then the "killer" <note>In certain calculations, even a "good" planet could signify the end of life if it reached a specific terminal point</note>, which happens sometimes. Then you will subtract the ascensions which are in the direct degree of the Hyleg from the ascensions which are in the direct 28th degree of Virgo, where the opposition of the killing planet is; and the degrees that remain will be the years of the native's life, which are 41. Similarly, you will see if any of the planets that add years add anything, or if any of those that subtract years diminish anything from those years, and in this way you will judge the number of years of the native's life, of which I shall tell you below when I treat the direction of the planets according to their terms. Alomar <note>original: "Alomar" - likely refers to Omar of Tiberias, an 8th-century Persian astrologer</note> indeed said that Ptolemy used another method, but nevertheless it was not contrary to this one, even if it seemed diverse from it; perhaps it seemed more difficult to some. For I say that the intention of Ptolemy was according to the disposition of the lords of the

<column-break/>

terms and according to the division of their disposition in them. For he said that all the rays are gathered together at the cusp <note>The starting point of an astrological "house" or division of the sky</note> of the earth and become one thing: and that it is necessary for us to know the diversity of the rays according to the position of the place, beginning to calculate the rays by the longitude of the planets from the angles through the ascensions of the city in which we are, and through the ascensions of the direct circle. And when you have done this and ordered the places of the planets, you shall direct the Hyleg through the ascending degree according to these longitudes as has been said. And when you see the direction arrive at the malefics, judge the contrary according to what you see their state to be—their strengths or weaknesses, and their good or bad fortune—and this is if the Hyleg is from the tenth house unto the seventh, according to the succession of the signs. If, however, it is between the seventh and the tenth, that direction is made backwards, that is, against the succession of the signs, by subtracting the ascensions of the degree of the Hyleg from the ascensions of the degree of the malefic, if it is in the aforesaid places toward which you are directing; although some seem to want otherwise. And you should understand the same concerning the Dragon's Head <term>Dragon's Head: The North Node of the Moon, traditionally viewed as an increasing or beneficial point</term>: that is, if you direct the Hyleg to the Head, whatever the Hyleg may be—whether the degree of the Ascendant or the degree of the Moon or another—you shall direct backwards, that is, against the succession of the signs, by subtracting the ascensions of the degree of the Head from the ascensions of the degree of the Hyleg. But toward the Tail <term>Dragon's Tail: The South Node of the Moon, traditionally viewed as a decreasing or malefic point</term> you shall direct according to the succession of the signs as I told you above: and according to the number of degrees of distance, you shall give the years. And when the Hyleg arrives at the western degree or at the degree of a malefic which was between the tenth and the seventh to which you directed the degree of the Hyleg, then the native shall die, unless a strong fortune then beholds that degree from a trine or sextile aspect and with reception <note>A condition where planets "accept" each other's influence, softening bad effects</note>: because then it will not kill, but the native will be endangered by a peril similar to death; and if he does not then recover himself by the proper regimen, he will die, even if the error be slight.

### Chapter Five: On the number of malefics and fortunes.

The ancient wise men said there were four malefics; to me, however, it seems that they could be called seven: because if they divided them into four, they do not seem to have excluded the others. Whence I say that there can be seven: two naturally, such as Saturn and Mars; two accidentally, such as the Sun and Mercury; one by misfortune, such as the Moon; and two locally, such as the Dragon's Head and its Tail. The Sun is malefic when it is joined with Mars bodily, or in its opposition, or in its square aspect without perfect reception. And Mercury when it is combust <note>So close to the sun that its power is "burnt up"</note> or in their aforesaid aspects, with or without reception. And the Moon when it is unfortunate, as was said in the chapter on the impediments of the Moon. And Tiberiadis <note>Omar of Tiberias</note> said that when these are gathered over Venus without the aspect of a fortune, then the native will be a *spadus* <note>original: "spadus" - a person who is impotent, a eunuch, or sexually impaired</note>. If the first lord of the triplicity of Venus is strong, it provides for him against this; but if not, he will be, in addition to this, a sufferer, laborious and in need of food for his belly all the days of his life. The Dragon's Head is malefic when it is with the malefics; and similarly the Tail when it is with the good planets. There are eight fortunes: namely four naturally, like Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, and the Moon; two accidentally, like Mercury when it is joined to them or any one of them bodily, or in their trine or sextile aspect, with or without reception, or in a square aspect or opposition with perfect reception—and if no one of the infortunes <note>malefics</note> hinders it without reception. And Mars and Saturn when both are made united by body—which is when they are both in the same minute in the house or in the exaltation of either of them, or in two of their minor dignities—or also if there are five [degrees] between them...

And because of this, it is said that two infortunes joined together make one fortune: two also locally, like the Head <note>original: "caput" – the North Node of the Moon, traditionally considered increasing or "benefic"</note> with the fortunes increasing [good], and the Tail <note>original: "cauda" – the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered decreasing or "malefic"</note> with the evils decreasing [it]. # Chapter six: On the knowledge of the life of the native and its masters of the terms.

To know the lifespan of the native and the disposition of its master through the divisions of the terms <term>terms: specific sections of each zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet, used to fine-tune predictions</term> of the planets, you must first consider the projections of the rays <note>astrological "aspects" or angles cast by planets toward one another</note> of the planets; then you shall direct further and to that very degree, just as was said above, which I now summarize for you. For when you wish to direct further to any planet or its rays, you shall consider how many degrees of distance there are between them according to the ascensions of the region of that birth through the oblique circle <note>the ecliptic or the local horizon's relationship to the zodiac</note>, and you shall give one year to each degree, one month to every 5 minutes, and 6 days to every minute in this manner. For you shall begin from the first minute of Aries both in the further direction and in the degree of the planet or its ray to which you are directing, and you shall subtract the smaller from the larger, and that which remains will be the distance or length between them; you shall then give a year to each degree and so on for the others as I have told you now. And Aomar <note>original: "aomar" – likely referring to Umar al-Tabari, an 8th-century Persian astrologer influential in the medieval West</note> said that you should always direct the degree of the Ascendant in nativities so that you can know the lifespan of the native, since it is the divisor which is called the *algebutar* <term>algebutar: the "divisor," a planet that rules a specific span of years in a person’s life based on the movement of the Ascendant</term>. Although I have received this work briefly from the ancients, I hand over such instruction to you: namely, that you see the ascending degree and its minute, in whose term it might be, and how many degrees of that term remain to ascend through the oblique circle; for that planet which is the master of that term will dispose the life of the native from the day and hour of his birth up to as many years and as many days and as many hours as there are degrees, minutes, and seconds. Then you shall subtract the ascensions of the last degree of that term from the ascensions of the last degree of the following term and its minutes, and you shall give one year to each degree of what remains, one month to every 5 minutes, and six days to every minute; and the master of that term will dispose the life of the native according to what its condition may be, and also the disposition for as many years, months, and days. Then you shall subtract the ascensions of the last degree of the second term from the ascensions of the last degree of the third term, and you shall give one year to each degree of the residue that remains, etc., as was said above. For the master of that term will dispose the life of the native for so many years, months, and days; and you shall do this from term to term until the end of the sign, for as long as the native's life lasts; and you shall always consider the state of that planet whose term it is, since according to whether its state is good, evil, or mediocre, so will it dispose the life of the native, provided nothing else interferes. But if that work of direction reaches the end of Pisces, you shall begin from the start of Aries and do as I have said.

### When the division is with any fortune.

<column-break/>

When, however, you find that division to which you are directing with any of the fortunes or in its rays without the aspect or presence of any infortune, and the *algebutar* or divisor is a fortune, the native will be in those years in a good and praiseworthy state, and in tranquility and goodness of his life; and likewise in the increase of his affairs: and this shall last until the degree of direction reaches an infortune or its degree. But if an evil one casts its aspect, it will diminish that goodness according to how great its malice is, unless those degrees are its own dignity. If indeed it has dignity there, it will impede less.

### When the division is with any infortune.

And if this should be with any of the infortunes and with the aspect of a fortune, and the divisor of those years is an infortune, the native will be in those years in an evil and detestable state: and he will be in distress, griefs, tribulations, and sorrows; and evils will find him, along with a decrease and poverty of goods. But if a fortune casts its aspect, it will diminish that malice according to how great its goodness is. And if that degree is its own dignity, it will be more beneficial.

### If several planets are present.

If, however, several planets have dignity there and cast their aspect upon that place, the one who has more dignities or strengths there will be more worthy in the disposition itself. If, however, one has one dignity and casts its aspect, and another has more but does not cast its aspect, each will be a participant and worthy of the disposition; and each of them will dispose the life of the native according to a good or evil outcome as was said above.

# Part Three: On the form and figure of the native’s body: and hence also regarding the accidents themselves, generally and particularly, and regarding the qualities of the soul and those things adjacent to them.

<margin>
<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'D' depicting a scholar or astrologer in a hooded gown, sitting at a desk with an open book, pointing towards celestial or scientific instruments. The initial is framed in a circle with floral motifs.</image-desc>
It has been **stated** above in those things which preceded this part regarding all the masters or differences of nativities and those things adjacent to them, and how many years or what span of life is attributed to each of the born; it follows in this third part to make mention of the accidents and the form and figure of the body of the native, both particularly and generally, and regarding the qualities or accidents of the soul.
</margin>

# Chapter one: Regarding the form and figure of the native.

You shall therefore consider, when you wish to know this in the birth of anyone, the Ascendant and its master, and you shall see which planet is the *almutez* <term>almutez: also called the Almuten, the planet with the most combined dignity or "power" in a specific location of the zodiac</term> in it, according to the form and figure which it attributes; and according to the figure which the ascending sign of the native attributes, it will provide the general form to come, since the action of nature is according to the necessity of the form. Nevertheless, by judging proportionately from the meaning of the planet to the sign and the sign to the planet: adding also something from the essence of its ancestors, since from similar causes, similar effects are produced. And this can endure up to the seventh generation of their descendants: and each descendant can give something of its own essence to its descendants up to its seventh generation, yet according to more or less in one or another of their individuals, since one person proceeds from another person, for it is a rational individual.

the rational substance of our nature. This same quality can exist within the human species; nor would it seem to those observing that individuals of a species would derive their likeness or temperament and complexion from their hands rather than from their other sensory parts, since they are nourished by the humors of the mother in the womb, and the limbs are organized from the paternal seed. It is, therefore, necessary that the outcome follows the necessity of the matter. And because the variety of all the forms or figures of the world, including those of the human species, cannot be fully defined or described—except perhaps in a very long discourse that would breed boredom in the reader—it is necessary that you consider, with your own industry and discretion, the mixture of meanings of both the planets and the signs, as well as the appropriate places in the circle <note>The zodiacal circle</note> for attributing a form and figure to the newborn. Everything that is established is established to do what is given to it by its creator. You will not find anyone who is so simply "Saturnine" or "Jovian" or "Mercurial" or "Solar" or "Venerian" or "Martial" or "Lunar" that they are devoid of the influence of all other planets, such that no other has a part in them. Even the sign interposes something of its own parts, as well as its location in the circle of signs and—as I touched upon above—the science of parentage. As Ovid says: "A son is often like his father" <note>original: "Saepe solet similis filius esse patri"</note>. Therefore, one must consider the <term>Almuten</term> <note>The planet that holds the most astrological strength or "dignity" over a specific degree of the zodiac</note> at the hour of birth of the one whose accidents <note>External traits or occurrences</note> you wish to know, taking the degree of the ascendant at birth. From the planet that is then the ruler, one takes the meaning of the form and figure of the newborn's body. It seems appropriate to me to speak first of the form of the body due to its physical density, rather than mentioning the qualities of the soul, because of the daily occurrences that appear in its physical composition, which naturally precede the qualities of the soul. The qualities of the soul do not appear as clearly as the qualities of the body, but those qualities are perceived which are acquired little by little and step by step from the stars after its creation and birth—the stars which formed the complexion of the body that we see appearing.

### Chapter Two: On those things which are outside the body, which are not of its substance nor of the substance of the soul.

Other things exist outside the body, such as becoming wealthy, marrying, or fathering children; these usually happen a long time after the aforementioned traits. All these things can and should be known naturally from the hour of birth and the Ascendant, but they are often diverted from their nature by accident or by some custom. Hence, in order to know these things, we must rightly consider both the stars that are in the Ascendant or look upon it, and similarly the state of the Moon, as will be said below concerning each one particularly in its proper place. For the operations of nature are diversified in many ways: they are diversified by the planets and stars according to customs, by nutrition, by the locations of regions, by social interactions, and similar things; it would be useful to know all of these if possible. We can also know each knowable thing better when we know its cause. For the act of knowing lies in the knowledge of the thing known or knowable. Every mixed body is owed a place according to the person and the disposition of the worker, since the perfection of a thing is taken from its totality; for the operation is nobler than the action that follows the agent. Hence, through the actions of the supercelestial bodies, their nobler effects or operations are produced. For the stars regulate all inferior, corruptible things—namely, each individual nature. While the operations of the stars are the same according to reason, they are diverse according to their effects, because the forms and figures of those born are understood from the nature of the figures of the Ascendant, from the planets, from their conjunction with others, and from the signs and fixed stars existing in those places.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 3: On the form and figure of the newborn's body, and first on that which Saturn attributes.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration divided into three sections. On the left, a goat-fish hybrid (the zodiac sign Capricorn). On the right, a man pouring water from a jar (the zodiac sign Aquarius). In the center, a personification of the planet Saturn as an elder seated on a throne holding a scythe, accompanied by a six-pointed star and the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄).</image-desc>

When Saturn is the sole significator of the birth, without the help or mixture of another, and is <term>Oriental</term> <note>Rising in the east before the Sun</note> in the world and away from the Sun, Ptolemy said the native will be of temperate size and moderate thickness, of a honey color <note>original: "melini coloris"</note>; his hair will be black, but it will be thick on his chest; his hair curly; and coldness and moisture will prevail in his complexion. But if he is <term>Occidental</term> <note>Setting in the west after the Sun</note> in the world and away from the Sun, he will be thin, blackish, of a small body, having flat and thin hair, with a fit joining of his limbs; his eyes will be black, and dryness will prevail in his complexion. And Dorotheus told me that he signifies a very hairy man with eyebrows joined together. And Adila <note>Likely referring to the 9th-century astrologer Al-Andarzaghar</note> said Saturn gives a man who is dark, with few hairs in his beard; he will have a bluish-grey color; a thin chest sometimes; rough and unkempt hair; and <term>rhagades</term> <note>Cracks or fissures in the skin</note> or fissures in his heels.

### On the participation of Jupiter with Saturn.

If Jupiter participates with Saturn, it signifies a man having a face that is not truly white, whose color will be brownish or olive, yet with a praiseworthy comeliness. His eyes will be blackish and of moderate size, yet expressive; his stature will be more than average; he will be somewhat pot-bellied; some of his teeth will not be truly white; his hair semi-curly and of a chestnut color; his body hair not entirely black; and it will be between thin and thick. This is the case if both of them are Oriental. But if one is Oriental and the other Occidental, he will be something in between this. If indeed both are Occidental, he will be much less than this.

### On the participation of Mars with Saturn.

If instead Mars participates with Saturn, it signifies a man who is not quite straight, somewhat thick, whose color will be blackish, participating in a certain unsightly redness; he will sometimes have some unsightly blemishes <note>original: "palestras" - likely referring to skin marks or lesions in this context</note> on his face; his body hair somewhat thin; his head hair not very black, but rather participating in a certain dark redness.

### On the participation of the Sun with Saturn.

But if the Sun participates with Saturn, it signifies a man having a moderate stature, leaning more toward the tall side than the short side; his color will be as if envious <note>original: "emulus" - possibly meaning sallow or competing colors</note>, so that it will seem at times to share in every other color, but rather with blackish; he will be of a more decent stature than with any of the other planets; he will be semi-fleshy, having large eyes; a semi-full beard, chestnut or honey-colored hair between semi-curly and straight. And the Sun adds something to the fatness of the body of the native and to his beauty and form more than the other planets. Furthermore, when the Sun is Oriental in the world, and the other planets, when they are Oriental in the world or away from the Sun and participating with Saturn, they add something to the magnitude of the native's body. And if it is in its first station, it helps the bodies...

...of the newborns, making them stronger and more vigorous than at other times. If, however, they have passed their first station <note>The point where a planet appears to stop before turning retrograde</note>, they will diminish the aforementioned qualities, and the body will become smaller or weaker the further they move from that station and the closer they approach the second station. And when they fall into <term>combustion</term> <note>Being so close to the Sun that the planet’s influence is "burnt up" or hidden</note>, it detracts from the beauty and form of the newborn’s body, making it heavy, hindered, and miserable.

The locations and degrees where the "significators" <note>Planets that indicate specific traits</note>—the governors of the birth and the Moon—are placed also contribute to the form and figure of any newborn's body and their <term>complexion</term> <note>The balance of bodily humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, according to the nature of the signs in which those places or degrees are found. Furthermore, if the significator of the newborn has no latitude at the hour of birth—meaning it is exactly at the degree of its <term>Zenith-Node</term> <note>original: "çençahar", a Latinization of an Arabic astronomical term referring to the nodes or the peak of a planet's orbit</note> or its opposite—it signifies that the newborn will be lean. If the latitude is great, the person will be fat. If it is between great and small, they will be fleshy, light of step, and carrying their weight easily. If the latitude is between the greatest and the middle point, they will increase in fleshiness toward fatness. If it is between the middle and the minimum latitude, they will decrease in fleshiness as they move toward the Zenith-Node until they reach thinness.

These effects occur especially if the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is at the end of a sign and the ruler of the tenth house is in the west. If the Lord of the Ascendant and other significators are at their "near distance," it leads to fatness; at their "far distance," it leads to thinness. If the latitude is southern—that is, if the significator is within the 179 degrees from its Zenith-Node toward the south—the newborn will be very light of step, as Haly <note>The Arab astrologer Haly Abenragel</note> testifies. This lightness depends on whether the latitude is greater or lesser, because that southern part is hot and dry, which causes everything residing there to be light. If, however, it is northern—from the "tail" to the Zenith-Node (that 179-degree distance)—the person will be ponderous and heavy in their gait and movement. This is because this part is of great coldness and moisture, which adds weight to all things residing there.

Know also that the first station and retrograde motion tend toward a "fighting" or robust build, while the second station and direct motion tend toward a thinning effect. Nor should it escape you that the lineage of one's ancestors contributes greatly to the fatness or thinness of the newborn—often more so than the stars—and similarly to their fleshiness.

### On the participation of Venus with Saturn.

If Venus participates with Saturn, it signifies that the newborn will have a body of this sort: their complexion will be somewhat blackish, honey-colored, or olive-toned, yet becomingly so. Their hair will be neither truly grey nor truly chestnut; the face will be somewhat round, the jaws of moderate size, and the eyes will be praised for their beauty by most who see them. Their darkness is greater than when Saturn is the sole significator. They will have a suitable amount of hair and will generally be moderately fleshy.

### On the participation of Mercury with Saturn.

If Mercury is a participant, it signifies the newborn will be of a darkish color, having a somewhat raised forehead, a longish face, and a similar nose. The eyes will be reasonably attractive, leaning toward black rather than any other color. The beard will be black and thin, the fingers moderately long, and the person will be of a suitable height.

### On the participation of the Moon with Saturn.

If the Moon is a participant with Saturn, it signifies that the newborn will tend to have a white color; however, this whiteness will not be clear or pure, but somewhat "cloudy" with a certain mixture of redness. They will have beautiful eyebrows, black eyes, a round face, and a beautiful, quite decent stature, with limbs well-joined together. You should understand this to be the case for each of the aforementioned planets if they are "well-disposed" <note>Placed in a favorable sign or position</note>. If they are "ill-disposed," all these traits will be much worse than what has been said, according to the extent of each one's impediment. This will signify that the newborn will be deformed, clumsy, foul-smelling, horrible and vile in appearance, and with an uncoordinated composition of limbs. The more Saturn or his partners are afflicted, the more the deformity and clumsiness of the body will increase.

The wise have also said that the Moon assists the form of the newborn when it is in a balanced temperament, and makes them leaner when Saturn is the sole significator—especially when she is separating by conjunction or aspect from someone and applying more closely to Saturn. This varies according to whether her body is illuminated or how far she has moved until she passes the protection of her rays over his.

### Chapter 4. Regarding how the quarters of the circle of signs work in the disposition of the body’s form and figure; and first, regarding the first quarter.

The four quarters of the circle of signs also work to shape the form and figure of any newborn. The first quarter—from the beginning of Aries to the end of Gemini—is called "Vernal" <note>Spring-like</note>. It contributes to the goodness and improvement of the body’s form. When the Moon and all other significators are in that quarter at the hour of birth, they will assist the form and figure, increasing the beauty of the body, the suitability of the stature, and the attractiveness of the eyes. It gives a suitable fleshiness. In this temperament, as Ptolemy <note>The famous Greco-Egyptian astronomer/astrologer</note> testifies, heat and moisture prevail. If only some significators are there, they will work according to their nature. Those in other quarters will work according to the nature of those quarters.

### On the second quarter, namely the Estival.

The second quarter—from the beginning of Cancer to the end of Virgo—is called "Estival" <note>Summer-like</note>. It also improves the form and figure. When the significators are here, they give a tempered quality to the body, a moderate and firm stature, suitable fleshiness, large (but not unattractive) eyes, and thick, curly hair. In this temperament, according to Ptolemy, heat and dryness prevail. Those significators present will act according to their nature.

### On the third quarter, namely the Autumnal.

The third quarter—from the beginning of Libra to the end of Sagittarius—is called "Autumnal." It also contributes to the goodness and improvement of the body's form. Thus, when the Moon and all other significators of someone’s birth are...
