### Concerning the last quarter, namely the winter quarter.

Indeed, that last quarter—which is from the beginning of Capricorn until the end of Pisces and is called winter—contributes to the goodness and improvement of the form and figure of any newborn's body. Wherefore, when the Moon and all other significators at the hour of someone’s birth are in this quarter, they will aid the form and figure of that newborn’s body, giving him a color verging toward blackness: a becoming and temperate quality and quantity of body: flat and thin hair, and a fitting symmetry of his limbs: in whose complexion coldness and moisture will dominate. If some of them remain in it, they will work the aforementioned effects according to their own nature. Those found in other quarters will work according to the nature of those quarters.

### Chapter 5: Concerning other aids to the forms and figures of the bodies of newborns, besides the aids of the quarters.

Again, Ptolemy says that there are certain other aids that particularly help the aforementioned traits according to the places and positions in which they are found: and those are the signs that resemble human figures: such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, and Aquarius. For they contribute to the conformation of the bodies of newborns and also to the fitting joining of limbs. Wherefore, if the Moon and other significators at the hour of birth are in them, they will aid all these things and make the bodies of the newborns more suitable and fit for physical activity. Those signs, however, which do not resemble the human form—such as Aries, Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, the last part of Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Pisces—contribute to the goodness of the bodies of newborns: for they render the limbs assigned to those signs in which the Moon and significators are found stronger and more temperate, and more inclined and suitable for the actions assigned to them.

### Those things which specifically aid according to size.

Likewise, among the signs, there are those that specifically aid the form and figure of the body of any newborn and their limbs in making them large, such as Taurus, Leo, and Virgo: since their forms are large in the heavens: but Taurus and Leo likewise aid in making them stronger.

### Those things which aid according to smallness.

For certain signs contribute to the smallness of the body and limbs, such as Cancer, Capricorn, and Pisces: because their forms in the heavens are found to be smaller in the back part than in the front part. Furthermore, the first part of Aries, the first part of Taurus, and the first part of Leo aid the limbs of newborns in making them more prone and suitable for taking on fatness. However, the last half of any of these inclines the bodies of newborns to take on thinness. But the first half of Gemini, the first half of Scorpio, and the first half of Sagittarius make the bodies of newborns lean. Their last parts, however, adapt them to take on fatness. Also, Virgo, Libra, and Sagittarius undoubtedly prepare the bodies of newborns for a temperate and good complexion of the body, and a fitting joining of limbs. Taurus, Scorpio, and Pisces, however, hinder those things and relax them from a temperate state, although perhaps that relaxation is not extreme.

...for you would see that by your own diligence you should judge all the aforementioned things according to "more or less," according to the proximity of the signs to the aforementioned places or their distance from them, and according to whether they are strong or weak, fortunate or unfortunate, so that you may judge more truly, certainly, and securely concerning the accidents of any newborn according to the state of his birth: and skillfully perceive all things rightly and deliberately in your mind.

### Chapter Six: Concerning the form and figure of the newborn which Jupiter bestows.

Jupiter is depicted as a bearded, crowned figure sitting in a four-wheeled chariot. He holds a scepter in his right hand and an open book or tablet in his left. Above the chariot is the astrological symbol for Jupiter (♃). The chariot is drawn by two eagles. The wheels of the chariot are inscribed with zodiacal symbols, with Pisces visible on the upper right wheel and Sagittarius on the lower right wheel.

When Jupiter is the sole significator of the birth and he is oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note> in the world and influenced by the Sun or another planet, he signifies that the newborn will be of a white color: of a suitable and moderate stature and medium size: having white hair that is prominent and becoming: his eyes will be medium, neither very large nor very small: in whose complexion heat and moisture will prevail. If indeed he is occidental <note>setting after the Sun</note>, his whiteness will not be as fitting as when he is oriental: he will have straight hair: and he will be bald: medium eyes: medium stature: in whose complexion moisture will conquer.

### Concerning the participation of Mars with Jupiter.

But if Mars is a participant, there will be a small amount of redness mixed into his color: and he will have eyes slightly larger <note>original: "grossiores", thicker or larger</note> than when Jupiter is the sole significator. Now, if Mars is oriental, he will have a mark on his right foot. If, however, he is occidental, he will have it on the left; this rarely fails.

### Concerning the participation of the Sun with Jupiter.

And if the Sun is a participant with Jupiter, it signifies that something is taken away from his whiteness: he will, however, be more becoming than when Jupiter is the sole significator: and his stature will be something less than medium, yet suitable and becoming; his hair will have some curliness: and his eyes will have a yellowish tint <note>original: "crocetatis", saffron-colored</note>.

### Concerning the participation of Venus with Jupiter.

If, however, Venus is a participant with Jupiter, it signifies that the newborn will have a color inclining toward blackness: yet becoming rather than unpleasant: beautiful hair, almost honey-colored: yet they will not be of a fixed color: for their color will be changing: he will have a beautiful stature, a semi-round face: cheeks not large but becoming: beautiful eyes, except that their blackness will be somewhat greater than is due: yet it will not be unbecoming: with a becoming and beautiful face: and he will be partially hollow-faced <note>original: "semicauus", which could mean hollow-cheeked or partially bald</note>.

### Concerning the participation of Mercury with Jupiter.

For if Mercury is a participant with Jupiter, it signifies that the newborn will have a color slightly different from the first: a semi-raised forehead: a semi-long face: and a nose likewise: becoming eyes, not entirely black: a black and sparse beard: semi-long fingers: a semi-slender body: medium stature: thin lips.

### Concerning the partnership of the Moon with Jupiter.
If the Moon should be in partnership with Jupiter, it signifies a person who is not truly pale, but possesses a certain complexion that is not quite a healthy redness <note>original: "non vera rubedine"</note>; they have becoming eyebrows and eyes that are not truly black, with one eye occasionally being larger than the other or otherwise defective; a round face, and a moderate height.

### Concerning the partnership of Saturn with Jupiter.
And if Saturn is found to be a partner with Jupiter, it signifies that the person born will have a color that is somewhat more beautiful, being honey-toned <note>original: "mellinus," a warm, amber skin tone</note>; they tend to cast their eyes toward the ground while walking along the road; their feet are bowed <note>original: "recuruos"</note> and they knock them together as they go; their eyes are not large, their eyebrows are joined, and their skin is unpleasant and seemingly dry; they have thick lips, visible veins, a thin beard, and hair that is rough and unkempt.

### When Jupiter is impeded, what form he grants to the newborn.
And if Jupiter should be <term>impeded</term> <note>in astrology, "impeded" or "afflicted" means the planet is in a weak position or under the harsh influence of "malefic" planets like Saturn or Mars</note> at the time of birth—that is, if he is unfortunate, ill-situated, or poorly disposed—it signifies the opposite of those things which have been said. For if the planet that is in partnership with him is likewise impeded, there will be an even greater defect in the form and figure of the newborn's body, resulting in a deformity of evils. The greater the "impediment" or misfortune of the planet, the more the newborn's deformity will increase; many contrary traits will arise, just as was stated above in the chapter concerning Saturn.

### Chapter Seven: Regarding the form and figure of the newborn's body granted by Mars.

When Mars is the sole significator of the birth and is <term>oriental</term> <note>rising in the east before the sun</note> in the world—that is, when he is above the earth and rises in the morning before the Sun—it signifies that the person born will have a color that is not bright, but partaking in a whiteness that is not quite clear and a redness that is not true. And <term>Ptolemy</term> <note>the famous 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian astronomer and astrologer</note> said that such a person will be of a good size in their body, yet not overly fleshy; their eyes will be variegated or shifting in color; their hair thick and of medium length; and in their <term>complexion</term> <note>the balance of bodily fluids or "humors"</note>, heat and dryness will prevail.

### When Mars is occidental.
And if he should be <term>occidental</term> <note>setting in the west after the sun</note>, it signifies that the person will be of a red complexion, of moderate stature, and have small eyes; their hair will be flat and thin, yet with a certain yellowish tint; in their complexion, dryness dominates. And <term>Messahallah</term> <note>an influential 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer</note> said that this signifies a man of deformed features who has a red color, red hair, a round face, large eyes, a frightening appearance, and a mark or spot on the foot. <term>Dorotheus</term> <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> said the same regarding the appearance. "The Priest" <note>likely referring to a traditional Egyptian or Hermetic source</note> said that Mars gives a man a curved body, and makes him "semi-brown"—that is, neither truly red nor truly black, similar to those who stay too long in the sun or walk for a long time through the heat. Sometimes a "Martial" person has red spots or grains on the face, and most often carries thin hair in the beard, like a eunuch.

<column-break/>

### Concerning the partnership of the Sun with Mars.
If the Sun should be in partnership with Mars, it signifies a man having a color that is neither truly white, nor truly red, nor truly brown—it is as if he were covered in a color that is not quite red; he is half-stout and half-thick; his stature leans toward beauty and grace; his hair leans toward a blond or greyish-blue tone <note>original: "glaucedinē"</note> rather than any other color; and his eyes are not truly black.

### Concerning the partnership of Venus with Mars.
If Venus should be a partner with Mars, it signifies a man having a semi-red color with a certain becoming whiteness; a moderate and beautiful stature; plenty of becoming hair; a semi-round face; medium cheeks; and becoming eyes where the blackness is more pronounced than usual, yet not unbecomingly so. He is well-fleshed so that he might be called "semi-fat," and his face will be cheerful.

### Concerning the partnership of Mercury with Mars.
If Mercury should be a partner with Mars, it signifies a man having a semi-slender body, a moderate stature, and a color leaning more toward the color of Mars than any other (unless the conjunction of other planets interferes); a beautiful but thin and small beard; and similarly thin lips and a thin nose.

### Concerning the partnership of the Moon with Mars.
If the Moon should be in partnership with Mars, it signifies a man having a beautiful and white color with a certain mixture of semi-redness; semi-large eyes; beautiful eyebrows; an almost round face; and a becoming stature.

### Concerning the partnership of Saturn with Mars.
If Saturn should be a partner with Mars, it signifies a man who is semi-thick and not quite upright, having an unpleasant color that partakes in a certain redness mixed with blackness. He occasionally has some unsightly spots on his face; his hair is semi-thin, and its color is between black and a certain dark, stained red.

### Concerning the partnership of Jupiter with Mars.
If, however, Jupiter should be a partner, it signifies a man having a color that is somewhat reddish, with semi-large eyes, and having a mark on one of his feet. I say all these things if Mars and his partner are well-disposed and in a good state. If, however, they are in a bad state and poorly disposed, say the opposite, just as was said above in the chapters regarding the others.

# Left Column

Know that the appearance of the Sun and Moon will be like the appearance of the planets which are with them. And it is said that when the Sun is in the <term>nativity</term> <note>the astrological chart at the moment of birth</note> of someone in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, there will be a mark on the person’s face; they will have hair between saffron-yellow and sharing in a certain redness; the eyes will be somewhat saffron-colored. If, however, the Sun is <term>Occidental</term> <note>positioned in the western part of the chart, or setting after the sun</note> in the world, it signifies a person having a stature more than medium; a sallow color <note>original: "colorem emulum," often meaning a wan or sallow complexion</note>; and hair that is blond, straight, and sometimes a little bit curly.

### Concerning the partnership of Venus with the Sun.
But if Venus should be a partner with the Sun and she is <term>well-disposed</term> <note>positioned in a favorable zodiac sign or house</note>, it signifies a person having a medium and beautiful stature; a color mixed from whiteness and a semi-clear and becoming redness; much and suitable hair, and in the front part of the head they will seem to share in a certain baldness, yet they will not be truly bald; a face that is almost round and joyful; cheeks that are not large; beautiful eyes; and fleshy enough that they could be called almost plump.

### Concerning the partnership of Mercury with the Sun.
If indeed Mercury should be a partner with the Sun and he is well-disposed, it signifies a person having a honey-toned color <note>original: "colorem mellinum"</note>; their color will share in the color signified by the planet looking at him or which is joined in body with him; having a beautiful beard, yet not large nor too thick; and eyes that are moderately large and becoming.

### Concerning the partnership of the Moon with the Sun.
And if the Moon should be a partner with the Sun and she is of good condition, it signifies a person having a beautiful and becoming color with a certain semi-clear whiteness and with some mixture of redness; beautiful eyes; and beautiful eyebrows and a round face.

### Concerning the partnership of Saturn with the Sun.
But if Saturn should be a partner with the Sun through good condition, it signifies a person having a medium and suitably becoming stature; a honey-toned color; eyes that are moderately large; being semi-fleshy; with hair that is chestnut or honey-toned and somewhat curly.

### Concerning the partnership of Jupiter with the Sun.
If Jupiter should be a partner with the Sun, it signifies a person having a honey-toned color, or olive, or chestnut—which is almost the same—mixed with a certain whiteness and quite becoming; a quite suitable stature; eyes that are somewhat saffron-yellow; and hair tending somewhat toward curliness.

### Concerning the partnership of Mars with the Sun.
If, however, Mars should be a partner with the Sun, it signifies a person having a dark complexion <note>original: "nigredinem"</note> but tending toward redness, and not far from a sallow color; a stature near medium and becoming; hair of moderate thickness that is almost <term>glaucous</term> <note>original: "glaucos," a blue-gray or sea-green color</note>; and eyes of moderate size.

# Right Column

When Venus is the sole <term>significator</term> <note>the planet that rules the specific area of life being examined, in this case, physical appearance</note> of the birth, and she is <term>Oriental</term> <note>rising before the Sun</note> in the world and apart from the Sun, she signifies a person having a color that (as Ptolemy says) is beautiful and more becoming than the color which Jupiter attributes; their face will be soft and elegant, more closely resembling a woman’s face than a man’s; they will have a beautiful and becoming stature; and eyes that are darkish and likewise becoming. And Messahala <note>an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer</note> said that regarding the figures of men, she signifies a white person drawing toward a certain dark shadowing; and from this, they will seem more becoming, having a beautiful stature; beautiful eyes in which the darkness is found to be somewhat greater than in others, yet becoming; beautiful hair; a round face that is not large, and neither are the jaws. And Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> said that she signifies people having a beautiful face; beautiful eyes in which the darkness will be more than is necessary; many and beautiful hairs; a thick, white complexion finished with redness; in whose <term>complexion</term> <note>the physical and psychological temperament</note> a tempered moisture prevails. But if she should be Occidental, her significations will be less than the aforesaid; in their complexion, coldness will prevail.

### Concerning the partnership of Mercury with Venus.
But if Mercury should be a partner with Venus and he is well-disposed, it signifies a beautiful and becoming person; having a beautiful color; having a somewhat elevated forehead; a long face; and a nose that is similar and sometimes slender; beautiful eyes that are not entirely black; and long fingers. And "the Priest" <note>likely referring to Hermes Trismegistus or an Egyptian authority</note> said they have a large body; medium stature; a beautiful but rare beard, yet not small; sometimes having thin lips.

### Concerning the partnership of the Moon with Venus.
If the Moon should be a partner with Venus and she is well-disposed, it signifies a person having a beautiful color mixed with whiteness and redness; eyes that are moderately large; eyebrows that are beautiful and pleasing; and a beautiful and medium stature, yet a round face; sometimes having one of the eyes somewhat larger than the other or perhaps defective.

### Concerning the partnership of Saturn with Venus.
But if Saturn should be a partner with Venus, it signifies a person having a honey-toned or darkish color, yet with a suitableness and becomingness to that color; hair between glaucous <note>blue-gray</note> and honey-toned; and they will have hair in a competent and becoming quantity; a semi-round face; medium jaws; beautiful eyes whose darkness will be of a suitable size; and they will be semi-fleshy.

### Concerning the partnership of Jupiter with Venus.
And if Jupiter should be a partner with Venus, it signifies people having a darkish and becoming color; beautiful hair; for they will be of an emulous <note>sallow or pale</note> color; a beautiful stature and blessed with beauty. For beauty is the suitability of parts with a certain sweetness of color; a semi-round face; medium and becoming jaws; beautiful eyes; their darkness will seem to be somewhat greater than is necessary, yet this does not detract from their beauty; a large, beautiful face; and they will be semi-fleshy.

### Concerning the partnership of Mars with Venus.
If, however, Mars should be the ruler with Venus, it signifies a person having a suitable color mixed from a certain whiteness and redness; a beautiful and medium stature; many and becoming hairs; medium jaws; a semi-round face; beautiful eyes; their darkness will somewhat superabound, although it is not unbecoming; moderately thick; having a cheerful face.

# Chapter 10: Concerning the form and figure of the body of the newborn which Mercury attributes.

When Mercury is the sole <term>significator</term> <note>the planet that determines a specific life area, in this case, physical appearance</note> of the birth and is himself <term>Oriental</term> <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note> in the world or in relation to the Sun, and otherwise well-disposed, he signifies a person having a honey-toned, chestnut, or olive color; limbs that are sufficiently fit and well-joined; small eyes; and hair that is medium in both quantity and color. In his <term>complexion</term> <note>the balance of bodily fluids or "humors"</note>, heat will prevail. But if he is <term>Occidental</term> <note>setting in the west after the Sun</note> in the world or in relation to the Sun, he signifies a person having a saffron-yellow color mixed with a certain blackness; lean or thin; having a shrill voice; and hollow eyes whose pupils will be goat-like <note>original: "caprina," likely referring to a pale iris or a particular gaze</note> tending toward a certain redness, in whose complexion dryness will dominate.

### Concerning the partnership of the Moon with Mercury.
But if the Moon should be the principal ruler with Mercury and she is Oriental in the world and well-disposed in relation to the Sun and otherwise, it signifies a person having a beautiful color in which whiteness mixed with redness will prevail; beautiful and kind eyebrows; eyes that are not entirely black; a round and becoming face; and a suitable and beautiful stature. If, however, she is Occidental, her significations will be less than this, and even more so if the Moon is <term>impeded</term> <note>weakened by a difficult astrological position or aspect</note>.

### Concerning the partnership of Saturn with Mercury.
If indeed Saturn should be the principal ruler with Mercury and is Oriental, it signifies a person having a color that is almost blackish; a somewhat elevated forehead; a medium face and likewise a medium nose; semi-becoming eyes tending toward blackness; a thin and black beard; medium fingers; and a suitable stature. If, however, he is Occidental, his significations will be less than those mentioned above.

### Concerning the partnership of Jupiter with Mercury.
But if Jupiter should be the principal ruler with Mercury and is himself Oriental, it signifies a person having a color leaning toward a certain becoming blackness; enviable hair <note>original: "emulos," suggesting hair that rivals others in beauty or thickness</note>; a semi-round face; medium and suitable jaws; beautiful eyes in which blackness will prevail; a suitable and beautiful face; a becoming stature; and they will be semi-fleshy. But if he is Occidental, the aforementioned significations will be less than this.

### Concerning the partnership of Mars with Mercury.
And if Mars should be a partner and is himself Oriental, it signifies a person having a color determined more toward a certain "false" redness <note>original: "rubedine non vera," meaning a flush or hue that is not a solid red</note> mixed with a certain "false" whiteness than toward any other color; a thin and small beard, yet not unbecoming; thin lips and likewise a thin nose; a medium stature; and often a slender body.

### Concerning the partnership of the Sun with Mercury.
If indeed the Sun should be a partner with Mercury and is himself Oriental in the world, it signifies a person

### Concerning the partnership of Venus with Mercury.

### Concerning the shared influence of Mercury with the Moon.

When Mercury is the primary ruler alongside the Moon and is well-positioned, he signifies a person possessing a complexion mixed of white and red, resulting in a beautiful skin surface. They will have semi-dark eyes, a round face with pleasing proportions, and a stature that is both decent and filled with beauty. All these things that have been said concerning the forms and figures which the planets attribute to a person’s birth should be understood as common to both sexes. Understand also that such things ought to occur as described elsewhere if the planets are fortunate and well-disposed; if they are not, you must judge according to the degree of their affliction. Having considered all the individual points mentioned regarding the planets and other factors as I have touched upon above, and by connecting them with your own discretion while interspersing their parts with the help of our Redeemer, Jesus Christ. You should also know that there is something else which sometimes hinders the course of a birth: namely, that the conditions change in the births of sons over the years, just as they change in the revolutions of the years, as will be touched upon below when the "matter of fathers" is treated.

### Concerning the First House.

Chapter One: concerning the qualities or accidents <note>In medieval philosophy, an "accident" is a non-essential quality or characteristic of a person.</note> of the soul of the born person. Having mentioned in the preceding parts the form and figure of the body of the newborn and its physical accidents, I believe I should subsequently speak of the qualities or accidents of that person's soul and write about them as far as I am able. First, I will speak of the rational soul, as it is the more worthy and noble part, and subsequently of the sensitive and vegetative souls <note>Aristotelian psychology divided the soul into three levels: rational (human reason), sensitive (animal perception/movement), and vegetative (basic life/growth).</note>. It should be said, therefore, that what properly pertains to reason and intellect is grasped through Mercury; however, that which belongs to growth and sensation is grasped through the luminary which holds authority. If it is a daytime birth, this is through the Sun; if it is a nighttime birth, it is through the Moon and the planet with which she is joined. The nature of the soul truly depends on her connection or "application" to that planet. However, we cannot arrive at a knowledge of the soul by a single path alone, but by several. There are six methods, of which:
1. The first is the consideration of the state of the Moon and Mercury. 
2. The second is the consideration of the zodiac signs in which they are located.
3. The third is the consideration of the "lords" <note>The planet that rules a particular zodiac sign.</note> of those signs.
4. The fourth is the conjunction of the planets in the "figure" or chart at the hour of birth.
5. The fifth is the specific significance of each of the planets participating in the birth chart which the astrologer intends to consider.
6. The sixth is the consideration of the "angles" <note>The four most important points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note> and their lords, because the aforementioned significators, as well as the signs in which they reside, aid and favor the qualities of the soul and many of its accidents.

When the significators and the angles are in "fixed" signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, associated with stability.</note>, they cause these qualities to descend into the soul: they make it benevolent, upright, law-abiding, not deceitful, and not easily changed. Such a soul is stable, capable of sustaining many inconveniences, much labor, and much study; it is intelligent and ingenious, truthful and firm, fulfilling its own desires; it defends itself excellently against worldly malice and pleasures. It is a collector of things seen or heard and of words, both common and precious, leaving nothing or little of them behind but committing them to memory in

<column-break/>

useful matters. Such a soul is envious, especially in the sciences, for it does not wish to be surpassed by another in them. It is a lover of honor and of things from which praise is acquired (and in a good way); it is contentious in lawful matters, surpassing the wits of other souls, and is changed from one purpose to another only with great difficulty.

### Concerning the three superior planets.

When the three superior planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.</note> are "Oriental" from the Sun or from the lord of the Ascendant; or if they are in the Ascendant or in its angle; or in the *almuguea* <term>almuguea</term> <note>A complex medieval astrological relationship between planets based on their distance from the Sun or Moon.</note> of the Sun, the Moon, or the lord of the Ascendant: they make the soul liberal and fit for liberty, fierce and confident in its own counsel, generous and open, exalted, and bringing forth its thoughts openly, though not with great indiscretion.

### Concerning the significating stars.

And when the significating stars are in their first "station" <note>The point where a planet appears to stand still before moving retrograde.</note> and are fortunate and strong—especially if they are found near the cusp of the tenth house <note>The house of career and public standing.</note>—they announce that the soul of the born person will be thoughtful and a dispenser of good things. They will have a good memory, good capacity, and good intellect; they will be stable, quiet, and immovable; great, unchangeable, truthful <note>original: "fallacem" (deceitful). Context suggests a scribal error for "infallecem" (not deceitful), as it is paired with "legalem" (lawful).</note> and law-abiding; knowledgeable, a lover of work, and a true interpreter of dreams. In such things and similar ones, they will be very skilled.

### Concerning the three inferior planets.

When the three inferior planets <note>Usually refers to Venus, Mercury, and the Moon.</note> remain in the aforementioned places and are "Occidental," moving directly and strong—specifically in nighttime births, though in daytime births they do something similar—they make the soul of the born person prone to changing easily from one purpose to another. It may be small-minded and unfortunate, false, slow to know or understand, timid and fearful, a lover of a great storm of falsehood, and one who freely dwells in solitude. Ptolemy <note>An ancient Greek astronomer and astrologer whose works were foundational in the Middle Ages.</note> appears to say that when the three superiors are in opposition to the Sun (in the middle of their retrograde motion), they are hidden at the beginning of the day. If they are united with the Sun, they are hidden at the beginning of the night. This is true, and then they become as weak as they can be, making the soul vile and of little goodness. When they are Oriental or in their first station, they are strong and make a strong soul. When they are retrograde, they are weak and make the soul inert. When they are in their second station, they make it mediocre. When they are direct and Oriental, they are at their strongest, making the soul strong and fit for exercising its strengths.

### Concerning Venus and Mercury.

Concerning Venus and Mercury, it is said that when they are in their first station and the birth is during the day, or in their second station and the birth is at night, they are mediocre. They make a mediocre soul, neither good nor bad, yet inclined to be moved toward either good or evil. Albobali <note>A 9th-century Arab astrologer often cited in Latin translations.</note> appears to say that when they are in their first station and the birth is at night, or in the second station and the birth is by day, they are very strong and make a strong soul. When they are in the middle of their direct motion, they are weak and make a weak soul, agile and changing easily from purpose to purpose, small-minded, unfortunate, and one who loves smallness and dwelling in solitude.

### Concerning common signs.

When the <term>Ascendant<note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term> and the aforementioned significators are in <term>common signs<note>Also known as "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note></term>, because of their manifold nature and tendency toward change, they make the soul multiform. ### Concerning movable signs.

If indeed they are in <term>movable signs<note>Also known as "cardinal" signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn.</note></term>, they make a person who stays willingly in cities and associates with others because of the mobility of those signs. They make the soul love the affairs of universities and colleges, and similarly, the person will strive for praise. These signs make the soul a thinker on divine matters; the person will be of praiseworthy talent and fit to move toward the things they ought to. They will be an investigator of things, liberal toward almost everyone without distinction, of good reputation, and wise and perceptive in the judgments of the stars.

### Concerning the stars that dispose the soul of the native.

Again, the Moon and Mercury must be considered: whether they are in the aforementioned places or in their own proper <term>dignities<note>The specific signs or degrees where a planet is thought to have its greatest strength or influence.</note></term>; or if they are in the houses, exaltations, terms, or triplicities of those planets; or if they are in their <term>hayz<note>original: "ayz"; an Arabic astrological term for a planet being in a favorable position relative to the sun and the horizon.</note></term>. For then they make the soul of the native generous and open. Its qualities will be free, prosperous, and healthy, nor can this be thwarted unless something against nature breaks it. This is even more certain if one and the same significator rules all the places in which the Moon and Mercury are found, or if it is associated with them, or at least if one of them has an <term>application<note>original: "aluthisal," from the Arabic "al-ittisal," meaning the approaching aspect between two planets.</note></term> with the Moon. But if it should be otherwise than what has been said—that is, if the aforementioned stars are not the rulers of the places of both the Moon and Mercury, or any of them, nor are they associated with them, nor any of the other planets looking upon them to which one of those two more closely approaches—then the soul of the native will be disposed according to how Mercury or the Moon is disposed, or the planet associated with them. If the aforementioned planets are outside their dignities or otherwise poorly disposed, they will signify and make the soul of the native the opposite of what has been said: for its qualities will be harsh, hidden, and imperfect, without prosperity.

And <note>The text likely refers here to the Prophet Baruch or an astrological authority of that name.</note> Baruch says that the stars ruling the places where the Moon and Mercury are, or those elevated above them, will make the soul of the native perform rigid and "knotty" <note>original: "nodua"; likely meaning complex, difficult, or troublesome.</note> works. I say this if they are <term>infortunes<note>The "malefic" planets, traditionally Saturn and Mars.</note></term> or are unfortunate, making the native do wicked things. The soul of that native will be easily moved to hinder others and will be willfully harmful to them. Such a person will not be correctable by their own discretion; nor will it seem laborious to them to hurt others, but rather they will find delight in it. But if those hindering infortunes are in the places of stars that are in the <term>hayz<note>A favorable placement.</note></term> of the opposite, they will make the soul of the native weak and detestable, and easily changing

<column-break/>

from one purpose to another, and toward evil rather than good. On that occasion, misfortunes will happen to the native with punishments harmful to them. By that same measure, the soul of the native will be made to incline toward the aforementioned things; just as one becomes joyful in doing good to others and inclines toward the good when <term>fortunes<note>The "benefic" planets, traditionally Jupiter and Venus.</note></term> are the significators and are themselves free from hindrances, with nothing hindering being elevated above them. Then it will please the soul of the native to do good to others, and they will delight in this; nor will trouble follow from that good-doing, but rather utility and good praise.

But if those fortunes themselves are the significators, yet infortunes are elevated above them, the state of the native's soul will not be the same as described before; for it will be altered. The qualities of the native's soul will be soft and benevolent, not rigid or harsh, but rather quiet. But I tell you what happens to the native because of this: because of their humility, smoothness, softness, gentleness, benevolence, and abstinence from doing evil, and the piety and love they have for people, they will be looked down upon and despised by them. They will be blamed and accused even when they are guiltless and innocent; people will rashly believe the evil things that are falsely said about them, and they will find no one, or very few, to offer a word in their defense. They will be regarded as almost nothing in all things, even when they deserve praise and should be considered an authority. People will find "healthy" <note>original: "sana"; perhaps meant ironically or implying a pretense of sound reasoning.</note> excuses to judge them and will falsely impose many accusations upon them. Friendships will depart from them easily and almost without cause; the more the native serves, the less they will be thanked. Their services will be considered as nothing, and people will generally strive to harm them—not only strangers, but even those very people whom they served best. And for the most part, in everything they involve themselves in, the outcome will turn out poorly for them. This is the way by which the qualities of the souls of those born are known and predicted generally. However, concerning the particular qualities that happen to occur one by one according to the nature of the stars or planets, we must look further.

### Chapter two concerning the qualities of the native's soul occurring particularly according to the natures and significations of the stars.

Having already spoken of the qualities of the native's soul occurring universally, mention must now be made of the particular properties of the qualities which are accustomed to happen according to the natures of the stars and the qualities of the soul themselves.

### Concerning the signification of Saturn when he alone is the disposer of the qualities of the native's soul.

### Concerning the significance of Saturn when Jupiter is joined with it.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a regal male figure representing Jupiter seated on a throne, wearing a crown and holding a scepter. The astrological symbol for Jupiter (♃) is in the upper right corner.</image-desc>

But if Jupiter is joined with Saturn, and is itself of a good state and well-disposed, being <term>oriental<note>Rising before the sun, which was considered a position of strength.</note></term> (that is, in the world and relative to the sun) and located in the <term>angles<note>The "angles" (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses) are the most powerful points in a birth chart.</note></term>, it will make the soul of the native just. Such people gladly honor the old and the decrepit, and they are of sound counsel, gladly helping and assisting others. They have good knowledge, are generous givers, greatly patient, quiet, intelligent, lovers of friends, and seekers of philosophy.

### When Jupiter is ill-disposed.

If, however, its disposition is contrary to the one mentioned above, it will make the soul of the native ignorant of doing good, senseless in practical matters, and one who gladly studies and converses about diabolical things. They delight in and love <term>hypocrisy<note>original: "ypocrasim"</note></term>, pretending to linger gladly in places of prayer while inwardly receiving the opposite. They even predict the future without any knowledge of letters <note>meaning they claim prophetic powers without being educated or literate</note>; they do not care for pleasant things; they abhor having children, or have no desire at all to have friends, desiring to live in places far removed from human dwellings and not wishing to converse with men. And since such a person is foolish, they sometimes speak words similar to those of a wise man; they do not seek honor nor care to be praised; they choose evil rather than good and gladly cling to it. They are weak and malicious, and if they ever perform any good deeds, they quickly repent of them; they are hardworking and do not love the people.

### When Jupiter is neither well nor ill-disposed.

If, truly, Jupiter is found in a disposition that is neither entirely good nor entirely evil, it will make the soul of the native have qualities according to the state in which it is found. If its state leans more toward good than toward evil, the qualities of the soul will lean more toward good than toward evil. But if its state leans more toward evil than toward good, it will make the qualities of the soul lean more toward evil than toward good

<column-break/>

now <note>This "now" continues the sentence from the previous column.</note> lean, and you will always be able to prognosticate according to its state.

### Concerning the significance of Saturn when Mars is joined with it.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a warrior representing Mars clad in armor, holding a sword and a shield. The astrological symbol for Mars (♂) is in the upper right corner.</image-desc>

But if Mars is joined to Saturn and is itself of a good and praiseworthy state—namely in the angles and oriental in the world and from the sun—and is not <term>hindered<note>In astrology, a planet is hindered or "impeded" if it is in a weak sign or under harsh aspects from other planets.</note></term>, as <term>Ptolemy<note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the 'Tetrabiblos,' the foundational text for Western astrology.</note></term> says, it will make the soul of the native (on account of the malice of both planets) not knowing those things which it ought to know. The person will be miserable, weak, harmful, hardworking, and small-minded; they will hardly ever attempt anything without great fear. They are impious, heavy, and a <term>schemer<note>original: "baratatricē"; likely referring to one who commits "barratry" or fraud.</note></term>, acting as if they possess greatness, yet despising everything and having no orderly way about them. Through a kind of hypocrisy, they pretend to be warlike against their own nature, though they are timid in all things; yet they pretend to be warlike in everything even though they are the "daughter of fear." They love disturbances and are envious with the worst kind of envy; a traitress who perseveres in her malice and is not easily moved from it. Such a person is hardworking and gladly makes others work hard; they love hypocrisy and hate kings, princes, rulers, nobles, and all their elders. They boast of others' victories or claim them for themselves; they have no depth in goodness, are full of rudeness, and are difficult to tolerate. I say: they gladly harm men, hating, belittling, and despising them. They will neither be altered nor changed from the aforementioned traits but will always persevere in them; interfering in crafts and many other diverse matters, yet persevering well in none of them.

### When Mars is in a contrary state to the above.

If Mars is in the opposite state to what has been said, it will make the soul of the native a plunderer and a highwayman. Mars also makes the soul possess the worst qualities: not knowing God, nor even revering, fearing, or loving Him. Such a person gladly gains through wickedness and is a blasphemer and a disturber, truly loving no one. Mars will make them persist in robbery, being a traitress, a deceiver, a murderer, and shameless. They will be a lover of their own destruction <note>original: "sui ipsius homicidiū facientem"; literally committing suicide or being self-destructive</note>, a fornicatress, a violator of tombs, and generally wicked in all things.

### Concerning the significance of Saturn when Venus is joined with it.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a female figure representing Venus holding a pair of scales and a small branch. The astrological symbol for Venus (♀) is in the upper right corner.</image-desc>

But if Venus is joined to Saturn and is itself of a good state and well-disposed, being oriental in the world and from the sun, and likewise in the angles, it will make the soul of the native peaceful, benevolent, faithful, modest, abstinent, and deliberate. Such a person is a lover of knowledge, abstaining from impurities, loving and fearing God, and holding Him in reverence.

### When Venus is in a contrary state.

If, however, Venus is in a state contrary to the one mentioned above, it will make the soul of the native of bad reception and bad reputation, and of a bad moral law. It makes them shameless, unclean, tedious, jealous, hating women, foul...

## On the significance of Saturn when it is with Mercury and the Moon.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a crowned figure seated in a two-wheeled chariot. The figure holds a scepter in one hand and a tool (possibly a sickle) in the other. If Mercury is joined to Saturn and is itself in a good state and well-disposed: such as being <term>oriental<note>Rising before the sun, which was considered a position of strength in astrology.</note></term> in the world and similarly from the sun, and located in the <term>angles<note>The four most powerful houses in an astrological chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note></term>, and not otherwise hindered; it makes the soul of the native a seeker of laws and of kingly affairs, an investigator of necromancy, a lover of medical science, a deliberator of occult things, and one who hides themselves from others; a <term>sophist<note>A person skilled in reasoning and rhetoric, though sometimes implied to be deceptive.</note></term> of necromancy who shows themselves to do wonders before men and even without their presence; of good natural talent; a gentle explainer of things to be expounded; a good investigator of things to be researched; yet possessing a sharp bitterness within; a lover of the understanding of almost all works; and good things shall happen to them as a result.

### When Mercury is poorly disposed.

If, however, the disposition of Mercury is contrary to the aforementioned, it will make the soul of the native turbulent, envious, and full of labor: a hater of men and especially of their own kinsmen, nor will they desire to see them; desiring the goods of others; rejoicing in their misfortunes; a lover of sorrows; seeing <term>fantasies<note>Refers to vivid nightmares or disturbing hallucinations.</note></term> at night by which they are troubled; a deceiver and a traitor; a concealer of their own business, willingly adhering to necromancy; and no benefit shall follow from it, but rather its opposite.

## Chapter three: on the significance of Jupiter when it is the sole indicator or ruler of the qualities of the soul.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting a crowned figure, representing Jupiter, seated in a chariot. The astrological symbol for Jupiter (♃) is in the upper right. The chariot is drawn by two large eagles.</image-desc>

If Jupiter alone is the ruler of the soul’s qualities of the native and is the <term>almuten<note>The planet that holds the most dignity or power over a specific point in the zodiacal chart.</note></term> over the place where the Moon and Mercury are located; and if it is oriental in the world and from the sun, and likewise located in the angles and otherwise well-disposed and not hindered; it makes the soul of the native just, generous, magnanimous, pious, and modest; and making the person famous, benevolent, liberal, equitable, mild, distinguished, and pious; and of great thought in their works; lovable to men; willingly doing good; a leader of affairs, knowing how to conduct government and similar things.

it will make the soul of the native weak and secretive; without

## On the significance of Jupiter when Mars is joined to it.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration showing a crowned figure seated in a chariot. The astrological symbols for Jupiter (♃) and Mars (♂) are displayed. The chariot is drawn by two horses.</image-desc>

If Mars is joined to Jupiter and is itself in a good state and well-disposed, namely being oriental in the world and from the sun, and located in the angles and in no way hindered; it makes the soul of the native accustomed to being a pleader of cases; willingly litigious and delighting in controversies; warlike and an arranger of battles; a leader of armies; and especially on the side of those where justice lies; fortunate; serving no one; a lover of taking vengeance upon others, neither wishing to be placed under nor subject to anyone; wishing to promote themselves to dignities and lordships; not ignorant of the truth of things; seeking honor and grace; following prosperity therefrom; foresighted, irascible, and a liar; also commanding many things to many people.

### When Mars exists in the opposite state to the aforementioned.

If the same Mars exists in a state contrary to the aforementioned, it makes the soul of the native a blasphemer and shameless; a revealer of the malice of their own words, both their own secrets and those of others; a grasper of things to be grasped; an expounder of things to be explained; a despiser of others; a proud and deceptive hypocrite, disobedient; making the native a beggar, a plunderer, a cutter of clothes <term>abscisorem<note>Possibly referring to a tailor or, more likely in this context, a pickpocket or someone who ruins garments.</note></term>, a robber, a loser of their own things; a man of evil words; a disturber, vile, unfaithful, unstable; of bad reputation and bad counsel; senseless, changing easily from one purpose to another; for they exist of diverse qualities, and a certain manner of existence is not easily found in them.

## On the significance of Jupiter when Venus is joined to it.

### On the significance of Jupiter when Mercury is joined to it.

If indeed Mercury is joined to Jupiter and is itself in a good state and well-disposed, fortunate, and strong in the world, <term>oriental<note>rising before the sun, a position of strength</note></term> from the sun; and if it is in the <term>angles<note>the four most powerful houses of an astrological chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note></term> and not otherwise hindered, it will make the soul of the newborn apt for <term>syllogizing<note>logical reasoning</note></term> and geometry; they will willingly devote their leisure to the reading of books and study them, and will be skilled in every part of mathematics; a good speaker, victorious, compliant, well-ordered, a lover of gatherings; exhibiting sound counsel; of good character, good reputation, and good faith; bountiful, and possessing a good natural talent; and one who completes everything they begin willingly, swiftly, and well. And if they apply themselves to medicine, they will be very proficient in it, and from that will follow honor and suitable usefulness. By that occasion, the newborn will be summoned by kings, great men, the wealthy, and the noble, and they will willingly submit themselves to their care; they will also hold the newborn in reverence and fear. They will be a lover of their kinsmen and relatives, possessing riches, rational, and a lover of the sciences.

### When Mercury is in its contrary state.

If Mercury is in a state contrary to what was said and is hindered, it will make the soul of the newborn foolish, ignorant, senseless, and very talkative in their speech, often and very frequently deceived; and they will easily lose what little sense they have; impulsive, wishing to cling to divine matters but not knowing how to do so; bitter and proud, persevering in their folly; considering themselves wise; putting themselves into the service of another; disordered in their acts and their movements; wordy and seeking public attention; for they will not know how to hide the things they affect, yet they will have some degree of memory and some degree of learning.

### Chapter four: when Mars alone is the significator of the qualities of the newborn's soul.

### When Mars is badly disposed.

# On the significance of Mars when Mercury is joined to it.

If Mercury should be joined to Mars and is itself well-disposed and in a good state—that is, <term>oriental<note>Rising before the sun, which was considered a position of strength in medieval astrology.</note></term> in the world and similar to the Sun, and in the <term>angles<note>The four most powerful houses of a zodiac chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note></term> and not otherwise hindered—it will make the soul of the <term>native<note>The person for whom the astrological chart is cast.</note></term> mixed and of diverse qualities. It will make them gentle, wise, and powerful; a lover of those who love them; a seeker of knowledge; skilled in governance; easily changing from one purpose to another; desiring to reach their goals quickly. At other times—indeed, more often—they will be inclined toward evil deeds, a habitual betrayer, astute, unstable, furious, possessing a quick intellect, deceptive, a lover of <note>original: "vprocasim," likely hypocrisim</note> hypocrisy, rebellious, and <note>original: "vñspellem," likely versipellem</note> shifty. They will delight in quarrels and discord, being a great seeker of such things. However, they will not be reprehensible in all these things when the outcome is unfavorable; they will be diligent toward those like themselves, freely helping and aiding them, while holding those who oppose them in hatred, intending to harm them in every way and knowing well how to do so.

# On the significance of Venus when Mercury is joined to it.

And if Mercury should be joined to Venus and be in a good state and well-disposed—oriental in the world and from the Sun, and in an angle and not otherwise hindered—it will make the soul of the native a lover of crafts and sciences, especially practical ones. They will be of good wit and genius, seeking out music and diligent in all commendable things. They will likewise seek after delights and use them well and appropriately. It will also make them a lover of quiet, delighting in it, and cheerful. They will be diligent toward their friends, intelligent, and likewise followers of good law and good reputation. They will be a lover of horses, walking the straight path and deviating in nothing. They will learn freely both from themselves and from others, being studious in their learning. They will be a quick imitator of good and upright men, likening themselves to the lives of the just. They will be cheerful in their speech and apt and lovable in conversation; temperate in the soul, and very great in spirit. They will be a helper of the needy. Yet they will be corrupted by a desire to abuse pure things and commit shameful acts with them, wishing to prefer these to women; and they will be a jealous person.

# When Mercury is poorly disposed.

She will freely commit shameful acts and be blameworthy in many things; sometimes she will be blamed even when she does not commit a fault at that moment, but this will happen to her because of her bad habit of committing blameworthy acts.

### When Mercury is in a state contrary to the above.

#### But if Mercury should be in a state contrary to what was said—that is, if it is of an evil nature and poorly disposed—it will make the soul of the native base, deceptive, and one who takes pleasure in leading others into error. Such a person will be overconfident in their own counsel, light and hurried in movement, easily changing from one purpose to another, ignorant, fallacious, lying, unstable, and disorderly in their qualities. They will be unfaithful, lacking in reverence, disobedient, unjust in all things, and a user of falsehoods in every way.

### When Mercury is joined with any of the aforesaid.

#### But if Mercury should be joined with any of the aforementioned planets, in whatever condition you find it, it will be converted to the nature of that planet with which it is joined. According to that planet's disposition and effect—whether it be good or evil—you shall judge the future qualities of the soul.

### What each of the planets effects in the qualities of the soul when they are contrary.

When indeed any of the other planets is joined with another planet, and one is well-disposed and of a good nature, while the other is poorly disposed and of an evil nature, it will not signify the qualities of the soul exactly as described above. Instead, the qualities will participate in both, following the nature of each through a certain "middle significance" between those extremes—neither truly good nor entirely evil.

### Chapter 7: On the significance of the luminaries regarding the qualities of the native’s soul, and first concerning the Sun.

-><image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the Sun (Sol) personified as a crowned king seated on a throne, holding a scepter and a shield decorated with a lion (the zodiac sign Leo). Above him is a radiating sun symbol. The scene is enclosed in a decorative architectural arch.</image-desc><-

Regarding the significance of the <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon, distinguished from the other planets because of their brightness and size in the sky.</note></term> over the qualities of the soul, there is a rule that differs slightly from the rules of the other planets, yet it is not contrary to them. For since the Sun naturally signifies religion and those qualities of the soul that seem to look toward piety, it shares in the qualities of the native's soul along with the other planetary dispositors. Hence, if at the hour of birth the Sun is of a good nature and well-disposed in the world—that is, if it is in the angles—and is joined with the planet governing the soul's qualities, it will help in making that soul more discrete, more mindful, and more inclined to separate itself from unjust and illicit things. It likewise makes the person more generous, more powerful, a follower of better laws, and more fortunate.

### When the Sun is of an evil nature and poorly disposed.

#### But if the Sun should be in a state contrary to what was said, it will assist the governor of the soul's qualities—if joined to it—in making that soul miserable and full of bad qualities: base in its own ruin, laborious, overconfident in its own counsel while doubting others, foolish, and possessing a heavy and wicked will against everyone, not easily retreating from its own vices.

<column-break/>

### Chapter 8: On the significance of the Moon regarding the qualities of the native’s soul.

-><image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the Moon (Luna) personified as a female figure seated on a throne, holding a crescent moon and a shield decorated with a crab (the zodiac sign Cancer). Above her is a crescent moon symbol. The scene is enclosed in a decorative architectural arch.</image-desc><-

To the Moon, however, is given significance over the qualities of both the body and the soul, though not specifically over the qualities of the soul in the same way as the others. It holds its significance by aiding the other planets through its own placement: good placements lead to good, and evil to evil. Hence, <term>Ptolemy<note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer whose 'Tetrabiblos' was the foundation of medieval astrology.</note></term> said in the <note>original: "alarba" - the Arabic-derived name for Ptolemy's *Tetrabiblos* or *Quadripartitum* (The Four Books)</note> *Alarba* that when the Moon is in the place of its <term>nodes<note>The points where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic.</note></term> or at its greatest distance to the north or south, it will assist those souls and cause them to change suddenly. But if the Moon is in either of the two "nude" places, or in the place where the Moon's circle crosses the Sun's path, it will assist the qualities of the native's soul so that they perform more quickly the things they ought to do. Furthermore, when the Moon is above the earth and increasing in light, or in its <term>fullness<note>original: "bederez" - likely an astrological term for the full moon or its opposition to the Sun.</note></term> (opposition to the Sun), it helps the qualities of the soul by making them active and fit for necessary tasks. And if it is below the earth or waning in light under the Sun's rays, it helps by making the qualities more hidden, less likely to come into action, and slower in the future.

### On the significance of the Moon when joined with planets in their dignities.

To know the significance of the Moon when it is with the planets in their <term>dignities<note>The signs of the zodiac where a planet is considered to have the most strength or "honor," such as its House or Exaltation.</note></term>, look to its place in the birth chart—in whose house or exaltation it resides. If it is in the dignity of Saturn and joined to it by <term>aspect<note>The geometric angle between two planets, such as a square or trine.</note></term> or conjunction, it makes the native’s soul sad, laborious, and foolish in the use of its strength, as well as fleeing and cold; it will make the native [prosper] only if Saturn is <term>oriental<note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note></term>, for then the native's state will be improved. If it is in the dignities of Jupiter and joined to it, it makes the native magnanimous, mixing with kings and great men, religious, fortunate, and praiseworthy in all their acts. If it is in the dignities of Mars and joined to it, it makes the soul audacious, a lover of quarrels, labor, and travel, and one who freely mixes with warlike men, acquiring good therefrom. If it is in the dignities of the Sun and joined by a good aspect, it makes the soul mix with kings and high-ranking men, or the native will be one of them. But if joined by an evil aspect, it makes the native of a poor state, short-lived, and full of many infirmities. If it is in the dignities of Mercury and joined to it, it makes the soul cunning, ingenious in pursuits, wise, and a seeker of fortune and goodness.

### Regarding the Second House.

### Chapter 1: On the significance of the native’s prosperity and substance, and regarding its acquisition.

Having dealt in the preceding sections with the form and figure of the native’s body and the qualities of their soul, there remains the matter of the native’s <term>substance<note>In this context, "substance" refers to wealth, property, and material possessions.</note></term> and prosperity: likewise, from where and how they shall acquire it, and in what part of their life. For after birth, this is among the most principal and necessary accidents to consider.

It is necessary to make mention of the native's birth. For <term>Ptolemy<note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer whose 'Tetrabiblos' formed the basis of Western astrology.</note></term> says that we must understand how, in what way, and from where wealth will come to the native from the <term>Part of Fortune<note>A mathematical point in a horoscope representing worldly success and well-being.</note></term>. Nor does his saying differ from what <term>Aomar<note>Umar al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer and architect.</note></term> or <term>Alboali<note>Abū 'Alī al-Khayyāṭ, a student of Māshā'allāh and author of 'The Judgment of Nativities.'</note></term> wish to say; for in Ptolemy, the speech was general. Others truly followed in his footsteps, but they added certain things which they experienced in their own times, affirming that these sayings were not at variance.

The knowledge of the coming of wealth is found by looking at the Part of Fortune and the planet that is the <term>Almuten<note>The planet that holds the most "dignities" or essential power over a specific degree of the zodiac.</note></term> over the degree in which that Part is located. Consider its strength and weakness, and the planets that are conjoined to that Almuten at the hour of birth, or those which are elevated above it in the manner previously described, whether it be of its own <term>sect<note>Original: "ayz." Likely a corruption of "hayz," a condition where a planet is in a favorable hemisphere and sign according to its gender.</note></term> or not. For if the Almuten over that place should be of good condition, well-disposed, fortunate—that is, lucky—and strong, and free from impediments, you may judge that the native will abound in many riches. This is even more certain if an aspect of some fortunate planet intervenes, and especially <term>Jupiter<note>Traditionally known as the "Greater Benefic," the planet of expansion and wealth.</note></term>, whether by day or by night, or the Sun by day, or the Moon by night.

And if that significator of wealth should be Saturn, or if the Almuten over it is Saturn and he is of good condition, as we have said, it will signify that the native acquires riches from heavy labors or from great buildings. But if it should be Jupiter, it demonstrates the native will obtain riches from offices and stewardships—both extraordinary ones, such as the governorship of castles, vicarages, or dukedoms, or from other forms of uprightness—rather than from ordinary ones. But if Mars should emerge as the significator of the native's riches, you will not doubt that he gathered them from the plundering of armies and the ruling of cities as well as other things.

If indeed the Sun should be the significator of the native's wealth, he brings riches from the discovery of raw gold, or gold not yet recognized, or gold bought at some risk. And if the Sun is in the <term>fourth house<note>The house associated with the home, foundations, and hidden things under the earth.</note></term>, he will find it underground. If likewise Venus should be the significatrix of the native's wealth, she will make him accumulate substance from women or from gifts. Furthermore, if Mercury should be his significator, he will announce that riches will come to the native from merchants and trade, and from the native’s own industry and skill. Moreover, if the Moon should signify the native's substance, she will bring it to him unexpectedly from silver, or from journeys, or from voyages, or from the uses of commerce.

Furthermore, if Saturn is the Almuten over the Part of Wealth and Jupiter is joined to him—and more strongly so if he is in an angle of the <term>Ascendant<note>The 1st house, representing the self and the beginning of life.</note></term> or in the <term>tenth house<note>The Midheaven, representing career, public standing, and honors.</note></term>, or in another good place in a <term>common sign<note>Also known as mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note></term>—it will signify inheritances that will come to the native from strangers, and especially through women. This is even more likely if Jupiter has a visual aspect with the Moon; and again more so if the planets which are of the sect of the significators of wealth are in conjunction with it. This will also signify that those inheritances will remain in the native's possession. But if any of the planets which are not of that sect, but of the <term>domicile<note>Original: "d[omi]nio." Referring to the planetary ruler of the sign.</note></term>, should be elevated above the Almuten or follow it closely, it signifies that the native will lose the things acquired in the aforementioned manner, nor will they remain in his possession for long.

When these things that have been said about gain or loss ought to happen, you can perceive through the aforementioned significators. For they will occur when they come to the <term>angles<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, where planetary influence is most manifest in the physical world.</note></term> of the birth figure, the distance from the angle having been considered, through which they signify years or months, for example.

<term>Tiberiadis<note>Al-Tabari.</note></term> indeed said: when you wish to look into the matter of the native's wealth, look according to the Ascendant of the birth, and see what planets are in it, and the lord of the second house, and the Part of Substance and its lord; likewise Jupiter and the Part of Fortune, and similarly its lord. Then look at the Almuten over these places, whether it be one or many. After this, see what the condition of its Almuten is—whether it is free from impediments, fortunate, and strong. See how it stands with the lord of the Ascendant, whether they aspect each other or are joined together bodily, and whether with <term>reception<note>A condition where one planet is in the dignities of another, suggesting cooperation or a favorable outcome.</note></term> or not. For reception signifies the completion of the matter. See if they join by op-

<column-break/>

position or by a <term>quartile aspect<note>A 90-degree angle, traditionally considered a "hard" or challenging aspect.</note></term>; for these signify the detriment of the matter itself. And according to what you see regarding his substance, so judge.

<term>Alboaly<note>Abū 'Alī al-Khayyāṭ.</note></term>, however, was seen to intend that you should look into the matter of the prosperity and substance of the native—from where it might come to him, and its abundance or scarcity—from the lordship of the <term>triplicity<note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note></term> of the sign in which the <term>luminary<note>The Sun or the Moon.</note></term> that has authority is located, as will be said below. This is to make the task easier: if they should be in the angles, fortunate and strong, they signify prosperity and riches for the native at all times of his life. This is especially true if they are in the first 15 degrees before the <term>cusps<note>The "entrance" or starting line of an astrological house.</note></term> of any of those angles—that is, the degrees that go toward the cusp of the angle, not those which have already passed the angle. However, this is more so in the seventh house than in the fourth; more in the tenth than in the seventh; and likewise more in the first than in the tenth; for then his circumstances will prosper more. Also, the closer they are to the cusp, the greater and more praiseworthy will be his status, prosperity, and fortune. And if they should be after the aforementioned 15 degrees until the end of the angle, the further they are from the angle, the less his prosperity and fortune will be.

You shall therefore consider all the things mentioned above which I told you must be considered: namely, all the aforementioned methods and all the aforementioned significators. If you find them all fortunate, strong, and free from impediment—which a man is hardly ever accustomed to encounter—you can know and declare that the native will have immense and inestimable riches, and his prosperity and status will be sublime and most excellent. This will be to such an extent that he can never be resisted, and he shall be promoted to the lordship of the whole world, of whatever race or condition he may be—even if he is found born of the lowest lineage—and it shall remain with him all the days of his life. 

This is true unless perhaps some of the <term>fixed stars<note>Stars that do not move relative to each other, unlike the "wandering stars" or planets.</note></term> which I named to you above should diminish this in some way. Or if the <term>Heart of the Lion<note>Original: "cor leonis." The star Regulus, the most important star in the constellation Leo, associated with royalty and great power.</note></term> is found in the Ascendant or in the tenth house, one degree before the line or three degrees after it; for it will increase his heights almost innumerably. However, it will end in evil unless a strong fortune looks upon it from a <term>trine<note>A 120-degree aspect, considered very harmonious.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>A 60-degree aspect, considered helpful.</note></term> aspect; for it signifies the native is to die an evil death, or at the very least will fall from all his dignities, powers, and heights. But if a fortune looks upon it from a fourth part, it will diminish the malice of the Heart of the Lion. And if an infortune looks upon it, it will increase its misfortune. 

And if all these aforementioned significators should not emerge safe and free, but only a part of them, you can judge the native's prosperity, valid status, and abounding riches according to that quantity which was safe. You should therefore render each thing to its proper part, so that you may rightly discern the native's prosperity, riches, and status.

# When you wish to look into the prosperity and substance of the native.

When you have erected the figure of anyone's birth and you wish to look into their prosperity and substance, look first at the Part of Fortune; for it takes precedence over the Part of Substance. For the Part of Fortune signifies the native’s substance, prosperity, status, and all his being; whereas the Part of Substance is attributed only to riches. See in whose house, or exaltation, or term, or triplicity you find it has fallen. Consider which of the aforementioned significators was stronger in that place by the multitude of dignities or strengths; because he shall be called the Almuten, and he will be the significator of the prosperity and substance of the native and of his being. For if he should be in the Ascendant, or in one of the angles, or in some of his own houses—and especially in that in which the Part of Fortune is located—free from impediments, fortunate, and strong...
