...it will signify the prosperity of the native and their profit, as well as a great quantity of riches to come. And if the Lord of the <term>Ascendant<note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, representing the self.</note></term> or any of the <term>fortunes<note>The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus, traditionally associated with positive outcomes.</note></term> aspects it, and if that aspecting planet is free from impediments, fortunate (that is, lucky), and strong—even more so if that aspect is a <term>trine<note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>An aspect of 60 degrees, considered helpful and productive.</note></term>—and further still if it is with <term>reception<note>A condition where two planets are in each other's signs of dignity, allowing them to cooperate.</note></term>, then their substance will increase by more than half of its total. If, however, it is the Lord of <term>Exaltation<note>A specific sign where a planet’s influence is particularly powerful or "honored."</note></term>, the wealth will increase by a third part, but with greater fame. If it is the Lord of the <term>Term<note>A small subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet; an "essential dignity."</note></term>, it will increase by a fifth part. If it is the Lord of the <term>Triplicity<note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note></term>, it will increase by a seventh part. If it is the Lord of the <term>Face<note>A 10-degree division of a sign, also known as a decan.</note></term>, it will increase by a twelfth part. But if the aspect is from a <term>square<note>Original: "quarto". A 90-degree aspect, traditionally considered tense or challenging.</note></term> or an opposition, the wealth will be much less than this; and it will be even less and worse if the aspect is without reception.

**¶ When the Lord of the house does not aspect or is impeded.**
If the Lord of the house does not aspect or is <term>impeded<note>Afflicted by bad aspects from "malefic" planets like Saturn or Mars, or being too close to the Sun ("combust").</note></term>, look then to the Lord of the Term. If that planet is also impeded, look to the Lord of the Triplicity. If you see that he is also impeded, look finally to the Lord of the Face; and judge concerning each of them and their significance just as I have told you. Indeed, if the <term>Part of Fortune<note>A mathematical point in the chart representing worldly success.</note></term> and all the aforementioned indicators are impeded—and especially the <term>Almuten<note>The planet that holds the most power or "dignities" over a specific degree of the zodiac.</note></term> over the place of the said Part—you shall firmly announce the opposite of everything said above; in that same manner, you shall predict for the bad side just as was judged for the good.

**¶ When the Part of Fortune cannot be the significator of the good or the riches of the native, nor his state, nor the planet that is the Lord of the house in which it is located, nor of the Exaltation, nor the Term, nor the Triplicity, nor the Face, nor the Almuten over that place: look then to the <term>Part of Substance<note>Original: "prem s̄re," likely an abbreviation for "partem substantie." A secondary point used to calculate wealth.</note></term>. You will see into whose house or any of the aforementioned dignities it falls, and you will consider the Almuten over that place in the same way I told you regarding the Lord of the house; for such a planet will be the significator over the prosperity and substance of the native.**

**¶ When the Part of Fortune cannot be the significator of the native's well-being.**
But if neither the Part of Fortune nor the planet in whose dignity it resides can be the significator of the native's prosperity and substance, look to the <term>Second House<note>The house of the zodiac traditionally governing money, possessions, and livelihood.</note></term> and its Lord, or the planet that is within it. If there is any fortune in the Second House, or if it is joined with the Lord of the Second by a trine or sextile aspect, it will signify that the native will acquire much substance—and even more so if that fortune is Jupiter. If, however, the Sun is there in the <term>day<note>Original: "ioie," likely a corruption of "die."</note></term>, its significance will be less than that of Jupiter. If the Moon is there at night, it will be less than the Sun. If it is Venus, it will be less than the Moon.

**¶ When neither the Second House nor its Lord or the planet within it can be the significator of the native's substance.**
And if neither the Second House nor its Lord or the planet within it can signify the native's substance, look then to <term>Jupiter<note>The "Great Benefic," traditionally the primary planet governing wealth and growth.</note></term>, who naturally signifies substance. If you find him in the Second House, judge with certainty that the native will abound in affluent riches according to Jupiter's disposition, and that they will never come to poverty at any time. This is even stronger if Jupiter is the Lord of the Ascendant. According to that saying of <term>Almansor<note>Likely referring to the 'Propositions' or 'Aphorisms' of Al-Mansur, a popular medieval astrological text.</note></term>: "He whose birth-lord is Jupiter shall never be poor or needy." And it is even more sublime if Sagittarius or Pisces is on the <term>Fourth House<note>The house of the home and end-of-life matters; Jupiter rules these two signs.</note></term>, for this does not admit the contrary. But if Jupiter is impeded so that he cannot be the significator as described, then look to the Sun, who, if he is in any good place from the Ascendant, free from impediments, fortunate, and strong, signi-

<column-break/>

-fies that the native will obtain money or substance; but this will be less than the natural significance of Jupiter. If it is a nocturnal birth, then look to the Moon; if she is in the Second House, fortunate, strong, and free, or in another good place from the Ascendant, she will signify that great riches will come to the native. However, her significance will be less than that of the Sun.

**¶ When the Sun or Moon cannot signify the substance of the native.**
In that case, look to the planet that is the Almuten over the place where the Almuten of any of the aforementioned parts of substance—namely, Fortune or the Part of Substance—is located. Appoint him as the significator of substance; if he is fit for this, he will signify that the native will acquire much substance, but his significance will be less than that of the Moon.

**¶ When that planet cannot be the significator of the native's substance.**
If such a planet cannot signify the native's substance, look to the planet in whose house the Moon is located. If it is in the Ascendant, or in the Second, or in an <term>angle<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful positions in a chart.</note></term>, or in another good place from the Ascendant, and is free from impediments, fortunate, and strong, it will bring much money to the native; however, its significance will be less than the aforementioned Almuten.

**¶ When the planet in whose house the Moon is located cannot be the significator of the native's substance.**
Truly, if that planet cannot be the significator of the native's substance, look to the planet that is in the Second House. If it is free from impediments, fortunate, and strong—and even more so if it has some dignity in the Second or is itself fortunate—it will signify that the native will obtain a good quantity of money. However, its significance will be less than the planet in whose house the Moon is located.

**¶ When the planet in the Second House cannot be the significator of the native's substance.**
If the planet in the Second cannot be the significator, then see if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Fourth House are the same planet; for that planet may rightly be called the significator of the native's prosperity and substance. If you find him free, fortunate, and strong, take it as a certainty that the native will gather much money, just as well as if a fortune were in the Second House.

**¶ When the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Fourth are not the same planet.**
If you do not find this, look then to the <term>Lords of the Triplicity<note>Every sign has three planets that govern it as "triplicity rulers." Medieval astrologers used them to divide a person's life into three chronological periods.</note></term> of the house of substance (the Second House). If you find them all free, fortunate, and strong, it is signified that riches will come to the native according to their status, or even quite affluently beyond it. If only two of them are "saved," riches will come to them in two parts of their life, but not in the third. But if only one of them is saved, riches will come to them only in one-third part of their life, and not in the others. If none of them are saved, riches will never come to them from this source—though they might still come from the other causes previously mentioned or those yet to be discussed.

**¶ When the Lords of the Triplicity of the house of substance cannot be the significators of the native's substance.**
And if the aforementioned Lords of the Triplicity of the house of substance cannot be the significators for the native, then look to the Lords of the Triplicity of the sign in which the Sun is located, if it is a daytime birth; namely, the Lords of the Triplicity of the sign...

...in which the moon was located, if it was a nocturnal birth, and judge according to what I told you concerning the lords of the <term>triplicity<note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water. Each triplicity is ruled by a set of three planets.</note></term> of the house of <term>substance<note>original: "substantiae"; refers to the native's wealth, property, and material means.</note></term>.

### ->When the lords of the triplicity of the sign in which the sun or moon is located cannot signify the wealth of the native.<-

If indeed the aforementioned planets cannot be the significators of the <term>native's<note>The person for whom the astrological chart is cast.</note></term> wealth, nor are they fit for this, look then to the lords of the triplicity of the <term>Ascending sign<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, also known as the First House.</note></term> and judge from them just as you judged from the lords of the triplicity of the sun and moon; however, their significance will be less than that of the significators of the lords of the triplicity of the sun by day, and the moon by night.

### ->When the lords of the triplicity of the ascending sign cannot signify the wealth of the native.<-

But if the lords of the triplicity of the ascending sign are not fit to signify the wealth of the native, look then to the sign in which the <term>Part of Fortune<note>A calculated point in the horoscope representing prosperity and success.</note></term> is located and its lord. If you find that lord in the <term>Second House<note>Traditionally the "House of Wealth," governing money and personal possessions.</note></term> or in another good place from the ascendant, free from impediment, and <term>fortunate and strong<note>original: "fortunatus .f. atqȝ fortis"</note></term>, it will be the significator of the native's wealth and prosperity. It will bring a competent quantity of wealth to them. Nevertheless, its significance will be less than the significance of the lords of the triplicity of the ascendant.

### ->When the lord of the sign in which the Part of Fortune is located cannot signify the wealth of the native.<-

If indeed the lord of the sign in which the Part of Fortune is located cannot be the significator of the native's wealth, look then to the sign in which the <term>Part of Substance<note>Another calculated point specifically related to movable goods and riches.</note></term> is located and its lord. If you find it in the second house or in another good place from the ascendant, free, fortunate, and strong, set it as the significator of the native's wealth and devoted matters. Its significance will be equal to the significance of the lord of the sign in which the Part of Fortune was located; for it will vary only slightly from that.

### ->When the lord of the sign in which the Part of Substance cannot signify the wealth of the native.<-

Even if the lord of the sign in which the Part of Substance is located cannot be the significator of the native's wealth, look then to see if the sun is in the line of the descending house two degrees before or five degrees after (or less), and the moon is moving toward it from its left side by a <term>trine<note>A harmonious aspect of 120 degrees.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>A helpful aspect of 60 degrees.</note></term> aspect; and if the lord of the house of substance is in its own house or its <term>exaltation<note>A sign where a planet's influence is particularly powerful and dignified.</note></term>, moving toward a conjunction with the lord of the ascendant or toward its trine or sextile aspect. This is even more significant and powerful if **Jupiter** is the lord of the house of substance, for this will signify that the native will be of great name and great fame, and very powerful. If, however, there is another significator of wealth alongside this while Jupiter approaches it, wealth will come to them immensely, but they will not all be of such exceeding fame. If the 19th degree of Aries is the <term>Tenth House<note>The 'Midheaven,' representing career, public status, and honors.</note></term>, and the ascendant is the 25th degree of Cancer, and it—or at least the Sun and Jupiter—is free from <term>malefics<note>original: "infortunijs"; refers to the difficult influences of Mars or Saturn.</note></term> and their lords, the name of that native shall be exalted, and their fame shall be greatly spread and published throughout the whole earth.

And **Ptolemy** said a certain word that seems to disagree with the consideration of this house, but nevertheless, it does not disagree in meaning. For he said that when the planets ruling the houses or signs that give children (which will be discussed below in the chapter on the matter of children) are in their own proper places—which are the tenth, eleventh, first, and fifth—and they are <term>oriental<note>Rising before the sun; considered a more active and positive state for most planets.</note></term>, the native will be powerful and of great name. If, however, they are <term>occidental<note>Setting after the sun; considered a weaker or more passive state.</note></term> and in places contrary to them, the native will be miserable and unknown. If, moreover, the aforesaid rulers of said places and the Part of Fortune are in the ascendant or with the lordship of the ascendant, the native will live until he takes a wife, will be loved by his parents, and will be made their heir. But if it is not so, or if they are contrary to each other, or if they aspect each other from a <term>square aspect<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually indicating tension or conflict.</note></term> or an

<column-break/>

**opposition**, the native will be a litigator and will accumulate extreme hatred toward his parents and treat them badly; nor will he succeed them in inheritance.

### ->When the aforesaid planets cannot be significators of the native's wealth nor in the tenth house.<-

But if neither the lord of the sign in which the Part of Substance is located nor any of the aforesaid planets can be significators of the native's wealth, and the sun is not in the tenth house in the manner I described to you, look then to the planets with which the aforesaid significators are joined, or those which are <term>elevated<note>A planet that is higher in the chart or closer to the Midheaven than another.</note></term> above them—that is, those which precede others in the junction of the <term>Almuten<note>The planet that has the most dignity and power over a specific point or house in the chart.</note></term> that I mentioned—or those which are north of it. For they themselves shall be the significators of the native's wealth and **Mars**, and whichever among them is more powerful in dignity or fortune. However, its significance will be far below the significance of the planet in whose house the Part of Substance was located.

### ->When the aforesaid planets with which the significators are joined cannot signify the wealth of the native.<-

If indeed the aforesaid planets cannot be significators of the native's wealth, look then to the Almuten over the aforesaid places or any one of them. If it is free from impediments and fortunate—that is, strong—it will signify the native's wealth; but its significance will be below all the significations mentioned above.

### ->Which of the said significators are preferred over others.<-

And know indeed that among the significators, the most principal and strongest are the Part of Fortune, the Part of Substance, the Second House and its lord—these are more universal in the matter of wealth—and similarly **Jupiter**, who, although he is not always stronger than the others, is nevertheless always more universal than all others in the signification of wealth.

### ->If all the aforesaid significators should be impeded.<-

But if all the lords of the aforesaid houses and all the aforesaid significators should be so impeded that none of them can signify the native's wealth, look then to the lords of the Exaltations; and this is not a redundancy. If, however, the lords of the Exaltations are impeded, look to the lords of the <term>Terms<note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs that grant a specific planet "essential dignity."</note></term>. If truly the lords of the Terms are impeded, look to the lords of the Triplicities. But if the lords of the Triplicities are impeded—which would be marvelous and unheard of—look lastly to the lords of the <term>Faces<note>Also known as decans; ten-degree divisions of a sign.</note></term>, and judge through them just as you would judge through any of the others as I touched upon above.

### ->When the significators of the native's wealth are malefic.<-

And know that if the significators of the native's wealth are <term>malefics<note>original: "mali"; referring to planets like Saturn or Mars which are traditionally challenging.</note></term>, even if they are found to be well-disposed, they will not bring as much good as the fortunes. If indeed they are unfortunate and poorly disposed, they will bring the opposite: intolerable poverty. If, however, you find a misfortune in the second house, or the rays of a misfortune that has no dignity there, without the presence or aspect of a fortune, or even in any of the aforesaid places signifying wealth, or the significators of wealth themselves are impeded, you should expect and judge the opposite of those things that were said.

### ->When the fortunes are significators of the native's wealth.<-

When the **fortunes** are strong, they will present much good; however, when they are impeded, they will present little good to the native.

## ->Chapter Two: From where the native acquires wealth or money, and in what manner, and in what part of their life.<-

Lastly, one must look at the planet and the place signifying from where the native may acquire wealth, and by what manner, and in what part of their life, and similarly in what part of time. Therefore, after the wealth of the native...

...you find the <term>significator<note>The specific planet or point in a chart that represents a particular area of life—in this case, wealth.</note></term>: consider in which house you find it has fallen. For you shall announce from where the <term>native's<note>The person for whom the birth chart is being read.</note></term> <term>substance<note>original: "substantia"; refers to money, property, and material possessions.</note></term> should come and by what means, according to the significations of that house, and also by the significations of the planet <term>Almuten<note>original: "almutez"; the planet that holds the most cumulative astrological strength (dignity) over a specific point in the zodiac.</note></term> of that house, and similarly by the significations of the planet actually found within that house.

### ### Chapter Three: In what time of his life, and in what part, the native may acquire substance.

**I**n which specific time and in what part of his life the native will acquire substance can be weighed through the lords of the <term>triplicity<note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water). Each triplicity is ruled by a set of three planets that govern different stages of life.</note></term>. For the first lord brings substance in the first part of life, the second in the second part, and the third in the third part of the native's life. Thus, whichever of them you find fit for this purpose, you may judge the money appointed for the native in that corresponding third of his life. If you find all of them well-disposed, the native will enjoy the gain of substance throughout his whole life. If, however, you find only two of them fortunate, you shall predict he will attain substance in two parts of his life. And if you find only one of them fortunate, you can affirm that substance will come only in the single third of his life assigned to that significator.

### ### Chapter Four: Why the ancients avoided some of the aforementioned significators.

**T**he ancient wise men—not as if they were ignorant, but rather to avoid unnecessary labor—used only the lord of the <term>Ascendant<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term>, the lord of the second house, the <term>Part of Fortune<note>A calculated point in the chart representing prosperity.</note></term>, the Part of Substance, and their lords, as well as Jupiter, in the matter of signifying the native's wealth, leaving almost all other factors to the industry of the wise. Because of this, it often happens that the matter of the native’s wealth is not judged correctly to a hair's breadth by astrologers, because they do not care to consider any significators except those I have just told you. However, you can see, if you wish to consider the matter correctly, that the riches or substance of natives do not always arrive exactly according to those few signs. For we see some who are very rich, some even richer, some merely rich, some moderately so; some are neither rich nor poor; some are moderately poor, some poor, some poorer, some most poor; some are beggars, some even more beggarly, and some the most beggarly of all. We see some who always abound, some who are always in need, and some who sometimes abound and sometimes are in need. Some flee from poverty with great labor, while others escape it and support their household with ease. This variety occurs only because of the many significators named above and their <term>dispositions<note>The state, position, and "comfort" of a planet in the zodiac, which determines how effectively it can act.</note></term> and their overlapping influences, even though those the ancients use are the primary ones. Hence, according to how fortunate you find these significators, you may judge the prosperity and substance of the native. And according to how unfortunate you find them, you may announce his adversity according to their succession and order which I have shown you. For just as the significators of substance mentioned above will bring wealth when they are fortunate and strong, so when they are fortunate but weak and ill-disposed, they will take it away and bring hardship, misery, labor, sadness, and poverty. Therefore, be industrious and wise so that you know how to consider all these things. You shall also consider if the Part of Fortune is with the Moon in the birth chart and if Jupiter <term>aspects<note>Forms a geometric relationship or "stare" with another planet, exerting influence over it.</note></term> it in a daytime birth, or if Venus aspects it in a nighttime birth: for this will signify the good nourishment and upbringing of the native—and even more strongly if the Part of Fortune is in a favorable place relative to the Ascendant. You will similarly see the disposition of each and every one of the aforementioned significators, namely the lords of the triplicities

<column-break/>

and the others. For if any of the lords of the triplicity is well-disposed, but the lord of substance or the Part of Fortune or its lord is ill-disposed, the former will take away from the latter according to its state. And if the significator of the birth is in a masculine sign in daytime births, or in a feminine sign in nighttime births, and is not otherwise hindered, its strength will be greater and its testimony will more firmly affirm the truth regarding good nourishment, whether the life of the native be long or short.

### ### Chapter Five: From where and from what cause the native may acquire substance.

**S**ince we have spoken in the preceding sections about the acquisition of the native's substance and the accumulation of its quantity, we must now look at from where, by what mode, and from what cause he acquires it. You shall therefore consider the lord of the house of substance <note>The Second House.</note> or whatever other significator of it you find, and you will see in which house you find it has fallen. Similarly, see with which of the planets you find it joined; for that will signify how and from where the native is likely to acquire money. For if it is in the first house—as I remember touching upon in my summary of the treatise on the significations of the twelve houses—it signifies that the native is to acquire substance from his own person, that is, through his own industry with little worry and little labor, or through any of the causes signified by the first house.

¶ When the significator of the native's substance is in the second house.
**I**f it is found in the second, he will find it from his own existing wealth, such as the fruits of his own possessions and goods, through trade, or other arts that are practiced with money and the like, or any of the causes signified by the second house.

¶ When the significator of substance is in the third house.
**I**f it is in the third, he will find it by cause of brothers or sisters, or neighbors not related to him, or by short journeys of two days or less, or by cause of his relatives or minor kinsmen by marriage who are lesser than him in wealth and power according to age, or those who look to him as their superior, or any of the causes signified by the third house.

¶ When the significator of substance is in the fourth house.
**I**f it is in the fourth, he will find it by cause of fathers or grandfathers, or fathers-in-law, or other ancestors and elders of long life; or from the trade of lands, houses, or things dug from the earth. Perhaps he will even find buried treasure, although this happens very rarely; or it may come from the use of furnaces and similar things, or any of the causes signified by the fourth house.

¶ When the significator of substance is in the fifth house.
**I**t may come through the favor and gifts of the great men who practice such things, or by cause of moderate journeys (which I reckon as being from two to four days), or by cause of eating or drinking sold in taverns or similar places, or by cause of games and the like, or any of those things signified by the fifth house.

¶ When the significator of substance is in the sixth house.
**I**f it is in the sixth, he will acquire it by cause of male or female servants or attendants, or small animals that do not work—such as sheep, goats, pigs, dogs, birds, and the like—or by cause of any of those things signified by the sixth house.

¶ When the significator of substance is in the seventh house.
**B**ut if it is in the seventh, he will acquire it by cause of women, or partners, or enemies, or by cause of any of those things signified by the seventh house.

### ¶ When the significator of substance is in the eighth.

**If** indeed it is in the eighth [house], he will find it through the dowries of women or their goods, or the goods of associates, or enemies, or through the cause of someone's death, or goods inherited from the dead, or <term>paraphernalia<note>original: "parafernaliu[m]"; personal property belonging to a married woman beyond her dowry.</note></term>, or through any of those things signified by the eighth house.

### ¶ When the significator of substance is in the ninth.

**But** if it is in the ninth, he will acquire it through religion or religious people, or through long journeys—as merchants and others traveling far are sometimes accustomed to do—and similar things, or through those things signified by the ninth house.

### ¶ When the significator of substance is in the tenth.

**If** you find it in the tenth, say that he will acquire it through royalty, or a mastership, or a magistracy, or an office, or another lay dignity, such as dukedoms or <term>podestariates<note>original: "potestarie"; the office of a high-ranking official or chief magistrate in medieval Italian cities.</note></term> and the like, or through any of those things signified by the tenth house.

### ¶ When the significator of substance is in the eleventh.

**Furthermore**, if it is in the eleventh, he will find it through friends, or soldiers, or members of a household; through governance or business, or loans and <term>banking tables<note>original: "mensibus"; refers to the tables used by money-changers and bankers.</note></term>; or he will acquire it from unexpected fortune coming to him, or from things in which he had hope of profit, or through those things signified by the eleventh house.

### ¶ When the significator of substance is in the twelfth.

**Finally**, if it is in the twelfth, he will acquire it through prison or the imprisoned—as the guards of prisoners are sometimes accustomed to do, or because he released those in prison for the sake of profit—or through hidden enemies, or large animals, or some hereditary office, or through theft, or through any of those things signified by the twelfth house. These are the figures of all twelve houses, as I told you above in the treatise on the twelve houses; there is no need to summarize them all for you here.

## Chapter Six: In what manner the native will acquire substance.

**We** must see in what manner the native acquires substance. You shall consider the significator of substance—whether it be the lord of the <term>Part of Fortune<note>A mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity.</note></term>, or the lord of the <term>Part of Substance<note>A specific "Arabic Part" related to wealth.</note></term>, or the Sun or Moon, or any of the lords of the <term>triplicities<note>Planetary rulers of the elements.</note></term>, or whichever other of the aforementioned significators it may be. For if **Saturn** is the significator of the native's substance and is well-disposed and in good condition—free from impediments, fortunate, and strong, joined with fortunate planets, and in the <term>angles<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful positions in a chart.</note></term> or the <term>succedent houses<note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow the angles.</note></term>—the native will acquire substance and riches through the aforementioned labors or similar things, by lawful and proper means. If, however, he is impeded and unfortunate—that is, weak, <term>retrograde<note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually considered a weakening influence.</note></term>, or <term>combust<note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns" or obscures the planet's power.</note></term>, or joined with malefic planets, falling from the angles, and in poor condition—the native will gather substance through unlawful means rather than otherwise, even through deception, lies, and theft.

### ¶ When Jupiter is the significator of substance.

**If** indeed **Jupiter** is the significator of the native's substance and is in good condition—fortunate and strong, free from impediments—the native will gather riches through lawful and praiseworthy means. But if he is impeded and in poor condition—unfortunate and weak, retrograde or combust, or joined with malefic planets and falling from the angles—the native will acquire substance sometimes by lawful means, sometimes by unlawful; sometimes by permissible ways, sometimes by illicit ones.

### ¶ When Mars is the significator of substance.

**If** **Mars** stands as the significator of the native's substance and is in good condition and well-disposed—fortunate and <column-break/> strong, free from impediments—the native will strive for the acquisition of substance through both lawful and unlawful means; indeed, he will care greatly about how he might seize it. For he will say: "It is good to extort money from everywhere; a penny in the purse, a peasant in the ditch." <note>original: "denarius in bursa: rusticus in fossato." A cynical medieval proverb implying that having money is better than the welfare of the common worker.</note> If, however, he is found in poor condition—unfortunate and weak, overcome by impediments from every side—he will investigate ways of acquiring money through lawful and unlawful means: through robbery, highway robbery, arson, the illicit shedding of blood, and every way possible, not considering servant, order, or dignity.

### ¶ When the Sun is the significator of substance.

**If** indeed the **Sun** signifies the native's substance and is in good condition—free from impediments, fortunate, and strong—the native will acquire substance through lawful, proper, and famous means. But if he is impeded and in poor condition, he will acquire it by all means he can, not caring whether it be lawful or unlawful; yet he will know how to pass off his unlawful acts so they are not manifest, even though the malice will be apparent.

### ¶ When Venus is the significatrix of the native's substance.

**If** **Venus** is the <term>significatrix<note>The feminine form of "significator," used because Venus is a feminine planet.</note></term> of the native's substance and is in good condition—fortunate and strong—the native will gather substance and riches praiseworthily and through lawful means. But if she is found in the contrary state, he will usurp it through reprehensible ways involving lies, nor will he be ashamed of such profit.

### ¶ Concerning Mercury and the Moon.

**Concerning** **Mercury** and the **Moon**, it is not the same as the others. Whichever of them is the significator of the native's substance will indicate that substance is acquired according to the nature and signification of the planet with which they are joined. If neither is joined to anyone and acts as the significator of substance, it shows the native will acquire substance through the carrying of small trade goods and through short journeys. ¶ And always take care if the planet that is the significator of substance is joined with any of the planets, because the one with which it is joined will interpose its own qualities. For if the significator of substance is good and is joined with a good planet, its goodness will be increased. If it is bad and joined with a bad planet, its malice will be increased. If it is a <term>fortune<note>A benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note></term> and is joined to a <term>malefic<note>A harmful planet, like Saturn or Mars.</note></term>, its goodness will be diminished. If it is a malefic and joined to a fortune, its malice will be diminished.

## Chapter Seven: At what age or in what part of his life the native is to acquire substance.

**Finally**, it must be seen in what age or in what part of life the native is to acquire substance. It seemed to some of the ancient wise men that you should consider the lords of the triplicity of the Sun by day, and the lords of the triplicity of the Moon by night; to others, something else seemed correct according to the opinions that pleased them. I do not contradict their sayings, yet I do not absolutely agree with these or those, nor do I absolutely dissent from them. It seems to me, however, that whichever planet is more powerful in the nature of a thing is more powerful in the judgment of its effects. For the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance <note>The second house in the zodiac.</note> seem to signify it more effectively and more naturally than the others. Thus, it seems more appropriate that the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance be preferred over other significators in the indication of the times or the part of life in which the native or the petitioner is to have or acquire substance.

**For** if the first of these planets is good and well-disposed, it will increase wealth in the first third of his life; in the other two parts, he will be in need. If it is the second lord that is well-disposed, it increases wealth in the second third of his life; in the other two, he will be in need. If indeed it is the third, it increases wealth in the final third of his life; in the other two, he will be in need.

**But** if only two of them are fortunate, and the third is not, wealth will not increase in the third of life assigned to that planet; in that period, he will be in need. For if the first and second are fortunate, wealth increases in the first and second thirds of his life; in the third part, he will be in need. If it is the first and the third, wealth increases in the first and in the final third of his life; in the middle part, he will be in need. If it is the second and the third, it increases wealth in the second and third parts of his life; in the first part, however, he will be in need.

But if all are unfortunate, he will be in need for the whole time of his life and will always live in misery. And if another <term>almuter<note>original: "almuter"; the planet that holds the most combined dignity and power over a specific point in the birth chart.</note></term> is over the place of substance <note>referring to the Second House of the birth chart, which governs money and possessions</note> from the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance—namely, whether it is oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note> or not: because if it is oriental, it will signify substance in youth, that is, in the first half of the native's life. But if it is occidental <note>setting after the Sun</note>, it signifies wealth in the final half of the native's life. 

**From** this you may know from the beginning the significance regarding the acquisition of substance along with the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance. If indeed both agree in being good, wealth will increase in that time and will produce more than could be signified by only one of them. But if they disagree, it will diminish the significance of the better planet, and there will not be as much substance for the native as there ought to be at that age.

### Chapter 3. How other significators increase or decrease the native's substance along with the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance.

**You** shall therefore consider the significator of the native's substance, whichever planet it may be, and I will mix its power with the power of the lord of the triplicity of the house of substance who is the significator of the period in which the native is to acquire substance. If both of these are found to be good, wealth will increase then and in that part of the native's life, and it will become more abundant. But if both are bad, it will decrease in that time more than it would seem it ought to decrease, and the native will become more needy. 

**If**, however, one is fortunate and the other weak, the goodness of the fortunate one will be diminished. If indeed the more worthy significator of substance is fortunate and the other unfortunate, the goodness of the good planet will be diminished and a smaller quantity of substance will be signified. But if it is unfortunate and the other fortunate, the evil will be diminished and a smaller scarcity of substance will be signified.

**And** <term>Abu Ali<note>original: "aboali"; likely referring to Abu Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were translated into Latin.</note></term> said regarding the significance of the native's substance: if the lords of the triplicity of the luminary <note>the Sun or the Moon</note> which has authority are all safe and free from impediments, and are in the <term>angles<note>original: " angulis"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of the chart, considered the most powerful and active positions.</note></term>, it signifies the prosperity of the native for all the days of his life. And this is even more so and more strongly if the significator of that wealth is in the degree of the cusp of the angle; and the further it is removed from the angle toward the end of that house, the more his prosperity and fortune will be somewhat less according to the distance from the angle, diminishing degree by degree. 

**If**, however, the first lord of that triplicity is free and the second and third are impeded, it signifies the native's fortune and his prosperity in the first third of his life; in the second and third parts of his life he will be in need, as has been said. But if the second is healthy and the first and third are impeded, the native will prosper in the second part of his life; in the first and third, he will be in need. But if the third is fortunate, he will prosper in the final third part of his life; in the first and second, he will be in need. 

**But** if the first lord of the aforesaid triplicity is impeded and the other two are healthy, it signifies that there is impediment and evil for the native and his detriment in the first third part of his life; but not in the others. If, however, the second of the same triplicity is impeded and the others healthy, that native will be impeded in the second third part of his life; but in the others, no. If indeed only the third is impeded, it signifies his impediment in the final third part

<column-break/>

of his life; but in the other parts of his life, he will prosper. 

**And** if all the said significators are impeded, it signifies evil and detriment for the native and his poverty for the whole time of his life, and a diminution of life itself, just as was said above concerning the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance. Nevertheless, if with these misfortunes the "Fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> are in the angles, and the "Infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> are in <term>cadent<note>original: "cadentes"; houses that "fall away" from the angles, considered weak positions.</note></term> houses, and the luminaries are well-disposed, the malice of the infortunes will be diminished, and sometimes the native will prosper, nor will his life be diminished on that account. You can say the same thing if the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the angles, free from the impediments of the evils, or if they apply to planets in the angles; and this is better and stronger if <term>reception<note>original: "deceptio"; likely a scribal error for "receptio," an astrological condition where planets interact through their respective signs of dignity.</note></term> intervenes.

### When the lord of the Ascendant applies to the luminaries or they to it.

**If**, however, the lord of the Ascendant applies to the luminaries or they to it, and it is in Aries or in Leo, and the Moon is in Taurus or in Cancer when she applies herself to the lord of the Ascendant; or if the lord of the Ascendant is in its own house and in its exaltation when it applies itself to the luminaries; or if any of them are in two of their other lesser dignities when one applies to the other as was said—it signifies fortune and prosperity for the native in all times of his life, unless the lords of the triplicity of the house of substance work against it. For if the lords of that triplicity are impeded, they will take away something from this disposition; and his prosperity and fortune will be something less than this.

**If** the <term>Part of Fortune<note>original: "ps̄ fortune"; a mathematical point in the chart representing material luck.</note></term> and its lord are oriental and free from the impediments of the evils, and are in the angles, and <term>the Alchocoden<note>original: "alc̄is"; a contraction for Alchocoden, the planet that determines the length of life.</note></term> regards them, and the Fortunes regard them, it signifies the prosperity of the native and his durable fortune, and an increase in the goodness of life, and its firmness, excellence, and strength. And if the Moon is in her house or in her exaltation, safe and not impeded by the Infortunes, it signifies the exaltation of the native and the greatness of his name. 

**But** if the said significators are cadent and impeded, it signifies a laborious life for the native and of little use; and even more so if they do not regard the Ascendant. But if the good and the bad planets together regard the Part of Fortune and its lord, and they are in the angles, he shall judge a mediocrity of fortune and prosperity for the native. 

**When**, however, the lords of the triplicity of the Ascendant are joined to planets in the angles, and they themselves are cadent from them, they will signify fortune and prosperity for the native, but after labor and fatigue. Say the same regarding the lord of the Ascendant if it is joined to a planet in an angle and in its house or its exaltation, while it is itself cadent and in its <term>detriment<note>original: "defectiōe"; a sign where a planet's power is weakened.</note></term>. 

**Nor** indeed are these things true unless the aforesaid significators of substance work against them or any one of them; for each one will interpose its parts according to how it is disposed. If indeed it is well-disposed, it will increase the significance of the good things in a good way and diminish the significance of the bad. But if it is ill-disposed, it will increase the significance of the bad things in an evil way and diminish the significance of the good. Nor should you forget to consider how all the aforesaid significators are disposed; for if they are all well-disposed, the prosperity of the native will be increased and his fortune will be enlarged. If they are all ill-disposed, the prosperity of the native and his fortune will be diminished. But if the more principal significators are well-disposed, and the less principal are ill-disposed, his prosperity and fortune will be diminished and he will profit less. If however the principal ones are ill-disposed and the less principal are well-disposed, their misfortune will be diminished and will do less harm.

### Whether the birth occurred during the day or at night.
**Y**ou shall also observe whether the birth is by day or by night; for if it was a daytime birth, you will look to the <term>lords of the triplicity<note>The three planets that rule the zodiacal element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water) of a specific sign.</note></term> of the sign in which the Sun is located, as was said above. If, however, it was a nighttime birth, then you will look to the lords of the triplicity of the sign in which the Moon is located. If these lords are in <term>angular houses<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, considered the most powerful and active positions.</note></term>, fortunate, and strong, and if the "fortunes" <note>The beneficial planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> aspect them—and it is even better and stronger if the fortunes "receive" them—it signifies that the fortune of the person born will be prosperous and happy. But if they are in the <term>succedent houses<note>The houses following the angles: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th.</note></term> of the angles, it will judge his fortune to be mediocre. If, however, the "malifics" <note>The challenging planets, Saturn and Mars.</note> are in the angles and the fortunes are in the succedent houses, it signifies the poverty of the person born and his labor in the first half of his life, but in the latter half, his fortune and well-being will be good. If, however, the fortunes are in the angles and the malifics are in the succedent houses, it will judge the opposite of what was said before. But if they are in <term>cadent houses<note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, which "fall away" from the angles and are considered the weakest positions.</note></term>, it will signify his misfortune and that his life will be bad and laborious, unless the aforementioned significators work to the contrary.

### Who aspects the house of substance.
**L**ikewise, look to the <term>house of substance<note>The Second House, which governs personal wealth and possessions.</note></term>, which is the second sign from the Ascendant, and the second sign from the house in which the <term>Part of Fortune<note>original: "pars fortune"; a mathematical point in a chart representing worldly success and well-being.</note></term> is located, and the second sign from the house in which the Sun is located in daytime births, or from the house where the Moon is in nighttime births. And see if any of the malifics are in any of the aforementioned places; for even if the person born has other good indicators, this must signify a reduction of those and of his well-being. If, however, he does not have other good indicators, it signifies a fall from prosperity and the loss of fortune and a bad state, unless that malific planet has its own home, or its <term>exaltation<note>A specific zodiac sign where a planet's influence is significantly strengthened.</note></term>, or two other minor dignities there. And <term>Aboali<note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat (c. 770–c. 835), a famous Persian astrologer whose work was widely translated into Latin.</note></term> said that if the Sun does not aspect the Part of Fortune or its lord—or if the Part of Fortune does not aspect the Sun in daytime births or the Moon in nighttime births—it signifies losses to the person’s fortune and a reduction of his prosperity. You can see the same regarding the Moon if it is besieged by malifics in either day or night births. Likewise, the <term>Alcocoden<note>The planet that "gives years," used in medieval astrology to calculate the length of a person's life.</note></term> will signify the same if it is cadent from the angles or from the Ascendant and in a bad place from it, and in aspect to any misfortune. If indeed you find malifics in the angles, but fortunes in the succedent houses of the angles, it signifies the labor of the native and his hindrance in the beginning of his life, but prosperity and good at the end. You can judge this same thing if the Sun in daytime births (or the Moon in nighttime births) separates from the malifics and joins a fortune. Likewise, you may say this of the lords of the triplicity of the luminary <note>The Sun or Moon.</note> that holds authority: if they are cadent from the angles or from the Ascendant, but are joining themselves to planets existing in their own houses or exaltations, or in two of their other dignities.

### When the planet that is the significator of substance is oriental.
**I**f the significator of substance is <term>oriental<note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note></term> and above the earth, then it will signify the fortune and well-being of the native and his prosperity in the beginning of his life. If, however, it is <term>occidental<note>Setting in the west after the Sun.</note></term> and below the earth, then it will signify these things at the end of his life. But if it is oriental below the earth or occidental above the earth, then it will signify it in the middle of his life.

<margin>
Chapter 9: On the significance of the places of the circle.
</margin>
**T**he places of the circle <note>The astrological houses.</note> signifying those times are these: for the Ascendant and the second house signify the beginning of the native's life until the end of his adolescence. The tenth and eleventh houses signify youth until the end of the mature age. The seventh and eighth

<column-break/>

signify from the end of youth until the middle of old age. The fourth and fifth signify from the middle of old age until the end of the native’s life. And Aboali said the Part of Fortune signifies the beginning of life, and its lord signifies the end. And each of the aforementioned indicators signifies the state of the native in his own time according to how he himself was disposed in the birth chart of someone. When you know all the accidents and those things you perceive concerning the dispositions of his significators at the hour of his birth—when and in what time they ought to be prosperous and useful or fortunate, or contrary or laborious or unfortunate or sinister—you will look at the "direction" of the rays of the planets to the places signifying his fortune or misfortune. You will see the distance between them in signs, degrees, and minutes, and you will see at what times of his life good or bad things ought to happen to him through those indicators. Look then to the Part of Fortune, which you shall direct to the bodies of the fortunes and malifics or their rays; and when you see it joined to a fortune—especially to Jupiter or Venus—judge then that it is good for the native. When you see it joined to malifics—especially to Saturn or Mars—you can judge the contrary, unless the aforementioned significators work to the contrary. For when the fortunes or their rays come to it, and the significators are joined to a fortune or their rays, his prosperity and his fortune and well-being will be doubled. If, however, the malifics or their rays come to it, and the significators themselves are joined to the malifics or their rays, his misfortune and evil and labor will be doubled, and his goods will diminish. If, however, the Part of Fortune is joined with fortunes and the significators with malifics, or the Part itself with malifics and the significators with fortunes, there will be no doubt that the significance of both is diminished.

### From what cause the wealth of the native comes or is acquired.
**W**hether in these things that follow a native acquires substance, and by what means, must be seen further: from what cause he acquires them. And although this seems to wish to be similar to those things that have already preceded, it is nevertheless not the same as them, but something else.

### When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of Saturn.
**Y**ou shall therefore consider the Part of Fortune in the hour of someone's birth: if you find it in the house or in the exaltation of Saturn, or in two of his other minor dignities, and Saturn is joined to it or aspects it, it signifies that the native acquires substance from the cause of male or female servants, and men of middle age—that is, from fifty-year-olds and those older, up to the middle of old age—and from common persons. His fortune will be in them and in mixing with them; and its significance will be stronger if the Part of Fortune is in his exaltation than if it were in his house or in other dignities. But if the Part of Fortune is in the angles, his fortune will be extolled and he will be greatly exalted.

### When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of Jupiter.
**A**nd if it is in the dignities of Jupiter in the manner aforesaid, he acquires it by cause of mixing with and the use of great and noble men, also bishops and the like, and other wise men; and his fortune will be in them and with them.

### When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of Mars.
**E**t if it is in the dignities of Mars in the same manner, he acquires it by cause of leaders of the army and warlike and warring men, and those who delight in war and the exercises of wars; and his fortune will be in mixing with them.

¶ When the Part of Fortune is in the <term>dignities<note>Dignities refer to the signs or specific degrees of the zodiac where a planet has its greatest influence or "power."</note></term> of the Sun.
If it should be in the dignities of the Sun according to the aforesaid manner, he shall acquire wealth through association and interaction with kings and other princes like unto kings; and his fortune shall be found among them, with them, and those like them.

¶ When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of Venus.
If, however, it should be in the dignities of Venus in the same way, he shall acquire wealth through women and <term>eunuchs<note>original: "eunuchoz." In historical astrology, eunuchs were often categorized alongside women or those outside traditional gender roles as specific social groups one might interact with in a courtly setting.</note></term>, and similarly through effeminate men; and his fortune shall be found among them, with them, and those like them.

¶ When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of Mercury.
If, however, it should be in the dignities of Mercury in the same way, he shall acquire wealth by reason of association with wise men, scribes, and also merchants; and his fortune shall be found among them, with them, and those like them.

¶ When the Part of Fortune is in the dignities of the Moon.
If indeed it should be in the dignities of the Moon in the aforesaid way, he shall acquire wealth by reason of association with legal experts and men of the law; and his fortune shall be found among them, with them, and those like them.

¶ How the aforesaid things will be signified by the aforesaid <term>significators<note>A planet or point in a chart that "signifies" or represents a specific area of life, such as wealth or health.</note></term>, in whatever way they are disposed.
And know that whatever may be the state of the aforesaid significators, and wherever the Part of Fortune may be in their dignities, the things which have been said will be signified naturally according to their disposition and according to their places in the <term>circle<note>original: "circulo," referring to the zodiac or the astrological wheel.</note></term>. For if they should be in the <term>angles<note>The most powerful houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note></term>, in a good state, and otherwise well-disposed, then the Part of Fortune will signify an increase in fortune and prosperity for the person born. If, however, they are in the <term>succedent houses<note>The houses following the angles: 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th.</note></term>, they will signify a mediocre fortune for the person born. If indeed they should be in <term>cadent houses<note>The weakest houses: 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th.</note></term> or otherwise ill-disposed, it will signify for the person born a fortune of labor, hardship, impediment, and decrease.

### ¶ Chapter 10: Regarding the same method, according to Aboali.

There is also another method which is said by some to be similar to the above, although not simply for knowing the state of life of someone born throughout the various times <note>ages or phases of life</note> as signified by the lords of the <term>triplicity<note>The three planets that rule the zodiacal element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water) of a specific sign.</note></term> of the <term>Ascendant<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term>. For the first lord of that triplicity signifies the beginning of the life of the person born—that is, the first third part of it. The second lord signifies the middle—that is, the second third part of it. The third lord signifies the end—that is, the final third part of it. If any of these should be in its own <term>house<note>The zodiac sign where a planet is "at home" and most comfortable.</note></term> or in its <term>exaltation<note>A sign where a planet’s influence is heightened and honored.</note></term>, or in two of its other dignities in the angles, then that "fortune" <note>benefic planet</note>, being free from impediments, signifies a good and prosperous state for the person born during the times of its signification. If, however, it should be in the succedent houses, his state will be somewhat below this. But if it should be in cadent houses, it signifies his state to be much below this. And if any of them should be "falling" from the angles, or in its <term>fall<note>original: "casu," the sign opposite the exaltation, where the planet is weakened.</note></term>, or in its descent, or in a bad place relative to the Ascendant, or if it should be <term>retrograde<note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually signaling delays.</note></term>, <term>peregrine<note>A planet with no essential dignity, like a traveler in a foreign land.</note></term>, <term>combust<note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns up" its power.</note></term>, or joined with the "malifics" <note>Saturn or Mars</note>, it signifies a bad state for the person born and his impediment during the times of its signification; but in the cadent houses, this will increase even more. Again, the impediment will increase more and more strongly if the lord of the Ascendant is impeded along with the first lord of the said triplicity; or the lord of the tenth house with the second lord; or the lord of the seventh house with the third lord. ¶ If, however, the first lord of the said triplicity is impeded and the lord of the Ascendant is "safe" <note>well-aspected and strong</note>, or vice versa, the misfortune of the impeded one and the fortune of the safe one shall be diminished. ¶ If indeed the second lord is impeded and the lord of the tenth is safe, and vice versa, the misfortune of the impeded one and the fortune of the safe one shall be diminished. ¶ And if the third lord is impeded and the lord of the seventh is safe, or on the contrary, it diminishes the misfortune of the impeded one and the fortune of the safe one. But if all should be safe, their fortune will be increased and the fortune of the person born will prosper. If, however, they are impeded, his misfortune will increase and

<column-break/>

his state will be evil. ¶ You shall also observe the Moon, for she has a great significance over the state of fortune of any person born; for if she is in a good state and well-disposed, joined with the "fortunes," she signifies generally for the prosperity and fortune of any person born, adding to the goodness of the good and taking away from the malice of the evil. If indeed she is joined with the "malifics," she signifies adversity for the person born and his evil state, adding to the malice of the evil and taking away from the goodness of the good. And if she should be <term>void of course<note>original: "vacua cursu." But if you see the opposite arrangement, you may judge the opposite.

### ¶ Chapter 11: Another somewhat extraordinary [chapter] concerning the condition of the birth.

[This is judged] through the lord of the Ascendant of that birth and through his place in the houses, according to which of them you find him in. For if he should be in the **first house**, it signifies that the person born will be powerful among his relatives, household, and acquaintances, and born among them <note>high-born within his own social circle</note>. If indeed he should be in the **second**, and is in a good state and well-disposed, joined with the fortunes and "received" <note>An astrological relationship where one planet welcomes another into its dignities.</note>, it signifies him to be fortunate in the acquisition of wealth. But if he should be in the opposite of the aforesaid state, you shall judge the opposite: that he will be a future destroyer of wealth. If, however, he should be in the **third**, it signifies him to be fortunate among his brothers; indeed, he will be very fortunate, because of which he will gladly travel on short journeys, and sometimes moderate ones. But if he should be in the **fourth**, it signifies him not to be malicious, and that he will be loved by his father and will follow the good of his elder ancestors. If he should be in the **fifth**, it signifies that he will rejoice in children and because of them, and will be loved by men in a good way. Similarly, if he should be in the **sixth**, it signifies that he will be a laborious man, involving himself in worries, and will have many infirmities. In the **seventh**, it signifies that he will be a man of many quarrels <note>original: "riraz" likely for "rixarum"</note>, irascible, a maker of causes <note>lawsuits</note>, allowing himself to be dragged here and there by women, obeying their will. But if he should be in the **eighth**, it signifies that he will be faint-hearted, a deceiver, guileful, and sad; not caring for others, rejoicing in the misfortunes of others, and grieving at their prosperity. If indeed he should be in the **ninth**, it signifies that he will be a man of the sciences and a lover of them; he will also be a man of many pilgrimages and especially a lover of traveling on long journeys. If, however, he should be in the **tenth**, he will be a man gladly having interaction with kings and magnates and those who are fit for a kingdom, wishing to lead his life with them. If indeed he should be in the **eleventh**, it signifies that he will be a well-mannered man of good habits, beloved by men, among whom he will count many friends, but having few children. Finally, if he should be in the **twelfth**, it signifies that his life will be heavy, laborious, and impeded; and he will be able to count many enemies, but no friends—or if some, yet very few.

### ¶ Chapter 12: Regarding the acquisition of wealth, again according to Aboali.

Another method of the acquisition of wealth for the person born according to the opinion of Aboali, tending toward a similar end: for he said that the **second house** from the Ascendant must be observed, and it must be seen which planets are in it. For if "fortunes" should be in it, and the "malifics" are absent, as is their aspect, and its lord is free...

And if [Jupiter] is in a good place from the ascendant and similarly from the Sun, it signifies the **fortune** of the native himself along with **wealth** and in wealth. You should also look at the Lord of the Ascendant and similarly at Jupiter; for if one of them is joined to the other by body or by aspect, and they are fortunate, strong, good, and well-disposed, it signifies prosperity of the native's life and much acquisition of wealth: and this is all the more powerful if the application of one to the other is <term>received<note>Reception occurs when one planet is in a sign or dignity ruled by the planet it is aspecting, creating a "hospitable" relationship between them.</note></term>. If, however, their state is not such as I have said, their significance will be below what has been stated, according to the quantity of the decrease of their strength and goodness. 

The same can be said regarding the **Part of Fortune** and its Lord, if they are in good places from the ascendant, free from malefics and from their rays. Similarly regarding the Moon, if she is in a good place from the ascendant beholding it, and Mars, if she is received: and this is stronger and better if the reception is from a benefic. For the Moon has this prerogative: that if she is in the angles or in their succedents, increased in light and number, and commits her virtue or disposition to a planet receiving her, it signifies the goodness of the native's fortune and a multitude of goods and an abundance flowing and coming to him. 

Look also at the **eleventh sign** from the sign in which the Part of Fortune is located: in which if there is another benefic, it signifies the honesty of the native's acquisition of wealth and his good manner of acquiring it. You shall also see whether the Lord of Wealth, or the Lord of the sign in which the Part of Fortune is, or the Lord of the 11th sign from the sign in which the Part of Fortune is, enters into <term>combustion<note>Combustion occurs when a planet is very close to the Sun, which was thought to "burn up" or hide the planet's power.</note></term>: because this signifies the lessening of the native's fortune and prosperity and his wealth, and similarly his well-being. You shall similarly look whether the Part of Fortune is joined with another of the benefics, or is in their opposition or square aspect, and the malefics are cadent from it: because this signifies good fortune and prosperity for the native, and an increase of his wealth. But if it should be the contrary, you can rightly judge accordingly. 

You shall also consider whether the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Wealth are joined or apply themselves together, because this signifies the good of the native. If, however, they are not joined together by body or by aspect, and the benefics are cadent from the ascendant and from the house of wealth and from their lords, it signifies detriment to the native and his ill-being, and his laborious and grieving life and poverty in all times of his life: because the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the second house do not join nor apply together, which naturally signify the gain 

<column-break/>

of the native and his profit. ¶ These things which have been said will happen just as I have told you, unless the aforesaid significators of the native’s substance work to the contrary, which are the lords of the <term>triplicity<note>The three zodiac signs associated with one of the four elements (Fire, Earth, Air, Water). Each triplicity had specific planetary rulers.</note></term> of the house of substance; the lords of the triplicity of the luminary whose authority the Part of Fortune follows; and its lord; Jupiter similarly; and its part. For if you find these significators, or the greater part of them, in good places from the ascendant, and especially the more authoritative of them and those who have more dignities in the places where they are, they will work against the malice of the aforesaid, namely, the planets which were in the 11th sign from the sign of the Part of Fortune, the Lord of the Part of Fortune, and the planets to which they are joined, or to whose conjunction they go, or in whose opposition or square aspect they were. If, however, you find them impeded in the places where they are, they will work against their goodness by detracting from them.

### Chapter 13. Concerning the same.

You shall further see the Lord of the House of Wealth, or the planet which is the <term>Almuten<note>The planet that holds the most combined dignities (power) in a specific degree or house of the zodiac.</note></term> over the native's wealth, and consider where it is. 
For if it is in the **first [house]**, it signifies that the native will acquire wealth without labor, exhaustion, or worry: and this is more powerful and abundant if it is received by a benefic existing in an angle or succedent. 
And Aboali said: if it is in the **second**, it will be from the native's own property. 
And if it is in the **third**, it signifies the malice of brothers. 
And if it is in the **fourth**, it signifies the well-being of the fathers and the advancement of the house in which he was. 
And if it is in the **fifth**, he said that he will have children known in the palaces of kings. 
And if it is in the **sixth**, it signifies the flight of servants and the loss of small animals. 
And if it is in the **seventh**, it signifies the perversion of things from injustice and the scattering of wealth with women through strife. 
And if it is in the **eight**, it signifies the acquisition of things from the remains of the dead; nor will he care how he profits or how he spends them. 
And if it is in the **ninth**, it signifies acquisition by reason of pilgrimages and religions from sects. And he said that he will not care except for hidden things, and his business will be from pilgrimages. 
And if it is in the **tenth**, he will obtain wealth from kings and through their affairs. 
And if it is in the **eleventh**, he will find wealth from friends and businesses and loans and from merchandise. 
And if it is in the **twelfth**, it signifies that he will gain money from prisons and hidden enemies and from every vile and shameful work. And he said that he will be a thief and a robber.

## Concerning the third house.

### Chapter two: on the masculinity and femininity of siblings.

Look further at the aforesaid places, whether they are **masculine signs** and the significators are in masculine signs: for these will signify that the greater part of the siblings will be of the male sex. If, however, the aforesaid places and the aforesaid significators, or the greater part of them, are in feminine signs, they will signify that the greater part of the siblings will be of the female sex. But if they are in signs signifying **few children**—which are **Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Capricorn, and Aquarius**—they signify that there will be a scarcity of siblings for the native; the other signs show a moderate amount. If the House of Siblings is a <term>common sign<note>original: "signum cōmune"; also known as "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which suggest plurality or change.</note></term> and its lord is in a common and masculine sign, it signifies the native has siblings from the same father only. If, however, both signs are masculine, it signifies they are males; if both are feminine signs, it signifies they are females. If indeed one is masculine and the other feminine, it signifies they are both males and females. But if the House of Siblings is a feminine sign and its lord is in a feminine sign, it signifies the native has siblings from the same mother only. If, along with this, **Venus** and the **Moon** are in feminine signs, it signifies females only. If indeed the Moon is in a masculine sign and Venus in a feminine sign, or vice versa, he shall judge that the native has both males and females. This is even more the case if the ascendant is among the signs signifying many children and the Moon is in one of them. And I also say that if the ascendant and the House of Siblings are masculine signs (or one of them) and their lords (or one of them, or the lord of the fourth house) are in them, and Venus and the Moon are in feminine signs (or vice versa), it signifies that those siblings will be born from the same father and from the same mother. You shall also look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Siblings, whether they agree with each other or are from among planets that love each other; for if it is so, or if they aspect each other from a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies that

Likewise, look at the Lord of the House of Siblings to see if he is **combust** or has entered into <term>combustion<note>When a planet is within roughly 8.5 degrees of the Sun, it is said to be "burnt," making its influence weak or hidden.</note></term> in nocturnal births: for it signifies a scarcity of siblings and their detriment and destruction; and even more strongly if the Moon separates from **Saturn** while he is in an <term>angle<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful positions in a chart.</note></term>, or from **Mars** in diurnal births while he is likewise staying in an angle. And Umar said: look at the lords of the triplicity of Mars—namely the first, second, and third—and see which of them is stronger and of better condition: for that one has the significance of the matter of the siblings: for the first signifies the older siblings, the second the middle ones, and the third the younger ones. You shall also look at the Lord of the **Part of Fortune**: for if he is with the Part of Fortune, it will signify that the older siblings will hate each other.

### Chapter four on the matter of siblings.

Ptolemy indeed is of the opinion that the matter of siblings is governed by the matter of the mother, making mention of siblings from the same mother; nor did he care to make mention of those from the same father, because we are more certain that siblings are from the same mother than from the same father: though sometimes it happens not to be so, it is generally believed to be the case. It was Ptolemy’s wish that the eleventh house signifies the mother, just as the tenth does; and because the third house from the Ascendant is the fifth from the eleventh—which signifies the mother just as the tenth does—therefore the third is the house given to the siblings of the person born and the children of the same mother, because it is the fifth from the eleventh. ¶ One must consider the tenth and eleventh houses: if fortunes are found in them or in either of them, he shall judge a multitude of siblings and their prosperity. If, however, malefics are present, he will undoubtedly pronounce the opposite of what was said. If Jupiter is in them, you may say without a grain of doubt—or Venus by day, or the Moon by night, as both have a cause to signify the mother. If indeed Saturn should aspect from a <term>trine<note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>An aspect of 60 degrees, considered helpful.</note></term> and they are fortunate and strong, they will signify a "goodly" nature and a good number of siblings: yet it will be less than previously predicted, nor will their prosperity be as great. If indeed they are poorly disposed and remain in the predicted places, or aspect from a <term>quartile<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, often signifying friction.</note></term> or an <term>opposition<note>An aspect of 180 degrees, usually considered challenging.</note></term>, they will show a scarcity of siblings and their weakness; and they will be more prone to misfortune if they are "under the sun's rays" <note>Too close to the sun to be seen, which weakens a planet's power.</note>. If indeed they or any of the infortunes are found in any of the angles—but most strongly in the Ascendant—Saturn will judge the firstborn, while Mars will judge a scarcity and evil state for those born later. And Mars, for the most part, will shorten their number through death. And although I have touched upon this same thing for you above, I say it again: if the planets that are significators of siblings are well-disposed and aspect the place of siblings from a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies that the siblings of the person born will be virtuous and powerful, and exalted among other men. If, however, those significators of siblings are in the opposite state, the siblings will be found to be weak and powerless. If several infortunes impede the significators of the siblings, they will signify the shortness of their lives.
