### Chapter five on the masculinity of those born and of siblings according to Ptolemy.

And Ptolemy said: the givers of males are the masculine planets in their mundane qualities—that is, in being free from impediments—while the givers of females are the feminine planets. And he said a certain word that seems ambiguous, though it is not: that if the signifying planets are joined in the figure and associated with Saturn—that is, from a trine or sextile aspect—the siblings will love and honor one another. If, however, they are not joined to each other, or they aspect each other from a quartile or opposition, the person born will be a bringer of adversity [to them]: nor is it useful to seek why the significators of children should act in the matter of siblings. And he said the <term>oriental<note>Planets that rise before the sun.</note></term> planets grant the first siblings, and the <term>occidental<note>Planets that set after the sun.</note></term> grant the last. ¶ And <term>Aboali<note>Another reference to Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat.</note></term> said: look at the planets between the Ascendant and the "angle of the earth" <note>The 4th house.</note>: if they are fortunes, it signifies that his mother will give birth again to children after him, and they will live. If indeed they are malefics, it signifies then that she will give birth again, but those born after him will not live; or if the mother conceives, she will miscarry. And if there are neither fortunes nor malefics, it also signifies that his mother will not conceive after this child was born. And Aboali said: look at the lord of the house of siblings <note>The 3rd house.</note>: if he is in the Ascendant or the seventh, say the person born has no siblings; if he is in the Midheaven, he has siblings older than himself; and if he is in the fourth, he has siblings who will be born after him. Again, I say to you: if the Moon is in the Ascendant of someone, separated from a fortune, it signifies the good state of the siblings of the person born, and especially that they are long-lived and have a good disposition of life. And if she is separated from malefics, it signifies their detriment and the approach of their death.

### Chapter six on the prosperity of siblings.

Look for the prosperity and goodness of the siblings according to the lords of the triplicity of their house: namely, the first, second, and third [lords]: for the first signifies the older siblings of the person born, the second the middle ones, and the third the younger ones. For such will be the state of the siblings as will be the state of the lords of the triplicity of their house at the hour of the birth of the one whose nativity you are investigating; and such things ought to be found. For if the first of those is in a good state and well-disposed, it signifies the good state of the older siblings; if the second, the middle ones; if the third, the younger ones. For if the first lord of the triplicity of the house of siblings is in his own house or <term>exaltation<note>A sign where a planet's influence is particularly strong and honored.</note></term>, or in two of his other dignities, or in an angle or a <term>succedent<note>Houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which follow the angles and have moderate strength.</note></term> house, and in a good place from the sun and the Ascendant, free from impediment, it signifies the good state of those siblings, and their good disposition, exaltation, and likewise their fame. If the second lord of that triplicity is thus impeded, [it signifies the same] for the middle siblings; if the third, for the younger ones, according to what was said of the older ones it will show detriment. ### Concerning the Fourth House.

### Chapter One: On the condition of fathers and their circumstances, and from which part of the circle it is determined.

Having provided the reasoning in the preceding chapter regarding the matter of brothers, it seems appropriate to me to subsequently mention the matter of fathers, and from which place in the <term>circle<note>The zodiac or birth chart.</note></term> the matter of fathers is to be taken. For <note>original: "aomar"</note> Aomar <note>Umar al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> says that you ought to look at the fourth sign from the Ascendant of the newborn's birth and its Lord; also at the <term>Part of Fathers<note>A mathematical point in a chart calculated to provide specific information about the father.</note></term> and its place, as well as at Saturn; and at the Sun during the day, or at Saturn during the night. We must look at the Part of Fathers and the sign of the fourth house both by day and by night. You will see the location of each of these in the aforementioned figure of birth and you will consider the <term>Almuten<note>The planet that holds the most cumulative strength and "dignity" over a specific degree of the zodiac.</note></term> of that place for each of them. Whichever of them you find to be stronger, work with that one first: namely, starting from the Lord of the fourth house, then the Part of the Father and its Lord, then the Sun, then Saturn, and finally the planet that is in the fourth house. For through the one you have worked with, you will be able to know the length of the father's life—whether it will be long—and especially for the firstborn, and more freely if the father's own birth chart is unknown. For the life of the parent varies in the aforementioned birth chart just as the years of the world and the birth vary through their <term>revolutions<note>Solar returns or annual updates to a birth chart.</note></term>, as was treated above in the chapter on the form and figure of the newborn's body. The strongest of them will be the one in an <term>angle<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful areas of a chart.</note></term>, not removed from the <term>cusp<note>The literal boundary or "doorstep" of an astrological house.</note></term> of the angle by more than three degrees before or five degrees behind, or one of the lords of the other four dignities of the degree in which he is located. After you have seen the length of the father's life and wish to know what the quality of that life will be, you shall look at the degree of the aforementioned Part and the fourth house, and the degree of the Sun or Saturn, and see which is more fit to be the Almuten, and <term>direct<note>A predictive technique (profections or directions) used to determine when events will happen in time.</note></term> it to the places of the fortunes and malefics. According to the quantity of years signified by the predicted Almuten, you shall declare the end of the life of that newborn's father, which will rarely or never disagree with what was signified in the father's own birth. You shall similarly direct every year to know the truth of the father's condition—to the degree of the father's <term>profection<note>An ancient timing technique that moves the chart forward by one sign per year.</note></term>, to the degrees of the fortunes and malefics—and according to what you see of the state of said year's profection or revolution, so you may judge the father's condition and the health of his body. In the knowledge of his dignities, sublimities, or honors: you shall consider the "leadings" of the Sun from the diurnal planets if the birth was by day, which is signified by the planets that are <term>oriental<note>Rising before the Sun.</note></term> to the Sun. And if it was a nocturnal birth, you shall consider the "leadings" of Saturn from the Sun specifically. If this 

<column-break/>

leading is favorable, it signifies that great dignities and great honors will come to the father. But if you find the contrary, you may judge the contrary.

### Chapter Two: On the timing of the aforementioned things.

To know at what time these things ought to happen, you shall consider the lords of the triplicity of the Sun if it was a birth by day; but if it was by night, you shall consider the lords of the triplicity of Saturn, and according to what you see of their condition, so shall you pronounce regarding the first, second, or third periods of life.

### Chapter Three: On the type of the father's death.

If you wish to look into the matter of the father's death—whether it be heavy or peaceful: consider the Almuten over the matter of fathers, specifically whether it is free from impediments. For this will signify that the father will pass away in his own bed; this is even more certain if Jupiter or Venus is found in the eighth house from the father's house. But if the planet is impeded, the opposite of what was said is to be suspected; and all the more so if Saturn or Mars is located in the eighth house from the father's house. For if it is impeded by Mars during the day or by Saturn at night—by <term>opposition<note>An aspect of 180 degrees, usually indicating conflict.</note></term> or a <term>square aspect<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, indicating tension.</note></term>—without the presence or aspect of any of the fortunes, and if that malefic does not "receive" him, this signifies a bad and heavy death for the father. If, however, the malefic that impedes the said Almuten is the Lord of the Ascendant or the Almuten of the Ascendant, it signifies that the newborn will kill the father or be the cause of his death. Regarding their harmony, look to the Almuten over the Ascendant and over the house of the father; if they come together and are in agreement, it signifies that there will be concord and benevolence between them, even more so if they "receive" each other. But if it is not so and they are in discord, it signifies that discord, strife, and hatred will exist between them. And Aomar said that you might then even say he is not a legitimate son. And if the Sun is impeded by Mars during the day or by Saturn at night, the father will fear that such might happen to him from that child. Similarly, if the Moon is impeded during the day by Mars or at night by Saturn, he will not trust the child and will always suspect evil from him. Aomar also reports that certain of the wise men said that when the Lord of the Part of Fathers does not behold the house of sons, nor does the Sun then behold the Lord of the house in which it is located, nor does the Lord of the Part of Fathers behold it, that newborn is not the son of that father; but if either of them beholds it, he shall be legitimate.

### Chapter Four: On the condition of the father and mother.

<note>original: "aboali"</note> Aboali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat.</note> said that you ought to look into the matter of the father in a diurnal birth from the Sun; if, however, it is a nocturnal birth, you must look from Saturn. And both by day and by night, you must look at the father from the fourth house, the Part of Fathers, and their lords. And Aboali said again that you must look into the matter of the mother from the fourth house just as in the matter of the father; and by day and night from the Part of the Mother and its Lord, which is taken during the day from Venus to the Moon and at night the reverse, and is projected from the Ascendant. If indeed you find the sign of the father and mother, or the lords of the signs in which they are, or many of them in angles or in their <term>succedent<note>Houses that follow the angles: 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th. They are moderately strong.</note></term> houses, and any of the fortunes is in the house signifying the father; and if the lords of the triplicity of the house in which the authoritative luminary is located are safe and well-disposed and in a good place in the figure of birth, it signifies prosperity and a good condition for the father, and an abundance of joy and cheerfulness. If indeed you see the contrary, you may judge the contrary regarding the father's condition, and the durability of his misfortune and infirmity. But if the Sun is in a good place in the figure of birth and its Lord...

## ¶ Chapter five: on the condition of the father through direction.

If you intend to know what the father's future state and disposition will be according to <term>directions<note>An astrological timing technique where one degree of the zodiac is equated to one year of life.</note></term>, if the birth was by day, direct from the place of the Sun and from the place of the <term>Part of the Father<note>A mathematical point in the chart representing the father's life and fate.</note></term>. If, however, it was a night birth, direct from the place of Saturn and the place of the Part of the Father, as you do when directing from the place of the Sun to the bodies of the <term>fortunes<note>Benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus that bring favorable outcomes.</note></term> and <term>infortunes<note>Malefic planets like Saturn or Mars that bring challenges or hardship.</note></term> and to their rays. For in those places they take on the significations of the good or evil accidents that are to come to the father after the son's birth. When [the directed point] reaches the body of any fortune or its rays without the presence of an infortune or its rays, it will then signify good occurrences, prosperities, profits, bodily health, and pleasure coming to the father. This is even stronger if the Part of the Father and the lord of the house in which it is located are found in <term>angles<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most active and powerful areas of a birth chart.</note></term> or in the houses following them. But when it reaches the body of any infortune, then it will signify the opposite of all those things mentioned: that illnesses, obstacles, and lowliness will happen to the father; and this is more so and stronger if the Part of the Father and its lord are in houses falling away from the <term>Ascendant<note>The "cadent" houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th), which were traditionally considered weak or hidden.</note></term>. And <term>Aboali<note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were widely translated into Latin.</note></term> said that the same is to be observed in the affairs of the mother: namely, from Venus by day and from the Part of the Mother; and from the Moon at night and the Part of the Mother. And he said that we ought to observe the degrees of the <term>conjunction and prevention<note>The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth.</note></term>, which if the fortunes behold, and the malefics are falling away from it, it signifies the father's well-being and his exaltation. If, however, the malefics behold it and the fortunes are falling away from it, it signifies his [the father's] utility. If both fortunes and infortunes behold it together, the father’s state will be mediocre. And he said that the sign of this conjunction and its lords signify the father's causes, while the sign of the prevention and its lord signify the mother's causes. And he said: look at the fourth sign, for if Jupiter, the Sun, or Venus is in it, or if any of them behold it with a favorable aspect, it signifies the mother's exaltation, high status, and fortune. And if any of the malefics are in it, or if it beholds it with a bad aspect without the presence or aspect of any fortune, or if the fourth sign is the house or <term>exaltation<note>A specific zodiac sign where a planet is said to have its highest and most dignified expression.</note></term> of the planet in whose house the lord of the fourth resides, it signifies the weakness and fall of the father and his servitude. But if that same fourth sign is Taurus or Cancer, it signifies the mother's ill state, her weakness, and likewise her fall and servitude. And if the Sun and Moon are in <term>moveable signs<note>Also known as "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which represent change and initiation.</note></term>, it signifies that the father will not be of the same nobility as the mother, but one will be of lower parentage than the other; and according to whoever is in the lowlier and weaker place, that one will be signified as less noble—for if it is the Sun, it signifies the father, but if it is the Moon, it signifies the mother. And Aboali said that the Sun by day and the Moon by night signify the father's affairs at the time of the son's birth; and the house of the houses in which they are located signifies that which will be of the father in the future. And when the significators of the father—which are the lord of the house in which the Sun is in day births, and the lords of the triplicity and its ex-

<column-break/>

-altation and the Part of the Father and the lord of the house in which it resides, both by day and by night—are in their own houses or exaltations, free from evils, and the fortunes behold them, it signifies the father's exaltation, sublime dignity, and the acquisition of wealth. This is even more so and stronger if the Part is supported and the lord of the house in which it resides remains fortunate and strong. And again, it is greater if with this the Part of the Father is fortunate and its lord signifies it; for by this it signifies that the father's fortune, dignity, and honor will be of great durability and constancy after the birth of that son. You shall also look at the health of the father, as well as his value, in day births; if any diurnal planet is in the <term>custody of the Sun<note>original: "in custodia solis"; likely meaning the planet is in the same sign as the Sun or otherwise protected by it.</note></term>, it will signify the magnitude and exaltation of the father's health, unless the father's own birth chart works strongly against it—for if it were so, the aforementioned would be diminished. But if they agree, they will increase. And if the aforementioned significators are impeded and in bad places, <term>void of course<note>A planet that is not making any major aspects to other planets before it leaves its current sign.</note></term>, and especially the <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon.</note></term> in these cases, in their <term>descensions<note>The sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where its power is considered at its lowest.</note></term> and <term>detriments<note>The sign opposite the planet's home sign, where it is "out of its element."</note></term>, it will signify the fall and impediment or detriment of the father and his interests, a miserable life, and the lessening and loss of his goods; and this is stronger if Venus and Saturn are in a bad state and poorly disposed. And again more so if Mars rises after the Sun or Saturn after the Moon, and the fortunes do not behold the Sun or Moon. And always look at the father's state by day from the Sun and the lord of the house in which it resides and the lords of its triplicity. By night, however, from Saturn and the lord of the house in which it resides and the lords of its triplicity. And Aboali said: know that when the Sun and Moon, the lords of those houses, and the lords of their triplicities are in angles, free from evils and impediments, it signifies the good fortune of the newborn's father and mother. And when they are impeded and joined to malefics, and are falling and void of course, it signifies the ill state of the newborn and his parents, and the destruction of their affairs.

## ¶ Chapter six: on the death of the father.

And <term>Ptolemy<note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer whose "Tetrabiblos" is the foundation of Western astrology.</note></term> said: look at the birth [chart] and direct it to the bodies of the malefics and to their rays by the degrees of <term>ascensions<note>A calculation based on the time it takes for a sign to rise over the horizon.</note></term>, giving one year to each degree. And if the ascending Sun does not behold [them] and Saturn does, direct him just as you directed the Sun. But if Saturn does not behold them and is rising, direct then the degree of the <term>angle of the earth<note>The fourth house cusp, also known as the Imum Coeli, traditionally associated with the end of life and family roots.</note></term>. Then look at how many years it reaches. If that which is reached is equal to the years signified by the planet which has the greatest dignity—by day from the Sun and from the lord of the house in which it resides; by night, however, from Saturn and from the lord of the house in which it is found; and by day and night from the fourth [sign] and its lord and from the Part of the Fathers (taking also [the years] near them)—it signifies that his father will die in that same year.

## ¶ Chapter seven: on the death of the mother.

And Ptolemy said: regarding the life of the mother, look if the birth was by day from Venus; if she is beholding the Ascendant, direct her to the bodies of the malefics and to their rays by the degrees of ascension, giving one year to each degree. If, however, Venus does not behold the Ascendant and the Moon beholds it, direct her as was said of Venus. If the Moon does not behold the Ascendant, then direct the degree of the tenth house. And begin in night births from the Moon, afterward from Venus, then from the degree of the tenth house. After this, you shall foresee how many years it reaches; if it is equal to the years signified by the planet which has the greatest dignity by day from Venus and the lord of the house...

### Chapter eight: on the knowledge of the years of the father's life.

**T**o truly know the years of the father's life, if the birth occurred during the day, you will see if the Sun is in an <term>angle<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of an astrological chart.</note></term> or in a <term>succeedent house<note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses, which follow the angles.</note></term>. See if the lord of the house, or of the <term>exaltation<note>A sign where a planet's influence is particularly harmonious and strong.</note></term>, or of the <term>term<note>Specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet.</note></term>, or of the <term>triplicity<note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element.</note></term> is aspecting it. If so, you can then take the <term>hyleg<note>original: "ylez"; the planet or point that acts as the "giver of life" in a chart.</note></term> from it, whatever the aspect may be. However, if none of the planets aspect the Sun, but the lord of the <term>face<note>A ten-degree division of a zodiac sign, also called a decan.</note></term> aspects it from a <term>trine<note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very favorable.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>An aspect of 60 degrees, considered favorable.</note></term> aspect, and it is otherwise in good condition and well-disposed, you can also take the hyleg from the Sun and direct the father's life. And the planet that is the <term>almuten<note>original: "almuter"; the planet with the most essential dignity/power over a specific degree.</note></term> over the degree in which the Sun is located will be called the <term>alcochodon<note>original: "alchocoden"; the "giver of years" that determines the length of life.</note></term> and the significator of the years of life for that newborn's father. And if the conditions described for the Sun are not met, then look to Saturn. If you find him in any of the angles or succeedent houses, and any of the lords of the aforementioned dignities is aspecting him, you can then take the hyleg from Saturn; the planet that is the lord of that degree's dignity will be the significator of the years of the father's life. If Saturn is not disposed as described, then look to the <term>Part of the Father</term>. If you find it in any angle or succeedent house, and any of the lords of the aforementioned dignities is aspecting it, the Part itself will be the hyleg. And the planet that is the lord of that dignity and aspects it will be the significator of the years of the father's life. <note>original: "aboaly"</note> **Abu 'Ali** said that if the Part of the Father does not meet these conditions, look to the degree of the father's house <note>the 4th house</note>; if any of the lords of its dignities aspect it, that degree will be the hyleg and the lord of the dignity aspecting it will be the alcochodon. If the birth was at night, you begin by looking first at Saturn, then at the Sun, then at the Part of the Father, and finally at the degree of the father's house. And **Ptolemy** said that if the <term>fortunes<note>Benefic planets, specifically Jupiter and Venus.</note></term> aspecting the Sun or Moon also aspect the <term>Part of Fortune</term> in births, it signifies that the parents' substance will endure and be usefully preserved. But if you find the opposite—that the fortunes do not aspect the Part of Fortune or either of the <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon.</note></term>, and even more so if the <term>infortunes<note>Malefic planets, specifically Mars and Saturn.</note></term> aspect them—the newborn will not enjoy the parents' goods, nor will they benefit him.

### Chapter nine: on the length or shortness of the father's life.

**R**egarding the length or shortness of the father's life, look to the days: if Jupiter and Venus are joined to the Sun or Saturn, or if Jupiter is joined with Venus and the Sun and Saturn are joined together by such a connection—whether by aspect or by body—where one receives the other by <term>mutual reception<note>When two planets are in each other's signs of dignity, allowing them to cooperate.</note></term>, and both are fortunate and strong, they will signify a long life for the father. If you see the opposite, you can judge the opposite, except that you cannot be certain <note>original: "ad vnguem," literally "to the fingernail," meaning perfectly</note> to the letter about the length or shortness of the father's life; however, one should fear shortness rather than hope for length. Similarly, you can know if Mars is northern from the Sun or Saturn, or if he is <term>oriental<note>Rising before the Sun.</note></term> from Saturn and <term>occidental<note>Setting after the Sun.</note></term> from the Sun, or if he is following them in the figure—that is, if one is in one house of the figure and Mars is in the next house immediately following it—and likewise if Saturn is joined with the Sun by a <term>quartile<note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful.</note></term> aspect or by opposition. If the connection is by trine or sextile, it will diminish the malice, especially if reception occurs. And if the Sun and Saturn are <term>cadent<note>Falling away from the angles; houses 3, 6, 9, and 12, often considered weak.</note></term> from the

<column-break/>

angles, they will signify misfortune and weakness for the father. And **Ptolemy** said that if the Sun and Saturn are in angles or in places ascending toward the angles, they signify a short life for the father. Yet this is not contrary to what Ptolemy said above—that when the Sun or Saturn are in angles they signify the father's life—because there he speaks regarding the hyleg, whereas here he speaks of the life *after* the hyleg, or some other detriment or harm similar or equivalent to it. This is even more true if they are in the first, tenth, second, or eleventh houses, since these two angles <note>the 1st and 10th</note> are swifter than the others. If they are in the 7th, 4th, 8th, or 5th, they will judge the father's life to be less short. But if Mars aspects the Sun from a quartile or opposition, it signifies the death of one of the two "winds" of the father—namely, a sudden end to life or a nearby detriment to his eyes. If the aspect is from the eighth house, it will signify death, especially if the eighth is Scorpio. If it is from the seventh, it signifies the aforementioned impediment, especially if the seventh is Virgo. If Mars aspects Saturn from these same aspects, it will judge the death of the father, or a fever of a very cold type, or mutilation, or burning, or loss through robbery. If the connection is from the eighth house, death; if from the sixth, fever; if from other places (except the 12th), mutilation; and from the 12th, loss through robbery or hidden enemies. If Saturn and the Sun are then joined by the aforementioned aspects without perfect reception, whatever house is the lord of that connection will be the cause of diseases, and they will announce the father's future death, particularly through cold illnesses.

->Concerning the fifth house.<-

### Chapter first: on children and their condition.

**A**lthough it seemed right to some of the ancient wise men to put the chapter on marriage before the chapter on children—because children follow marriage—it nevertheless seems appropriate to me to mention children after the account of the fathers. This is not without reason, as children are held as dearly as parents, and the house signifying children <note>the 5th house</note> precedes the house signifying marriage <note>the 7th house</note> in the sequence of houses. **Annuz and Baruth** <note>Likely referring to Al-Nairizi and another medieval authority.</note> said in the chapter on children (and it does not seem to differ from the opinion of Ptolemy) that regarding children you must look to the tenth house in the birth of any newborn, and similarly to the 11th, and also the 1st and the 7th. See if any of the planets or other significators indicating children are found in any of those places, which are: Jupiter, Venus, also the Moon and Mercury, and the lord of the fifth; also the Part of Fortune and the <term>Part of Children</term> and their lords. Or see if there are any who deny children, which are: the Sun, Mars, and Saturn. For if the aforementioned significators of children, or any of them, are in the specified places (or even in the fifth house) and they are fortunate and strong, and any of the fortunes aspect them from a trine or sextile (with or without reception) or even from a quartile with reception, it will be signified without doubt that the person will have children. This is true unless that significator is joined with any of the <term>fixed stars<note>original: "stellis liris"</note></term> of the nature of Mars or Saturn at the same minute. If they are weak, however, they will judge that there will be few children. But if no such significator is present...

### Chapter 2. At what age the native shall have children.

One should also consider, when Mercury signifies that the native will have children, whether he is joined to a planet that is <term>oriental<note>Rising in the morning before the Sun, associated with early life events.</note></term>; for this will signify children in youth. If, however, that planet is <term>occidental<note>Setting in the evening after the Sun, associated with later life events.</note></term>, it signifies them after youth. You may say the same regarding the <term>lords of the triplicities<note>The three planets that rule the element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water) of a specific house or planet.</note></term> of Jupiter: if the first is oriental, it signifies children in youth; the second in middle age; the third in old age. If all are oriental, it signifies children at any age, but most especially in the first 25 years. If indeed all are occidental, it signifies children after the prime of youth is gathered. Similarly, if the <term>Almuten<note>original: "almutez"; the planet with the most combined dignity and power in a specific location of the chart.</note></term> over the house of children, or Jupiter, or the planet in whose house the Almuten is located, is oriental, or if the Part of Children is in the <term>Ascendant<note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term>, it signifies that the native is to have children in his youth. For if that planet appears in the morning before the Sun, at a distance of three signs or more, or if the Part of Children is in the <tenth house>, it signifies children in middle age. If indeed it is occidental, or if the Part of Children is in the seventh or fourth house, it signifies that he will have children in his old age, and you shall judge the other houses according to these.
<note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat</note> <insert>Abu 'Ali</insert> truly said that if the Part of Children is in the Ascendant, it signifies children in youth; if it is in the <term>Midheaven<note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th house, the highest point in the chart.</note></term>, it signifies them in middle age. And if it is in the fourth or seventh house, it signifies them in old age; nevertheless, you may combine all their sayings, and thus by weighing them, you may judge more rightly and securely.

### Chapter 3. On the multitude or paucity of children.

Regarding a multitude of children, look to Jupiter and Venus, and you shall judge all their positions. For a paucity, you shall look to Saturn and Mars and the lords of the same, seeing their disposition. For a moderate number, look to the Moon; regarding Mercury, you shall speak as you see of him, as was said above. If, however, the aforementioned places are in <term>common signs<note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces; signs that often represent doubling or multiplicity.</note></term> (so long as they are not sterile signs) and the significator of children is likewise in a common sign, it signifies that the native will have twins, and of that sex which the aforementioned places or significators indicate. And if those places are in signs that signify children, such as the <term>watery signs<note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, which are traditionally considered the most fertile.</note></term>, which signify a greater quantity of children than the others, it signifies that the native will have many children. For if the planet signifying children is feminine and the place signifying children is a masculine sign, or vice versa, you shall announce that he will have children of both sexes. If the planet and the place are of the same sex, they will judge the children to be of that sex. And if the givers of children are in the aforementioned sterile signs, or if malefics are <term>elevated<note>A planet is "elevated" when it is closer to the Midheaven than another planet, exerting more power over it.</note></term> above them, or if the Almutens over the places signifying children are afflicted, they will strive to prevent the native from having children. If they cannot resist the native having children, they will never permit him to have more than one child; and the father shall see the death of that child, and the child will not live long; and if he does live, he will be unfortunate and troubled, and

<column-break/>

evil will find him. If, however, Mars and Saturn or the Sun are in the Ascendant, or in the 10th, 7th, 11th, or 5th houses, or if they aspect those places without the conjunction or aspect of any benefic to those places or planets, or if the Ascendant is a sterile sign and the places signifying children are sterile signs, it signifies that the native will have no children. And <note>Claudius Ptolemy</note> <insert>Ptolemy</insert> said that if the said <term>infortunes<note>The malefic planets.</note></term> are in masculine or sterile signs, even if benefics aspect them, they signify that he will have no children; because masculine signs are, as it were, sterile and deny children. But if they are in feminine signs or signs of many children and the benefics aspect them, they signify that the native will have a child with some personal defect which he will suffer; for feminine signs, like the watery ones, grant children; or the child will not be of long life, but short. But if in some of the aforementioned places signifying children there is a masculine or sterile sign, and in another there is a feminine sign or one of many children, it is signified that the native will have some children whom no one will affect with familiarity; rather, they will utterly abhor them, or the children themselves will be outcasts; and this will happen according to whether the greater part of them are in any of the aforementioned natures. For if the greater part is in masculine and sterile signs, or according to which of those planets is stronger than the other or elevated above it, or if they are more in number, or if they are in those places where they are stronger, or according to whether the greater part of them is oriental or closer to the aforementioned angles or moving toward them under the said conditions, then the quantity of those significations will be greater. And <note>Umar al-Tabari</note> <insert>Omar</insert> said after this to look to the sign of children and the sign of the Almuten over the native's affairs and the Ascendant: if these are signs of many children, the native will have children. If there is no concord between the Almuten of the Ascendant and the Almuten over the house of children, and if Jupiter is <term>combust<note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns up" the planet's power.</note></term> and Venus is impeded, it signifies that the native will be sterile without children; and this is to be observed in both sexes. And <note>Claudius Ptolemy</note> <insert>Ptolemy</insert> said that the particular matters of children can be grasped by estimation when we place the planet that gives children in the location of the Ascendant; for then we shall generally recognize all the particulars of the children just as we know them from a birth chart. <note>Umar al-Tabari</note> <insert>Alomar</insert> truly said to look to the planets that are Almutens over the house of children, whether there be one or many. If some or many of them agree with the lord of the Ascendant, the children will be good, just, and loving toward the father; but if the contrary is true, they will be hindrance-makers. And he said if the significator of children greatly hinders the Ascendant and its lord, the children will bring various hindrances to the father. And if they hinder the Moon, they will bring various hindrances to the mother. And he said if the significators of children are safe, the children will be saved and not perish. And if the significators of children are impeded, the children will rarely be in concord. Therefore you may speak of the Part of Children: if it is in the angles or the <term>succedent houses<note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses.</note></term> of the tenth or fourth, it signifies a multitude of them, as well as goodness and joy with them. If, however, it is in the other six houses, it signifies a paucity of children and also their death. If it is void of course, it signifies the death of the native's firstborn, or perhaps the mother will miscarry, and she will be saddened over the children or because of the children. And <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat</note> <insert>Abu 'Ali</insert> said that if the lord of the Ascendant is joined with the lord of the seventh, it signifies a multitude of children from concubines. If, however, it is joined with the lord of the sixth, it signifies them from his own foot-servants or handmaids. Look also at the lords of the triplicity of Jupiter, who, if they are in angles...

If it looks upon it from a square aspect without reception, it will signify children, but the significance will be much less than this. But if that benefic planet is hindered, or if a malefic looks upon the Part of Children—and even more strongly if that aspect is from a square or an <term>opposition<note>An angle of 180 degrees, indicating direct conflict.</note></term>—its significance will again be weaker and will indicate fewer children. If Jupiter does not look upon the Part of Children, and Venus is hindered by Saturn, it can announce the sterility of the native or very few children; and even more so if, along with this, the Moon is hindered. If, however, they are hindered by evil planets, or in their <term>detriment<note>The sign opposite the one a planet rules, where it is "uncomfortable."</note></term>, or in their <term>fall<note>original: "descensione"; the sign opposite the exaltation, where a planet's power is diminished.</note></term>, or under the rays of the Sun, he will have no children; or if he does, they will die before the father. You shall also look to the Fifth House: if a benefic is in it and its lord is free from the aforementioned hindrances, and it looks upon the Tenth House, it signifies the native will have many and well-disposed children. If, however, a malefic is in the Fifth and its lord is hindered, it signifies a scarcity of children and their hasty death; and especially if its hindrance is in the third or sixth house. Similarly, if the Sun or Moon are hindered by evil planets without the aspect of any benefic, it will signify a scarcity of children and a sudden diminishing of the native's offspring.

### Chapter 4. Concerning the timing of children according to Aboaly.

Likewise, Aboaly said, summarizing the aforementioned: look to the planet that is most worthy in the significations of children; if it is <term>oriental<note>Rising before the Sun.</note></term>, it signifies children in youth; if it is <term>occidental<note>Setting after the Sun.</note></term>, it signifies children in old age. And if it is in the Tenth or Eleventh House, it signifies children in youth; and if it is in the Fifth, Eighth, or Ninth, it signifies children in middle age. And if it is in the Fourth or Seventh, it signifies children at the end of life. Likewise, he said if the Part of Children is in the Ascendant, it signifies children in youth; and if it is in the <term>Midheaven<note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the chart, the 10th house.</note></term>, it signifies children in middle age. And if it is in the Fourth or Seventh, it signifies children at the end of life. Likewise, he said that when Jupiter or Venus arrives in the <term>revolution of years<note>A solar return chart calculated for the native's birthday each year.</note></term> at the place of the Part of Children, or looks upon

<column-break/>

it from a square aspect or opposition, it signifies that he will have children at that same time; but Jupiter has the greater significance in children. And similarly, when the year reaches the sign in which Jupiter or Venus was in his <term>nativity<note>The birth chart.</note></term>, it signifies children in that same year. And he said: look for the invention of children toward the father <note>meaning the child's relationship to the parent</note> at the planet that is worthier in the significations of children and the lord of the Ascendant; if one makes the other fortunate, it signifies their harmony; if one hinders the other, it signifies their discord and enmity. You, however, shall industriously apply your intention and discretion to this, predicting house by house and significance by significance. For all the things that fall into practice cannot be written down individually, otherwise, study would be reduced to nothing.

# Concerning the Sixth House.

## Chapter One: Concerning male and female servants, attendants, or household slaves of the native, and concerning smaller animals that are not ridden or yoked, as well as his infirmities and diseases.

Having spoken in the preceding chapter about children, it is appropriate in this subsequent one to treat and make mention of male and female servants, attendants or household slaves, and smaller animals that are not ridden or yoked, as well as the native's infirmities and diseases. For Aboaly said regarding the matter of male and female servants or attendants and handmaidens: you ought to look to the Sixth House and its lord, as well as to Mercury and the Moon. See if Mercury is oriental and in the Ascendant or in the Tenth, joined to Jupiter by physical conjunction or by an aspect in a <term>movable or common sign<note>Movable (cardinal) signs indicate change; common (mutable) signs indicate flexibility.</note></term>; or if either of the <term>Luminaries<note>The Sun or the Moon.</note></term> or any of the other benefics is in the 6th or 12th; or if the lord of the house of servants is fortunate and free from hindrances, joined to Mercury in any of the angles; or if Mercury is free and joined with any of the benefics or seeking a conjunction with it; or if the lord of the house of fortune is in a good place from the Ascendant; or if he himself is in the Ascendant or in the 6th, free from hindrances, fortunate, and strong, joined to any benefic—when this is the case, it signifies that the native will abound in male and female servants, attendants, familiars, and household slaves, and that he will have from them, for them, and by them good, profit, joy, and utility. But if Mercury is retrograde or combust or joined with evil planets in a <term>fixed sign<note>Signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which indicate stability or stagnation.</note></term> or seeking their conjunction; or if any of the malefics is in the house of servants or in the 12th; or if the lord of the house of servants is a malefic; or if it is retrograde or otherwise hindered by evil planets, or falling from the angles or from the Ascendant without the aspect of any benefic; or if what was said of Mercury applies to the lord of the house of servants; or if the <term>Tail<note>original: "cauda"; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of loss or drain.</note></term> is in the house of servants—this signifies a penury of servants, their scarcity, and anger, sadness, and inconvenience arriving for the native because of them and by their occasion. And Aboaly said: look at the inconvenience, hindrances, and profit of the native with servants by the planet which is worthier in the Sixth House, and the lord of the 6th, and the Part of Servants and its lord, and the planet that is in the 6th, and Mercury, and the lord of the Ascendant. You shall see if they make each other fortunate, for if so, they signify profit, goodness, and harmony...

## Chapter 2: On cattle and other animals which are signified by the sixth house.

$\P$ Having looked at servants, handmaids, and other matters in the preceding sections, we must now consider cattle and other beasts which are signified by the sixth house before we come to the infirmity of the native. Indeed, it was known to the ancient sages—with whom I agree quite familiarly—that the matter of cattle, captured pigs, and other animals, both bipedal and quadrupedal, which are neither ridden nor driven <note>original: "non equitantur nec fugantur"; referring to smaller livestock like sheep or goats rather than horses or oxen.</note> but are domesticated and tame, should be taken from the sixth house. Therefore, the sixth house and its lord must be observed; similarly Mars, and how they are disposed, and in what places from the Ascendant they—or either of them—are found; and whether Mars is <term>direct or retrograde<note>Direct motion is a planet's normal forward movement through the zodiac; retrograde is when it appears to move backward, usually suggesting a reversal or weakening of its power.</note></term>, for he naturally holds significance over the aforementioned animals. When he is in Aries or Capricorn, in the Ascendant, or in the 10th, or even in the sixth; and if Jupiter or the Sun is aspecting him from a <term>trine or sextile aspect<note>Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees that indicate flow and support.</note></term>; and if he is otherwise fortunate and strong, free from impediments, it signifies that the native will be fortunate in possessing a multitude of the aforementioned animals, and that he will follow goodness, utility, and joy from them and because of them. And even more so if Mars should be in any of his <term>dignities<note>Positions where a planet has natural strength, like its home sign.</note></term> and if he is in Leo; similarly, if the sixth house is one of the aforementioned signs and its lord is joined in any of them with one of the <term>fortunes<note>The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note></term>, or in their trine or sextile aspect, it signifies that he will have gain and profit from them, and that his usefulness from them will be multiplied. But if the sixth house is Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius and Saturn is in it or aspects it from an <term>opposition or square aspect<note>Difficult angles of 180 or 90 degrees that indicate conflict or hardship.</note></term>, it signifies that the native will be saddened and impeded regarding the aforementioned animals and will suffer losses therefrom; and more strongly in Leo than in the others, but less so in Aquarius. And if Mars or Jupiter then holds dignity in the sixth, the impediment of Saturn will be greater unless one of them aspects it from a trine or sextile aspect and with <term>reception<note>A supportive relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other.</note></term>, being themselves fortunate and strong. And <term>Aboaly<note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note></term> said that if there is any of the "beast" signs there, and the Ascendant and the lord of the Ascendant are fitting and joined with Mars or in his aspects from laudable places, the native will be a lover of beasts and will rejoice with them. Similarly, if the Moon is in the aforementioned places, it signifies as much as the lord of the Ascendant.

## Chapter 3: On the infirmity of the native and his disease.

$\P$ Since we have dealt with the native's servants and handmaids and his small and non-ridden animals in the preceding sections, it now remains to speak of his infirmities and diseases. For "infirmity" and "disease" differ. $\P$ For an infirmity is an accident or weakness coming upon and leaving the body. $\P$ But a disease is an infirmity or accident coming upon the body and not leaving. Therefore, you must consider that in the birth of any native, you ought to look at the Ascendant and its lord; the sixth house and its lord; the Moon and the lord of the house in which she is; and the planet

<column-break/>

which is in the sixth, if any is found there; also Mercury and the <term>Part of Infirmities<note>A calculated mathematical point in a chart specifically related to health.</note></term>, and the planet in whose house it is, regarding both the native’s disease and his infirmity. Similarly, you should see the <term>Almuten<note>original: "almutez"; the planet that holds the most combined power/dignity over a specific location in the zodiac.</note></term> over those places and especially over the sixth house, which has the significance of the native's infirmities and his diseases. If it is a fortune and there is a conjunction between it and the lord of the Ascendant—and even more strongly if reception intervenes—it signifies the native's health and his prosperity: namely, salvation from infirmities and diseases, and that his infirmities and diseases will be few and light. And <term>Aomar<note>Umar al-Tabari, a Persian astrologer and architect from the late 8th century.</note></term> said that he will be fortunate in animals, servants, and home-born slaves if the Almuten over the aforementioned places is a fortune or is joined to the lord of the Ascendant. If, however, the aforementioned Almuten is of an evil quality, and it is the strongest of the aforementioned significators, and is joined to the lord of the Ascendant or is in any of the <term>angles or succedent houses<note>The strongest and second-strongest positions in a chart (Houses 1, 4, 7, 10 and 2, 5, 8, 11).</note></term> impeding the lord of the Ascendant or the Ascendant itself by whatever impediment it might hinder him, it signifies that the native will be involved in and impeded by many infirmities and many diseases. For if the Almuten is Saturn, it signifies that his infirmities will mostly be from a cold and dry cause; they will likewise be long-lasting, such as <term>cancer<note>This could refer to the disease or to "creeping" skin ulcers.</note></term>, hunchback, <term>gout<note>original: "podagra"</note></term>, <term>epilepsy<note>original: "epilensia"</note></term>, <term>dropsy<note>original: "ypropsia"; an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid.</note></term>, <term>anasarca<note>General swelling of the whole body.</note></term>, <term>morphea<note>A skin disease causing discolored patches.</note></term>, <term>elephantiasis<note>original: "elephancia"</note></term>, <term>paralysis<note>original: "paralisis"</note></term>, and similar ailments that are incurable or almost incurable, or very difficult to cure. But if Mars is the Almuten and is joined with the lord of the Ascendant in any of the angles, impeding him, it signifies that the native's infirmities and his diseases will arise from a hot and dry cause, such as those which come from red choler or even from the blood, such as acute fevers, <term>phrensy<note>original: "frenesis"; a state of delirium or brain fever.</note></term>, and <term>abscesses<note>original: "apostemata"</note></term> which do not easily ripen. And Aomar said regarding the <term>azemens<note>original: "azemens"; certain degrees of the zodiac associated with "lameness" or physical disabilities.</note></term> parts that there is an inseparable accident when the Moon is in the ninth and Mars is in the eighth in a sign of "severed limbs" <note>Signs associated with the loss of body parts</note>; in the birth, some of his limbs will be cut off by iron. Similarly, if Mars is with the Moon in another quarter and the Ascendant is impeded by some evil planet, accidents will befall the native in the limb associated with the sign in which the Moon is, or in the left eye in daytime births, and in the right eye in nighttime births. And he said when the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> are in <term>conjunction or prevention<note>original: "preuentione"; refers to the full moon preceding the birth.</note></term> and the malefics are in the square aspect of the conjunction or prevention, and a malefic rises afterward, the native will lose the right eye from the Sun and the left from the Moon. Furthermore, if both luminaries are impeded by the square aspect of the malefics or by their opposition, or if they are in bodily conjunction with them, or if no fortune aspects them, he will lose the eye signified by that luminary. If, however, both luminaries are impeded, he will lose both eyes. And Aomar said if the Moon is impeded in a birth in any sign by the malefics without the protection of the rays of the fortunes to its <term>term<note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note></term>, the very limb which belongs to that sign will be destroyed. <margin>$\text{\small (manicule/pointing hand)}$</margin> And he said when the Moon is in signs that signify impediment in the eyes, such as Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Aquarius, it signifies an impediment of the eyes; similarly the Ascendant. And he said when the Moon is in Sagittarius, whether she is impeded by the malefics or not, an impediment in the eyes will happen to him, and blindness is feared for him unless a fortune aspects her. But if the Moon is impeded in Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius by Mars, it signifies a rotting of the eyes and their <term>lippitude<note>original: "lippitudinem"; a chronic inflammation or rheuminess of the eyes.</note></term>. And Aomar said [this] unless some of the fortunes aspect her. But if she is impeded in Cancer...

### Chapter 4: In what age these things happen.

And if the planet which signifies the infirmities is oriental <note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note>, the infirmities will occur in the first half of the native’s life. If, however, it is occidental <note>Setting in the west after the Sun.</note>, they will be in the last half of his life. And if it is in the Ascendant, they will be at the beginning of life. If indeed it is in the tenth house, they will be in the prime of his life. If it is in the seventh, they will be in the decline of his life. If indeed it is in the fourth, they will be near the end of his life. You should also look at the state of that significator, for according to its strength

and its weakness, the diseases will be weak or strong. $\P$ You shall also see if the <term>Part of Infirmities<note>A specific mathematical point used to predict health issues.</note></term> and the lord of the house in which it resides are free from impediments, for that signifies the native's salvation and health regained from illnesses. ### Chapter Seven: On the impediments of the soul and its infirmities and their types.

Having made mention above of the infirmities of the body and its impediments, it now remains to see and add something concerning the infirmities of the soul and its impediments. And infirmities and impediments differ: for the infirmities of the soul, as the astrologer primarily takes them, are two: <term>magnanimity<note>Greatness of spirit or high-mindedness.</note></term> and <term>pusillanimity<note>Smallness of spirit, cowardice, or lack of resolve.</note></term>. These two can hardly or never be cured, although perhaps sometimes some are cured from them; for the magnanimous person disdains great things as cheap, while the pusillanimous person magnifies small things, as is said elsewhere. Certain others are secondary, such as cheerfulness, sadness, anger, and the like, which are easily cured and removed from the soul and depart. But the impediments of the soul for the most part do not depart but are almost always inseparably within; as when the soul ought to be wise in equality and goodness, it is excessively "wise" so that it becomes deceived by that excess, or it is less wise than it ought to be, so that it does not know how to beware of doing evil, or it is more impulsive than it should be, or less timid. All these and similar things are impediments of the soul, and such that they rarely or never depart from it.

If, however, <term>Venus</term> alone is feminine, the woman will excessively fulfill illegitimate sexual acts and with anyone, so that she will deny intercourse to no one, whether the intercourse be deformed or against the law; men, however, will be effeminate and soft and very prone to sexual acts, nor will they prohibit anyone from illicit intercourse or from its shames, except that they will perpetrate it in secret. Likewise, if <term>Mars</term> is feminine so that <term>Venus</term> is not, they will perform the fornication and shames of these two sexes and illicit acts openly and without a blush of the brow, so that they will be cursed because of excessive detestation. <term>Oriental</term> positions in the figure (namely, from the <term>Sun</term>) assist the qualities of <term>Venus</term> and <term>Mars</term> in masculinity and detestation; and their <term>vespertine<note>Appearing in the evening after sunset.</note></term> quality from the Sun and <term>occidental<note>Setting in the west.</note></term> quality in the figure helps femininity and concealment. Similarly, also, if <term>Saturn</term> is with them, it helps them to incur horror, rot, and great shame—namely, for both the male and female native—because his nature helps each of these according to his custom. But if <term>Jupiter</term> is with them, it will increase the beauty and decorum of things and an appropriate shame. And if <term>Mercury</term> is with them, it will help the detection of things and the haste of future events, and the multitude and increase of their kinds.

->Concerning the seventh house<-

### Chapter one concerning the marriage of the native and his companions and his enemies openly opposing him.

Having made mention in the previous chapter concerning servants and smaller animals and the infirmities of the native, we must immediately see concerning the marriage and companions of the native himself, as well as his enemies openly opposing him. Therefore, in these matters, one should consider the <term>seventh house</term> and its lord, and which of the planets may be found in it—one or several—as well as the <term>Moon</term> and <term>Venus</term>; and also the planet joined to them and the planet in whose house you find her. And look at the planet which is the <term>Almuten</term> over those places or over the angle of the figure of the birth you seek and those succeeding it; and you will see if they are free from the many impediments that have been mentioned and are fortunate and strong. If they are then joined to the lord of the Ascendant of the birth, or its Almuten—all or any of them—especially the lord of the <term>seventh house</term> or the <term>Almuten</term> over it by a <term>trine or sextile aspect<note>Harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note></term>, and even more so if <term>reception<note>A condition where two planets are in each other's signs, indicating mutual support or cooperation.</note></term> intervenes, and if the planet itself is lighter than the lord of the Ascendant, it indicates that the native will marry a good and suitable wife with whom he will rejoice according to his will. If, however, the aforementioned aspect is without reception, or if it is a <term>square aspect<note>A challenging angle of 90 degrees.</note></term> with reception, it signifies that the native will marry, but his marriage will be much below the aforementioned quality. But if it is a square without reception, it will be again much further below it. But if the lord of the <term>Ascendant</term> is joined to the lord of the <term>seventh house</term> so that he is lighter than it, it signifies that the native desires to be joined with women. If indeed the seventh sign is <term>Cancer</term> or <term>Scorpio</term> or <term>Pisces</term>, or there is a conjunction of the lord of the <term>seventh</term> or its <term>Almuten</term> with the lord of the <term>first</term> or its <term>Almuten</term> in them, or from them, or any of them, it signifies the native will have several wives and will have a great abundance of other women. If indeed you find the contrary of what has been said, you can judge the contrary. For if Venus is then in an angle or...

And Abu 'Ali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century Persian astrologer whose work was central to medieval Latin astrology.</note> says: If **Venus** in the births of women or men is free from malefics and impediments and in optimal locations, it signifies a good and fitting betrothal. Umar <note>Umar al-Tabari, another influential Persian astrologer.</note> indeed said: If **Venus** is exalted above **Saturn** from the tenth house, the marriage will be in middle age, at a time suitable to himself, and it will be a middling marriage with fruitful children. When, however, **Venus** is in someone’s birth in a "movable" sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>, and especially in **Cancer** or **Capricorn**, it signifies the firm stability of the native with one wife. If indeed the **Moon** and **Venus** are opposite each other or in a "square" aspect <note>an angle of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</note>, it signifies evil and impediment in marriage. And if they are in **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Sagittarius**, or **Pisces**, it signifies that the native will contract marriage with more than one woman.

### ¶ Chapter 2: On the Manner of the Sexual Acts of the Native.

**Look** also to see whether **Venus** is in **Aries** or **Scorpio** while **Mars** is in **Taurus** or **Libra**; for this will signify an excessive abundance of the venereal cult <note>sexual activity</note> in that native, and impediment to his person and the destruction of his affairs for that reason. But if **Venus** is in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius**, and **Saturn** is in **Taurus** or **Libra**, or if she is in **Gemini** or **Virgo**, and **Mercury** is in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius**, and they are joined together with one seeking conjunction with the other, it signifies the filthiness of the native’s intercourse and his practice of the sodomitic vice <note>a medieval term for non-procreative or same-sex acts</note>; and he will take more pleasure in the filthiness of intercourse with men than with women.

If indeed **Venus** is in her own house or her "exaltation" <note>the sign where the planet is most powerful</note>, a woman will rise above that native and predominate over him—and even more so if the lord of the seventh house is "northern" relative to the lordship of the Ascendant. If, however, she is in her triplicity or her "term" <note>specific degrees of a sign</note>, she will predominate over him but much less so. But if she is in her "face" <note>a ten-degree segment of a sign</note>, she will predominate a great deal, though much less than before.

And Umar said: if **Venus**, the **Sun**, and the "Lot of Marriage" <note>original: "pars coniugii"; a mathematical point in the chart</note>, or several of the native's significators and the lord of the house of marriage are in **Aries**, **Leo**, **Libra**, or **Capricorn**—which are signs signifying foulness of intercourse—it signifies that the native will be excessive in intercourse with a shameful and foul excess. But if **Venus** is physically joined to **Mars**, or in opposition to him, or in a square aspect, and **Mars** is in **Aries**, **Scorpio**, or **Capricorn**, it signifies that the native will be shamefully abusing himself with foul intercourse; and more so if **Venus** is in a masculine sign, for then he will be defiled by that foul vice of the sodomites. If, however, she is in a feminine sign, he will be mocked by women. If the native is a woman and she is in a feminine sign, she will be insatiable and unsatisfied by intercourse and will become a harlot. If, however, she is in a masculine sign, she will abuse women and desire to rub against them, and will also delight in being bent over by men.

### ¶ Chapter 3: Who the Future Wife of the Native Shall Be.

**And** Umar said: When **Mercury** is the "Almuten" <note>the planet with the most combined dignity or power</note> over **Venus**, the **Moon**, and the house of women in their part, or over several of them, the native’s pleasure will be in boys and he will delight in playing with them. If, however, the **Moon** is "combust" and **Saturn** aspects her from opposition or a square aspect, and neither **Jupiter** aspects her nor **Saturn** "receives" her <note>a technical relationship where a planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note>, it signifies the native will not take a wife.

But if the **Moon** is joined with "fortunes" <note>beneficial planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> by a "trine" <note>120 degrees</note> or "sextile" <note>60 degrees</note> aspect, and she herself is of good essence and well-disposed and with "reception," it signifies the native will take a good, useful, suitable, and fitting wife. If, however, she is joined with "infortunes" <note>malefics</note>, you will predict the opposite. For if she is joined to **Saturn** by a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies the native's wife will be laborious, fierce, and rigid. If, however, it is from a square or opposition, it signifies she will be vile, fetid, and sodden. If she is joined to **Mars**, it signifies she will be unlearned, untamed, poorly understanding, unstable, and a devastator; if **Mars** is of good essence, it will lessen that malice. And if he is of evil essence, he will add to the malice and make her an adulteress.

If indeed she is joined with **Jupiter**, and he is not impeded, it signifies she will be good, suitable, fit, and wise and sagacious in managing household affairs. But if she is joined with **Venus**, it signifies she will be jocose, joyful, and very beautiful. If, however, **Venus** or **Mercury** is impeded, the significance will be less than what I have said. But if she is joined with **Mercury**, it signifies she will be well-studious, well-diligent, and intelligent.

And Ptolemy says: if **Venus** is with **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, or **Mercury** in those things which pertain to life, she will be of great benefit—that is, the wife to the husband; she will also greatly love him and the children. And Umar said: when **Venus** is in the houses of **Saturn** and **Saturn** aspects her, the native will be cold in intercourse. Similarly, when **Saturn** conquers and is the Almuten over the house of marriage, while the lord of the seventh house does not aspect the seventh, and the lord of the Moon does not aspect the Moon, and the lord of the Lot of Marriage does not aspect the Lot of Marriage, and the lord of Venus does not aspect Venus: then the native will not taste the taste of women and will not marry.

And he said: when the Almuten likewise is the victor over the Ascendant, the Moon, the Sun, and the "Part of Fortune," as well as the conjunction and prevention <note>the New or Full Moon</note> that occurred before birth according to what I have said, and several of the planets are in the "fortunes," the native will be effeminate and soft. And if masculine planets conquer in the aforementioned places in the births of women, the girl born then will be virile, as if she were a male.

But if both the part and the planet are falling and impeded, and the "fortunes" do not aspect them <note>an "aspect" is a specific geometric angle between planets that allows them to "see" and influence each other</note>, it signifies that the native will consummate a marriage with vile and unchaste women.

You shall also consider if **Venus** is in **Taurus**, **Cancer**, **Libra**, or **Pisces**, for this will signify that the native has contracted marriage with women close to him <note>likely meaning relatives or neighbors</note>. If, however, **Venus** is in **Sagittarius** or **Pisces** and **Jupiter** is in **Taurus** or **Libra**, it signifies the native's betrothal will tend more toward greatness than insignificance, and toward goodness rather than malice; and he will be praised by men with becoming praise. 

But if it is in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius**, it signifies the native is joined in marriage to an elderly woman. If it is in **Gemini** or **Virgo**, it signifies he has contracted marriage with an ignoble and vile woman, or a very poor one, or perhaps a maidservant. 

If, however, the planet that is the significator of the woman is "free" <note>unimpeded by malefic planets</note> in its own "house" or "exaltation" <note>signs where a planet is particularly strong</note>, it signifies he has contracted marriage with a noble woman. If it is in its other "dignities," it signifies he has contracted with other competent women. If, however, it is "received" <note>a state of mutual support between planets</note> and joined to a vile planet, he is not joined to one who is too much so. But if it is "peregrine" <note>having no essential dignity or "standing" in that sign</note> and not received, it signifies he has contracted marriage with a maidservant. 

If, however, it is in **Cancer**, it signifies the native will contract marriage with an incongruous and malignant woman, who will not allow him to rejoice or even to be at peace. Furthermore, when **Venus** is in **Taurus**, **Libra**, or **Pisces** and is in an "angle" or in its succeeding house, free from impediments—namely "combustion" and retrogradation—as well as from the conjunctions and aspects of "evils" <note>malefics</note>, say that the native has a good and apt marriage. **Saturn**? Because from there good follows, and more so if **Jupiter** then aspects it, and he himself is not impeded in any evil way. And again, more so if "reception" occurs between them. 

But if **Venus** is "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note>, it will signify a certain dominance of the wife over the husband, yet in the manner of cheerfulness, play, and dancing. If, however, she is "occidental" <note>setting after the Sun</note> or in **Virgo**, it signifies a lack of affection from the native toward his wives and toward other women as well, unless perhaps **Jupiter** then aspects **Venus**. 

But if you see her impeded—that is, retrograde or combust or falling—say that the marriage of the native will be delayed and will be characterized by heaviness and annoyance. If the Ascendant is **Aries** or **Scorpio**, and **Venus** is combust either in front or behind—that is, "behind" meaning after—it signifies the native will contract marriage with a sick woman, and with a hidden illness.

### Chapter 4. Concerning the time when a wife will be taken, the number of wives, and durability in general.

And know that the time of that marriage is when the [significator] of that marriage reaches the seventh [house] of the nativity, or 

<column-break/>

when his seventh house is the Ascendant of the "revolution" <note>the Solar Return chart for the year</note> of the nativity; this signifies betrothal in that year. Or it will be when it is signified by the "direction" <note>a timing technique</note> of the **Moon** to the planet that is the significator of betrothal. And if [the planet] is according to Albohali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century astrologer</note>, and if that sign is "movable" <note>Cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, it signifies the betrothal of several women. 

You may say the same if the **Moon** is joined to several planets in the same sign, or has reached them by a "trine" or "sextile" aspect <note>harmonious 120-degree or 60-degree angles</note>. If, however, it is a "common" sign <note>Mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, he will be betrothed to two women. But if it is "fixed" <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, or if the **Moon** is then "void of course" <note>making no further aspects before leaving its sign</note>, or joined to only one planet, it will indicate the native has contracted marriage with only one woman. 

Look also at the "cusps" <note>the starting points</note> of the seventh and fourth houses; if the birth is that of a man, and any of the "infortunes" <note>malefics</note> stand in them, it signifies the death of the native’s wife. If, however, it is the birth of a woman, it signifies the death of her husband. If it is "occidental" and "peregrine," joined to infortunes or in a "square" aspect or opposition to them, it will signify their swift death. 

You will also see in the nativities of males if all the significators, or the majority of them, are "feminine" <note>signs or planets classified as receptive/feminine</note>; for this will signify that the native will be vile, effeminate, soft, stupid, sluggish, and "moist," so that his bones will not be seen, as if he were entirely made of flesh. And **Aomar** <note>likely Albumasar or Abu Bakr</note> said that the life of such men is usually greatly shortened because of the abundance of "moisture" dominating his "complexion" <note>the balance of the four humors</note>. 

In the nativities of women, however, if the majority of these significators are "masculine," the woman born will be a "virago," almost like a man; for, except for her sex, she could be called a man rather than a woman. The life of such women is usually shortened due to the abundance of "dryness" predominating in them.

### Concerning the marriage of women.

**Ptolemy** said that we ought to consider the solar quantities in the marriages of women in their nativities, saying: we must see whether the **Sun** is found in either of the two "oriental" quarters—which are, as said above, from the tenth house to the Ascendant, and from the fourth to the seventh. For this will signify the woman is betrothed to a husband in her youth, or in her old age she will take a young man and not an old man for a husband. 

But if the **Sun** is between the Ascendant and the fourth house, or between the seventh and the tenth, her marriage will be delayed, or while she is a young girl she will marry an old man. If the **Sun** is from the beginning of **Aries** to the middle of **Taurus**, or from the middle of **Leo** to the end of **Virgo**, or from the middle of **Scorpio** to the middle of **Aquarius**, and the significator of the woman is "oriental," the aforementioned things will happen in her youth or with a young man. 

If, however, the **Sun** is from the middle of **Taurus** to the middle of **Leo**, or from the beginning of **Libra** to the middle of **Scorpio**, or from the middle of **Aquarius** to the end of **Pisces**, and the significator is "occidental," these things will happen in old age or she will be joined with an old man. And **Haly** <note>Haly Abenragel, an 11th-century Arab astrologer</note> said that if the significator is "under the rays" <note>combust</note>, it signifies she will have no husbands. 

But if the **Sun** is in a "fixed" sign, it will signify she is joined to only one husband. If there is some oriental planet in that sign, you shall announce that he will be a young man; and it is possible she will acquire another after him. If, however, it is "occidental," he will already be past his youth. If indeed it is in a "common" sign, you shall pronounce that she will have two husbands. If some oriental planets are found in that sign, you shall add another husband for each of them. But if they are not "good," they will signify fewer husbands. If indeed the **Sun** is in a "movable" sign, you shall judge the woman will have many husbands.
