# ¶ On what the future husband of the bride will be like.

You shall see if **Saturn** has then held a partnership with the **Sun** through a trine or sextile aspect <note>trine: a harmonious 120-degree angle; sextile: a harmonious 60-degree angle</note>: for that will signify a husband born wise, upright, just in his deeds, and diligent and hardworking regarding the affairs of others. If, however, **Jupiter** is associated with the **Sun**, this will signify a husband who will turn out to be humble, gentle, magnanimous, and of good thoughts. But if **Mars** is associated with the **Sun**, it signifies that the girl’s husband will come to be untamed, cruel, implacable, disobedient, and of evil thoughts. Indeed, if **Venus** associates with the **Sun**, it signifies that the husband will be upright, decent, very beautiful, and handsome. And if **Mercury** is associated with the **Sun**, it will demonstrate a husband who is hardworking and proficient in matters pertaining to human life. 

¶ If **Venus** is joined to **Saturn**, it signifies a husband for the native who is weary and who restrains himself from venereal worship <note>original: "a venereo cultu," referring to sexual activity</note>. If she is indeed joined to **Jupiter**, it signifies that her husband will be good, chaste, honest, and modest. If, however, she is joined to **Mars**, it signifies a husband for the native of a hot complexion, a fornicator, and one who will turn out to be gladly exercising and busying himself in venereal worship. But if she is joined with **Mercury**, it signifies that he will be prone to loving his wife, yet he will not be firm in his love, nor will he continue well in loving his own; nevertheless, he will love his children and will have piety toward them. 

If, however, the **Sun** and **Moon** look upon each other from a trine or sextile aspect in the nativities <note>birth charts</note> of both—namely, of the man and the woman—it signifies that the marriage which the native (male or female) has contracted shall not be dissolved unless this happens for a great cause. If, truly, the **Sun** and **Moon** do not look upon each other, or if they look upon each other from a "fourth aspect" <note>a square: a 90-degree angle of tension</note> or from opposition, or if any of the "infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note> looks upon them, it signifies that there will be litigation or separation in their marriage. For if an infortune looks upon the **Moon** in the man's nativity, there will be dissension on the part of the man. If, however, it looks upon the **Sun** in the woman's nativity, there will be dissension on the part of the woman. And if the marriage stands, it will remain with litigation, hardship, contention, and hatred. 

But if the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> look upon the **Sun** or **Moon**—signifying the **Moon** for the man and the **Sun** for the woman—the marriage will remain in pleasantness, joy, love, and health. If, however, the "evils" and "goods" <note>malefic and benefic planets</note> testify to the **Sun** or **Moon** at the same time, it signifies that the marriage will be dissolved (though not simply so) and after that dissolution, it will be reiterated and remain in restlessness and love. But if the "evils" look upon the **Sun** from a fourth aspect or from opposition, unless they receive him <note>a technical term for a planet being in the "dignity" of another, which mitigates its malice</note>, it will signify that the divorce will be with strife and similar atrocity, great ferocity, and likewise complaint. Wherefore, if **Mercury** then looks upon those "evils," he will divulge them, and then that divorce will fall into the rumors of the people. If indeed **Venus** is testified by those "evils," it signifies that the divorce happens through suspicion of adultery or the like.

## ¶ Chapter five: How marriage is perceived through the significations of Venus, Mars, and Saturn.

Look in this matter whether **Venus**, **Mars**, or **Saturn** are joined bodily <note>in conjunction</note> or by good aspects in a suitable mixture: for that will signify that the native (male or female) will be joined in a good, useful, and legitimate marriage. Because if **Venus** joins to **Mars** in a good aspect, and the **Moon** looks upon **Mars** or **Venus** from a favorable aspect, it will signify a marriage blooming with a young woman. But if **Venus** is joined to **Saturn**, he shall wed an old wife. And if the **Sun** is joined with them or with any of them, it signifies the female native will do the same with a young husband. If **Mercury** is joined to them, the predicted things will be made manifest and similarly will be di-

## Chapter Six: On what happens to the native from companions, and by companions and those participating with him.

To know the state of the native with companions and those participating with him, and what happens to him from them: Look at the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and its Lord, and the **Moon** also for the native; but look to the **Seventh House** and its Lord for his companions and those participating with him. To know what their future state will be in partnership and participation, you shall know from the **Tenth House** and its Lord; and you shall perceive the end through the **Fourth House** and its Lord. For if the Lord of the Ascendant (who is the significator of the native) and the **Moon** are in fixed signs, and the Lord of the Ascendant is a fortune <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> and the **Moon** is free and not hindered, it signifies that the native has companions with whom he will participate in a good and lasting partnership, but he will not gain much with them, nor they with him; nevertheless, their gain will be of some sort, namely, below mediocrity. But if it is an infortune <note>a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</note> and the **Moon** is hindered, it shall judge the opposite.

If, however, they are in common signs, it will signify that the native is to have good and faithful companions; he will profit with them and they with him, unless something else hinders; and it will turn out well for both on all sides, and they will repeat their business dealings again and again, and for the most part with utility and profit. But if they are in moveable signs, it signifies that his participation will not be uniform, but sometimes there will be litigation and suspicion between him and his companions, and similarly disturbance; after this, there will be reconciliation and durability between them. If there is an infortune in the Ascendant hindering them, it signifies deceit, fraud, and a cause for separation and a desire for profit arising from the native's side. If truly it is in the Seventh House, you may judge that same thing arising from the side of the companions and participants.

If indeed you see that there must be a separation between them and you wish to know what kind it will be and what its manner will be: Look at the **Moon**, which, if she is joined to the Lord of the house in which she is, or to the planet <term>Almuten</term> <note>the planet with the most dignity/power in a specific degree</note> in that sign, and he is good and well-disposed, it signifies his separation from companions or participants will be full of affection and with utility and profit. But if the Lord of her house or her Almuten does not aspect her, or if he aspects her but is unfortunate and ill-disposed, it signifies the native's separation from companions or participants through their ill will and through the suspicion which one has of the other, lest he deceive him and defraud him of his goods; and this is more powerful if those infortunes are hindering from below the earth <note>the lower hemisphere of the chart</note>; for then the bad estimation which one has toward the other will be the cause of their separation; nor will they remain as friends, but will treat each other as if back-to-back. And **Sahl** <note>original: "Zael," referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer</note> said if the fortunes are in the Midheaven, their profit will be multiplied; but if the evils are there, it will be diminished. And he said if the **Moon** is joined to the Lord of her house and a malefic is joined to them in one sign or aspects them, they shall not be separated except by death.

For if the said places and the aforementioned significators, or the greater part of them, are ill-disposed—that is, if there are infortunes in them or with them, or aspecting them...

## Concerning the eighth house.

### Chapter one concerning the death of the native and the accidents by which death is accustomed to happen.

Having made mention in those things which preceded concerning the life of the native, his substance, brothers, father, children, servants, and his marriage, it seems fitting to me in this chapter to treat of his death and its causes in sufficient ways. And although death is the final accident <note>in the philosophical sense, an "accident" is an event or attribute that occurs to a person</note> that can happen to the native, it is more fitting that it be placed in the **eighth house**, which is said by the wise to be the **house of death**. 

You shall therefore consider those things which occur to you to be considered: namely the ascendant at the hour of the birth of any native and its lord likewise, and its **Hyleg** <note>original: "ylez"</note>, and the projection of the rays of the planets toward it, and its arrival at the seventh house of the birth itself. For if death is signified as having to arrive because of the projection of the rays of the planets toward that Hyleg, or by its conjunction with any of the **killing planets** <note>specific planets like Mars or Saturn that are positioned to "cut off" life in a chart</note>, we must then consider the places in which the Hyleg is joined with the killing planet: for the cause of death will be the significance of that house in which that "killer" then falls, and even more so if such a conjunction or aspect occurred when the Hyleg arrived at the seventh house of the birth. 

You shall also look at the **Part of Death** and the planet in whose house you find it, and the eighth sign from the ascendant of the birth and its lord, and the planets which you find in the eighth or which aspect it, whether they be benefics or malefics. You shall similarly look at the **lords of the triplicity** <term>Triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> of the fourth house from the ascendant of the birth, and the eighth sign from the Sun if it was a daytime birth, or from the Moon if it was a nighttime birth, and the planets in whose houses you find them. If these conditions are met, the person born under this fortune will end their life peacefully and pass away in their own bed.

But if **Jupiter** is the Almuten over the house of death and is in a good state and well-disposed, it signifies that death will occur due to a liver condition, or **pleurisy** <note>inflammation of the lungs</note>, or a stomach ailment. It could also signify a **tertian fever** <note>a fever recurring every three days</note>, or **quinsy** <note>original: "squinantia," a severe throat infection or abscess</note>, or other passions of the throat, or heart trouble, or **colic** and intestinal pain, or any other illness arising from trapped "windiness" in the body. It might also result from **synocha** <note>a continuous, burning fever</note> or illnesses caused by an overabundance of blood. 

If **Mars** alone is the significator of death and is well-disposed, he signifies death by a tertian or daily fever, or by **frenzy** <note>original: "frenesis," a delirium or brain inflammation</note>, or **hemoptysis** <note>coughing up blood</note>, or some other sudden or unexpected death. But if he is ill-disposed, he signifies death by "the iron"—meaning a sword or some other instrument of war.

If the **Sun** alone is the Almuten over that house and is well-disposed, it signifies death by fever, or superfluous heat, or any illness arriving from an excess of blood. If he is ill-disposed, it signifies death caused by one’s parents, or by a king or authority figure, or some prince; or it could be caused by heart trouble or "heat of the stomach" ending the person’s life. **Aboaly** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> also says such a person may die in "horrible places."

If **Venus** alone is the Almuten over the house of death and is well-disposed, it signifies death from stomach pain or from over-indulgence in food or drink. But if she is hindered, she signifies death from poison given by women, or from "excessive worship of Venus" <note>a euphemism for extreme sexual exhaustion or venereal disease</note>, or from ailments of the stomach or liver, or heart trouble, or perhaps from excessive bleeding, or **fistulas** and **abscesses** <note>original: "apostemate"</note>—especially those born of "sanguine" matter—or from taking a poisonous potion. Beyond these, death may come from any other illness arising from the malice or excess of the humors.

If **Mercury** alone is the significator of death and is well-

<column-break/>

disposed, you can judge that the person's life will end through a true **frenzy** or through various pains coming from an overabundance of different humors mixed together. But if he is hindered, you can announce that the person will die from uncertain and almost imperceptible pains. If, however, he is joined with another planet, he hands over his role to his companion, and the life will end according to the nature of that other planet. It might also be a "maniacal passion," a loss of the senses, **syncope** <note>fainting or sudden loss of consciousness</note>, **phthisis** <note>tuberculosis or a wasting disease</note>, or, as **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century foundational authority on astrology</note> says, an overabundance of phlegm, or "hectic" fever, or any illness arising from excessive dryness.

If the **Moon** alone is the significatrix of death and is well-disposed, then excessive lust, or gluttony, or a disordered way of eating will bring about death. But if she is hindered by one of the malefics, her significance will be judged by the nature of that hindrance. If the hindrance comes not from a planet but in another way, the death is judged to come from seafaring, or hunting, or extreme exhaustion, or frequent moving from place to place.

**Aboaly** says that when the aforementioned "authors of death" are in their own houses or **exaltations** <term>Exaltation: a sign where a planet is exceptionally strong, even more so than in its own home</term> and free from malefics, the person will die among their relatives and neighbors. If they are hindered by malefics and are **peregrine** <term>Peregrine: a planet that has no "dignity" or strength in its current position; a "wanderer"</term>, the person will die while traveling abroad. If they are in **cadent houses** <note>original: "cadentes," houses that "fall away" from the main angles of the chart, often associated with weakness</note>, it signifies death by falling from a high place. If they are in their **descension** <note>the sign opposite their exaltation, where they are weakest</note>, it signifies death in wells, pits, caverns, or deep water. If they are also the significators of the birth, the person may die by being killed, perhaps by being strangled or even stoned.

There are other significators of death whose effects do not happen through the ways mentioned above but by a natural failure of the body; these are the ones over whom the planets signifying a "bad death" have no power. An "unnatural death" occurs when **Mars and Saturn** are both in the place of death, or rule that place, or aspect it from **opposition** <note>180 degrees apart</note> or the **square aspect** <note>90 degrees apart</note>. It is the same if they rule the place of the Sun or Moon, or aspect them in the same way. If other planets aspect these malefics, they will contribute to the death according to their own nature and the nature of the signs they are in.

The same happens if, while he is "oriental" <note>rising before the sun</note>, the Moon follows him while he is the lord of the house of death. If he is in **Leo** or **Scorpio**, it signifies the person will die from the bites of wild beasts. If he is in **Aries**, **Taurus**, the last half of **Sagittarius**, or **Capricorn**, it signifies death caused by domestic animals. If you find him in **Cancer** or **Pisces**, I can announce death by fish or creatures that live in water. But if he is in Scorpio, it signifies death by venomous animals, whether they crawl on land or swim in the water. If **Jupiter** is then joined to Saturn and is hindered, it will strengthen Saturn’s malice; it also signifies that the person will be killed by wild beasts on a festival or solemn day. If the Moon remains in the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> and **Saturn** is in opposition to it, this signifies that the person will die by imprisonment. However, if **Mercury** is joined with Saturn in the birth chart—and even more so if their conjunction occurs in the signs of **Leo** or **Scorpio**, or with the **Tail of the Dragon** <term>Tail of the Dragon: the South Node of the Moon, often viewed as a point of depletion or misfortune</term>—it signifies that the person will end their life because of poisonous or predatory animals. 

If, however, **Venus** adds her influence, it signifies that the person will be subjected to death by a poisonous drink given to them by women. But if Saturn is in **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, the first half of **Sagittarius**, **Aquarius**, or even in **Pisces** (as **Ptolemy** says), and the Moon is associated with him in the birth chart, the person will end their life by drowning. 

If the Moon is in **Leo** with the **Tail of the Dragon**, it signifies that the person will die from poison given to them in the form of purging medicines. ¶ And **Abu Ali** <note>original: "Aboaly," likely referring to the 9th-century Persian astrologer Abu Ali al-Khayyat</note> said that if the lord of the triplicity of the Earth angle, or the degree of the Ascendant and its lord, or the **Sun** in daytime births, or the **Moon** in nighttime births are hindered, they will complete their lives with a strange or violent death. 

If the significators of death are above the earth, or in the **Air signs** <note>Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius</note>, or if **Mars** is in the **fourth** or **tenth house** and the lord of the aforementioned quality is present, it signifies that the death of the person will come openly and publicly, perhaps on the gallows, or on some wood similar to the gallows, or in a place raised up from the ground. But if it is below the earth and in an **Earth sign** <note>Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn</note>, it signifies that the death must be hidden, or perhaps will occur under some falling ruins. 

If it is in **Fire signs** <note>Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>, it signifies that the person will be burned or die in some other way by means of fire. But if any of the **Benefics** <note>original: "fortunas," referring to the lucky planets Jupiter or Venus</note> are in the **eighth house** or with its lord, or in the **fourth house** or with its lord, it signifies that the person's death will come peacefully. However, if any of the **Malefics** <note>original: "infortunis," referring to Saturn or Mars</note> are in the aforementioned places or with their lords, they will indicate that the person will die a bad death. 

<margin>☞</margin> If that Malefic is **Mars**, that death will occur by iron or fire. But if it is **Saturn**, it will be from poison, or ruins, or a fall from a height, or a stormy flood of the sea, or some other drowning. 

If Saturn is between the 4th degree of **Sagittarius** and the 15th degree of **Capricorn**, or from the 20th degree of **Cancri** to the 15th degree of **Leo**, or if he is in **Aries** or **Taurus** bodily joined to the Sun, or if Mars is opposite him, or if Saturn himself is opposite the Sun, it signifies the person will die by the fall of some ruins. But if Saturn is in the **tenth house** and Mars is also in the **fourth**, or bodily joined to him, and if Mars himself is the lord of the aforementioned quality (meaning he is the lord of the house or the bound of the degree signifying death), it signifies the person will end their life by falling from a precipice. 

If Mars is in the **fourth house** from the Ascendant of the birth and is the lord of the quality of the person's death, or if either of the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun or the Moon</note> is opposite him and he is outside of his proper place, and if he is in **Gemini**, **Virgo**, **Libra**, the first half of **Sagittarius**, or **Aquarius**, it signifies the person will enter the gallows because of a quarrel or dispute among their kinsmen, or will not escape the cutting off of their head due to some other war. ¶ And **Ptolemy** said he will either lay hands on himself because of women or be killed by the hands of women. And he said this will happen when **Venus** again testifies to **Mars**.

But if **Mercury** is associated with **Mars** in the chart, he will be torn to pieces by the hands of thieves, pirates, or ambushers. And he said that if Mars is among "severed limbs," such as at the star **Algol** <note>original: "capite algol," a star in the constellation Perseus traditionally associated with beheading</note> or in signs of "imperfect forms," or with the **Head of the Dragon** <term>Head of the Dragon: the North Node of the Moon</term>, and Mars himself is the lord of the aforementioned quality, the person's head will be cut off, or they will perish due to the mutilation of some other limb. 

If the significator of death is in **Taurus** or **Scorpio** and Mars is present there under the conditions mentioned before, it will signify that the person will be deprived of life by some burning, or by cauterization, or other cuttings or perforations, or by the incisions of doctors performed as a medical treatment, or perhaps by a spasm. And if Mars is in the **Ascendant** or the **seventh house** and is the **Almuten** over either of them, and Saturn testifies to him from a **Fire sign**, it signifies the person will be cast into fire to be burned alive.

But if he is joined in the aforementioned places to the **Sun**, the **Moon**, or **Jupiter**, and they themselves are hindered, it signifies the person's death will be most wretched. And if they are opposite him, it signifies the person will die by the hand of kings or other powerful men.

# Concerning the Ninth House.

### Chapter One: Concerning the religion and faith of the native, as well as their knowledge, and likewise concerning their travels or long journeys.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'C' depicting a scholar seated at a desk in a study, wearing a cap and gown. He is consulting a book. In the background, a window reveals a night sky with stars, and various scholarly objects are visible on the desk and shelves.</image-desc>

**S**ince the preceding chapter sufficiently discussed the death of the native <note>The "native" refers to the person for whom the birth chart was cast.</note> and its causes, I believe it is appropriate in this chapter to settle upon their religion and faith, as well as their travels or long journeys. You must, therefore, examine the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, representing the self</term> in the birth chart you wish to investigate and see whether the lord of the Ascendant and the **Moon**, or the stronger of the two, is in the ninth house or joined with its lord. This signifies the faith of the native, as well as their knowledge and religion. For if both are as described, and are in a good place in the circle—especially in the predicted state of being good and well-disposed—and if the planet itself is a **Fortune** <term>Fortune: a "benefic" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring positive influence</term>, it signifies a nature that will adhere to a religion that is appropriate, decent, or lawful. 

Now, if **Saturn** is the significator of religion, it signifies that the person will adhere to a heavy and laborious religion, especially one whose followers believe themselves better than other religious groups and more worthy of God; these are particularly those who wear black garments. If, however, **Jupiter** is the significator of religion, it signifies that he will adhere to the religion whose followers are called secular clergy because of the liberality of that religion, such as bishops, archbishops, and others who lead the church. If **the Sun** is the significator of religion, it signifies he will adhere to a broad and noble religion, specifically living among religious people who balance spiritual and worldly matters, and similar things. If **Venus** is the significatrix, it signifies he will adhere to a religion in which he might spend time with the women living within it, and similar things. If **Mercury** alone is the significator of religion and is in a good state, it signifies the native will adhere to a religion of the young, or of literate and quite wise men, and their associates. But if **the Moon** is the significatrix of religion, it signifies he will adhere to a religion of unstable men who change easily and quickly from one purpose to another, and who do not keep their religious vows well. Furthermore, if the significator of knowledge or religion—namely the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: the planet that holds the most power or "dignity" over a specific house or point in the chart</term> over the ninth house—is joined to Jupiter or the Sun by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <term>Trine and Sextile: favorable angles (120° and 60°) between planets that allow their energies to work together harmoniously</term> and with **reception** <term>Reception: a cooperative relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</term>, and if it is in the first degree, whichever planet it may be (except for **Mars**), it indicates that religion will come to the native by chance, without his knowledge and unexpectedly, and that this will happen inevitably.

### Chapter 2: Concerning the faith of the native and the depth of their knowledge.

**I**n the investigation of the native's faith and the depth of their knowledge, you must look at **Mercury** and see how he is disposed; for he, above all other planets, is the Almuten for the signification of the native's faith and the depth of their knowledge. If he is **oriental** <term>Oriental: rising before the Sun in the morning, considered a position of strength and action</term>, free from impediments, and fortunate—that is, strong—it will signify that the native will be of good faith, a willing student of knowledge, profound in those matters, a willing companion of religious people, and one who loves them. Look similarly at the **Part of Faith** <term>Part of Faith: a mathematical point in a chart calculated to show spiritual leanings</term> and the place in which you find it, as well as its lord, to see how he is disposed. For if he is safe and exempt from impediments, and if the **third house** <note>The 3rd house traditionally governs short journeys and basic communication, contrasting with the 9th house of higher wisdom.</note> and the **ninth house** and their lords are free from

<column-break/>

impediments and are fortunate and strong—that is, free from **combustion** <term>Combustion: being so close to the Sun that the planet's power is "burned up" or hidden</term> and **retrogradation** <term>Retrogradation: the appearance of a planet moving backward, usually signifying a weakening or reversal of its influence</term>, and likewise free from a **fall** <term>Fall: a sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</term> and the aspects of **Malefics** <term>Malefics: planets like Mars or Saturn that are traditionally associated with challenges</term>—and if the third and ninth houses and the lords of the houses in which you find them are similarly favored, this signifies that the native will be, as said, religious and very profound and sublime in the sciences, so that few similar to him will be found. 

And if you find such a lordship, you may judge accordingly. If you find Mercury, as has been said, free, fortunate, and strong, and the significator of the native's religion, faith, and knowledge to be free, look to see which of the signs or which planet's aspect he has fallen into. For if he is in **Capricorn** or **Aquarius** and **Saturn** regards him from a trine or sextile aspect, and if Saturn is in a good state and well-disposed, it signifies that the native will be religious and of good faith, and will be profound and sublime in the sciences. He will commit those sciences very well to memory and will freely devote himself to reading and study. He will not seek monetary gain from those sciences, and if he does seek it, he will not obtain it. He will be a solitary man who flees worldly pleasures like laughter, games, and secular joys, nor will he desire them in any way; he will withdraw from them entirely. He will also be humble and will well endure almost everything that happens to him, no matter how adverse. He will not easily be saddened by such occasions, but will carry them lightly and in peace; he will not care to avoid distress, tribulations, labors, or inflicted attacks. 

If, however, Mercury is in **Sagittarius** or **Pisces** and **Jupiter** regards him from a trine or sextile aspect, and Jupiter himself is in a good state, well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies the native will adhere to civil and **canon laws** <note>Canon law refers to the ecclesiastical laws governing the Christian Church.</note>. From these he will obtain praise, honors, and a good reputation, as well as clerical dignities, both general and specifically named. Along with this, he will be generous, of good spirit, of good faith, and rejoicing in what he has—unless **Mars** interferes. For if Mars regards him, it signifies that he may despise his own law and become a transgressor of it. 

If Mercury is in **Leo** and **the Sun** is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, and regards him from a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies the native will turn out wise, humble, and discreet. He will be of good faith and a lover of religion, profound in matters of faith, understanding them well, and will freely converse with religious people. 

But if he is in **Taurus** or **Libra** and **Venus** regards him from a trine or sextile aspect, and she is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies the native will adhere to a religion in which he will not persevere well, and he will become a man who abandons it. He will not freely devote himself to study nor will he go deep into the sciences; although he may be found to have good belief, he will delight in many merry-makings. 

If he is in **Gemini** or **Virgo**, and Mercury himself is in a good state, well-disposed, fortunate, strong, and the sole significator, it signifies the native will be of good faith and religious. Blessed on all sides by the gift of knowledge, he will understand books of science well, wonderfully explaining both divine and other books. From this will follow praise and a good reputation, and these things will happen to him even more strongly if **Jupiter** then looks upon him from a trine or sextile aspect—provided Jupiter is in a good state, fortunate, and free. 

If indeed he is in **Cancer** and **the Moon** is in a good state, well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies the native will be of a good nature, good faith, and good belief, and will seek a good reputation. 

**C** And **Abu Ali** <note>original: "Aboaly," likely referring to the 9th-century astrologer Abu Ali al-Khayyat</note> said that if the ninth house is a **common sign** <term>Common Sign: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces; signs associated with changeability and duality</term>, it signifies that the native will be unstable in the faith or religion to which he adheres. This is even more the case if **Mars** then regards it from a trine or sextile aspect, because he will be a mocker and despiser of the law or religion he has taken up; nor will he keep it well, but rather he will be one who reviles and mocks it. And...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Ninth House, moving from the general temperament of the native's faith into specific planetary influences—specifically focusing on the roles of Mars, Mercury, and Saturn in determining one's religious sincerity and intellectual depth. Likewise, it is even more significant if **Mars** <term>Mars: the planet of war, energy, and conflict; usually considered a "malefic" or harmful influence</term> is unfortunate and weak, aspecting the native from a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <term>trine/sextile: favorable geometric angles (120 or 60 degrees) between planets</term> or from an **opposition** <term>opposition: a 180-degree angle, often indicating conflict or tension</term>, for it will then strip all goodness from the native. It will make him a shedder of others' blood and one who willingly inflicts injuries upon others; and this occurs after he has worn away or cast off the yoke of the religion he had assumed. However, if Mars is free from impediments when it aspects the native, he will be a teller of many lies—even while living within a religion—devising things that will never seem credible nor be thought possible by anyone else.

And if it is in a **movable sign** <term>movable sign: also known as "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), associated with change and initiation</term>, and its lord is also in a movable sign, it signifies that the native is not well-secured in another faith; he will change easily and quickly from one opinion to another, nor will he persevere well in another, nor will he know how to choose the better among them. If, however, it is in a **fixed sign** <term>fixed sign: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius; associated with stability and persistence</term>, it signifies his constancy or firmness in the faith and religion to which he adheres. He will work for the good within it and will be firm in his own counsel and purpose, and even in the counsel of others once he has perceived its truth, provided Mars does not work against him. 

And **Abu Ali** <note>original: "aboali"; likely referring to Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that if the lord of the ninth or the third house is in the **Ascendant** or in the **Midheaven** <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the chart, representing career and public reputation</term> and is free from evils, it signifies the prayer of the native is stronger than his efforts; he will be of good sense, excellent character, and perfect in faith—especially if **Jupiter** is the lord of the ninth, or if the lord of the ninth is in the **ascite** <note>likely a scribal error for "ascendant" or "aspect"</note> in the aspect of Jupiter. 

And know that when things are as described, and **Mercury** is **oriental** <term>oriental: rising before the Sun; associated with external, visible action</term>, the native will clearly and manifestly follow the faith, the law, and the religion in which he lives, and he will do well and keep those things which belong to that law and faith. But if Mercury is **occidental** <term>occidental: setting after the Sun; associated with hidden or internal matters</term>, he will hide and conceal his law and faith. You should also observe whether Mercury is in **Gemini**, **Cancer**, or **Virgo** with the **Moon**, and if the **Part of Faith** or the **Part of Knowledge** <term>Parts/Lots: mathematical points in a chart used to predict specific life themes</term> is with them in any of the aforementioned places; for this signifies a native who is profound in science and wisdom, and almost like a prophet. 

If **Jupiter** aspects them from known aspects or is bodily conjoined with them, and the Moon is present, it signifies the native will be truthful and law-abiding, and an experienced, famous, and trusted counselor in deep, advanced, lofty, and great matters. Even if he is not, he will believe in and stand by his own counsel, nor will he believe that anyone else knows better than he in these matters. 

Likewise, observe if the **Dragon's Head** <term>Dragon's Head: the North Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with increase and good fortune</term> is in the ninth house in a daytime birth, or in the third house in a nighttime birth; for it signifies a native of good memory, firm in purpose, and a diligent keeper of his faith and law. This is even stronger and more fervent if **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and **Mercury** aspect that place from known aspects, for then his goodness and fame will be exalted on high and will fly through many regions or provinces.

And **Abu Ali** said if the ninth house is the house of Jupiter and the Moon is in it in a nighttime birth, it signifies that the native will be an astronomer, wise in divinations and an announcer of future things. It is the same if Mercury is the lord of the ninth and is placed within it. 

And when you find the Moon in the Ascendant, and the Ascendant is a sign having a human form <note>Human signs include Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</note>, it signifies that the native will be horrible and of an evil mind. It is similar if **Saturn** is in the Ascendant or in the **Angle of the Earth** <term>Angle of the Earth: the fourth house, representing the depths of the sky and the home</term> at the time of birth. 

You shall also see if the **Part of Faith** is with **Saturn**, for this signifies that the native will be an inquirer into deep and subtle things and an investigator of their intricacies; he will be grave in speech and utter words that are weighty and full of meaning. If it is with **Jupiter**, it signifies the native will be a keeper of good law and good faith, uttering beautiful and honest words. If, however, it is with **Mars**, the native will be of bad faith, bad opinion, and a wicked disposition. If it is with the **Sun**, and the Sun is then fortunate and in a good state, it signifies the native will have a great appearance—even more than he truly is—nevertheless, he will be of good faith,

<column-break/>

good law, and a praiser of good religious practices. And if it is with **Venus**, it signifies the native will be benevolent and a lover of games and joy. If it is with **Mercury**, it signifies he will be skilled in the science of measurement <note>geometry/surveying</note>, likewise in numbers and trade. But if the said Part is with the **Moon**, it indicates generosity of soul and the cleanliness of the native. 

If the ninth house is **Aries**, **Cancer**, or **Pisces**, and the Sun, Jupiter, or Venus—whichever is the **lord of the triplicity** <term>Triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element</term> of the sign in which the luminary <note>the Sun or Moon</note> who has authority is placed—is in a good position in the birth chart, it signifies the native will have a good and honorable livelihood because of his faith or law, and will possess or acquire the recognition, praise, and love of men. This is even more certain and stronger if any of the **Fortunes** are found in the third or ninth house, and even stronger still if the lords of the ninth or third houses are healthy and free from impediments.

And **Aomar** <note>Umar al-Tabari, a Persian astrologer and architect</note> said if Mercury is the lord of the ninth house and agrees with the lord of the Ascendant, the native will be a contender in faith and a debater, possessing discipline in words. If Mercury is then fortunate and oriental, there will be prudence in this, and he will acquire substance and a good, even laudable, state from it. But if it is impeded and occidental, evil will come to him from this.

And **Abu Ali** said if **Saturn** is the lord of the ninth, it signifies the native is wise, especially if it is in the aspect of the Fortunes and not **retrograde** <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward, often weakening a planet's power</term> nor **under the rays of the Sun** <term>under the rays: too close to the Sun to be seen, making the planet weak</term>. 

And **Bernard** <note>Possibly Bernard of Chartres or another medieval commentator</note> said a planet existing in **combustion** <term>combustion: very close to the Sun (within 8.5 degrees), which "burns up" its influence</term> in someone's birth signifies laziness and the native's odiousness and illegality; when it is retrograde, it signifies he will be a liar. 

And **Remigius** <note>likely Remigius of Auxerre</note> said: look at the third and ninth signs, as well as their lords, the Part of Faith, and the lord of the sign containing it. If these three planets are in a good state and well-disposed—that is, fortunate, strong, and free from evils and other impediments—it signifies the native will be of good faith, good law, and likewise of good religion. If they are impeded—especially in the ninth or third house—by the conjunction of **Malefics** <term>Malefics: Saturn or Mars, planets associated with challenge</term>, or by their **quartile aspect** <term>quartile: a 90-degree angle (square), indicating struggle</term> or by opposition, it signifies a native of bad faith, bad law, and corruption; one who is a great pretender, committing deeds against the faith and belonging to no religion.

And **Vuellius** <note>likely Vettius Valens, a 2nd-century astrologer</note> said if **Cancer** is the third or ninth house in someone's birth, and the Moon or Mercury is in one of them, and Jupiter or Venus is in the Ascendant or the tenth house—and these are free from impediments, namely fortunate and strong—this signifies the native will rise to great dignity or a **prelature** <term>prelature: a high office in the Church, such as a bishopric</term> because of his faith, law, and religion. 

And **Bernard** said if you correctly consider the state of the lords of the triplicity of the Part of Faith, you will be able to perceive in which third of his life the native will be of better faith, better law, and better religion. 

And **Aomar** said: look at the ninth or third houses and the planets within them, and at the Part of Faith and its lord. Look also at the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: the planet with the most combined strength/dignity in a specific degree</term> over these places; if it is Saturn and is safe from evils, combustion, and retrogradation—or if it is Jupiter, Mars, or the Sun and they are free from evils—the native will be a worshiper of one God without division of intent, and the native will be saved by that faith and will keep it and not change to another.

### Chapter 3: Concerning the pilgrimages of the native and his long journeys.

## Chapter 4: Which planets help journeys and which do not.

**K**now that the planets help journeys and sometimes impede them. For **Saturn** and the **Sun**, if they are in a good state and well-disposed—that is, fortunate—they will help journeys made toward the East; but if they are impeded, they will oppose them. **Jupiter**, indeed, will provide his help for journeys made toward the North. **Venus**, likewise, will help journeys made toward the South. **Mars** and the **Moon** strive to strengthen journeys that are toward the West. **Mercury**, truly, will provide support for journeys according to the nature of the planet to which it is joined. Consider which planets are the significators assisting the journeys or pilgrimages: for if it is **Saturn**, and he is in a good state and well-disposed, he will signify that the native will exercise their journeys and pilgrimages in the service of great prelates, especially those wearing black clothes, or of the elderly, or of Jews. If indeed it is the **Moon**, they will perform their service among the common people and the rural nations. **Mercury**, however, will provide support for those whom the planet he is applied to serves, and also for literary matters and for young people. # Concerning the tenth house.

When you wish to be certain concerning the matter of the mastery <term>mastery: "magisterium," referring to one's profession, trade, or vocation</term> of the native, and also what kind of works they will have in the future, and concerning their health and prosperity, their kingdoms, as well as their offices and maternal matters: Look at the ascendant of that birth and see if any of the planets are found in it; for that one whom you find in the ascendant must be considered, and from that one you shall receive the aforesaid significance. And **Mars**, or at least **Saturn**, should be present; and if **Venus** is in any of the dignities <term>dignity: a place in the zodiac where a planet has particular strength or influence</term> of the **Sun**, the **Moon**, or **Saturn**, and if she herself is in a good state and well-disposed, it signifies that the native will be a buyer and seller of gold, silver, and spices. If the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> do not signify specific things, they signify them generally, and especially in such a case.

Tiresias was a famous blind prophet of Apollo in Greek mythology.</note>. 

If, however, **Venus** is in the dignities of **Jupiter**, and **Jupiter** bears witness to her, it signifies that the native will frequent religious houses and willingly live in them, dealing with the customs of religious people, and from there he will obtain his living and fulfill his necessary requirements. He will similarly know how to manage marriages and wisely bring them to fruition, following from which is great utility; he will also be an augur <term>augur: a priest or official who interprets omens, such as the flight of birds</term>. 

If **Venus** is in the dignities of **Mars**, and **Mars** bears witness to her, it signifies the native will be capable in the medical science in a competent way. He will delight in the wearing of arms, though more so in the wearing of them than in their exercise; he will delight in carrying them because of **Mars**, but will not care to use them much because of **Venus**. 

And not only do the planets signify the works or masteries of the native, but also the zodiac signs help in this, as Ptolemy testifies. For if the significator of the native's work or mastery runs through any of the signs that resemble human figures, it will aid every mastery that belongs to the native. If it is in the sign of quadrupeds <note>four-legged animals</note> and the native applies himself to the mastery of mines, or the trade of metals—gold, silver, copper, lead, iron—or of buildings, or the use of birds and similar things, he will know them perfectly, because the quadruped signs aid all the aforementioned, and especially the domestic ones. 

And Ptolemy said that the equinoctial and solstitial signs <term>equinoctial and solstitial signs: Aries, Libra, Cancer, and Capricorn, which mark the turning points of the seasons</term> aid the masteries of translation, variation of interpretation, geometry, and also the affairs of houses of prayer. And he said that the signs whose figures resemble wild beasts and aquatic animals aid masteries related to moisture, such as fishing, sailing, and those in which liquids are used—such as making vats and winepresses and the like—and of herbs, as a guardian of gardens and harvests, and the skill of building ships; also salting, such as salting fish in whatever way, and the making of salt. 

And he said that if the **Moon** properly rules the place of mastery—I mean that she has dignity in the Ascendant or in the tenth house—and emerging from under the rays of the **Sun** after separating from him she is first joined to **Mercury**, and you find her in Capricorn, Taurus, or Cancer, it signifies that the native will be wise in subordinate sciences such as augury, and will become a diviner using geomancy <note>divination by patterns in earth or sand</note>, hydromancy <note>divination by water</note>, chiromancy <note>palm reading</note>, and will be a priest, an incantator, a conjurer, and a sacrificer, in this manner: 

For if the conjunction of the aforementioned significators of the native's work and mastery, and the **Sun** and **Moon**, is in Taurus—since it is the house of **Venus** and the exaltation of the **Moon**—it signifies the native will be a soothsayer or an augur. But if it is in Capricorn—since it is the house of **Saturn** and the exaltation of **Mars**, and of the triplicity of the **Moon**—it signifies the native will be a sacrificer. If indeed it is in Cancer—since it is the house of the **Moon**—it signifies the

native will be a hydromancer. And Ptolemy said: if it is in Sagittarius or Pisces, he will divine by means of the dead, and will even cause evil spirits to be moved from place to place through his incantations. But if it is in Virgo or Scorpio, he will become an astrologer and a necromancer, and will judge hidden things, and predict future things even if he has little or no knowledge of the science of Isaiah <note>original: "scientiam isay," likely referring to prophetic or biblical knowledge</note>. 

If it is in Aries, Leo, or Libra, he will be a prophet or a wise man and an interpreter of dreams. And this is the way by which we must observe the qualities of the native's masteries and their types, in order to know them reasonably, according to Ptolemy's testimony. 

You will weigh the qualities of the native's works or masteries through the planets that signify them and through their disposition, if you look closely. For if you see them well-disposed and fortunate—that is, strong, oriental <term>oriental: rising before the Sun, considered a position of strength</term>, direct in the angles (and especially in the tenth or even the first), or in any of their dignities—namely their house, exaltation, term, or triplicity—it will signify that the works or masteries of the native will result in honors, strengths, and dominions. 

But if you find them outside the predicted dignities, occidental <term>occidental: setting after the Sun, considered a weaker position</term> or cadent <term>cadent: planets in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, generally weaker</term>, you shall pronounce his masteries or works as being subject to others; and all the more strongly if any of the infortunes <term>infortunes: the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</term> look upon the said significators or are elevated above them. For they will signify that the native’s works or masteries will be base, contemptible, and despicable, and that he cannot be secure in them, and he will be deceived in them and by them and because of them. 

If that infortune is **Saturn**, and he is of the same triplicity as the significator of the native's mastery, it signifies that this will happen because of his laziness, his slowness, and a cold, ill-tempered disposition. But if it is **Mars**, and he is in a sign agreeable to his nature, this will happen because of the native's timidity, his baseness, and small-mindedness, and he will suffer evil and destruction from it. If indeed both the aforementioned infortunes are impeding the significators of the native's work and mastery, his work and masteries will be displeasing to almost everyone, indifferently and always. 

Whether the native is to have a multitude or a few works or masteries, and whether he is called or not called to establish or exercise masteries or works, you will perceive from the state or disposition of the significators of the works. For if they are well-disposed, they will indicate good; if badly, they promise the contrary. If indeed the fortunes <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> look upon them or are elevated above them, the native's works and masteries will be signified as convenient as well as profitable. And from that, the native will be commended, and in those things and from those things he will remain secure; nor because of them will he suffer any shame or reproach, but rather honor and utility, according to the nature of the work or mastery. And all the more so if **Jupiter** and **Venus** look upon them; and on that occasion he will be exalted and will be called a master.

### Chapter Two: Concerning the health and prosperity of the native, and concerning his offices and his kingdom.

When you wish to investigate the health and prosperity, as well as the offices and the kingdom of the native: look to the **Sun** in daytime births; to the **Moon** and **Saturn** in nighttime births; and to the tenth house and its lord; and to the Part of Kingdom <term>Part of Kingdom: a specific mathematical point in a birth chart related to social status</term> and the planet in whose house you find it. 

And if you see the said significators—namely the **Sun** and the **Moon**, or either of them—fortunate in the angles, and strong, joined to a fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, or even with others well-disposed and with reception <term>reception: an astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</term>, and they are oriental looking upon the **Sun**, or looking upon the **Moon** and **Saturn**...

But if he is weakly disposed, his significance will be much below what was predicted.

If **Mars** is his significator, it will signify his health and prosperity through victory over enemies or opponents, and from his subjects who will fear and revere him for coming causes. 

But if **Mercury** is the lord of health, it signifies that he will be raised up by his own intellect and the discipline of the things he manages, and from there he will prosper and have capability.

Observe also whether the lord of the first house joins with the lord of the tenth, or vice versa. For if the lord of the first joins the lord of the tenth—and if it is lighter <note>Moving faster in the zodiac</note> than it, by a trine or sextile aspect <note>Favorable geometric angles of 120 and 60 degrees</note> with reception or without reception, or by a square <note>A challenging 90-degree angle</note> with reception—it signifies the native will obtain goodness, utility, and profit from kings and by kings, but not without his own inquiry and petition. But if the lord of the seventh is lighter and joins the lord of the first by the said aspects, it signifies he obtains the predicted things without his own inquiry or petition; all the more so if reception intervenes and they are not "cadent" <term>cadent: Houses (3, 6, 9, 12) where planets are traditionally thought to be weaker or less effective</term> or otherwise unfortunate.

And **Abuali** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said if this application is from the angles, the dignity he follows will be great and famous, especially if it is from the Ascendant or the Midheaven <note>original: "medio celi," the 10th house</note>. 

And he said: if the lord of the Ascendant is in an angle and the lord of the Midheaven is cadent, it signifies the native is famous but his work is lowly. And if the lord of the Midheaven is in an angle and the lord of the Ascendant is cadent, it signifies the greatness of the work but that the man himself is lowly. If both are cadent, it signifies the lowliness of both the native and the work. 

And he said: when the lord of the Ascendant is in the Midheaven, it signifies he is born of the lineage of kings or connected to it. And if the aspect between them is good, it signifies friendship between the native and the king; but if it is bad, it signifies enmity and heaviness. 

And he said: if there is no application between the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the Midheaven, look to the application between the lord of the Ascendant and the **Sun**, and judge by it just as you judged the application of the lord of the Ascendant and the Midheaven.

## Chapter Three: How you must look into the matter of the mother.

Since the matter of the father is looked at from the fourth house of the native's birth, and we wish to look into the matter of his mother—just as the matter of a wife is looked at from the seventh house from the husband's house—it is necessary that we look into the matter of the mother from the tenth house, because the tenth is the seventh from the fourth <note>This is "derivative house" logic: if the Father is the 4th, his wife (the Mother) is the 7th house *starting the count from the 4th*, which lands on the 10th</note>. 

Therefore, if it happens that you must look into the matter of the mother, look at the *hyleg* <term>hyleg: The "life-giver," a planet or point used to determine the lifespan and vitality of a person</term> from the tenth house and its Lord; similarly from the Moon and Venus; and also from the **Part of the Mother** and the planet in whose house it stands, and the planet which is the *almuten* over any of the predicted places; for that planet itself will be the "significator" of the mother. 

Next, look at which of the planets is the significator of the mother's years; see if any of the others increase any years or months for her, or decrease her years or months. For if any of the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> aspect it from a trine or sextile aspect, and it is in a good and well-disposed state—fortunate and strong—and is in the angles, it will increase her "minor years" <note>A fixed number of years assigned to each planet in ancient systems</note> and, moreover, as many months as there are in its "mean years." It is even stronger if it "receives" the significator. 

But if it is in the "succeedent" houses <term>succeedent: The houses (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th) that follow the powerful angles; they are of moderate strength</term>, it will increase her months. If it does not receive the significator from the said aspects, it will increase her minor years but not the months. But if it is "impeded" <note>Weakened by bad aspects or being in a difficult sign</note>, it will not increase her years, but instead of years, it will increase months. 

If indeed the planet that aspects it is a "malefic" <note>Mars or Saturn</note> and aspects it from a square or opposition, it decreases her years by the number of its minor years. But if that malefic is in a good and well-disposed state—that is, fortunate and strong—it only decreases it according to three parts of its minor years. 

After this, you shall look into the state and health of the mother, and her being, whether in work, mastery, or dignity, and her fortune, from the "escorts" of the planets from the Moon <term>escorts: Planets that rise or set near a luminary, acting as "bodyguards" that enhance its power</term>. For if you see Mars or Venus in the escort of the Moon, or Mercury when it is joined with any of them, and they are in a good and well-disposed state—fortunate and strong—it will signify an increase in the mother's dignity, her exaltation, and the greatness of her value and honor. 

Next, look at the mother's *hyleg* and the planet from which you took it; direct it to the places of the fortunes and the malefics, and in whichever place you see them reach the fortunes...

From the significance of that house, judge the good in all the aforementioned matters. However, when you perceive it reaching misfortunes, from the significance of that house, it will be judged that the contrary will come to the mother in all the aforementioned things. And Omar <note>Likely referring to the 9th-century astrologer Omar al-Tabari.</note> said that if the Moon is not there for the mother in that place, and you wish to know the place you should direct for the mother, direct it from the degree of the Moon; whenever it reaches the "malifics" <term>malifics: Planets considered naturally challenging, traditionally Mars and Saturn</term>, it will signify danger and the death of the mother.

After this, look at the harmony and affection of the mother toward the son, and her hatred against him, from the <term>Almuten: The planet that holds the most cumulative power or 'dignity' at a specific point in the zodiac</term> of the Ascendant and the Almuten over the mother’s place. For if they are in harmony with each other and love each other mutually, judge that there will be future affection between them. But if they are mutually hateful, you shall judge the opposite. You will also look for the harmony between the father of the native and his mother; just as you saw their harmony through their significators, pronounce that it will be so between them.

Regarding the death of the mother, whether it will be near or remote, Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrologer whose work on "interrogations" was foundational for later traditions.</note> said it is signified by the entry of the Almuten "under the earth" <note>This refers to a planet moving into the houses below the horizon line of the chart.</note>. And Abu 'Ali <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a prominent 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said regarding the life of the mother: look at whose birth is by day, it shall be from Venus; if she is aspecting the Ascendant, direct her toward the bodies of the malifics or through their rays by the degrees of the ascensions, giving one year to each degree. But if Venus does not aspect the Ascendant, and the Moon aspects it, direct her just as you would have directed Venus if she had been fit to be directed. If indeed the Moon does not aspect it, then direct the degree of the Midheaven. And this should be done in daytime births: first from Venus, then from the Moon, and afterwards from the degree of the Midheaven.

In nocturnal births, however, you shall begin first from the Moon, then from Venus, and afterwards from the degree of the Midheaven. Then look to see if the years signified by the <term>Hyleg: The planet or point in a chart that acts as the 'giver of life' and determines the lifespan</term> are equal to the years signified by the Almuten over the degree in which Venus is found, or over the degree in which the Lord of the house in which she is found resides in daytime births. In nocturnal births, look at the degree in which the Moon is found, or the degree where the Lord of the house in which she is found resides; and both in day and night, look at the degree of the Midheaven or the degree in which its Lord is found. For by this, the death of that native's mother will be signified before the completion of one year from his day of birth.

Furthermore, you shall look at the state of the mother from the <term>Lords of Triplicity: Three planets that share guardianship over a specific element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water) in the zodiac</term> of the sign that the Moon then possessed. For if you see them well-disposed, you shall judge good from it, or if poorly, the contrary of good. Because if all are good in state and well-disposed, fortunate and strong, you shall pronounce that good will come for the whole time of her life. But if they are ill, they shall judge evil. Indeed, the first Lord shows its significance at the beginning of life from the birth of that native. The second shows it in the middle of life. If indeed the third is in the final part of the mother’s life, you shall predict what it has signified for the future.

By what death the mother is to die—namely, whether easy or heavy or deformed—you shall perceive from the state of the Moon and from the Lord of the house in which she is found, as well as from the "Lot of the Mother" and its Lord, and from the "Lot of the Death of the Mother" and its Lord. For if they are of good state and well-disposed, they will judge a common and laudable death. If however they are impeded and ill-disposed, they will signify that the mother will die an evil and deformed death; nevertheless, the significator of her death in her own birth chart will also play its part.

You shall foresee who among the father and mother dies first from their significators. For whichever is first found to be "combust" <term>combust: A planet is 'combust' when it is so close to the Sun that its influence is thought to be burned up or weakened</term>, or whichever falls closer to the angle of the Fourth House of the birth chart, signifies that one as dying first.

<column-break/>

## Concerning the Eleventh House.

### First chapter concerning the friends of the native, and likewise concerning his fortune and his hope.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop-cap "U" featuring intricate floral and foliate scrollwork in a woodcut style, contained within a square border.</image-desc>

Having seen in the preceding chapter the study of the native's mastery and his offices and his health, as well as the matter of the mother, etc., it seems fit and convenient to me in this present chapter to treat of his friends and his fortune and his hope, and to make mention of all these things. Therefore, if you wish to exert yourself over any of the aforesaid in anyone’s birth, you shall look in this manner.

You shall consider the Eleventh House from the Ascendant of the birth of any native, and its Lord, and also the "Lot of Friends" and its Lord; as well as Venus, who naturally has the figure of friends, since we take delight in them. Look similarly at the planets that are in the 11th house, and in the house where the Lord of the 11th is, and the Lord of the house in which he resides; and where the Lot of Friends is, and the planet in whose house it resides. Similarly look at the planet in whose house Venus herself resides. Look also at the luminaries and their Lords: namely the Sun by day, and the Moon by night. Having inspected these, you will see which planet was the Almuten over the locations of the aforesaid; and which of them was of better state and better disposition. For from that one, you will be able to take the figure of the native’s friends and his fortune and his hope.

Look first from the 11th house and its Lord; then from the planet which is in the 11th; afterwards from Venus; then from the Lot of Friends and its Lord; then from the Lord of the house in which Venus is; then from the luminary which holds authority; and finally from the Lord of the house in which that luminary is.

For if there are "fortunes" <term>fortunes: Benefic planets, traditionally Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring positive outcomes</term> in the 11th, and there is a friendly mixing or "application" between the Lord of the 11th and the Lord of the Ascendant—whether from love or some friendly aspect, and especially with "reception" occurring from their houses or exaltations or from two of the other minor dignities—it will signify a multitude of friends for the native who hold affection for him. This is even more likely if the 11th house is Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces.

But if the 11th house is Aries, Taurus, Libra, Sagittarius, Capricorn, or Aquarius, they will diminish the number of the native's friends by a fourth part. If indeed the 11th house is Gemini, Leo, or Virgo, they will diminish the number of his friends by a third part. And if there are no "fortunes" in the 11th, but they look upon it with known or laudable aspects, and those fortunes are of good state and well-disposed—namely, fortunate and strong—they will have that same effect which was stated regarding the number or multitude of the native's friends.

If however it is not as was said of the 11th house, you shall consider its Lord. For according to how you see him disposed and the planet in whose house you find him, so you shall pronounce concerning the facts of the native's friends toward him. And look also at the Lot of Friends and its Lord; if you find them or either of them well-disposed, you will be able to judge through them concerning the matter of friends; for they will indicate a good outcome for the native from his friends. Then look at Venus: if she is of good state and well-disposed and is aspecting the Ascendant or its Lord with an aspect of friendship, or the 11th house or its Lord, it signifies the native will have present friends, and for the most part of the feminine sex, from whom he will follow utility and good; and those friends will be fortunate in their own right. Look similarly at the Lord of the house in which Venus is, for he too will help the figure in the goodness of friends. But if the luminaries...

For if the Sun is good and well-disposed, it signifies that a large portion of friends will be wealthy and noble—specifically those who are suited for a kingdom. If, however, the house of any of the seven planets is in the Eleventh, it signifies that the friends of the native will have the substance and the sign of whichever planet’s house it is. For example, if it is the **house of Saturn**, the friends of the native will be according to the appearance, being, and disposition of Saturn: namely, old men, servants, Jews <note>original: "iudei." In medieval astrology, Saturn was frequently associated with Judaism because of the Sabbath and the antiquity of the faith.</note>, and other low-ranking persons.

If indeed it is the **house of Jupiter**, they will be according to the state, disposition, appearance, and age of Jupiter; they will be either bishops or those faithful to Jupiter <note>This refers to religious authorities or men of high moral character.</note>. If it is the **house of Mars**, they will be according to the nature and disposition of Mars and his appearance: princes and warlike men.

But if it is the **house of the Sun**, they will be according to the nature, disposition, and being of the Sun and his appearance: and they will be noble kings and counselors, as has been said. And if it is the **house of Venus**, they will be according to the nature, disposition, and being of Venus and her appearance: such as women and effeminate men. But if it is the **house of Mercury**, they will be according to the being, nature, and disposition of Mercury and his appearance: they will be wise men, merchants, and scribes. If, however, it is the **house of the Moon**, then the friends of the native will signify according to the nature and disposition of the Moon and her age and appearance.

And if all the aforementioned significators <term>significators: Planets that "point to" or represent a specific area of life</term>, or the majority of them, are in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; signs known for stability.</note>, it signifies that the friends will love the native diligently, and their friendship and affection will be firm, constant, and lasting. If they are in **bicorporeal signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces; also known as "mutable" signs.</note>, it will signify a mediocrity in the aforementioned things and their durability. But if they are in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; signs associated with change.</note>, it signifies that friends will quickly depart from that friendship and will become enemies to him.

And Omar <note>Omar al-Tabari, a 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said: if the Almuten <term>Almuten: The planet with the most combined strength at a specific point in the zodiac</term> over the Ascendant is bad and harms the Almuten over the house of friends, evil will come to the friends and the native. And if it is the opposite, speak of good. And he said: if these significators are fortunate, they will have good, reverence, and profit from one another. 

Then he said: If the Lord of the Eleventh does not behold <term>behold: To form an astrological aspect (angle) with another point</term> the Eleventh house, nor does Venus behold the Lord of her own house, nor the Lord of the **Part of Friends**, the native will be among those who have no mixture with friends; he will not be a sociable man but will mostly live willingly as a solitary person. And if **Fortunes** <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus.</note> are in the Eleventh, then you can judge that his friends will be good, of good agreement, and of good character, and that they will abound in riches; and this is even stronger if the Fortune is in the Twelfth. If, however, a **Misfortune** <note>Malefic planets, usually Saturn and Mars.</note> is in it, it signifies that the friends of the native will be bad, with much discord and poverty.

### Chapter 2. On the types of friends.

And Ptolemy said that friendships and enmities occur in three ways: namely, either because of the **concord of spirits** by which it is necessary for a man to love his companion; or because of **profit**; or because **joy or sorrow** compels them. 

And he said: those who love each other because of the concord of spirits are those in whose births it happens that the Sun and Moon are exchanged from their places—this means that the Sun is in the sign or place where the Moon was in the birth of the other. Or, that their significators or luminaries <term>luminaries: The Sun and the Moon</term> are in a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note>. And this becomes even stronger if **reception** <term>reception: When two planets occupy each other's signs, indicating mutual support</term> intervenes; then their friendship will be outstanding and naturally lasting. This is even more so if any of the Fortunes behold the said significators or luminaries in the birth charts without the aspect of any Misfortune.

Then he said: those whose affection is because of **joy or sorrow** are those for whom it happens that their sign and Ascendant are one and the same; or the sign of the birth of one beholds the sign of the birth of the other from a trine or sextile aspect; or a Fortune beholds the sign of both births from a trine or sextile aspect, with the aspects of the Misfortunes being entirely removed. 

But those whose friendship agrees because of **profit** are those in whose births the **Part of Fortune** was in the sign of one in which it was in the birth of the other, or in its triplicity <term>triplicity: A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term>, or in its trine or sextile aspect; thus there is concord between them and they will profit from one and

<column-break/>

the same thing or trade; and both will strive to profit and gain the same; and for that reason their friendship will come about and affection will fall between them. Or, there will happen to them, or to one of them, something sinister from one and the same cause, from which both will grieve and one will have compassion for the other; and for that reason they become friends. This happens when the Fortunes behold the Ascendants of their births or their significators without the aspect of any Misfortune.

Furthermore, if the Almuten and the power of the birth behold each other from known aspects, they will be friends and love each other mutually; and this is even stronger if both receive each other. But if their aspects are from a **square** or from an **opposition** <note>Tense angles of 90 and 180 degrees respectively.</note>, and especially if they do not receive each other, malevolence will fall between them from one and the same cause. This is even stronger if any of the Misfortunes behold those significators; and even more so if that aspect occurs without reception, and more and more if it is from a square or opposition, or if there is bodily contact <note>A conjunction, where planets are in the same degree.</note>. 

If that Misfortune which beholds them is **Saturn**, and he was in the birth of both of them in some sign that is the house of the significator of the birth of one of them (or his exaltation, term, or triplicity, or some dignity of the other), and the aspect was a trine or sextile—and even stronger if reception intervened—there will be friendship between those natives on account of waters, or lands, or other estates, or because of old men or old age, or because of possessions which will be the occasion for their friendship, or because of other agreements or familiarities happening between them. But if the aspect was from an opposition or a square, or there was bodily contact—and even stronger if it was a conjunction or aspect without reception—enmities will fall between them, as well as discord and contentions from any of the aforementioned causes. 

If, however, it is **Mars**, the aforementioned things will happen by the occasion of any of those things signified by Mars <note>Such as war, tools, fire, or conflict.</note>. If any of the Fortunes behold him, and it is **Jupiter**, friendship and concord will happen between them by occasion of substance (wealth), or acquisition and profit, or any other significators of Jupiter. If it is the **Sun**, it will happen by occasion of some lay dignity, or mastery, or office, or raw gold, or any other of the things signified by the Sun. 

If indeed it is **Venus**, it will happen by occasion of nuptials or any delightful thing which is signified by Venus. But if it is **Mercury**, it will happen by occasion of writing or sculpture, or trade, or money-changing, or any other of the sciences signified by Mercury. But if it is the **Moon**, the aforementioned things will happen by occasion of embassies or mandates to be imposed, or some distinguished ministry, or any cause from those things signified by the Moon. And you shall look at her significations according to her disposition in the quarters and dichotomies <note>The phases of the Moon.</note> of any lunation. You shall also consider the being and disposition of the aforementioned Fortunes, for according to how they are disposed, so ought the aforementioned things to happen.

And Ptolemy said that in the matter of the native's friends and the friendship itself, there are **four places** in the figure of his birth which are called "greater" or "major," namely those which have greater lordship and greater power over the native and his friends: which are the place of the Sun and the place of the Moon; and the place of the Ascendant and the place of the Part of Fortune. For if all these places, or the majority of them, are in one sign, or if the places are mutually exchanged—that is, the Sun in the birth of one is in the place where the Moon was in the birth of the other, or vice versa; or the Lord of the Ascendant of one birth is in the place of the Part of Fortune of the other birth, or vice versa—and there are 7 degrees or less between those two places, it signifies between the natives a firm, increasing, and inseparable love. If, however, the said significators or the lords of the said places behold each other from a trine or sextile aspect...
