But if the <term>almuten</term> <note>The "almuten" is the planet that holds the most cumulative dignity and strength in a specific house or degree of the zodiac.</note> of the Ascendant is joined with the almuten of the Eleventh House, or with the almuten of the Seventh House, by a trine or sextile aspect with reception, and they are not otherwise unfortunate or hindered, you shall undoubtedly predict a future friendship between them through joy and eagerness. If you perceive any planet transferring light or power between the significators of two births, and that planet itself is of good being and well-disposed—that is, both fortunate and strong—you may judge that a friendship will occur, though it may not last forever, but for a time that is not very brief.

But if Jupiter and Mercury are the hyleg, joined with the almuten of the Seventh or Eleventh House, they will naturally love each other by reason of the <term>trivium or quadrivium</term> <note>The "Trivium" (grammar, logic, rhetoric) and "Quadrivium" (arithmetic, geometry, music, astronomy) comprised the seven liberal arts of medieval education.</note>, and because of science and philosophy. This was the standard legal and theological term in the Middle Ages for same-sex acts or "unnatural" sexual behavior.</note>; yet their friendship will not be at all long-lasting because it happens that Mars is a misfortune while Venus is a fortune. Note that if Venus and Mercury are the significators of the birth or the almuten over the Ascendant, and have a mixture with the aforementioned significators as stated, a friendship will be confirmed between them by reason of women, or perhaps the study of music or books, or by reason of the food which men use for their nourishment.

You shall consider all these aforementioned things according to whether you see the said significators to be of good being and well-disposed—namely, fortunate and strong—and in good aspects with the Sun and Moon: either in the Ascendant, or with its almuten, or with the Part of Fortune. For according to how those four factors are, or according to how they aspect those four aforementioned places, their significations will appear. And if they do not aspect them, their significations will vanish entirely.

## On the Twelfth House

### Chapter One: Regarding the matter of secret enemies and the envious; and regarding the considerations which you ought to have in the significations of the Twelfth House, as well as the judgments that result from the aforementioned significations.

<margin>a</margin>
Look into the matter of secret enemies and the envious in the Twelfth House from the Ascendant, as well as the judgments that result from the significations of the houses and their lords. See what the being of the almuten of the Twelfth is in relation to the almuten of the Ascendant. For you shall look at Saturn and the Part of Enemies and its lord, to see how they are disposed. For if the almuten over the Twelfth, or over the house in which the Part of Enemies is located,

<column-break/>

or Saturn is of evil being and ill-disposed, or if some misfortune hinders any of them—and more strongly so if it hinders the lord of the Ascendant or its almuten or the Moon—and again stronger if the hindrance is by an opposition or a quartile aspect; or if the almuten of the Twelfth is in the Ascendant or in opposition to either of the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>, it signifies that the native will have many secret enemies and many enviers. These will be able to harm him greatly in secret, and they will strive to harm him and shall indeed harm him; and even more so if that misfortune has any dignity in the Twelfth House, and again more so if that hindering planet is the almuten over the lord of the Ascendant or the lord of the Twelfth.

But if the almuten over the Twelfth does not aspect the almuten over the Ascendant nor the Moon, or if any of the fortunes aspect them, or if any of them is the almuten over the Twelfth and is not hindered, it signifies the native will have few secret enemies and few enviers.

If the almuten of the Twelfth is **Saturn**, it signifies that the secret enemies and enviers will be old men, Jews <note>original: "iudei." In medieval astrology, Saturn was associated with Judaism due to its perceived coldness, antiquity, and its rule over the Sabbath.</note>, low-ranking people from the crowd, religious figures wearing black clothes, and unrefined or wild men and the like. If it is **Jupiter**, they will be men who appear wise, lawyers, secular clergy, and also middling nobles from travel and the like. If, however, it is **Mars**, they will be warlike men, evildoers, whisperers, and cursers and the like. But if it is the **Sun**, they will be nobles and magnates—and more so if the almuten of the Twelfth is in an "angle" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> or in a house succeeding an angle in which he has some dignity. But if it is **Venus**, they will be for the most part women, effeminate men, drunkards, and gluttons and the like. If, however, it is **Mercury**, they will be literate men, youths, scribes, and the like. If indeed it is the **Moon**, they will be unstable and common men, and low-ranking persons and the like.

If the almuten of the Twelfth is retrograde, or <term>combust</term> <note>A planet is "combust" when it is so close to the Sun that its power is said to be burned away or hidden.</note>, or besieged by misfortunes, or <term>peregrine</term> <note>A planet is "peregrine" when it has no essential dignity (like being in its own home or exaltation) in its current position, making it wanderer-like and weak.</note>, or in a house falling away from an angle, or in its "fall" or its "detriment," or if it is in a house falling away from the Ascendant (namely in the 2nd, 6th, or 8th house), or if the almuten of the Ascendant hinders it, or if any of the malefic planets are in the Twelfth and are hindered by misfortunes—it signifies that the native will prevail over all his secret enemies and enviers and will trample them down. They will be able to harm him little or almost not at all, but he himself shall hinder them.

And if there is a misfortune to the lord of the Ascendant and it hinders the lord of the Twelfth or its almuten, they shall suffer loss and detriment from him. If indeed Saturn or Mars is in the Twelfth, or either of them, and is of evil being and ill-disposed, or hinders the lord of the Twelfth or its almuten, it signifies that the native will see from his secret enemies and enviers what they themselves desired to see of him <note>Meaning the native will witness his enemies' downfall or the very misfortunes they wished upon him.</note>.

## Chapter 2: On the judgments that result from the significations of the Twelfth Houses and their lords.

Having seen in the preceding sections regarding the native's secret enemies and enviers, it now remains to be seen regarding the judgments that result from the significations of the Twelfth houses and the presence of planets in them, which are contained under this chapter. This follows the method which you ought to observe in these matters, according to what the ancient wise men, our predecessors, are seen to have commanded. For it is one of those things where we ought to look at the aforementioned houses and their lords, and judge concerning them according to their disposition. And therefore, you ought to look at all the houses in the birth of any native once you have erected the figure of that birth, and see in which houses a planet may be found, and how they are disposed, and what their being is—both of the fortunes and of the misfortunes. For in whichever house you find a fortune, or whichever house it aspects...

...perishes through a favorable <term>trine</term> <note>A trine is a harmonious astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart.</note> or <term>sextile</term> <note>A sextile is a harmonious aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart.</note> aspect; if she herself is free, fortunate, and strong, and not hindered by any impediment, and if no malefic planet <note>Malefics traditionally include Saturn and Mars, known for bringing challenges.</note> is in the place where the <term>benefic</term> <note>Benefics traditionally include Jupiter and Venus, known for bringing good fortune.</note> casts its aspect, and no malefic planet looks upon that place, and if the superior benefics are <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the Sun, considered a position of strength.</note> and the inferior ones are <term>occidental</term> <note>Setting after the Sun.</note> and not otherwise hindered, and if the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>An Arabic Part calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant, representing prosperity.</note> is well-disposed and free—by this conjunction of malefics and their aspects, it will signify the things indicated by those houses in which the aforementioned good things are found, bringing utility and profit to the native. And if they are hindered, they signify some utility, though little and mixed with many dangers. If, however, they are malefics and are aspected by benefics, and are not otherwise hindered, and are fortunate and strong in their own <term>dignities</term> <note>Specific degrees or signs where a planet has more power, such as its "Exaltation" or "Domicile."</note>, they will again signify some good coming from the meaning of the houses in which they are located or which they aspect with good aspects; yet this will come with such great exhaustion, complication, and heaviness that it will seem to the native that little is being achieved. And if they are hindered, they will signify all evils, all losses, all things sinister and harmful, as well as misfortunes coming to the native based on the meanings of those houses in the birth charts.

### Concerning Saturn in his own house.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Saturn. A bearded man sits in a chariot pulled by two winged dragons/serpents. He holds a scythe. In the upper right corner, the astrological symbol for Saturn ♄ is visible inside a small circle.</image-desc>

If the birth occurs during the day and Saturn is the <term>significator</term> of that birth, and he is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, and is in Capricorn, Aquarius, or Libra <note>Saturn rules Capricorn and Aquarius, and is "Exalted" in Libra.</note> and in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, this signifies that nobles, magnates, and wealthy men will willingly befriend the native. It also signifies that he will remain healthy and sound in body and mind. It will further signify that he will be a great accumulator of wealth, especially if he has a connection with the Part of Fortune or the <term>Part of Substance</term> in the Ascendant, the Second House, or another praiseworthy place in the chart. If, however, his disposition is the opposite, it will indicate a multitude of sicknesses of the body and mind, as well as the opposite of all the things mentioned above.

### Concerning Saturn in the house of Jupiter.

If he is in Sagittarius or Pisces and the birth is during the day, it signifies a native with a beautiful body and stature, a "son of truth," and one who will accumulate wealth from just, fitting, and lawful means. In a nocturnal birth, however, it signifies that the native will willingly spend time with nobles, magnates, and the wealthy, and that he will receive an inheritance from his own father upon his death.

### Concerning Saturn in the house of Mars.

If he is in Aries or Scorpio, it signifies a native of strong purpose, but hard-hearted, with little or almost no mercy, no compassion, and one who will be very prone to anger. And if the birth is at night, he will be found twice as bad and more cruel.

### Concerning Saturn in the house of the Sun.

If he remains in Leo in a daytime birth, it will indicate a fortunate native and father, unless the father’s own birth chart works against his own deeds. If, however, the birth is at night, it portends the opposite of these things and will show their downfall.

<column-break/>

### Concerning Saturn in the house of Venus.

If you find him in Taurus or Libra, in both daytime and nighttime births, it shows the native is inclined toward sexual acts, especially with low-born women. He will suffer loss because of this and will be of a poor physical constitution. For the most part, he will live in a semi-sickly state and will be shown to be of bad faith.

### Concerning Saturn in the house of Mercury.

If you find him in Gemini or Virgo, whatever the birth may be, it signifies that he will be noted for the investigation of sciences and the study of books, and he will unlock hidden secrets. You can say that through much study and exhaustion in these matters, his tongue will be hindered <note>This could imply a speech impediment or simply difficulty in communicating his complex thoughts.</note>; and as is often the case, that labor and study will result in his own loss and shame. He will be unfortunate among men, especially among those whom he serves; for they, unwilling to reward his service, will find occasions to speak ill of him and blaspheme him, lying that he has committed evils he never even thought of, which will lead him to a troubled conscience, bad thoughts, and a heavy spirit.

### Concerning Saturn in the house of the Moon.

And if you find him in Cancer—since Cancer is the sixth sign from his own house <note>The 6th House is traditionally associated with illness and servants.</note>—it signifies that the native will often be burdened with infirmities. His mother, on account of his birth, will fall into a severe illness; or perhaps the native will consume her goods while she lives, or scatter her substance in a bad way, or perhaps even be the cause of her death.

### Concerning Jupiter in the house of Saturn.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of Jupiter. A crowned figure sits in a chariot pulled by two horses. He holds a scepter. In the upper right corner, the astrological symbol for Jupiter ♃ is visible inside a small circle.</image-desc>

If Jupiter is in Capricorn or Aquarius and is the significator of the birth, and is free from impediments, it signifies a native who is anxious and gasping for gain, distressed by the desire for money. He will always show himself to be needy and poorer than other men, living a life of utility but misery. He will always be thinking of bad things, and in everything that men value, he will be base and weak; thus, many inconveniences will come to him from this cause.

### Concerning Jupiter in his own house.

If he is in Sagittarius or Pisces and it is a daytime birth, it signifies a native who is wealthy and fortunate in substance, which he will accumulate in great quantity. He will also be a discreet man, knowing how to be influential among nobles, magnates, and the wealthy. If, however, it is a night birth, it signifies he will be fortunate in the aforementioned things, but much less than what was said. In truth, he will be at home among religious people and those who worship God, and he will willingly dwell with them.

### Concerning Jupiter in the house of Mars.

If he remains in Aries or Scorpio, whatever the birth may be, it signifies a native fortunate among kings, nobles, magnates, and bearers of arms. He will be a man of great stability and of many excellences; even more so if Jupiter is then in the <term>angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> or their succeeding houses in a masculine sign. He will be a good warrior, a good fighter, and a good leader of armies, especially of large and famous ones.

### Concerning Jupiter in the house of the Sun.

If you find him in Leo during a daytime birth, it will signify that he will be named, famous, wise, and of profound genius. He will willingly spend time with kings, by whom he will be loved—not even by serving them much—and he will be loved not only by the magnates but also by the common people. And <term>Aboaly</term> <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat (c. 770–c. 835), a famous Persian astrologer and student of Mashallah.</note> said: if with this he is in the angles or their succeeding houses, and free from evils...

If, however, the birth is at night, the predicted things will happen but much less than what was stated, even if the planet is fortunate and well-disposed.

### On Jupiter in the house of Venus.

If the birth is during the day and Jupiter is in Taurus or Libra <note>These two signs are the "houses" or domains ruled by the planet Venus.</note>, it says that he will willingly associate with noble and wealthy women and those with dowries; he will enter into marriages with them and become wealthy through that. If, however, it is a night birth, he will willingly dwell with religious people and be a possessor of good faith; for that reason, he will profit and become rich.

### On Jupiter in the house of Mercury.

If he is found in Gemini or Virgo free from impediment in both day and night births, it signifies that he will be a great accumulator of wealth <note>original: "tbe" likely for "thesauri" (treasure)</note>; for that reason, he will be preferred over many other men and will seem almost as if he were a king.

### On Jupiter in the house of the Moon.

If you find him in Cancer, and he is fortunate, strong, and well-disposed in a day birth, it signifies that the man must be fortunate almost beyond measure, especially if he is in the **angles** <note>The four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note> or in the **succedent angles** <note>The houses that follow the angles, representing the stabilization of energy.</note>. And if the birth is at night, the predicted things happen but will be much less than what was said; he will still be a man of great name and fame, though that fame won't necessarily result in much practical profit.

### On Mars in the house of Saturn.

<image-desc>Woodcut illustration of the deity Mars. He is depicted as a knight in armor holding a sword and a shield with a face on it, riding in a chariot pulled by two horses. In the background sky, the zodiac symbols for Aries and Scorpio are visible. The word "MARS" is printed at the top.</image-desc>

If Mars is in Capricorn or Aquarius and is the **significator** <note>The planet that represents the person for whom the chart is cast.</note> of the birth, and is well-disposed, fortunate, and strong, it signifies the native will be high-spirited, bold, and arrogant in all matters of arms, wanting to accomplish whatever he thinks of in his heart; he will complete many of the things he begins, his fame will be exalted, and he will have kingly manners. And if he is of a lineage where it is possible, he will be made king; his fame will fly to distant parts; he will be a great spender and squanderer of both his own and others' substance. And if he has older brothers, he will send them to death before himself, or he will be the cause of their death, especially if the **Lord of the Eighth House** <note>The house associated with death.</note> aspects their significators or is joined with them bodily.

### On Mars in the house of Jupiter.

If Mars is in Sagittarius or Pisces and is the significator of the birth, and is fortunate and strong regardless of whether it is a day or night birth, it signifies the native will associate with kings, nobles, and the wealthy, and he will be greatly loved by them; for they will put him in charge of their business and leadership of their armies, and even more so if Jupiter is then in Aries or Scorpio, fortunate and free.

### On Mars in his own house.

If Mars is in Aries or his other first house <note>Scorpio</note>, and even more so if it is a night birth, it signifies the native will be a master of war machines, such as trebuchets and other engines, and will be very ingenious and sharp in geometric reasoning. If, however, the birth is by day and he is **oriental** <note>Rising before the sun.</note> or away from the sun and no benefic aspects him, it signifies the native will be an evil,

<column-break/>

diabolical whisperer, a wronger of men, and one who willingly studies their misfortunes; he will suffer from hidden diseases like internal cancers and similar things, and if he is in Aries, he will fall from a high place, and from that fall his body will be injured in the part attributed to the sign <note>Aries rules the head in medical astrology.</note>. For if he is in Scorpio, his malice will be lessened.

### On Mars in the house of the Sun.

If Mars is in Leo and is the significator of the birth, whether it is day or night, it signifies that misfortunes will occur involving the destruction of his person and property, and diseases of the eyes will surround him, especially the right eye; diseases of the stomach will prevail, and his mastery will be mostly in things involving iron and fire. It also signifies he will meet a sudden death, or perhaps be beheaded or hanged, especially if Mars is then in the **tenth house** <note>The highest point in the sky, associated with public status and judgment.</note> or otherwise killed by the hands of men. And **Aboaly** <note>Abū 'Ali al-Khayyāt, a 9th-century Persian astrologer whose work was widely used in medieval Europe.</note> said he or his father will die on a journey.

### On Mars in the house of Venus.

If Mars is in Taurus or Libra and is the significator, it signifies the native will be lustful, a fornicator, a sodomite, and a criminal in all sexual abuses, a deceiver and mocker of women; he will be mocked and deceived by them and will marry some just so they can commit adultery, and some he will commit adultery with and later marry them; and in all these and similar things he will follow an evil way and suffer loss and detriment. And Aboaly said if he is in Taurus, it signifies the native will be a traitor, a malicious liar, a threatener, and a fornicator. If you find him in Libra, it signifies he will suffer wounds in hidden and shameful parts of his body, or perhaps be burned on some part of his body.

### On Mars in the house of Mercury.

If he is found in Gemini or Virgo, regardless of the type of birth, it signifies the native will be negligent; yet he will be carnal and changeable regarding worldly matters; he will be crafty and not very law-abiding; he will strive to profit however he can, both through theft and other illicit means. If he applies himself to writing, he will be a good scribe; he will easily learn foreign languages and understand books and various speeches well, clarifying their intent; his talent will be very good, and he will be distinguished in the sciences above others who study with him.

### On Mars in the house of the Moon.

If he is found in Cancer, it signifies he will be inconstant, changing easily from one purpose to another; he will have a deep talent in all sciences and succeed in them; he will willingly study evil acts. And Aboaly said he will suffer an illness or impediment in the hidden parts of his body; he will die a sudden death and squander his mother's goods; his mother will suffer a long infirmity from his birth.

### On the Sun in the house of Saturn.

If the Sun is the significator of a birth and you see him staying in Capricorn or Aquarius, I say it is a sad birth; if by day, it signifies the native is a man of good quality, benevolent, and cheerful. Good at commerce, of good temperament, yet with some...

### On the Sun in the house of Jupiter.
If you find the Sun in Sagittarius or Pisces <note>These two signs are the "houses" or domains ruled by the planet Jupiter.</note> and the birth is during the day, it signifies that the native will be more excellent than all his relatives and will be very famous among men. He will gladly keep company with nobles and great men. He will be inclined toward the worship of Venus <note>Meaning sexual activity or physical pleasures.</note> beyond what is appropriate, to such an extent that for that reason he will be called a fornicator and will commit incest; he will not avoid fornicating with the wives of his relatives, nor even with his own stepmother.

### On the Sun in the house of Mars.
If you find the Sun in Aries and the birth is during the day, and he is the "figure" or ruler of that birth, being good and well-disposed—that is, fortunate and strong—it signifies the native will be fortunate, exalted, and of great name in the future. He will be especially favored among kings, nobles, and great men, and will gladly participate in wars; this will last for him as long as he lives, unless the **lords of the triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water); their "lords" are specific planets that govern them.</note> of the Ascendant work against it; while they cannot take away the predicted things, they can diminish them. If, however, the birth is at night, it signifies the predicted things will happen for only a third part of what was said above. And indeed, if you find him in Scorpio in a daytime birth, it signifies he will not be very fortunate unless the lords of the aforementioned triplicity provide their help; but whatever his fortune may be, it signifies he will have illnesses and will be "hepatic" <note>original: "epaticus"; relating to the liver, often associated with a melancholic or sluggish temperament.</note>. And **Aboali** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat (c. 770–c. 835), a famous Persian astrologer and student of Mashallah.</note> said he would be weighed down by a terrible death. If the birth is at night, it signifies the predicted things will be diminished or increased according to the disposition of the lords of the triplicity.

### On the Sun in its own house.
And if the Sun is in Leo at someone’s birth, and the birth is during the day and he is well-disposed in an **angle** <note>The strongest points in a chart: houses 1, 4, 7, and 10.</note>, and especially in the tenth or in a **succedent angle** <note>The houses following the angles: 2, 5, 8, and 11.</note> (and particularly the tenth), it signifies the native will be a great, strong, and exalted king. If he is born of such a lineage that great offices or higher dignities are appropriate, he will achieve them. If, however, he is born of a mediocre lineage, even if he does not reach the ultimate kingdom, he will nevertheless reach the greatest honors, the greatest dignities, wealth, and unexpected income. If he is of low birth, he will reach great offices and dignities at which men will greatly marvel; he will, however, fear lest great troubles come upon him for that reason. And Aboali said that in night births, it signifies a person full of folly, and he will be quickly overcome by death; yet he will gain good things during travels.

### On the Sun in the house of Venus.
If indeed you find the Sun dwelling in Libra or Taurus, whether that birth is by day or night, and he is the figure of that birth, it signifies a good native and a clever interpreter of dreams, and a finder of secret and even hidden things, but in the end, he will sin in the shamefulness of sex <note>original: "coitus"</note>.

### On the Sun in the house of Mercury.
And if the Sun is in Gemini or Virgo during someone's daytime birth, and he is the figure of that birth, it signifies the native will be very profound in the sciences and a teacher of other teachers of his time, as well as being of good character and future fame. And Aboali said perhaps he will be known in **astronomy** <note>In this period, "astronomy" and "astrology" were often used interchangeably as the same science.</note> and beloved by kings and nobles. If, however, the birth is at night, it signifies him to be needy and unfortunate; he will gladly perform evil works. And

Aboali said that in youth he will indeed be poor, but when he reaches middle age, he will abound in riches; yet pains will happen to him in the aforementioned areas and in the hidden parts of his body. He will be a "pourer out" <note>Someone who leads others astray.</note>, causing men to fall into the lapse of demonic works.

### On Venus in the house of Saturn.

For that reason, he will incur many contentions and quarrels, and by occasion of those contentions, many sinister things will happen to him. He will fall into suspicion of his wife, and it will be possible that on account of that suspicion, he will kill her.

### On Venus in the house of the Sun.
And if Venus is present in Leo, being the significator of that birth, whatever her state may be, and similarly whatever that birth may be, it signifies that the native will burn with love for women, and that he will abound in the worship of Venus, and will be improperly lustful, and will desire to abuse boys <note>A common medieval astrological reference to pederasty or non-procreative sexual acts.</note>.

And Aboali said that he will be fortunate and will follow good in all his times.

### On Venus in the house of Mercury.

### On Mercury in the house of Saturn.
<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the planet Mercury. Mercury is depicted as a man in a chariot pulled by two roosters. He holds a caduceus, his traditional winged staff. And if you find Mercury dwelling in Capricorn or Aquarius <note>These are the houses of Saturn.</note> in anyone's birth, whether by day or night, and he alone is the "shaper" <note>original: "figutor," referring to the planetary ruler of the chart.</note> of the birth, whatever his state may be, it will signify the person born will be of evil suspicion and of a heavy tongue; nevertheless, he will have an outward association with religious and wise men.

### On Mercury in the house of Jupiter.
But if in anyone's birth you find Mercury in Sagittarius or Pisces <note>The houses of Jupiter.</note> and he is the shaper of the birth, and the birth is by day and he is of good being and quality, it signifies the person born will have association with kings and will manage their affairs and those of the common people; he will be wise in judgments and in judging. If, however, it is a nocturnal birth, whatever his state may be, it will signify this, but much less than what was said before.

### On Mercury in the house of Mars.
But if you find Mercury in Aries or Scorpio <note>The houses of Mars.</note>, whether the birth is by day or night, and he is the shaper of that birth of whatever condition, it will signify the person born is a thief, a deceiver, false, a liar, cunning, and surrounded on all sides by every kind of malice, and from that, he will perpetrate many evils.

### On Mercury in the house of the Sun.
If indeed you find Mercury dwelling in Leo <note>The house of the Sun.</note> and he is of good being and well-disposed, being the shaper of the birth, whatever the birth may be, it signifies the person born will acquire the friendship of the great and noble and will gladly stay among them. But if you find him ill-disposed, whatever the birth may be, it will signify that he will turn out to be a deceiver and incompetent.

### On Mercury in the house of Venus.
And if you find Mercury in Taurus or Libra <note>The houses of Venus.</note> in anyone's birth, whatever the birth may be, and he is the shaper of it, it signifies the person born will be lively and humorous: and he will be knowledgeable in all sciences and all things from which and in which men take delight.

### On Mercury in his own house.
If however you find Mercury dwelling in Gemini or Virgo <note>These are Mercury's own houses.</note> and he is the shaper of the birth, and he is of good being and well-disposed, it signifies the person born will be upright and perfect in all sciences, both the theoretical and the practical, as well as the mechanical arts.

### On Mercury in the house of the Moon.
When however you find Mercury dwelling in Cancer <note>The house of the Moon.</note> and he is the significator of the birth, being of good being and well-disposed, it signifies the person born will gladly feast and know well how to prepare foods, and will be of good will, not delighting himself in the worship of Venus <note>Meaning sexual excess.</note>, and will turn out faithful and benevolent.

### On the Moon in the house of Saturn.
<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the Moon (Luna). Luna is depicted as a female figure with a crescent moon above her head, sitting in a chariot pulled by two human figures. Below the chariot are scenes representing the Moon's influence on earthly life: a man plowing a field with oxen, and another figure near a gate or prison. To the right, a scholar stands holding a book. Above the chariot is the zodiac symbol for Cancer, which is the Moon's own house.</image-desc>
If you know that the Moon remains in Capricorn or Aquarius <note>The houses of Saturn.</note> and she is well-disposed, and the birth is at night, and she is the significatrix of that birth—and if she is waning <note>original: "in diminutione lune"</note> it signifies less—it signifies the person born will suffer from ailments of the eyes and pains of the kidneys <note>original: "renum"</note>, and generally suffer from the aforementioned. If however the birth is by day, he will be less unstable from the aforementioned ailments. In either birth, whatever her state may be, it signifies that the person born will not be commended by men: but they will strive to blaspheme him and speak ill of him, even while he is doing good and speaking well.

### On the Moon in the house of Jupiter.
But if you see the Moon as the significatrix in Sagittarius or Pisces <note>The houses of Jupiter.</note> in either birth, it signifies the person born will prevail among all his blood relatives: and that he will seem like a king among them in respect to them, and his fame will be exalted; nevertheless, he will be stained by the vice of lust <note>original: "luxurie"</note>, and will behave lustfully with forbidden women.

### On the Moon in the house of Mars.
If indeed you find the Moon in Aries or Scorpio <note>The houses of Mars.</note> and she is the significatrix of the birth, whatever type of birth and whatever her state may be, it signifies the person born is a deceiver and a thief, avoiding good works, studying in evil things, gladly staying with robbers and other wicked men, and desiring to associate with them.

### On the Moon in the house of the Sun.
When you know the Moon remains in Leo <note>The house of the Sun.</note>, she being the significatrix of the birth in either type of birth, it signifies that the person born will have association with kings, the wealthy, and the great: and even more so if the Moon dwells in the first or last **terms** <note>Subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by specific planets.</note> of Leo.

### On the Moon in the house of Venus.
But if the Moon is found in Taurus or Libra <note>The houses of Venus.</note>, whatever the birth may be, and she is the shaper of the birth, it signifies the person born will burn with love for women, provided she [the Moon] is not afflicted <note>original: "impedita"</note>: and he will delightfully rejoice with them and obtain good and profit from them.

### On the Moon in the house of Mercury.
And if the Moon stands in Gemini or Virgo <note>The houses of Mercury.</note> and she is the significatrix of the birth, let it signify that the person born will be benevolent, keeping a good life, and will strive to harm no one; he will be of good intelligence and good natural talent; he will gladly indulge in lust with girls and young women.

### On the Moon in her own house.
When however you find the Moon in Cancer <note>The Moon's own house.</note> and she is of good being and is the shaper of the birth, it signifies that the person born will have association with kings and the great: and will pursue good, utility, and profit from them. And **Aboaly** <note>Likely referring to Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works were translated into Latin.</note> said: if she is joined or applied to the malefic planets <note>Usually Mars or Saturn.</note>, it will signify various ailments for the person born. If, however, she is joined or applied to the fortunes <note>Usually Jupiter or Venus.</note>, it signifies health of the body and temperance.

## Chapter Three: On the years of the Firdaria and their dispositions.
The ancient wise men considered certain years in births which are not all "greater," nor "middle," nor even "lesser" <note>Referring to the three standard lengths of years assigned to planets in medieval astrology.</note>; but they called them the years of the **Firdaria** <note>original: "sirdarie." A Persian astrological system of planetary periods governing different stages of a person's life.</note>, that is, the "disposed years." For any planet disposes its part of the life of the person born according to its portion of the Firdaria years in this manner: for whatever the birth may be, the disposition of the years will begin...

<summary>This page details the character traits and physical health predicted by the positions of Mercury and the Moon in the houses of other planets. It concludes by introducing the Firdaria, a system of planetary periods used to divide the human lifespan into astrological stages.</summary>
<keywords>Mercury, Moon, Cancer, Capricorn, Firdaria, astrology, character traits, health, Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, planetary houses</keywords>

--- Page 364 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Firdaria," a Persian system of planetary periods used to predict the stages of a person's life, which began at the end of the previous page.</meta>

The <term>Firdaria</term> <note>A system of time-lords or planetary periods of Persian origin used to divide a human life into specific chapters ruled by different planets.</note> are determined by the luminary which holds authority, and that planet will govern the life of the person born according to the number of years of its Firdaria. However, this is not done without the participation of the other planets. For if the birth is by day, the period begins with the Sun—the diurnal luminary—which will govern the life of the newborn according to the quantity of its Firdaria years, which are ten, with the participation of all the other planets. But the Sun itself holds the primary leadership, especially in the first seventh part of those years. In the second part, Venus will participate with it, as she follows the Sun in the order of the celestial spheres. In the third seventh part, Mercury will participate, as he follows Venus in the order of the spheres. In the fourth seventh part, the Moon will participate, following Mercury. In the fifth seventh part, Saturn will participate, following the Moon’s sphere. In the sixth seventh part, Jupiter will participate, following Saturn. In the seventh and final part, Mars will participate, who follows Jupiter and is the seventh planet from the Sun. 

After this, Venus—who follows the Sun in the order of the spheres—will govern the life of the newborn for the quantity of her Firdaria years, which are eight. All the other planets will participate with her in the governance of those years, each taking their seventh part, just as was described for the Sun's participation. Next, Mercury will govern for the length of his Firdaria, which is thirteen years, and the others will participate with him for their seventh parts. Then the Moon will govern for nine years, with each of the others participating for their seventh part. Then Saturn will govern for eleven years, with the participation of the others as described for the Sun. Then Jupiter will govern for twelve years, then Mars for seven years, both with the participation of the other planets as stated above. Then the <term>Head of the Dragon</term> <note>The North Node of the Moon.</note> will govern for three years. Then the <term>Tail of the Dragon</term> <note>The South Node of the Moon.</note> will govern for two years. After this, the cycle returns to the Sun, proceeding successively as described until the end of the person's life.

### On the nocturnal birth.

But if the birth should be at night, the governance begins with the Moon, which is the nocturnal luminary. Everything will proceed exactly as was described when the period begins with the Sun, both regarding the participation of the planets and their succession in the order of the spheres. All these "shapers" or governors will dispose of the life according to their condition: if a planet is well-disposed, it increases good fortune and diminishes misfortune; if poorly disposed, it increases misfortune and diminishes good fortune. This is a laborious task but one that must be carefully observed, for some astrologers, seeking to avoid the work, do not consider it in their judgments and thus fall into error. These Firdaria years all together total seventy-five, which—though it rarely happens—some newborns live through entirely. In such cases, the years are not given to the person by the <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>original: "alcocoden"; the "giver of years" in a birth chart, a planet used to calculate life expectancy.</note>, for that planet might be so weak that it could not grant the number of years that the Firdaria provides. Therefore, an astrologer may sometimes be deceived when predicting the number of years for a newborn if he is not careful—and it is no wonder.

### Chapter 4. On the eminence or transit of one planet over another.

Regarding the eminence or transit of one planet over another, <term>Alchabicius</term> <note>A 10th-century Arab astrologer and mathematician, Al-Qabisi, whose "Introduction to the Art of Judgments of the Stars" was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> says that you must look at the "mean course" of each planet as well as its "equated place" <note>Medieval astronomers distinguished between a planet's average position (mean course) and its actual, corrected position in the sky (equated place).</note>. For if its equated place is less than its mean course, the planet itself will be ascending from the middle of its <term>epicycle</term> <note>A small circle whose center moves around the circumference of a larger one; used in Ptolemaic astronomy to explain the complex motions of planets.</note> toward its summit, reaching its farthest distance from Earth. And if its equated place is

<column-break/>

more than its mean course, the planet will be descending from the middle of its epicycle toward its lower part, coming to its closest distance to Earth. But if both are equal, the planet will be in the middle of its epicycle—that is, between the farthest and closest distances. You can find this most accurately by subtracting the smaller from the larger, multiplying the remainder by 7, and dividing the result by 22. The result of this division will be the quantity of the planet's ascent or descent in its circle.

### On Venus & Mercury.

Following Alchabicius, you must take the distance between the place of the Sun and the place of Venus, and likewise between the Sun and Mercury, and subtract the smaller from the larger, then multiply and divide as described above. By this, we shall know which of them is stronger in its circle. He also said that when Venus and Mercury are "oriental" <note>Rising before the Sun in the morning.</note> and the place of either of them is less than the place of the Sun, we must take the remainder between the Sun's place and the planet's place and calculate with it as described for the superior planets. He stated that the significance of the planets is stronger and more immediate when they pass over one another in conjunction; however, in opposition or in a "square" aspect, their significance will be weaker and less apparent. And when one is ascending and the other descending, the ascending one goes "over" the descending one. If both are descending, the one with the lesser descent goes over the one with the greater. If both are ascending, the one with the greater ascent goes over the one with the lesser.

### On another way a planet is elevated over another.

There is also another way a planet may be elevated over another and be stronger. If one planet is northern and the other southern <note>Referring to celestial latitude, or the planet's position north or south of the ecliptic line.</note>, the northern one goes over the southern. If both are northern, the one that is more northern goes over the one that is less so. If both are southern, the one that is less southern goes over the one that is more southern. Therefore, it is said that the Moon goes over all the planets, and each of the others goes over all the rest in these two ways. Likewise, if any planet is in the middle of its epicycle—at its farthest or closest distance—or if it is in its <term>gençahar</term> <note>original: "gençahar"; from the Persian "jawzihr," referring to the lunar nodes or the "Dragon" that intersects the path of the Sun and Moon.</note>, then the one ascending in the epicycle goes over the one at the farthest or closest distance. The northern planet goes over the southern, over the descending planet, and over the one in its *gençahar*. And the one in its *gençahar* goes over the southern, the descending, and the one at the closest distance.

### Chapter five. On the opening of the gates according to Alchabicius.

Following the above is the "opening of the gates." This happens when two planets whose "houses" are opposite join together, such as Saturn with the luminaries [Sun/Moon], Jupiter with Mercury, or Mars with Venus. When one of these lighter planets joins with one of the heavier ones and finds it in its own house, or its exaltation, or in two of its other minor dignities, it "receives" the lighter planet and is said to "open the gates" for it. This is like a man who, finding his enemy in his own house, would honor him and show him no rudeness, provided he was not a mortal enemy—unless he were a bold, wild, or beast-like man who lacked any civility toward people. Such a man was <term>Ecelinus de Romano</term> <note>Ezzelino III da Romano (1194–1259), a notoriously cruel Ghibelline warlord in northern Italy, often used in medieval texts as the archetype of a tyrant without mercy.</note>, who spared neither sex nor age, neither religious order nor dignity. All that has been described above is the "opening of the gates."

<meta>This page transitions from the discussion of the "Firdaria" (planetary periods) to two other specific time-keeping methods in medieval astrology: the system of planetary hours following a conjunction (New Moon) and the technique of "profections," which involves moving the chart forward by one zodiac sign per year to predict annual events.</meta>

# Chapter 6. On the 12 hours of the Sun and Moon which are joined to the Sun.

Alchabicius <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century Arab astrologer whose work was a standard textbook in medieval Europe.</note> mentions that "Albuzit" <note>A Latinized reference to Abu Ma'shar, another highly influential Persian astrologer.</note> names those hours which follow immediately after the Moon separates from its physical conjunction with the Sun. Alchabicius says that the ancient wise men divided these 12 hours into groups of three—that is, into three equal parts, each consisting of four equal hours. They applied these 12 hours to the Sun and judged them based on the <term>lords of the triplicity</term> <note>A group of three planets that rule the zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> in which the Sun was located at the hour of the conjunction, and so on for the Moon. They began with the Sun, giving it the first four hours; the second four hours were given to the second lord of that same triplicity; and the final 4 hours were given to the third lord of that triplicity. 

Next, the aforementioned wise men gave 12 hours to Venus following the Sun's 12 hours, and they divided those into three divisions just as was described for the Sun. They judged each of those divisions by giving the first four hours to Venus, the second four hours to the second lord of Venus's triplicity, and the final four hours to the third lord of that triplicity; they then judged the outcome based on which of these triplicity lords was best positioned. They did the same for Mercury and its entire triplicity. Similarly, they did this with the Moon and its triplicity division. Then with Saturn and its entire triplicity, as well as with Jupiter and Mars and their lords of triplicity. After this, the cycle returns to the Sun until the next conjunction occurs.

# On the 12 burnt hours after the conjunction.

And Alchabicius says that Albuzit claims that after the conjunction of the Sun and Moon, there are 12 equal hours which are called <term>burnt</term> <note>original: "combuste." In astrology, "combust" usually refers to a planet being too close to the Sun, weakening its power. Here, it refers to an unlucky period of time.</note>; no one ought to begin any work during them.

# On the 72 unburnt hours.

After those 12 burnt hours, there are 72 "unburnt" hours, and after those 72 unburnt hours, there are another 12 burnt hours; it continues thus for each group until the next conjunction follows. After this, he says one must observe the ages of the 12 burnt hours in three equal divisions. They said that if someone begins to wage war in the first four hours, the loss of his soul <note>In this context, "loss of soul" likely means death or the loss of one's life.</note> is to be feared. If he begins in the second four hours, harm to the body is to be feared, but without the loss of the soul. And if he begins to plow <note>meaning to begin a new agricultural or business venture.</note> in those hours, great loss in his possessions and his body is to be feared, though without loss of life, yet there is a fear of ruin regarding their affairs. And if he begins in the final four hours, the loss of his substance <note>Wealth or physical property.</note> is to be feared, as is mentioned elsewhere.

# Chapter seven on the profection of years, both for the world and for births.

Having mentioned above the number of years attributed to everyone born, it seems fitting and right to me to speak subsequently about the <term>profection</term> <note>original: "profectio," meaning "advancement." A technique where the Ascendant of a birth chart is moved forward by one sign for every year of life.</note> of those years. Now, a profection is the meaning that results from the things that happen from the sign that immediately follows the sign that was the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> of the birth and its lord—whether good or evil—or indirectly as shall be said in the sections above. For it is called a "profection" because it advances by changing itself every year by one sign according to the continuous succession of the signs. The meaning of this one sign provides support for the entire <term>revolution</term> <note>The "Solar Return," a chart cast for a person's birthday each year.</note> of the year, whether in good or evil, sometimes increasing or sometimes diminishing. Its interpretation is the <term>alcocoden</term> <note>original: "alcocoden." While usually referring to the "giver of life," here the author defines it as the "prince of accidents/events."</note>, which is the "prince of events" that are to come to the newborn in any year of their revolution. 

The knowledge of finding this is as follows: you shall consider the year, day, month, and hours of whatever birth you wish, and you shall see how many solar years the person has already completed. You shall take one sign from the birth ascendant for every solar year, beginning from the hour of that person's birth according to the succession of the signs, giving one sign to every year.

<column-break/>

And where that number ends, the sign that follows immediately is the "sign of profection" from the birth ascendant, and it will be the ascendant of the profection for the year that then follows (which you have not yet included in your count). The profection of that year will be at the same degree of that sign as the degree of the ascendant was at the hour of birth. Understand this regarding every profection: it will always be in every year at the same degree of the sign in which it falls as it was in the sign that preceded it in the year that has just passed. 

The planet that is the lord of that sign is called the <term>alcocoden</term>, which is the "helper" of that planet which is the lord of the sign that was the ascendant of the year's revolution. Through such a planet, the disposition of that person's status in that year is shown to you, even if many revolutions were to occur within it. 

For annual honors and dignities of the person born, you shall look to the sign of profection from the Sun, taking one whole sign for every solar year to perceive that profection. For the state of the body and the mind of the person, you shall look to the sign of profection from the Moon. For their mastery <note>Skills or career.</note> and offices, you can look to the sign of the <term>midheaven</term> <note>original: "medii celi," the highest point in the chart, representing career and public reputation.</note>. To know their profit and prosperity, you can look to the sign of profection from the <term>Part of Fortune</term> and from the sign of the <term>House of Substance</term> <note>The 2nd House, governing money and possessions.</note>. 

For the profection of brothers, look to the sign of profection from the House of Brothers <note>The 3rd House.</note>. For the profection of fathers, look to the sign of profection from the House of Fathers <note>The 4th House.</note>. For the profection of children, look to the profection of the sign of the House of Children <note>The 5th House.</note>. For the profection of male and female servants, look to the sign of profection from the House of Servants <note>The 6th House.</note>. For the profection of wives, partners, and enemies, look to the sign of profection from the House of Wives <note>The 7th House.</note>. For the profection of their substance, look to the sign of profection from the House of the Wives' Substance <note>The 8th House.</note>. For the profection of religious matters, look to the sign of profection from the House of Religion <note>The 9th House.</note>. For the profection of kings, look to the sign of profection from the House of Kings <note>The 10th House.</note>. For the profection of friends, look to the sign of profection of the House of Friends <note>The 11th House.</note>. For the profection of hidden enemies, look to the sign of profection of the House of Hidden Enemies <note>The 12th House.</note>. 

And know that a profection is a thing that in some way alters the revolution, which happens singularly according to the succession of the signs. For whatever the ascendant [of the revolution] may be, the profection only happens from sign to the sign that follows it immediately, which does not happen in a revolution. And the profection alters the revolution in this manner: if the revolution signifies good in that year and the profection also signifies good, it increases the good signified by the revolution. If, however, it signifies [bad] through them, it diminishes the good signified by the revolution. If both the revolution and the profection signify evil, it increases the evil signified by the revolution. But if the revolution signifies evil and the profection signifies good, it will diminish the evil signified by the revolution; and thus the profection and the revolution interact with one another.

# Chapter 8. On the order of profection.

The order of profection is such: let us suppose that someone is born with Aries as the ascendant at 10 degrees. In the following year, Taurus will be the sign of profection at 10 degrees; it will not, however, be the ascendant of the revolution, but it will in some way take its place. In the third year, Gemini will be the sign of profection at 10 degrees, but it will not be the ascendant of the following revolution; and so on in order through the end of the signs. After the completion of the 12 signs, the profection returns to the first sign; and so you shall arrange it until the end of the person's life. And from this, I will provide you with a true example.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions on "profections," a predictive technique where the natal chart is advanced by one zodiac sign per year. The author, Guido Bonatti, provides a personal case study using his own nephew’s birth chart from 1267 before moving into "mundane" astrology—the study of world events, kingdoms, and religious orders.</meta>

<sig>m iii</sig>

A certain nephew of mine was born in the Era of the Arabs <note>original: "era arabum"; refers to the Hijri calendar</note> in the year 665, in the third month, on the 9th day. And in the Era of Christ, 1267, on the sixth day at the beginning of January. The **ascendant** of his birth was **13 degrees of Capricorn**, with **Mars** in it at 6 degrees and 25 minutes. The **Sun** was in it at 12 degrees and 10 minutes. The **second house** was in **Aquarius** at 20 degrees. The **third house** was **Aries** at 2 degrees. The **fourth house** was **Taurus** at 12 degrees; the **Moon** was in it at 5 degrees and 12 minutes. The **Part of Fortune** was at 6 degrees and 5 minutes. **Gemini** was the **fifth house** at 4 degrees, with the **Tail of the Dragon** <note>The South Node of the Moon</note> in it at 1 degree and 31 minutes. The **sixth house** was **Gemini** at 24 degrees and 15 minutes. The **seventh house** was **Cancer** at 13 degrees, with **Saturn** in it at 4 degrees and 15 minutes. The **eighth house** was **Leo** at 20 degrees, with **Jupiter** in it at 23 degrees and 20 minutes. The **ninth house** was **Libra** at 2 degrees. **Scorpio** was the **tenth house** at 12 degrees. **Sagittarius** was the **eleventh house** at 4 degrees, with the **Head of the Dragon** <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> in it at 1 degree and 31 minutes, **Mercury** at 5 degrees and 55 minutes, and **Venus** at 22 degrees and 16 minutes. That same **Sagittarius** was the **twelfth house** at 23 degrees.

When he had already passed five solar years, I looked at a certain <term>revolution</term> <note>An annual chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to its birth position</note> of his. The 5th year's <term>profection</term> <note>A technique where the chart is moved forward by one sign for every year of life</note> arrived from the ascendant of his birth to **Gemini**, which is the sixth sign from Capricorn, reaching the 13th degree. The profection of the Sun reached the 13th degree of that same sign, and **Mercury** was the <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>The planet that "gives years" or determines the length of life</note> or the lord of that year and revolution. The profection of Mars reached Gemini at the 7th degree; the profection of the Moon reached the 6th degree of Libra (which is the sixth sign from Taurus); the profection of the Part of Fortune reached the 7th degree of that same Libra; the profection of Saturn reached the 5th degree of Sagittarius (which is the sixth sign from Sagittarius <note>original: "sextum signum a sagitario"—likely a scribal error for Aquarius</note>); the profection reached the 24th degree of Capricorn (which is the sixth sign from Leo); the sign of Virgo was included. The profection of Mercury reached the 6th degree of Taurus (the sixth sign from Sagittarius), and the profection of Venus reached the 13th degree of that same Taurus. The profection of the **tenth house** reached the 12th degree of Aries, which is the sixth sign from the degree of the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The highest point in the sky at the moment of birth</note> at birth. 

To tell all the things that happened to him in that year would be too long a story to dwell upon, so I will instead pursue more useful matters. You shall therefore consider every profection you wish, for it will always be in such a degree of a sign as you found it at the hour of birth, moving itself from one sign to the next in immediate and successive order every solar year by one whole sign. The planet which is the <term>Almuten</term> <note>The planet with the most dignity or "power" at a specific point in the zodiac</note> over that place, or which is in it, or which projects its rays toward it, shall be called the "helper" of the ruler of that revolution along with the Alcocoden. However, it is not called the Alcocoden unless it is the lord of that sign. 

And if any planet or its rays are in that place, and you wish to know when the profection will reach it or its rays: **Alchabicius** <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century authority</note> said that you should look at the distance in degrees and minutes between the degree where the year's profection has arrived and the planet. Multiply that by 12 <unclear>and a measure of oil</unclear> <note>original: "fertaz vnt⁹ olei"; this is likely a corruption or a highly specific technical measurement formula in the source manuscript</note> and whatever result you get will be the day of that year on which the event occurs.

## Chapter 9. On the profection of the years of the world.

The profection of the years of the world varies somewhat from the profection of the years of a birth. For the profection of the years of a birth is taken from the ascendant of someone's birth and then changes every solar year by one whole sign,

as was said. However, the profection of the years of the world is taken from the first minute of **Aries**, or from the beginning of some other great matter, such as a kingdom, an empire, a sect, or a religion. For example: when the reign of **Nebuchadnezzar** began, or the reign of **Ptolemy**, or the reign of **Philip**, the reign of **Alexander**, the reign of King **Yezdegerd**, or the reign of the **Romans**. 

It is the same as when the sect or religion of **Augustine** began, or the sect of **Benedict**, or the **Order of Friars Minor** <note>The Franciscans</note>, which began in the Era of the Arabs in the year 609, in the month of Rabi' al-Thani <note>original: "rabe vltimi"</note>, and in the Era of Christ, the year 1211. Its beginning was such—it had such an ascendant—that it will "under-root" <note>original: "subradicabit"; meaning to take root beneath or perhaps to undermine</note> all other sects and all other orders living under the Roman Church. But concerning its end, I do not dare to speak for fear that I might fall into common rumor. Indeed, it will be very public when it arrives, and there will be an immense outcry about it. 

Those who understand the beginnings of things always know their accidents through their annual revolutions based on that beginning. The profection will place the parts according to their being, sometimes adding, sometimes diminishing or taking away from the revolution. By considering it from sign to sign successively as I have said, the accidents of that matter whose revolution you desire can be known. However, this profection of such "beginnings" is not quite as simple as the profection of the years of the world, but it resembles it in some way because of its long duration.

As for the profection from the ascendant of the profection, and concerning the <term>significator</term> <note>The planet that represents a specific person or topic in a chart</note> which might be in one of the <term>angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of a chart</note> or in any other place besides the angles; and concerning the significator of the direct circle and the significator of the oblique circle, and certain other things found in the "Fourth Difference" of the *Introduction* of **Alchabicius** regarding the judgments of this art—I will not speak of them now. In that treatise, he has determined enough about all those things with a long discourse, so it is not necessary for me to sweat over them now. Furthermore, although that work is useful and deep in knowledge, it requires a greater...

## Chapter 10: On the direction of significators and those things
## to be directed in the circle, and how many significators we 
## must direct which are directed by the wise.

The significators which are directed are seven, namely: the degree of the **ascendant**; the degree of the **Sun**; the degree of the **Moon**; the degree of the **Part of Fortune**; the degree of the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medium celi"</note>; the degree of the **Conjunction**; and also the degree of the **Prevention** <note>original: "preuentionis"; the New Moon or Full Moon occurring immediately before the birth.</note>. Indeed, the degree of the **ascendant** is directed according to the accidents <note>External events or physical changes.</note> that are to come to the native in their person, whether good, bad, or middling. Thus, if you see the direction coming to "good" planets <note>The "benefics," Jupiter and Venus.</note>, it says that the accidents of his body will be good. If, however, it reaches "bad" planets <note>The "malefics," Saturn and Mars.</note>, you shall judge justly. But if it reaches the lords of the <term>bounds</term> or those that are changeable or of a middling disposition, you shall pronounce a mediocrity of accidents—that is, neither truly good nor truly bad.

The **Sun**, truly, is directed to know to which dignities or exaltations the native ought to reach, regarding honor and secular fame. Whence, if the Sun is of good state and well-disposed, and the direction reaches well-disposed fortunes, it will signify the native coming to great and famous honors. If you find it so by its <term>aspect</term>, you can judge accordingly. But if the Sun is of middling disposition, or the fortunes it reaches are middling, it signifies the native coming to some dignities that are not very famous.

The **Moon** is directed to know the disposition of the native's body and the quality of their soul; likewise their marriage. Now, if the Moon is of good state and well-disposed, and the direction is to well-disposed fortunes, it signifies that the disposition of the native's body and the quality of the soul will be good and laudable. It also signifies that they will marry well if you find the lord of the **seventh house** is of good state and well-disposed, and in a good aspect with the lord of the ascendant, or with the Moon itself, or with the lord of the **Part of Marriage**. From middling factors, judge mediocrity.

The **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point representing prosperity.</note> is directed to know the native’s profit and the progress of their money, as well as its acquisition. Whence, if the Part of Fortune is well-disposed and the direction reaches well-disposed fortunes, it signifies the native acquiring and accumulating much money by lawful means. But if the fortunes are hindered, it signifies they will acquire money but will dissipate it after acquisition. If you see it joined by aspect, you can judge; if you find mediocrity, pronounce mediocrity.

The **Midheaven** <note>original: "medium celi"</note> is directed to know the works of the native and their arts or mastery, as **Alchabitus** <note>A 10th-century Arab astrologer.</note> says, or to all particular dispositions regarding their king. Whence, if the lord of the Midheaven or the Midheaven itself is well-disposed and the direction reaches well-disposed fortunes, the native will fare well in their trades, offices, and all secular affairs and stories related to them.

The degree of the **Conjunction** <note>The New Moon before birth.</note> is directed to foreknow and consider all the aforesaid matters up to the middle of the native's life, if the birth was "conjunctional." Whence, if it is well-disposed, it will increase the significance of those things signifying good and diminish those signifying evil. But if it is ill-disposed, it will increase the evil and diminish the good. You can say the same of the degree of **Prevention** <note>The Full Moon before birth.</note> for the period after the middle of life if the birth was "preventional." And the conjunction or aspect of fortunes or misfortunes with the <term>Almuten</term> <note>The planet with the most combined strength over a specific point.</note> over the aforesaid degrees and 

<column-break/>

conditions: for they will add or subtract according to their being and their dispositions. These things are to be considered not only in births but also at the beginnings of other things whose end is awaited.

If you wish to find the aforesaid in the **revolutions of the years** (both of the world and of births), look at the ascendant of any of those years. For if you wish to direct for a "Year of the World" <unclear>blackout</unclear> to foreknow the state of the **peasants** <note>original: "rusticorum"; referring to the common people/agriculture.</note>, we ought to direct <unclear>blackout</unclear> <unclear>blackout</unclear> giving 59 minutes and 8 <unclear>blackout</unclear> to everyone. <unclear>unclear</unclear> It may happen that the direction reaches fortunes or misfortunes; according to that, you can judge their state and status in those days until the end <unclear>unclear</unclear>. This is according to the **oblique circle**.

But if you wish to look at the direction of **kings**, look at them from the degree of the Midheaven according to the **direct circle**, giving 59 minutes for each <unclear>unclear</unclear>. Thus you will know the accidents that ought to happen to kings in that revolution in that they are kings. But in their own private deeds and in their persons, one should look at them just like other individual persons. According to whether the direction is seen to reach fortunes or misfortunes, you shall judge their being as good, bad, or middling, whether for kings or for peasants. You can say the same regarding the being of the revolutions of births; however, you must consider the revolutions of births from the ascendant of the birth and from the ascendant of the revolution. As for revolutions of the world, judge from the ascendant of the revolution of the years of the world: to know the state of the common people according to the oblique circle, but for revolutions of kings, according to the direct circle, to know their state as was said.

## Chapter 11: On the nature of the degrees of the signs in
## any sign.

It is necessary to know something else that the wise men of old, and especially the **Indians**, considered in births and rarely at their beginnings: they called it the "**Twelve-part division** of the planets or houses or signs" <note>This refers to the *Dodecatemoria*, where each 30-degree sign is divided into 12 parts of 2.5 degrees each.</note>. For it divides any sign into twelve divisions, each of which consists of two and a half degrees. They give these divisions to the twelve signs so that each sign has its own "twelfth" in every sign. In that twelfth, that sign signifies what pertains to the property of its nature, as **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> seems to intend.

Whence, when you wish to know in what sign's nature any degree of a sign lies, take the degrees from the start of the sign to the degree whose twelfth you seek, multiply that by 12, and divide the total in this manner: giving 2 degrees and 30 minutes to each sign, and see where your number leads you. For there will be the nature of that degree in the sign into whose twelfth it falls. 

Some of the modern wise men think it should be understood thus: that one takes the degree of the ascendant of any sign or any other house (according to what that house signifies), multiplies it by 12, and then adds the total to the degrees of the ascending sign or whichever house was the starting point. They then project this by 30, giving 30 to each sign or house, and the number is projected from the ascendant or the house you chose. Where the number ends, there will be the significance of the 12 signs and planets. Then, in whatever sign's twelfth the number falls, that sign and its lord will provide "assistance" to the ascendant or other house from which you began, and to its lord. Whence, if that sign and its lord are well-disposed, they will add something to the good and diminish something of the bad—specifically for a twelfth part of each. But if the sign and its lord are ill-disposed, it adds something to the bad and diminishes something of the good for a twelfth part. When the sign is well-disposed and its lord bad, or vice versa...
